Willing soul sellers might get decades of glory, riches, fame, adoration, hookups, or whatever the deal constituted, but at what cost? Compared to eternity, a lifetime is a mere blink of an eye. Not even a blink. Shoot, compared to eternity, a billion years is nothing, a trillion years, any defined number of years, is a mere moment. Eternity is a really long time to suffer fire, brimstone, and trident stabs in exchange for a few fleeting years of instant gratification.Fortunately, bargaining of souls is not a requirement to enjoy Devilish Fortunes, an online slot by Game Global partner Triple Edge Studios, and a reskin of Fire and Roses Joker. It does have a devilish character, though, sporting a purple waistcoat and flames for hair. He might be an inhabitant of the underworld, but this is one snappy-looking dude with his thumb firmly on the pulse of what's fashionable in his domain. Devilish Fortunes has a real snap to it in general. The reels have a pleasing spin to them, the animations are slick, and the whole operation functions with a well-oiled flow.Devilish Fortunes slot - base gameAs stated, no bargaining takes place around here, but if you want the chance to lay your hands on some of the potential fortunes, you'll have to pick a stake of 20 c to $/€50 per spin. The devilishness is held on a 5-reel gaming grid, placed in a 3-4-5-4-3 pattern, with increasing jackpot prizes displayed above each reel. Rated very highly volatile, Devilish Fortunes churns out a 96.01% RTP, though two lower return values are also available.In keeping with the theme, Devilish Fortunes' pay symbols include clubs, spades, diamonds, and hearts for the low pays, then dice, chips, cards, and a red diamond as the high pays. With 720 ways to win, winning combinations pay left to right from the rightmost side of the grid and right to left from the rightmost side of the grid. A payout of 0.8 to 1.2 times the bet is made for hitting 5 matching low pays, or 2 to 8 times the bet for 5 matching high pays. The devilish character is the game's wild, appearing on reels 2, 3, and 4, substituting all regular pay symbols.Devilish Fortunes: Slot FeaturesDevilish Fortunes slot - Wheel bonusOther symbols appearing on the reels are jackpot trigger symbols that are needed to activate the Jackpot Wheel and free spins scatter symbols.Jackpot WheelPossible in the base game only; when jackpot trigger symbols hit, they are collected to increase the jackpot on their reel by 0.5x the bet. Jackpots scale with the bet and reset when they are won. Collecting at least 1 jackpot trigger symbol gives a chance to spin the jackpot wheel. When activated, the Jackpot Wheel spins to award 1 of 5 guaranteed jackpots:The Mini starts at 5x and may go up to 75x.The Minor starts at 10x and may go up to 100x.The Major starts at 50x and may go up to 250x.The Mega starts at 200x and may go up to 1,000x.The Ultra starts at 1,000x and may go up to 5,000x.Free SpinsScatter symbols appear on all reels, spelling the word L, U, C, K, Y. Landing one scatter on each reel triggers 6 free spins. In addition, each triggering scatter awards either +1 extra free spin or increases the free spins win multiplier by +1. Free spins can be retriggered by landing a scatter on all reels. When this happens, players win 1x the bet plus the number of free spins when starting the feature.The free spins multiplier is displayed in a meter by the reels. The multiplier is applied to free spins way wins, and retrigger pays. Its value increases by 0.5x when scatter symbols land on exactly four reels in the base game. The maximum the multiplier meter can reach in the base game is x10, and upon entering free spins, x15. The multiplier resets to x1 when free spins are complete.Devilish Fortunes slot - free spinsDevilish Fortunes: Slot VerdictDevilish Fortunes' shiny presentation and particular subject matter helped make it a more enticing proposal than both Fire and Roses Joker and Fire and Roses Jolly Joker - the Christmas clone. Not saying it turned out to be a great game or anything like that, but it's one which pleasantly surprised when seen in action, after the so-so reactions to the two slots preceding it. The game can feel quite busy as if there's more going on than simply looking out for the two main features - the Jackpot Wheel and free spins (with multiplier). This was also partly due to the ongoing collection of jackpot trigger symbols and the increasing multiplier when scatters hit on four reels. Paying both ways doesn't hurt either.Once the initial warm reception simmered down a notch, Devilish Fortunes settled into a fairly entertaining groove. It's kind of sweet the way Games Global studios pass ideas around amongst one another, as Devilish Fortunes also brought back memories of Tippy's Golden Pot, which was reviewed not long before this one. What connects the two is the rising jackpot collection system, where each prize has a start and maximum point. Tippy's was higher, for the competitive types, reaching 10,000x, compared to Devilish Fortunes' 5,000x. The free spins/rising multiplier combo is the same as before, where being able to make use of 4 scatter near misses to boost the multiplier meter in the base game for use when the round is triggered is no bad thing.So, while not groundbreaking, Devilish Fortunes turned out to be a perfectly fine slot. The dual collections, the pay both ways, the jackpot element, and the round of multiplier free spins have been dressed up in subject matter with a higher intrigue factor than before, making Devilish Fortunes' outer shell a more interesting vehicle for what it has to offer mechanically.

Title: Spinman
review: Spinman: Slot OverviewWhen factoring in the likes of Marvel, DC, and all the other outfits producing comic books, there are a lot of superheroes keeping the world safe. So many in fact, it's amazing there are any baddies left to fight. Well, in case we needed more heroes in capes, here is one from developer Hacksaw Gaming, fighting crime in a luckless city 'where the Villains of Misfortune hold the reels hostage'. His name is Spinman, and he pops justice on the reels with the aid of three bonus rounds, one a Hidden Epic Bonus round, and expanding, multiplying wild symbols, a feature Hacksaw Gaming can't seem to resist.The mighty Spinman hovers on the right side of the screen, looking a little like a neon green and grey version of Prowler from Spiderman. Modern comic books might be riots of colour, but Spinman goes in the opposite direction, being a largely monochrome noir-hued escapade that uses pay symbols to splash brighter colours on the grid. Extra colour is injected when higher bonus rounds trigger, too, but dark mystery appears to be Spinman's preferred MO.Spinman slot - base gameIt would appear that Spinman is available with two math models, one rated 2 out of 5 for volatility, the other 4 out of 5. The highest RTP is the same for both at 96.23%, though the hit frequency differs from 38.95% to 46.88%. Players can stake 10 c to $/€100 to get the 5x4 gaming area moving, and there are 14 paylines evaluating winning combinations left to right from the leftmost reel.Black and white 10-A card ranks are joined by colourful masks, shields, happy faces, fists, and BOOMs as the high-paying symbols. Royal 5 OAK wins pay 0.5x to 1x the bet, increasing to 1.5x to 10x the bet for lines of 5 matching premiums. Spinman is wild, substituting for any of the regular paying symbols. Five wilds in a line pay 10 times the bet.Spinman: Slot FeaturesSpinman slot - free spinsTucked away in his tights or cape or somewhere, Spinman's features are multiplying Wild Justice Reels, three bonus rounds - Power Surge, Spinfinity, and Reel Heroes, and feature buys.Justice ReelsWhen a Spinman symbol hits, it expands to form a Wild Justice Reel if the expanded symbol would be part of a winning combination. When the Justice Reel expands, it triggers a Booster Wheel, which spins to land on a multiplier or the Max Win, which is awarded instantly. Possible multipliers range from x2 to x500, which gets applied to the entire Justice Reel.Power Surge Bonus Game10 Power Surge free spins are awarded by landing 3 FS scatters in the base game. This bonus round has a greater chance of landing Spinman symbols. In all bonus rounds, players win +2 or +4 free spins when landing 2 or 3 FS scatters, respectively.Spinfinity Bonus Game10 free spins Spinfinity free spins are awarded when 4 FS scatters hit in the base game. This feature guarantees at least one Spinman symbol landing on each free spin.Reel Heroes Hidden Epic Bonus RoundTriggered by landing 5 FS scatters in the base game, players get 10 Reel Herpes Hidden Epic free spins. At least two Spinman symbols land on each spin, and the multipliers on the Booster Wheels are all a minimum of x5.Bonus BuyActivating BonusHunt Feature spins costs 3x the bet to make each spin 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game. Heroic FeatureSpins cost 50x and guarantee that at least two Spinman symbols land. Lastly, two bonus rounds may be bought - Power Surge for 90x or Spinfinity for 200x.Spinman slot - free spinsSpinman: Slot VerdictIt was hard not to shake the feeling Spinman was created as much to hit production numbers as anything else. Whilst a fine game and all, it lacked a burning white spark of Hacksaw Gaming ingenuity to make it anything really special. On the features side, Spinman relies on expanding wild symbols with multipliers that the studio just loves to stuff in its games. Prior slots that use a form of this feature are numerous in number, and by the looks of things, the list is only getting larger. The Multiplier Wheel element is somewhat different, but it's just a fancy way of generating a multiplier value. The only slight major eye-opening element was the chance of striking the max win straight from a wheel, which isn't something Hacksaw Gaming does much, although it's been seen previously in SixSixSix.The max win number itself is an attractive 10,000x the bet, so no issue with Spinman's payout potential. As always, full reel wilds with additive multiplier values are a powerful feature in any slot, and are so here. They're technically available in ascending order, from the randomness of the base game to a greater chance of getting them in the Power Surge to guaranteed to get them in the two latter bonus rounds, though full potential can be achieved in any phase. Another technique Hacksaw Gaming seems to be employing with greater regularity is the Hidden Epic Bonus that, like in Pray for Three or Le Bandit, can only be organically triggered and not bought. It adds a little something for players who prefer to grind their way through the base game on a 5 scatter hunt rather than fork out for them.And so, Spinman turned out to be an enjoyable slot, capable of blasting off with reliable features, but it wasn't the most exciting thing Hacksaw Gaming has ever produced on account of feeling like the studio cobbled it together out of old parts rather than choose to make something crazy innovative.

Title: Fortune House Power Reels
review: Fortune House Power Reels: Slot OverviewDeveloper Red Tiger crams a wide selection of Eastern imagery onto one gigantic game grid for their Asian inspired slot, Fortune House Power Reels. It's not the first time the studio has done so either, as Fortune House Power Reels shares one or two similarities to an earlier game called Dragon's Luck Power Reels – including theme and pay system. The two are far from clones, though, as Fortune House Power Reels comes with a new batch of features, including Dragon Wheel wilds, Fortune Trees, Mystery Coins, and Fortune Respins.Fortune House Power Reels has a classic Asian slot look, where a gold embroidered red carpet leads players up to the game to find a full 8-reel, 6-row grid. Red Tiger has included just about everything that proponents of the style will love, such as frogs, dragons, and elephants galore. Also dropping in are stacks of square punched coins, a bunch of gold trim, and turned up tile roofs to make Asian fans well as comfortable as possible in the surroundings. Obviously, Fortune House Power Reels won't be to everyone's tastes, but it certainly doesn't try to be something it's not. You know straight away what to expect from Fortune House Power Reels, and one look is all it takes to fall for it, or not.One of Fortune House Power Reels' main attractions is its 8,302x max win, pushing it to second place in the series when it comes to possible payouts. Big potential has been paired with a medium-high volatile math model, producing a default theoretical return to player value of 95.66%. The stake range, meanwhile, isn't overly broad, starting at 10 p/c, rising to $/€10 per spin.Another similarity Fortune House Power Reels has with Dragon Luck is its pay system. In this game, wins occur when three or more matching symbols land anywhere on one of the 30 paylines. Successful combinations can start on any reel, and more than one winning symbol type can share the same payline.Asian culture is further represented on the game's paytable, led by brushstroke fashioned 10-A card royals, worth up to 10x the bet for an eight of a kind combination. Four premium symbols follow, depicting fish, dragons, elephants, and a smiling chap holding a giant gold coin. Manage to land a full eight premium symbol payline to collect a win worth 14 to 25 times the stake. Substituting for all paying symbols is the wild. It appears on all reels, and combinations of wilds have the same value as the most lucrative pay symbol.Fortune House Power Reels: Slot FeaturesThe features in Fortune House Power Reels are provided by four special symbols that land at random anywhere on the board. These are Dragon Wheels, Fortune Trees, Mystery Wins, and Fortunes Respin tiles.The Dragon Wheel is a red, black and gold prize wheel that lands as a 2x2 Super Symbol. It activates when it lands, spinning to award either an x3, x5, x18, or x33 multiplier. It also becomes a wild symbol that substitutes for all paying symbols. The awarded multiplier is applied to all lines the wild symbol participates in.Fortune Trees are also 2x2 sized Super Symbols. When they appear on the reels, a number of wild symbols fly out of the tree to random positions on the reels. Up to 5 activations can appear from a single Fortune Tree symbol.Mystery Wins are frog embossed 2x2 sized symbols that are triggered when they land. When they do so, multiple Mystery Symbols are added to the reels, and they may activate up to 5 times to reveal a win.The last one is the Fortune Respin symbol. This 2x2 Super Symbol activates when it hits, triggering a respin with only high paying symbols on the reels for a win. It is possible to have up to 5 activations from a single Fortune Respin tile.Fortune House Power Reels: Slot VerdictIf you like the idea of Asian themed gaming on an outsized game grid, then Fortune House Power Reels is one to check out. There's an atmosphere of wealth which these slots often have, but it's also expressed in a slightly understated way. Red Tiger has gone for a traditional setting, elaborately designed, yet sort of humble too due to the wood flooring, soft lighting, candles and Joss Sticks. Despite a modicum of restraint, there is no subterfuge, and Fortune House Power Reels makes it clear from the outset whether it will be a right fit for players or not.From a non-theme standpoint, the pay anywhere wins system matches Power Reels' larger than usual space quite well. It makes better use of all those reels and rows than others in the range that only pay from the left-hand side. More than one symbol type can win from a payline, which doesn't happen often. However, it can come in handy with some of the features, Fortune Respins, for example, where only the high paying symbols land. Fortune House Power Reels is surprisingly lucrative, too, paying out wins of up to 8,302 times the stake, making it second only to Five Star Power Reels as the most potentially profitable game in the Power Reels line up to date.While there are plenty of ticks in the pro column for fans of Asian gaming, Fortune House Power Reels still comes across as another fairly generic entry in the genre. There is entertainment here if the style suits your taste, but otherwise, there's nothing about it that you haven't really seen before.

Title: Football Glory
review: Football Glory Slot: OverviewWith the World Cup mere months away, Yggdrasil is the first developer out of the gate to capitalise on football fever. No doubt others will leap on the bandwagon and release their own versions soon enough, but the first one is often the benchmark to which the others are judged. Football Glory is an okay start to the season with good and not so good points. It’s certainly not short of features, Yggdrasil has stacked the game with loads to land, trigger, and collect. And the result? Have fans found something to play during half time, or in between games perhaps? Time to blow the start whistle and put Football Glory through its paces.When locating a football-themed slot, there aren't too many places it can logically be set. Yggdrasil has plumped for the most obvious - smack bang in the middle of a raging stadium. Where else could it be really? A locker room? Let's see if later competitor slots can be a bit more imaginative. Not to worry, the setting is perfectly natural, and the grid is made up of 5 reels, 4 rows, and 25 fixed paylines. Not the most exciting setup, but let's see. Visually, it looks a bit dated and far from being Yggdrasil's most beautiful game which is a little ironic given football's motto. After lacing up, the next step is selecting the appropriate bet with a wide range from 25 p/c up to $/€125 per spin to choose from. Technically, it's powered by a medium volatile math model along with a solid 96.1% RTP setting. Nothing to complain about there.The rest of the UI consists of the usual spin/auto spin buttons, but under the reels are four intriguing meters. These are the Glory Meters which are filled when the appropriate wins occur. Winning combinations, incidentally, are formed when three or more matching symbols land consecutively from left to right. The symbols are pretty average and haven't exactly been given free rein with the theme.On the low side are four J-A royals, while the high pays are four anonymous soccer players in green, blue, red, and yellow kit. The yellow guy is the most valuable at 2.5 times the stake for five of a kind. Obviously, the game would have been a lot more enticing, and costly, if it had included actual superstars. But, that is not really the kind of slot Football Glory is. It feels more banged together with speed in mind to get out there as quickly as possible rather than a no expenses spared project. There is also a golden wild symbol that can substitute for any of the pay symbols and comes into play more during features.Football Glory Slot: FeaturesFree spins round in actionFootball Glory is not short of features. Whether you manage to see half of them is the real concern. So let's run through them. First up is the Gold and Silver Cup feature which can trigger randomly at any time no matter what game mode is active.The Silver Cup awards:During base game: 50 – 1000 coins. 7 – 21 free spins.During free spins: 50 – 1000 coins, +2-4 free spins, Wild reel, 1-2 extra wilds.The gold offers:During base game: 250 – 10,000 coins, 7-21 free spins, All Star glory Spins, Glory Boost.During free spins: +2-4 free spins, Wild reel, 2 extra wilds.The next symbol of note is the Free Spins scatter. When 3, 4, or 5 of these are in view they award 7, 14, or 21 free spins respectively. The bonus game cannot be retriggered, but extra free spins can be awarded from the Gold and Silver Cups. Now, during free spins, high pays have the chance to score goals and if successful they turn into sticky wilds. Also, before the feature begins, one of these bonuses is randomly awarded:All players have Superstar Mode activated.Start the round with 1 sticky wild in a random position.A random sticky wild reel.5 extra Silver Cups, or 5 extra Gold Cups are added to improve the chance of landing these extras.On a final note, each time a high pay combination lands, the respective meter is filled with Glory. When a Glory Meter is filled, it triggers 7 free spins with that specific player in Superstar Mode. What that means is that whenever that player symbol lands he is guaranteed to score a goal and transform into a sticky wild.Football Glory Slot: VerdictAlthough Football Glory is a clone of Yggdrasil's Vikings slot, it still manages the feat of being a total borefest which just goes to show what kind of impact the visual presentation can have on a game. We mentioned a slot that could be used as a half time diversion, but if you are shopping around for a quick fire slot, Football Glory probably won't fit the bill. It's a game that suits a long term time approach, rather than used as a quick thrill. This is due to many of the features taking their sweet time in showing up. It's a long haul slot, and filling Glory Meters can take an absolute age.If you are a player with an aversion to collecting items to trigger features, you probably won't appreciate Football Glory's glacial pace. We are talking about England managing to win the world cup again before the Glory meters are filled. Maybe twice.If Yggdrasil's first football slot for the World Cup sets the bar, it isn't a particularly high one. There is plenty of room for other developers to swoop in and dazzle fans of the beautiful game away. The most tedious aspect is the base game which is the equivalent of a dull nil-all draw between a couple of local sides. Random Cup drops help, and the features can be quite promising, provided you possess the heroic levels of patience required.Overall, Football Glory is not the most exciting slot around but might cater to recreation players who like their slots absolutely crammed with features. Yet there is no need to rush, given the year we’re in, a torrent of football-themed slots is a pretty safe bet.

Title: Super StarTurns
review: Super StarTurns: ReviewLooking for something to sink our teeth into, we accidentally stumbled upon Super StarTurns. Having tried a few spins, we quickly abandoned it and vowed never to go back ever again. Yet here we are, morbidly curious like passersby rubbernecking at the scene of an accident. So, despite the disorientating looks, as if someone just allowed a five-year-old kid to go crazy with a pack of crayons, and the extremely banal gameplay, we decided to head back for another round.Developed by Barcrest and powered by SG Digital, Super StarTurns is a 5-reel, 3-row slot with 40 paylines. With a vibrant colour palette and taking inspiration from classic television game shows, it comes with Big Bet options and bonus wheels that can deliver multiplier wins as well as free spins. You can play it for as little as 10 cents per spin and all the way up to 500 Euros if you're a high roller.The design is a confusing mess we have to say. The game window looks crowded and is literally plastered with buttons and flashing lights. It's possible that it was intentionally made to look vulgar in order to convey the feel of a tacky old game show. If that is the case, we certainly missed the joke. On the reels you will see A, K and Q royals of lower value alongside cocktail drinks, champagne bottles and wads of cash. It is the red Ferarri that is the most rewarding, however. Land a 5 of them on a full payline and you'll win 5 times your stake. The wild performs all the regular substituting actions and will give you 250 times your stake if you get 5 on a payline.Super StarTurns: FeaturesFree spinsNot a very exciting slot up to this point, but things get slightly more interesting when you trigger the Super StarTurns Bonus feature. To do just that, you will have to land 3 or more scatter symbols anywhere on the reels simultaneously. Your reward is decided by the wheel, with the following prizes on offer:Green Lucky Wheel - this is the wheel lowest in value where you can win 4 to 8 free spins or an upgrade to the next wheel.Blue Lucky Wheel - the medium value wheel, here you can win 8 to 12 free spins, cash prizes of 20 and 50 times your stake or an upgrade to the top wheel.Red Lucky Wheel - if you've arrived at the high-value wheel, there's a chance to win between 25 and 50 free spins or a cash prize of between 250 and 500 times your total stake.If you get to play the Free Spins you'll play on a different set of reels containing high-value symbols only (this means no A, K and Q royals). Furthermore, each scatter symbol appearing on reel 5 will award an additional spin.As is often the case when it comes to Barcrest, Super StarTurns gives you the opportunity to up your stakes and take it on in Big Bet Mode. There are three options available if you decide to go for it:20€ big bet - 5 spins, all scatters are double height symbols for better bonus frequency.30€ big bet - 5 spins, includes the awards of the 20€ bet plus increased awards for Super StarTurns wheel bonus.€50 big bet - 5 spins, includes the awards of the 30€ bet plus further increased awards for Super StarTurns wheel bonus.In the main game, you're up against a miserable 94% RTP. Activate the Big Bet Mode, however, and you'll benefit from an increase in RTP that reaches all the way up to 98% which is far above standard.Super StarTurns: VerdictSuper StarTurns is what we imagine a bad acid trip to be like. Not only does it look like a fun house for kids, it's also frustratingly slow and choppy to play. The count-ups are so sluggish and annoying that we literally started to wish for dead spins in order to avoid a mental breakdown. When you add the ridiculous 500x max win potential to the equation, gruelingly insipid is what comes to mind when thinking of words to summarise the game. Unless you're Monty Brewster from the 1985 American comedy film Brewster's Millions, with a mission to burn $30 million in 30 days, there is no need to even think about playing Super StarTurns.

Title: Merlin's Grimoire
review: Merlin's Grimoire: Slot OverviewMerlin, from the ever-popular Arthurian legends, has been labelled everything from wizard, prophet, and enchanter to an adviser for King Arthur. We imagine a man with such connections and wisdom to own a personal Grimoire stuffed with lore, magic, and secrets. To find out what might lurk between its pages, Play'n GO has designed Merlin's Grimoire, an online slot that uses the expanding symbol feature from the 'book of' genre, then adds splitting symbols and a ways paying system to present something outside the normal run of things.What's not unusual, and this is a good thing, is that Play'n GO has crafted a lush, overgrown world to host the Merlin-inspired experience. The game uses a 5-reel, 3-row matrix set in stone, and covered in ivy as the central play area, while about it lies a thick forest full of trees, shrooms, and the like. It's not a game which flaunts a lot of magical effects, so if you were hoping Merlin would go all Dumbledore and shoot sheets of fire from a wand, prepare to be let down. One reason why is that Merlin's Grimoire is something of a prequel, telling the story of a young Merlin taking a journey to become the most powerful wizard in the world. The visual effects are pleasing and are helped by the fact that this is far from being Play'n GO's first Merlin slot.As far as 'book of' games go, Merlin's Grimoire is a beast. It's not like a rampaging rhino sort of beast, but something more devious, as the features are more intricately developed than usual. On the back end, it runs on a highly volatile math model, spitting out a return to player value of 96.0% at the upper end. It accepts stakes of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin on any device and packs some big win numbers for Grimoire seekers to play for.To score a win, you'll need to land at least two high pays or three low pays from the left side of the grid in adjacent reels. At the default grid size, this means 243 ways to win, but when splitting symbols start to hit, ways can quickly skyrocket, maxing out at 7776 ways. For the low pays, players get six esoteric looking tokens, worth 0.8-1x the bet for five of a kind, and scrolls, potion bottles, gems, and Merlins as the highs, worth 2.5-4x the bet for five of a kind. The only other symbol is the Grimoire itself, covered next.Merlin's Grimoire: Slot FeaturesTo our knowledge, this is the fourth overtly Merlin slot from Play'n GO, the other three being Rise of Merlin, Merlin and the Ice Queen Morgana, and Lord Merlin And The Lady of the Lake. So far, all have featured expanding symbols in some way, so its stands to reason that Merlin's Grimoire does as well; plus, it has a splitting symbol feature for originality.Splitting SymbolsOn any base game spin, there is a chance 1, 2 or 3 of the middle three reels activities. When it does, any symbol landing on an active reel is split into two, increasing ways to win.Free SpinsIn Merlin's Grimoire, the Grimoire in question is used as the wild and scatter symbol. As a wild, it replaces any normal pay symbol to help link winning ways. As the scatter, landing 3, 4, or 5 of them awards 10 free spins and a payout of 0.8, 1.6 or 4 times the stake. Before free spins launch, one pay symbol is randomly selected to be the special expanding symbol. If expanding symbols can create a win, they expand to cover all positions on their reel and pay from any position – they do not have to be adjacent. Crucially, all reels in free spins can create splitting symbols when they are activated, not just the middle three. Naturally, the most optimal outcome is to land expanding symbols on all five reels when they are active. Then there'd be 7,776 ways to win.Merlin's Grimoire: Slot VerdictNolimit City might be the reigning king of splitting symbols, but Play'n GO shows that it knows a thing or two about using them as well. Till now, this has generally been in their Gems range of slots - Forge of Gems, Prism of Gems, Frozen Gems, et al., yet these were fairly elaborate compared to Merlin's Grimoire. By keeping things simple, Merlin's Grimoire has fewer moving parts to keep an eye on while still possessing everything it needs to produce spectacular results. It's not overly repetitive, due to random splitting symbols and audio-visual effects which are easy on both the senses, through triggering free spins may require a bit of patience.It's funny, we went on about Merlin's Grimoire being somewhat basic compared to its Gem forebears, but its bonus game is more complex than those found in a regular round of Book of Ra free spins. However, the core experience, the highs, lows, thrills, and spills remain the same. In fact, Merlin's Grimoire is a rather potent slot, so the emotional roller coaster ride can potentially be more viciously up and down. Strong hits are technically possible, and the game can produce wins of up to an extraordinary 30,000x the bet, which is far greater than what is usually found in a regular symbol expansion game.Merlin's Grimoire's prime attractions should have little problem pulling in 'book of' connoisseurs, as well as those with a soft spot for the Arthurian legends, for a look. It is a bit more complicated than regular 'book' slots, requiring several game elements to come together to really step up. As such, some might call it fiddly, fair enough. However, there is little doubt Merlin's Grimoire has the firepower to blow most 'book' slots out of the water on its day. On the whole, Merlin's Grimoire is a highly functioning slot that should appeal to 'book of' players looking for something original to tool around with.

Title: Odin Infinity Reels Megaways
review: Odin Infinity Reels Megaways: OverviewOdin Infinity Reels is the third slot in Australian developer ReelPlay’s Infinity Reels Series franchise. So far, all have had a fantasy/historical element to them and their latest addition continues on that tradition. This time around, players spin in the mythical world of Odin, the King of Asgard. There is nothing new about that you might be thinking. The Old Norse Gods are wheeled out regularly to theme a slot. What stands out though is ReelPlay's decision to combine the famed Megaways engine with their own in-house developed Infinity Reels.Odin Infinity Reels Megaways - base gameThe project was a little iffy there for a while. Initially, there had been a squaring up between ReelPlay and NetEnt over who invented the Infinity/InfiniReels thing first. Curious parties gathered around to witness the fracas like a schoolyard scrap. However, there were no blood noses, no pushing or shoving. The disagreement ended with a gentlemanly handshake and a civil parting of the ways. That’s good news for players, especially those on the harder edge of the spectrum. This comes up often, but if you’re doing mythology themed slots, you either go cartoon-style visuals where everyone wears a goofy grin, or you do what ReelPlay has done in Odin. You won’t find any grinning around here. This is serious business, and the tone matches the games math model.For one, volatility is rated Very High, which puts it in a completely different category to the previous Infinity Reel slots. Potential has been upsized too, which we will get to. RTP, on the other hand, is down from the other two, but still decent enough thanks to a rating of 96.18%. So, ReelPlay has wound the math model up like a tight spring while boosting just about every other aspect of the game. Part of the overhaul is of course due to the inclusion of the Megaways game engine. We are used to seeing Megaways produce big numbers, such as the oft quoted figure of 117,649 win ways.Odin Infinity Reels makes that number look pitiful, theoretically at least. Technically, since there is no limit to how many reels may be added, there is no limit to how many Megaways can come into play. Or as ReelPlay describes it: ‘Odin is the first slot in the world to offer Megaways to infinity.’ A great catchphrase, but how does it work in reality? Hitting winners remains the same - land three matching symbols on consecutive reels which, on average, occurs once in every 3.56 spins. Initially, the game uses 3 reels, meaning winning symbols are required on each of them.When a combo hits, the Infinity Reels mechanic kicks into play, adding a new reel for a chance to keep the wins rolling. If more winning symbols land, more reels are added, without limit, until no new winners appear. Also, the game has a symbol multiplier starting at x1, increasing by +1 with each added reel. Playable across all devices from 30 p/c to $/€12 per spin, Odin is undoubtedly the best looking game ever produced by ReelPlay. The step up from their previous release, Giza Infinity Reels, is quite astonishing really. Set in a dream-like mountain valley in something that almost looks like a beautiful oil painting, the designers have left no detail to chance in this stunning masterpiece.Plenty of effort has been invested into the design of the symbols as well of which there are 10 (regular) in the paytable – 6 runes, plus wolves, ravens, and an eight-legged horse. Odin is the top symbol with 3 on a payline giving you 8 times the coin value. The Valknut symbol is wild, substituting for all symbols except the scatter.Odin Infinity Reels Megaways: FeaturesAs well as the Infinity Reels driving the action, a Jackpot and a batch of free spins are up for grabs. Players win a jackpot of 888 times their bet, on top of any other wins that accrue in the process, whenever a spin results in 12 or more added reels. This might sound easy, but statistically only occurs around once in 63,323 spins.Keep an eye out for Odin’s spear, Gungnir, since any win using the symbol triggers free spins. Before free spins begin, which have a frequency of 1 in 315 spins, players are presented with two wheels. The first wheel awards 8, 10, or 12 free spins whilst the second one selects the win multiplier increment level. In level 1, 2, 3, or 4, the win multiplier increases by 1, 2, 3 or 4 respectively every time a new reel is added.Now, during the feature, players benefit from the win multiplier not resetting between spins, which can grow quite high if you get to play with an incremental win multiplier of 4. Moreover, players may extend the feature when any Gungnir symbol win occurs to pick up an extra 4 spins.Odin Infinity Reels Megaways: VerdictOdin Infinity Reels Megaways promises much with all this talk of Infinite Reels and Megaways, does it deliver? For the most part, yes. It’s definitely a more refined slot than the previous two due to the improved graphics and far superior reel-spinning animations, yet apart from that, the inclusion of Megaways does feel a little gimmicky. Now there can be different symbols on each reel, but the difference isn’t as pronounced as it often is in a Megaways reboot. The two mechanics do work well together, but Odin’s gameplay is not enormously different from what came before.The worrying part is, having reviewed three Infinity Reels slots now, there's this sensation creeping in that maybe the Infinity Reels mechanic doesn't have all that much left to give. It's far less dynamic than Megaways and at times it even feels like it obstructs the Megaways engine from doing its thing.Aside from that, the changes beneath the surface are significant. Odin Infinity is far more volatile than the previous two, while potential makes the others look like chump change. Factor in the 12 reel jackpot and max wins now top out at 20,000 times the stake now. Odin gave his eye for knowledge, and players get a glimpse of how that might feel trying to trigger free spins. Rewards are there, but it can be tough going, a little monotonous in fact while waiting for big wins or features to appear.At the end of the day, it feels like the Infinity Reels franchise is evolving. Odin is an improvement in the looks department, the theme is well done, and the potential is huge. The game can be brutal, not to mention repetitive, ideally making it better suited to patient players or harder-edged gamblers.Don't Miss...In case you haven't had enough of the Infinity Reels/Megaways combo ReelPlay has another one on offer titled Tiki Infinity Reels Megaways.

Title: Vegas Fortune
review: Vegas Fortune: Slot OverviewFew cities sell the dream of winning it big like Las Vegas does. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, and hopefully, no one gets offended, but it looks like something, say, Just For The Win might have produced, not a studio that has given us such optical delights as MonkeyPop and HippoPop. Not to worry, a lot of software providers go down the classic casino slot route, which AvatarUX has done here to give gamblers a non-nonsense, pretend you're at Vegas (or Reno or wherever), all flashing lights, blurred background, and loads of common casino items on the reels effect. Some like it, and Vegas Fortune sits in a certain visual niche, which the studio hasn't explored a lot in the past.Vegas Fortune slot - base gamePlayed on a 5x5 reelset, Vegas Fortune makes use of 3,125 ways to win, paying out when landing matching symbols on adjacent reels, starting from the leftmost side of the game board. In addition, it is possible to activate an ante bet to increase the chance of entering the bonus round at a doubling of the stake.Dazzlingly grey backgrounded 9-A card ranks are Vegas Fortune's low pay symbols, awarding 0.3 to 0.5 times the bet for a 5 OAK winning combination. Up from them on the hierarchy are cocktails, roulette wheels, cards, dice, and chips, awarding 1 to 2 times the bet for a 5-matching symbol win. Winning symbols get taken off the reels by a cascading mechanic, dropping symbols downward from above to replace them, providing the chance to achieve multiple wins off the same spin.Vegas Fortune: Slot FeaturesVegas Fortune slot - free spinsOn the features side of Vegas Fortune, the slot has Infinity Stacks, Giant Stacks, random multipliers, synced reels, free spins, and three bonus buy options from the Xpress.Infinity Stacks & Giant StacksWhen a stack of 3 or more matching symbols appears, they merge and move downwards to form a single symbol, generating a multiplier for each. A stack of 2 matching symbols at the top or bottom nudges the reels for a chance to create an Infinity Stack. If the adjacent symbols match, they merge and generate a multiplier like an Infinity Stack. If they don't match, they go back to their original position.Random MultipliersA random multiplier of x2 or higher may spawn and merge with matching symbols, increasing the multiplier.Synced ReelsWhen 2 or more adjacent reels are highlighted, all symbols on those reels will match. The more adjacent reels, the higher the probability of triggering winning opportunities.Free SpinsHitting 3, 4, or 5 scatters triggers 5, 10, or 15 free spins, respectfully. During the free spins bonus round, players can experience synced reels and a global multiplier that increases with each spin. Unused multipliers on the reels remain on the grid in free spins until used in a win.XpressAt the Xpress, users may buy 5 free spins for 40x, 10 free spins for 100x, or 15 free spins with synced reels on every spin for 400 times their bet.Vegas Fortune slot - free spinsVegas Fortune: Slot VerdictAvatarUX really has really become the studio you don't know what to expect next. Where once the team released a steady stream of PopWins slots, they've really diversified as of late, and Vegas Fortune is another slot which hard forks away from the sort of popping antics the developer made its mark with. In saying that, some of Vegas Fortune's components might be traced back to AvatarUX's earlier work, such as the cascading mechanic on a ways to win game board, that can be expanded (in a way, by merging symbols) when certain features are present and firing. This is a very broad, generalised way of looking at Vegas Fortune, though, and it's not till drilling down on the details that the game manages to stand out.Its main standout feature is surely the Infinity Stacks, and not a bad concept it is either. The Giant Stack feature adds extra anticipation, as well, since when it nudges favourably, it will form an Infinity Stack to keep the ball rolling. On a productive roll, complimented by cascading hits, the overall repeat win effect isn't a million miles away from a PopWins trip, possibly helping Vegas Fortune appeal to fans of AvatarUX's back catalogue.The game's theme might be a dividing factor, though, as the fairly plain casino imagery is hardly big news in an online slot. But, classically presented slots have an enduring allure in their own right for some, so when adding in a 10,000x win cap with one or two interesting feature ideas, you can see how Vegas Fortune could appeal to the right gambler.

Title: Anderthals
review: Anderthals (Just For The Win): OverviewNo one ever questioned Swedish developer Just For The Win's knack for designing pretty games, and from what it seems, their target audience (soccer moms?) seem to like what they're being served. Beneath the hood, on the other hand, things have not been quite as interesting given the fact that we've been fed what feels almost like a recycled mathematical model - and a rather awful one too. Looking at the specs of their latest release, we hold little hope that things have changed. But we'll see about that.This time we go way back in time to meet lovable couple Andy and Annie Anderthal. These two club-wielding, animal skin wearing troglodytes are the stars of JFTW’s latest slot Anderthals. They’re the friendly type who keep dinosaurs as pets, and eat massive portions of dino ribs by the campfire. Yes, it's all a bit Flintstones-ish. If anything, the game world is even more primitive than Fred’s was – feet powered cars are yet to be invented. The two Anderthals, and the slot in general, might appear cute, but they’re amiable antics bely another highly volatile slot from Just For The Win with not so great rewards for the risky undertaking. It’s good to see the developer turning up the heat in that regard; it’s just a shame that the rest of the slot is way way back playing catch up.Obviously, Anderthals is a cleverly shortened version of the word Neanderthals. Those ‘cavemen’ that existed alongside early humans for generations, potentially interbreeding and preserving some of their DNA down to modern times. What that means for players, is a game set in prehistoric times, populated with plenty of volcanoes and dinosaurs. We all know dinosaurs never actually existed alongside humans, but a bit of creative license never hurt anyone.As usual, Just for the Win has crafted a good looking slot with a cartoon, dreamy look to it reminiscent of the move The Good Dinosaur. The action takes place on a grid that uses 5 reels, 4 rows and 40 fixed paylines. As mentioned, a highly volatile math model runs the show and produces an RTP of 96.12%. The game has been extensively tested to produce those results, more on that in the verdict.Players are able to head back in time by first choosing a bet from 10 p/c up to $/€100 per spin. The key aim of the game is to land combinations of 3 or more matching symbols on a payline for a win. The regular pay symbols on the table include stone cut royals (J-A) roughly hewn into shape, and three premiums. These premiums include Andy, Annie, and the logo which is worth 32 times the stake for five of a kind. Rounding off the regular symbols is the wild which can substitute for any pay symbol. It usually lands in 1x1 tile size but can be expanded via certain features.Anderthals (Just For The Win): FeaturesFeature in actionAnderthals benefits from several random features as well as a round of free spins. Just above the reels is a horizontal line of 5 spaces that reveal different features/enhancers on every spin. These are called Feature Spots, and each one corresponds to the reel below it. The burning torch is called the Feature Symbol, and if two or more land on a spin, they activate the Feature Spots above them. There are several different Feature Spots with these individual benefits:1x Bet or 2x Bet– when the spin is complete a 1x or 2x the bet prize is awarded respectively.Expanding Wilds – any wilds that land beneath these active Feature Spots will expand to cover the whole reel.Extra Wilds – additional wild symbols are added to the reel beneath this active Feature Spot.Wild x2 or Wild x3 – turns any wild symbols on active reels into x2 or x3 Wild Multipliers. Wild x2 and Wild x3 cannot occur on the same spin.Respins – during the base game, this activates a feature spot with Expanding wilds, Wild x2, Wild x3. The respin cannot activate new features, and only one respin can be awarded per spin.Free spins – triggers the free spins bonus round.If one Free Spins spot is activated it awards 8 free spins, and every additional activated free spin spot awards 2 more to the round. During free spins, all feature spots that were active when the bonus round was triggered remain active for the full duration.Anderthals (Just For The Win): VerdictJust like their previous release Treasure Skyland, Just for the Win has once again surprised by dialling up the variance. It’s a pity they couldn’t have dialled up the rest of the game to go with it. Now, for low-rollers, things are actually not all that bad as the setup allows for wins of over 11,000 times the stake when playing at the default 0.10 bet. For highrollers, meanwhile, the game is not equally rewarding as the game is capped at 2,219 times the stake at max bet.To hit either of those numbers is, of course, highly unlikely in any case when you consider it was achieved during 110 billion simulated spins. In other words, don’t hold your breath; the next ice age is more likely to arrive before a big payday. Knowing that, any appeal that Anderthals had quickly disappears faster than the dinosaurs did on impact day.Still, Just for the Win make pretty games, and they know their audience. They will be banking on players drawn to Anderthals from both European and Asian markets. That aim is evidenced by the alternative Chinese Logo symbol on different game versions. What might win certain punters over is a cuteness that draws the eye and a couple of mechanics to keep them spinning. One is the relatively steady hit rate of around 1 in 5 spins. The second is that two scatters will theoretically land once every 25 spins on average. Each time they do Feature Spots become active. The issue is that the modifiers aren’t all that special, and unlikely to make huge impacts on a session.All up, Anderthals is another looker from Just for the Win which is more flash than substance. Yet, with a ton of features and fairly regular hit rate, it has all the right ingredients to rock their target market. Otherwise, unless you are completely enamoured with the thought of dinosaur and human cohabitation, there is no reason to seek out Anderthals to play.

Title: Survivor Megaways
review: Survivor Megaways Slot: OverviewThat tribal chanting you might be hearing on the slot grapevine isn't announcing a new season of Survivor on the telly. Thanks to Aussie developers Big Time Gaming, the hit TV show is making an appearance directly on the reels. Usually, it's BTG issuing licences for fellow developers, but this time they've obtained one for their latest release from Banijay Group - a French production company that recently signed a multi-season deal to extend the life of reality show Survivor for a few more years. Now slots players get the Megaways powered version to keep them busy on dry land. So what have the Big Time Gaming wizards cooked up this time? That makes Survivor a less intimidating prospect than previous BTG slots such as Lil Devil, and likely putting it more in a similar bracket to Bonanza.Survivor Megaways Slot: FeaturesThe features available in Survivor Megaways include a mixture of progressive wild multipliers and free spins. Right next to the reels are the two tribal leaders – red and blue. Each one starts with a default win multiplier of x1. Whenever a red urn symbol lands it increases the red leader's multiplier by x1 to x3. The same occurs to the blue leader's multiplier when the blue urn symbol lands. When more than one multiplier is in view they multiply each other's values and get reset back to their original value of x1 following a losing spin.The one time the wild multipliers do not reset is when Free Spins are triggered. Any multipliers accrued on the triggering base game spin have their values carried over to the free spins. To trigger it, players are required to land 3 logo scatters in view simultaneously. Each additional logo scatters adds another 5 spins to the starting total. During the bonus game, the tribal leaders do not reset their multiplier until the feature has completed. It's also possible to extend the life of the feature by landing 3 or more scatters to receive 5+ free spins.Survivor Megaways Slot: VerdictSurvivor Megaways is another solid release from the talented group at Big Time Gaming. For starters, the game is a looker, with animations that are as seamless as its features. Things are no less enjoyable on the aural front either with a tremendously powerful tune thundering through the bonus game. It's like the soundtrack accompanying the end of season contestant highlight reels. Stirring stuff indeed.Now, Survivor Megaways is not the most innovative of slots to come out of the BTG production line, but it's undoubtedly one of the more easy going, mainstream titles we've seen in a while. Players turned off by, or left feeling brutalised by the chase mechanics found in Lil Devil, or Royal Mint, can enjoy a more straight forward slot experience.For fans, if you were going to compare Survivor Megaways to a contestant, then Malcolm Freberg wouldn't be far off the mark. Malcolm was a repeat contender and firm island favourite who consistently did well but didn't quite have the goods to go all the way to nab the million. Yet, while Survivor Megaways might not revolutionize the industry, it nevertheless conjures up entertaining gaming - not to mention lucrative. At full power, players have the chance to win up to 44,000 times their stake.Survivor Megaways highlights a fundamental area where BTG truly excels. That is, to come up with a machinery so perfectly fined-tuned and well-balanced that it can make any player walk away feeling like some good value gameplay has been achieved in spite of busting out.Nevertheless, the volatility is quite high which means you should be prepared for plenty of low paying bonuses although the bonus game does have the ability to heat up quickly. For example, a 5x total multiplier can instantly turn to 10x if, let's say, the blue tribe multiplier sits at 5x whilst the red receives a 1x boost. Sure, you will need to land both wild mutipliers in view for them to come into effect, but still.At the end of the day, it's kudos to the team for creating something fresh and new with Survivor Megaways. In typical Big Time Gaming fashion, the build quality is exceptional, the thought and care that went into it are evident, and enough potential has been piled on to satisfy most players. The tribe has spoken.

Title: Pyramyth
review: Pyramyth: Slot OverviewThunderkick is a creative bunch, no arguments there. They've come up with subjects as diverse as pink elephants, vampires, and all manner of mythical beasts to give their games colour. Pyramyth is another mythologically inspired game, yet instead of packing your archaeology kit to head back in time, the game goes in the opposite direction – the future. Futuristic Ancient Egypt might sound odd, but it works well, counterbalancing the features and format, which are more traditional. Here you'll come across wild multiplier symbols and sticky respins in a free spins bonus game.Played using 5 reels and 15 fixed paylines, as you might have gathered from the game's name, this is Ancient Egypt of the future. It's as if the civilisation hadn't petered out but powered on into the 21st century and beyond. Modern-day Cairo, as represented in the game, looks like one of those uber-modern Emirati cities full of towering high rise buildings that glint in the Gulf sun. In Pyramyth, it's not hard to imagine a benign species coming down to help advance the civilisation, like an episode of Stargate SG1.Pyramyth is playable on desktop, mobile, or tablets, providing stakes from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. The game is highly volatile, generating a theoretical return value of 96.17%. To score wins, players need to hit three or more matching symbols from the left side of the grid while having several features in the base and bonus game to boost winning potential.Asf or the paytable, Thunderkick has split it into three segments – lows, mids and high-value symbols. Low pays are 9-A card tiles, while mids are Egyptian style hounds, crocodiles, and eagles. The lone high paying symbol is a high priestess, who fires off a win worth 75 times the stake if a full line of her lands across the grid. Wilds play a more central role in Pyramyth than usual so let's cover them next.Pyramyth: Slot FeaturesPyramyth - free spins with roaming wild in actionScarab beetles were important in Ancient Egyptian culture, associated as they were with the sun god Ra, and are pretty important in Pyramyth as well. In the game, scarabs are depicted on the wild symbols, which appear on every reel, substituting all other symbols except the scatter. In addition, wins including a wild symbol apply a multiplier based on the number of wilds on the pay line. Having 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 wilds in a pay line grants a multiplier of x2, x4, x8, x16, or x32.The other critical symbols in Pyramyth are the sun scatters, also appearing on any reel. When at least 3 are in view in the base game, free spins are triggered. The number awarded is 10, 15, or 20 free spins when 3, 4, or 5 scatters are in view. During free spins, every pay line win activates a sticky respin feature. Here, winning symbols are locked in place while all others respin. If new winners land, they are locked too, and respins continue – ending when no additional winning symbols land or if all positions on the reels are locked.As well as respins, free spins also do fun things with wilds. When wild symbols land in the bonus round, they become Roaming Wilds that stay on the reels for the remainder of the round. Keep in mind that wilds on pay lines multiply wins as they do in the base game. Before each new spin, all Roaming Wilds shift to another position on the game grid. This applies to sticky respins as well, so before each respin, wilds move to a new unlocked position unless they are included in a win. In the bonus game, it is possible to have up to 5 awarded wilds roaming around. Lastly, should a total of 3 scatters symbols land on a free spin, including a sticky respin sequence, +5 additional free spins are awarded.Pyramyth: Slot VerdictMuch like Thunderkick's Beat the Beast range, Pyramyth is a slot that doesn't try to go against the grain but gets on with the job of delivering straightforward gaming, which is uncomplicated yet effective. It also looks a lot like the Beat the Beast series as well due to a similar graphic quality to its reels and background imagery. Speaking of imagery, setting Ancient Egypt in the future is a pretty cool idea which makes you wonder – what would the world be like if the mysticism of Ancient Egypt had carried on down to the present day to be blended with science and technology?The features aren't quite as original as the theme. It's not to say they are bad in any way, though, all being proven performers that crop up repeatedly, for good reason. Wild multipliers always go down a treat and help keep the base game interesting, for one. When free spins trigger, players not only get sticky respins to build wins, there's the added bonus of having up to five roaming wilds helping to connect more symbols. It's not a feature combo you really see, and when wound up, the system can work to excellent effect as well. When Pyramyth is firing the game can produce wins of up to 10,000 times the stake. It's probably capable of doing more than this, but the 10k is a win cap Thunderkick has whacked on, and game rounds terminate when hitting this level.When we've received a Thunderkick game recently, it's typically gone in one of two directions. Title: Vikings Unleashed Reloaded

Title: Ice And Fire
review: Ice and Fire (Dreamtech Gaming): OverviewIce and Fire is a fantasy slot powered by Yggdrasil Gaming and the first ever title from Dreamtech Gaming to be released on the Yggdrasil platform. During this round, additional wilds are added, but even better is the introduction of the Win Multiplier. This starts at x1 and increases by +1 after every cascade. Title: Temujin Treasures

Title: Outlaws Inc

Since the multiplier is persistent at these times, it continues to grow until you blast a regular line win with it. Or not, because if no Gorilla lands, it will go unused. Not all the time, of course. This is Hacksaw, and they are well versed in mixing tease with potential rewards. As to rewards, Outlaws Inc can reach 10,000x the bet, and there is very little doubt it is capable of hitting this amount with a monstrous Global Multiplier burning a hole on the screen.All in all, Outlaws Inc had its hair-raising moments, and its multiplicative powers can be a thrill, but it was overshadowed by the more engaging stuff Hacksaw Gaming has been doing of late.

Title: Power of Thor Megaways
review: Power of Thor Megaways: Slot OverviewDeveloper Pragmatic Play takes on one of the hardest-hitting characters from mythology, the mighty deity Thor, in their game Power of Thor Megaways. As well as being the god of thunder and the sky, Thor was also the god of agriculture. Set in a glorious Midgardian landscape, all majestic mountains and rugged valleys, players get a pretty sweet tract of land to try their luck in. From the moment the home screen loads, you get a good idea of what Power of Thor Megaways is all about. This is no-nonsense mythology, where you keep up with the gods or get left behind. For players after something serious with a bit of passion, Power of Thor Megaways could be ideal.Once the 6-reel Megaways grid hits, the nods to other slots become apparent. Firstly, the mohawked character symbols bring to mind Vikings Unleashed Megaways, which is one of Power of Thor’s direct competitors. However, Pragmatic Play’s game has even less good-natured humour about it than Blueprint Gaming’s did. Power of Thor Megaways’ business attitude is accentuated by a dramatic soundtrack that gets even more punishing during free spins.Getting amongst the Vikings is possible on any device where bets from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin may be set. Volatility is high, rated 5 out of 5, though the 5,000x potential is somewhat on the modest side. There are no major issues with the max win, but it’s not quite as exciting as you might expect from this setup.Power of Thor Megaways uses 10 regular symbols which pay left to right on adjacent reels, starting from the leftmost reel. Card symbols 9-A lead off the paytable and make up the bulk of the winning combinations. After them, we get 4 Viking warriors making up the high pay character symbols - a lady in a horned helm, a couple of craggy gents, then Thor as the highest value symbol. A line of 6 Thors will get you 20 times your stake, while 6 of the other three vary from 2 to 5 times your bet.Wilds appear in the game in one of two ways. The least exciting way is the regular 1x1 version that appears only on the upper horizontal reel. In both cases, wilds replace regular pay symbols to complete a win. The second wild, let’s look at below.Power of Thor Megaways: Slot FeaturesAs is standard for most Megaways slots, when a win lands on the board, it is removed via the tumble feature, which then drops new or existing symbols into the gaps. This can lead to consecutive wins, and tumbles keep tumbling until no new wins appear.Thor’s hammer, Mjolnir, appears only on the horizontal reel, taking up 2 positions. Whenever it lands fully in view, whether on an initial spin or by a tumble, all positions below it turn wild, randomly adding between 2-6 wilds per reel in a sort of xNudge fashion. The created wilds on the main reels are removed if part of a win, but the original hammer symbol does not. This means The Hammer Feature can trigger again if the hammer symbol changes position after a tumble.Triggering free spins (frequency 1/510 spins) require players to land 4 or more scatter symbols land in view to spell T, H, O, R which awards 10 free spins. Up to 9 scatters may land, each additional one adding +4 free spins to the pot.Before the round starts, if 10 to 18 free spins were won, players can gamble them on an Extra Chilli type wheel to win more or collect. If you gamble, the wheel spins, landing on either a green winning segment or a blank losing one. Losing means all free spins are lost, and you move back to the base game. Winning adds +4 more free spins, up to 22, then the round launches. In free spins, a win multiplier enters the game, increasing by +1 after each tumble. The Hammer feature remains in the game, as do scatter symbols, adding +4 free spins if 3 scatter symbols hit.The second way of entering free spins is by buying them if the option is available. Doing so costs 100x the bet and gets you enough scatters to win 10 to 22 free spins on the next spin. You can gamble free spins as well, following the rules laid out above.Power of Thor Megaways: Slot VerdictPragmatic Play might have borrowed a few ideas from elsewhere, but they’ve wrapped them in such an entertaining bundle they stop registering after a while. Power of Thor Megaways also has a similar spirit to Yggdrasil’s Hades Gigablox, being a serious mythological number so passionate about what it does it’s hard not to get caught up in the whole shebang.Punchy graphics drag you kicking into Power of Thor Megaways’ game world, and from there, the pace doesn’t let up. What also helps is the way Pragmatic Play has added nice little touches throughout, such as the way symbols animate when they are removed during a tumble. A small addition, yet each thing adds up to a polished experience, perfect for some mythological gaming.The Hammer feature is a good one, too, leading to some tidy repeat wins when it shifts positions in a tumble sequence. Of course, creating extra wilds instead of multipliers doesn't have quite the same impact, though it is useful nonetheless and goes hand in hand with a win multiplier in free spins. Potential isn’t quite as high as you might expect from this sort of game - through no fault of its own, it should be added. If the game achieves 5,000x during free spins (hit frequency approx 1 in 860,000), the round ends, and all remaining free spins are forfeited.For a good, wholesome Norse-inspired slot, it’s hard to fault Power of Thor Megaways. You could say it’s a bit of mish-mash of other ideas, but it’s also easy to see past that to enjoy some well-executed Thor gaming. All in all, Power of Thor Megaways comes across as one of the more exciting Megaways offerings we've seen in quite some time, blowing new life into this particular category of slots.

Title: Danny Dollar
review: Danny Dollar: Slot OverviewAround mid-2024, the gambling world was introduced, courtesy of developer Hacksaw Gaming, to Donny Dough, a fun-loving kind of guy with literal dollar signs in his eyes. Apparently, Donny was only one half of the Cash Kings, and you're about to meet his brother, Danny Dollar. Staring in a slot of the same name, Danny might share some commonalities with his brother, but features aren't exactly one of them. We're not heading into entirely brand new territory, though, as Danny Dollar pulls in one or two ideas from previous Hacksaw Gaming slots as it drops expanded wilds with multipliers, Nudge symbols, and a couple of bonus rounds into players' lap for their approval, or dismissal.It appears that Danny shares the same love of the limelight as his sibling Donny. This guy also sports dollar sign eyes and looks like some sort of money-motivated ringmaster or MC at a show as he bobs around beside a gaming grid in a heavily curtained stage-like environment. The artwork possesses a vaguely Cuphead, 1930s animated cartoon look, and the whole show exudes slapstick sass. While the two games clearly look related, similarities are in some ways only skin deep, for Danny Dollar delivers a different kind of gaming experience.Danny Dollar slot - base gameDanny Dollar's 5x5 reelset comes equipped with 19 paylines for evaluating winning combinations from the leftmost side across adjacent reels. Rated 4 out of 5, or medium-high, Danny Dollar is a more volatile slot than its bro, though the RTP is slightly lower at 96.21% at its highest return configuration. When choosing a bet, the stake range is 10 c to $/€100 per spin, as it usually is in a Hacksaw Gaming slot.Shiney 10 through Ace card ranks are joined by coins, coins and notes, hats of dough, drums of dough, and giant gems on Danny Dollar's hierarchy of pay symbols. Royal 5 OAK wins pay 2 times the bet no matter the type, and a line of 5 matching premiums pays 5 to 10 times the bet. Wilds are present on all reels. They substitute all paying symbols and award 10x when 5 of them land in a line.Danny Dollar: Slot FeaturesDanny Dollar slot - Dollar Dash featureFor features, Danny Dollar rolls our Dollar-Reels, Nudge symbols, a Dollar Dash bonus, a No Bills, No Thrills bonus, and feature buys.Dollar-ReelsWhen a Danny symbol hits, it expands into a Wild Dollar-Reel - if the expanded wild would be part of a win. Danny symbols only expand upwards to the top of the reels, and those that do not expand count as a single wild symbol. Only one Danny symbol may land on a reel at a time, and if a Dollar-Reel expands through a wild symbol, a multiplier is applied to the entire Dollar-Reel of x2 to x200 in value.Nudge SymbolAny Nudge symbols on the reels activate after all Dollar-Reels have expanded. After activating, they nudge all Dollar-Reels on the grid downwards by one row.Dollar Dash Bonus GameLanding 3 FS scatters in the base game triggers 10 free Dollar Dash spins. This feature is played using Reel Indicators, which are markers on each reel displaying the position where a Danny symbol last landed and activated. Any new Danny symbol on the same reel cannot land higher than the marked position. If a new Danny symbol lands below the marker, the marker moves to the new position. In both bonus rounds, landing 2 or 3 FS scatters awards +2 or +4 free spins.No Bills, No Thrills Bonus GameLanding 4 FS scatters in the base game triggers 10 free No Bills, No Thrills spins. This feature also has the same mechanics as the base game with the addition of a Progressive Global Multiplier. All Dollar-Reel Multipliers are stored in a Progressive Global Multiplier that is always active and applies to all wins.Feature BuysDanny Dollar provides four feature buys. They are BonusHunt FeatureSpins for 3x the bet, where each spin is 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game and Danny FeatureSpins for 50x that guarantee at least 3 Danny symbols land on each spin. Buying the Dollar Dash costs 100x, while No Bills, No Thrills has a price tag of 300x.Danny Dollar slot - No Bills, No Thrills featureDanny Dollar: Slot VerdictSo, Danny or Donny? Interestingly, despite sharing visual similarities and familial blood, they're not exactly two sides of the same coin, or dollar bill, as it were. The first surprise was to see LootLines/Multi-Dough symbols left out of the game. Like, they're totally absent. Not that Danny had to bring them back or anything, but shunning them entirely was not expected. What was less of a shock was to see Danny symbols expanding to the top of the reel, producing multiplier values if they passed through a wild symbol on the way. Amongst other things, this effect brought to mind Fist of Destruction, which triggers a very similar, if not bang on the same sort of action.No major complaints about the feature, though. Expanded wilds with a multiplier of up to x200 on them are nothing to sniff at. Danny Dollar improves on the idea, too, by tossing Nudge symbols on the reels, improving the reach of expanded Dollar-Reels by dropping them down a row. Simple but clever. The Dollar Dash bonus game mutates off this idea with the introduction of the Reel Indicator markers. Charming, but No Bills, No Thrills is where players really want to be due to the Global Win Multiplier. Again, this is not the most original idea Hacksaw Gaming ever had, but it is effective nonetheless. Its possible potency is reflected in the significant cost difference between the two bonus buys.The final potential deal maker or breaker is, drum roll, a max win of 12,500x, which is 25% greater than the figure slapped on Donny Dough. Once the stars or dollar signs or whatever have cleared from the eyes, Danny Dollar is a well-made slot, not as uniquely innovative as its brother, perhaps, but a chunky double cheeseburger and fries type game that's easy to enjoy if a little on the mass production line side, mechanically speaking.

Title: Running Sushi
review: Running Sushi: Slot OverviewWhen you're out and crave food that is quick, easy, tasty, fairly exotic, and potentially nutritious, it's hard to sleep on sushi as the primary option. This neatly packaged cuisine is hugely popular around the globe, and while sushi is strongly associated with Japan, others have said it originated elsewhere. Food origins can be a hotly contested topic, so let's not get into that. Instead, let's bust out the mental chopsticks and dissect Pragmatic Play's food-themed online slot, Running Sushi.For non-traditionalists, it is relaxing to take on an Asian slot which doesn't try to ram dragons and koi into every orifice. Those slots have their place, acknowledged, but the quiet harmony Running Sushi delivers to your eyes is appreciated. This game isn't held in any casual corner sushi joint, either. Its tasteful wooden decor hints at an upmarket establishment in the base game before getting all dancey karaoke for the free spins round.Running Sushi slot - base gameThis reservedly cheerful game is played on a 5-reel, 4-row matrix, putting on 1,024 ways to win. Winning combinations begin on the leftmost reel, and matching symbols must land on adjacent reels to form a combo. Betting choices consist of picking a stake of 20 c to $/€240 per spin, whether or not to use the ante bet, and if the feature buy is a better option. It's a fast way to get into free spins, at least. The ante bet ups the stake by 25% to double the chance of getting free spins. However you play Running Sushi, its highest RTP is 96%, while the volatility is high.Diamonds, clubs, hearts, and spades are joined by avocado, rice, meat, a shrimp, soy sauce, and more sauce as Running Sushi's pay symbols. Card suits pay 0.75-1.5 times the stake for a 5 OAK winning combination; the rest are worth 1.75 to 7.5 times the bet for 5. Wild coin symbols are present only in free spins on the middle three reels. Wilds substitute for anything except scatters, Take Sushi, and Take All symbols.Running Sushi: Slot FeaturesRunning Sushi slot - free spinsCollecting money is what Running Sushi is all about. This is possible through the Take Sushi feature, available in both phases of the game, and a meter collection dynamic in free spins.Take Sushi FeatureUnder the reels, on every spin, 1 to 10 Money symbols appear as if rolling along a conveyor belt. Hitting 3 scatter symbols awards 10 free spins. During free spins, the values of all Money symbols that appear are collected in a meter. A special Take All symbol exists in free spins on the middle three reels. When 3 Take All symbols hit, they collect the current value of the meter, including the values of Money symbols that landed on the spin. After this, the meter resets to zero.Buy Free SpinsThe free spins round can be instantly triggered from the base game by buying it for 85x the bet. Buy free spins and the RTP remains the same.Running Sushi slot - free spinsRunning Sushi: Slot VerdictFor all its deliciousness, sushi has become a pretty commonplace food choice, and Running Sushi is also a commonplace game. Interestingly, in certain ways, it was relaxing to play; in others, it was a real pain in the keister. Actually, this judgement can be broadly split down further. The base game was okay, but the free spins round could be torturous. What's funny is that it was the extra features added to the free spins round that made it so. This is the Take All symbol and the collection meter combo. Collecting money in the meter was no trouble. Racking up 100s of times the bet took no effort at all. Winning it by landing the required Take All symbols, hmm, that was the challenge.Some may enjoy the challenge. Some may find bonus rounds floating by like sushi on a conveyor belt, not awarding decent wins from the collection meter a kick in the nattsu. For the review, it got tiring staring at sizable prize pots gathering dust in the meter, never getting won. Then, play moves back to the wood-panelled base game to chill out and try over again. On the other side of the coin, managing to win a big chunk of change from the meter would probably trigger a wee thrill. Running Sushi doesn't go large, though, despite a possible 2,500x hit from a single Money symbol, the game is kept in check by a 3,000x win cap.If Running Sushi was real sushi, it felt akin to those heavy mayo or cream cheese variations with stodgy rice from the supermarket that some might not even consider to be 'real' sushi. Running Sushi goes through the motions and looks pleasant but fails to fully satisfy.

Title: Red Hot Riches
review: Red Hot Riches: Slot OverviewIf you're going to be chasing 'riches', it might as well be of the red-hot kind, right? Collecting 5 Upsizer Max Coins triggers free spins at the maximum Upsizer level.Upsizer BuyBefore free spins begin, players are able to purchase higher Upsizer modifiers. In free spins, each Roll increases the win multiplier by +1, and the multiplier does not reset until the round ends. The maximum multiplier is x10, x20, or x50, depending on the Upsizer level. Title: Gods of Death
review: Gods of Death: OverviewWith a name like Gods of Death, Novomatic owned studio Stakelogic makes no illusions about where it plans to lead players. Those into dark tourism - visiting places like Chernobyl or Pompeii will appreciate the approach since we are taking a shadier route back to Ancient Egypt this time around. Gods of Death has a look reminiscent of older Egyptian slots due to the classic 5-reel, 10-payline setup, but comes across as more of an R rated version.Seriously, the characters that greet players have a Lovecraftian appearance which some might find slightly sinister. Graphically, the effect is striking and conjures up memories of that chamber Indiana Jones is pushed into full of serpents and giant statues. Add in the rhythmical soundtrack and the mood is well set before the spin button has even be pressed.Also before hitting spin, bets need to be set which is a little more complicated than usual. What makes bet choice a little trickier is Stakelogic's' new Super Stake feature, which is optional and doubles the cost when activated.
