Let's crack open the paytable like a dusty old sarcophagus and see what lies within. On the low side, Gods of Death is decked out with 10-A golden royals that have been embossed with various colours that give them a faded glory look. The premiums, meanwhile, are some of the most terrifying characters seen in a slot. They start with a Pharaoh Mummy, followed by Sobek, Ra, and Anubis - all glowing-eyed and looking like a robber has just looted their tomb or temple. Values are quite high across the board, with Anubis the most prized at 100 times the stake for five of a kind.Stakelogic has stuck to rather conventional core rules, with 10 paylines stabbing across the grid where winning combinations of at least three of a kind can line up. This mechanic is backed up with an RTP right on average at 96.0%, along with medium+ volatility rated at 4/5. The base game might sound relatively simple, but a lengthy list of features add intrigue and depth to the game.Gods of Death: FeaturesGods of Death - free spins round with walking stacked wild in playGods of Death may initially draw your mind to classic Egyptian slots like Book of Ra Deluxe and Book of Dead, but actually has very few things in common with those. Unlike said games, Gods of Death is packed with base game features. Aside from Super Stake option that we've already covered, there are a bunch of modifier extras as well.Racing across the desert is the Tornado feature which can appear on any non-winning spin in the base game. When activated, one of the reels is selected and copied onto one or more of the other reels to provide extra chances of scoring a winner or two.The Snake Queen symbol is wild and can substitute for any of the regular pay symbols. When it lands on the third reel, it expands to cover the full reel and awards 3 respins. It then moves down one position with each respin until it finally drops off the reel. Lines of Snake Queen symbols also payout, with 2, 3, 4, or 5 of a kind worth 1x, 10x, 40x, and 200 times the stake respectively.Next is one of the most desirable symbols in the game – the Pharaoh scatter. Two or more of these symbols trigger a payout, but more importantly 3, 4, or 5 award 10, 20, or 50 Free Spins respectively.During free spins, the wild Mummy symbol comes into play. When this symbol lands, it expands to cover the full reel and can substitute for anything except the scatter. It remains on the grid and after each spin it moves one position to the left until it falls off the first reel. The Mummy symbol can appear on any reel and more than one can be active at once. Finally, scatters remain in the bonus game and 2, 3, 4, or 5 of them in view bestow an extra 2, 10, 20, or 50 free spins respectively.It wouldn't be Stakelogic without a gamble feature which players can participate in after a win. This is a typical blind card guessing game where the correct suit pays 4x the win, or the correct colour pays 2x the win.Gods of Death: VerdictGods of Death turned out to be quite a pleasant surprise. Despite the high number of slots in the Egyptian category, Stakelogic has created a game that manages to stand out from the bunch. It does this by taking a slightly different approach to the theme and by incorporating a bunch of useful features. In regards to the look, okay it's more Mummy Returns than a horror, but it is a refreshingly darker tone than usual.It gets a little weird during free spins when the background serpents start pouring blood or lava, but it doesn't get too over the top. Having several wilds that appear at different stages with unique modifiers is also a nice touch which keeps things fresh.As to Stakelogic's new feature, the Super Stake can feel a little underwhelming at first, but it turned out to be quite beneficial in the long run. The first time it appeared, +363 Ra symbols were added to the spin resulting in the first four reels stacked and a handy 100x win. Another time the Super Stake added 99 scatters which ended up triggering free spins along with a decent win on top. The Super Stake feature kicks in around 1 in 43 spins and may not always work in your favour, but it is more interesting than the standard gamble feature.If there is one thing explorers want to see when prising open a tomb is the glitter of gold. When it comes to rewards, Gods of Death doesn't disappoint either with potential returns of up to 11,800 times the stake. Keep in mind though that there are caps of $472,000, or $236,000 depending on the operator's settings.Overall, Gods of Death is a well-crafted game and one of Stakelogic's better releases. The look is a good one, a little different, and the features are well designed and relatively new when taken together. It might not be quite as volatile as some would prefer, but on the whole, Gods of Death brings the right elements together to provide some satisfying gaming.

Title: Finn's Golden Tavern
review: Finn’s Golden Tavern (NetEnt): OverviewFinn's Golden Tavern sees the return of NetEnt's cheerful flute-playing leprechaun Finn who we first got to meet in the 2017 title Finn and the Swirly Spin. Although it failed to charm the cork-sniffers, it did fare much better with the recreational players much thanks to its gentle volatility, happy visuals, and the use of a unique, never before seen, spiral spin mechanic. In our case, we lost interest almost instantly as we found the mechanic to be somewhat annoying, frustrating and the payouts too weak. But with its cutesy Nintendo-inspired visuals, it's likely to speak to a demographic that grew up playing Super Mario World, Kirby, and whatnot.As will instantly become apparent to anyone that's ever played the original, the sequel builds on the same concept. The action still takes place on a 5-reel, 5-row layout, the spiral pattern is there as well, and the Avalanche mechanic and cluster pays system is still at the core of the game. In fact, most of the technical aspects are kept in line with Finn and the Swirly Spin to ensure it doesn't stray too far off the beaten path. The 96.1% RTP is a tad bit lower (96.62%), the volatility as well while the hit frequency is nearly the same. Although the max win potential is yet to be confirmed, that part seems to have increased as well, coming in at around 1,000 times your stake. Available across all devices, you can play Finn's Golden Tavern from 0.10 up to a staggering €/$500 per spin.On the visual side of things, the sequel is not quite as colourful as the original. But there's a good reason for that. Finn, probably bored out of his mind from playing the flute all day long, has relocated himself from the outdoors to his tavern, hence why the game has a less cheerful feel. With the reels set on a table, you get to see a closeup of Finn's flute along with some other objects that include a compass, dice, a candle and beer mats.Then, on the reels you'll see an assortment of beverage containers, all four of them being of the same value giving you 5 times your stake for a combination of 5 on a payline. There are also four different gold coins included in the game. Each coin symbol on the reels has a value assigned, and any match of 3 or more coin symbols pays out the sum of all the coin values in the match. The star is once again the wild, and to illustrate the drunken atmosphere of Finn's Tavern, we assume, it now wears an eyepatch.Finn’s Golden Tavern (NetEnt): FeaturesFree spins feature in actionFinn's Golden Tavern benefits from a Free Spins feature and two different random features. Here's what you can expect. In the main game on a no-win spin, the Fist Slam feature can be randomly triggered. You'll see Finn slam his fist on the table which will move a coin symbol so that a win is generated. The other random feature is known as the Random Coin feature - if the free spins chest symbol is in the direct loop of symbols around the central position, this feature will activate to turn low value symbols into coin symbols.In the original version, the objective was to move a key scatter through a swirl to the central position - all in the same series of avalanches (in one spin basically). review: Chi (ELK Studios): ReviewThe games released by ELK Studios during the first quarter of 2019 have been somewhat inconsistent in quality. The first release, The Wiz, was a rather mediocre title that failed to make a lasting impression, whilst Ecuador Gold turned out to be a smash hit and even one of the best titles ever released by the company. It was followed up by the much weaker Hit It Big slot, so going by this order, Chi should be a strong game. But we'll see about that.If you've read our recent reviews, you have probably seen us rant about how sick we are of all the generic Chinese-themed slots that we're continually being forced fed. It's lazy, annoying as hell and shows a total lack of creativity, which goes against everything gaming should be about. Some might not care as long as lady luck smiles at them, but a good portion of players are looking for an escape in their stressful lives to a world that tickles their imagination. Some find it in movies, others in video games, and then we have the degenerates who love to play slots. Anyway, the point we were going to make is this. Although Chi is indeed an Asian-themed slot, it's far from generic. Chi has a narrative, characters with names and most importantly, unique design.Central to the story are two fox-like creatures (spirits) known as Chi and Mow that represent fire and wind (and we're not talking about the kind of symptoms you get from eating at Taco Bell). The action takes place on an unconventional looking reel set with cylindrical wheels that spin laterally. The actual setup is not that far out, however. Chi is a 5-reel, 3-row slot with 27 paylines paying from left to right and right to left, giving you 54 paylines in total. You can play it on all devices from 20 cents to 20 Euros per spin.Set in the Himalayan highlands with beautiful natural scenery in the backdrop, you join the two spirits, Chi and Mow, on their journey to find the lost city of treasures. The game has a soft Asian touch that is backed by tranquil background music to set the mood. On the reels you'll see lower value carp fish, cups, fans, flutes, golden gourds, jade stones, fire lanterns and lotus flowers. There's a wild symbol included as well that replaces all symbols except the scatter.Chi (ELK Studios): FeaturesFree spins feature in actionOn either side of the reel set you'll see totems. If a totem symbol lines up, it activates the respective spirit. The red totem to the left will awaken Chi - when he appears, he'll shoot fireballs onto the reels which can result in 1 to 6 wilds being added to the reels. The blue totem to the right summons Mow who will hit the gong-gong, subsequently boosting your payouts with a multiplier from 2x up to 5x.There are two bonus features included in the game. Firstly, you have the Free Spins feature which is played when you land 3, 4 or 5 free spins symbols anywhere on the reels, giving you 10, 15 or 20 free spins respectively. When it comes to retriggers, you can get plenty of those here as there's no limit to how many times you can retrigger the feature. Now, in the free spins game, all wilds generated by Chi stick throughout the round. In addition, a first hit on Mow activates a progressive multip0lier that starts off at x2 but can go up to x5.The most lucrative feature is the Stairway to Fortune bonus which is triggered by landing 3 bonus symbols. Here, Chi and Mow will work together to reach all the way to the Fortune Reels. As Chi draws a random number between 1 and 6, Mow moves the corresponding number of steps along the cloud path of ever-increasing multipliers. This goes on until Chi draws collect, in which case the multiplier held by Mow is paid out in accordance with your bet level.There's an even better outcome, however, the one where you reach all the way to the heavenly Fortune Reels. Here, a spin on each of the 5 reels is awarded with all the multipliers collected now added on top. The top award comes from hitting the arrow on the uppermost reel which will add the final 10,000x multiplier to your winnings. In total, you can pocket up to 12,500 times your stake in this feature.Chi (ELK Studios): VerdictThere is a lot to like about Chi. Not only is it a gorgeous tale loaded with charm that has restored our faith in the genre, it also offers innovative gameplay, unique and well-designed visuals as well as outstanding potential. Although the game mechanic at play here won't be to everyone's liking, ELK Studios has established a decent foundational system when it comes to the features which are sufficiently engaging to absorb us and fall into the world of Chi and Mow.Chi is a slot that some will love and others will hate. If you ask us, it's a slot that is absolutely worth playing. It's a volatile game, however, so tread carefully. May the spirits be with you in your quest to find the lost city of treasures.

Title: Polterheist
review: Polterheist IntroductionPolterheist is the result of a collaboration between a small Canadian studio called Side City. They're not freshmen, however, and have a few games listed here and there - Venice Magic and Fortunes of the Dead to name a couple of them. The excitement level of seeing a new NextGen slot dropped considerably upon learning it's the result of a collaboration. In fact, we can't figure out why established, and respected game developers insist on working with smaller studios, a trend that seemed to have been started by Microgaming and failed every single time. Is Polterheist the slot to prove us wrong? Let's find out.Polterheist is a 5-reel, 4-row video slot with 100 fixed pay lines and a 96.6% RTP, which is a bit higher than the more common 95%-ish RTP we otherwise often see in NextGen slots. Playable on all devices between €0.50 and €50, this western themed slot with a ghost twist benefits from two random main game features as well as a free spins game with the potential for unlimited free spins.Visually, it's quite childish looking which is likely to be a bit of a turn off to some players. Nonetheless, it's a fairly well-designed slot that is played along to a classic western score that goes well with the game. The playability is fine tuned, although the speed of the gameplay could have been increased a bit.Polterheist Symbols & FeaturesA, K, Q, J, and 10 represent the low-value symbols while the premiums are made out of blue, red, green, purple, and golden ghosts, known as the Hauntin' gang. The Golden Sheriff ghost is the most valuable symbol and gives you 10 times the stake for 5 across a full pay line. None of the symbols appears stacked on the reels which means the payouts in normal mode are low. The Wild symbols come in the form of a wanted poster, and only appears on the three middle reels.There are two main game features included in the game to make up for the monotonous gameplay. These are both randomly triggered, which means they can activate before any spin. The Haunted Wild feature will add a random number of wilds to the three middle reels, while the Ghost Break-In feature adds stacks of one randomly chosen ghost to the reels, with all other ghosts turning into that particular ghost as well.Polterheist Free SpinsFree spins mode with the Ghost Break-In feature activatedThe free spins game is what it's all about in Polterheist and where the tedious wait for the free spins to drop can pay off. To trigger it, players need to land the Golden Safe Scatter symbol on reels 1, 2, and 3 which awards 8 free spins. The free spins game is played out on the same reel set as in the main game, but players will now benefit from a random multiplier being added before each spin, meaning each win is subject to a multiplier of 2x, 3x, or 5x.Furthermore, both the Haunted Wilds and Ghost Break-In features are included and actually appear more frequently here, with the latter allowing the potential for a full screen of the top paying symbol. Should this drop along with a 5x multiplier, you can cheer along to a win of 5000 times the stake. There's also room for endless of spins (at least in theory) as 1, 2, or 3 scatter symbols landing on the reels will add another 1, 5, 0r 8 free spins respectively.Polterheist ConclusionIn theory, Polterheist has potential for endless free spins, but since we haven't seen a fact sheet we must assume that the game is capped. It's unreasonable to think that the free spins would go on forever, or that players would be able to land 4-5 full screens with the max multiplier and walk away with 25,000x wins. If we'd be talking about Big Time Gaming, or any other provider with proven wins of that magnitude, then sure, but in this particular case we're going to hold back a bit on the sugar. The max cap could very well be 2000x for all we know.The two random features did little to help carry the game which felt slow and tedious to us. Sure, there's potential for a 1000x win outside of the bonus, which is not terrible for any main game, but it still doesn't make up for the horrendous gameplay. Polterheist is far from the worst collaboration we've seen, in fact, it's one of the better, but it doesn't reach all the way, unfortunately.

Title: Easter Island
review: When we wrote the sneak preview article, we weren't too excited about Easter Island to be quite honest. The reason was the medium volatility index of the game. It just didn't have that crazy potential that we like to see in slots.But what it lacks in maximum potential, it makes up in entertainment value! And let's face it, what fun would it be if ALL games were mega high potential monsters, on which we rarely, if ever, hit any monster wins on anyway. We need some decent wagering games too, don't we?When we fired up this game we didn't expect much, that's why the intro cought us by surprise. It's likely one of the weirdest slot moments we've ever had to be honest. You have to watch the video to understand what we mean.Easter Island is a light hearted slot and the two animated Moai stones standing next to the game table makes this slot special to say the least! Yggdrasil have done an outstanding job, creating a visually stunning game with surprisingly good mechanics.The GameplayWe'll try to keep it short and then you can watch the video.The base game is made up of 5 reels, 3 rows and 27 paylines. If you land a winning combination on reel 1-3 you will get a respin with extra of the winning symbols added to increase the chance of a big win on the re-spin. A 4-of-a-kind win awards a 5 reel tall respin (65 paylines) and a 5-of-a-kind win awards a 7 reel tall respin (103 paylines). This of course increases the number of paylines and thus the max win.There is a Wild symbol which is present on reel 2 and 4. Wilds that land on winning spins are sticky and expand to cover the entire reel. This means the Wild will follow you into the expanded respin if one is triggered.That's pretty much it. There is no traditional bonus on this game but we never felt like we were missing one. The way this slot is produced it will keep you occupied and entertained with heart stoppers and animated features that will make you smile.ConclusionWe played the game for nearly an hour and during this time it performed really well in terms of maintaining the balance and doing some great wagering. We even stopped with a decent profit. The game can pay quite well, there is no doubt about this if you managed to land a full screen or close to a full screen of the high value symbols, but don't expect any super wins.Don't MissBe sure to try the sequel, Easter Island 2, which sees the wacky characters return for another adventure in a game featuring 6-reels and a 2,500 times the bet max win jackpot.

Title: Sugar Monster
review: Sugar Monster: Slot OverviewNormally, with a sugar-themed slot, we might warn players to make sure to protect their teeth before chomping in. Public health warnings aren't required when playing Sugar Monster from developer Red Tiger though, because it comes with an in-game character who does the munching for you. Sugar Monster is a pay-anywhere slot with sprinklings of cascades, multiplier symbol spewing wild, and free spins where the wild symbol plants itself on the board for the full duration.Cute and quirky is a way of summing up not just Sugar Monster as a whole but certainly its main character and the world it lives in. This is a place where the buildings are quaintly crooked, there's a cupcake shop, and little candies lie spilt about the place. Perhaps the health risks associated with the overconsumption of sugar don't exist in this realm. Or maybe they do, but no one around here really cares. Certainly not the main monster, as it can't seem to get enough of the stuff.Sugar Monster slot - base gameWhen the monster is eating, it generally means wins are happening, too, so that's a good thing. As a scatter paying slot, it means when at least 12 matching symbols are in view in any position on the grid, a win is formed, and players collect a reward. A highly volatile slot, Sugar Monster's RTP wavers between a default value of 95.68% and 95.72% when buying a bonus. When choosing a stake, the options are 10 p/c to $/€8.Each symbol in a win is removed from the board, making space for symbols to drop and replace them. These cascades continue like this until no new win appears on the reels. As for the symbols, since we're dealing with sugar, it makes sense the low-pay symbols are made up of 5 candies, while the high pays are 5 cake-like objects. Payouts for landing winning combinations are 0.3 to 2.5 times the bet for a 12-14 of-a-kind win and 4 to 50 times the bet for a 20+ sized scatter win.Sugar Monster: Slot FeaturesSugar Monster slot - free spinsSugar Monster's features are built around a cascade mechanism, a very hungry Sugar Monster, Cotton Multipliers, free spins and bonus buys.Sugar MonsterThe Sugar Monster is a 1x1 sized wild symbol that may only land on an initial spin and can substitute for any regular pay symbol. However, the wild is not removed by the cascade feature when part of a win but stays on the board where it may be used again. Only one Sugar Monster can land at a time. Above the reels is a progress bar with 4 levels. When the wild participates in a win, it eats the symbols and causes a cascade. Each cascade fills the progress bar by +1 level. When 4 cascades on a single spin sequence occur, the bar is filled, and free spins are triggered.Cotton MultipliersSugar Monsters may also barf up to 3 Cotton Candy symbols with multipliers after consuming a winning combination. At the end of the spin, the sum total of all multipliers is applied to the total win and paid. The multiplier values possible are x2-x6, x8, x10, x15, x20, x25, x50, and x100.Free SpinsWhen the free spins bonus round is triggered, players are awarded 10 free spins. At the start of the feature, the Sugar Monster grows to 2x2 in size and locks itself in the middle of the reels, where it stays. During free spins, accumulated Cotton Multipliers persist for the full duration of the feature. The multiplier applies to all wins which occur on spins where Cotton Multipliers appear. If a multiplier was present on the triggering spin, it is used on that spin, then reset when the free spins round begins. Should the Sugar Monster consume 4 consecutive wins on a single free spin, +3 extra free spins are awarded.Feature BuyThe feature buy comes with two options. One is a spin with a guaranteed Sugar Monster for 3x the bet, and the other triggers free spins for 80x the bet.Sugar Monster slot - free spinsSugar Monster: Slot VerdictScatter-paying slots have really taken off recently, and one studio that has shown considerable gusto is Red Tiger. As well as Sugar Monster, other scatter-paying related slots the studio has released around the same time were Here Kitty Kitty, Peggy Sweets, and Piñatas & Ponies. All very different games, and Sugar Monster manages to differentiate itself not just from them but other scatter-paying sweet slots like Sweet Bonanza. This is in part because its wild symbol appears in the form of a voracious monster. Wild symbols are easy to leave out of a scatter pays game as their inclusion may well throw a spanner in the mathematical works. Not only are wilds used in Sugar Monster, but Red Tiger has imbued them with a personality all their own.So much so that Sugar Monster's whole hungry sugar-eating monster thing is so central it might be the game's make-or-break element. Too kiddy for some, just right for others, perhaps. For players who like the personal touch, and if eating sweets and barfing Cotton Multipliers appeals, then Sugar Monster lays on bags of monster charm. What's kinda neat is how much of the personality has been integrated with the features, such as the eating and barfing and so on. Kinda silly, kinda fun, and a max win of 10,806.6 times the bet helps negate the former.So what is it with the regular matching of candy and scatter-paying slots? Is there a link we've overlooked somewhere, something that ties the two things together, like waffles and Nutella? Whatever it is, software providers can't get enough, and players who feel the same way get something fun, if not remarkable, to try in Sugar Monster.

Title: Sticky Joker
review: Sticky Joker Slot: OverviewIt appears that Play’n GO's Joker Series of Vegas-style slots is still alive and kicking. Not only does the original, Fire Joker, remain one of the studio's most popular slots to date, but it also kicked off the series which is now on its sixth incarnation. So far we've had the original, followed by Inferno Joker, Chronos Joker, Xmas Joker (yes, we skipped reviewing that one), and Star Joker doing their pared-back, simplistic thing. The latest is Sticky Joker, and the title should come with a spoiler alert, because sticky jokers make up most of what the game is all about. Fans of the series will no doubt be fired up over the latest release; others might be wondering whether the gambling world really needed one more of these. Well, consumerism is all about choice, so they say, so let's put Sticky Joker through its paces and see if it's a viable one.The first impressions don't disappoint. If you're expecting a big bright, basic slot, then Sticky Joker is all that and less. Play’n GO have gone for a classic 3 by 3 set up, with a fading blue constellation thing going on in the background. Peripheral effects feel like an afterthought though, as the focus is on the reels and the 9 huge symbols they hold. The symbols used are also everything you hoped or dreaded they would be. The paytable containing a bunch of fruit such as cherries, lemons, grapes, and plums - almost your five a day right there, followed by bars, stars, and lucky sevens. Sevens are the most valuable regular symbol with 3 of a kind paying out 5 times the stake. There are only 5 paylines in play which only allows you to land combos of three of a kind.Low and high rollers will appreciate the range of betting options Sticky Joker has on tap. As a homage to its fruit slot DNA, bets start at just 5 p/c per spin, but can be raised to $/€100. Ticking away in the background, Sticky Joker’s math model is far from being a high thrills beast. Play’n GO has rated the volatility at 6/10, or a medium setting in other words. The other key stat is RTP and the game ships with adjustable rates which can be set by the provider. The best-case scenario is a generous 96.74% RTP, but you can find it a lot lower, so make sure to check the paytable to ensure you play the right one. The game's overall potential is hardly inspirational, but high RTP figures like that should help boost its appeal amongst the casual fruit crowd.Sticky Joker Slot: FeaturesSticky Joker Respin featurePlay’n GO has kept the learning curve low throughout and this goes for features as well. Two accompany the base game, and are the only ways of getting anything close to significant returns. The star of the show is the Joker symbol which is wild and is worth 8 times the stake for three of a kind. The joker can appear in any position, and when one or more land, they are locked in place and trigger a Respin. If another wild lands during the respin, it is also locked and triggers another respin. This respin feature continues to run until no more wilds land, or the grid is covered in them.If 4 or more wilds are in view at the end of a respin, then the Wheel of Multipliers is activated. This wheel is split into 12 segments, each with a multiplier of x2, x3, x4, x5, or x10 on it. When it stops spinning, the selected multiplier is applied to the total win accumulated during the respins feature. A bit like Fire Joker in other words.Sticky Joker Slot: VerdictWell what can you say? Without free spins, or anything particularly new, there's not much to Sticky Joker. If you are not into the genre, it for sure won't do anything to win your heart, or your coins. Occasionally, a developer injects something super original, compelling, or high stakes into a Vegas slot to tempt the naysayers in for a spin or two. Sticky Joker isn't one of those games. Instead, it sticks to the basics and does what it says on a tin, is unashamedly bright and fruity, and carries about its business at a reasonable pace.Fans will probably be able to squeeze out a dose of entertainment value. Its quick, it's easy, and collecting four or more jokers and a multiplier to go with them can be fun. A quick mental calculation comes up with a best-case scenario where a grid of joker wilds and an x10 multiplier is worth a quick fire 400 times the stake. Expanding on that figure, the official maximum exposure is 1,650 times the max bet which is pretty so-so for this type of game. If you consider that potential arose during just 100 million spins compared to billions often found elsewhere, it provides a tick in Sticky Joker’s favour.All told, Sticky Joker is never going to do enough to change minds. Like most slots in this category, fans have something to keep them busy, for like, five minutes, before the next one is dropped. On the other side, those that feel like the world is already drowning in a sea of annoying fruit slots will automatically swipe left.

Title: Rocket Reels
review: Rocket Reels: Slot OverviewAs billionaire trio Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, and Richard Branson take three very different approaches to outer space, Hacksaw Gaming quietly steps in with their version of off-world exploration. Rocket Reels is a space-themed addition to the popular Pocketz Series of slots. These mobile-focused creations look cute, pack solid winning potentials, yet are run by math models that rarely reflect their affable outer appearance. We get all of this in Rocket Reels, where we come across cluster pays, reactions, multiplier rockets, symbol beaming UFOs, and free spins.If you're playing Rocket Reels on a mobile, you'll have to flip it to landscape mode to take in the full view - otherwise, the 7x7 sized grid takes up nearly the full screen. On landscape or a desktop, you get a vision of some purple planet with alien floating rocks and a starry night sky. It feels like a totally benign planet to explore, thanks largely to the cheerful music, which switches between trancey and kids cartoons. It's certainly not the sort of soundtrack that would play as baddy aliens stalk humans.Rocket Reels may be played on any device you prefer, offering stakes of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. The theoretical return value varies from 96.3% when playing in regular mode, rising a teensy bit to 96.34% when buying the free spins bonus game. Loads of multipliers appear throughout the game, though this doesn't mean they always connect with clusters though. However, combined with the high volatility, when they do link together, it can be quite a thrill.When at least five matching symbols land adjacent to each other vertically or horizontally, they form a winning cluster. In total, 10 regular pay symbols appear throughout; half are different coloured rocks, half are colourful planets or asteroid symbols. The most valuable clusters consist of 15+ matching symbols, and when made up of premium symbols, are worth 150 to 300 times the stake. Also included in the package are wild symbols which appear in any position, substituting all paying symbols.Rocket Reels: Slot FeaturesCascades, multipliers, and free spins sound pretty standard, but Rocket Reels manages to do something neat with them that is pretty unique and can lead to some excellent results. First of all, winning clusters are removed from the grid whenever they hit to make way for new symbols. These symbol drops continue to occur until no new winning clusters are created. Any multipliers on screen remain on the reels for the duration of a cascade sequence.Appearing on any reel are 3 types of rocket symbols. In the base game, if 3 or more rockets are in view, they trigger a rocket launch when any cascades have finished. When activated, the rocket symbols blast off, exiting from the top of the grid. As they move, any symbols they pass over are destroyed and replaced with multiplier values. New symbols then fall into the gaps beneath these multipliers, and new win evaluations can be made. Any cluster with a multiplier overlaid on top is multiplied by the value. If more than one multiplier is used in a winning cluster, their values are added together before being applied. The 3 rockets possess these possible values:Rocket 1 – multipliers of x1, x2, x3, x4, or x5.Rocket 2 – multipliers of x10, x15, or x20.Rocket 3 – multipliers of x25, x50, or x75.From time to time, you might get lucky and see a UFO randomly appear when rockets have launched. When one appears, it floats over the grid, hoovering up between 20 and all of the symbols from the reels. New symbols then drop in. UFOs appear in the base or bonus game.Landing 3 spaceman symbols awards 8 free spins. In free spins, rocket symbols always launch, even if there are less than 3 in view.Lastly, if buying the bonus features is an option for you, the cost is 129x the bet. This initiates a spin where 3 spacemen symbols land to trigger free spins.Rocket Reels: Slot VerdictOf the three billionaires mentioned above, each has their own motivations for heading off-world. Jeff Bezos has visions of a trillion human beings trailing out across the stars living in colonies, Richard Branson seems more focused on the tourism dollar, and Elon Musk's company Neuralink can implant chips into human brains, so he seems to be going for the cyborg driven future angle.Rocket Reels, on the other hand, isn't quite so ambitious. In some ways, Rocket Reels feels a little formulaic, but in a warmly familiar way rather than a negative one. You get the feeling Hacksaw Gaming's creative team has dreamed up dozens of these sorts of games and has them on standby, ready to evolve from concept to fully formed game at a moment's notice. These are the cluster paying, reaction-based slots that use multipliers in a variety of clever ways. We're talking about the likes of Xpander, Hop'n'Pop and Toshi Video Club, to name just three, which Rocket Reels sits comfortably alongside.Like those games, the multipliers in Rocket Reels can really make or break your day. It's astonishing how many of them the rockets create yet end up going begging as nothing lands to make use of them. The good part is x10-x25's aren't as rare as you might think and occasionally link with a cluster, though there is a lot of teasing going on. However, the multipliers are such that one or two good spins can change everything, as we've seen in previous Hacksaw games, and Rocket Reels' rewards max out at 10,000 times the stake.In summation, Rocket Reels is one more highly playable slot from the Hacksaw team that mixes, clusters, tumbles, and multipliers to good effect. It's no revolution but has everything needed to entertain players up for something simple yet potentially effective.

Title: Volatile Slot
review: Volatile Slot (Golden Rock Studios): OverviewVolatile Slot comes from young development company Golden Rock Studios in partnership with Microgaming. Golden Rock was founded by two industry heavyweights and state that their games are made by gamblers, for gamblers (we've never heard that one before). Their mission is to "place players at the forefront of their ideas and take them to a happy place". Okay, lofty goals so far, so how does reality compare to the company goals?It is easy to have a reaction that sits on the scale between negative and lukewarm when Volatile Slot first loads. It’s largely due to the name - aren’t all slots by default volatile, whether that is low, medium, or high? You would assume they mean highly volatile, but the first view of the game would suggest otherwise. It’s a completely underwhelming 5-reel, 3-row slot with 10 paylines set against a South Pacific background. A volcano smoulders menacingly in the distance, while palms and beach fronts frame the foreground. Players choose a stake from 10 c/p up to $/€10, and away they go.The first initial spins do little to improve enthusiasm, and we were quick to write this one-off. A space above the reels plays a different message with each spin. One of the first we got was ‘You are a golden rock star’, after winning 40c which did not seem like a good omen. However, you know what they say about not judging a book by its cover. There is a whole lot more going on here than initially meets the eye.As the name would suggest, the volatility of Volatile Slot is high, and comes with an RTP rating of 96.1%. Symbols are adequate to the task, and are made up of 10 - A icons where three or more make a winning combination. The remaining four base game symbols are drums, a fire, a shrine, and a mystical Pacific Island lady. Winning combinations of these symbols are formed by two or more of a kind. The lady is the most valuable at 40 times the stake. So far, so what. Right? That’s how it felt during testing as well.Volatile Slot (Golden Rock Studios): FeaturesBonus featureVolatile Slot has several extras, and on the whole, they are simple and stand back to let the gameplay flow rather than dominate it. There are two wilds – Volcanic Wilds and Exploding Wilds. Volcanic Wilds appear on reels 2, 3, and 4 and substitute for any other symbol. They can also randomly become Exploding Wilds which also substitute for other symbols but explode and award a multiplier of x2, x3, or x4. When more than one Exploding Wild lands the multipliers are multiplied together. The most there can be is 3 Exploding wilds which result in a decent multiplier of x64.Any 3 wilds in view on the grid also trigger 10 Free Spins. During this round, the rules remain the same as the base game, and free spins can be retriggered. What players get though is a different set of reels with more Volcanic Wilds and Exploding Wilds added to make the action somewhat more interesting.Volatile Slot (Golden Rock Studios): VerdictThe Golden Rock website claims that the company uses innovative maths and proven mechanics in their games, and while that may or may not be true, you can't help but feel that the developers deceived themselves by simply thinking high volatility and huge potential would be enough to make a great slot. Sure, knowing the potential that could be lurking just around the corner does extend the game's shelf life, but the gameplay and graphics are so basic that it gets extremely tedious real quick. Much of the time it's about as exciting as scrolling through an Excel sheet.Golden Rock state that they know players want to win BIG! (their capitals, not ours). Since they have largely lived up to their claims so far, players will want to know exactly how big. With Volatile Slot, we are talking about max potential of up to 25,600 times the stake. The first time that flashed across the message bar, it felt like a typo. Initially, however, it can be hard to correlate that figure with the basic graphics, and a name that feels like it was lost in translation. Just how realistic those numbers are remains to be seen. We certainly didn't come anywhere close to that during our testing. Moreover, with a max bet of €/$ 100, there is good reason to believe that the max win is capped.Of course, the high potential alone could be enough to get people talking, but it will need more than that to stand up against all other other insanely popular high variance, ultra high potential slots out there. Unless the potential is actualized real soon in the form of screenshots and Youtube videos, Volatile Slot will become an extinct volcano.

Title: Shaolin Master
review: Shaolin Master: Slot OverviewSoftware provider Hacksaw Gaming gets its 'hi-yah' on in the online slot Shaolin Master, which is more or less a reskin of the nightmare on reels gambling machine that was Hand of Anubis. Shaolin Kung Fu is a highly respected martial art, and mastery is no doubt a long and difficult process. Reskinning, by comparison, is probably not so tough. Oftentimes, the copy isn't as thrilling as the original either, but Hand of Anubis was a top-shelf Hacksaw Gaming release, so maybe some of the magic has rubbed off.Depending on where you live, Shaolin Master is probably every bit as exotic as Ancient Egypt, though this one is far less scary. On one side of the game board, we find the master, while on the other side, his student stands in an elaborate pose, sort of like Daniel LaRusso's crane kick that won him the 1984 All Valley Karate Tournament, busting Johnny's face with his controversial strike. There's nothing controversial about Shaolin Master's look, though it puts on a nice enough kung fu in the mountains view.Shaolin Master slot - base gameShaolin Master's symbols land on a 5-reel setup, with 6 rows and a cluster pays win system. 10 cents to $/€100 may be wagered on each base game round, and several bonus buy modes may be activated for gamblers who would prefer to play that way. Title: Ankh of Anubis Awakening
review: Ankh of Anubis Awakening: Slot OverviewAnubis, one of the most important Gods of Ancient Egypt, is also one of the more popular deities in online gambling, and the jackal-headed entity headlines Play'n GO's slot Ankh of Anubis Awakening, a follow-up to the 2019 release Ankh of Anubis. There's a twist in these slots, however. Instead of inhabiting a world thousands of years old, Play'n GO has placed Anubis in a world of the future, somewhat similar to what Big Time Gaming did in Book of Gods. Running Ancient Egyptian elements in a futuristic setting is an enticing, if not totally unique idea, and running alongside this world of tomorrow are some just as enticing game elements.The Anubis character in this slot is certainly not the sort of being who sits back passively and watches the world go by. As well as being linked to wild symbols, the Egyptian God offers vocal commentary throughout the game, and generally comes across as an entity keen to get amongst the action. Metaphorically speaking that is, there is no guarantee how effective or frequent the Anubis features will be. Play'n GO's world-building has again largely been a success, resulting in a moody futuristic landscape residing beneath a brooding circular sky. Hard to say exactly what is going on, but it looks ominous, as well as nicely displayed up on the screen.Ankh of Anubis Awakening slot - base gameSitting in a 3-4-4-4-3 formation is Ankh of Anubis Awakening's 5-reel gaming grid. Winning combinations pay left to right across 576 ways to win. Rated 6 out of 10, Ankh of Anubis Awakening is a medium volatile slot, and of the several RTP versions available, 96.2% is the most desirable. With no extra gambling options in sight, the only decision to make when playing Ankh of Anubis Awakening is picking a base bet. The options range from 10 c to $/€100.Ankh of Anubis Awakening's pay table lists 9 regular paying symbols. Five of them are 10-A card ranks, and the other four are jewellery-type objects. Hitting 5 royals in a win is worth 0.3 to 0.8 times the bet or 1.5 to 10 times the bet for landing five premium symbols. Anubis is printed on the wild, and it is part of all reel strips. The wild symbol substitutes for any symbols except the scatter to help link winning combinations. Five wilds in a winning way pay 25x.Ankh of Anubis Awakening: Slot FeaturesAnkh of Anubis Awakening slot - free spinsJoining players on the features front are the Anubis Wild feature, Anubis Respins, and free spins.Anubis Wild FeatureThe Anubis Wild feature activates randomly on any base game spin. When triggered, 4 to 8 wild symbols are added to the grid while the reels are spinning. This feature does not guarantee a win.Anubis RespinScatter and wild symbols appearing in non-winning payways trigger the Anubis Respin feature. During this feature, all wild symbols remain on the reels and spread vertically up and/or down until they cover the whole reel. A fully stacked wild symbol is removed on the next respin. During the feature, new wild symbols do not land. Up to 3 respins are awarded, depending on the wild landing position. The feature ends when all wild symbols are fully visible on the reels.Free SpinsThe Ankh scatter symbol may land on any reel. Hitting 3, 4, or 5 scatters triggers 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. Collecting 5 Ankh symbols on the collection meter during free spins adds wilds to the reels, triggering the Anubis Wild feature. Collection persists between free spins. Landing the wild symbol during free spins triggers the Anubis Respin feature. Ankh symbols do not land during the Anubis Respins feature, and free spins resume once Anubis Respins are complete. The bonus spins round is extended by +3, +4, or +5 free spins by landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters, respectively, up to a cap of 500 free spins.Ankh of Anubis Awakening slot - respin featureAnkh of Anubis Awakening: Slot VerdictWe've probably said it before, and we'll probably say it again, but gosh darn, doesn't Play'n GO get weak at the knees for all things Ancient Egypt? The studio has taken a break from aged temples and sand for a moment, though, for another push into the future. Transporting Ancient Egypt to the future might be more common than you think, with Thunderkick and Pragmatic Play being two studios which have also gotten in on the action via Pyramyth and Rise of Pyramids, respectively. The concept works well, and you can only help but wonder what the world would have been like if the Egyptian Dynasties had defeated the Romans to flourish for another few thousand years.The world might have looked like the one in Ankh of Anubis Awakening; it's fun to pretend. Ankh of Anubis Awakening features had their moments of fun, as well. They're not as futuristic as the location they've been placed in, but they've somewhat revamped, where spreading wild respins and up to 8 wilds added to the reels can come in handy. Anubis Respins in the base game are interesting since they are triggered by wilds and scatters on non-winning ways. That may mean wilds aren't exactly in the most helpful positions to start with, though the ways system counterbalances this effect to a degree. You get Anubis Respins in the bonus round, as well, which, capped at 500 free spins, seems like a ludicrously large amount (though not as many as Ankh of Anubis' 'indefinite'). It'll be the future before so many spins play out. What's good in the bonus round is when 5 Ankhs are collected, wilds are randomly added to the grid, triggering Anubis Respins. It happened that 4 wilds were placed on the leftmost 4 reels, which ended up quite favourably.500 free spins would surely give you a decent chance of achieving Ankh of Anubis Awakening's 15,000x the bet max win (the same figure as before). Given Play'n GO's reputation, perhaps that many free spins are required for doing so? Sarcasm aside, Ankh of Anubis Awakening was a solid game that does some nifty tricks with wilds and respins in a gripping neo-cyber-techno-Ancient Egyptian world.

Title: Freeway 7
review: Freeway 7: Slot OverviewJoin software provider ELK Studios as it heads out on the highway, once again, in an online slot titled Freeway 7. The last related one was Route 777, which took place on an enigmatic stretch of asphalt, and if anything, Freeway 7 is even more enigmatic. A quick Google turned up a Freeway 7 in Greece, Iran, and Taiwan, but it doesn't seem like any of these destinations are what the studio had in mind when making the game. Anyway, it's to the open road players are slung in Freeway 7, in a simply arranged slot, with Road Block Nudges, bonus games, super bonus games, and maybe an X-iter menu to keep you company as the miles roll by.Freeway 7 slot - base gameAt the time of writing, it wasn't explicitly stated, but it's a safe-ish bet to assume Freeway 7 is another instalment in ELK Studios' burgeoning Classic Series of slots. This is a line of fruit slots that blends new elements with old-school bits for players who might not happen to be in the mood for something overblown, like, say, Nitropolis 2 with its mind-boggling number of possible ways to win. Instead, Freeway 7 is held on a 3x3 game grid with 17 connecting paylines. Like its cousin Route 77, Freeway 7 finds itself on a straight stretch of road, blazing its way through a mountainous part of the world. Somewhere like Arizona? Players can choose with their imaginations. Accompanying the blurred highway graphics is a blazing rock track that encourages easing into a higher gear while putting your foot on the gas - respecting the speed limit, of course.Freeway 7 has been designed to play on any device, taking bets of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. When banging away on the play button or switching to Bonus mode via the X-iter menu, the return to player value remains constant at 94%, while volatility is high. Only three-of-a-kind winning lines are possible, and there are eight normal pays. Each one is a throwback from the classic era of slots, where from low to high, we find cherries, oranges, watermelons, BARs, gold 7s, red 7s, blue 7s, then Stars and Stripes 7s. Winning combos of these symbols pay 0.5 to 7.5 times the stake. Should wild symbols hit, they substitute for any pay symbol.Freeway 7: Slot FeaturesFreeway 7 slot - free spinsThe first extra to cover is the Road Block Nudge which is similar to Route 777's respins feature. When identical symbol combinations appear on reels 1 and 3, they trigger the Road Block Nudge with respins. Reels 1 and 3 step down 1 position on each respin, while the middle reel spins. If during respins, the two outer reels hold bonus symbols, they are nudged towards the centre where they are locked.Bonus GameLanding 3 bonus symbols triggers free spins. Alternatively, landing 2 bonus symbols and a super bonus symbol on the middle reel triggers the super bonus game. If this happens during Road Block Nudges, free spins immediately trigger. The remaining respins are played when the bonus round has ended. During the bonus game, all wins award additional free spins. A counter above the reels tracks how many you have left. At the start, all symbols are active. When they form a win, they increase the win multiplier and become deactivated, meaning they cannot increase the multiplier in that state. However, landing 3 bonus symbols retriggers the bonus game (or super bonus game) and reactivates all symbols, so they can be used again to increase the multiplier when they win next. The rules of the super bonus game are the same, except that the win multiplier starts on a higher level and each win always increases its value – symbols are always active. The amount it increments by is higher, too.It is possible to trigger the Road Block Nudge during Bonus mode. When this happens, free spins are not consumed, but wins during the Road Block Nudge award extra free spins, and wins with active symbols increase the multiplier. The final point is if the bonus or super bonus game triggers at the same time as the Road Block Nudge, then the Road Block Nudge will be played when the bonus or super bonus game is finished.X-iterClicking the X-iter feature buy button activates bonus mode, where these five options may be selected:Bonus Hunt – 2x the bet to double the chance of triggering the bonus game.Chili Spins – 10x the bet for a spin where only sevens, cherries, wilds, bonus or super bonus symbols land.Road Block Nudge – 25x the bet to trigger the Road Block Nudge.Bonus - 100x the bet to enter the bonus game.Super Bonus – 500x the bet to enter the super bonus game.Freeway7 slot - feature buy menuFreeway 7: Slot VerdictFreeway 7 is a textbook Classic Series slot type experience. If you do get caught up in the flow in the rapid three-reel pace of the thing, it can be quite fun. Symbols slam away on the reduced gaming matrix to the thrumming soundtrack and the fiery outdoor scenery. Of course, it'll help to be interested in this format, as these retro-ish games are pitched to a certain audience. If you liked what ELK Studios has done in the past with them, especially the Route 777 one, there's a good chance Freeway 7 will blow your hair back as well.The features are when Freeway 7 gets the chance to hit the accelerator and open things up. Road Block Nudges are good for a few respins, no complaints there, but it's not till the win multiplier enters the picture that Freeway 7 really showed its stuff. Decent multiplier values were achieved during testing, both in super and regular bonus games, though the super version benefits from symbols never being deactivated. How often the super triggers naturally is an interesting question because it costs substantially more to buy from the X-iter menu, though that's a common occurrence in many ELK Studio games. Also quite common and less desirable is the noticeably low RTP value, made more obvious when compared to Route 777's value. It seemed like ELK Studios had bucked the downward trend in Propaganda, but no, it appears the downward race is back on. Ah well, for the record, Freeway 7 comes with a win cap of 5,000x the stake.If percentage differences are neither here nor there, and you're looking to let rip along a virtual highway with some classic gaming with a modern twist, Freeway 7 might well fit the bill. On the other side of the coin, if previous games in the Classic Series have failed to impress till now, it's unlikely Freeway 7 will break the trend.

Title: RagingPop
review: RagingPop: Slot OverviewProving its ongoing popularity, RagingPop is, count 'em, the eleventh PopWins game to roll off Avatar UX's production line. For RagingPop, the studio has left the 'land of the rising sun' where we last encountered them in MonkeyPop and moved to another exotic part of the world. This time, they're in the swaying grasslands of Africa, a popular slot destination, and brought with them dynamic reels, increasing rows, ways, and potentially hefty random multipliers sprinkled in for good measure.While not as immediately eye-catching as MonkeyPop, RagingPop is nevertheless a smart-looking game, cramming in most of the visuals this genre is famous for. If a new win is created, the process repeats, though reels can expand up to 7 positions high at the most.Raging RhinoIn the base or bonus game, there is a chance the Raging Rhino feature randomly activates. When it does, the reels grow to 5, 6, or 7 symbols tall, and a multiplier is generated, which gets applied to any win. The multiplier can be as high as x500.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols awards 10, 15, 20, or 30 free spins. The reels start at 4 positions high and can grow to 7 high through the PopWins feature; however, they return to their starting height at the start of each new free spin. In addition, for every 10 consecutive free spins, the reels grow by +1 symbol in height, which they stay at for the rest of the feature. Before free spins begin, however, players have the option of gambling what they've won for more on the gamble wheel. The gamble feature has several stages, allowing players to win 15, 20, 25, or 30 free spins. Losing the gamble on the first stage returns you to the base game but losing at higher levels triggers the bonus round with a lower number of free spins, as indicated by the wheel.Buy BonusWhere applicable, players can buy a standard free spins trigger for 100x the bet, which can be gambled for more, or by paying 500x the bet, players instantly get 30 free spins.RagingPop: Slot VerdictAvatar UX slots are usually quite successful when the studio picks traditional themes, such as CherryPop or PapayaPop, and the same can be said about RagingPop. It looks the business and flows as smoothly as any they've done so far. There are a few surprises from a gameplay perspective, which may be perceived as negative or positive. The biggest shock was finding out PopWins was missing from the base game. That was odd. It's like playing a Megaways slot without Reactions for the first time. It doesn't ruin the experience as such, though, and after a few spins, veterans should be well-adjusted.It's not a complete desert of features either, since the Raging Rhino can trigger at any moment, but without PopWins, RagingPop's base game is one of the most uneventful in the range. If you're the kind of player who prefers Megaways without cascades, then Raging Rhino could be the ideal PopWins slot to transition with. It does mean that more than any other PopWins game, RagingPop is all about its free spins bonus round. There is where things can heat up, and payouts up to a cap of 20,000x the bet may be possible. On a side note, RagingPop also comes with one of the more forgiving gamble wheels Avatar UX has designed. Often, these wheels will brutally tax you of all free spins when a gamble is unsuccessful. At least now, players can walk away with a few free spins when losing from the second level onwards.For players looking for an all bells and whistles PopWins experience, RagingPop probably isn't the number one choice. There are others in the series that ram in way more popping possibilities than RagingPop does. Perhaps it's a sign of maturing that Avatar UX doesn't feel the need to impress by stuffing in every kind of firework. After seeing this and MonkeyPop, it feels like the studio is putting a greater focus on theme presentation rather than going all out with features. So, while RagingPop might not be the zenith of PopWins gaming, it's evidence of Avatar UX striving to create a more refined experience.

Title: Reindeer Royale
review: Reindeer Royale: Slot OverviewStockholm-based software provider ELK Studios has leaned towards the yearly Xmas redo bandwagon with the release of Reindeer Royale, a slot built from the bunny-infested 2023 release Rabbit Royale. It is volatile, too, with ELK Studios having rated this part of the game as 9 out of 10, and despite any Christmas leanings, the RTP remains at 94%. When opening up the X-iter bonus buy menu, players get 5 choices, while the base bet range is 10 c on the lowest side to $/€100 on the highest.For whatever reason, symbol values have fallen since Rabbit Royale, so a line of 5 matching low pays (darts, traps maybe, bottles, and grabbers) award 0.3 times the bet. For high pay, Reindeer Royale has a vehicle, a meat mincer, a dude with a gun, and a dude with a knife, paying 1 to 3 times the bet for 5 OAK. A payline of all wilds has the same value as the highest-value symbol.Reindeer Royale: Slot FeaturesReindeer Royale slot - free spinsReindeer Royale fires off features such as ammunition reveals, Reindeer Respins, a Ghost feature, free spins, and X-iter bonus buys.Ammunition Reveals, Reindeer, and Reindeer RespinsAmmunition cache symbols may simply land or, when a wild contributes to a win, it reveals an ammunition cache with a random value. All reindeer symbols in view collect the values of the ammunition caches after paylines wins. Ammunition cache collections trigger a respin.Reindeer symbols are also blockers, and their job is to collect ammunition cache values on the reels. They also collect other reindeer symbol values when they are vertically and horizontally adjacent to each other. This occurs after ammunition cache collection. A collect triggers a respin, and reindeer symbols may move to new positions. If a reindeer lands on a respin without ammunition caches, 1 respin is granted.Ghost FeatureThe ghost feature triggers randomly on a respin or free spin when there are at least 2 reindeer in view. It triggers a face-off between a random number of visible reindeer, which takes place over spinning reels where the selected reindeer are located. Reindeer do not need to be adjacent to each other.Free SpinsIn the base game, landing 3 scatters awards 3 free spins with 1 reindeer on the first spin. Landing 4 scatter symbols award 4 free spins with 2 reindeer on the first free spins, while 5 scatters trigger 5 free spins with 3 reindeer on the first free spin. During the feature, landing 3 or more scatter symbols retriggers additional free spins and reindeer, determined in the same way as when the bonus was first triggered. Any reindeer present on the triggering base game spin are carried over into the bonus round, in addition to any reindeer awarded from the scatter trigger - up to a maximum of 5 reindeer. All reindeer stay sticky in free spins, their collected values persistent, and free spins are not consumed by respins.X-iterReindeer Royale's X-iter offers several different bonus buys: Bonus Hunt (2x the bet) - buys one spin with triple the chance of triggering free spins, Oh Deer! (10x the bet) - buys one game round with a reindeer symbol, It's Reining Deers (25x the bet) - buys a game round with 2 reindeer and a wild symbol, Bonus (100x the bet), or Super Bonus (500x the bet) - 5 free spins and 3 reindeer.Reindeer Royale slot - free spinsReindeer Royale: Slot VerdictReindeer Royale doesn't ooze enough tinsel, decorations, or Santas to be considered a traditional white Christmas slot, but there are enough references in the form of reindeer and a reindeer called Rudolf to lump the game in the general Xmas direction. That would at least explain why ELK has basically reskinned Rabbit Royale, as many developers do for the Christmas season. The skin change has been successfully accomplished, however, due to ELK Studios flexing its art, sound, and fury department to create an amusing atmosphere of desolate violence perpetrated by a group of maniacal reindeer.The Ghost Collect feature is a new named addition, that's one thing, and symbol values have been decreased, potentially making Reindeer Royale's base game more painful than Rabbit Royale, as it seemed to drop a large number of dead spins. Although, maybe the lowered symbol values mean more of the measly RTP has been shared with the reindeer symbol collection feature. That would be good because the action only really heated up when reindeer and ammunition cache symbols were in view. Then the game could be quite exciting, the music cranking up several notches, as does the violence, along with the chance to collect some dough. As in its predecessor, the magic of Reindeer Royale is the way adjacent reindeer symbols grab each other's cash values and add them to their own. Two reindeer on the board swapping values can be entertaining, 5 might be crazy. They would need to be unbelievably crazy to get near Reindeer Royale's 25,000x the bet max win. Without the power of multipliers it's a little hard to picture this occurring. But, with a planetoid amount of luck and a whole lot of reindeer symbol swapping, technically, at least, it appears possible.All in all, Reindeer Royale isn't one of ELK Studios' greats on account of the second time around reason. But it was a fun game to review, such is the talent the developer's graphics and sound team has for knocking together slots that appeal to the senses, augmented by equally appealing features (if and when they go pop).

Title: Banana Drop

Title: Dice Dice Dice
review: Dice Dice Dice (Red Tiger): OverviewThe fruit slot freight train rumbles on and refuses to die thanks to Dice Dice Dice from Red Tiger partners R7. This game marries slots with dice and incorporates this oldest of gambling devices to add a new twist to the fruit theme. Some people do things for money and glory; others do them for the sheer love of it. It seems that R7 belongs to the latter because they remain as enigmatic as ever with virtually no information about them available online, not even a website. That is almost unheard of these days. They are becoming like the controversial Satoshi Nakamoto, the supposed inventor of Bitcoin, do they really exist? Someone exists in a well-hidden lab somewhere because they continue to turn out popular slots.Their initial release, Devil's Number, was an exciting journey to the dark side and a solid debut effort. R7 are a company that is a little unorthodox in what they do. Instead of starting out mainstream, building a following and moving out to the fringe, they have done the opposite. And it doesn't get much more mainstream than a fruit slot, though DDD does possess a couple of unique features.Dice Dice Dice is a sweet looking game, with a 5x3 grid set in a realistic-looking slot machine, all chrome and bright colours that give it a classic American look. Depending on your device’s screen size, the background can appear as a blurred casino gaming hall which adds a touch of atmosphere to the proceedings. Sound effects are more minimal with the odd beep and rumble when the reels spin and features kick in. Players set stakes from as low as 10 p/c and as high as $/€20 per spin. Hit the spin button manually, or get into the flow of the game by engaging auto and/or turbo spins. The game has just 10 paylines on which to create winning combinations of three or more symbols.Symbols are exactly what you would expect. In ascending order we get cherries, plums, oranges, watermelons, bells, and diamonds. Fiery lucky 7s top the paytable at 15 times the stake for five of a kind. Fruit slots often work best when motoring along at a steady pace, and Dice Dice Dice is no exception. There are no scatters to look out for, so no free spin rounds as such, nor any bonus games to get in the way of the action. RTP is a hair's breadth below the average at 95.74%. This helps wins come in flurries and lulls due to the medium/high volatility, and overall the returns can be pretty decent.Dice Dice Dice (Red Tiger): FeaturesRolling Reels feature in playLike the majority of fruit slots, Dice Dice Dice doesn't come packed with features. Instead it's more about simplistic, rhythmic gameplay and pace. With that said, the features that are available can pack quite a punch nonetheless.The middle reel is the domain of the Lucky Dice symbols. When one of them lands as part of a win line, it is rolled, and the number that turns up is multiplied against the win. Most of the time a Lucky Dice symbol will have just one die to it, but they can land with two or three dice as well. They can also completely cover the third reel to increase win rates even further.The second feature is the Rolling Respins which gives the grid a real shake to let you know it is in play. This feature is activated at random at any time, and while it's in play, Lucky Dice are more likely to land. Not only that but when they do land, the multiplier is added from Respin to Respin, which can reach some impressive levels. There is no set number of Respins, so the number of them is also random. During testing, they generally arrived in batches of around 10, and with the multiplier racking up, some decent payouts were coming through.Dice Dice Dice (Red Tiger): VerdictThe fruit slot theme is certainly not in short supply. Every developer is obliged to crank out at least one just to keep the conservative gamblers happy. It may be a category that has been flogged to death, yet ater seeing what Dice Dice Dice is capable of you would have to say that R7 has done a good job overall. It's not unmissable, or very innovative, and it does remind us a tiny bit of NetEnt's Grand Spinn, but on the whole it does offer a couple of new features that make it stand out from the crowded bunch.Speaking of originality, it's hard to track down any slot that use dice rolls to calculate multipliers. It's a good idea, and when you see it in action, it makes perfect sense. It's one of those effectively simple concepts that make you wonder why so few have implemented it before now. And what a difference multipliers can make. Without them, a full grid of 7s will get you 150 times your bet. Get the Rolling Respins feature to shake up the game and that figure can rocket as high as 5,497 times the stake. A juicy potential, and along with the clever features make the game interesting even if fruit slots aren't totally your thing.As far as fruit slots go, Dice Dice Dice is certainly above average. In the looks department, it scores good marks, and they are paired with fast-paced gameplay. Fruit slots are meant to be quick and easy, and R7 accomplishes this with DDD. There are no complicated rules, or reel dynamics to get in the way of the action. If fruit slots are your thing, or you're just in the mood for an attractive, modern fruit slot, consider taking a look. Dice Dice Dice is certainly capable of serving up some entertaining gaming.

Title: 24k Dragon
review: 24K Dragon: Slot OverviewThe title might sound like it comes from an Asian themed slot, conjuring up images of golden beasts wrapped around green or burgundy reels. However, Play'n GO's 24K Dragon is based on the mythical creatures populating fantasy literature or movies. The name actually has more to do with potential wins, rather than metallic purity. It means there is more going on here than first greets the eye, in more ways than one. As well as extra meaning in the title, 24K Dragon also has features which expand rows and win ways.The game’s bright 5-reel, 1,024 win ways action area sits in a cavernous space, where a fortune in gold lies piled around stone pillars. The view is similar to the mountain of gold Smaug slept on in the Hobbit film. Then again, many dragons slept on treasure hordes in fiction, so it's an apt location. Equally apt is the dramatic soundtrack, heavy on the brass, which sounds like a dragon taking flight to spread terror amongst the common folk. You can easily close your eyes to picture Dany on top of Drogon as the beast lays waste to King's Landing.24K Dragon is available on all devices, offering a standard range of Play’n GO bets from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Players get a default RTP rating of 96.2%, though this could be lower depending on operators' settings. Play’n GO slots often tend to the highly volatile side of the spectrum, and with such massive potential up for grabs, it stands to reason 24K Dragon's is high as well. It certainly played out like that during testing where even expanding reels to their full height in free spins was no guarantee of success.All of the pay symbols involved can land stacked, consisting of five low pay 10-A royals designed in a font that wouldn't look out of place in one of Play’n GO's heavy metal slots. Then there is a lion, a green gem, and a couple of crossed swords as the mids worth 2-2.5 times the stake. Last up are two dragons – a silver and gold one both worth 5x the bet for five of a kind.Assisting with win frequency and value is the treasure chest wild, appearing on the middle reels. The wild replaces any regular pay symbol to complete a combination, while occasionally upping the value in the base game by revealing an x2 or x4 multiplier.24K Dragon: Slot Features﻿There are two extras to cover here - a respin feature and the showpiece expanding reels free spin game. Nothing is especially new, both having shown up in past Play’n GO games in one form or the other. They have been tweaked since previous outings though and can be exceptionally effective when the dragon's in the right mood.Any time a golden dragon symbol lands in the base game, a 24K Dragon Respin is awarded. For this respin, a random number of 1-4 extra rows is added to the grid. These rows contain 3 symbols each and sit above the middle rows. Players get a single spin with the extra rows and extra ways to win.Next is the bonus game, triggered when 3, 4, or 5 diamond scatters land to award 8, 15, or 20 free spins respectively. As in the base game, free spins begin on the standard 5x3, 1,024 win ways grid. Now, when golden dragon symbols land, they do not trigger a respin, but are instead collected. A meter to the left of the screen tracks your progress as you go. When a certain number has been accumulated, extra rows are added above the main reels in a similar way to respins, except they remain in play for the duration. The collection system goes like so:3 collected dragons unlock row 1, increasing win ways to 2,000.7 collected dragons unlock row 2, increasing win ways to 3,456.11 collected dragons unlock row 3, increasing win ways to 5,488.15 collected dragons unlock row 4, increasing win ways to 8,192.In free spins, treasure chest wilds always reveal a multiplier. If more than one wild is used in a win, their values are multiplied together up to a maximum of x64. During the feature, 5, 8, 15, or 20 more spins are awarded every time 2, 3, 4, or 5 scatters are in view on the reels to lengthen the round. There is no limit to how many free spins players can rack up in this way.24K Dragon: Slot VerdictTake the creatures from Dragon Maiden, the style of Testament, and the reel expansion capabilities of both, then mix them to get an idea of what 24K Dragon is all about. The game world has been well crafted with plenty of the winged beasts to satisfy fantasy fans looking for a fix. Graphically of a fairly high standard, the stirring orchestral piece adds another layer of spectacle to the game, resulting in another striking Play’n GO slot.Moving on, 24K Dragon might not be super original when it comes to gameplay, but overall, the experience does feel somewhat fresh in action. A few alterations to the features help 24K Dragon stand apart from its forebears. What also makes it stand out is the much higher than normal potential. Play’n GO usually stick to 5 or 10k wins like clockwork. That rule has been tossed out in favour of potential up to 24,000 times the bet this time around - hence the title. Quite why they decided to go so huge on this one is a mystery. While a decent game, 24K Dragon doesn't feel like a flagship release or a game the studio is going to majorly hype.All up, 24K Dragon is certainly good for few spins, though Tolkien enthusiasts will get more out of the D&D visuals. Regular players can still get a kick, particularly big win chasers due to the much larger wins on tap than we are used to seeing from Play’n GO.

Title: Thrill to Grill
review: Thrill to Grill: Slot OverviewHey players, feeling a bit stressed, work got you down, need a little break from the grind? If so, then why not take a moment to have a look over Thrill to Grill from software provider NetEnt? The tee-up sounds pretty neat, as the game sheet talks about embarking on a 'sizzling adventure to a tropical paradise' and feeling the heat of summer as a BBQ grill takes centre stage.' So, if frying up food by the beach sounds pretty darn sweet, grab a steak or a portobello mushroom, and let's get a grillin'.As far as tropical paradises go, Thrill to Grill isn't the most exciting. Part of the reason is because its bird's eye perspective reveals a bunch of plain-looking rocks, sand, sea and palm trees. Don't know. It looks more desolate than paradisiacal, like a deserted island with nothing to do but lose your grip on reality and start personifying inanimate objects to have someone or something to talk to. This is a bit niche, but Thrill to Grill brought back The Larva Island Movie vibes and memories of all its odd wee critters. Basically, the first impression of Thrill to Grill was pretty tepid, as if this BBQ needed more gas.Thrill to Grill slot - base gameLaid out on the sand is Thrill to Grill's gaming grid, constructed with 5 columns holding 5 symbols each and providing 3,125 ways to win. Its cutie pie antics are aimed at players who favour low/medium volatile slots, and it is available in two RTP options, the default return value weighing in at 96.05%. Bets go from 20 p/c up to $/€200 per spin, and a buy feature is on hand for users who wish to skip the base game altogether.Thrill to Grill's pay symbols award wins when matching symbols land on at least 3 adjacent reels, from the leftmost reel onwards. As its low pays, we find 9 to A card ranks, awarding 0.75 to 1.25 times the bet for a 5 OAK hit, then broccoli, aubergine, corn, ribs, and meat as the highs where a 5 OAK win is worth 2.5 to 10 times the bet. Each food item has eyes, adding personality, but also guilt over the thought of consuming them. Whatever, Thrill to Grill also drops wild symbols onto reels 2, 3, and 4 in the base game, as well as in free spins to substitute for any pay symbol.Thrill to Grill: Slot FeaturesThrill to Grill slot - free spinsAlso found in both phases of play is Thrill to Grill's Collection feature, which is accompanied by a free spins round and a bonus buy option.Collection FeatureThis feature may randomly trigger during any spin in the main game and is always active in free spins.
