A random symbol is chosen to be a special Grill symbol, which stays in the collection area for the duration of the feature. This could be any type of symbol in the base game. Grill symbols stay in their positions or move about within the collection area at the start of the next spin. In the main game, when 5 or more Grill symbols appear in the collection area, a respin is awarded. Grill symbols do not move position for the respin, and following this, the Collection feature ends. Collection features are saved at bet levels.Free SpinsHitting at least 5 scatter symbols on the reels triggers 3 free spins, where the Collection feature is constantly active. When a Grill symbol lands in the collection area, free spins are set back to 3. The Grill symbol in free spins cannot be a wild or a scatter. Also, these 3 features may trigger at random:The Expand symbol may land above or below the collection area, making the position it landed on part of the collection area until free spins end.The Slap feature picks a Grill symbol without a multiplier. On the next spin, this Grill symbol absorbs all other Grill symbols in the collection area before converting into a Grill symbol with a multiplier of x1 plus the number of symbols it absorbs, plus the multiplier of all Grill symbols with multipliers it absorbs. Multipliers are applied to winning Grill symbol combinations.The Extra Spin symbol increases the maximum number of free spins to 4 till the round ends and resets the spin count to 4. This symbol can only land once in free spins.If a respin and free spins are triggered at the same time, the respin plays first, with scatters disappearing from the reels before free spins begin. If scatters are the Grill symbol in this scenario, then respins play first, and the scatter symbols, which are also Grill symbols, stay in the collection area. Then free spins begin when the respin ends.Buy FeatureFor those keen to cook, the free spins round may be bought for the cost of 60 times the bet. The RTP when doing so is 96.02%.Thrill to Grill slot - free spinsThrill to Grill: Slot VerdictThrill to Grill started slow but did get better once it was given time to strut some of its stuff. Although, that might not be saying a lot since the first impression was pretty weak. The game just didn't look very appetising, despite being covered in food items, and the so-called tropical paradise looked like a deserted island where someone would lose their mind out of boredom. A glimpse over the stats didn't help either, though it might if players are in the mood for a low-medium volatile slot with a max win of 1,946 times the bet and eyeballed food items.Given a chance, though, Thrill to Grill is capable of producing certain moments, considering its limitations. The Collection feature is an interesting idea. Sticky/roaming wilds are an established concept, but rarely do you see the roaming/sticky duties fulfilled by regular pay symbols. It's novel, but the novelty comes at the expense of wishing they were just wilds up there, roaming and possibly multiplying the wins they are part of. However, Thrill to Grill probably would have been a completely different game if that was the case. Instead, it's a dash more experimental while dialling back on the volatility in the process, having a wider range of ingredients it can toss into the Collection feature.In the end, Thrill to Grill wasn't a game which caused outrageous adrenaline rushes while playing, nor is it one that looks great. It's a lower-powered performer, all things considered, with the sort of numbers better suited to some causal side gambling than a massive stakes rocket ride of a game. If it sounds cool, cool, but Thrill to Grill wasn't a deeply satisfying dish that got all manner of mouths watering.

Title: Tome of Madness
review: Tome of Madness (Play'n GO): ReviewPlay'n GO poster boy and widely travelled veteran adventurer, Rich Wilde, embarks on yet another expedition in search of gold and glory in this H.P Lovecraft inspired game titled Tome of Madness. If you're not familiar with this handsome Indiana Jones lookalike, he's made several appearances in various Play'n GO creations such as Aztec Idols and Pearls of India, but is undoubtedly best known as the "explorer guy" from iconic slot Book of Dead. Sporting a suit vest and red tie combo, Mr Wilde is looking slicker than ever as you will see!Unlike Wilde's other adventures, we're not taken to a historical place this time. Instead, we travel into the mind of legendary American writer H.P Lovecraft and his fictional universe Cthulhu Mythos, a place ruled by the mighty, and equally feared, godlike creature Cthulhu. Tome of Madness is a cascading slot played on a 5 by 5 grid where winning combinations are formed by landing 4 or more matching symbols horizontally or vertically in a connected cluster, something that can lead to consecutive wins from each spin as winning symbols are removed and replaced by new ones. The main attraction here is the Portal Effects feature which adds Special Wilds while also offering you a chance to trigger additional features. You can play Tome of Madness on desktop computers, mobile devices and tablets from 10 cents to 100€ per spin.Set inside a dark forgotten hall, you'll see Mr Wilde confidently standing to the right, holding the ancient Book of Madness. Symbols on the reels include lower-value green, blue, red, and purple stones with alien writings on them. More rewarding are the  Cthulhu skulls, rings, daggers and octopus pendants, the latter being the most valuable giving you 100 times your stake for a cluster of 10+ symbols. Keep an eye on the Portal Meter to the left of the grid as every win cascade contributes to charging the meter.There are 3 different wilds on offer here to help you on your way. First you have the book which acts as the standard wild symbol. Then you have a x2 multiplier wild represented by Rich Wilde himself. Finally, the alien-like octopus creature is the Mega Wild which can only appear in the bonus round.Tome of Madness (Play'n GO): FeaturesDuring gameplay, you'll see special positions appear randomly known as Eye Marks. If you land winning combinations on these tiles, 2 Special Wilds will be added on your next losing cascade.Similar to most other grid games developed by Play'n GO the excitement builds up as you gradually fill the meter, something that will trigger modifier extras as well as various features. A losing spin/cascade, however, will revert the meter back to zero. The Portal Meter awards extras and features accordingly:7 symbols: 2 Special Wilds are awarded and added to the grid.14 symbols: 2 Special Wilds are awarded and added to the grid. If a winning combination is created with any Special Wild at this stage, the Abyss Portal Effect feature is activated.27 symbols: 2 Special Wilds are awarded and added to the grid. If a winning combination is created with any Special Wild at this stage, the Void Portal Effect feature is activated.42 symbols: Reaching this stage will trigger the Other World Free Round feature.In the Abyss Portal Effect feature, a column or row will be removed from the winning Special Wild symbol with cleared symbols adding to the Portal Meter. If the Void Portal Effect feature is triggered, the Void will choose 1 regular symbol at random and clear all instances of that symbol from the grid.Filling the meter with 42 symbols triggers the Other Wold Free Round where you're awarded 1 free round with 3 random Portal Effects. Now, over-charging the Portal Meter will give you an additional Portal Effect for every 3 winning symbols collected (but no more than 7 Portal Effects). During the feature, a Portal Effect is activated when no wins are created following a cascade - these are:Special Wilds: 4 Special Wilds are awarded and added to the grid.Abyss: 4 Special Wilds are awarded and added to the grid. If a winning combination is created with any Special Wild, the Abyss Portal Effect feature is activated.Void: 4 Special Wilds are awarded and added to the grid. If a winning combination is created with any Special Wild, the Void Portal Effect feature is activated.In similar style to Reactoonz (Play'n GO) and its Gargantoon feature, you can benefit from a Mega Wild here as well. During the bonus round, 11 or 12 Eye Mark positions appear in view. If you manage to open all eyes, which is achieved by forming wins on all eye positions, the Mega Wild Cthulhu symbol is added to the grid. It will then move down with each cascade before falling out of view, helping you create bigger wins.Tome of Madness (Play'n GO): VerdictAs is the case with most of these cascading grid slots from Play'n GO, trying to explain them in writing is far more confusing than actually playing them hands on. Title: Rise of Cleopatra

Title: Lucky Leprechaun Clusters
review: Lucky Leprechaun Clusters: Slot OverviewLike the alpha crocodile at a water hole that only needs to feed once in a year comes iconic developer Microgaming with a slot built in-house titled Lucky Leprechaun Clusters. A wheel is spun a certain number of times, moving players along the trail. Make it all the way to the end, where a pot at the end of a rainbow contains a top 1,500x prize.Lucky Leprechaun Clusters: Slot VerdictLucky Leprechaun Clusters is jaunty, leprechaun-y, possesses pleasant visuals and a cracking Celtic tune. Players into older looking Irish slots would do well to consider having a wee jig with Lucky Leprechaun Clusters then. A Rainbow Riches vibe permeates every single one of Lucky Leprechaun Clusters' pores, so if you have a soft spot for that series, then this should be right up your rainbow. Of course, the corollary is true too, though, so if you think that sort of game should have hung up its boots years ago, then nothing Lucky Leprechaun Clusters says or does will make you change your mind.On to the gameplay, and if the aesthetics haven't won you over, then it's unlikely the features will either. They're a tad predictable, not necessarily in a bad way, but don't come to Lucky Leprechaun Clusters looking for trailblazing imagination. The modifiers released when the right number of winning symbols have been released are okay, nothing special, mainly involving adding wilds or removing existing symbols for second chance cascades. The Lucky Coin modifier can be surprisingly effective should enough coin symbols land in the right places.That just leaves the Trail of Fortune, which will probably be just as divisive. The bonus round isn't really as intense as some fevered pitch feature-filled free spins session, yet a Trail was included in the original game, so it kind of had to be jammed in here somewhere. In saying so, though, the original slot managed to squeeze free spins in as well, just saying. This just leaves potential, and at 4,600x the bet, it's pretty decent, nothing amazing, but on the same level as the Reactoonz range, for comparison, so no complaints.Lucky Leprechaun Clusters is a kind of a strange release. Microgaming isn't exactly slinging slots off the production line in great numbers, more often parcelling out jobs to their partners instead. So why did they choose to do this then? Hard to say. Perhaps it was a personal pet project done for the lols. Like some banker that's amassed a fortune greater than they'll ever be able to spend and can now step out of the rat race to do something they're passionate about like fishing, golf, or découpage. The question is whether Lucky Leprechaun Clusters will better suit old-school leaning players who are looking to branch out or modern gamers pining for something retro? Maybe both, maybe neither.

Title: Yum Yum Powerways

Title: Pearls of Gold

Starting with x6 gives you x6, x7, x8, x9, and x10. Bear in mind the multiplier applies to Pearls of Gold prizes as well. Lastly, each scatter landing in the bonus round adds an extra free spin to the remaining amount.Pearls of Gold: Slot VerdictWe banged on a bit about Pearls of Gold's imitation status, but Stakelogic has made a slot that should intrigue fans of 9 Masks style of gaming. It is close, but the intricate layering of features, the way it both does and doesn't function exactly the same way, offers something of a unique experience for this style of game. The changes are quite technical, though, and work in ways that could potentially turn off as many players as it excites.One addition that's hard to knock is the avalanches/multiplier meter feature. The chopping and changing of gameplay elements does have a 'six of one, half a dozen of the other feel, though. Still, in the end, players looking for a 9 Masks of Fire alternative, Pearls of Gold should offer enough to tempt a spin or two.

Title: Cubes 2

If that sounds a little gimmicky, be assured the gameplay can be deceptively compelling.As we're becoming increasingly accustomed to the unique style of Hacksaw Gaming, the stripped down, retro-feel look of Cubes 2 doesn't stand out all that much at first sight, where its rather plain 5x5 grid made up of multi-coloured blocks fronts an equally plain background. Looks aren't everything though, and Hacksaw has a real talent for squeezing as much as possible out of a few minimal elements. The first change is the 'X' has been moved from the middle position to the outer four corners. As before though, 'X' symbols trigger a couple of features when used in a win.Cubes 2 - free spinsPocketz games, as they are referred to by Hacksaw, are designed with mobile users in mind, so the grid is pretty much all you see on a smartphone. Playing Cubes 2 on a larger-screen doesn't expand the visual experience much, except during bonus games, when a new 3D animation has been added. Don't expect anything fancy though, as the focus remains almost entirely on getting cube symbols to perform.As alluded to, Cubes 2 is playable on any device, allowing bets from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. As part of the transition from casual gaming to a high powered gambling machine, volatility has been cranked from medium to a high setting, rated 5 out of 5. The RTP configuration has ever so slightly dropped from 96.35% to 96.33%. Strangely, instead of increasing RTP, as is typically the case, the bonus buy option offers a lower configuration at 96.30%. Whether this has to do with the volatility of the feature or not is up to anyone's guess.As for the paytable, it's taken up by six plain square tiles, and that's it - there are no scatters or wilds around here. Each symbol possesses the same values from 0.10x for five of a kind up to 40x for clusters made up of 25+ similarly coloured symbols.Cubes 2: Slot FeaturesCubes 2 does everything the original did, it just does a whole lot more of it. Fundamentally, the goal is to connect at least five matching symbols of the same colour anywhere on the grid. If a winning combination hits (which has a frequency of 15.68%), the game area grows 1 cube in every direction, creating a 7x7 sized grid. Expansions occur on consecutive hits until the grid reaches a maximum of 11x11 in size. When no new wins form, the grid is restored to its default 5x5 size for the next spin.Corner multipliers are up next. If a winning cluster is formed containing one of the cubes marked with an 'X', the 'X' transforms into the number of symbols in the winning cluster. The final win is then multiplied by this number. If the winning cluster connects with more than one 'X', the multipliers are added together before being applied.The free spins feature in Cubes 2 is triggered when 5 cluster wins made up of different colours occurs in a spin sequence - 5 free spins are initially awarded and before starting, several cubes appear on the screen for players to click. The revealed numbers add free spins until your designated colour comes up, at which point the picking game is over and free spins commence. During the feature, any wins made of the chosen colour become sticky. Also, the grid does not reset between spins, so if you make it to the max configuration of 11x11, the grid stays at that size. What also makes free spins stand out is the Color Blast feature; if 50, 70, or 90 sticky blocks of the chosen colour are on the grid, an instant prize of 500x, 2,500x, or 7,000x the bet is awarded.The second bonus game is Multi Color free spins, triggered when all corners of the grid are the same colour on the initial spin. Again, players pick cubes before the feature starts to determine the number of free spins and the block colours that will be sticky. The rules of this round are the same as the previous bonus game, except the Color Blast does not appear.One last addition sure to delight some fans of Cubes is the feature buy. There are 2 options here; one is Multi Color free spins costing 109x the bet, and the other is free spins which sets you back 129x the total stake. Alternatively, hitting a bonus organically happens once in 223 spins on average.Cubes 2: Slot VerdictCubes is one of those games you might not think was ripe for a sequel, but once you've played part 2 the decision is obvious in hindsight. Hacksaw has wisely left in or fine-tuned everything which made part one so playable, while adding a few extras to make the sequel a much stronger game. Cubes already felt like playing a fun betting version of Tetris (even more so than the actual Tetris slot), yet Cubes 2 takes the experience next-level.Players who liked the look and feel of Cubes but were turned off by its medium volatility or so-so potential, would do well to check this one out. Cubes 2 goes a long way to redressing any shortfalls. The math model certainly packs additional punch, making it possible to win a much larger pile of coins this time around - 7,500x in Multi-Color free spins, or 11,000x in free spins.Gameplay-wise, the highlight is building a big sticky cluster early in a bonus round while banking a bunch of repeat wins off it. Getting on a solid roll in this way makes the game real hard to put down. This is especially so if you also score a Color Blast reward in the process, which occurred a couple of times during testing.It doesn't take long for the differences between the two Cubes slots to become apparent. Looks might not have changed much, but Cubes 2 is an upgrade in every other respect, making it a much more potent game than the first. Cubes one still has its place on the morning commute, but for an extra dose of lethality, Cubes 2 is a bigger game in every regard.

High Voltage was a slot that slapped from start to finish. Title: Jingle Spin

Title: Drago - Jewels of Fortune

Title: Lucky Neko Gigablox
review: Lucky Neko: Gigablox: OverviewSwedish developer Yggdrasil Gaming reveals the second of their two hot new features in the Asian themed slot Lucky Neko Gigablox. The other, Splitz, offered tiles that could literally split into several symbols to squeeze more out of individual paylines. The reels are located in a quaint shop full of Japanese objet d’art that shakes as the massive Daruma symbols rumble through. A peaceful traditional Asian tune tinkles away behind the sound effects and the effect is relaxing, harmonious even. Perhaps Yggdrasil Gaming pulled in a Feng Shui expert to arrange things just so?During the base game, there are 40 paylines in play on which winners of three or more matching symbols can land. Bets start at the low roller friendly sum of 8 p/c per spin and can be raised to $/€100 for those with larger requirements. Yggdrasil is helpful as ever when it comes to numbers which start with a solid RTP of 96.4%. The hit frequency, on the other hand, is a little lower than usual on 15.45%, though volatility heads in the opposite direction with a medium/high setting.So no issues behind the scenes. In front of them, players get 8 regular pay symbols to contend with. Half are card suit icons - spades, clubs, hearts and diamonds that have been designed like miniature screens. The high pays are the Darumas mentioned above and come in four different colours – purple, green, yellow and pink. The pink one offers the best value at 8x the stake for 6 of a kind, down to 10x for the purple Daruma. The final symbol in this section is the golden wild which can substitute for any pay symbol to form a winning combination. From here it is on to the reel shaking features.Lucky Neko: Gigablox: FeaturesLucky Neko Gigablox free spins featureSince Lucky Neko is the debut outing for Yggdrasil’s new Gigablox feature, it makes sense to start there. It is vaguely similar to Splitz in that it involves multiple symbols in one. How it works is that at least one set of synced reels appears on every spin to create big blocks of symbols. On synced reels, Gigablox can land in 2x2, 3x3, or 4x4 sizes, and there can be more than one synced reel on each spin.The next feature transforms almost every part of the game. This is a round of Free Spins which is triggered when at least 5 scatter symbols land in view anywhere on the reels. The actual amount of scatters in view equals the number of free spins that are awarded. The game undergoes quite a change during free spins with the number of rows doubling to 8 and paylines increasing to 85.Another change is that Gigablox symbols get bigger and can land in 5x5 or 6x6 size, bringing more symbols to the table. Lastly, before free spins begin, one pay symbol is randomly selected to become the special Blessed Symbol. During free spins, the Blessed Symbol’s payout value is increased by x5, making the high paying pink Daruma worth 40x the stake for six.Lucky Neko: Gigablox: VerdictSo how did the first run with new Gigablox feature go? Well, it’s not quite a paradigm shift and we've seen Yggdrasil experiment with mega symbols in the past in their outstanding release Gem Rocks, but it is fun all the same. Compared to the more intricate Splitz mechanic, Gigablox is a bit more effective, simple and straightforward which is always nice.When a freaking enormous block drops out of nowhere to smother the grid, it’s a sweet moment. And if that happens to be the Blessed Symbol with the x5 multiplier, the adrenal gland receives a solid kick. Keep in mind too that wilds and scatters are available in Gigablox form. Solid wins can happen and as to potential, Yggdrasil Gaming state wins of up to 6,953 times your stake are possible. Not a princely sum perhaps, but respectable figure to be sure.All up, Yggdrasil Gaming deserves bonus points for creating a uniquely refined Asian slot. The appearance is gorgeous, as you expect from this particular developer, and the wee shop setting is warm and cosy. The theme has been put to excellent use and the appearance of Darumas is a nice change. After playing Lucky Neko you kind of feel like you have experienced something new, seen a different side to the Far East. Lucky Neko goes to show that you can develop a fun, lucrative slot set in Asia without a dragon or Caishen in sight.

If there weren't so many alternatives available, or Max Win Gaming picked something other than bass for a change, Sea Boat Adventure might have made a greater impression. Still, it should do enough to avoid being chucked straight back into the sea by fishing fans.

Title: Polar Paws
review: Polar Paws (Quickspin): OverviewWith the arrival of Christmas, slot players can expect two things - casinos littering your mail client with promos, and a barrage of cloned Christmas themed slots competing for your attention. Playing it now, it feels more like a children's game rather than a proper slot machine.There's nothing wrong with the mechanics. Built using the classic industry standard 5x3 format, the game hasn't gone completely sour, and the progression free spins bonus is just as great as we remember it. The problem is with the low payouts. New players won't know better, but for veteran gamblers, it will be as exciting as shopping at IKEA. On the positive side, it's quite a "kind" slot, so it won't ruin your Christmas the same way the more modern video slots with their brutally high volatility can.If you're looking for a Christmas themed slot with a bit more action, we suggest you take a look at Secrets of Christmas (NetEnt), Jingle Spin (NetEnt), Santa's Wild Ride (Microgaming), and Flowers Christmas Edition (NetEnt).

Title: Cash Express
review: Cash Express: Slot OverviewIf we said here's a Western-themed slot featuring a streak respin bonus round held on the side of an old locomotive, it wouldn't be a surprise if Relax Gaming's smash hits Money Train or Money Train 2 sprang to mind. However, Cash Express is no Money Train, though the names are comically similar. Instead, it's Stakelogic's turn to take players out West in a gunslinger filled slot, built around a scatter collection system that unlocks special Enhancer symbols which get put to use during its hold & win Cash Bonus feature.Rumbling into town like the slot it seems to be trying to emulate is a train holding the game's 5x3, 25-payline reel-set. You can't see a lot around the edges, but a wooden built, dusty road frontier town can be made out during cutscenes. There's not much more to add except it's all pretty standard stuff for the genre; guys and gals wielding pistols, a few badges, little to really distinguish Cash Express from a host of other games.Playable on any device, Cash Express also comes with Stakelogic's ubiquitous Super Stake feature. Regular bets range from 25 p/c to $/€12.50 per spin, or when Super Stake is active, 35 p/c to $/€17.50. Switching Super Stake on increases the chance of triggering the bonus game. Any way you choose to gamble; the standard RTP appears to remain the same at 95.7%, while volatility comes in at a medium-high level.The eight standard pay symbols fire off a win when at least three of them land left to right on adjacent reels from the left-hand side of the panel. Half of them are J-A card ranks worth 2x the bet for five of a kind, while the other half are four gun-toting characters worth 8-20 times your stake for a line of five. Wild sheriff badges land on any reel to substitute all symbols except train symbols and possess the same value as the highest paying premium.Cash Express: Slot FeaturesCash Express is a mix of collecting train symbols to unlock Enhancers, which can be used during the Cash Bonus feature once triggered or bought.Cash Bonus FeatureLand 6 or more train symbols in the base game to win the Cash Bonus feature and 3 respins. Here, train symbols either contain no value, or they contain multiplier values. When symbols land, they fall to the lowest possible position, whilst also resetting the number of spins back to 3. Now, filling the bottom row with 5 symbols awards any respective multipliers and removes them from the grid. The remaining symbols drop to the lowest space on their reels; then, the remaining spins are set to 3. When spins run out, the total collected multiplier is applied to the stake and awarded.Cash Bonus EnhancersWhen train symbols land in the base game, they count as one step of progress to unlock Bonus Enhancers. You can track progress on the meters above the reels, which is saved at each stake level if you decide to change your bet. Unlocked Enhancers are held until the Cash Bonus feature triggers where they are used. When returning to the base game after free spins, the collection system resets. Each Enhancer brings its own effect to the bonus round:1st Enhancer – reveals a multiplier value of x2 to x30.2nd Enhancer – reveals a multiplier value of x2 to x50 and adds it to all others on the grid.3rd Enhancer – reveals a multiplier value of x2 to x50 and adds an extra row to the grid.4th Enhancer – reveals a multiplier value of x2 to x100 and collects all other multiplier values in view.Buy BonusWhere possible, players may have the option of buying the bonus round rather than go through the collection/triggering process. The cost is 140x the bet and unlocks random Enhancers to go with the free spins.GambleAfter any win, players can gamble the prize amount. Picking the correct colour or suit of a downturned card leads to doubling or quadrupling your winnings. However, guessing wrong means you lose the whole amount.Cash Express: Slot VerdictA bit of an odd game this one. It's like the more Stakelogic tried not to be Money Train, the closer Cash Express got. The gameplay is quite different, though, so we can't accuse Cash Express of being an outright copycat. Nor can we accuse Cash Express of being a particularly great game either. The features were rather awkward at times, detracting from the game's enjoyment, and the innovations proved to be as much of a reason not to pick Cash Express as to give it a crack.The bonus game is unusual, mainly because you have to collect symbols along the bottom row before you can accrue their multipliers. Not sure if the method will catch on over the more orthodox way of having sticky money symbols, though. A strange emotion was generated the first time the bonus round ended and there were several money symbols left on the grid, uncounted because they didn't fulfil the bottom row rule. Blue valueless train symbols often got in the way, taking up space. Others piled up on reels and didn't get used because they failed to make it to the bottom row. Cash Express was okay at times, mostly though, it felt bitsy and unwieldy.Another possible issue is the collection system. Occasionally, bonus rounds trigger before you've had the chance to unlock even one Enhancer, meaning you have to start collecting again from scratch once it's over. To bypass this, it might be tempting to just buy the feature but it's quite pricey, seeing as the Money Train bonuses can be bought for 80-100x where you don’t get all the dead train symbols or non-bottom row wastage.Cash Express is a strange duality of original elements and imitation. One part tries hard to be different, while the other clings to a wildly successful bandwagon with questionable results. Good on Stakelogic for trying something new, but Cash Express comes across a tad messy and is outclassed by more exciting hold & win styled games. There's no need to repeat names; there's a clear favourite in the category Cash Express is competing in.

Title: Genie Jackpots Even More Wishes

When 3, 6, 9, or 12 have been collected, players get +5 extra free spins at each stage, along with a multiplier of x2, x3, x5, or x10, respectively. review: Hoard of Poseidon: Slot OverviewGreek God slots are a dime a dozen, yet the lord of the deep is one of the lesser staring deities. The waterborne immortal gets a game all to himself in this collaboration between Red Tiger and partner studio R7 titled Hoard of Poseidon. The aim of the game isn't just hanging with the salty guy, but getting your hands on his rich stuff. When you weigh it all up, despite the number of ships that have gone down, there isn't quite as much rich stuff as you might expect.As usual, players get a good looking game, though Hoard of Poseidon isn't as striking as others we've seen from Red Tiger and partners recently. The action takes place on a 5 reel, 4 row grid, with about as many ways to win as there are prongs on Poseidon's trident. Okay, an exaggeration, there are actually 30 fixed paylines which clank across the board when wins light them up in typical Red Tiger fashion. The surrounds are in theme, though not outrageously so. We get a bunch of coins, some clams, and more gold in what must be the big man's cavernous digs. The graphics do the job, without inspiring major feelings either way. The same can be said for the soundtrack bubbling away in the background, not doing a whole lot.Playable from 10 p/c on the low side to $/€20 for the higher rollers, it might seem like we copy and paste the statistical information. The default RTP sits slightly on the sad side of average at 95.72% to be precise; a common occurrence from these guys. It's not outrageously low and not a deal breaker if you can find a place to play it on the default setting, though it would be nice to see the trend reverse occasionally. Volatility weighs in at a medium/high setting, so while the wild features trigger fairly regular, it's a lot more often the less lucrative ones. Even when the big hitters come out, don't expect miracles on the potential front.A bunch of heavily pixelated symbols make up the paytable, 5 low pays joined by 4 high. Seriously, taking off your specs if you're short-sighted might help bring them into focus. Symbols start with some standard 10 to A card royals, followed by a shell, a ship in a bottle, a book, and a gemmed ring. Premium values range from 2.4 to 15 times the stake for six of a kind.Hoard of Poseidon: Slot FeaturesHoard of Poseidon - Poseidon strikes featureHopefully you're into wilds because that's most of what Hoard of Poseidon has to offer. There are no bonus games or free spins to unlock, it's a lot simpler, though the wild rules have a touch of complexity about them. There are 4 wilds altogether – Chest, Kraken, Ink, and 1x2 sized Poseidon Wilds. Combinations of them trigger different effects. All can substitute for regular pay symbols, and each has the same value as the top premium.When a Poseidon + Chest Wild land on the same spin, Poseidon unleashes sea monsters which clone a random number of the Chest Wilds.A Kraken Wild at the same time as a Chest Wild locks the Chests to the reels with its tentacles. The locked Chest Wilds stay on the reels for one more spin.If a Poseidon Wild and Kraken Wild are present at the same time, the Kraken is chased away by the sea monsters, leaving a trail of Ink Wilds along the row.The most optimal is Poseidon's Plunder where Poseidon + Chest Wilds + Kraken Wilds appear. When this happens, the game runs through the 3 modifiers mentioned above. That is, sea monsters clone the chests, which are then locked by tentacles, while the sea monsters create trails of Ink Wilds in their wake. A full-on wild fest.The last feature is a random Stacking Multiplier. On any spin, a multiplier of up to x35 may appear, applying to the next line win.Hoard of Poseidon: Slot VerdictPlayers have no doubt noticed there's a distinctive look that lets you know you're on a game from Red Tiger, or partners. What is it? The UI is usually the same, and the big yellow spin button is a dead giveaway, but it's something more intrinsic. There's a quality about them which is unmistakable. A tried one - tried them all jaded feeling after you've played a few that is hard to shake off. For the sake of a balanced review, let's try our best to do so.Well, Hoard of Poseidon is alright, it has moments. It's hard to get too excited about it though. Different wilds occasionally come together for an okay win. They pop up often enough to make things interesting for a while too. Since there are no free spins, you end up hanging on just to see what Poseidon's Plunder will do. Once you have, the game deflates, there's nothing else to stick around for - certainly not mega payouts.The game can crack wins of up to 3,423 times the bet, but it's hard to see it happening any time soon. Full screen wins top out at 450x, so you'll need to be extraordinarily lucky, landing that in conjunction with a big Stacking Multiplier to boost the win. While it is nice to know Hoard of Poseidon can technically come raging together, most of the time you're one arm doggy paddling in the same spot.Hoard of Poseidon feels like another forgettable Red Tiger collaboration. It looks okay; the wild combos are interesting, but it lacks a knockout feature to give it longevity. Unless you're mad for wilds or calamari, there are stronger options in the Greek God category.

Title: Dreadworks
review: Dreadworks: Slot OverviewAmongst an industry flooded with fruit, jokers, and candy, the creative crew at Print Studios has the distinction of designing one of the more genuinely terrifying slots gamblers have the pleasure (or the repugnance) to put themselves through. The game was Darkness, and when one of the core aims of a slot is to summon Lucifer, you know you're about as far away from fruit, jokers, and candy as it gets. Whilst the studio is by no means fixated on the dark side of life, having also produced smile inducers like Pine of Plinko, the team is back on spine-chilling ground for another dimly lit borderline horror slot titled Dreadworks.Dreadworks is held in Big Jack's Toy Factory, described as 'once a place of joy, now haunted and sinister where the remnants of forgotten playthings come to life.' Big Jack's Toy Factory really isn't the sort of place you want to find yourself on a dark and stormy night. Or in the daytime, for that matter. Where once it might have churned out loveable toys for kiddies, now, about all it's going to produce are nightmares. Inhabiting the sort of place Tool might have made its older music videos, the dolls here seem more than happy plunging a rusty blade into your back if you ever had the forsaken notion of hugging one of them, Chucky style. It is dark, though an in-game darkness meter can be adjusted to set the desired level of gloom. And doom. Player reaction may depend on their personal belief system or life experiences, but Dreadworks felt closer to uncomfortably creepy rather than the terrifying defiance of natural laws on display in Darkness.Dreadworks slot - base gameRumbling vertically between rusty pipes and whatnot is Dreadworks' 5-reel game grid crossed by 26 paylines. Wins begin on the leftmost reel, and if lucky, they'll pass through a stack of active SuperSpinner multipliers. Big Jack's math model is a highly volatile one, producing different RTPs depending on how players take on the game. When default betting 10 c to $/€50 per game round, the return value maxes out at 96.08%.Dreadworks' low-pay symbols are the letters G, O, T, Y, A, followed by a spinning top, a teddy bear, and 3 doll character symbols. The rewards for hitting 5 matching low pays are 1-2 times the bet, while the highs pay 4x to 50x for 5-of-a-kind combinations. Wilds may land anywhere on the grid, substituting for everything except scatter symbols. Lines of 5 wilds pay 50x.Dreadworks: Slot FeaturesDreadworks slot - free spinsDreadworks' constituent parts include SuperSpinners, Jack-In-The-Box Wilds, a Big Jack Bonus, and Feature Bets.SuperspinnersSuperspinners are the 14 multiplier values that appear between symbols on the reels. If a winline crosses a SuperSpinner and the SuperSpinner is to the left of a winning symbol, its value multiplies the win. Multiple multipliers are independently applied to the win one by one.Jack–In-The-Box WildsJack–In-The-Box Wilds symbols substitute for all other symbols bar scatters. Where they differ from regular wilds is that they randomly distribute a displayed values to boost SuperSpinners. As part of this feature, it is also possible for multiple mystery symbols to be added to the grid, possibly triggering new wins.Big Jack BonusLanding 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols anywhere on the grid awards 5, 7, or 9 free spins, respectively, triggering the Big Jack Bonus. When winning with low-pay symbols, an extra spin is awarded, and the corresponding low-pay symbol is removed for the rest of the bonus round. Removing all low-pay symbols triggers Big Jack and grants +4 free spins. Big Jack covers 3, 4, or 5 reels for the remainder of the feature, displaying randomly chosen pay symbols of the same matching type on each spin.Feature BetThe Feature Bet is where players may activate the Scatter Boost for 1.2x the bet per spin, the Enhanced Scatter Boost for 10x the bet per spin, or buy the Big Jack Bonus for 99x the bet.Dreadworks slot - free spinsDreadworks: Slot VerdictIt goes without saying that Dreadworks won't be to all tastes. There is a reason why joyfully presented slots are so popular - people like them, they're jazzy, they're upbeat, and perhaps the finger-clicking optimism makes losing money easier to bear. But people, in general, also have a wide variety of preferences, and for those who like to experience chills down the spine while having a punt, then Dreadworks is one to try. There is apparently a link between horror, adrenaline, fight or flight, and all that, so maybe scary slots amplify the thrills?On the whole, however, Dreadworks turned out to be quite good. The base game has a double whammy of SuperSpinners and Jack–In-The-Box Wilds keeping things moving, though eyes were firmly fixed on activating the Big Jack Bonus. There are crossovers between this bonus round and the Dark Ritual Bonus, except the task of hitting Dirge Wilds in the five designated spots is replaced by winning with low-pay symbols, and the all-wild Lucifer symbol has been swapped out for the mystery symbol elements of Big Jack. Wilds tend to have more utility than mystery symbol action, but both games have win caps of 20,000x the bet, so Dreadworks' mysteries can theoretically end favourably.When looking at the bigger picture, there are quite a few crossovers in general between the two slots, meaning if Darkness floated your boat, there is a good chance Dreadworks will too. It has hints of other successful Print Studios slots, such as Royal Potato, so fans of the studio's work should be enticed by the thrills on offer in Jack–In-The-Box Wilds. The thrills might not be as terror-tinged as they were the first time around in Darkness, but they are exceptionally moodily enticing all the same.

Title: Dr Toonz
review: Dr Toonz: Slot OverviewIn life, as in fiction, there's nothing like a good back story to really flesh a character or set of characters out. We wouldn't have half the understanding of someone like Black Widow without knowledge of her training in the infamous Red Room. If we didn't know who James Howlett's real father was, who could fully grasp Wolverine's goodness, deeply buried beneath all those layers of pain. And so, we come to Dr Toonz from Play'n GO, which on the surface might appear a follow up to Reactoonz or Reactoonz 2. However, in the game world, Dr Toonz is actually a precursor and creator of the Reactoonz. So, if you ever wanted to know how those cute little characters morphed into being, Play'n GO has helpfully filled in the blanks.Dr Toonz believed that life forms could be created in new ways, and he does this on a 6-reel, 4-row game grid set up like a series of test tubes. Into these tubes, various colourful symbols appear, forming combos using a dynamic payways system, producing 4,096 to 262,144 ways to win. The scientific tinkering takes place in a modern lab that looks like it's beneath the sea, though we could be wrong, littered with various miscellaneous scientific instruments. Extra lols are provided by Dr Toonz himself, who sits next to the game grid as it bubbles away. There's a Reactoonz feel to Dr Toonz, largely due to the multitude of cheerful critters but also due to a similarly fun-loving environment.The experimentation is made possible on all devices, from smartphones to desktops, offering stakes from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. One thing to keep an eye out for is a variable RTP setting, where the most optimal is a 96.25% version. Out of the 'Toonz' range of games, Dr Toonz has a significantly higher max win figure, plus a highly volatile math model to match. Play'n GO hasn't pushed it to extreme levels, yet a rating of 8 out of 10 certainly makes Dr Toonz an unpredictable experience.Winning combinations hit in Dr Toonz when three to six matching symbols land left to right from reel number 1. This equates to 4,096 ways to win, to begin with, which quickly builds when the dynamic payways start firing. Pay symbols are divided into four one-eyed aliens as the low pays and four two-eyed aliens as the highs. Values are quite low, where six premium symbol combinations are worth 0.5 to 1 time the stake. One last symbol, for now, is the wild, landing on any reel to replace any of the pay symbols. Wilds payout, but only for a line of six which is worth 2x the bet.Dr Toonz: Slot Features﻿The features in Dr Toonz have a grid slot feel to them and perform just as effectively, if not more so, on the 6-reel game grid. Extras include cascades, three Quantumeter features, payway multipliers, and free spins.Winning combinations are removed from the reels via the cascade feature. New symbols cascade into view to fill the empty spaces, potentially forming new wins. This process repeats if new wins are continually created, stopping when no more combinations hit.On each base game spin, the Quantumeter starts at 0-2 charges. Each winning cascade charges the meter by 1, and 3 charges mean it is full. The fully charged Quantumeter activates when the cascade sequence ends, awarding 1 charge feature per spin or free spin:Quantum Wilds: adds 2 to 6 wilds in random positions on the reels.Metamorphosis: transforms 5-8 regular pay symbols into another symbol type.Disintegration: removes all one-eyed alien symbols and adds 2 wilds to the reels.Landing 3 or more double helix scatter symbols triggers the free spins feature. When 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters are in view, the reward is 10, 15, 20, or 25 free spins which cannot be retriggered. During free spins, the Quantumeter starts with 1 or 2 charges, improving the chances of triggering Quantumeter modifiers.On each spin, keep an eye above the reels, where x2 payway symbols randomly appear. If they do, they double the number of ways to win on that particular reel. Landing an x2 on each reel maxes out payways at 262,144.Dr Toonz - free spinsDr Toonz: Slot VerdictIn a similar manner to the life-creating doctor of this story, Play'n GO has brought together elements of several previous games to create the potent mix that is Dr Toonz. There's the Reactoonz connection, of course, but mainly in regards to characters and visuals, as the gameplay is very different. Dr Toonz makes a switch to reels, and while cascades and charge meters provide a snowball element, you don't get the same lengthy win sequences as in the previous grid slots.This doesn't make the game any less enjoyable, however. Dr Toonz' charge features keep the pace flowing, and combined with payway multipliers, can take the game to places Reactoonz can only dream of. Winning potential, for example, now reaches 22,000x the bet, equating to roughly 4-5 times Reactoonz 1 or 2 (though we are yet to see these big potential PnG releases live up to their stated potential it should be mentioned). A big max win figure is only part of the story, however, and Dr Toonz isn't quite as infectious as its sibling slots could be. Another possible concern is that Dr Toonz faces competition from Play'n GO's own slot Hotel Yeti-Way. The two offer similar reel formats and gameplay, yet the Yeti one comes with more features, as well as nearly 30% extra potential.However, Dr Toonz continues a slots tradition that has proven hugely popular; therefore, it oozes pedigree and name recognition. It also has the winning looks, great features and win potential to make it a worthy sequel/prequel.Don't MissIf you're a fan of the Reactoonz franchise, be sure to have a look at the Gigantoonz slot as well, which continues from where Dr. Toonz left off.

Title: Buffalo Rising Megaways All Action
review: Buffalo Rising Megaways All Action: OverviewWhat is the one thing about playing slots that can wear a person down? How about spinning endlessly, waiting for a bonus round that stubbornly refuses to drop while slowly (or quickly) draining your balance? Over time these things can even out, but a long run of base game spinning without the hint of a scatter can get tiring. Bonus buy options circumvent this first world problem by shortcutting players to the best bits. But even they have their limitations, such as jurisdictional restrictions, and in some cases exorbitant price tags. Blueprint Gaming has come up with a nifty idea that allows players to access the most exciting part of a slot without having to break the bank in the process - the result is Buffalo Rising Megaways All Action.The All Action version is a remake of the popular Buffalo Rising Megaways slot released in the later months of 2019. The original is a pretty sweet slot in its own right, and is based around the North American plains and wildlife. If you're familiar with the original, you will instantly feel at home as the new version looks identical. When it comes to the remake, it’s not so much what has been added but what it has taken away. To earn the 'All Action' in its title, Blueprint has removed the base game and turned it into a big bet slot.All of the symbols, characters, and of course, the Megaways engine has been brought back. However, despite a lot you will recognise, the difference in gameplay will be obvious to you. To gain access and get the game flowing, players must first choose a stake. Betting on the original slot maxed out at €/$10 per spin. Here, meanwhile, betting options, begin at that level and only go higher. This time around high rollers will be stoked to see max bets of €/$1,000 on offer. Select the bet that suits your bankroll and sit back and enjoy the show.In a nutshell, placing a bet buys a batch of Buffalo Spins which is basically a free spins round in the original Buffalo Rising Megaways slot. The round comes with an unlimited multiplier and runs using the regular Megaways cascade feature. This system removes winning combinations from the reels to let new symbols cascade into the gaps. That means chains of wins are possible from one single spin. It also means a setup that uses 6 main reels with 2-7 symbols on each and an extra horizontal reel along the top. Win ways can go as high as 117,649 with the reels maxed out with symbols. Along with the major rule changes, RTP has increased slightly to 97.01%, and volatility remains generally high, although the game essentially allows you to choose your own volatility.Due to the cascade wins system, symbol values are typically low(ish) on a Megaways slot as they can quickly rack up. Due to the way Buffalo Rising Megaways All Action works with an unlimited multiplier always active, symbol values are even lower than that. There are 10 regular pay symbols - 6 low and 4 high. The low pays are 9-A royals, while high pays in ascending order are a moose, coyote, bear, and buffalo. The buffalo only needs two of a kind to pay out while all of the others need 3 or more. To give you a clear picture of rewards we’ll use the minimum stake of 10 credits as an example. At this level 3 ‘9s’ are worth 1p/c while 6 buffalos payout $/€5. It sounds low at first, but the wins can quickly add up due to the way the rules operate. Helping with the win rate is a wild which can substitute for anything except the scatter. Also, there are Mystery Symbols, and when they land they all transform into common symbols which can be anything but the scatter.Buffalo Rising Megaways All Action: FeaturesGameplayOnce the bet has been set in motion, players are presented with 4 options of varying volatility. These options are as follows:15 Buffalo Spins which start with a x1 multiplier (lowest risk).10 Buffalo Spins which start with a x5 multiplier (medium risk).5 Buffalo Spins which start with a x10 multiplier (high risk).The fourth option is the Mystery Choice. Here, players choose a blind batch of slots and a blind multiplier. The results come from the options above, so you could end up with 15 spins with a x10 multiplier, for example. Or, you could just as easily end up with 5 spins with the x1 multiplier. It is the total luck of the draw.During the round, the multiplier increases by +1 with each cascade. Spins can also be extended thanks to the diamond scatter symbol - land 3 or 4 of these and you will be rewarded with an additional 5 or 10 spins respectively. Considering that can effectively double the duration of the game, then they are like gold dust.Once the spins have been used, that game is over, like, totally over – there is no base game to go back to. To play again, players need to make another bet and choose how many spins they want to start with.Buffalo Rising Megaways All Action: VerdictBuffalo Rising Megaways All Action is a unique and clever slot, and what it does will probably appeal to a significant number of players. Initially, a minimum of 10 credits to play might seem high. Then again, how easy is it to burn through that amount without triggering the bonus feature? There are merits and disadvantages for having a base game or removing at as Blueprint has done. Games are shorter and more intense, that’s for sure. Not only that, but this approach can be more economical than piling on a batch of auto spins and hoping for the best. Or, it might not, and many players will balk at fronting a big bet for entry. It’s not the best option for stretching out a bankroll, but that isn’t the game’s aim at all. Many, especially high rollers, will appreciate making a big bet to play what is effectively a bonus round.Yes, it may seem like an obvious attempt to bypass the recent regulatory changes and the UK feature buy ban, but one could argue it's no difference to placing massive bets on Roulette. In any case, our job is not to pass judgement whether big bet slots are right or wrong, we'll leave that part to our readers.As to the game, yeah it was quite exciting to play using this new set of rules. There were no base game lulls to wait out, and each round offered some pretty intense moments. How certain regulators are going to judge what this game has to offer will be an interesting question to ponder. Until that matter comes up, no, not everyone will go for this format, but those that do will be all over it.

Title: King's Mask
review: King's Mask: Slot OverviewUp alongside Zorro or Darth Vader, Tutankhamun's mask must be one of the most famous in history. It was discovered in 1925 in Howard Carter's famous dig and now sits in the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, where it dazzles onlookers thousands of years after it was made. Pretty nifty when you think about it, and according to software provider Play'n GO, the mask gives those who possess it the key to King Tut's riches. At least it does in their online slot; the Egyptian themed King's Mask, a straightforward slot that focuses on delivering multipliers and free spins.King's Mask opens rather splendidly, displaying an indoor bathing area surrounded by columns, statues, a pyramidal structure, and stacks of gold coins just casually lying around. You only get a glimpse of the sumptuous scene, though, before the game grid pops on screen. It looks a bit like Eye of Atum in all its simplicity, but then again, a lot of these Egyptian slots from Play'n GO have a similar appearance, at times blending into one another. They are fairly attractive most of them, though, if a little dime a dozen, and a sultry Egyptian tune caps the experience off.The gaming is held on a panel made up of 5-reels, 3-rows and 20 static paylines. All wins pay left to right except scatter wins and all pay symbols except the two most valuable and the least valuable need at least three to do so. These special three symbols payout for two of a kind for some reason. A medium volatile slot, King's Masks' return to player tops out at 96.28%, while players can select stakes from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin.Paytable time, and here we come across 11 regular symbols in total, split between 6 lower value 9-A royals, worth 5 to 6.25x the bet and five higher value tiles. Premiums consist of five recognisable symbols of Ancient Egypt, paying 12.5 to 37.5 times the stake for five of a kind - decent values, which can be boosted by two different multiplying elements.King's Mask: Slot FeaturesThere might not be a long list of features in King's Mask, but they are the kind that can deliver a solid gut punch if and when they ignite. Instrumental in creating King's Mask's exciting moments is the wild symbol, which lands on any reel. Wilds not only substitute for any normal pay symbols but they are also worth up to 500x the bet for a line of five. What's more is that, when wilds are used in a payline, they multiply it by x2.Free SpinsAnother pyramidal shape you'll want to see in King's Mask is the game's scatter symbol. This one also lands in any reel, and when 3, 4, or 5 are in view, players collect 5x, 20x, or 100x their bet, plus access to free spins. Once the bonus round has been activated, there are three options to choose from. These are 15 free spins with an x3 win multiplier, 10 free spins with an x5 multiplier, or 5 free spins with an x10 win multiplier.King's Mask: Slot VerdictIf a studio has mass-market saturation in mind, then releasing slots like King's Mask is one way of going about it. In a vacuum, the game isn't bad at all. It looks alright, is thoroughly Egyptian, offers basic yet highly effective features, and squeezes out a few enviable numbers. If anyone else had crafted King's Mask, it might have been easier to be less critical. But they didn't, and there's a slight feeling Play'n GO phoned this one in. It brought to mind an actor who's over the whole acting thing but goes through the motions to collect a paycheck at the end of a shoot – who may or may not have even learned their lines. Play'n GO has been around the Egyptian block enough times to fire these off in their sleep, which it kind of seems like they've done.On the other hand, it feels harsh to say this about what is solid as you like it Egyptian gaming. The features, while basic, can turn out strong results; simply by virtue of all the multipliers it is possible to pull on board. Mix a multiplier wild with a big win multiplier in free spins, and line wins can be quite impressive. As is the game's max win figure of 10,000x the bet. It's hard to shake the feeling that established developers like Microgaming were releasing this sort of thing back in the day. Perhaps, players pining for an earlier online gambling age will be thrilled to find it in such a handsomely exotic package.So many conflicting pros and cons made King's Mask a tough game to review. There's no denying how professionally designed everything is, the extras are far from being elaborate, yet they can go ballistic, and the stats are steady as a rock. Then again, King's Masks looks and feels like a number of PnG games and ultimately lacks major x-factor, no matter how much golden splendour might be on the screen. It was difficult to stop the mind from seesawing between these two impressions. Anyway, when all is said and done, King's Mask is a well-made game for Egyptian fans, but one that is unlikely to really stay with you long term once it's done. Not to worry, though, there is bound to be another one along soon enough.

Title: Eye of Cleopatra
review: Eye of Cleopatra: Slot OverviewWhen you think about it, the iGaming world's obsession with Cleopatra is kind of odd. The ancient Egyptian ruler must be one of the most popularly used characters in slots, and it made us wonder how exactly we got here. Of all the billions of people who have walked the earth since records began, why Cleopatra? There is a direct association between her and Ancient Egyptian slots in general, of course, but still. Anyway, developers' main queen returns in a slot called Eye of Cleopatra from Pragmatic Play. Before 'book of' fanatics reach into their wallets, we're going to have to stop them right there. Eye of Cleopatra does not feature expanding special symbols at any point. Instead, what it does have is a spreading wild feature, governed by a wild pattern device, to provide the main thrills.Eye of Cleopatra is played on a 5-reel, 4-row game panel, which sits to the left side of the screen, while the pattern device rests on the right. In the disused space, Pragmatic Play has squeezed in old school Egyptian columned structures. Yes, it is Egyptian-y looking, as is the soundtrack. There's nothing hugely out of the ordinary, but the sensory load is aggregable enough.The math model Eye of Cleopatra runs on is as reliable from this developer as the theme, really. That's not a bad thing since Pragmatic Play is pretty liberal when it comes to the return to player figure. The default RTP, at least, is solid at 96.5%, though Eye of Cleopatra can be found at 95.5% or 94.5% tiers, so be on the lookout. Volatility is high, and stakes vary from 20 p/c to $/€100 – available on any device.To start collecting coins, players must land at least three identical symbols across any of the 40 fixed paylines, starting from the leftmost side. Nine pay symbols, divided into four low pay and five high pays have been used. Lows are J-A royals, paying 0.25x to 1x the bet for five of a kind, whereas the highs are snakes, cats, birds, Pharaohs, and Cleopatras worth 1.25x to 10x your stake for a five symbol win line. Wilds are one of the most instrumental parts of Eye of Cleopatra, landing in any position to replace anything except the scarab scatter.Eye of Cleopatra: Slot FeaturesEye of Cleopatra packs a feature called random wild patterns, which intermittently appears in the base game and on each free spin when triggered.Random Wild PatternsOn the right-hand side of the screen sits a device with a golden inner circle, surrounded by 8 outer positions. The inner-circle represents wild symbols. On any spin, outer positions on the device may randomly light up blue. If this happens when there are wild symbols on the reels, the respective symbols adjacent to them are transformed into wilds. For example, if all outer positions on the device turn blue, each adjacent to the wilds in view turn wild. Wins are evaluated after any transformations have taken place.Free SpinsHitting 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols anywhere on the screen activates the free spins feature. Before the round begins, players choose one of these four possible options:4 light patterns – 10, 20, or 30 free spins awarded for a landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters.6 light patterns – 8, 16, or 24 free spins awarded for a landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters.8 light patterns – 6, 12, or 18 free spins awarded for a landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters.A random number of spins and light patterns is awarded from the above options.During free spins, the chosen light pattern is active on every game round. Elongating the bonus is possible when at least 3 scatters land, thereby retriggering the same number of free spins as were initially awarded.Ante BetThe Ante Bet lets users increase their stake by 25% to double the chance of winning free spins. With the Ante Bet switched on, RTP remains the same at 96.5%.Eye of Cleopatra: Slot VerdictAs long as users aren't put off by the prospect of heading back to Ancient Egypt one more time, there are fine moments to be had in Eye of Cleopatra. There are no qualms with the game's presentation, however trite. Pragmatic Play has a way with pixel placement, and Eye of Cleopatra is as vibrant as most in this category of slot are.So Egyptian enthusiasts should be down with the looks and sounds, how about the gameplay? There were mixed impressions, overall positive, though while the random wild pattern feature is intriguing and can create pleasing results, it did feel like something was missing. As if the feature on its own was a little too one dimensional to really carry a game. That's too bad because random wild patterns is all Eye of Cleopatra really has going for it. As such, once we'd seen it do its thing a few times in the base game, ploughed through the eight-light pattern bonus round, we were pretty much done.Maybe if Eye of Cleopatra had a secondary feature supplementing the wild pattern, it might have extended the game's shelf life. What would have boosted the effect, though? Throw in the towel and add some sort of Book of Ra inspired expanding symbol element? Title: Adventures Of Doubloon Island
review: Adventures of Doubloon Island: Slot OverviewFollowing on from Assassin Moon, a secret agent game possessing several similar features, comes this pirate-themed slot from Microgaming partner Triple Edge Studios titled Adventures of Doubloon Island. The headliner remains the trademarked HyperHold mechanic, which, for whatever reason, has been tweaked to offer even lower benefits this time around. Played using 5x3 layout along with 20 paylines to land winners on, the reels are set against what looks like blank parchment, as if a map is yet to be drawn. The screen isn’t as cluttered as Assassin Moon, nor does it dive as deeply into the theme. The view here is pretty, though not as unique or as richly atmospheric as Assassin Moon where your imagination could more easily run wild through its world of espionage. Pirating games are common, so while pretty, Adventures of Doubloon Island is the less intriguing slot.Above the reels, four fixed jackpots display their values, which adjust according to bet size and whether the Win Booster has been activated – doing so increases the bet. Five of a kind is what you want where premium values range from 10 to 20 times your stake. The lady buccaneer is a wild, appearing in 1x1, 1x2, or 1x3 sizes on any reel. Five of a kind are worth 50x the bet, which, if you’ve played Assassin Moon, is a massive reduction from 12,500x for a full screen, down to 1,000x.Adventures of Doubloon Island: Slot FeaturesAdventures of Doubloon Island - free spinsWhile the features are similar as before, they have been toned down, making Adventures of Doubloon Island a less enticing proposal from a ‘win big’ standpoint. Thrills peak during the HyperHold feature, accompanied by free spins and the Win Booster.The Win Booster is an optional function that increases the bet by 1.5x when activated. Doing so does not alter line wins, but it does boost the value of wins during the HyperHold feature. Cash prizes are increased by 3 times, and jackpots receive a 2-2.5x boost. Win Booster can be switched on or off at any time in the base game.Landing 6 or more HyperHold symbols on the reels trigger the HyperHold feature. With 3 spins awarded, the triggering symbols are now held in position. Whenever new HyperHold symbols land, the spins are reset. The feature ends when either all positions are filled, or spins run to zero. In either case, the symbols in view then reveal a cash prize of 1-50x the bet if the Win Booster is off, or 2-100x the total bet if it is.Symbols may also reveal one of the four jackpots. The Mini, Minor, Major, or Mega awards 25x, 100x, 500x, or 2,000x the bet with Win Booster off, or 33.33x, 133.33x, 666.67x, or 3,333.33x the total bet when the Win Booster is activated.One final feature is free spins, triggered when 3, 4, or 5 scatters land to award 10, 15, or 20 free spins. The benefit here is that all low pay symbols are removed from the reels, allowing only premiums to land. It is possible to retrigger the round, as 3, 4, or 5 scatters top you up with 10, 15, or 20 more free spins.Adventures of Doubloon Island: Slot VerdictAt a glance, Adventures of Doubloon Island appears quite similar to Assassin Moon. HyperHold remains the core feature, four jackpots line the top of the reels, and you get a bunch of free spins to accompany them. Scratch slightly deeper, where you find the differences are quite stark, making Adventures of Doubloon Island a very different game altogether.Initially, this is via the theme, which is personal, but it wasn’t as easy to go with the flow and lose yourself in Adventures of Doubloon Island like it was in Assassin Moon. Slots are awash in pirating themed games, so the initial grab wasn’t so pronounced despite having an attractive look. As such, Doubloon Island needs to work harder to differentiate itself, and here it falls a little short. Perhaps if its stats were more impressive it might have done so, yet they have been cranked back from Assassin Moon. Gone are the huge full-screen wild wins, and even the jackpots are less. It all adds up to a less tempting game all around.If sailing the seven seas, plundering merchant ships, or raiding settlements isn’t your bag, there isn’t much point in having a crack with Adventures of Doubloon Island. Even then, once the ‘arr me hearties’ thing has worn off, lower potential means there is little left over to stick around for.

Title: Super X
review: Super X: Slot OverviewDeveloper Pragmatic Play follows up on an earlier slot called Super 7, with a souped-up version titled Super X. The names are related, and there's a jazzy vibe, but really, the two games offer completely distinct gambling experiences. Super X is based around a bet multiplier building feature that is rather unique and available via free spins or respins. The game is also another to offer Pragmatic Play's handle with care Super Spin Ante Bet feature. Engaging it thrusts players right into the heart of the action, making every single spin like a bonus spin, though one with a hefty price tag attached.Super X has a slightly ambiguous theme, based around gold, money, crowns, casino chips, that sort of thing. Everything is more or less tied to wealth and its (hopefully) acquisition. Pragmatic Play defines the visuals as 'punchy', which is as good a word as any to describe the bright, gold coin littered screen. The game is not as easy to pigeonhole as the fruity filled Super 7 was, neither in looks nor in terms of features.Played on a 5-reel, 3-row game grid, the base game provides players with 20 fixed paylines to land regular winning combinations on. Volatility has been increased from the 3.5/5 rating of Super 7 to the 5 out of 5 rating of Super X. This serves as an indicator to expect bigger and better things this time around in all regards. RTP included, which is up a smidgen to 96.51% when playing in the normal mode, dropping to 96.48% when the Ante Bet is on. Keep in mind though, RTP can be lower depending on where you play.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, Super X makes use of red, purple, green, and blue poker chips as the low pays, followed by gold coins, dollar bills, gold bars, diamonds, and crowns as the high pays. Hit a five of a kind combination of premium symbols gets you a payout worth 2.5 to 20 times your stake. Finally, crystal star wilds appear on reels 2, 3, or 4 to substitute for all symbols except the scatter.Super X: Slot FeaturesThere are several ways of potentially maximising returns when playing Super X. These are through the X Bet Respins feature, free spins, and the Super Spin Ante Bet.X Bet Respin FeatureThe 'X' symbol appears only on the first reel. Whenever an X hits, then a respin is triggered. The triggering X symbols are held in place for the feature, while all other symbols fade out of view. On the respin, only blank symbols or digits 0-9 may land on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5. After the spin, each row that contains an X forms a bet multiplier made up of the following numbers. For example, say an X lands on row 2 next to the numbers 1 and 0 on the same row - this creates a reward of 10x the bet. All created multiplier rewards on different rows are added at the end of the respin then awarded.Free SpinsHitting 3 golden dice scatter symbols triggers the bonus round and awards 5 free spins. The free spins feature is played only with X symbols, blanks, and digit symbols the same way respins are. For the duration of free spins, all 3 positions on reel 1 have X symbols, while blanks or digits may land on the other reels to build bet multiplier values. If a spin occurs where only blank symbols land on reels 2-5, then +3 additional free spins are awarded.Super Spin Ante BetIn the base game, players can activate the Super Spin Ante Bet, which increases the cost of every spin by 10x. When the ante bet is on, each spin is played like a respin where only X, blanks, or digits appear.Super X: Slot VerdictWhile Super X officially follows on from Super 7, the two games are very different in terms of gameplay and maths. Super 7 is by far the simpler of the two, a straightforward fruit slot that climaxes in hitting instant scatter prizes or five '7' symbols for the fabled 1,000x win. Super X, by contrast, bears little resemblance. This one doesn't even have fruit in it; not even a humble pair of cherries are in sight. Players who enjoyed Super 7 should brace for a totally different experience should they fire up Super X if they were expecting a comparable slot.Super X is easily the brawnier game, packing a more volatile math model and much larger potential rewards to match. It also serves everything up in an unusual way, and some may well be drawn to the fast-paced multiplier building found in free spins or respins. There's no mucking around here during these features. Players are tossed right in to start accruing multipliers – or not.The pace can be quickened further for players with the constitution for the Ante Bet feature. We saw the device used recently in Book of Fallen, so the same pros and cons apply. Sure, the Ante Bet potentially gets you to the most thrilling parts quick smart, yet at 10x the bet, it can also empty pockets just as swiftly, if not more. Ante Bet is optional, though, so if it doesn't suit, players can minimise the screen and scroll right to avoid the temptation. As to max win, payouts are capped at 9,000x the bet – nine times Super 7, and with an attractive probability of being struck, it might be added.For players after a punchy looking slot, with an even punchier set of features, Super X might be the ticket. Super X is not a game you really play to enjoy the scenery; rather something players can cut to the chase in if they so choose to try their luck.

Title: Book of Ultimate Infinity
review: Book of Ultimate Infinity: Slot OverviewNext to have a shot with ReelPlay’s Infinity Reels mechanic is SG Digital in Egyptian themed slot Book of Ultimate Infinity. Proving to be a bit of a money-spinner for ReelPlay, SG Digital is the third developer to license the mechanic so far and have decided to incorporate a bit of an old school twist to it all. Alongside the modern dynamic is a bonus game replete with full reel expanding symbols chosen out of a dusty old tome. This is 'Book of' gaming in a modern setting, so, does it work?We might have used the word 'modern', yet the backdrop is thoroughly ancient. There’s sort of no choice when using this theme where pyramids sit on the horizon, joined by the Nile, palm trees, and temples - the classic Ancient Egypt look. Clouds drift lazily across the sky, while an Arabian inspired soundtrack make it all come together. It’s brightly appealing, though nothing you haven’t seen a dozen times before.Book of Ultimate Infinity fires up on any device where bets from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin can be set. It’s a game that requires patience to get to the good bits since triggering free spins takes perseverance to battle through a sand storm of dead spins. Its moody volatility means the game does pop at points, and overall potential isn’t bad at all. Neither is RTP on 96.5%, a figure comfortably above average.At the start of every spin 3 reels display 4 symbols on each. If at least 3 identical symbols land on reels 1, 2, and 3, another reel is added for another chance to win. This process continues as long as the rightmost reel improves the win. In a nutshell, you have the Infinity Reels system. Incidentally, reels are capped at 50, which isn’t exactly infinite, so there's that. The first time a reel is added, a win multiplier of x2 is awarded, increasing by +1 for each subsequent new reel.A winning combination is formed when at least 5 matching symbols land from the first reel onwards. The amount you win equates to the number of symbols in the combo multiplied by the individual symbol value. At the lower end of the scale, we find J-A royals, followed by knives, Ankhs, a queen, a gold statue, and a pharaoh. The premium picture symbols are worth from 0.10 to 0.25x the bet per symbol, so a five of a kind win net 0.5 – 1.25 times the stake. Keep in mind that multipliers and extended reels do pep the values up occasionally. Also helping up the win rate is an un-Egyptian looking wild substituting all other symbols, except the Gold Book or special Expanding Symbols.Book of Ultimate Infinity: Slot FeaturesBook of Ultimate Infinity - free spins with special expanding symbolAs well as Infinity Reels, players benefit from free spins triggered by the Gold Book scatter. Triggering the bonus is a bit unconventional - at the start of every spin, a reel (from 6 to 15) is randomly selected to contain the Gold Book. If reels are added during a win sequence and reach the selected reel, 10 free spins are awarded. In other words, you will have to expand the reels to a minimum of 6 to be able to trigger the bonus.At the start of free spins, one symbol is randomly chosen as the special expanding symbol. If free spins are retriggered, the special symbol remains the same. Landing a special symbol or a book on the rightmost reel always adds another reel, regardless of whether the win is improved. Similar to regular ‘book’ slots, when 2 or more reels contain the expanding symbol they expand to cover all positions and pay whether they are consecutive or not.Book of Ultimate Infinity: Slot VerdictLike Bill Hicks might have said, just as evolution didn’t end by us growing thumbs, SG Digital shows there are still evolutionary opportunities for ‘book of’ style gaming. In one regard, Book of Ultimate Infinity shows how transferable ReelPlay’s set up is. We’ve seen vanilla versions, in-game jackpot versions, Megaways, and now a Book of Ra edition. Is the time ripe for a host of classic slot updates? With the likes of SG Digital on board, the flood gates could be blasted wide open.Book of Ultimate Infinity does suffer the same drawbacks as previous incarnations. Namely, the peripheries may differ, but the core gaming, the grind, is the same old, same old. Grind it can too, due to an abundance of dead spins, interspersed with the odd larger win. Often you get a long multi-reel win pile up alongside a hefty multiplier, yet are left wondering where the rest of the payout is after it’s been awarded. Another thing that feels strangely missing is Megaways, which showed up in the past to add a touch of randomness to a base game often verging on being tedious.One nice touch is the map expanding and contracting below the reels indicating where the triggering scatter is. The fact the scatter changes position adds a bit of tension to since you never know quite where it will be. Once triggered, Book of Ultimate Infinity starts to make more sense and separate itself from the others in the range. It’s also where players have a chance of hitting the max win which has been capped at $/€250k. Again, low symbol values hold you back since stacks of chosen symbols can easily add up to not much at all.Book of Ultimate Infinity doesn’t match the gold standards of the genre such as Book of Dead, but fans of Infinity Reels or expanding special symbols might get something out of it. All in all, SG Digital has done a good enough job of harnessing the mechanic’s capabilities with a feature not seen in them yet, making it one of the better Infinity Reels offerings in a while.Don't MissIf you want to explore more slots utilising the Infinity Reels mechanic we suggest to try out Relax Gaming's leprechaun themed offering titled Emerald's Infinity Reels. Alternatively, Red Tiger has a similar game engine known as InfiniReels with Dragon's Fire InfiniReels being a prime example.

Title: Buffalo Rising Megaways

These are available in the following formats:15 Free Spins with the Unlimited Win Multiplier starting at 1x10 Free Spins with the Unlimited Win Multiplier starting at 5x5 Free Spins with the Unlimited Win Multiplier starting at 10xMystery number of Free Spins with a Mystery Unlimited Win Multiplier starting levelDuring the Free Spins round, the Unlimited Win Multiplier will increase after every successful Reaction, with an unlimited level able to be reached.A final part of this slot game that is important to mention is the Buffalo Bonus Bet possibility.
