Title: Sevens High Ultra
review: Sevens High Ultra: Slot OverviewSevens High Ultra sees its maker Quickspin revisit and remaster a slot they released back in 2015, titled Sevens High. If you missed it, Sevens High was a glitzy, fruity, Vegas-style slot with a catchy respin feature that could turn its premium symbols wild, much like Quickspin's hit Big Bad Wolf. Sevens High Ultra keeps all these things while adding a new Ultra mode where the going might be tougher, but the potential rewards are greater.If you have played the original, you'll be happy to know Sevens High Ultra is as glitzy as ever. Yet, even more importantly, the epic soundtrack is back, floating effortlessly from ambient to house to pounding dubstep for big win count ups. Played using a 5-reel, 25-payline reelset, what's new is the 'Ultra' button which can be switched at any time in the base game. The Wild Meter is there, too, so consecutive winning respins remain a focal point. In a world overflowing with fruit slots, Sevens High Ultra manages to mix its parts in such a way to provide a uniquely entertaining experience.Switching between Ultra Mode and Classic Mode has no effect on stakes, which vary from 25 p/c to $/€100 per spin. What it does do is make the game more volatile, where Ultra is rated high (5/5) compared to the original's medium setting. The RTP is slightly different in both modes, too, Classic generating a value of 96.54% while Ultra's comes in at 96.06%. The benefit of Ultra mode is more scatters on the reels, bigger symbol values, and higher winning potential.Knocking together a win occurs when at least three matching symbols land adjacent to each other on a payline from the first reel. From bottom to top, the symbols include plums, lemons, oranges, cherries, and stars as the low pays, then bells, red 7s, green sevens, and blue sevens as the mids. Landing a five-symbol combination made up of mid pay symbols is worth 3-4x the stake in Ultra Mode or 1.6-2x in Classic. The highest paying symbols are the 7s when they have been converted into wilds, worth 100x the bet for a line of five in Ultra Mode, or 20x the bet in Classic. The standard wild is worth the same as the '7' wilds, and all wilds substitute for regular symbols to help complete winning lines.Sevens High Ultra: Slot FeaturesSevens High Ultra - free spinsSevens High Ultra uses the same set of features the original did, but Quickspin has juiced certain elements of them like they have to the volatility. Respins remain one of the key features and are where the majority of the RTP has been allocated. Any win activates the Wild Meter on the side of the screen and awards a Sevens High Respin. Respins continue to be awarded as long as consecutive wins keep hitting. In addition, every two consecutive wins turns a '7' symbol wild, maxing when all three of them have been converted. During the base game, a losing respin ends the feature and resets the Wild Meter back to its starting position.In Classic Mode, landing 3 bonus symbols pays 3x the bet and activates 10 free spins. Or, if playing in Ultra Mode, 3, 4, or 5 scatters in view awards 10, 15 or 35 free spins and results in a payout of 3x, 10x, or 500x the bet. In both game modes, landing at least 3 scatters in the bonus game retriggers free spins.When free spins are active, every two consecutive wins turns a '7' symbol wild and grants +2 free spins. What's different in the bonus round is that the Wild Meter does not reset, so activating the premium wilds early on means you've got them for the remainder of the feature.Sevens High Ultra: Slot VerdictYou can see how players with a soft spot for classic, Vegas-style games would be excited by this remake. The original isn't looking bad for a game more than half a decade old, and Sevens High Ultra is as flashy as before, more so actually, when flipping into the more volatile mode. The good news about doing so is players don't have to pay extra to switch modes; they simply pick the one that matches their mood the best. Then, as Quickspin puts it in the blurb, 'Grab a drink and a bite to eat while you put your feet up and spin the reels.' Sounds pretty alright.While the stakes stay the same, the RTP does dip slightly in Ultra mode, not that you can really notice the percentage difference. The two modes were distinctly different in action, though, performing the way they are described in the paytable. In a nutshell, that means more wins in Classic, bigger wins in Ultra. Ultra is for those who like to live a little further out on the edge where it is easier to slip but where the greater rewards can be found. The difference in value between the Wild symbols in the two modes is significant, where a full screen of them in Classic is worth 500x compared to 2,500x in Ultra Mode. It means Ultra now cranks the max win figure up to 6,768x the bet. If knowing the odds helps you pick a slot, this win occurred during 300 billion simulated spins.It is nice the game lets you slip into either mode without changing the bet, so if you are in the mood for more wins or bigger wins, flip the switch, and you're there. In either, Sevens High Ultra's atmosphere is as groovy as ever, the Wild Meter hooks you with its achievement style of play, and payouts aren't shabby either. Players who liked the old Sevens High slot or glam fruit slots, in general, are in for a treat with Sevens High Ultra.

Title: Big Bass Bonanza Megaways
review: Big Bass Bonanza Megaways: Slot OverviewBig Bass Bonanza and its younger sibling Bigger Bass Bonanza are by far two of Reel Kingdom's most popular games. So, it stands to reason the first Megaways powered slot from the Pragmatic Play partner studio would be another entry in their bass fishing range. Big Bass Bonanza Megaways mixes the original with a couple of new extras thrown in to freshen the experience. However, at its heart, Big Bass Bonanza Megaways retains the angler's dream of reeling in as many prize-bearing fish symbols as possible during free spins to pile up wins.Visually, Big Bass Bonanza Megaways is almost the exact likeness of Big Bass Bonanza, with an upsized game grid as the only major difference. This time, the action occurs on a game panel made up of 5 main reels, plus an extra 4 symbol reel up top spinning horizontally. Reel Kingdom has not pushed the Megaways matrix to its full capacity, so ways to win top out at 46,656. As to the rest, fans of the original bass fishing experience will feel right at home amongst the deep blue waters, shimmying fish, and of course, the chilled island soundtrack.Putting everything on a larger reel format has meant that each number associated with the game is larger than the original's as well. Starting on a positive note, default RTP has increased to the respectable value of 96.7%, while volatility comes in as officially high, with a 5 out of 5 rating. There are mixed feelings on the game's potential, though, which is higher than the original but still feels lacking, particularly for a Megaways game. If chasing fish rather than major riches appeals, the game may be played on any device, accepting stakes of 20 p/c to $/€100.Regular paying symbols are the same as those used previously, and pay from left to right on adjacent reels, starting from the leftmost reel. Low pays are 10-A card ranks, while high pays are tackle boxes, dragonflies, fishing rods, and a fishing float. Values for landing six premium symbol combinations are 2 to 50 times the stake. The other paying symbols are the fish symbols. In the base game, combinations of fish pay up to 1.75x the bet, and during free spins, their prizes are collected by the fisherman symbol. Finally, appearing only on the upper four-position reel is a wild symbol which substitutes anything except the fish or fisherman symbols.Big Bass Bonanza Megaways: Slot FeaturesFor the most part, the features have remained reassuringly the same, meaning free spins with the fish and fisherman collection system. On top of these are tumbles, plus random Bazooka or Dynamite features which may appear in the bonus game.TumblesOn any spin, winning combinations are paid and removed from the reels. Remaining symbols fall into the gaps, and new combinations may line up, creating additional wins. Tumbles continue until no wins occur.Free SpinsHitting 3, 4, or 5 scatters triggers the bonus game, awarding 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. First thing to note is that in free spins, fish symbols are not removed from the reels as part of the tumble feature but fall to the bottom of the screen as tumbles happen. Also, when fish symbols land at the same time as a fisherman symbol, the fisherman collects all of the values and awards them to the player. If there is more than one fisherman symbol in view, the collection is repeated.In addition, when fisherman symbols hit, they are collected in a meter to the side of the grid. Every 4 fisherman collected retriggers the feature, awarding +10 extra free spins and a multiplier which is applied to the values on the fish symbols. The first, second, and third retrigger awards a x2, x3, and x10 multiplier, respectively. After the third, no more retriggers are possible.Bazookas and DynamiteIn free spins, if there are 1 or 2 fisherman symbols on the screen with no fish, two random features may activate. One is a Dynamite feature that adds fish symbols to the screen in various positions. The other is the Bazooka, which explodes all symbols in view, except for the fisherman symbols.Big Bass Bonanza Megaways: Slot VerdictThere's just something about reeling in fish in conjunction with collecting cash prizes that clearly resonate amongst a large number of online gamblers. A trend that started a while back is still going strong and has since been used alongside a variety of non-fishing themes. Big Bass Bonanza Megaways shows there is gas left in the mechanic's tank, and Reel Kingdom shows it is willing to wring as much out of the concept as possible - Megaways being an ideal excuse. While the experience remains much the same as it was in Big Bass Bonanza, Megaways brings its usual extra thrills and ways to win. This is not revolutionary gaming by any stretch of the imagination but should be enough to entertain players into the type of scatter collection system started long ago by Fishin' Frenzy.It was inevitable we'd mention Fishin' Frenzy sooner or later since it was Big Bass Bonanza's primary muse. In this case, let's switch to Fishin' Frenzy Megaways as Big Bass Bonanza Megaways direct competitor, and both games have merits if you're after a fish-themed action. Where Blueprint Gaming's slot wins out is in overall payout ability. Big Bass Bonanza Megaways tops out at 4,000x the bet, nearly double the original, but unusually low for Megaways, whereas Fishin Frenzy Megaways boosts that figure to 10,000x (though we are yet to see proof of that potential). So, if bigger is better, then there is a clear winner.If you're the sort of player who enjoyed Big Bass Bonanza but would've liked extra pep, then Big Bass Bonanza Megaways makes an ideal next step. However, it's a shame Reel Kingdom didn't add even more pep in the form of bigger winning opportunities, which might have made the game more enticing to a wider audience.

Title: Hypernova Infinity Reels
review: Hypernova Infinity Reels: Slot OverviewSometimes in life, you take one thing, add something else, and the result equals more than the sum of its two parts, like mac 'n cheese or Chewie and Han. If you're a major ReelPlay fan, then the coming together of two of their favoured concepts – Infinity Reels and Hypernova will be a dream come true. On the other hand, if your response is less enthusiastic, it can feel as though ReelPlay is flogging both in an attempt to squeeze every last mile out of them before they collapse like a white dwarf star nearing the end of its immense life cycle.If you find yourself leaning towards the latter group described above, it won't help that Hypernova Infinity Reels is essentially a clone of a previous release titled Thor Infinity Reels. Both run on a reel set that starts in a 3x4 configuration before adding reels after wins, and both use a jackpot infused streak respin bonus round as a headliner. The outer graphical layer is totally different from Thor's battlefield, though far from new since the red and blue nebula clouds have turned up in several games such as Hypernova Megaways, Hypernova Radial Reels, as well as Hypernova 10K Ways. After seeing the list, it's no shocker to find the Hypernova theme being powered by ReelPlay's Infinity Reels mechanism. Statistically, Hypernova Infinity Reels' math model basically performs the same way the Thor one did, starting with a default RTP value of 96.2%, increasing to 96.6% if you are able to buy the Respins Bonus round. It's also worth mentioning that a progressive jackpot version was released in 2023 titled Hypernoiva Infinity Reels Dream Drop, which utlises a lower RTP math model coming in at 94.0%.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€25 per spin, the regular symbols have been recycled from the original Hypernova Megaways game, where we come across low pay 9-A royals, then four higher value gems. Values are a little difficult to deduce at first until you've collected a few wins, yet as an indicator, a winning combination of 5 diamonds is worth 0.25x the bet. Five is the minimum number of symbols required to create a win, by the way. It might sound low, but there are other ways of boosting payouts. One way is with the help of wild symbols, which substitutes for everything except the Hypernova bonus symbols.Hypernova Infinity Reels: Slot FeaturesFeatures in the game revolve around Infinity Reels, an Infinity Bonus, Symbol Multipliers, and the Hypernova Respin Bonus. How Infinity Reels works is when a winning combination hits, which includes the rightmost reel, an extra reel is added. If this new reel improves the win, another reel is added. New reels are continually added until the win is no longer improved. Then the grid resets back to its original size for the next paid spin.In addition, whenever a new reel is added, the symbol multiplier increases by 1. When a win sequence ends, the number of winning symbols is multiplied by the current symbol multiplier. This multiplier does not have an upper limit and resets back to x1 at the start of each spin.Also, should any game round result in 12 or more reels being added, players collect the Infinity Bonus on top of any other wins. The Infinity Bonus is a separate prize worth 888x the total bet.Next, we have the Hypernova Respin Bonus round, triggered when at least 6 Hypernova bonus symbols are in view on the reels. The triggering bonus symbols are locked in place, all other symbols removed, then 3 respins are awarded. If new Hypernova symbols land, they lock to the grid and reset the respins counter. If a reel is filled with 4 Hypernova symbols, a new reel is added to the right, and it is technically possible to win the Infinity Bonus this way. When the feature ends, the total value of all Hypernova symbols is awarded. Each symbol possesses either Non-bonus prizes of 1 – 100 times the total bet or more lucrative bonus, silver, gold or platinum bonuses of 10x, 50x, 250x, or 2000x respectivelyIf possible, players may buy the Bonus Respin feature for 100x the bet. When paid for, a spin occurs that results in 6-15 reels, with 7-24 Hypernova symbols to start the feature.Hypernova Infinity Reels: Slot VerdictSince Hypernova and Infinity Reels are two of the key pillars in the ReelPlay toolkit, you might have thought their coming together would have been an excuse for the studio to lift the creative lid and go crazy with them. For whatever reason (convenience?) ReelPlay has done the total opposite and simply dressed a previous slot up in the familiar Hypernova graphics. The results are hardly original or very inspiring, though galaxy fans with a penchant for hold 'n win features might be on board.As far as streak respins go, the Hypernova Respin Bonus isn't a bad one and has a few things going for it. The grid can get quite large, meaning there's plenty of room to land bonus symbols on and gets even bigger whenever a reel is filled. Play your cards very well, and there is the technical possibility of scoring the x888 Infinity Reels Bonus in the process. Then there's Platinum bonus 2,000x as the main prize, which isn't supernova, but hey, it's a tidy sum for this sort of thing.Infinity Reels has proven to be a fairly successful business venture for ReelPlay. As well as licensing it to several other studios they've used to power a number of their own games as well. After seeing three previous incarnations of Hypernova in various forms, it stands to reason an Infinity Reels version was on the cards too. Now we've got Hypernova Infinity Reels, the main surprise is it didn't turn up sooner. However, instead of the amalgamation of two key ReelPlay tropes coming across as a labour of love, the fact they have cloned another slot by throwing some nebulaic gases and stars over Thor's game engine feels a little sad. It creates an impression that the Hypernova concept may be on its last legs, and this is a final, half-hearted hurrah.

Title: Hex
review: Hex: Slot OverviewHex is an online slot from now Kindred owned (Unibet) studio Relax Gaming that not only delves into the esoteric side of life but uses what it has learned to power its features. The magic in Hex is predominantly expressed through a mystery symbol reveal feature found in the base game and an expanded form during free spins. At first, Hex may come across as a simple game, and by Relax Gaming standards, it kind of is. However, for the right student of the dark arts, or light arts, there is juicy stuff here to uncover and solid potential to boot.The action takes place in a laboratory that looks like it was designed by the same person who did Severus Snape's office and Push Gaming's Mystery Museum. While we're on the subject, the game's logo has an uncanny Peter & Sons look, too; we're talking doppelganger levels of familiarity. Quite how the logo came to be remains as mysterious as the potion, skull, candle, and book-filled shelves making up Hex's background imagery. Capping everything off is an equally mysterious soundtrack, and though Hex might appear a little standard for Relax Gaming, it has also been pleasantly rendered for players keen to uncover one or two of life's hidden secrets.Hex's base game is played utilizing a 5-reel, 3-row, 243 ways to win grid, which expands to 5x4, 1,024 ways when free spins are active. To get the ball rolling, players select stakes of 10 p/c to $/€30 per spin, hit play, and when the reels stop, random symbols land with blue frames around them. This is part of the Mystery Reveal feature covered below. The RTP, meanwhile, is generated in two ways. One is playing naturally, where the figure is 96.43%; the second is buying free spins, which bumps the return value up to 96.58%. Also to note is that the volatility in this slot is high, no matter how you tackle the game.Wins hit when three to five matching symbols land in adjacent reels starting from the leftmost side of the grid. Hex has ten regularly paying symbols, five low pay, five high. Lows consist of a test tube and four potion bottles shaped like the four suits in a pack of cards. A five-symbol winning way of low pays is worth 0.5 to 1.2x the bet. Greater returns come from the high paying bird's foot, cards, snakes, voodoo dolls, and skull symbols. These pay out 2-10 times the stake for a five of a kind hit. Lastly, for now, is the wild symbol, appearing on all reels to substitute any pay symbol. Should five wilds land across the reels, a payout of 20x the bet is coming your way.Hex: Slot FeaturesThe main extra in Hex is the Mystery Reveal feature, available in the base game and in free spins. How it works is on the rightmost reel, Sorceress symbols may appear. When one lands, it transforms itself and all symbols marked with a frame into the same matching symbol type. If a Silver Sorceress lands, symbols transform into an identical pay symbol. If a Golden Sorceress lands, then the symbols convert into wilds.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 book scatter symbols awards 7, 10, or 15 free spins, respectively. While the bonus round is active, +1 additional free spin is awarded each time a scatter symbol hits. For free spins, an extra row is added to the reels, increasing the number of win ways to 1,024. Also, any symbols transformed by the Mystery Reveal have their position framed for the rest of the feature. In this way, it is possible to progressively build the number of framed positions as free spins continue.Buy FeatureIf buying free spins is available, players can pay 100 times the total bet to land at least 3 scatter symbols on the next spin, which also increases the RTP to 96.58%.Hex: Slot VerdictHex is one of the more conventional slots we'd reviewed from Relax Gaming for a while. This impression was formed the moment the game began, with its regular reel setup, to the framed cells idea, to the symbol transformation feature. The theme might be based on potions and magic, but initially, Hex was slightly less wonderous for a Relax Gaming slot, from a gameplay perspective. Not trying to take anything away from Hex; it's a fine slot, but it didn't have the immediate wow or intrigue factor of a Chip Spin, Beast Mode, or Deadman's Trail, to name but three.To be clear, however, we're certainly not dealing with another Deep Descent. Hex has an attractive look, wears the theme well, and has been polished to a high finish. Its main feature is a good one too. Randomly framing cells then converting them to matching symbols or wilds might not be unique, but it's not hugely overdone either. Hex' contribution is worth checking out if this sort of device interests you for several reasons. One is that Hex uses winning ways rather than a payline system this feature usually comes with, which ramps things up. Combining so many ways to win with a large number of Mystery Reveal symbols can quickly stack up a solid win. Potentially more so if the Golden Sorceress transforms framed positions into wilds, though she was very rare during the review.While the main feature is available in the base game, the rule changes to free spins make them extra desirable. The additional row brings in more symbols and creates a lot more ways to win, so that's a major plus. What really jacks the tension in free spins is the way cells stay framed throughout. Building up a useful number of frames can potentially lead to big wins. Get lucky, and Hex is capable of payouts of up to 25,000 times the stake - the game's cap.Hex might not be a Relax Gaming masterpiece, but there is certainly enough here for the right armchair sorcerer or sorceress to enjoy. The team has taken a break from being hugely intricate to do something less complicated, but no less exciting when the right reagents have been mixed just so.

Title: Loot & Labyrinths
review: Loot & Labyrinths: Slot OverviewIf rolling a d20 before adding bonuses and modifiers gets your blood pumping, then software provider Play'n GO may have made the online slot for you. Titled Loot & Labyrinths, it's a fantasy slot with a healthy dose of swords crossing, dice rolling, like actual dice rolling, and a Dungeons & Dragons mentality. Play'n GO are actually quite good at making these sorts of games. Maybe not roleplaying slots per se, but the studio has produced solid Arthurian slots in the past, The Sword & the Grail (2019), for example, so it's no stranger to legends, quests, and adventures, which bodes well.They're not usually as tabletop-orientated as this, though, and that is meant in a good way. Loot & Labyrinths litters its screen with miniatures, dice, and game sheets as if a group of buds have gotten together for a night of roleplaying. Voiceovers reinforce the effect, while passionate music adds to the drama, so for a fantasy roleplay style slot, Loot & Labyrinths is about as close as D&D on the reels as it gets.Loot & Labyrinths slot - base gameThe questing takes place on a 5x3 matrix that awards winning combinations along 20 paylines. Before taking on this medium-high volatile slot and rolling the dice, players choose a stake of 20 c to $/€100 per game round. Five RTP configurations exist, where the highest value of the lot is a 96.34% version.Four monster symbols are Loot & Labyrinths' low pays, while 4 adventurers are its highs. Winning combinations created by landing 5 matching low pays awards players 1 to 1.5 times their bet, increasing to 6 to 10 times their bet for hitting 5 matching high pay symbols. Wilds hit on all reels to substitute any regular paying symbol. Winning lines of 5 wilds pay 40x.Loot & Labyrinths: Slot FeaturesLoot & Labyrinths slot - random encounter featureIn Loot & Labyrinths, players can roll their way through 3 bonus games, free spins with various buffs, as well as a Dice & Ranks side quest.Bonus GamesThe Random Encounter symbol may land on the leftmost reel in the base game. It triggers 1 of 3 bonus games, determined by the symbols on the following reels on the same row. A mix of high and low-pay symbols triggers the Monsters Attack bonus game (win 10x-50x), only low-pay symbols trigger the Treasure Lair Bonus game (win 15x-75x), and only high-pay symbols trigger the Tavern Night bonus game (win 20x-100x).The bonus games have a starting win potential of 10x in Monsters Attack, 15x in Treasure Lair, and 20x in Tavern Night. The symbols that landed in the row with the Random Encounter symbol affect the rules of the bonus game. Each low pay symbol increases the difficulty level of the dice roll - low pay 1 by 3, low pay 2 by 4, low pay 3 by 5, and low pay 4 by 6. Each high pay symbol adds a dice bonus of +1 to the roll.To win in the bonus game, a 20-sided dice is rolled, revealing a result of 1 to 20, before any dice bonus is added to the result. Players win the prize if the final result is greater or equal to the total difficulty level. If the final dice roll is equal to or greater than 20, the player unlocks the next multiplier level and rolls again. In each bonus game, multipliers of x2, x3, or x4 may be unlocked.Free SpinsHitting 3 scatters awards 10 free spins. Each free spins round awards 3 random buffs that are revealed by picking 'n clicking. The same buff can be revealed more than once:Golden Artifact - transforms a random high-pay symbol into a wild, with wild payout values.Lady Death - removes the lowest low-pay symbol from the reels.Forgotten Temple - adds +5 free spins.Abandoned Alter - adds +3 free spins.During free spins, multipliers of x2, x5, x20, and x100 are unlocked in sequence. The unlocked multiplier applies to the total win at the end of the free spins round. Each multiplier level is unlocked by landing 5 high pay symbols with a crossed swords icon attached to them. The attack icon appears at random on any high-pay symbol. Hitting 3 scatters awards an extra +10 free spins, up to a cap of 75 free spins.Dice & RanksPlayers may open the character sheet to change the appearance of the dice and track their progress. It is possible to level up while playing, unlocking new dice skins and ranks. Levels may be gained by completing quests, and defeating the dragon bestows the rank of Dragonslayer. The part of that game would appear to be cosmetic.Loot & Labyrinths slot - free spinsLoot & Labyrinths: Slot VerdictOne of the attractions of a roleplaying game is a big, thick core book full of rules and lore, and Loot & Labyrinths brings a fair amount of rules, as well as features, to the table. The bonus games are brief, but they're pretty neat and add hits of enjoyable theme-based entertainment to the base game. Basically, a target number is presented, players roll a d20, add any modifiers, and if the total beats or equals the target, the prize is theirs. Bonus game prize money isn't huge for the most part, but that's okay; they're more of a side quest anyway and provide a fun diversion in the base game while attempting to trigger the free spins round.Free spins might be hit or miss, and whether Loot & Labyrinths' levelling up system is better than, say, The Sword and The Grail's wild multiplier is one for players to decide on. During testing, free spins didn't trigger huge amounts of suspense, but you can see how this method could be exciting when nearing the upper multiplier values in the sequence. Activating the x100 might trigger a thrill or 2, and Loot & Labyrinths' win cap is rather large at 20,000 times the bet. Play'n GO has even halved its usual max exposure probability, though at 1 in 500 million, don't expect Loot & Labyrinths to rain down max wins like a storm of lightning bolts.Play'n GO has explored fantasy gaming slots before, with Tower Quest Legacy and Champions Of Mithrune as comparable examples. However, Loot & Labyrinths takes the TTRPG influence even further, possibly too far for some, resulting in an overstuffed experience that struggles to balance its elaborate theme with engaging gameplay. While the idea of rolling the dice as an adventurous gnome sounds fun, the execution feels more exhausting than compelling.

Title: Blazin' Bullfrog
review: Blazin' Bullfrog: Slot OverviewFor such humble wee critters, frogs are certainly not underrepresented in the iGaming space. Partly due to their charming looks, partly to their connection with Asian culture, where they are perceived as symbols of fortune and luck, they habitually pop up to brighten a slot. Bullfrogs are not quite as numerous, being more aggressive than their cute green siblings. They get their name from the bull-like bellowing sound they make during the breeding season. Bullfrogs might secrete poison from glands located behind their ears, yet they still manage to end up on the dinner, their legs do at least.It is this misunderstood creature Play'n GO has chosen to star in their slot Blazin' Bullfrog. In an unforeseen plot twist, Blazin' Bullfrog is an attempt to follow on from Fire Toad, yet aside from flaming frogs and toads, the two games bear few similarities. Blazin' Bullfrog is a toned-down slot that offers little to attract the discerning gambler. Let's not get too judgemental before a full dissection, but the initial response was 'filler' after a preliminary glance, and it never really recovered from there.Played over a 5-reel, 3-row game panel, putting up 243 ways to win, Blazin' Bullfrog has an old school look, kind of plain, with just a fiery red background to contrast the gold-lined grid and copious amounts of jewels. It doesn't come across as related to Fire Toad at all. Instead, the tenuous link seems like it was used as the minutest justification for Blazin' Bullfrog's existence. Players who liked the volcanic world Play'n GO created for Fire Toad will be bored by Blazin' Bullfrog's design. There's mention of Blazin' Bullfrog being the Fire Toad's retirement, and if so, then the poor chap needs a hobby.Playable on smartphones, tablets, and full-blown desktop devices, Blazin' Bullfrog allows stakes to be selected from 10 p/c to $/€100 a spin. Play'n GO has dropped the volatility to a medium setting (5 out of 10), while the default RTP is 96.20%, though it can be found lower depending on operator configurations. Everything has been pulled back for Blazin' Bullfrog, not just the math model. This means fewer features, less excitement, and ultimately, less potential as well.Six regular symbols make up the paytable, split between 4 gems on the lower side of the table and 2 high pay symbols. These are BARs and 7s, the two of them worth 1.5-3 times the stake when a five of a combination hits. The other two symbols used in Blazin' Bullfrog are a scatter and a wild, which are sort of the same thing as you will see in the next section.Blazin' Bullfrog: Slot FeaturesPlayers looking for a cutting edge Play'n GO slot will not find it in Blazin' Bullfrog. The game comes with one simple feature, revolving around wild respins along the lines of the iconic Starburst.Golden bullfrog scatter symbols appear on the middle three reels, and landing them triggers the Blazin' Respins feature. The triggering scatter transforms into a stack of wild symbols, covering all tiles on its respective reel.A respin is then awarded, where the wild stack is locked in place. If another scatter lands, it also turns that second reel wild, and another respin is awarded. On this respin, two stacked wild reels will be available. The best-case scenario is to have all three middle reels covered in wild symbols, in conjunction with premiums on the outer two.Blazin' Bullfrog: Slot VerdictMaybe some will go for the simplistic, frog and jewels mash-up Blazin' Bullfrog presents, but even then, the game is unlikely to have much of a shelf life. There is nothing noteworthy to rave about, and really, Blazin' Bullfrog seems out of place in the Play'n GO line-up. There are similarities to Crystal Sun – Play'n GO's answer to Starburst, though on a lesser scale. Usually, if the team designs a simple game, there'll be an interesting theme or imagery colouring the screen or a feature with at least a trace of originality about it. Blazin' Bullfrog is empty of anything like that, raising more question marks than interest.Big win vehicle this is not, and while respins with middle reels stacked in wilds have their moments, they are limited. At full blast, Blazin' Bullfrog is capable of wins as high as 1,215 times the bet, which fair enough would be a pretty exciting respins sequence. Compared to what others are doing, including Play'n GO themselves, it's nothing special, though.It feels like Play'n GO might've missed a deadline on this one and had to quickly ship something out the door to keep up. It's hard to see who it might appeal to. With the widespread use of frogs in Asian themed slots, you might go in expecting some sort of Caishen experience, though it's not at all. It's not really a fruit slot either, despite the presence of sevens and bars. Blazin' Bullfrog winds up being a disconcerted heap of disparate elements that function, just.

Title: Born Wild
review: Born Wild: Slot OverviewIf you've been keeping tabs on Hacksaw Gaming, you'll be aware of their successful transition from online scratch cards to online slots. They still do the scratch card gig, but they also develop a line of big fixed jackpot slots. We're not talking about the 1,000x the bet jobs players get from run of the mill hold-&-win features - Born Wild dangles the sort of money most will only daydream about winning. The team showed their hand in games like Haunted Circus, where a top prize of €2.5 million was there for the taking, while the game under review here, Born Wild, quadruples that to produce an astonishing eight-figure sum.Born Wild starts innocently enough, where a 5x4 game board, lit up like Chaos Crew, sits before a monochrome patterned background. In total, 20 paylines are provided to hit winning combinations of three or more of a kind across, making it all sound so regular in the beginning. Hacksaw isn't known for going huge audio-visually, but they have a unique style that is pleasingly minimalist. Born Wild is very much in this vein, where the stylishly simple aesthetics fit the features and gameplay like a favourite hoodie.As well as the astonishing €10m max win, the game throws up other numbers which may surprise - RTP being the main culprit. If players approach Born Wild as a high-value jackpot slot, they might be able to ignore a low value of 93.80%. What's not low is volatility, and this thing can buck like the untamed beast it is. Whether triggering features naturally or buying them, don't expect Born Wild to be a forgiving game if it's not in the mood.10 pay symbols appear on the paytable - 5 low-values and 5 premiums. Lows are animal noises, such as Howl, Claw, Hisss, Grrrr, and Roar, all worth 1x the bet for five of a kind. Next up, the highs are all dangerous animals, including wolves, rhinos, gorillas, tigers, and cobras. Landing five premiums in a line triggers payouts worth 10 to 25 times the stake. Wilds are highly sought out symbols, not only because they replace any pay symbol to complete a win line. They also pay out 250 times the bet when a line of five hits; maybe not so common in the base game, but a genuine proposal in either feature where they become sticky.Born Wild: Slot Features﻿Born Wild provides two features to maximise returns. One is a round of free spins; the other is Lion's Roar respins where the big money may be found. Landing 3 bear scatter symbols triggers the free spins feature. In this one, all wild symbols are sticky and remain that way for the duration of the round. The feature starts with 10 free spins and ends when they've been used.3 or more lion symbols in view trigger Lion's Roar respins. In this mode, respins continue to be awarded as long as new lion symbols hit. When they land, they turn sticky and are locked in place until the feature ends. Filling the grid with lion symbols rewards the lucky player in question €10,000,000 (not a typo). In the vast majority of cases, if the max win is not reached, one last spin is awarded where all stuck lion symbols are converted into wilds.Depending on territory, players also get the chance to buy respins for the cost of 129 times the stake. Much like before, RTP remains low at 93.78% if buying Lion's Roar respins.Born Wild: Slot VerdictIf ever there was a slot Johnny Lawrence (Karate Kid/ Cobra Kai) would play, Born Wild would be it. You can picture him kicking some teenager's butt at his dojo before busting out a stone washed denim jacket with a hooded cobra patch sewn on, gearing up to give Born Wild a ride. For Johnny, everything had to be 'badass', and some of that chutzpah will be required to take on Born Wild. So will self-restraint as its massive rewards are tempered by an insanely capricious math model.The respin bonus game is the focal point of Born Wild, and after an extensive bout of them during testing, the verdict was – handle with care. Results varied wildly from a €12,900 bonus buy returning €50, to decent payouts at other times. Like the soulless machine it is, Born Wild has scant regard for feelings. Score a good win, and you might think you've cracked it, only to be brutally savaged without mercy from then on.Born Wild feels custom made for casino streamers or players with the nerve to handle the game's severe swings and roundabouts. There was a story floating around, probably an urban legend, telling of a certain astronaut who was so calm that at blast off, his heart rate barely increased despite the rocket being hit by lightning twice. These are the sort of cast iron cajones ideal for tackling Born Wild.We might have wandered into the realm of exaggeration there, but not by much. There is no doubt huge rewards are possible from Born Wild, though it should be approached with the right expectations – as a jackpot slot producing a lower than average RTP which has no problems tearing trepid players to shreds, or diehards too, for that matter. It was vaguely similar-ish in some ways to Blueprint Gaming's slot Tivoli but individual enough to provide a refreshing blast of creative air through the, at times, cobweb-clogged cash collect set of slots.

Title: Outsourced Payday
review: Outsourced Payday: Slot OverviewAh, payday, what a roller coaster of emotions that day can be as the money flows in then just as quickly flows out to cover bills, rent, mortgage, groceries, and all the rest of the blood-draining, spirit-crushing vampiric institutions we're required to satiate in order to exist in society. From the heights of Croesus to participating in medical experiments for ramen money in a single day… This (exaggerated) emotional roller coaster ride of ups and downs has been distilled by developer Nolimit City's Labs people and bottled in the experimental online slot (is that even the right word?), Outsourced Payday.Outsourced Payday's backstory explains how the Outsourced factory's production is up 2,000% after all the workers were fired and replaced by claws. The best bit, the claws don't complain about the working conditions. A classic capitalist fairytale. Outsourced Payday returns the scribbly, in a good way, cartoon graphics, pairing the visuals with tip-top audio work to drop players into a game world where playfulness tinged with punishment abounds.Outsourced Payday slot - base gameAs Nolimit City games tend to do, Outsourced Payday comes with a lengthy list of optional betting options, though players must pick a base stake of 20 c to $/€100 per game round. The RTP varies when activating the buy modes, but the maximum baseline value is 96%. It's not quite as volatile as a lot of NLC's beasts, though - this one has earned a 6 out of 10 medium rating for volatility.It won't take more than a nanosecond to work out that Outsourced Payday is not your typical rows and reels slot. In this game, a single row of 5 symbols slides onto the screen from right to left for claws to potentially pick up, potentially drop. As well as plenty of no-value symbols, there are 7 symbols depicting various 'prize' objects worth from 2 times the bet up to 1,000 times the bet for each individual symbol.Outsourced Payday: Slot FeaturesOutsourced Payday slot - Clawiest spinsOutsourced Payday is easy to work out, and here's how the game goes. At the bottom of the gaming area is a conveyor belt displaying 5 symbols per spin. A claw can pick up one of the symbols randomly from the conveyor belt. If the claw picks up a symbol without dropping it, the player wins the corresponding prize. The claw does not pick up anything with a zero multiplier value.Claw SpinsA claw picking up the Claw Spins bonus symbol without dropping it awards 3 Claw Spins. Bonus symbols picked up during the bonus award a further +3 spins. During Claw Spins, only symbols with multipliers greater than 2x will appear.Nolimit Bonus BuysBy opening the bonus buy menu, players are able to activate these modes: Claw Spins - for 35x the bet, players get 3 Claw Spins with 1 Claw; Clawier Spins - for 150x the bet, players get 3 Claw Spins with 3 Claws; Clawiest Spins - for 400x the bet, players get 3 Claw Spins with 5 Claws; God Mode - for 997x the bet, a MAX WIN symbol is guaranteed to land on the conveyor belt.Nolimit BoosterOutsourced Payday's Nolimit Booster options include these: xBet - at a cost of 6 times the bet, a bonus symbol is guaranteed on the conveyor belt; Safe Claw Mode - at a cost of 1.6 times the bet, symbols picked up by the claw cannot be dropped; Three Claws, One Spin - at a cost of 4 times the bet, players get 3 claws per spin; Five Claws, One Spin - at a cost of 10 times the bet, players get 5 claws per spin.Outsourced Payday slot - Clawiest spinsOutsourced Payday: Slot VerdictLike 'em or loathe 'em, it's hard to deny the Nolimit City Labs folk are pushing boundaries. They did so with Outsourced Slash Game, followed up in the unusual Munchies, and have kept the ball rolling with Outsourced Payday. This release is obviously thematically linked to Slash Game and slightly further back to the original Outsourced slot. Where Outsourced and Nolimit City slots, in general, came with all manner of bells and whistles, Labs creations like Outsourced Payday are quicker to the point, have less fussing around, and chuck a ton of betting options at a relatively simple game mechanic.This claw reaching down to grab stuff gaming mechanic can be your best friend or your worst enemy. On the negative side, one of the worst things about Outsourced Payday is the way the claw is not guaranteed to keep hold of the prizes it grabs (unless playing in Safe Claw Mode). Dropping an x100 is bad enough; try dropping a MAX WIN symbol, especially after dishing out 997x for God Mode. Ouchy. It's worse than manoeuvring an actual claw machine IRL and having it drop that Pop Toy your nephew really wanted and watching him tear up. For the record, the max win, with a 1 in 1.3 million spins probability, is 10,000x. On the flip side, Outsourced Payday is a bit gimmicky but not overly so due to it having more depth than a crash game, for example. There is a bonus round to bust into, and having multiple claws picking things up (and not dropping them) in the base game or in Claw Spins can be amusing.Outsourced Payday was one of the more easily enjoyable of the Labs releases so far. The rules are simple, it's built from quality materials and wasn't as punishing or repetitive as a crash-style game. Outsourced Payday's creators have stacked the game with betting opportunities, a bit of depth, and smatterings of the Nolimit City humour we've come to appreciate.

Title: Fizzy Pennyslot
review: ﻿Fizzy Pennyslot: Slot OverviewBack in the day, a penny could get you a trip into town, a full bag of groceries from the shop, a new suit, a pint and a pie from the pub, and still have some left over to get you home on the omnibus. Okay, that was made up, but the point is you can't get much for a penny these days, can you? No doubt this is why some countries have withdrawn them from circulation. They were just cluttering up wallets and shopping tills, doing nothing. However, within the realms of online gambling, a penny can still, at times, get you a spin on the reels. When playing Big Time Gaming's slot Fizzy Pennyslot, a penny not only buys a spin, but the spin also comes with 4 paylines, rather than the customary 1 to attempt hitting wins along.So, it was a while back when a penny could really buy anything substantial, and Fizzy Pennyslot gives off the air of yesteryear via some audiovisual cues, as well. There's a slight retro look to the graphics, where memories of Star Clusters Megaclusters wafted to mind, and the music sounds like it comes right out of a 90s cartoon show. It does when the reels are in motion, that is. When Fizzy Pennyslot is at rest, a sweet menagerie of miscellaneous gaming sounds plays while the slot waits to kick into life. It's worth having a close listen to see if you can pick out familiar bleeps. Pacman is in there, right?Fizzy Pennslot slot - base gameFizzy Pennyslot does indeed allow players to stake from 1 penny up to $/€90 per spin. What you get is a 4x4 gaming grid, something of an oddity in itself, and 4 paylines. Each row is basically its own payline, landing 4 OAK winning combinations only. It is hard to complain about the 96.44% RTP or the volatility if you like it on the high side.A vending machine was the first thing that popped to mind when going over Fizzy Pennyslot's pay symbols. Not the Q-A symbols, though they look like they're encased in ice, but the three Asian writing adorned bottle symbols, and the pack of sweets wild bright a snack dispenser to mind. A win made up of card royals pays 1-2 times the bet, one made up of the bottles is worth 2 to 5 times the bet, while an all-wild result is worth 10 times the stake. Wilds also substitute for any other pay symbol.Fizzy Pennyslot: Slot FeaturesFizzy Pennslot slot - free spinsFizzy Pennyslot isn't the most complicated slot BTG has ever made. Not a criticism. What it has is a Bonus Reel that links wins to some pretty sizable multipliers, free spins, a bonus buy, and Win Exchange functions.Bonus ReelThe Bonus Reel spins to the right of the main regular reels. It displays blank spaces or multipliers. If a win occurs next to a multiplier, the multiplier value is applied to the winning combination. In the base game, x200 is the biggest possible multiplier.Trigger Coin & Free SpinsIf a Trigger Coin lands anywhere on the Bonus Reel in the base game, 6 free spins are awarded. Now, on every free spin during the feature, the lowest multiplier on the Bonus Reel is upgraded to a higher multiplier. In free spins, the maximum multiplier possible is x500. If a Trigger Coin lands anywhere on the Bonus Reel in the round, an extra free spin is awarded.Bonus BuyAt the bonus buy, players are able to buy 6 free spins for 65 times the bet. The bonus buy RTP is the same at 96.44%.Win ExchangeWhenever players win 65x their bet or more, they have the option of exchanging 65x the bet for 6 free spins. When scoring a win between 20 and 65 times the bet, players can exchange the entire win for the chance to win free spins from a gamble wheel.Fizzy Pennslot slot - bonus buyFizzy Pennyslot: Slot VerdictFizzy Pennyslot is like the Pied Piper of low rollers; really, there is a lot here for gamblers looking to stretch a bankroll to the absolute hilt to sink their teeth into. First, there's the 1 penny minimum bet, meaning it don't really get no lower than this when real money with your own funds wagering. This stake level is not super common, though it admittedly does happen from time to time. However, rarely, if ever, do gamblers get 4 paylines for their buck, err, penny, which opens Fizzy Pennyslot up and prevents users from burning their retinas out staring at a single performing payline.Furthermore, 65c for a bonus buy, damn, you just don't see price tags like that, upping Fizzy Pennyslot's desirability even further for players with an eye on the pennies. As a comparison, just yesterday, we reviewed Nolimit City's controversial slot, Kenneth Must Die, where the most expensive bonus buy, at the lowest stake, would set you back $/€1,393.80. Okay, okay, apples and oranges, but the point is... 65c! Mind-blowing.The gameplay itself, okay, it's not bad. Pacey, simplistic, tough in parts, potentially rewarding in others - up to 2,000x in the base game and up to 10,170x in the bonus round. Fizzy Pennyslot is a bit like Candy Blitz/Candy Blitz Bombs or Aztec Gems, where linking wins to multipliers on a special reel is one of the key objectives. Whilst the gaming's alright, one gets the impression Fizzy Pennyslot's status as a penny roller's paradise is what's going to create bigger reactions.

Title: Agent Royale
review: Agent Royale: Slot OverviewThe spy game is a complicated world of cloak and dagger, but Red Tiger has chosen to keep their slot version relatively straight forward. While spinning for rather low rewards in Agent Royale, players get sticky wilds plus free spins as they take on femme fatales and disarm explosive devices. Located downtown, Agent Royale uses a viewpoint that looks like someone's passed out on the street staring skywards. Buildings on each side of the screen tower over a 5x4, 40 payline grid, while a couple of signs convey messages such as 'Win Now' or 'Good Luck'. It's a little cheesy, yet a bit of positivity never goes amiss.On the aural side of things, the music and sound effects have a generic quality that could be used in absolutely any type of slot. There is something equally recognisable about the leading star of the show, Agent Royale, who is a dead ringer for English fashion model David Gandy. Maybe he's angling for a spot in a future spy movie and allowed Red Tiger to use his mug to plant seeds. In fact, the whole game has a familiar look, mixing parts of NetEnt's Hotline 2 with a touch of Red Tiger's own 24 Hour Grand Prix.Players get their spy on by selecting bets from 10 p/c to $/€40 per spin, across any device. Don't expect to strap onto a highly volatile rocket ride playing Agent Royale despite having a decent enough bonus game. Return to player isn't exactly a selling point either at 95.77% RTP, but acceptable nonetheless. To Agent Royale's credit, triggering free spins wasn't the battle it can be in some Red Tiger games, though without the official bonus frequency to go by that might have simply been good luck.Nine regular pay symbols occupy the reels, starting with five metallic 10-A card royals worth 1 to 4 times the bet for five of a kind. Things get a bit more glamourous amongst the premiums where we find dice, cocktails, sports cars, and bombs. Land five of these symbols on a payline to pick up wins from 2.5x to 4x the stake. Not massive values, mitigated to some extent by the features.Agent Royale: Slot FeaturesSecret agents, the ones in movies at least, always pack the latest gadgets whether it's a watch which doubles as a laser, or a key finder that explodes when the agent whistles the right tune. Always, the hero has the exact device needed to get out of the jam they find themselves in. In contrast, Agent Royale is rather light in the features department. This is an agency running on an austerity affected budget which has to make do with sticky wilds and free spins.The first thing we need to cover are the 2 wild symbols. One is a regular 1x1 bomb wild, the other a 1x2 sized Agent Royale wild. Substituting for any of the regular pay symbols is their primary job. When the 1x2 wild lands on the same spin as bomb pay symbols, he attempts to defuse them. If he successfully cuts the wire, the bomb symbol is turned into the wild counterpart. It is then locked in place for one more spin. If on the next spin Agent Royale defuses more bombs, all wilds are locked for an additional spin.The female seductress is displayed on the scatter symbol which may land in any position. It's hard to tell if she's a goody or a baddy, but the dragon tattoo on her back is a red flag. In any case, 3 scatters in view award 8 free spins. On the first spin, an Agent Royal wild is locked to the centre position of the slot. Also in free spins, each wild that lands in view and is part of a winning combination remains locked for the remainder of the feature and awards 1 extra free spin.Agent Royale: Slot VerdictDespite the hazardous task of disarming bombs, Agent Royale doesn't feel dangerous at all. Quite the opposite, it comes across as a bit of light entertainment aimed at those who prefer mid-ground thrills rather than pushing lady luck to her extreme. Other than a modicum of spy glam provided by the two characters, it doesn't seem like too much passion went into the game's design either. Sound effects seem like they could have been bolted on any slot, and the rest of the graphics are okay, yet they don't stand out much.As is often the case, the part Scottish part Swiss MI6 agent, can't help but crop up as a comparison. Where Bond was all about risking it all on the flip of the next card, Agent Royale isn't so extreme. Modesty certainly applies to potential where the most you can win is 1,760 times the bet. It's not exactly high stakes gambling with Hugo Drax at Blades.Still, Agent Royale might be alright for a few spins to see Red Tiger's take on the spy genre. The base game loses some of its appeal once you've seen Royale turn a few bomb symbols wild resulting in meagre wins. Free spins hold more promise since wilds are sticky for the remainder of the feature possibly leading to full screens of them. A concern for some is since symbol values are quite low, a full screen of wilds is worth a scant 200x the bet.Once Agent Royale has done its thing, maybe rolled through free spins once or twice, there is little reason to darken its door again. The game might be based on agent stuff, yet it comes across as the pushing pencils side of spy work rather than getting your hands dirty in field operations.

Title: Dracula
review: Dracula: Slot OverviewDeveloper Stakelogic braves the Transylvanian wilds in their vampire-infested slot Dracula. Interestingly, they have managed to trademark the title, which is odd since Dracula was made famous in a novel written by Bram Stoker over a hundred years ago. Perhaps because the book is in the public domain, it’s free to be pillaged as others see fit. Whatever the legal status, players looking for a somewhat toned down Nosferatu-themed adventure will find that in Dracula the slot, brimming with slick visuals and several features.A sinister room in Dracula’s castle has been provided to host the 5x3, 25-payline action area. Several chandeliers cast an eerie red light over the whole scene, made more unsettling by a dramatic, gothic soundtrack. On a side note, it’s a good thing vampires can fly because it must be a mission getting up there to light all those candles. Bats flap across the screen at intervals and the whole game has a movie-like quality which is quite well done.In some ways, the team has plastered bigger fangs on the game’s audio-visuals than its low/medium volatile math model. Dracula is a game playable on any device, giving players stake options ranging from 25 p/c to $/€100 per spin while the RTP measures 95.60%. The game also comes with Stakelogic’s Super Stake feature, doubling the bet when activated. The payoff for doing so is having 1 to 10 wild symbols inserted onto the reels at random following non-winning symbols. There is no mention if doing so affects RTP.If you’ve ever wondered what actor Tim Curry would look like playing Dracula, then the slot gives you a pretty good idea. The Count appears on the top pay symbol, possessing the same devious grin as the famous thespian. Landing 5 Dracula symbols on a line are worth a payout of 80x the stake, followed by a Van Helsing type, a vampiress, and an oddly cheerful chap wearing specs. These other 3 premiums are worth 16 to 40 times your bet for lines of 5. Making up the bottom of the paytable are a set of bejewelled card suits – hearts, clubs, spades, and diamonds.Worth substantially more than the Dracula symbol is the wild. Lines of 5 of these provocative symbols are worth 300x the bet, though most of the time, the wild is busy substituting all symbols except the scatter or bonus symbols.Dracula: Slot FeaturesDracula - picking bonusTwo additional symbols grace the reels in Dracula, leading to a round of free spins or a pick-me-style bonus game. One is the chained door bonus symbol, landing on any reel. When 3 or more bonus symbols land in succession from the leftmost reel on a bet line, they launch the bonus game. In this one, 12 chests cover the screen for players to pick one at a time. The first chest is always a cash prize, and players keep clicking until an empty chest is revealed. If the bonus game is triggered by 4 or 5 scatters, then a win multiplier of x1.5 or x2 respectively applies to the winning amount.The other special symbol is a Grateful Dead logo looking scatter, also appearing on any reel. When 3, 4, or 5 scatters hit, a win of 4x, 25x, or 100x is awarded, on top of 10 free spins. All wins are tripled in value during free spins, except for cash won from the pick me bonus game, which can be triggered from free spins. Scatters remain on the reels, and 3 in view retriggers +10 free spins.The final extra to cover is a gamble feature. Following wins, players can double or quadruple their prize by correctly guessing the colour or suit of a face-down card. The gamble feature can be disabled if you’re not into it.Dracula: Slot VerdictDracula is another well-designed Stakelogic game, aimed at a more laid-back sector of the market than they usually cater for. The Count might be one of the most famous monsters in literature, yet the slot is far from being one itself. Dracula is a bit like those living card games such as Arkham Horror, where players can choose difficulty levels. The hardest setting is reserved for players who like to challenge themselves, while the lowest is for those who prefer to just follow the storyline. Dracula the slot leans towards the latter end of the spectrum, seemingly more focused on creating an immersive environment to get lost in rather than deliver high octane action.On the gaming side of things, not a lot stands out. Free spins with an x3 multiplier are a classic setup, and the pick & click feature serves up consolation wins every so often. Like other games offering a Super Stake feature, engaging it takes a bit of forethought. Landing a good number of wilds at once when triggered can cobble together a solid payout – and a hit rate of once every 29 spins (theoretically) is quite frequent for Super Stake. Then again, doubling the bet is a significant increase that could potentially plough through an account.To its credit, Dracula the game does have an entertaining quality, being ‘highly animated’ as Stakelogic calls it. There is certainly a lot of animation going on, from flutters of bats to creepy hands reaching up from the crypt grasping for the third scatter, to atmospheric cut scenes. With all the candles and curtains, Dracula is a bit like a night out at the theatre. These visual tricks serve to both entertain and cover up for the fact Dracula is fairly mild gaming. This assessment extends to winning potential, where the most you can collect is 3,750x the bet. Not an eye-watering amount of cash, but it’s a middle-of-the-road figure that fits in with what the rest of Dracula does.

Title: Rockabilly Wolves
review: Rockabilly Wolves (Just For The Win): ReviewMaybe even more than any other Microgaming partner, Swedish developer JFTW has been struggling to produce anything of relevance. Most games so far have been "meh" at best and at this point, the whole venture is starting to come across as rather pointless. So, without expecting fireworks to set our world alight we set out to give Rockabilly Wolves a try, and it didn't take long until it triggered the first face-palm.Despite of the intense rockabilly background music blasting, it was the geometric-style reels that caught our attention. Expecting to see a 3-4-4-4-3 reel design or for the colourful stacked symbols to go crazy in the middle reels, we were slightly disappointed to learn that it's in fact just a plain 5-reel, 3-row, 20-payline slot. Rockabilly Wolves is a high variance slot that benefits from a Re-Spin feature in the main game and Sticky Wilds and multipliers of up to 6x in the Free Spins game. You can play it across all devices from between 0.10€ to 50€ per spin.Visually, it's colourful and straightforward, although the childish cartoon-style graphics might be a bit over the top in our opinion. Seeing how strikingly similar in style some of the "wolves" are to Disney's characters, it would be interesting to hear their opinion on the game. Either way, visual design is the one area in which these guys actually know what they are doing and though it's far from the best looking slot we've seen, it's also far from the worst.With a 50s feel, you'll see A, K, Q and J royals on the reels as well as 3 fully stacked higher-value symbols represented by cherries, 8-balls and the Rockabilly Wolves logo. The latter is the most rewarding, giving you 20 times your stake for 5 across a full payline. There's also a fully stacked wild symbol that pays the same as the logo.Rockabilly Wolves (Just For The Win): FeaturesFree spins with sticky wildsThe scatter symbol is the one to your eyes on. Appearing on the three middle reels only, 2 of them in view will trigger the Re-Spin feature. The 2 scatter symbols are held in position as the reels respin, thus giving you a second chance to land the 3rd scatter needed to trigger the bonus as well as an opportunity to land a new winning combination.Landing 3 scatters will reward you 9 Free Spins with the 3rd reel scatter from the triggered spin converted into a Multiplier Sticky Wild, locked into position for the duration of the free spins that starts at 2x. Now, any sticky wilds or multiplier sticky wilds (these are two different wilds) landing on the reels will also lock and remain in place. Furthermore, any additional multiplier sticky wild appearing on the reels will increase the multiplier by an increment of 1 up to a maximum of 6x. You can also retrigger the feature once - when at least one wild has landed on each reel, 3 extra free spins are added to your total.Though unconfirmed, a max win of 2400 times your stake per single spin should be achievable in the unlikely event of landing a full screen of sticky wilds.Rockabilly Wolves (Just For The Win): VerdictSticky wilds is an exceptionally fun feature if implemented in the right way and has been used in iconic games such as Dead or Alive, Cazino Zeppelin, and more recently, The Dog House by Pragmatic Play. The feature comes to good use here as well, although it doesn't quite pack the punch we were hoping for.Unfortunately, the main game underperforms and we got thoroughly bored playing it - there's little to no potential and the free spins seemed to take ages to trigger. The respin feature initially helped make things a bit interesting, but after 9 or so teases without landing the 3rd scatter, it started to get a bit annoying instead.Rockabilly Wolves is a little step forward for JFTW although we're not sure that it says much considering the last few games have been dreadful. This is not a game we will spend our hard earned money on. It just doesn't cut it in this competitive market with thousands of games screaming for your attention. Sorry, Just For The Win but this one is Just For The Bin.

Title: Trolls Bridge 2
review: Trolls Bridge 2 (Yggdrasil): OverviewTrolls Bridge 2 is a 5-reel, 25 payline slot powered by Yggdrasil Gaming and a follow up to the 2017 release Trolls Bridge. With improved graphics and more action-packed than ever before, you once again get to enter the fairy-tale fantasy world of Yggdrasil's crazy trolls where you'll encounter colossal symbols, random multipliers, a bonus cauldron feature, and a free spins game where each round is different in setup from the other. Accessible via your desktop or mobile device, this medium variance slot can be played from 10 cents up to 140€/$ per spin.Although some of the childish and quirky charisma of the original still shines through, you'll find the sequel to be significantly darker, both visually and aurally. Not only has the quality of the visual design greatly improved, so has the building technique of the trolls. Instead of a rickety wooden fence, the troll fortress is now an intimidating stone structure decorated with spikes, flames, human skulls and red banners to signal doom and destruction.Free spins feature in actionWith the reels set over an intimidating drawbridge and a sinister soundtrack serving as the troll anthem, symbols include diamond, club, spade and heart card suits. More rewarding are the four troll picture symbols that can appear as 2x2 and 2x4 colossal symbols. The most lucrative of these is the red-haired troll, giving you 10 times your stake for five of a kind. There's also a golden wild symbol included in the game which substitutes for all symbols except the scatter.Trolls Bridge 2 (Yggdrasil): FeaturesFans of the original game will find Trolls Bridge 2 to be just as action-packed and feature-heavy. Before anything else, however, you'll need to make an active decision whether to play with the Golden Bet activated or not. Similar to the classic Yggdrasil game Golden Fish Tank, activating the Golden Bet will give you an extra feature pick in the free spins game and boost the RTP of the game by 0.6%, but it will also increase the cost of your spins by 40%.Once you've made your call, keep an eye out for the skull scatter symbol as 3 or more anywhere in view will activate the Free Spins - 3, 4 or 5 scatter symbols will give you 6, 8 or 10 spins with 3, 4 or 5 feature picks respectively. Before the action starts, you'll see a wall with 18 skulls and asked to use your picks to reveal your feature combo. This can include extra picks, additional free spins, random wilds on every spin, colossal symbols and symbol upgrades. With 18 different features on offer, no two free spins rounds are likely to be the same.In the main game, the Bonus Cauldron feature will trigger if the cauldron symbol lands on the last reel. Similar to the chest feature in Yggdrasil's Vikings series, it will either give you a cash prize of up to 50 times your stake or entry to the free spins game.Colossal Symbols do not only appear in the free spins feature but can hit randomly in the main game as well. On any spin, 2x4 colossal troll symbols can hit anywhere on the reels to increase your chance of landing big wins.Finally, a Bonus Stone feature might come into play following a winning spin in the main game. If randomly activated, you'll see a boulder catapulted at the reels with a multiplier attached that can boost your wins by up to 5x.Trolls Bridge 2 (Yggdrasil): VerdictTrolls Bridge 2 is a game that utilities the same fundamental mechanic as many other popular Yggdrasil titles such as Golden Fish Tank, Vikings Go To Hell, Lucha Maniacs and, of course, the original Trolls Bridge. And while there's a lot to like about it, in particular the stellar graphics and the entertaining free spins feature, there are also some factors that can put some players off. For example, all the base game features that seemed so intriguing at first eventually start to feel useless as the payouts, even with the help of colossal symbols and random multipliers, are quite low in general.With that said, it's well worth a try, especially if you're into previously mentioned games, as the free spins feature is entertaining enough to make up for the mediocre base game. Don't expect any life-changing wins, however. The original version offers a max win of around 2000x and Trolls Bridge 2 is likely in the same ballpark.

Title: Merlin's Moneyburst
review: Merlin's Moneyburst: ReviewIt must be quite comfy to be part of the Scientific Games family. If you run out of creative energy, you can always build yourself a Frankenstein slot using bits and pieces from other software developers, an opportunity NextGen Gaming has not passed up on. In the studio's third, or fourth (who knows), instalment in the Merlin series, the Moneyburst game engine has been borrowed from sister company WMS to lay the foundation. Those of you who have been around for some time will instantly think of classic WMS titles such as Bruce Lee, Fire Queen, Glitz or Queens Knight II when Merlin's Moneyburst loads up on the screen.Indeed, it comes with 60 paylines and the same odd reel arrangement made up of 4 single reels in a 2x2 formation followed by 3 reels with 4 symbols each. Playable on all devices from 30 cents t0 62.50€ per spin, this rather childish looking fantasy-themed game has plenty of diverse features to keep you busy throughout, such as respins, wild modifier extras, and a free spins game in which Mr Merlin himself makes an appearance.Maybe even more so than in previous titles in the series, Merlin's Moneyburst looks like an educational pc game for 6-year old kids to learn their ABC's. Take the cartoon-like royal symbols for example with their quirky eyes following your mouse pointer as you move it around - your toddler will love this game. Visually, it looks alright, although it has a slightly dated aura, especially when it comes to the cringy wizard animations.Set in an enchanted moonlit forest, on the reels you will see A, K, Q, J and 10 royal values (with eyes) alongside time glasses, money bags and bottles of potion. The spell-book is the most lucrative with 5 on a full payline yielding 8,33 times your stake. As you would expect, Merlin is the wild and substitutes for all symbols bar the scatter. Land 5 of him on a payline and you'll win 83.33 times your stake.Merlin's Moneyburst: FeaturesFree spin featureMaking use of the studios own in-house developed SuperBet feature, players can choose from a set of additional wagers with multipliers. This comes to use when the Merlin wild hits, as it can boost your winning combinations with multipliers of up to 10x. Title: 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor
review: 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor: OverviewLuke vs Darth, Rocky vs Apollo Creed, Predator vs Alien, take your pick; there have been some epic showdowns throughout history. However, battles don't get much bigger than they do in 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor from independent developer 4ThePlayer. Here, two of the biggest names in the Pantheon square off in a game full of new features and mechanics. When a studio chooses just one deity to theme a game, they need to go large. Can 4ThePlayer handle all the godly power of two, or have they bitten off more than they can chew?Released via the Yggdrasil Gaming YGS Masters program, 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor plays out on a 5-reel, 2048 win ways grid split into two zones. The left side is dominated by the lightning god Zeus, while the right is the realm of Thor, the Thunder God. It's a pretty titanic scene and 4ThePlayer has gone for a suitably serious tone in its treatment.The first thing that sticks out is the two spin buttons; one red, one blue. Red is the colour of Zeus, so blue goes to Thor. Dubbed the Dual Spin mechanic, on each spin players are free to choose either button. The Red Greek symbols pay left to right, while the Blue Norse symbols pay right to left. Having a pay both ways system effectively doubles the paylines. This is broken down into 1,024 win ways for red symbols from the leftmost reel; 1,024 ways to win for the blues from the rightmost reel.It's a little cross-eye inducing at first, but you quickly get into the swing of it. Basically, if the colour of a winning combination matches the colour of the button you pressed, you double the payout. If you hit the red button and a blue combination lands you get 1x the win value. However, if the symbols and button colour match you get 2x the value. The good thing is you always get the regular value of a combination or double - you never forfeit the win if the button colour is wrong. The history of winning colours is displayed just below the reels roulette style, if that helps you choose.Most likely for liability reasons, stakes are kept rather low with a max bet limit of 'only' $/€20 per spin. Most low rollers, meanwhile, will be satisfied with the 10 p/c minimum bet. When it comes to stats, the game produces some solid numbers, as typically is the case with this developer, starting with an RTP rating of 96.5% and an average hit frequency of one in four spins. 4ThePlayer tends to cater to the more core end of the gambling market by powering their slots with highly volatile math models - this game is no exception.As mentioned, pay symbols come in two forms – red for the Greeks, blue for the Norsemen. Both groups consist of three letters or runes for the low pays, followed by helms, boats, mythical hounds, and goddesses. Goddesses are the most valuable at 7 times the stake for five of a kind, dropping to 1.2x at the lower end of the paytable.Just as everything else comes in twos, so do the wilds. Players get a blue Thor wild and a red Zeus wild. Both substitute for their respectively coloured pay symbols, or pay out up to 10 times the stake for five wilds in a combination.2 Gods Zeus vs Thor: Features2 Gods Zeus vs Thor - free spinsAs well as the Dual Spin feature is a round of Win Spins unlocked by landing 3 scatters, though the process is not quite so straight forward. If the colour of 2 or 3 scatters matches your chosen spin button, you get 10 Win Spins. Otherwise, you get 7 Win Spins.Just as the name suggests, players are guaranteed a win on every Win Spin, similar to what you get in some of the games from Play'n GO such as Pimped or That's Rich. The Win Spin feature also adds a progressive Win Spin Multiplier into the mix. The multiplier begins at x1 and increases by +1 each time the winning symbols match your chosen spin button colour.Win Spins may be retriggered in the same way as mentioned above. So 3 scatters add 7 or 10 extra Win Spins to the remaining amount – no limit.2 Gods Zeus vs Thor: Verdict2 Gods Zeus vs Thor is another 4ThePlayer slot that deviates from the norm. The Dual Spin mechanic continues the studio's focus on player input. Whether the Dual Spin causes excitement or not, it's always interesting to see a studio trying something new. 4ThePlayer still fly relatively low beneath the radar, but they clearly aren't content to stay there or ride the coattails of others.Like 6 Wild Sharks, which came out around the same time, 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor is further proof of a studio that likes to experiment. Even if the two-button thing comes across a little too wacky for some purists, it beats cranking out generic white bread slots or going down the tempting route of copying classic games.For a bit of critique, the roulette-style win tracker is cute, but ultimately useless when selecting which button to hit. Like actual roulette, winning is down to pure luck and has no bearing on the next spin. Also, in its current form, the Dual Spins mechanic might struggle to stay fresh if rolled out in future slots. For now, it does suit the two gods doing battle format perfectly. Despite the quibbles, Dual Spin is a clever innovation, providing a nice wee thrill when wins are doubled.It’s even more useful during Win Spins as well. Here players get the extra benefit of increasing the Win Spin Multiplier when choosing the right colour. The multiplier, combined with retriggerable Wins Spins, results in potential of up to 15,630 times the bet. For the record, Win Spins theoretically trigger every 185 regular spins.Once again, 4ThePlayer has crafted an original game which works pretty well for the most part. 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor doesn't feel like a slot that's trying to be different just for the sake of it. The Dual Spin mechanic adds more than it takes away and Win Spins can be as epic as you'd imagine a showdown between two mighty gods might be.Yes, some will be turned off by the bland visuals and others, who may be into more straightforward gaming, might find it dull and confusing. If you are ok with those two factors, 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor is a pretty solid slot with some player friendly stats well worth a spin...or two, because, you know, there being two spin buttons and all.

Title: Power Vault

Suppose a lot of casino game makers drop a classic slot or two eventually, but Push Gaming has never been like just 'a lot of casino game makers'. Or at least it didn't use to be. Title: Olympus Infinity Reels
review: Olympus Infinity Reels: Slot OverviewAussie designer GamesLab teams up with fellow compatriots ReelPlay once again, licensing the latter studio's Infinity Reels engine. The 3-reel, 4-row grid is fairly captivating, with nicely drawn symbols that have a solid, mythological quality to them. A sweepingly dramatic soundtrack reinforces the approach GamesLab has chosen to tackle Hellenic mythology. Some studios use an easy-going cartoon approach; others, like Olympus Infinity Reels, take everything very seriously.Olympus Infinity Reels is available on any device, where stakes vary from 30 p/c to $/€120 per spin. The game is a bit of a mixed bag numerically. A highly volatile math model would tend to suit hardcore gamblers, but the game fails to back it up with solid potential – unless you are willing to lay it all on the line via a gamble feature. The RTP is a little up and down as well. The regular value hovers between 95.61% and 95.72% depending on the feature accepted (more on this below), rising to a generous 97.38% if buying free spins instead.Casting your eye over the paytable reveals 10 regular pay symbols, split into 4 low-value gems and 6 characters such as owls, cyclops's, minotaurs, Medusa, Cerberus, plus a ram. Mighty Zeus appears on the reels as the wild, substituting for all symbols except the Lightning Bolt tile, covered next.Olympus Infinity Reels: Slot FeaturesTying in with the Infinity Reels feature is a symbol multiplier, Frenzy Spins, an Infinity Bonus, a Feature Trail, Free Spins, and a Free Spins Gamble option – yeah, there's a lot to cover.Built using the Infinity Reels mechanic, all spins begin with 3 reels. Olympus Infinity Reels lives up to its name, technically speaking, as there is no limit on the number of reels that can be added.While reels are being added as wins grow, a symbol multiplier also comes into play.
