The base game is bathed in the green and gold hues we all know so well, which flips to red and gold during free spins. Music to the ears of players who go for these kinds of slots, others will be rolling their eyes. Each to their own.Symbols are also right out of the Asian theme playbook. On the low side are J – A royals desinged in a calligraphy font. The higher value symbols are turtles, frogs, dragons (naturally), and the game logo at the top worth a solid 300 times the stake for 10 of a kind. No, that’s not a typo. Tens are technically possible due to the symbols landing in standard singles, or in doubles. Bet levels range from 10 p/c per spin up to the maximum of $/€100. RTP is steady at 96.02%, and the game has a hit rate of around 1 in 4 spins. With its medium volatility don’t expect too much intensity; this slot is more about gentle rides that pay out small and steady.Double Lucky Line (Just For The Win): FeaturesFree spins feature in playLanding 10 symbols might be the dream but it will take some luck. So it is to the features we mainly rely on to increase the pay rate. Despite being an overblown Asian slot with 15 reels, the features are surprisingly sparse - and are exactly what appeared on Tweethearts. The game has a wild symbol which can appear on anywhere and in singles or double. The Random Wild feature pops up at any time and transforms between 2 and 6 symbol positions into wilds.The feature that gives the slot is moniker is the middle row called the Double Lucky Line. It is always active during the main game as well as when free spins are in play. Any symbols that land within it are double symbols and count for two regular symbols when it comes to calculating wins, or scoring free spins.That brings us to the final feature which is a round of Free Spins. The scatter symbol can appear in anywhere as a single or a double. When 5 scatter symbols land (including double symbols) 10 free spins are awarded. Each scatter symbol in view over 5 is worth 1 additional spin up to a maximum of 25 for the round. Lucky Wild symbols can appear during free spins and when they land they make that position a double symbol position while adding one more spin to the tally.Double Lucky Line (Just For The Win): VerdictWhatever your feelings are on Asian styled slots will more or less determine your opinion of Double Lucky Line. We wanted to kick off the verdict by acknowledging the positive aspects before launching into a critique but struggled to think of one.So, on to the constructive criticism. First, the graphics are sub-par. Just for the Win might not be famous for hardcore, volatile slots that spew forth mountains of coins, but they at least usually produce good looking games. Double Lucky Line is an exception to the rule. It’s plain and uninspiring. The background is a dull green wallpaper, and considering the theme, it has nothing of the flamboyant over the top vibe that can carry an Asian themed slot. Gamblers who play these sorts of games want to feel like they have rocked up to the Grand Lisboa in Macau, not some dingy Chinese takeaways that failed a hygiene inspection.The lucky line with its double symbols is a nice idea, but it means that for the majority of the time, players are stuck on the first two reels. Occasional combos move beyond that to the third, and rarely on to the fourth reel. Once in a long while you get something across all reels and it feels like a significant triumph, whatever the win was. There is no official word on max potential, but since everything else is the same as Tweethearts, you can expect a similar figure of up to 2,500 times the stake.Double Lucky Line manages to pack a stack of Asian themed clichés into its 5, sorry 15, reels. The result though is a limp slot that is less appealing than the mould it was cloned from. The lack of originality and wow factor means that only hardcore fans of this type of slot need apply. Of course, casuals might dig the hit frequency, but the constant drip-drip win effect is like Chinese water torture that will slowly drive you mad.

Title: Book of Spies: Mission X
review: Book of Spies Mission X: Slot OverviewBased in sunny Marbella, Spearhead Studios is the name of the team behind espionage-themed slot Book of Spies Mission X. We’d say creative team, but they have received help putting Book of Spies together. As you can no doubt gather from the 'Book of' inspired title, there is plenty of expanding symbol action during free spins. However, it’s not the only star attraction. Working alongside it are a suite of trademarked features on license from Nolimit City, namely xNudge™ Wild Multipliers and xWays™ Mystery Symbols.Where Spearhead has added a personal touch is in the way they’ve packaged everything. The star of the show is Lara Jones who, as it turns out, has popped up in previous Spearhead games. Her name is a combination of Lara Croft and Indiana Jones, so she is clearly the adventurous type. She’ll need to harness her hacking skills in Book of Spies where she is up against a bunch of modern digital crooks. Fortunately, she’s got a team backing her up along with a stack of features.The code-cracking action takes place on a 5x4 grid, offering 1,024 ways to win. That already sounds pretty mental when you factor in the pay-all-way expanding symbols, but it can get bigger thanks to Nolimit’s on-loan features. Surrounding the game grid are guns, bullets, computer drives, all set against a blurred city skyline. A Mission Impossible-style soundtrack hums away giving Book of Spies a modern espionage feel, not a million miles from The Vault by Snowborn Games.Players can do their crime-busting on all devices, by setting bets from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. When it comes to stats, Spearhead has made the most of the Nolimit license to go large, in almost all respects. Maybe not RTP so much, though there will be few complaints with a rating of 96.1%. Volatility, on the other hand, is ‘very high’ and testing confirmed the game could swing like a psychopathic Bond villain’s mood in a moment. Dedicated gamblers will appreciate the approach since Spearhead has paired the volatile gaming with a massive claimed potential that takes full advantage of the ‘x’ prefaced features.Wins are paid for combinations of three or more matching symbols landing on adjacent reels. Glow-light 9-A royals lead the paytable, followed by four characters – Extreme Harry Hack, Big Tech Terry, One Shot Suzie, and Evil Spy Master who looks a lot like the card-playing evil spymaster from Casino Royale. Land five baddies to reap rewards of 5 to 15 times the stake.Book of Spies Mission X: Slot FeaturesBook of Spies - free spinsThere's a lot of bells and whistles here as Spearhead decided to pack as many features as they could possibly fit. The features are a real mash-up of xNudge Wild Multipliers, xWays Mystery Symbols, and Free Spins where expanding symbols come into play.xWays Mystery symbols land to reveal 2 to 4 of the same symbol, expanding the reel up to 7 symbols high, increasing the number of possible ways. This could be any symbol except wilds or the tumbling scatters. During the base game, one Mystery Symbol can appear on each of the reels 1, 3, or 5, while in free spins they can land anywhere. So at the most, win ways can increase to 5,488 in the base game or 16,807 in the bonus.Pistol waving Lara Jones is printed on the xNudge Wild, landing on reels 2 or 4. It is always nudged to cover the full reel, each nudge increasing its Multiplier by +1 to a maximum of x4, or if combined with an xWays Mystery Symbol up to x7.Two Wild Multipliers at the same time in a win have their values multiplied together.To trigger Secret Agent Free Spins, 3 tumbling bonus scatter symbols must land on reels 1, 3, and 5 simultaneously. The amount of spins awarded is equal to the number of nudges required to move the scatters to the bottom position of its reel. Each nudge equals one free spin, so 3 to 21 are possible.Before free spins start, one of the four premiums is randomly selected to be the special symbol. After a spin has been evaluated, if 3 or more reels contain one of the special symbols, they expand to cover all positions. Expanded symbols pay anywhere; they do not have to be adjacent to each other. Free spins can be retriggered, and the same special symbol is used throughout in this case.The last feature is a bonus buy option where these sorts of things are allowed. For the cost of 70x the bet, players are awarded a straight 10 free spins.Book of Spies Mission X: Slot VerdictSpearhead has a couple ‘Book of’ style games in their portfolio now and the mechanic continues to prove it can be used anywhere. The interesting thing about it is the game isn’t solely focused on expanding symbols. Nolimit’s ‘x’ features manage to hog a lot of the limelight, meaning Book of Spies isn’t just about getting lucky with the right symbol selection, then having it appear in great numbers during free spins. It has that element for sure, but a lot more besides.Licensing Nolimit’s features have had a twofold result. One, it ups Spearhead’s profile, putting them on more players’ radars. Secondly, it makes for some pretty exciting gaming. xNudge Wilds are hugely effective when more than one moves into position building up a juicy multiplier. They can be the key to a good bonus round or not - often more so than the expanding symbols.In regards to chosen symbols, the one you want is the Le Chiffre looking baddy. Theoretically expanding him across the board would net at least 15,360x the bet. Much more than your typical Ra based game. Some may scoff at the likelihood of that happening, but Spearhead claim max wins in Book of Spies approach 27,000x the stake.When you break Book of Spies down to its constituent parts nothing is new. ‘Book’ slots are a dime a thousand, yet Spearhead offers a fairly refreshing take on this style. The somewhat gloomy look and average visuals might put some people off, but an enjoyable spy mood sets in while playing, and the way the studio has done things like naming characters to deepen the game world is appreciated.Make no mistake; this is no jolly gentleman Bond flick. There’s no parachuting into enemy territory while holding a Martini, wiping out SMERSH, bedding 13 women and being back in London without creasing your tux. This is rough around the edges espionage, volatile as you like backed by big rewards for successful hacks.

Title: Panda Bonanza
review: Panda Bonanza: Slot OverviewFor decades, China has gifted or leased panda bears to numerous countries around the world as part of what's been labelled 'panda diplomacy', using the bears to strengthen relations and as a sign of friendship. Panda bears are cute, and this form of soft power does tug the heartstrings harder than a container ship full of reasonably priced consumer goods. Pandas have also been flexing their soft power in the online gambling world, too. Following releases such as Cash Pandas, Pandastic Adventure, Fat Panda, Eye of the Panda, Panda Money Megaways, and Shaolin Panda Chaos Reels, Games Global studio Northern Lights Gaming is getting in on the black and white furball act with Panda Bonanza.Panda Bonanza is linked to Monkey Bonanza, another cute animal slot, released roughly a year or so before this one. Monkeys are on a break this time, as panda bears take the leading role. Part of Northern Lights Gaming's success with Monkey Bonanza surely must be attributed to the game's charming look, which the studio has poured on for Panda Bonanza, too. A bamboo forest is where the game lies, and a friendly panda can be found on one side of the screen while his friendly pals land on the reels. The sun dips for the free spins round, where the panda character dons a pair of shutter shades, so you know he's getting ready to party, and hopefully sling some coins players' way.Panda Bonanza slot - base gameMathematically, Panda Bonanza is a medium volatile online slot, maxing its RTP at 96.01% of the three models available. The stake range is 20 c to $/€40 per spin, and players can buy free spins or use a gamble feature to attempt entering them. The bamboo-lashed game grid makes use of a 5x3 layout while 10 paylines are included for landing winning combinations along.Royals covered in forest stuff, J-A are Panda Bonanza's lower pay symbol group, awarding 0.5 to 2 times the bet for a 5 OAK winning combination. Its higher symbols are a bird, a mouse, a snake, and another furry friend, paying 2 to 8 times the bet for a 5-matching symbol win. Wilds substitute all regular pay symbols and appear on all reels in the base game, as well as the Pandamonium Bonus. Hitting a line of 5 wilds pays 10 times the bet.Panda Bonanza: Slot FeaturesPanda Bonanza slot - bonus gamePanda Bonanza does largely what Monkey Bonanza did - plus a bit more. The features in the game are the Pandamonium Bonus, Pandemonium Spin, Piggy Bank & Win, Pot Bonus, free spins, and bonus buys.Pandamonium Bonus & Panadamonium SpinThe Jumbo Panda appears on the centre reel as a 1x3, 2x3, or 3x3 sized symbol in the base game. The 1x3 and 2x3 versions can be nudged randomly into a 3x3 Jumbo Panda symbol. When the Jumbo Panda lands fully in the base game, it triggers the Pandamonium Bonus. The Pandamonium Bonus starts with 3 respins on reels that land only Pandas or wilds. If any Panda or wild symbol lands, the number of respins returns to 3. Wild symbols which land are held on the reels. Panda symbols that land remove symbols on the Bamboo Splat bar from lowest to highest. When no respins remain, 1 Pandemonium spin occurs: The reels spin with the held wilds and any symbols remaining on the Bamboo Splat bar. Wins are awarded after the spin. Each wild can pay up to 5x.Piggy Bank & WinCoin symbols appear in the base game and in free spins. Each coin reveals a cash prize of 0.2 to 10 times the bet. Landing a +1 Coin symbol adds to the Panda Coin Multiplier, which can go up to x10 and applies to any Piggy Bank wins. +1 Coins appear in the base game and in free spins. The multiplier resets to x1 after being used in a Piggy Bank feature. A random multiplier is used when buying or gambling into free spins. The Collect symbol is present on the rightmost reel. It collects and awards the Cash Prizes on the reels. The Piggy Bank & Win is available in the base and free spins game.Pot BonusIn the main game or free spins, landing a Yin and a Yang symbol on the leftmost and rightmost reels, respectively, triggers the Pot Bonus. Players win 1 Pot Prize - the 20x Mini, the 50x Minor, the 500x Major, or the 5,000x Grand.Free SpinsFree spins scatter symbols land on reels 1, 3, and 5 in the base game. Landing 3 scatters awards 8 free spins where jumbo symbols appear on the centre 3 reels. Jumbo symbols can be 1x3, 2x3, or 3x3 in size. All regular symbols in free spins can appear as jumbo symbols, which split into individual symbols to pay. Jumbo coins and +1 coins may also land.Bonus BuyAt the bonus buy, players can buy the free spins round for 100x the bet or gamble on an adjustable wheel to try and win free spins.Panda Bonanza slot - free spinsPanda Bonanza: Slot VerdictLike a lot of follow-ups or sequels, Panda Bonanza builds off the slot that came before it by reusing pretty much everything (mechanically as well as vibe) while adding a bit more. Monkey Bonanza's set of features is back: the Banana Bonanza, the Super Monkey Spin, the Piggy Bank & Win, and free spins, though tweaked around the edges. Many have been renamed to reflect the leading animal change-up. Even if Northern Lights Gaming had left things here, players who fell for the charms of Monkey Bonanza would likely have been able to effortlessly transition to its panda counterpart. However, the studio did not just switch skins but expanded the game with an extra feature or two. Not the max win, though. That stays the same at 5,000 times the bet.The additions, while by no means negative changes, aren't crazy amazing. The Pot Bonus, for one, is a standard quad jackpot feature. Trigger it, win a Pot Prize, done, the sort of stuff you find in countless Games Global studios' slots. The other is the coin multiplier. Again, it's a handy add-on but not the most innovative idea Northern Lights Gaming might have come up with. But Panda Bonanza isn't a game that's trying to freak gamblers out from the fringes, show them things they didn't dare believe were possible. Like the Monkey Bonanza before it, Panda Bonanza is a well presented game, packing colourful characters and a familiar batch of features, the likes of which should sit well amongst followers of the Games Global family's style of work. Those weary of the local jackpot trend that the almost every Games Global studio seems adamant on sticking too, however, are unlikely to have their opinions swayed by this release.

Title: Professor Clank’s Combinator
review: Professor Clank's Combinator: Slot OverviewIt appears Australian developer ReelPlay has taken a slight hiatus from loading the market with Infinity Reels slots to concentrate on things like their 10K Ways mechanic, as well as brand new projects. One of the new projects to come flying from the ReelPlay production line is Professor Clank's Combinator. This is a scientific explosion of sights, sounds, and rambunctious characters, alongside such features as Explosions, Morphs, Boosters, and a unique Bonus Respins round.Apologies if this sounds judgmental, but with a name like Professor Clank, we had visions of all sorts of wacky scientific activity going on. Apparently, so did ReelPlay, who designed a Steampunk-esque workshop packed to the rafters with all sorts of brass-based gadgetry. With a similar visual quality to Money Mariachi, Professor Clank's Combinator is a very colourful slot where the workshop fizzes, pops and jiggles in time to the action taking place on the reels. The mechanical mayhem works too, and Professor Clank's Combinator has a playful Machinarium, Bioshock Infinite feel that made it fun to review.The cranking and clanking occurs on an initial 6-reel, 3-row game grid that provides up to 707 ways to win. Playable on all devices, tickets to Clank's experiment start at 0.25 p/c before rising to $/€25 per spin. Approximately every fourth spin fires off a win in what is a low volatile slot, producing a theoretical return value of 96.01%.Professor Clank's Combinator's paytable starts with welded steel looking card royals (9-A), paying 0.5 to 1.2 times the stake for six of a kind, then higher value spanners, goggles, blasters, and robots which are worth 2-10x the bet for six of a kind. The Professor wild symbol appears on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5 to replace all symbols except the scatter.Professor Clank's Combinator: Slot FeaturesThe main goal in Professor Clank's Combinator is its Bonus Respin feature, but on the way, players benefit from Explosions, Morphs, Boosters, and Drops, which are all interconnected. Let's take a look.Explosions, Morphs, Boosters & DropsWhen a winning combination hits, all non-winning symbols, except scatters, are removed from the reels. Those that remain drop to the lowest position available on their reel. After explosions have taken place, if more than one symbol type remains, they all morph into the highest paying symbol present. After Explosions and Morphs, if any previously winning symbol is no longer in a winning position, extra matching symbols are added to one or more adjacent reels to make it a winning symbol.After Explosions, Morphs, or Boosters have occurred, a new symbol is dropped onto the top of each column which is less than 5 symbols high. Any dropped symbol that improves the win is kept, others (except scatters) explode. If the new symbol win value is greater than it was before the Drop, an extra Drop is triggered. When no more Drops occur, the final win value is awarded.Bonus RespinsHitting 5 or more scatter symbols gains you access to the Bonus Respins round. All non-scatter symbols explode, drop to the bottom of the grid, and 3 respins are awarded. For each respin, a new symbol is dropped onto each column which is less than five symbols high. New scatter symbols are held, and they reset the spin count while non-scatter symbols explode. When respins run out, each scatter in view awards a cash prize of 1-100x the bet or a bonus prize. Bonus prizes are named Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum, worth 10x, 50x, 250x, or 2,000x the bet, respectively.GambleWhen the bonus round ends, players have the option of gambling the winning total. This can be done up to three times by spinning a green and black segmented wheel. You can choose to multiply the winnings by 1.25x to 10x and whether to risk half or all of the winning amount.Buy BonusEligible players have the option of buying the Bonus Respins feature for the cost of 50x the bet. This triggers a spin where at least five scatters land.Professor Clank's Combinator: Slot VerdictProfessor Clank's features might appear slightly complicated in written form, but in practice, they are straightforward. In the base game, it's a matter of landing winning combinations, then hoping additional matching symbols are added to improve the win. Same in the bonus game, really – hit as many prize symbols as possible before spins run out and collect the winnings. Or, gamble them for a chance to improve the win. However, unlike the sorts of gamble features ReelPlay has used in games like Bananaz 10K Ways, being unsuccessful means you lose the lot rather than drop down a notch on a multiplier trail.To be fair, the convoluted paytable instructions kind of suited Professor Clanks' Combinator's intricately designed Steampunk scientist in a lab scenario. With the theme, ReelPlay has come up trumps, and the activity taking place off the reels can be as exciting as on it. In a way, because winning possibilities in Professor Clank are pretty decent, where a win cap of 10,000x the bet has been put in place. Well, that's the limit ReelPlay has placed on the gamble feature. Outside this, the realistic max win is likely to be less impressive.Nevertheless, with the building element of the Explosion/Morph/Drop thing in the base game, decent wins are technically possible there, too. Bonus Respins are quite interesting as well, having a streak respin origin but with a new stacking twist. The low volatility might be a show stopper for some, and on the whole, Professor Clank's Combinator pours forth plenty of smoke and fireworks, yet it's hardly a heavyweight contender.That is unlikely to matter much to players drawn to Professor Clank's Combinator's excellent presentation, ReelPlay having done a great job with the playful, eccentric scientist trope. Professor Clank's Combinator's respins had a similar feel to Nunchucks Chicken's bonus round, too, so the game might appeal to players who appreciate a Tetris-like element while gambling online.

Title: Ozzy Osbourne
review: Ozzy Osbourne Slot (NetEnt): OverviewEven if you're not a metalhead, it's unlikely you've never heard of Ozzy Osbourne. To most, he's known as a heavy metal pioneer with a career spanning four decades and whose music remains as relevant today as ever. To others, he's best known as the confused rock star dad from the reality show The Osbournes. Gambling degenerates might also know him as the face of Metal Casino. Already involved in the casino industry, it's not all that surprising to see him appear in a slot of his own that sees NetEnt further expand its portfolio of branded rock-themed slots that also includes titles such as Guns n' Roses, Jimi Hendrix and Motörhead.Having been shrouded in great secrecy by NetEnt, we had no idea what to expect when booting up the slot for the first time. Fans of Ozzy will undoubtedly get a kick out of the splash screen in which The Prince of Darkness can be seen sitting on his throne whilst the hit track Mr. Crowley can be heard blasting from the speakers. Mechanically, it's not quite as exciting, but the foundation on which the game is built is solid. Glued together by 20 fixed paylines, the classic 5-reel, 3-row layout almost stands as a testament to the resilience of Ozzy himself. Playable from 0.20 to €/$100 per spin, the Ozzy Osbourne video slot is a medium variance offering that comes with two RTP settings. More on that further below.The game is nicely designed in 1980s comic book style, reminding us a bit of Red Tiger's 2019 release Devil's Number. Dark, sinister and gloomy, the reels are set against the entrance of a temple flanked by two demons and with the Ozzy Osbourne logo positioned at the top. Of course, you'll also hear various guitar licks and clips of original Ozzy tracks playing throughout the session such as Diary of a Madman and Bark at the Moon. Spinning on the reels you'll see 4 lower value symbols in the form of roses, crucifixes, skulls, and ravens. The 4 premiums are all portrayed by Ozzy himself with the bat-eating version of him being the most rewarding, giving you 50 times your stake for a combination of five on a full payline. The devil bat is the wild, it substitutes for all symbols bar the scatter and appears on all reels.Ozzy Osbourne Slot (NetEnt): FeaturesOzzy Osbourne main gameThe Ozzy Osbourne video slot comes packed to the brim with features. Before you start playing, however, it can probably be a good idea to decide whether you want to play with the Bonus Bet option enabled or not. Activating it will cost you twice as much playing (i.e. a bet size of €1 will increase to €2), but in turn you get to play with several significant benefits - hit frequency, bonus frequency, and multiplier values will all increase as well as giving you one extra free spin when triggered. Keep reading for more details.Moving on to the features, keep an eye out for the scatter symbol which appears on reels 1, 3, and 5. If you land two during the base game, the Re-Spin feature comes into play whilst also activating the Charge Up feature. In the upper left corner, the Symbol Spinner box defines the symbol. Next, the Feature Spinner box in the upper right corner defines the feature that is applied to this chosen symbol for the Re-Spin. If a scatter symbol appears on the Symbol Spinner, the Bat Head appears on the Feature Spinner, prompting the Free Spins to trigger after the Re-Spin feature.You can also activate the Free Spins feature the traditional way by landing 3 scatter symbols on reels 1, 3, and 5 simultaneously. Now, if you have activated the Bonus Bet, you get 5 free spins. Otherwise, you only get 4. Once in, you'll benefit from the Symbol Charge-Up feature triggering on every spin. Again; first, the Symbol Spinner defines the symbol while the Feature Spinner defines the feature that is applied to the chosen symbol until the end of the feature. If the Symbol Spinner reveals a scatter symbol during the free spins feature, one extra free spin is awarded up to a total of 7.Central to the action in the Ozzy Osbourne video slot is the Symbol Charge-Up feature. These are the features that can be revealed in the Feature Spinner box:Coin Win - Each chosen symbol that appears in view awards a coin prize equal to a 3 of a kind winSymbol Multiplier - All winning combinations with the chosen symbol receive a multiplier boost by the awarded multiplier. With the Bonus Bet option enabled, the multiplier values are 5x and 7x (which can combine to 12x) as opposed to 2x and 3x when deactivated.Wild - All instances of the chosen symbol are transformed into wilds.Upgrade - All instances of the chosen symbol will transform into the next premium symbol in the paytable for increased wins.Ozzy Osbourne Slot (NetEnt): VerdictLike many of NetEnt's branded titles, Ozzy Osbourne is quite an average slot. For a game that's based on an artist that became known for chewing on bat heads on stage, the slot is disappointingly tame. Moreover, with the features being so confusing, we can't help but feel that the developers have over-complicated the game a bit. It's certainly not a slot that you'll understand from the get-go. For most players, it will take quite a few spins before things start to make any sense.Unless you're a fan of Ozzy, there isn't that much here to get you on the hook. Even the payouts are quite disappointing. Although NetEnt's data sheet seems to imply that the game theoretically should be able to reward wins of over 10,000x, this was never achieved during a cycle of over 9 billion spins. Realistically speaking, don't expect to see wins of over 2,500x here.In the free spins feature, expect most returns to be around 40-100x. Moreover, activating the Bonus Bet option has a dramatic effect on the gameplay as it allocates significantly more RTP to the free spins feature instead of the base game. The free spins frequency also increases quite significantly.The Ozzy Osbourne slot comes across as more of a show-off product for NetEnt than anything else. Yes, fans of Ozzy will probably like it for the familiar imagery and music, and some might like the style of the game, but the majority of players will move on once the novelty wears off - which shouldn't take too long.If you're a fan of branded slots we suggest you also look into NetEnt's 2020 release Street Fighter 2. Based on the iconic 1991 arcade video game, the Street Fighter 2 slot utilises NetEnt's Avalanche and cluster pays system.

Title: Wilhelm Tell
review: Wilhelm Tell (Yggdrasil): OverviewThough known as little more than just a bedtime story for most of us, the legend of Wilhelm Tell actually has quite a profound meaning. A folk hero of Switzerland and an excellent crossbow marksman, the legend has it that Wilhelm assassinated a tyrannical ruler that encouraged the people to open rebellion, eventually marking the very foundation of the Swiss Confederacy. So what's up with the kid and the apple? Well, having refused to bow to the tyranny, Tell was consequently sentenced to death for his defiance, as was his son. However, Tell was told he could redeem their lives by shooting an apple off the head of his kid Walter in just one try, which he did.Based on the famous Swiss legend comes this 5-reel, 20-payline slot from Swedish provider Yggdrasil Gaming. It's relatively simple in gameplay and only involves two features - Stacked Wild Reels that can nudge into position and a Free Spins bonus with 3 games to choose from, one offering a multiplier of up to 50x. Wilhelm Tell comes shipped with a relatively high RTP of 97.0% which is always appreciated and can be played on any device from between 0.10 to 50€ per spin, making it a suitable slot for all gambling budgets.Set in a summery mountain valley, in the backdrop you'll see green hills, snow-capped mountains and a sleepy village. What immediately stands out with great effect, however, is the background music. The waltz soundtrack includes two tracks, a relaxed version that plays when you leave the game on idle and a more intense waltz that plays when you spin the reels. The sound effects, on the other hand, have been recycled from the old Yggdrasil database and will be recognisable to most who have played their games.The reels are dominated by 4 low-value card suit symbols - hearts, diamonds, clubs and spades. The high paying symbols are represented by various characters - the knight's guard, Wilhelm Tell himself and his nemesis, Gessler, the evil tyrant. It is Gessler that is the most rewarding out of the standard symbols, giving you 7.5 times your stake for 5 on a full payline.The wild symbol is represented by Wilhelm's son Walter, illustrated by an image of him tied to a tree with an apple on his head as we know him from literature. Walter is actually the leading character in Yggdrasil's interpretation of the legend. Not only is he the wild, but he also appears fully stacked on the reels as well. Furthermore, the wild comes with a nudge feature which means it will nudge to cover the full reel if a winning combination is guaranteed. It's possible to land a full-screen wilds this way which will give you 150 times your stake in the base game. Where you really want to do it, however, is in the free spins, which leads us to the next chapter in the legend of Wilhelm Tell.Wilhelm Tell (Yggdrasil): FeaturesFree spins featureWith minimal potential in the base game, Wilhelm Tell is all about the Free Spins bonus which you are granted access to when you land 3 or more scatter symbols anywhere on the reels. We always appreciate slots that give something extra for landing all 5 scatters. If you do so in this game, you'll pocket the scatter jackpot of 500 times your total stake. Anyway, once having activated the free spins, you'll be faced with 3 options:Play the bonus with 10 free spins and a multiplier of x5 (750 times your stake per spin).Play the bonus with 5 free spins and a multiplier of x10 (1500 times your stake per spin).Play the bonus with 1 free spin and a multiplier of x50 (7500 times your stake per spin).You cannot retrigger the bonus so make good use of that single free spin if you choose to opt for the x50 multiplier option. Extremely volatile as this option may be, it can potentially lead to wins of up to 7500 times your stake, although as you should understand, it's extremely unlikely ever to happen.Wilhelm Tell (Yggdrasil): VerdictWilhelm Tell is a hit or miss in the literal sense of the word. With little potential in the base game, it's a waiting game to gain access to the free spins. To us, the 5 free spins option seemed like the most sensible choice as you get some playtime along with a reasonable chance of landing some decent wins. The 1 free spins option is really only for the more adventurous gambler or those who have an adequate balance.Production-wise, there's nothing negative to say though we're not overly impressed either. While Yggdrasil slots are generally of very high quality when it comes to design, there's often something slightly off with the gameplay that is hard to pinpoint. It could just be that we haven't had much luck playing their games, and judging by the big wins shared on social media, others don't seem to be very lucky either.Overall, Wilhelm Tell is a decent slot that is more or less saved by its high potential, giving it the necessary kick needed to keep you from nodding off from the rhythmic beat of the waltz.

Title: Dorks of the Deep
review: Dorks of the Deep: Slot OverviewThe vast blue oceans are some of the least explored parts of planet Earth. Home to a myriad of life forms, one of the last things an intrepid explorer would expect to find beneath the waves is a 'dork', surely? Ah well, we're about to review an online slot, not watch a documentary, so creative license means the game's maker, Hacksaw Gaming, is free to let its mind wander where reality might not. The result is Dorks of the Deep, and as well as dorks, lucky deep sea divers in these parts may be rewarded with a finely tuned full reel wild with multiplier feature.The deeper one dives in the sea, the darker it gets as the water molecules and other particles absorb and scatter light. Dive deep enough, actually not that deep, around 200m or so, and the ocean is essentially pitch black. In other words, gamblers don't head too far down to play Dorks of the Deep, which is, by contrast, a brightly colourful place to take a dip. It's kind of dorky, maybe not Dork Unit (2022) level, but a quirky cast of characters such as the Octopus, Mermaid and the Ocean King greet visitors to their watery, columned domain. The first impressions were bubbly, as if Dorks of the Deep was designed by the sector of Hacksaw HQ that deals in charming wootsy-looking slots.Dorks of the Deep slot - base gameFramed in a smart white trim, Dorks of the Deep's 5x4 matrix comes equipped with 14 paylines calculating winning combinations of 3 or more of a kind. It is a medium volatile slot made with four RTP configurations, so if you want the highest return value, look out for the 96.2% variant. You can't buy the top tier bonus round, but four other bonus buy modes are available, as are stakes of 10 c to $/€100.Bubble-wrapped 10-A card ranks are Dorks of the Deep's low pay symbols, awarding 0.8 to 1.5 times the stake for a 5-of-a-kind hit. Next come 3 fish symbols, the Mermaid and the Ocean King, as the high pays, awarding 2 to 10 times the stake for 5-of-a-kind. Wilds hit anywhere to substitute for any paying symbols or award 10x the bet for a line of 5 wilds.Dorks of the Deep: Slot FeaturesDorks of the Deep slot - free spinsFloating about the deep are Expanding Wild Reels (with multipliers), a Deep Blue bonus, the Down Under bonus, a Hidden Treasure bonus, and feature buys.Expanding Wild ReelsWhen a Treasure Chest symbol hits, it expands into a wild reel if it is part of a win once expanded. Each position on the reel counts as wild. Expanded Wild Reels are fully stacked and display the Octopus, Mermaid, or Ocean King character. Each character comes with a different set of multiplier values. The Octopus has multipliers of x2 to x9, the Mermaid x10 to x20, and the Ocean King x25 to x200. The multiplier is applied to all winning combinations passing through the full reel wild, which substitutes for all paying symbols.Deep Blue Bonus GameLanding 3 FS scatters in the base game awards 10 free Deep Blue bonus game spins. During free spins, the Treasure Chest symbol always expands to become a Wild Reel, whether part of a win or not. Expanded Wilds reveal 0-3 lives and are sticky into the next spin as long as they have lives left. One life is removed from each sticky Wild Reel at the start of each free spin. Also, at the start of each free spin, sticky Wild Reels receive a new random multiplier from any of the 3 characters.If there is at least one Wild Reel with one or more lives remaining on the final free spin, the Last Chance feature activates, awarding free respins to keep the bonus going until no Wild Reels have lives left. New Treasure Chests may land during the Last Chance, turning into expanded Wild Reels with or without lives. The round ends when there are no more spins and no Wild Reels have lives remaining. Hitting 2 or 3 FS scatters during the round awards a further +2 or +4 spins, respectively.Down Under Bonus GameLanding 4 FS scatters in the base game triggers 10 free spins in the Down Under bonus game. This feature has the same rules as the Deep Blue bonus; plus, sticky expanded Wild Reels never receive a multiplier from a lower character tier than the initially revealed tier.Hidden Treasure Bonus GameHitting 5 scatters in the base game triggers this feature where players get 10 free spins. This bonus has the same rules as the Down Under bonus, with the addition of 2 expanded Wild Reels active on the grid at all times till the feature ends.Feature BuysActivating BonusHunt FeatureSpins makes each spin 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game for 3x the bet, or at 60x the bet, Bubbly FeatureSpins guarantee 2 Treasure Chests land on each spin, though FS scatters cannot in this mode. The Deep Blue bonus costs 100x to buy, while the Down Under bonus carries a 200x price tag.Dorks of the Deep slot - free spinsDorks of the Deep: Slot VerdictDorks of the Deep may look all innocent on the outside as if players are dipping their toes into warm water devoid of creepy creatures. But, spend a bit longer paddling around, and it soon becomes apparent that the game means about as much business as any other Hacksaw Gaming slot. It is fun spinning alongside a trio of cheerful chums, though how dorky they are is up for discussion. However, if you desire a slot's presentation to provide a pick me up or to turn a frown upside down, then the bright, watery realm on display here might be just the ticket.Maybe don't be counting on Dorks of the Deep's gameplay to be as uplifting if the symbols aren't falling your way, though. Just saying. On the flip side, the expanding wild multipliers on show here are a heavy-duty component. They might not be as complex as some of the features Hacksaw Gaming produces, but for transforming a grid, they're hard to beat - expand, substitute, and multiply. Done. Complexity has been added by the way the various characters adorning the wild have differing multiplier tiers, and the sticky lives system is an added bonus. Speaking of bonuses, you may have noticed the Hidden Treasure round cannot be bought, and since players get 2 expanded Wild Reels at all times during it, then that is the place to be and provides motivation for chasing an elusive fifth base game scatter.A 10,000x max win that can be hit in all game modes provides further motivation to keep on paddling in a game which may seem friendly after a quick peek, but rest assured, Hacksaw Gaming has injected the sort of features and gameplay that can alternate between rough, choppy, and relatively smooth sailing.

Title: Big Boom Riches
review: Big Boom Riches: Slot OverviewThe gold mining theme proves irresistible to developers once again, and this time it is Just For The Win leading players underground to scour for the stuff. It's a risky choice; on the one hand, you've got designers like Nolimit City blowing the genre wide apart with games like Fire in the Hole xWays, or Big Time Gaming with their timeless classic Bonanza, and others who churn out more generic gaming that barely raises an eyebrow. Let's not name any names. Big Boom Riches sits in the middle of the scale somewhere, being neither great nor a write-off. If you're keen on swinging a pickaxe at some rocks in the hopes of striking pay dirt, read on.The game starts off a little differently than most, where the base game takes place above ground in a pastel rich environment bearing a strong North American feel. The prospector reinforces this notion as well. Not only do players get a stereotypical gold miner, all floppy hat, big white beard, overalls and one remaining tooth on the reels. He also comments on the action throughout, kicking off the game by pronouncing 'Welcome miners, a fine day for gold', or something like that through a friendly Southern drawl. Other audio includes a toe-tapping banjo led number, creating an enjoyable audio-visual experience on the whole.One thing that's perhaps not so great is the diminutive size of the 5-reel, 3-row game grid, absolutely dwarfed by the mountainous background. Lining the grid are 20 betways where players land winning combinations of three or more matching symbols across. Wins occur at a rate of around 1 in 4 spins, or 27.34%, while the default RTP value is 96.06% - though it can be found low, so it pays to check. Just For The Win have branded the math model highly volatile, with the max win coming from a scatter feature awarding bigger prizes the more you can collect.When winning combinations hit, they set off the Rolling Reels feature, which removes the winning symbols, allowing new ones to drop into the gaps. With Rolling Reels, it's possible to link consecutive wins from a single spin, only stopping when no new win lands and no TNT Wilds or X-Wilds are present. Eight symbols make up the game's paytable. Half are J-A royals; half are purple, green, orange, and pink gems – this latter group is worth a payout of 3 to 15 times the stake.Big Boom Riches: Slot FeaturesBig Boom Riches - free spins with progressive win multiplierWilds play a critical role in Big Boom Riches for a number of reasons, partly because they are used to trigger instant cash prizes. There are 3 of them - a regular wild, an X-Wild, and a TNT Wild. All substitute any pay symbol to complete a win and possess the same values as the top premium. When TNT Wilds or X-Wilds land, they also explode, removing any adjacent symbols, triggering Rolling Reels.In the base game, when 3 or more TNT Wilds land during a cascade (Rolling Reels) sequence, they award a cash prize. The value of the prize is between 1x to 5,000x the bet when 3 - 12 of them land in view.The prospector chap appears on the scatter symbols, and when 3, 4, or 5 hit, 9 free spins are awarded, plus a payout of 2, 20, to 100 times the stake. Title: Gem Crush

Title: Crystal Quest: Deep Jungle

The other ponderable is what the thread running through, tying them all together, will be. Sure the beasts changed, features and stats mixed it up to an extent, but their similar feel made it tricky to tell them apart at times. Will Thunderkick go down the same route in the Gemma series? Title: William Tell & The Wild Arrows
review: William Tell & the Wild Arrows: Slot OverviewWilliam Tell might be most famous for shooting an apple on his son's head, but the Swiss folk hero had a deadlier side to him than that. Had the team done so, William Tell & the Wild Arrows might have felt like a more original production, maybe not as headline-grabbing as a marksman hitting an apple on his son's head, but somewhat original. Title: Magikspell
review: Magikspell: Slot OverviewOnline slot Magikspell comes from the inventive minds at Fantasma Games and sees them return to a grid pattern used in a previous game called Caravan of Riches, a game which had pros and cons, yet ultimately, we were a little hesitant about. All positions with Magik Rings or Golden Rings that did not turn into wilds on the triggering spins are carried over to the bonus round and turned into Prize Gem symbols – these symbols display bet multipliers. Now, 3 spins are awarded, which reset when new Prize Gem symbols hit and lock in place. If all positions on a reel are filled with Prize Gems, their values are collected, then they are removed so new Prize Gems can land. When free spins end, the total values of all Prize Gems are summed and multiplied by the current free spins multiplier. All rings are removed when returned to the base game.Magikspell: Slot VerdictIf you're persistent, Magikspell is a game that can grow on you, literally. The almost parabolic nature of the Free Spins Multiplier is a tantalising prospect, for patient players. Should you manage to make it all the way to the end, the x250 is quite a lure. For some reason, Fantasma chose not to reveal Caravan of Riches' max win, yet when Magikspell fires, wins of up to 20,000x the bet are possible, so being patient could pay off.Having such an ordered progressive element means players are kind of required to make a personal commitment to see Magikspell through till the end. Where most slots can technically unleash everything they've got on the very first spin, it takes time for Magikspell to coyly unveil its big guns. Fortunately, Fantasma has made the journey an eventful one, so optimistic grinders could well have a field day with this.

Title: Rainforest Magic

Title: Santa's Xmas Rush

Title: Leprechaun Goes Wild

Title: Tiger Kingdom Infinity Reels
review: Tiger Kingdom Infinity Reels: Slot OverviewWe're used to seeing developer Relax Gaming powering these Infinity Reels slots, but it's rarer to see the studio use the game engine themselves. First, you need to land matching symbols on all 3 reels. Then, the whole grid moves one position to the left. Winning symbols that fall off the grid are collected, and if the new reel lands new winning symbols, the respin process carries on. When no winning symbol appears on a new reel, the value of all collected symbols is awarded. Key points are that any winning symbols left on the reels are not paid, and added reels do not create multipliers as they do in some other Infinity Reels games.Behind the scenes, Tiger Kingdom is governed by a highly volatile math model, turning out an RTP value of 96.23%. Buy the bonus, and this increases to 96.87%. Any device may be used to play Tiger Kingdom, offering bets from 10 p/c to $/€50. A lot of symbols pop up at various points, including 7 regular pay symbols in the base game. These start with three Asian patterns, each collected one is worth 0.4 to 0.6 times your stake. Up to 2 additional rows can be added. Also, it is possible to land multiplier symbols with values of x2, x3, or x4. Collecting one of these symbols multiples the number of symbols collected up to that point.Tiger Kingdom Infinity Reels: Slot FeaturesCollecting 3 or more bonus symbols during a single spin triggers the bonus game. Do note, the bonus symbols need to be collected or the bonus won't trigger. Once in, the regular pay symbols are removed from the reels. Instead, reels display blank spaces, money symbols, or special symbols. The bonus round starts with 3 spins. If a symbol lands on the third reel, the grid shifts to the left and spins reset to 3. All symbols that fall off the grid on the lefthand side are collected, and the total is awarded when spins run to zero, or the win cap is achieved. Symbols used in the bonus round are:Golden money symbols – reveal a value of 1x to 10x the bet.Red money symbols – reveal a value of 20x to 100x the bet.Yin & Yang – when collected the spin counter reset value increases by 1.Scroll – when collected, an extra row is added to the grid. Two extra rows at most can be added.Collector – collects all other coin values on the reels.Payer – increases the values of up to 3 positions with the value it possesses.Sniper – multiples up to 3 positions with coin values by x2, x3, or x4.There are also Persistent versions of the Collector, Payer, and Sniper. These symbols begin to act when they have been collected and perform their modifier before each spin.Bonus BuyIf available, players may buy the bonus game for the cost of 100x the bet. Doing so immediately launches the bonus round.Tiger Kingdom Infinity Reels: Slot VerdictPerhaps Relax Gaming liked what they saw in Money Mariachi and were inspired to have another crack at the Infinity Reels game engine. Whatever the prompt, players can add an additional MT2 style Infinity Reels game to the list. The good news from a diversity perspective is Tiger Kingdom performs very differently to Money Mariachi. Whilst Money Mariachi's bonus round can take a significant amount of time when the going is good, Tiger Kingdom, by contrast, was like being fired out of a canon.The bonus round is a lot faster paced. Sometimes it's over before you've had a chance to settle in and see what's what. It has no problems bowing out after doling out just a few extra reels creating little in the way of rewards. A quick slap, and you're back to the base game. There isn't much to say about the main game, really, other than just be aware you have to collect symbols as they fall off the grid, which is quite different to how non-Relax made Infinity Reels games usually operate.The positive side is the bonus game occasionally gets on some pretty nifty runs. When the special symbols are boosting the daylights out of pay symbols, persisting, doubling on doubles and so forth, they can build some impressive results. The game is capped at 20,000x the bet, and a win at that level would be hilariously good to see. As to the experience, Tiger Kingdom didn't have the same sense of building an unstoppable momentum as can happen in MT2. It tended to pop in moments, or it didn't pop at all. There's another thing too. It is possible to have a sizeable money symbol sitting on the grid, but it's worthless until it's been shunted off the grid and collected. So, there are times when you miss out on something decent, and the round ends. Other times, you get lucky on the last spin, a symbol lands on the third reel, sliding a desirable money symbol off the board. In this way, Tiger Kingdom can be a bit like those coin pusher arcade games.Relax Gaming are masters of building suspenseful conditions which have to be met to extract reward or be denied. The MT2 style bonus round has been cleverly integrated with the way Infinity Reels functions to create a game that is adept at serving up well-earned rewards if everything falls into place.

Title: Miami Rise

After gaining rank 3, landing a Cash Hit Spins scatter on the second reel plus 2 free spins scatters on reels 3 and 4 awards +5 free spins and upgrades the round to Cash Hit Spins.Cash Hit SpinsIn the base game, hitting a Cash Hit Spins scatter on the second reel plus regular scatters on reels 3 and 4 triggers 5 Cash Hit Spins. Title: Piggy Cluster Hunt
review: Piggy Cluster Hunt: Slot OverviewHey players, if you're in the mood to step into a game 'where the simple joys of rural life blend seamlessly with the exhilarating thrill of gaming,' then we might have a slot for you. At least, that's the description of Piggy Cluster Hunt, its maker and Hacksaw Gaming sister studio, Bullshark Games, has provided in the About The Game section. Sounds alright, too, chilling out in nature, hanging with a porcine chap with a gun, trying to get lucky while spinning a cluster-paying grid slot. Oops, almost said "y'all" there, so in the mood we were getting for this.Piggy Cluster Hunt nails the rural life part, as players join a piggy character at his lake (or river) house, a million miles from the city, where the air is clean, a little chilly from the mountain snow, and the wild nature hasn't been completely sullied by human hands. Not sure about the gun part, though; what exactly is this pig planning on blasting? Pesky mosquitoes? Piggy Cluster Hunt does have Exploding Wilds, too, and they're one of its funner features, though, from a game world perspective, barrels detonating out here in the weeds would spoil the peace of the area.Piggy Cluster Hunt slot - base gameWhere the action takes place is on a 7x7 game board, which uses a cluster pays system to forge wins. When 5 or more identical symbols land next to each other in vertically and/or horizontally adjacent positions, a win is formed. The winning symbols are cleared from the reels, and symbols drop down to replace them by the cascade mechanic, a process that repeats until no new win hits. Garnering a 3 out of 5 rating, Piggy Cluster Hunt is a medium volatile slot, available in two RTP models, where the default return value is 96.23%.Taking bets from 10 c to $/€100 per spin, the objects of the outdoors are Piggy Cluster Hunt's regular paying symbols. They are a compass, rope, a knife, an ammo box, binoculars, a slingshot, a trap, and a bullet casing. Hitting a 5 OAK winning cluster pays out 0.2 to 0.6 times the bet, while the highest cluster levels have 36+ matching symbols in them, and they pay 25 to 300 times the bet. Wilds with the piggy character on them are able to help cobble wins together by substituting for any regular pay symbol.Piggy Cluster Hunt: Slot FeaturesPiggy Cluster Hunt slot - free spinsAs well as cascades, Piggy Cluster Hunt has features such as a progressive win multiplier in all phases of play, Exploding Wilds, free spins, and feature buys.Progressive Win MultiplierAbove the reels sits a multiplier bar with three slots. Each spin populates 0 to 3 win multiplier values in certain positions on the bar – they can be additive values of 2x to 100x or multiplicative values of x2 to x10. The value of the first multiplier is applied to any initial win. After the cascade, if there are additional wins, the first and second multipliers are either added or multiplied together and applied to the wins on the additional cascade. After this, the first, second, and third multipliers are combined and applied to any of the following cascades. Empty multiplier bar positions in the base game mean no multiplier is applied. Free spins cannot have empty positions.Exploding WildsWhen an Exploding Wild lands, it detonates and adds up to 8 extra wild symbols around the original wild. In the base game, at least 2 wilds are added; in free spins, at least 4 wilds are added.Wild Call Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 FS scatter symbols in the base game starts the feature with 8, 12, or 15 free spins, respectively. In free spins, all three positions on the multiplier bar always have values.Buy BonusFour options are presented at the feature buy menu, which are:BonusHunt FeatureSpins – each spin is 3 times more likely to trigger free spins for 2x the bet. Highly volatile, RTP 96.35%.FeatureSpins – each spin guarantees at least 1 Exploding Wild for 10x the bet. Medium volatile, RTP 96.2%.Wild Call Free Spins – 8, 12, or 15 free spins for 100x the bet. Highly volatile, RTP 96.19%.Wild Call Free spins – 8, 12, or 15 free spins where the minimum multiplier in the final position is 5x-10x for 200x the bet. Highly volatile, RTP 96.31%.Piggy Cluster Hunt slot - feature buy menuPiggy Cluster Hunt: Slot VerdictSometimes you play a cluster paying grid slot, and the focus is on collecting winning symbols, triggering features at set collection points, maybe going all the way to win free spins in a rule-heavy, feature-filled experience. Piggy Cluster Hunt, by contrast, is a relatively simpler game operating a streamlined process with fewer moving parts. So much so that it reawakened memories of partner Hacksaw Gaming's early days. Back when the studio was dropping stuff like Cash Compass, The Bomb, or Forest Fortune, to name three. Before Hacksaw discovered its dark side and began stomping all over the wrong side of the tracks, as such.Bullshark Games isn't quite there yet, but the team has made a playable grid slot that cluster pays groupies might find intriguing. Its significant top prize is 15,000x the bet, which you would assume is technically achievable in the base game and free spins, given the size of the potential multipliers available from the multiplier bar coupled with the higher level symbol payout values. Piggy Cluster Hunt relies on those multipliers a lot, too, as it's not really a game that dramatically snowballs as it progresses, like some can. There is a bit of snowballing when consecutive cascades chain multipliers together, though not like some grid slots can string along. You either get the multiplier values displayed on a spin (then activate them), or you don't. Exploding Wilds are a plus, though, and make a strong contribution to Piggy Cluster Hunt's overall entertainment value.All in all, Piggy Cluster Hunt was a decent cluster pays game. Not a future leader of the pack, perhaps, but Bullshark Games have thought up some neat ideas that fit together nicely when they're playing ball to provide a hard and fast uncomplicated grid slot.

Title: Baron Bloodmore
review: Baron Bloodmore and the Crimson Castle: Slot OverviewPlayers, take a walk on the undead side in Baron Bloodmore and the Crimson Castle, a vampire-themed slot from veteran Swedish developer Thunderkick. The studio has stepped things up for the Baron, where you'll come across a couple of classic features which have been expanded to increase their effects as well as produce a higher than normal max win figure we are used to seeing from this developer.With a look suggestive of their Beat the Beast range, you know you are playing a Thunderkick game when Baron Bloodmore fires up. Wilds substitute for pay symbols to complete winning lines, and if they land in combinations of their own, they have the same value as Baron Bloodmore.Baron Bloodmore and the Crimson Castle: Slot FeaturesOn the surface, mystery symbols, free spins, plus a hold-&-win feature might not sound cutting edge, but Thunderkick has added a few original touches to neaten them up and make them rather original.What's different about mystery symbols here is they are massive in size. They appear either partially or fully in view on the middle three reels in 3x3 size. Massive mystery symbols turn up completely at random during the base game and on every spin in the free spins bonus round. When it hits, this oversized symbol randomly changes into a pay symbol or a wild.Winged skull symbols are the scatters, and 3, 4, or 5 in view award 10, 15, or 20 free spins (which cannot be retriggered). As mentioned above, the main benefit here is that massive mystery symbols land on every spin.Baron Bloodmore - Crimson Cash Bonus splash screenSome games might have stopped there, but Baron Bloodmore's central feature is its Crimson Cash Bonus Game. Unlocking it occurs when 3 Cash bonus symbols land on 3 different reels, this is the tile with the castle silhouetted against the moon. When the Crimson Cash Bonus game is active, the normal reels are replaced with a different set which only contain special symbols, bet multiplier symbols (starting at x1 to x50) or empty spaces. Once in, 3 spins start the round, and every time a symbol lands, it locks in place plus resets the counter back to 3. At the end of the bonus round, the values of all bet multipliers are added together before being paid out.Baron Bloodmore - Crimson Cash BonusIt might sound pretty standard so far, yet Thunderkick has included a few extras to mix things up during this bonus round. One is a pattern collection feature. In the bonus game, you'll see a pattern of 5 illuminated symbol positions. When these positions are filled, the bet multiplier of the illuminated symbols is added together. The total amount is added to the middle symbols and then doubled. All affected symbols, except the middle position, are then removed, and a new pattern is generated.Two more symbols round off the bonus round. One is the spawn symbol which adds its own multiplier to all other symbols on the reels. Lastly, when copy Symbols land, the value of all other symbols in view is added to itself.Baron Bloodmore and the Crimson Castle: Slot VerdictAfter the Crystal Quest series sort of just faded away amidst a minimum of fanfare, the Thunderkick team must've felt like launching in a completely different direction. Baron Bloodmore and the Crimson Castle certainly makes a fresh change, odd given the undead nature of its subject matter. There are plenty of positive aspects about Baron Bloodmore that should appeal to players with a soft spot for classic features and straightforward base game rules. The slot is by no means a generic hold-&-spin special though. In Baron Bloodmore and the Crimson Castle, Thunderkick takes old school features and expands them to create something which displays a healthy dose of originality.Proving that small changes can make mighty differences, the tweaks made to the Crimson Cash Bonus Game are subtle yet significant. The pattern system has been put to good use in slots like Play'n GO's Gemix 2, and it works like a charm here as well. The round is nowhere near as sophisticated or gung ho as something like Money Train 2, though potentially it compares quite favourably. At 25,000x the bet, Baron Bloodmore and the Crimson Castle produces some of the biggest wins possible in a Thunderkick game, adding to the undead allure. Free spin rounds aren't quite as spectacular, yet having Massive Mystery Symbols land on every free spin means each one produces a little thrill as you wait to see what goodies will line up.To sum up, Thunderkick has produced a solid vampire-themed game for hardcore gamblers to sink their teeth into - sorry, pun intended. It does things seen elsewhere, but not usually to this extreme, thereby creating some exciting high potential gaming.

Title: Wonders of Christmas
review: Wonders of Christmas: Slot OverviewAs the name says, Wonders of Christmas is a festive online slot from developer NetEnt with a strong Xmas feel. Like many that preceded it, Wonders of Christmas is essentially an Xmas reskin of an older game; in this case, it has branched off from Rome: The Golden Age. A lot of these sorts of Christmas remakes have questionable origins. Sometimes, the most random subject matter is transformed into an Xmas game and has a shedload of snow dumped on them. Wonders of Christmas actually makes a bit more sense since the first recorded celebration of Christmas was at Rome in 336 AD, on, of course, 25 December. With that historical link ticked off, why don't we take a look at what else Wonders of Christmas has to offer?Visually, the base game offers a wintery outdoor scene as if players are part of a troupe of carolers, knocking on doors and singing festive songs for charitable donations. The game's 3-4-5-4-3 aligned game grid sits against a door next to a couple of wreaths, snow, and golden lamp light. Trigger the bonus round, and the action moves inside, where there's even more golden light provided by a roaring fire, heating a room with a cosy armchair decked out with a Christmas tree and stockings ready to be filled with gifts. The overall effect is nice, captures much of the season's spirit, and supplies a warm environment to get down to business.Wonders of Christmas slot by NetEntTraditional visions of modern Christmas are miles away from the Colosseum, but Wonders of Christmas' stats are basically the same as before. This means stake selection of 10 p/c to $/€50 to get the ball rolling in a game that is playable on any device. It's a highly volatile one, too, coming in a quartet of available RTP models, the highest of which is 96.06%. They are Frame Collections, multipliers, and free spins.Frame CollectionsOne symbol to look out for is the Gift Symbol. When these hit, they place a frame around their respective position. Randomly, Gift symbols may transform into Golden Gift symbols, thereby activating their frames. This position turns wild on the following spin while turning connecting framed positions into wilds as well. Frames are removed after this occurs.MultipliersGift Symbols add 1 point to the progress bar if they do not land in a Frame or an Active Frame. If they land in a Frame or an Active Frame, they add 1-4 points to the progress bar. When 200 points have been accrued, the Free Spins Multiplier is increased. Its possible values are x1, x2, x3, x5, x7, x10, x12, x15, x20, x30, x40, x50, x75, x100, x200, x300, x500, x750, or, x1,000. In the base game, the multiplier has no effect. Instead, it comes into play during the free spins round.Free SpinsLanding 3 bonus symbols on reels 2, 3, and 4 triggers the bonus round. It starts with 3 free spins, and any framed positions that did not turn wild on the triggering spin turn into sticky coins worth 0.5-50 times the bet. Only coins are present on the reels during the bonus round, and landing new ones not only sticks them to the grid but resets the spin count back to 3. When no more spins are left, or the grid is full, the feature ends. Each coin value is tallied up, and the multiplier from the base game is applied to the total before being awarded. The multiplier then resets.Wonders of Christmas slot - symbol valuesWonders of Christmas: Slot VerdictAs you might have guessed, whatever your reaction to Rome: The Golden Age was is pretty much going to be bang on, or very similar, when putting Wonders of Christmas to work. NetEnt has kept most things the same as it was in the Ancient Rome outing for its Christmassy shindig, too. The main exception, of course, is the Xmas atmos instead of the previous game's classical Roman stylings. Now the only thing in danger of being hacked with a sharp instrument is the turkey roast dinner when it hits the table.Put aside the change of window dressing, and everything else has sorta remained the same. This means a game where you want to trigger the bonus round, but kinda not too soon, since doing so utilises whatever multiplier has been achieved during the main game. So, the longer you can spend battling it out in the base game, the higher the potential multiplier might well be. As before, the multiplier can technically get rather high indeed, maxing out at a dramatic x1,000. Naturally, reaching as dizzying a height as that ain't a piece of cake - even building a modest multiplier might take its sweet time. Rewards are there, on paper at least (we are yet to so evidence of a max win on this, or even close to it), to the tune of 100,000 times the bet at full whack. Wonders of Christmas doesn't come across as a game which delivers devastating one-hit results, so squeezing it as tightly as possible may well require a sizable dollop of patience, and fortitude, to go along with luck.And so, NetEnt pads out the march of the Christmas clones with another reskin job. Not a bad one either, for players looking for a festive slot that comes with some eye-catching numbers. Wonders of Christmas hitting its impressive max win isn't going to be a regular occurrence, but the theoretical opportunities are there in a game drenched in seasonal good cheer.

Title: Cosmic Voyager
review: Cosmic Voyager: Slot OverviewSome far-out there thinkers have postulated that the pyramids of Egypt were built not by earthlings, but beings from another planet. It probably goes without saying, but the Cosmic Voyager symbol never expands.Cosmic Voyager: Slot VerdictCosmic Voyager is a game that lives up to its name, giving players a bit of galaxy-themed action to work through. Its graphics might appear a little basic, but like its features, they have no problem getting the job done. As in many of the games from this studio, Cosmic Voyager has a distinctly Thunderkick look, all of its own, bolstered by slick animations and effects. There's a touch of Starburst going on, although it is a little hard to avoid the comparison when hosting a 5 reel slot out in the universe. To help differentiate the two, we get planets and unusual geometric shapes instead of gems. There's also a bit of a mystical vibe to the gaming, largely provided by the masked main character who adds a bit of intrigue to set the mood.As far as the gameplay is concerned, it's pretty conventional for the most part with some similarities to their previous slot Sword of Khans. Letting mids or highs payout on two of a kind or higher ensures the hit rate keeps ticking over and plays well with the expanding symbols feature. On the whole, Cosmic Voyager is a nice alternative to 'book of' style expanding symbol features, if you're after something similar yet a little different. Both types offer full reel symbol mechanics where the ultimate goal is filling screens.For some straight forward highly volatile gaming with features that can blow up, Cosmic Voyager is worth taking the time to try. Especially if you're a fan of uncomplicated pacey gaming, expanding symbols, and potentially solid full screen wins.

Title: Dio Killing The Dragon

If a new wild lands in the cage, the process repeats up to a total of four times, as long as new wilds keep landing in the open cages. This feature is only present in the base game.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 scatters symbols awards players with 6, 8, or 12 free spins, respectively. During free spins, a cage is placed around the three middle reels and any wild that lands there become sticky as part of the Wild One feature. Also, a special symbol may land on the fifth reel awarding +2 free spins and triggering one of three modifiers.Fallen Angel – adds a wild at the top of reel 1. This wild moves down one position on each following free spin until it falls off the grid.Symbol Upgrade – the lowest value monster symbol is upgraded to the Dio symbol. Defeat the Dragon when all monsters are upgraded to Dio symbols.Wild Multiplier – one sticky wild in view has its win multiplier increased by +1 up to x5.Dio Killing The Dragon slot - free spinsDio Killing the Dragon: Slot VerdictPlay'n GO has a rather large selection of music slots now, and Dio Killing the Dragon is another solid entry for the right player. Naturally, its appeal will be stronger to fans of the band, but you can say that about a lot, if not all, music-themed slots. Players who bop exclusively to the top 100 hits probably won't have a major interest in playing games like Dio Killing the Dragon, Twisted Sister, or Testament, despite being playable slots. On the other hand, if metal wrapped in castles, monsters, and a truckload of powerful sounds is appealing, then Dio Killing the Dragon is well worth a look.On the topic of looks, Dio Killing the Dragon hearkens back to a certain golden era of heavy metal/heavy rock. Back when bands fell into an arms race of not just churning out heavier and heavier music, but heavier and heavier tape or CD covers. Anyone with fond memories of letting their eyes wander around a music store and being drawn to the most appealing or shocking album cover in the Metal section should be able to relate to the visuals (and sounds) used in Dio Killing the Dragon. The gameplay isn't bad either, which is divided between base game spins with the Lock up the Wolves feature and free spins where a number of triggerable modifiers are available. Lock up the Wolves tended to trigger fairly often in the review, though symbol values aren't enormous, so it didn't always blow up as you might expect. Title: Magic Tricks

Title: Sweet Alchemy 2

Title: Klowns
review: Klowns: Slot OverviewClowns have a bizarre way of being able to perform the role of a knee-slapping, humorous doofus, as well as that of a terrifying beast that haunts your dreams and waking moments. High Symbol Needle Boxes remove the high pay symbols, awarding 0.5x the bet per removed symbol.Lester's Cash CarouselLanding 3 FS scatters triggers 10 Lester's Cash Carousel free spins. Landing 2 FS symbols awards +2 free spins while landing 3 FS symbols awards a further +4 free spins.Jester's JackpotHitting 4 FS symbols in the base game awards Jester's Jackpot 10 free spins. Respins end when no new wild or gem symbols are visible on the reels or the max win is reached.Reign of the Mountain King: Slot VerdictWhile it makes sense SG Digital would want to capitalise on Rise of the Mountain King, a follow up had to really step up to make a bigger impression. Unfortunately, the complete opposite has happened, and Reign of the Mountain King is a lesser game in just about every regard.
