As before, the epic metal rendition of Grieg's 'In the Hall of the Mountain King' rampaging through features is a triumph. However, since respins generally don't last that long, you're quickly back to regular spins where the short blasts of audio have a slight awkwardness that wasn't there before. Basically, Reign of the Mountain King has none of the gleaming finish of the previous game.As to features, Reign's Mountain King Respins can admittedly get quite good. In this case, bigger is better since the longer you can draw out the feature, the better the chance of building some hefty multipliers. The gem collection is similar to the one used in Rise's free spins bonus round, and the potential multipliers here are huge. Yet, Reign never managed to blast off like its predecessor. There was just something about the combination of Rise's Wild Multipliers and King Respins, which could be outrageously good. Another downer is Reign of the Mountain King's reduced winning potential. Where Rise topped out at 50,000x, Reign produces wins of up to 10,000x the bet. An admirable figure in the larger scheme of things, but it is strange to see a sequel lop 40k off the max win figure.To summarise the let downs, RTP is less, potential is a fraction of Rise's, the features have diminished, and Reign doesn't look as impressive. If SG Digital had picked a different theme and not released Reign of the Mountain King as a sequel, the game would have been freer to do its thing without constantly being compared to a superior slot. As it is, sure, Mountain King Respins can be thrilling, but the catalogue of disappointments overrides the game as a whole.

Title: Dungeons and Diamonds
review: Dungeons and Diamonds: Slot OverviewSince 1974, bands of role-players have enjoyed the tabletop game Dungeons & Dragons to create characters, battle beasts, and complete quests, using little more than dice and a fertile imagination. Possessing a piece of litigation sidestepping wordplay is Dungeons and Diamonds, an online slot for players looking for some fantasy-based action from Microgaming partner PearFiction Studios. To date, the PearFiction slots we've encountered, such as Squelin' Riches and Blazing Mammoth, have tended to be okay looking yet somewhat unimaginative in terms of gameplay. Will Dungeons and Diamonds break the trend?The first impression would tend to suggest the answer to that question is no. One reason is the jackpots next to a gold-framed game grid set up is so common by now it appears to be PearFiction's signature move. Visually, Dungeons and Diamonds is quite appealing, possessing a bright, Pragmatic Play style of gloss. Players find themselves in one of those dark, misty caverns where a dragon slumbers on top of a pile of treasure. It's been neatly drawn, yet, the setting loses some spark, having appeared in stacks of role-playing scenarios, not to mention a bunch of books, movies, and slots.On a technical level, Dungeons and Diamonds is a video slot played on a 5x5 grid, providing 40 fixed paylines. It's a highly volatile game and comes with a quartet of RTP settings, with 96% being the most generous. Users experience winning combinations at a frequency of 28.28%, firing off when three or more matching symbols land from the leftmost reel. Adventurous types can embark on this quest using any device while selecting stakes from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin.PearFiction's graphics people have done a commendable job with the pay symbols used in Dungeons and Diamonds. Four nicely rendered characters appear on the 1x2 sized premium symbols, which feature rangers, warriors, sorceresses, and wizards, worth 5-10 times the stake for five of a kind. The low pays aren't quite as exciting, but the four card suit symbols do look valuable while actually being worth 1-1.5x the bet for a five-symbol winning line. Wilds appear on all reels and substitute for any regular pay symbol.Dungeons and Diamonds: Slot FeaturesOn this quest, larger rewards come the way of free spins, instant collects, and jackpots. Much of the extras are staples in PearFiction's tool kit or variations of them at least; let's see how they shape up.Instant CollectGem symbols display values of 1x to 25x the bet and land on reels 1 to 4. When gems land at the same time as a collect symbol on reel five, players are awarded the value of all gems in view. If a multi collect symbol lands on reel 5, players win the total value of the gem symbols in view multiplied by the multi collect symbol's value. Thirdly, if a respins collect symbol lands on reel 5, gems are locked in place, and the remaining positions respin. Players win the total value of all gems at the end of the respin.Wicked Wizard JackpotJackpot symbols also appear on reels 1 to 4, and if one lands at the same time as a collect, multiplier collect, or respin collect symbol on reel 5, the Wicked Wizard Jackpot game triggers. Players then pick gem pouches on a new screen until 3 matching jackpot symbols have been revealed. The jackpots are the Mini, Minor, Major, or Grand, worth 50x, 100x, 500x, or 5,000x the bet, respectively. Jackpots are not multiplied by the multiplier collect symbol.Free SpinsLanding 3 dragon eye scatter symbols triggers 8 Dungeons and Diamonds Free Spins. Additional gem, jackpot, and collect symbols are added to the reels for this feature, which can be retriggered.Dungeons and Diamonds: Slot VerdictGamemastering a successful D&D campaign that entertains, challenges, and excites a group of tabletop adventurers, requires a healthy dose of imagination. While a decent enough game, it wouldn't have hurt Dungeons and Diamonds if PearFiction had let their imaginations really fly. There are no issues with the audio-visuals, which provide a nice wee escape from reality, though a dragon sleeping on a mountain of gold is straight out of The Hobbit playbook. Gaming-wise, Dungeons and Diamonds is okay, but it might have been more magical if PearFiction had deviated further from their goto features. What players get in Dungeon and Diamonds is alright, but there is a feeling that unless PearFiction steps out of its comfort zone, they're destined to retain their mid-tier partner status.For one, we are yet to test drive a PearFiction slot which doesn't have jackpots or hold n' win/respin features. Not that there is something wrong with them per se, but using anything so consistently wears thin after a while. At least the game's classic features are executed well, and the three kinds of collection symbols add a certain level of twist to the instant collection feature. Players into fantasy should find Dungeons and Diamonds' presentation alluring, too. Although, like the features, there is a strong familiarity to most of the visuals as well - from the Saruman-esque wizard to the dragon eye bonus symbol to the Smaug-like background. At times in the review, the standard gameplay and stock characters had a way of lessening each other rather than blasting intrepid players into unmapped realms. Should you manage to defeat the virtual boss in this game, then rewards of up to 5,627x the bet are coming your way.In the end, Dungeons and Diamonds came across as the type of slot PearFiction has become completely comfortable making. Players happy with reliable gameplay in a fantasy setting might get a kick out of the colourful entertainment on offer here. For others, there are moments, but Dungeons and Diamonds felt like a free downloadable PDF scenario rather than a full-blown campaign sourcebook.

Title: Star Staxx
review: Star Staxx: Slot OverviewFads come and go, new threads, new sounds, new ways of thinking, but some stick. And one that's about as sticky as they get is retro, fruity, star, diamond, classic slots. True, there is a lot of room for manoeuvring within the classic slot category, which helps keep it fresh, relatively speaking. Within the broader format, studios have the opportunity to inject new features and gameplay limited only by their imagination. So, like a haiku, despite constraints, there is a certain freedom of expression as well. Having another go at the classic gaming with a twist format is developer Stakelogic, with an online slot called Star Staxx, which marries traditional slot elements with newer mechanical parts.Let's start with the traditional bits, and one quick glance is enough to confirm Star Staxx's lean to the classic side of things. Interestingly, one of the info pages classes this as a 'cosmic themed' slot, as evidenced by the purplish star-filled background image. Since Star Staxx doesn't have a separate bonus round, this is pretty much it as far as building a scene goes. The game grid is covered in bold symbols that gave Star Staxx a faintly Big Time Gaming Opal Fruits-ish feel. There's not a ton else to say really about the sights and sounds; it's a game that's built for a specific taste.Star Staxx slot - base gameA key part of the construction is the active gaming area itself which is split into two parts. The lower, larger part is where the regular symbols land and consists of 5-reels, 3-rows, and 20 fixed paylines. To win, matching symbols must land on a payline over at least three consecutive reels, but they can start from the left side or the right side of the grid. Star Staxx pays both ways, in other words. Medium-high volatile, the maximum RTP figure clocks in at 95.93%, with no mention of whether it changes when the Super Stake feature is switched on or off. When it's off, each paid spin costs 20 p/c to $/€200, or double when Super Stake is activated. The benefit of having it on is that more star symbols land on the reels.Next on the list are the regular pay symbols, and there are ten of them in total. The first four lower pays are J-A card icons, followed up by watermelons, cherries, bells, Bars, sevens, and diamonds. Royals pay 0.5 to 5 times the stake for five-of-a-kind, bumping up to 5 to 50 times the bet for five of the higher-pays. Perhaps to counterbalance the pay both ways detail, Star Staxx does not drop wilds onto the reels at any time.Star Staxx: Slot FeaturesStar Staxx slot - Wild Collect featureMoving on to features, this is where the upper Prize Reel comes into play. The Prize Reel sits atop the main grid, where Extra Spin or Bonus Win rewards are displayed. On each spin, the rewards on the Prize Reel move one position to the left, with new ones appearing on the rightmost position. Bonus Win symbols can possess values of 1x to 2,500x the bet, and Extra Spin symbols will either give +1 or +2 spins.To get your hands on the rewards from the Prize Reels requires landing Star symbols on the main reels. Each Star symbol landing on a reel awards the Bonus Win or Extra Spin prize located directly above it. When winning Extra Spins, the total amount won is added together when awarded. Free Spins are literally free base game spins, so the Prize Reel will move one position to the left when they are active. It is possible to win more Extra Spins from a free base game spin.Star Staxx slot - Wild Collect featureStar Staxx: Slot VerdictThere you have it, pretty short and sweet, Star Staxx living up to the idea of being a classically leaning slot with a twist. The twist might be relatively interesting for players who like to keep their foot on the gas and not let finagled rules or features get in the way of a pacey session. Spin the reels with the goal of landing Stars beneath the biggest Bonus Win reward possible (which can technically get quite big) while free spins and pay both-way line wins are accompaniments. Nothing too complicated about that.Simple doesn't necessarily translate to a smooth ride-in, though. When the test session kicked off, for a while, it felt like the demo might have been broken. So few were the payouts; even normal line wins felt as rare as hen's teeth. A few okay hits took place a little while later, smashing the initial suspicion over Star Staxx's broken status, but it did appear to be a game with a noticeably low hit rate. We might have hit a dry patch, fair enough, so just reporting the observations back as something to be aware of, really. Perhaps, because Star Staxx is such a simple game, minor quirks stand out more than they would in a slot with more depth. Here it's a simple case of hitting the play button in the hopes of hitting Stars, and hopefully, they land beneath a solid prize.And so wraps up Star Staxx, an uncomplicated if potentially hard-going slot that should trigger the interest of players up for a retro slot possessing what could be a bit of a challenge. The gameplay might not be the spark that ignites a revolution, but it is interesting enough to kindle a bit of interest, maybe not long-term interest, but it feels like there's an audience for Star Staxx out there.

Title: Dragon 50,000
review: Dragon 50,000 (ReelPlay): OverviewAfter its anticipated first Megaways release, it's now back to a more traditional side of things for ReelPlay - quite literally. In the studios latest offering titled Dragon 50,000, we head to ancient China where we get to experience some high variance slots action. These lines have been fixed in position as well, so you don’t have the option of customising them one way or the other. You can still alter the value of the bet that you place on those lines, though. Unless we've confused things, the developer appears to be speaking of coin value and not actual cash value. Title: Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways

So far, while there have been tweaks here and there, they've generally followed a similar script for the most part. We could be optimistic and say maybe Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways is going to be the one that shatters the mould and does something phenomenal which blasts the series into the stratosphere. However, since the game has a rather common theme and comes with essentially the same features as before, perhaps we should curb our zeal until the dust has settled on the review.To its credit, ReelPlay does occasionally surprise with the quality of their artwork, and Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways is one of their more picturesque slots. ReelPlay has presented an Irish slot which should please players who like a tastefully restrained version of the subject matter rather than one that explodes in a shower of shamrocks at every other turn.Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways slot - base gameThat assessment applies more to the background imagery since the game panel displays a fair share of theme-based icons. Mr O'Taters is displayed on the wild symbol, which only appears on the top reel to substitute for any normal pay symbol.Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways: Slot FeaturesShamrock Money Pot 10K Ways slot - free spins splash screenTill now, the 10K Ways Range hasn't exactly been known for jamming in masses of features, and Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways does nothing to break with tradition. If a new win is formed, the process repeats.Bonus RespinsThe Bonus Respins round is triggered when at least 6 scatter symbols are in view. Once underway, 3 respins are awarded, and when new scatters hit, they also lock in place and reset the spin count. Scatters either possess values of 1 to 100x the bet or carry one of the five bonus prizes. These are the Mini, Minor, Major, Grand, or 10K Bonus, worth 10x, 50x, 250x, 2,000x, or 10,000x the bet, respectively. The Mini or Minor can land more than once; the 10K, Grand, or Major can be awarded only once per bonus. The bonus round ends when there are no more spins left of all positions on the reels are filled with symbols.Buy BonusIf the Buy Bonus button is present, players can click it to buy the respins feature. The cost is 60x the bet for a triggering spin with 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12 scatter symbols.Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways slot - free spinsShamrock Money Pot 10K Ways: Slot VerdictShamrock Money Pot 10K Ways does pretty much what it says on the tin and offers few surprises. It's an Irish slot with 10,000 ways plus a hold and win feature. There's not much else to say beyond that, really, especially if you've played one of the previous 10K games like Hypernova 10K Ways or 10,000 Wonders 10K Ways. A couple of releases, Bananaz 10K Ways and Arrr! 10K Ways mixed things up with a wild symbol transformation/multiplier element and an after-feature gamble option, but these are absent from Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways, which keeps things straight up simple.It does mean the base game is a little drab, yet ReelPlay's graphics and sound team have injected a dash of life by doing a number on the theme. If Irish slots are an area of interest, then Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways should satisfy from an audio-visual standpoint. Most of what is here has been done a load of times before, though, so if you're not craving another journey to the Emerald Isle, it's probably going to be easy to dismiss Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways.What differentiates Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways from others in the range is the addition of the 10,000x Bonus symbol in the respins round. In some ways, that's a major increase over what was available before, but since most people are unlikely to score the 10K Bonus symbol anyway, its impact is kind of marginal.Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways isn't an innovative slot by many measures, recycling the same features with an omnipresent online slot theme. It runs smoothly and looks nice, but if you're after some novelty, Shamrock Money Pot 10K Ways is unlikely to deliver much as it was pretty predictable from start to finish.

Title: Temple of Fury Dream Drop

Coins can be used to buy or reduce the cost of bonus features. Changing bets updates the coins collected relative to the bet. When triggered, the Super Spinner spins to award either a cash prize of 60x up to 500x the bet or 5, 10, 15, or 25 Nitro Spins. The Super Spinner can be activated with 500 coins.Nitro SpinsWhen Nitro Spins are enabled, they guarantee at least 1 feature on each spin, coins are collected more frequently, and the Super Spinner triggers more often. Nitro Spins increase the bet by 50% or cost 4 coins per spin.Dream DropThe Dream Drop Jackpot Spin may trigger randomly before a normal spin. One spin occurs on a 5x3 grid where only DD symbols may land. Should 5 of them hit, players move to the Dream Drop Bonus. The Dream Drop Bonus has 5 reels, one for each jackpot. Crates fall onto the grid, and the dragon randomly burns them to reveal Dream Drop symbols. The first reel to fill with Dream Drop symbols awards the corresponding jackpot. This could be the Rapid, Midi, Maxi, Major, or Mega with starting values of €1, €5, €100, €25,000, or €500,000, respectively.Temple of Fury Dream Drop slot - Jackpot roundTemple of Fury Dream Drop: Slot VerdictThis isn't Four Leaf Gaming's first Dream Drop slot; previously, the studio released Dueling Jokers Dream Drop, and the two games could hardly be any more different. Where one was a 1970s boppin' disco party, this one is a fantasy hack-and-slash with a fire-breathing dragon. Dream Drop games, and slots in general, are a diverse bunch, and Four Leaf Gaming has rolled out something different to others in the DD lineup.However, while Four Leaf Gaming has helpfully supplied a bit of variety to the Dream Drop market, Temple of Fury Dream Drop's positives largely ease up there. The rest of the game struggled to stoke much of a warm campfire, let alone pour forth a raging blast of dragon fire. Sticky win respins do their thing but result in slow-paced gaming, and there are the four Fury Features also doing their thing, yet it may get a bit repetitive after a while with no real destination on the horizon to aim for. Aside from the Dream Drop, of course, that might be enough for some keyboard knights to keep battling away for. Non-jackpot top prizes aren't hugely exciting, though, topping out with the 500x from the Super Spinner, or should the grid expand and be filled with the dragon premium, a 1,780x win is coming your way.Admittedly, they wouldn't be the worst outcomes to occur, but when weighing up everything else Temple of Fury had to offer, the whole thing came across strangely light. Aside from having a crack at progressive jackpots in a fantasy environment, it was hard to get overly fired up about the rest of Temple of Fury, especially the non-jackpot version.

Title: Big Bam-Book

As to payouts, 6 low pays across a full payline, regardless of type, are worth 2x while a line of premiums range from 5x to 20x the stake. The wild is worth a bit more, at 30 times the stake should six land on a pay line. That is exceptionally rare though, most of the time, wilds simply substitute for any of the pay symbols to make a winning combination.Frequent Flyer: FeaturesFrequent Flyer - free spinsFrequent Flyer offers several varieties of two free spin features – Jetsetter Free Spins and Frequent Flyer Free Spins.Jetsetter Free Spins are much easy to trigger. They are activated when 5 flap symbols appear on the reels and spell out one of the destinations on the information board. When this happens, players are awarded 3 free spins with either 2 to 10 shuffling wilds, or a win multiplier from 2x to 6x. It is possible to spell out a city using the flap symbols at the same time as land a +3 icon. In this case, you get 6 free spins rather than 3.Each time you spell one of the destinations and trigger Jetsetter Free Spins, a stamp appears beside the respective name on the information board. Collect a stamp for each of the 10 destinations to be awarded Frequent Flyer Free Spins. This feature has 4 options to choose from:Unpack Relax – 5 free spins with a 3x multiplier + 3 wilds.Skytours – 3 free spins with a 2x multiplier + 6 wilds.Travel Gurus – 5 free spins with a 6x multiplier + 1 wild.The fourth option is a gamble option where you can win 4-20 free spins, 2-6x multiplier, and 1-10 wilds. If you’ve been playing around with bet levels, the Frequent Flyer round uses an average of all stakes used up until that point. After the Frequent Flyer feature, the stamps are removed from the board, so the globetrotting begins again.The last extra is the Final Call feature which randomly adds two flap symbols to spinning reels for better chances to trigger the feature.Frequent Flyer: VerdictOkay, so it’s not quite the same as chilling out in an airport before heading off to an exotic long-haul destination, but it has its moments. The jazzy, golden age atmosphere is quite relaxing and puts you in a positive mood. The arrival/departure board is clever too, integrating nicely with the features.The destinations picked by Relax Gaming include some less well-known cities, alongside the classic bucket listers. Of course, they were restricted to five letter cities, but still, it’s not every day you jet off to Perth, Delhi, or Quito - ticking them off as you trigger them. Jetsetter Free Spins pop up at fairly regular intervals too, breaking up the base game, while the Frequent Flyer Free Spins gives you a mission to settle into.As well as the positive aspects, there are a few possible concerns. For one, the 6x4 grid often feels a little too large for the number of paylines it’s packing. Also, the game does get a bit samey after a while, a bit of a tease. What we mean is when you trigger say Cairo or Miami, you still see the same imagery on screen. It might have been nice if there’d been more of a change of scenery when jetting off to these other destinations, like Aldo’s Journey.But that’s more of a wish list than a major critique. Beneath the veneer, the stats are solid if you like a bit of volatility in your gaming. Max wins of up to 5,000 times the stake are possible, so no complaints there. Use a bit of imagination, and Frequent Flyer is a gateway to the world, of sorts. It could have opened up the gateway a little wider perhaps, but what Frequent Flyer does offer is fine for a bit of escapism.

Title: Hockey Fever Penny Roller
review: Hockey Fever Penny Roller: Slot OverviewPlayers, 'Are you ready to experience the adrenaline-pumping excitement of the coolest slot game in town?' If so, then the marketing team at Games Global would have you believe that firing up the studio's slot Hockey Fever Penny Roller is just the thing. However, and there is a big however, this is a classic example of over-optimistic marketing hype. Some might even go so far as to call it BS. For Hockey Fever Penny Roller is a clone of Football Penny Roller, which was decidedly not 'adrenaline-pumping', nor was it the 'coolest slot game in town.' Pretty much the exact opposite.Maybe not for gamblers who like their slots to be virtually devoid of features and fun. There isn't a lot of visual variation, either. Since there are no bonus rounds flipping the flow, Hockey Fever Penny Roller plasters a diminutive 3-reel gaming panel to the centre-left of the screen as if it's smashing through a sheet of ice, and a list of pay symbols and their values on the right. That's it. Hopefully, you like the low-budget graphics.Hockey Fever Penny Roller slotThe gaming grid has just one single payline, so users are able to pick stakes of 1 c up to $/€100 per spin. This is the range when 1 coin is selected, but it is possible to change this to 2 or even 3 coins, making the maximum bet possible $/€300 per game round. In keeping with the less is more ethos, prepare for a lot of dead spins as well, as Hockey Fever Penny Roller posts a painfully low hit rate of 8.53% on the default 95.94% RTP model, though it remains about the same on the lower return configurations, as well. The volatility stays steady at a medium level.Only regular paying symbols land in Hockey Fever Penny Roller, meaning no wilds, scatters, bonus symbols, or anything like that show up at any time. There are 8 regular pays, which are skates, helmets/masks, rinks, two players facing off, refs, goalies, a white-shirted player, and a red-shirted player. Hitting 3 skate symbols pays 20x the bet, while 3 of the red-shirted players are worth 1,000x the bet, or 1,111x the bet if staking 3 coins per spin. In addition, hitting 1 red shirt symbol in any position pays 10x the bet, or hitting 2 of them in any position awards 15x.Hockey Fever Penny Roller: Slot FeaturesHockey Fever Penny Roller slotAs with its football sibling, Hockey Fever Penny Roller has zilch in terms of features to go over.Hockey Fever Penny Roller: Slot VerdictBack in the day, from around 2014 or so, Games Global, or Microgaming as it was known then, dropped fairly popular slots like Football Star, Cricket Star, Rugby Star, and Basketball Star. They all offered pretty much the same gameplay while switching up the specific sport-related skins. It seems that 10 years later, the studio is doing a similar thing, which is building a gaming engine and then slipping various sports skins over the top. What's weird is the Penny Roller slots pale in comparison to those sports slots Microgaming was making a decade ago. Instead of looking to the future, Hockey Fever Penny Roller feels like a massive leap backwards and was every bit as excruciating as its Football cousin was.Hopefully, this doesn't sound rough, but after playing another Penny Roller slot, the question arose whether Games Global has run out of ideas. Okay, in some ways, the penny slot, ultrabasic, no frills, simple as it gets 'action' of Hockey Fever Penny Roller is like not much else any other studio is doing, at the time of review. From a certain perspective, with these Penny Roller releases, Games Global is daring to be different by going against the trend of making slots boasting ever more volatility, features, and potential. It's like car companies pushing to develop all-electric self-driving cars while Game Global hitches a horse to a wagon. There might be something quaint about this approach, but that doesn't stop Hockey Fever Penny Roller from getting left in the dust by the galaxy of superior performing slots players have access to, just a mere click or two away.

Title: Let It Burn
review: Let it Burn: Slot OverviewHey players, get ready for a bit of heat from casino game maker NetEnt as it strikes a match or two in the online slot Let it Burn. The title is a bit of a giveaway, for Let it Burn follows in the tradition of slots doused in flames, the number 7, and a stack of other classic bits 'n pieces. Like a wiggly tooth you can't keep your tongue off, the fire genre is one that developers return to over and over again. If you're one of the players simmering within the studio's target audience keen on some retro gaming, feel free to come take a look-see.Retro is definitely the name of the game around here, as NetEnt has kept the graphics basic and to the point. A simple, fiery, burgundy background sits behind the more active gaming area displaying a number of typically old-school slot tokens. There's not much else to comment on from a front-end experience. These games aren't exactly famous for being visual feasts, and NetEnt has stuck with tradition by presenting a clean-lined, classic-looking game.Let It Burn slot by NetEntLet it Burn lets the kindling ignite on any device and supplies users with a bet range of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Sometimes, just sometimes, these retro slots surprise by packing masses of winning potential. Hate to burst your bubble, but Let it Burn isn't like that, really, possessing as it does more modest payout possibilities, though nothing especially out of the ordinary compared to what else is on offer here. It's highly volatile, though, and available in two RTP settings - 96% and 94.01%.On the technical side of things, depending on which phase of play you're in indicates the size of Let it Burn's gaming grid. In the base game, it works with a 5-reel, 4-row panel with 1,024 ways to win, increasing to 5-rows in free spins where 3,125 ways to win become a reality. If you've even glanced at the classic slot category for, like, a zeptosecond, you'll be familiar with the pay symbols in Let it Burn. These are, J-A card ranks as the low pays, then things like diamonds, cherries, a BAR, a bell, and the number 7 as the higher paying lot. A stack of wilds appear in the game, too, all with the ability to replace any pay symbol, plus added modifier abilities covered in the next section.Let it Burn: Slot FeaturesLet It Burn slot by NetEntAs well as the aforementioned allusion to the numerous wild types, Let it Burn has features such as Rolling Reels, free spins, and a bonus buy.Rolling ReelsIndividual Rolling Reels can appear on reels 2, 3, and 4. Each new Rolling Reel is given a starting multiplier value of x1. On each spin, Rolling Reels also spin individually as they move down a row while increasing the symbol multiplier by +1. Rolling Reels fall off the grid after they reach the lowest row unless they are affected by a moving wild. Rolling Reels are not carried over to free spins when triggered, but they will be waiting for you when going back to the base game.Wild SymbolsRolling Reels may be affected by a number of different wild symbols, depending on the type in view:Wild +3 – increases the Rolling Reels' multiplier value.Wild Up – moves the Rolling Reel to the highest reel position on the following spin.Wild Left – moves the Rolling Reel to the leftward reel instead of dropping down a row.Wild Right – moves the Rolling Reel to the rightward reel instead of dropping down a row.If 2 Rolling Reels move to the same position, they merge into one, and their multiplier values are summed.Free SpinsPlayers nab 10, 15 or 20 free spins when 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols land on the grid, respectively. While the bonus round is in action, landing 2, 3, 4, or 5 scatters awards an additional 3, 5, 8, or 12 free spins, respectively. For the free spins round, an extra row is added to the grid, increasing the number of ways to win to 3,125.Bonus BuyWhere possible, players are able to buy 10, 15, or 20 free spins for the respective cost of 100, 150, or 200 times their bet.Let It Burn slot - feature buy optionsLet it Burn: Slot VerdictBefore reviewing Let it Burn, we hadn't had a fire game in a while, not that there's a shortage of them for gamblers who happen to be in the mood for one. In a similar way to a popular fashion movement that's a little confusing, fire slots are a trend which refuses to lie down and go away. We had a number of contenders for fashion trends to list here that overstayed their welcome but decided not to get into a finger-waving exercise. The point is, fiery seven slots seem like they're always going to have an audience for the foreseeable future, and NetEnt's gone and added one more to the list for pundits to enjoy.It might appeal more to those with a soft spot for classic-looking games with slightly more contemporary aspects. Let it Burn isn't as basic as these games sometimes are. Its nifty Rolling Reels feature (not to be confused with Games Global and Co's Rolling Reels tumble mechanic) helps see to that. On its own, Rolling Reels might have been enough to embellish a regular fire game, but the bundle of wilds it also comes with manages to further the variety quotient. They can be handy, too, if they're moving the Rolling Reels around, helping to squeeze extra mileage out of the multiplier, saving it from falling off the board, like a game of keep the balloon in the air. As an aside, did you know there's such a thing as the Balloon World Cup? Yes, Francesco De La Cruz won glory for Peru as the Cup's first winner in 2021.Let it Burn isn't as contemporary an event as the Balloon World Cup though it manages to straddle the classic side through its presentation and the modern side via its features quite well. It by no means burns so bright as to transcend the genre, and the high risk, low reward approach might be a turn off for some, but for players partial to some toasty-looking gaming with a modern twist, Let it Burn could be okay.

Title: Multiplier Riches
review: Multiplier Riches: OverviewDeveloper Red Tiger transports players back in time to the turn of the 20th century in the richly decorated slot Multiplier Riches. Partnering the old school theme is old school gameplay via a 3-reel setup, and 1, count ‘em, 1 payline. This might be music to the ears of some, zzznore inducing to others. Give it a chance though, Multiplier Riches has a few flourishes that provide a more dynamic experience than you might expect.Loading the game is like opening the door to the Gatsby residence and walking into one of his legendary parties. We are talking the Leo Dicaprio rendition of course, rather than the original Fitzgerald novel. Red Tiger has done a great job on the graphics to conjure up the flair of the era, though the twangy guitar-heavy soundtrack is more 90s adult film than 1920s glam.The black decor and angular gold trim visuals hearken back to the seemingly carefree 1920s - an era when the hardest thing in life seemed to be deciding what cocktail to kick the night off. At least that’s how it often seems in pop culture. The not so tough choice for players is what bet to select with a range of options from 10 p/c to $/€20 per spin.As is often the case with Red Tiger releases, the default RTP is slightly down, not a deal-breaker, but still a little less than average on 95.72%. The game is highly volatile which, when combined with pacey gameplay and decent potential, can result in some pretty intense moments.The game mechanic might be somewhat of a litmus test for some players. This is because Multiplier Riches has just 1 payline on its 3x3 grid to land winners. The way symbols appear can be frustrating as they often land partially in view, but unless they are bang on the payline, they don’t count.The symbols involved are all beloved or despised (depending on your viewpoint) classic icons. In ascending order, we get Cherries, Single Bars, Double Bars, Triple Bars, Bells, and Lucky Sevens. All symbols need three on the line to win, except cherries which payout whether one, two or three land in view.Also, three of any Bar type on the line will pay out, though less than a pure combination of a common Bar type. As to rewards, payouts vary from x1 for one cherry up to 80x for a line of sevens. The game offers fairly decent values, given an extra kick thanks to the features.Multiplier Riches: FeaturesMultiplier Riches - locked wilds and multiplierLiving up to its name, Multiplier Riches dishes up a fair share of multipliers, as well as some pretty nifty wild action on the side. In keeping with the spirit of the game, there is nothing complicated about how the multipliers work.When a non-paying x2, x3, or x5 symbol lands, it is stored on the Rising Multiplier sitting above the reels. The reel on which it appeared then gets nudged up or down revealing a symbol which may or may not result in a win. The multiplier remains in place until the next line win occurs where it is applied. More multipliers can appear in the meantime which are added to the Rising Multiplier until the next line win.Keep an eye of for the wild. Styled as a big, sparkly diamond, it plays a central role and is highly desirable. For one, it can substitute for all paying symbols – though it does not substitute for a single cherry payout if you were wondering. Of course, one wild + one cherry pays the value of two cherries.On top of substituting, whenever a wild lands on the win line, it is locked in position and remains there until it participates in a win. While waiting, it is possible for another to land and lock as well. Wilds are the most valuable symbol in the game, where a line of 3 is worth 500 times the stake.Multiplier Riches: VerdictThe basic one line, three-reel dynamic might be perceived as an inherently limited format, at first glance. However, Red Tiger has done some interesting things with it, making Multiplier Riches one of the better slots they have developed recently. Its beauty lies in the way it is both simple, yet full of clever touches that keep engagement levels higher than they might have been.Mainly, this has been achieved by including a symbol (the cherry) which pays when just one or two appear in view. This is assisted by the fact that the cheery doesn’t have to land on the first reel onwards. This simple twist keeps the game chugging along a lot more smoothly. Also, making wilds sticky until they generate a win is another deft touch, subtle yet effective.The slot feels well thought out, as if Red Tiger went back to the basics, nailed them, producing a well-oiled game that seamlessly melds old and new. The art deco styling is the just icing on top. The only gripe, a small one, is a soundtrack that feels out of place. No biggie though.As to the question of potential, the answer is a surprisingly positive one. While it will never break records, Multiplier Riches is capable of hitting wins of up to 5,000 times the stake which isn’t bad at all off the back of one payline. Breaking out the calculator makes it clear you’ll need to combine some generous multiplier action with a line of wilds to hit those heights.Okay, it won’t win everyone’s heart, but in the right hands, Multiplier Riches is bound to entertain some. It’s a solid one payline option offering a couple of features that don’t clutter up the gameplay, along with some decent potential lurking in the background.

Title: Nero’s Fortune
review: Nero’s Fortune (Quickspin): OverviewEmperor Nero is infamous for his brutal reign over the Roman Empire in the first century. The review was going to start with one or two examples of the bizarre things he got up to, but it was hard to find any that were fit to print. Let's just agree that he was one of the worst rulers Europe has ever seen. He was cashed up through, no arguing that, with wealth befitting his position as leader of one of the greatest civilisations on earth. Swedish developers Quickspin have taken aspects of Nero's reign and the era to drive their latest tumble slot. It’s been a while since a top Roman-themed slot came by, let's see if Nero's Fortune is up for it.Quickspin promised 'drool-worthy graphics' with Nero’s Fortune and they certainly are high quality. The goal was to utilise their new 3D engine to take 'lighting and rendering to a whole new level' – also their words. It didn't quite induce drool, but it's a superb looking game nonetheless and the epic orchestral score provided by Quickspin's own talanted sound designer Andreas Hedlund significantly enhances the experience. Choosing Nero as a theme provided the chance to recreate a dark, red-hued Rome, burning while the emperor fiddled, as the story goes. The view is reminiscent of a painting called Fire of Rome by the French artist Hubert Robert, and is completed with animated ash floating by.Nero’s Fortune is Quickspin's third tumble slot, and is very different to the other two. Golden Glyph kicked things off with a 7x7 format and Wild Cauldron could be expanded to hit 6x7. Nero's Fortune contracts things down to a 5x5 grid that is set against a classical Roman structure. Full of statues, pillars and architecture, Rome has had life breathed back into it by the graphic team.Apparently, Ancient Romans were inveterate gamblers, and the pastime was deeply entrenched through all levels of society. Quickspin extends the courtesy by providing bet levels from 20 c/p up to $/€100 per spin. The grid might be a bit more compact this time around, but Nero's Fortune has the highest RTP of the trio at 96.21% whilst the high (5/5) volatility has been retained.This being a tumble slot, symbols drop to fill the grid and clusters of 5 adjacent matching symbols or more result in a payout. Winning clusters are removed from the grid which lets new symbols tumble into place. This can create chains of wins from just one spin and the process repeats until no new winning clusters form up. The symbols used in the game include J-A royals, and 4 high win symbols. These high win symbols include emblematic eagles, wolves and lions. The red ruby symbol offers the highest returns, with clusters of 12+ worth 150 times the stake. Helping form clusters is the 'W' wild symbol which can substitute for any symbol in the game except the scatter.Nero’s Fortune (Quickspin): FeaturesFlames of Nero bonus round in playAlong with cluster pays are features that either pop up randomly in the base game or need to be triggered. First up is the Burning Arrows feature which only appears during the base game. Whenever a winning cluster is removed from the grid, there is a possibility that the game will spawn a multiplier symbol in the empty positions. When the next spin occurs the new symbols cover any of the added multipliers. If a winning cluster is removed and it reveals one or more of these multipliers, they are accumulated until the end of the spin. Any wins that appear on that spin then have the accumulated multiplier applied to the total. The multiplier is then reset for the next fresh spin.The main feature is a round of free spins which takes the concept of the Burning Arrows and expands it, making it far more effective. Known as the Flames of Nero Bonus, the key to the round is the 'BNS' scatter symbol - when 3, 4, or 5 scatters are in view they award 10, 12, or 14 free spins respectively. The round starts with a dramatic animation and moves to a tilted view of the reels which produces an extra dose of gravitas. Every new free spin begins by having a bunch of multiplier symbols randomly spread over the grid. When winning clusters are removed to reveal these symbols their multipliers are accumulated and applied to the win. During free spins, the multiplier is not reset between spins but continues to increase until the round is over.Nero’s Fortune (Quickspin): VerdictNero's Fortune is another solid tumble slot from Quickspin. On the plus side, each one so far has something quite different to offer. First are looks. Graphics have been a big deal to Quickspin going into this project, and they have pulled off an excellent looking game. The vibe, atmosphere, and attitude capture the nature of the subject matter and the animations add drama. It lacks the warmth that Wilds Cauldrons provided perhaps, but those in the mood to get down to some serious no-nonsense gaming will appreciate the solemn tone. If you are looking for maximum payouts then be aware that Nero’s Fortune has the lowest potential of the three Quickspin tumble slots. Though at up to 8,100 times the stake there is still plenty to play for.When it comes to gameplay, Nero's Fortune’s straight forward nature is an asset. Not that the others were particularly complicated, but Nero’s has a good pace to it. It boils everything down to landing clusters and getting multipliers to rack up during free spins. The good thing is that it's not particularly hard to build-up a decent multiplier once the bonus round has been triggered. Loads of multiplier symbols are added with every new spin, so it's a case of scoring clusters to accumulate them. No, it’s not easy to land those gigantic wins we all aim for, but once set in motion the bonus game can get on some satisfying rolls.Quickspin may still need some work to perfect its tumble mechanic and mathematical model. Although not as refined as those on offer from Play'n GO, for example, Nero's Fortune is, however, still another decent tumble slot from Quickspin with excellent features and potential. Fans of the theme will be chuffed with the latest addition to the Ancient Rome category.

Title: Sugar Craze Bonanza
review: Sugar Craze Bonanza: Slot OverviewSugar Craze Bonanza is an online slot of the candy-themed variety from Games Global partner studio Hammertime. Hammertime is a project of software maker Stormcraft Studios, and Sugar Craze Bonanza links the two studios as it's a clone of a previous game - the all-hammer swinging slot Thunderstruck Stormchaser. Candy is a world away from the Norse gods, but beneath the hood, the two games share similar stats as well as features like Rolling Reels, Multiplier Symbols, Sugarstorms, free spins with a win multiplier and a second level to the bonus round where Sugarstorms are guaranteed.Norse gods and candy might be worlds apart, but they do share at least one commonality. Both are pretty common online slot themes, and for Sugar Craze Bonanza, Hammertime has stuck with the visuals typically associated with this genre. This means a candy-floss/cloud-filled realm, with lollipops galore and hard sweets all over the game grid. The anticipation of seeing what the Gargantoon could do when released built steadily as the review progressed, keeping the engagement level going through the near misses and what could have beens, so that when it finally did happen, we were ready to blast off to the outer reaches of the galaxy.When he, she, it did hit, the experience was a short, sharp run of merging from smallest, medium, till largest final form. On the other side of the coin, Gargantoonz has the second biggest potential of the lot (after Dr Toonz) at 7,000x the bet (though many within the community have started to question the advertised potential of Play'n GO slots).And so, Gargantoonz wasn't a genre-defining moment like its older sibling was, but there is still fine grid slot gaming to be had. Title: Vegas Dice Megaways

Prices vary from 30x the bet for 6 spins and no locked reel (RTP 95.79%) up to 130x the bet for 10 free spins with 1 starting locked reel (RTP 96.07%).Vegas Dice Megaways slot - bonus buyVegas Dice Megaways: Slot VerdictBranded Megaways slots tend to be quite samey as the features and gameplay are often identical. Title: Dracula Awakening

Title: Doom of Egypt
