The game's music was particularly cheerful as well, grooving away like the soundtrack at a laid-back Amsterdam lounge bar, making the overall experience of Dutch Flip a rather pleasant one.On the gaming side of things, Dutch Flip is essentially a copy of Super Flip, a slot Play'n GO released back in 2015. Quite how and why a relatively older game collided with The Netherlands theme to create Dutch Flip is anyone's guess. Whatever the explanation might be, Play'n GO has kept the gameplay basically the same as it was, with little in the way of new developments to explore. Well, there are none, really, meaning a pretty straightforward base game, interspersed with occasional near win respins until eventually unlocking the free spins phase. In the bonus round is where the flip dynamic comes into play, and the results can potentially be tremendous. One of the reasons for Super Flip's popularity was surely its maximum prize of a million coins, or 10,000 times the max bet. Again, this number is likely greatly exaggerated - more realistically speaking, players should aim for wins of around 200-1000x.A lot has happened in the iGaming space since 2015, but Dutch Flip's features stand up pretty well against modern innovations. It's not the most action-packed game a lot of the time, yet the numbers speak for themselves. So, for a taste of The Netherlands, or a well-known side of it at least, Dutch Flip could be worth a go.

Title: Treasure Heroes
review: Treasure Heroes (Rabcat): OverviewThe previous Rabcat slot to come our way was North Storm, an attractive slot with an etheric quality to it. The gameplay might have been so-so, but it was a looker all the same. Producing slots exclusively for Microgaming, Treasure Heroes is another fantastic looking game. It not only has appealing visuals, but it also possesses some innovative features and gameplay. In Treasure Heroes, players enter a fantasy world where the goal is breaking into a treasure room and scooping up as much loot as possible.Back before a time when first person perspectives dominated video games, the bird's eye view was common. That’s what we get with Treasure Heroes staring down into a neatly laid out dungeon. Visually, it undoubtedly dips its toes into video game territory. In the middle of the room is a 5x5 game zone full of bright, personable symbols. Hit play and the reels spin in an unusual way – they're all synchronised. They don't have the same symbols, but they spin in time. That might seem weird, but it ties in with the Moving Walls mechanic as we will see. Before hitting spin, bet levels need to be set and stakes start at 20 p/c and go up to $/€40 each.Wins come from clusters rather than lines in this dungeon. You need at least 6 matching symbols touching horizontally or vertically to make a winning cluster combination. There are only six pay symbols in the game, but they are all intricately drawn and unique to Treasure Heroes. In ascending order there is a blue gem, a dragon charm, a gold lantern and a Warrior. There are two premium symbols which are a Magician and a Treasure Chest which payout 1,000 times the stake for a full grid of 25 of a kind. Helping cobble winners together is a purple witchy-ish symbol that is wild and can substitute for any of the 6 pay symbols.Powering the game is a math model that might feel a little underpowered for harder edge players. RTP is solid on 96.12% and combines with a lower hit rate of 17.03% along with a medium volatility. The figures feed a math model that produces a fairly steady amount of wins, albeit with some downtime, and features that triggered quite frequently during testing.Treasure Heroes (Rabcat): FeaturesFree spins feature with sticky wilds in viewTreasure Heroes has two additional features which are both quite unique. The most common is the Moving Reels mechanic. This is triggered after every winning cluster is formed and is why the reels synchronise. First, the winning amount is paid out. After that, reels 1, 3, and 5 move vertically, in random directions with new symbols filling in any gaps. At the same time, rows 1, 3, and 5 move horizontally. Any new wins cause the feature to repeat until no new clusters are formed. If you like, picture the shifting reels and rows like a moving Rubik's cube. Twisting the columns and rows can put matching symbols together as well as pull them away. Fantastic when chains of wins occur, annoying when you see your winning symbols get torn apart.The last symbol is the scatter in the form of a Key. When two Keys are in view they trigger 10 Treasure Chamber Free Spins. The keys merge to unlock the door on the right, and the game moves into the Treasure Chamber. Every time a Free Spin ends a skeleton above the reels pulls a lever to spin any Magician or Warrior symbols in view. This may or may not turn them into sticky wilds which are held in place for the duration of the feature. Build up a collection of sticky wilds and the results can be quite rewarding. What's not so great is that Moving Walls are not active during free spins. Nor can free spins be retriggered.Treasure Heroes (Rabcat): VerdictTreasure Heroes is one of those games where you have absolutely no clue what's going on at first and thus may seem a bit over complicated at first. It doesn't take too long, however, until things start to make sense. Moverover, it has a number of elements that make it a likeable game - graphics are great, gameplay is unusual, and the features work well together. For the wider gambling community it could be cult favourite, but a few aspects hold it back from dazzling more dedicated gamblers. When it comes to potential, full grids of symbols return 1,000 times the stake on a single spin which isn't a bad prospect, yet the key sticking point is that the maximum win is 1,925 times the stake at max bet.Its relatively low hit rate might frustrate some, but it ensures that when things do happen they are more exciting than they could've been. What this means is that clusters snowball thanks to the Moving Walls features. Bear in mind that this can lead to as many non-wins as wins since the game moves symbols apart as often as it pulls them together. Also, it doesn't produce as long as the chains of wins which are possible with Megaways for instance. Moving Walls are quite unique in the way they move though so good on Rabcat for experimenting with a new feature although at times we couldn't help but feel that the animations could have been sped up a bit.Treasure Heroes is not a high volatility slot that will knock socks off and payout big when it's on. But it is entertaining all the same. Its singularly nature makes it worth investigating, at least in demo mode to get a feel for it. Whether players move past that stage to feeding in coins is an interesting question. Plenty are sure to. Its medium volatility and quirky dynamics, not to mention great graphics, make it an attractive option for casual gamblers. The features drop often enough to keep the pace up and the game ticking over. Its low overall potential and gentler volatility may prove a sticking point with the more dedicated players though. Overall, it'll never be slot of the year, but its charm and unique spinning action might just win you over regardless.

Title: Lock And Pop
review: Lock and Pop: Slot OverviewPins at the ready, people, we're about to go a-poppin' with software developer NetEnt in the online slot Lock and Pop. NetEnt, not sure; it can feel like the team has taken its foot off the gas recently, in some ways, content to push out slots that end up in the good but not great basket, at best. Generally playable stuff, but the studio is a shadow of the dominator it once was and, at times, seems okay cruising out these later years, happy to rest on former glories. Lock and Pop is a prime example of a passable slot, actually probably quite attractive to certain gambling appetites, but ultimately pretty mid by NetEnt standards. Let's see what you make of it.When you think of space slots, one that has stuck around since like forever is NetEnt's own classic Starburst. Joining its older sibling in the same, or at least a similar, category, Lock and Pop is also presented as if the action takes place out there in the vast drift of space, where pinprick stars can be made out in the bluey purple lighting. Starburst is getting on in years, and it shows, though while Lock and Pop is a more contemporary release, it doesn't exactly look like it's riding the cutting edge of slot art. In other words, the visuals are simplistic, a little sparse, and the same can be said about the gameplay, until free spins trigger, at least, where a sizable list of special effects technically becomes available.Lock And Pop slot - base gameLock and Pop is pitched at gamblers who prefer mathematics on the low-medium edge of the volatility scale and is available in several RTP configurations. The default return figure is 96.09%, though two lower values make their way onto relevant markets. Stake range is wide, going from a low of 20 cents per spin up to a maximum of $/€120. Lock and Pop's base game might be bland, but it can be skipped by taking advantage of the bonus buy function to move straight into the bonus round phase.Played on a 5x5 gaming space (only 3 rows are active in the base game), Lock and Pop provides 20 paylines for landing regular wins across. Classic slash generic icons make their way onto Lock and Pop's pay table. The low pays include 10 through Ace card ranks, while the higher value group consists of bells, 7's, and diamonds. Wild symbols substitute for everything except Prize symbols, so they can be used to help complete regular winning combinations.Lock and Pop: Slot FeaturesLock And Pop slot - free spinsIn the base game, Prize symbols may land bearing values of 0.5x to 1,000x the bet. Hitting 6 or more Prize symbols triggers the free spins round, where Prize symbols become Sicky Prize symbols. Prize symbols remain on the reels till the bonus round ends or until a Lock and Pop bonus feature is activated. Players begin the round with 7 free spins.During free spins, if 1 or more reels are filled with Sticky Prizes, 1 of 10 Lock and Pop bonus features activate on the bottom row. Lock and Pop bonus features are active only on its own reel. When the feature is over, the Sticky Prize symbols are removed from the reels and their values are added to the top row collection. These are the 10 possible features:Retrigger - awards +3 free spins.Adder - adds 1x or 2x the bet to all Sticky Prizes on its reel.Magnet - copies the values of the Sticky Prizes on the reels vertically adjacent to the magnet reel, on both sides.Super Magnet - copies the values of the Sticky Prizes in the same position on all other reels.Topper - finds the Sticky Prize with the highest value on its reel and copies it to all other Sticky Prizes on the reel.Blaster - adds 1x or 2x to all Sticky Prizes on its reel. The values of the Sticky Prize symbols in the reel are added to the top row collection. Then, 3 random empty positions anywhere on the reels are filled with the Blaster value.Duplicator - creates a second game area with all Sticky Prizes present reproduced on it, plus 3 additional reels without symbols on them. This duplicated game area spins horizontally. If the duplicated area lands on top of the existing one, the duplicated Sticky Prize symbols may fill empty reels or be placed on top of Sticky Prizes already on the reels. When this happens, the values of both prizes are added together.Big Bang - doubles the values of all Sticky Prizes in its reel, and once added to the top row collection, the total is also doubled.Super Collector - collects the values of all Sticky Prizes on this reel, adding them to the top row collection. The total values collected in all other top row collectors are then added to this feature's top row collection.Hammer - collects the value of all Sticky Prizes on the reel, adds them to the top row collection, then spreads the new value to every position on the reel. This means the new values of Sticky Prizes on the reel are once again added to the top row collection.Feature BuyPlayers are able to trigger the bonus round feature for 50 times the bet.Lock And Pop slot - free spinsLock and Pop: Slot VerdictFor fairly relaxed gambling that isn't too taxing on the thought processes nor overburdening on the eyes or ears, Lock and Pop might serve a purpose. The base game is absolutely forgettable since, you know, no features means nothing much is ever going to happen there. Sure, a solid line win or two might keep the pace turning over, but Lock and Pop is really built around its bonus round. Nice, then the feature can be bought for those who don't have the patience to wait it out. For the non-bonus buyers, maybe having a mildly interesting show playing on the telly in the background might be a helper for grinding through till the Lock and Pop bonus feature triggers.Is the bonus round worth the wait? Could be. The max win isn't enormous, so mentally prep for that, but the 4,046x feels like a cosy match for the low-medium volatility. As in, if the rest of Lock and Pop is fine, then mammoth winning potential probably isn't a major must-have attribute. Looked at positively, the Lock and Pop round's bonus features have a lot of variety. Not, for example, a Money Train 4 list of special symbols as long as your arm and leg, but there are no less than 10 features to check out, and they include some rather useful effects. In theory, what you want is to clear and rack up prize values, repeat, till the top row is looking rosy.So no, Lock and Pop isn't likely to impress cynically jaded, high-requirement gamblers who demand the slots they play blow their hair back. However, since Lock and Pop was unlikely to have been designed to take on the big prize accumulator/hold 'n win style games on the market, NetEnt has no doubt set its sights on a certain, shall we say a less raucous, segment of the market and come up with a cheerful slot to attempt satisfying it.

Title: Fishin' Pots of Gold
review: Fishin' Pots of Gold: Slot OverviewIf you ever wanted evidence that we might be running out of new ideas on this planet, here comes Fishin' Pots of Gold by Microgaming partner Gameburger Studios. Weaving together elements of some of the most numerously unoriginal genres imaginable, Fishin' Pots of Gold revolves around a money symbol collection feature a la Fishin' Frenzy, but where the angler character has been replaced by a leprechaun called Lucky Lad Flynn. Hence, players get a stack of Irish platitudes to go with the fishing action. Perhaps for some, this will sound like a match made in heaven; for others, it probably won't make much sense whatsoever. Time to work out which side of the debate you are on.To a sunlight pond in the cheerful Irish isles is where Fishin' Pots of Gold lays its scene. A transparent 5x3, 10-payline grid is used in the base game, growing in size when free spins are activated. The view is everything you'd think a big bass Irish bonanza would be. There's fish, rainbows, leprechauns, four-leaf clovers, jolly fiddle led tunes, and pots o' gold. The generic overload is bound to delight some players as much as it repels others.Fishin' Pots of Gold is playable on any device, offering stakes of 10 p/c to $/€40 per spin. As is common now with Microgaming releases, RTP is variable, maxing out at 96.47%, while volatility remains medium no matter the version you fire up. Also worth noting is the hit rate which is relatively low at 19.15%, though the high symbol values sort of makes up for it. To sum it all up, the name of the game is collecting money symbols, including four jackpot tiles.Ireland and fishing meet up on the paytable, which starts with Celtic-ish designed 10-A card ranks, all worth 10x the bet for five of a kind. Any combination of fish symbol is next, followed by floats, flies, Wellies, and tackle boxes where lines of five get you a payout of 20 to 200 times your stake. In all pay symbol cases, you'll need to land at least three of a kind, left to right, starting from the left side of the game panel.Fishin' Pots of Gold: Slot FeaturesCollecting prize bearing fish symbols is one of the main goals of the game, along with jackpot symbols. Manage to trigger free spins where it is possible to build on the value of money symbols by chucking a multiplier into the mix.Collect SymbolLucky Lad Flynn is used on the collect symbol, appearing on the rightmost reel in the base game, and all reels in free spins. The collect symbol is also wild, so it replaces all symbols except scatters or jackpot symbols. When a collect symbol lands at the same time as fish money symbols or jackpot symbols, the values are collected for the player. Jackpot symbols come in four types – Mini, Minor, Major, or Mega, worth 15x, 50x, 500x, or 5,000x the bet, respectively.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols triggers 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. While free spins are active, reels expand to 5 rows high, and 10 additional paylines are added. Also, the Big Bass Bonanza-style accumulation trail comes into force.Now, whenever the collect symbol hits, it gets collected. For every 3 scatters collected, the cash symbol multiplier increases to x2, then x3, x5, and x10. Every 3 scatters collected also awards an extra 5 free spins. This is the only way to extend the bonus round as scatter symbols do not land during free spins.Feature BuyFishin' Pots of Gold may come with a bonus buy option but it only becomes available after free spins have triggered organically at least once. Players can buy 10, 15 or 20 free spins for the cost of 50x, 100x, or 150x the bet.Fishin' Pots of Gold: Slot VerdictPickles and peanut butter, banana and tomato sauce, peaches and blue cheese, if there are two seemingly unrelated foods out there, you can almost bet someone has combined them to varying degrees of success. So, it is with Fishin' Pots of Gold that either brings together a few favourite themes in one outrageously good medley of entertainment or leaves you clichéd out. It manages to not only copy Fishin' Frenzy, the godfather of symbol collect games, it also drags in Pragmatic Play/Reel Kingdom's hit Big Bass Bonanza at the same time. There is a good chance fans of the latter game will find entertainment value in Fishin' Pots of Gold, since both games do similar things, with an extra sweetener laid on in Fishin' Pots of Gold.The extra sweetener is the expanded winning potential. Where BBB topped out at a so-so 2,100x, Fishin' Pots of Gold's four jackpot tiers help push that out to 5,000x. Relatively low potential didn't stop players lining up for a burn on Big Bass Bonanza, so is Fishin' Pots of Gold a shoe in to topple it off the fishing slot podium? Possibly, but the odd inclusion of all the Irish imagery might be a little too much.Why Gameburger decided to hitch fish with leprechauns is anyone's guess, and one of two things may happen. Either it's a little too bizarre and flops around like a rainbow trout on the riverbank, or it proves to be a winning combo. Of course, there is also the middle ground where Fishin' Pots of Gold sort of does neither, of course. There are other touches here to tempt in Big Bass players, too. For one, reels and ways expand for the bonus game, and you can always buy free spins, too, provided you've triggered them naturally once already, an odd rule in itself.Players into Irish and fishing themes should be overjoyed to see their two favourite genres collide on one massive leprechaun coloured angling fiesta. Others might not be so thrilled with the submarine sandwich of common slot ingredients.

Title: Chickenville Power Combo
review: Chickenville Power Combo: Slot OverviewIn most instances, loyalty is a desirable trait. Loyalty to a sports team through the ups and downs, sticking by a friend through the good times and bad, and loyalty to a partner is one of the most important elements in a successful long-term relationship. However, within the gambling industry, loyalty, in certain instances, can be boring. Specifically, we're talking about studios who repeatedly trundle out the same feature set over and over again. Today's slot is guilty of this repetition. For some reason, Chickenville Power Combo brought the TV show Sesame Street to mind as a way of comparing the wholesome, feel-good atmosphere.Chickenville Power Combo slot - base gameChickenville Power Combo's gaming grid sits in a wooden building, reminiscent of Quickspin's Big Bad Wolf slot; this one comes shipped with 5-reels, 3-rows, and 40 paylines. In addition, scarecrow wilds appear on reels 2, 3, and 4 to substitute all symbols except scatters.Chickenville Power Combo: Slot FeaturesChickenville Power Combo slot - Collection PowerChickenville Power Combo's central feature is the Link&Win bonus round, which is randomly triggered when 1 of 3 different scatter symbols hits, each scatter granting a different power. When this happens, more than one power is active.The Link&Win starts with 3 spins on a game grid that lands only blank spaces or egg symbols holding values of 0.5x to 20x the bet. Both sets of reels have individual spin counters.Red Scatter - The Red Scatter can trigger the Link&Win with Jackpot Power. During this round, eggs may appear in red, blue, or green and are collected when they land. When 3 of the same coloured eggs have been collected, the respective Jackpot is awarded. Three greens award the Mini, 3 blues award the Major, and 3 reds award the Mega.Blue Scatter - The blue scatter can trigger the Link&Win with Collection Power. When at least 1 egg lands on a spin in the bonus, the values on all coins that landed before the current spin are collected.Feature BuyFrom the feature buy section, players can buy the Link&Win bonus with individual features or combinations of features for 23 to 117 times the bet.Chickenville Power Combo slot - Twin PowerChickenville Power Combo: Slot VerdictHey ho, it's another Power Combo slot, offering a group of features which have appeared before, more than once. This did make Chickenville Power Combo a tough game to get really fired up over. Luck of the Devil Power Combo failed to smash it out of the park, as did Queens of Ra Power Combo before it, which did not bode well for Chickenville Power Combo's chances. On the positive side, as far as agricultural slots go, this is a cheerful one, boasting a colourful cast of characters, a fun farm yard atmosphere, and a rather excellent soundtrack that suits the game like a charm.From there, the glow starts to fade. The rest of Chickenville Power Combo is standard Power Combo fare. Land scatters to gain access to the Link&Win, or luck out and get 2 or even 3 scatters to trigger the feature at the same time to bulk up the powers. Getting all 3 at once is likely to be the most sought-after result. As in the other two related slots, giving players the opportunity to buy any combination of all 3 features is a useful addition, and the costs aren't exactly exorbitant when compared to what a lot of other studios are doing with feature buys. Brick Snake 2000's 8,360x the bet God Mode Deluxe represents the other end of the buy spectrum, for example.Chickenville Power Combo has a sizable max win figure of 15,000x the bet, though the Mega prize is possibly a more realistic target to aim for. And that's it, really, All For One Studios has turned out another Power Combo slot built off previous releases with a cheerful theme which tries hard but fails to raise itself above mediocre status.

Title: Jin Ji Bao Xi Megaways

Also, landing 3 coins at once retriggers 3 additional free spins.Jin Ji Bao Xi Megaways: Slot VerdictPrior to this, SG Digital had been on a bit of an innovative Megaways bender, but Jin Ji Bao Xi Megaways drags it back to normality. In Jin Ji Bao Xi Megaways' case, it has the four jackpots, though they aren't hugely lucrative. Jin Ji Bao Xi Megaways is bound to appeal to proponents of this style - it certainly doesn't do anything that might put a fan off. Title: Wings of Ra
review: Wings of Ra (Red Tiger): OverviewIt doesn’t feel long since we reviewed the last Egyptian themed slot from Red Tiger. That one, Jewel Scarabs, focused on a more humble subject, the lowly yet revered scarab beetle. Red Tiger’s new slot Wings of Ra elevates the action using mysterious Pharaohs and Gods. This theme might have been done plenty of times before, but it just keeps coming back. We have slots like the ‘Book of’ series to thank for that, and this new one, Wings of Ra is rather reminiscent of that classic range. Not saying it’s a clone at all, but Wings of Ra has more than a few nods to the Book range, and classic slot gaming in general.It’s not just the name that brings to mind an older age of gaming. The look is nice, but not as ultra-modern as say, the latest Play’n GO Egyptian creations, for example. It’s a bit more basic than that, more function over form if you will. In this particular case, the 5 reel, 3 row game area is set in a temple-like structure, but one that looks more Las Vegas flavoured Ancient Egypt rather than the real deal. It’s too clean, too sterile looking. There’s no real magic to it. You can imagine buff dudes in period costumes walking out from behind pillars to charge tourists a dollar for a photo with them. Either way, players get started by set bets which range from 10 p/c up to $/€20 per spin - betting options might have increased since Jewel Scarabs, but every other stat has been dropped. RTP is down slightly to 95.69% while volatility feels softer and overall potential has taken a hit – more on that later.For now, the aim of the game is landing matching symbols of three or more on a payline. There are 10 fixed paylines, and they light up in an old school fashion when winners land on them. Here is the first twist. Instead of having to land from the first reel, combinations can land anywhere. That could be the first three reels, or the middle, or the last three. It’s a nice touch, though unusually positioned combinations don’t seem to land all that often.Wings of Ra is also a game where full grids of symbols are not only possible but land a lot more often than you are probably used to. Another nod to the Ra series occurs when opening up the paytable. The low pay 10 – A royals use pretty much the same font as the Book of Ra Deluxe version does. After that bunch, we get an eye symbol, that bird god Horus, a Nefertiti looking ruler, and a pharaoh. The pharaoh pays out the most, at 30 times the stake for a line of five. Interestingly, there is no wild symbol in the game, though there is a scatter, let’s take a look.Wings of Ra (Red Tiger): FeaturesFree spins feature with symbol upgrade triggeredMaking up for the omission of a wild is the Mystery Coin symbol. As you might imagine, when these symbols land on the reels, they all spin and reveal the same random symbol. This will transform the lowest paying symbol into Mystery Symbols for the remainder of the free spins, and the bar is emptied.This process continues to fill the bar and convert the lowest symbols until the free spins end. Obviously, the more low pay symbols that are converted, the better the chances of landing higher paying combos. This is because higher paying symbols increase in frequencies, but also because the number if Mystery Symbols can really rack up in number.Wings of Ra (Red Tiger): VerdictWings of Ra is a passable game; one that pays homage to older, more successful slots that came before. It won’t shake things up like Book of Ra did, for example, but it has a few things that fans of the genre might appreciate. The first is its classic slot vibe. It might look new enough, but things like the winning payline effect give it a retro(ish) touch. Secondly, the land-anywhere-winners are fun, though they don’t seem to come into play as often as you might think, or hope for. In fact, wins, in general, are somewhat disappointing. The first stab of disenchantment occurs when you get your first full grid – usually thanks to Mystery Symbols. A triumphant fist pump quickly turns to ‘oh man, really?’ when the value is tallied up and paid out.It’s not rare to land full grids of symbols during free spins, or at least get close often. This is due to the sheer number of Mystery Symbols that can appear during the round. However, full grids aren’t worth a whole lot of coins on their own. In fact, the highest paying symbol will net you a mere 300 times the stake (as opposed to 5,000x in Book of Ra Deluxe). The overall potential isn’t overly exciting either at 3,166 times the stake. Not bad, but a quick scroll through Red Tigers’ game line up for Jewel Scarabs quickly eclipses that figure. All up, Wings of Ra is okay, it has its minor moments of innovation, but it leaves you wanting more once the session is done.

Title: Legend of the Ice Dragon
review: Legend of the Ice Dragon: Slot OverviewDragon's in pop culture are nothing new, but one of the less common members of the wider dragon family is the elusive ice dragon. Novels are probably your best bet for bumping into one of these mysterious beasts. Thanks to Swedish developer Play'n GO, players can now tangle with one of these fearsome serpents in Legend of the Ice Dragon, a cluster paying grid slot built on the back of a previous game titled Wild Frames.Play'n GO has come a long way from the purple-coloured Gentleman's Club of Wild Frames to the wind-swept snowy wastes of Legend of the Ice Dragon. Is Play'n GO going for Asian gamblers with this one? Perhaps, since there is an almost traditional Chinese looking dragon chilling on the right-hand side of the screen next to the 7x7 game grid. On the opposite side is the Ice Crystal Charger, while the background alternates between pastel-coloured day and a Borealis lit phase.Mathematically, Legend of the Ice Dragon deviates from Wild Frames but not in a way that will be highly apparent a lot of the time. Both potential and RTP have decreased, which might not be the best news, though the default return value of 96.29% isn't necessarily a showstopper. Volatility has been eased back to 8 out of 10, which is still technically high on Play'n GO's rating system. The biggest clusters consist of 30+ matching symbols, and premium versions of these are worth 75 to 500 times the stake.Legend of the Ice Dragon: Slot FeaturesLegend of the Ice Dragon does not come with a separate bonus game as such, but there is a menagerie of extras such as cascades, Ice Frames, Freezing features, and Ice Crystal features.CascadesWinning clusters are removed from the grid when they hit, and new symbols drop to fill up the empty positions. Cascades can lead to chains of consecutive wins, continuing until no more clusters are created.Ice FramesThe horned 'W' symbol is wild and creates sticky Ice Frames whenever they land. If a wild lands in an existing Ice Frame, it adds a multiplier to it that increases by +1 each time, up to a maximum value of x8. Only the highest multiplier is used for each winning cluster. Ice Frames remain on the grid for the full cascade sequence and are removed when a new spin occurs. The key point here is that Ice Frame Multipliers are inactive until the Dragon Blast feature is triggered - more on that below.Freezing FeaturesOn any non-winning spin, there is a chance Freezing features may randomly trigger. There are 3 of them in total:Hailstorm – 3 instances of one symbol type on the grid are randomly chosen. These symbols plus up to 5 symbols adjacent to them are destroyed or turned wild. Up to 9 wilds may appear.Avalanche – an avalanche covers the grid, destroying all instances of 2 symbol types, leaving up to 7 wilds in their place.Blizzard – up to 5 symbols in the pattern are transformed into wilds or destroyed.Ice Crystal FeaturesWinning symbols fill the Ice Crystal Charger, triggering Ice Crystal features when a certain number of symbols have been collected. 20, 40, 60, or 80 charges activate the Tail Lash, Ice Scorch, Destruction, and Dragon Blast features, respectively.Tail Lash – turns all high pay symbols into one type of high paying symbol.Ice Scorch – transforms 3-6 random symbols into wilds.Destruction – removes all low pay symbols from the panel.Dragon Blast – turns all symbols within Ice Frames into wilds. This also activates the Ice Frame Multipliers.It is also possible to overcharge the Ice Crystal Charger. For every 10 charges over 80, +2 additional Ice Frames are added to the grid.Legend of the Ice Dragon: Slot VerdictIf you're in the mood for some cluster paying grid slot action, and the options are this or Wild Frames, which one would you go for? Each has its pros and cons. The subject matter is completely different, obviously, and a few of the technical details further drive the two games apart, so you couldn't accuse Legend of the Ice Dragon of being an all-out clone as such. Legend of the Ice Dragon arguably offers a more exotic experience than Wild Frames' fruit/Vegas one. However, some players may well prefer tradition to fantasy.Diving into the nuts and bolts, there are clear differences between the two games, suggesting on a technical level at least, why some players might prefer one over the other. Legend of the Ice Dragon is the less volatile option, and its multipliers go to x8 compared to x9 in Wild Frames, resulting in a lower max win figure. However, it's hard to detect much real difference in the gameplay despite the numbers. The goal is still to pile on as many Ice Frames as possible, hit consecutive clusters to fill the Ice Crystal Charger, and hopefully, trigger the Dragon Blast where the multipliers can be put to use. Make it that far, and things can get pretty intense. Though, not quite as intense as Wild Frames, perhaps. Where the previous one could hit 7,000x (which we are yet to see evidence of at the time of writing, mind you), Legend of the Ice Dragon produces 6,000 times the bet in its best-case scenario. Factor in the lower RTP and Legend of the Ice Dragon loses an extra coat of sheen.If you're partial to a bit of Play'n GO grid slot gaming, Legend of the Ice Dragon is worth a look. The winning clusters leading to features dynamic has been put to good use and can produce the occasional big spin where it all comes together. For something slightly more vigorous, Wild Frames might be a better option, but the dragon theme is an entertaining compensation.

Title: Joker Maxima

From an audio-visual standpoint, the stand out feature is a soundtrack a notch or two trancier than the mainstream house music these games usually come with. Close your eyes, and you could be at a low key rave. Overlying the cosmic tune, the joker lady occasionally tosses out seductive one-liners like 'You can't win if you don't play' and so on.Available on any device, Joker Maxima offers stakes of 10 p/c to $/€200 per spin (max bet depends on operator settings). Lucksome is appreciably forthcoming with just about every stat you could ever want, starting on the load screen, which displays a volatilely rated 7 out of 10, plus bonus frequency and win frequency of 4/10 and 5/10, respectively. The game is laid bare right away, so players have a clear idea if Joker Maxima will be the right fit. Keep in mind that when free spins trigger, players are presented with two options, one being a lower volatile 'safer' choice, the other, a higher volatile, higher reward choice. Joker Maxima may ship with a bonus buy, yet RTP remains at 96.11% in all cases no matter how the feature is triggered.In ascending order, symbols include cherries, lemons, grapes, watermelons, bells, and fiery 7s, possessing values of 2-100 times the stake for five of a kind (the latter two symbols only need 2oak for a payout as opposed to three). There are also golden versions of each regular pay symbol; these are worth double the value of the equivalent non-golden symbol. The joker wild is one to keep an eye on for several reasons. Jokers are also involved in some of the features, as we'll see.Joker Maxima: Slot Features﻿When the wild symbol substitutes in a win line, it also applies a multiplier to the amount. The more wilds used, the higher the value, so 1, 2, 3, or 4 jokers on a win line multiply the value by x2, x4, x8, or x16, respectively.Powerbands are implemented in the game in both base game and free spins - the reels light on fire when special reels (Power Bands) are selected and guarantees a 20x or greater win. In free spins when you have a Joker Streak going on, things can get quite intense.One more symbol appears in the game; this is the diamond scatter landing on the middle three reels only. When 3 diamonds are in view 10 free spins are awarded. Before free spins begin, players choose from two options on the Volatility Picker:On the left is the Classic Mode which uses the same wild multiplier values as the base game and is less volatile/less rewarding.The choice on the right is Maxima Mode, where wild multiplier values may be higher or lower than in Classic Mode, so is more volatile/greater potentially rewarding.In free spins, any winning combination is locked in place and triggers a Joker Streak Respin. Respins continue to be awarded as long as new winning symbols land. It is also possible to retrigger +5 free spins when 3 scatters land in view.Should 2 scatters land during the game, Lucksome Locks is enabled. During Lucksome Locks, the 2 scatters are locked, and only scatters are active. If more scatters land in view, free games are triggered.Another way of possibly triggering free spins is by buying them. The cost is 74.6 times the stake, guaranteeing entry to the bonus. There is a limit to the bonus buy of $/€5 base bet, so if you're betting higher, the stake will have to be reduced.Joker Maxima: Slot VerdictAs with Divine Links, it might pay to temper any high expectations you might have regarding Joker Maxima. Like Lucksome's debut, Joker Maxima is a well-made game, possessing more positives than negatives, but you can't help feeling the team is capable of greater things. As far as these fruity, harlequin slots go, Joker Maxima pushes the right buttons, there are no issues with stats, and the potential is appealing as well. However, it is slot design 101, looks like dozens of other games out there and is missing a must-see innovative touch. Joker Maxima makes sure not to put a foot wrong, and if anything, is a safer game than Divine Links was.After clearing the gripes, let's move onto the positive. Features, for one, are quite good, though it helps they've proved their worth elsewhere. Games like NetEnt's Jack Hammer used a similar sticky win system, but Joker Maxima does up the ante by including some strong multiplier action. They do come together nicely at others, though, and multipliers can greatly impact the winning total. While Joker Maxima has what it calls a 'win focus' of 1000x, the studio also states payouts of over 10,000 times your stake are technically possible (though advertised as 7,000x as it's more realistically achievable) - a rather good total for this style of game.Add it all up, and Joker Maxima should prove a temptation for players into these sorts of slots. Once again, it's not the cauldron of innovation it might have been, so perhaps Lucksome is content churning out safe, albeit slickly made, slots for readymade audiences. Or, will the third time be the charm?

Title: Dragon’s Domain
review: Dragon's Domain: Slot OverviewAccording to the info, if you want to take on this game, you'll be needing armour, shield, and sword. When a Charred Land symbol is part of a win, it loses 1 charge before the next cascade. Each time a symbol cascade occurs, each Charred Land symbol on the reels increases its multiplier by +1. When a Charred Land symbol is hit by Dragonfire from a Gold Dragon, its multiplier is multiplied by the Gold Dragon's value.Dragon's Lair BonusHitting 3 dragon eye FS scatter symbols in the base game awards 10 free Dragon's Lair spins. In this bonus, all Charred Land multipliers are persistent between free spins as long as they have charges left. Hitting 2 FS scatters gets you +2 extra free spins, while 3 FS scatters gets you +4 extra spins.The Hatchery BonusLanding 4 FS scatters in the base game triggers 10 free The Hatchery spins. In this feature only non-paying symbols, Dragon Eggs, FS scatters, or Dragon symbols appear. Dragon Eggs are cash prizes that are collected when hit by Dragonfire. Green Eggs have a value of 1x-10x, Red Eggs have a value of 20x-40x, and Golden Eggs have a value of 50x-200x. All non-paying symbols are removed when hit by Dragonfire, causing a cascade. Hitting 2 FS scatters gets you +2 extra free spins, while 3 FS scatters gets you +4 extra spins.Bonus BuyThese bonuses may be activated from Dragon's Domain's bonus buy:BonusHunt FeatureSpins - each spin is 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game for 3x the bet.Scorched Earth FeatureSpins - each spin guarantees at least 2 Charred Land symbols for 50x the bet.Dragon's Lair - 100x the bet.The Hatchery - 200x the bet.Dragon’s Domain slot - The Hatchery free spinsDragon's Domain: Slot VerdictScatter paying slots aren't exactly a major Hacksaw Gaming speciality, but this isn't the first one the studio has made. Hacksaw Gaming's numbers people, with their cold-hearted sadistic mathematics, have balanced the game between potential wild multiplier mayhem and far less interesting to zilch result spins as well.For a slot with scatter wins, cascades, and multiplier symbols, Dragon's Domain executes its gameplay quite differently to Gates of Olympus and other similarly designed titans in its field. Title: Eye of the Storm

Eye of the Storm (the name is a clue), offers a totally different feel. This one is heavy. Dark clouds drift by; lightning flashes down as if war is on the horizon. Far and away, the mood is the most original thing happening in Eye of the Storm.Moving onto another alteration, default RTP is slightly up over Eye of Horus as well, generating a highly respectable figure of 96.71%. Volatility has remained high, so like being lost in the desert, prepare for a lot of sand before stumbling upon an oasis. Each level upgrades the premium high pay symbols. So, the first wild upgrades folding-fans to Ankhs, then the next wild turns Ankhs into scarabs. In turn, scarabs become birds, then jackals, until finally it is possible the only premium on the reels is the top paying eye symbol. Of course, this significantly increases the likelihood of landing higher value combinations. Lastly, free spins are retriggered when 3 or more scatters land.Eye of the Storm: Slot VerdictIt's hard to find much to commend about this enterprise. Maybe it looks a bit nicer, a bit more modern when compared to the somewhat dated graphics of the original. Then again, part of Eye of Horus' charm is its nostalgia-inducing old school look. As they say, beauty is in the eye of the beholder, so this will be up to individual players to decide of course. For some straw grasping, the wild has changed, so some may prefer the charms of a leggy warrior type over a traditional 2d image of a deity. Then there are the statistical changes, RTP being the most positive one if you play at a casino using the highest setting, though high rollers may also appreciate the ability to set much higher stakes if they so choose.So while Eye of the Storm isn't a bad game to play as such, did the world really need another Eye of Horus wannabe? Whatever the answer to the above question is, it's no surprise Reel Kingdom were the one to do it. A quick scroll through their catalogue reveals copies of Fishin' Frenzy, 'book of' rip offs, Reel King, and now Eye of Horus. It's like travelling through an alternate universe where everything is the same, yet not.Eye of the Storm ends up being one of those games that could well entertain Egypt fans who aren't aware of the original or who simply don't have access to it. The increased RTP is a positive too, of course. However, being such a shameless copy strips Eye of the Storm of whatever cool points it might have possessed. Title: Easter Eggspedition

If Foxy Loot lands, the Cash Pot value is returned to zero. If the Super Bunny and Foxy Loot land at the same time, Super Bunny takes priority over the Foxy Loot. The number of respins is capped at 155.Easter Eggspedition slot - bonus gameEaster Eggspedition: Slot VerdictIt might be a little hard getting hugely worked up over the thought of a reskin of a game that was average to begin with. Oh wait, despite the name, The Race Megaways doesn't involve fast-moving cars, fast-moving people, fast-moving anything, really. Instead, The Race Megaways has more of a gameshow vibe to it. In fact, a series called 'The Race' aired on British tv in 2006, but after a bit of YouTube-ing, the show and slot have virtually nothing in common. Back to square one then, so we might as well put a stop to the internet trawling, fire up The Race Megaways and simply let it do its stuff.Visually, it does feel like participants have stepped into a studio, about to be asked quick-fire questions in hopes of winning cash prizes or consumer goods. Not a billion miles away from Who Wants to Be a Millionaire, a format which Big Time Gaming is familiar with. In the middle of the, err stage, sits a 6-reel game grid, with a bolted-on 4-symbol extra reel located down the bottom rather than in its usual position up top, while red lights sparkle on either side and extra lighting beams down from above. Not sure what to make of it. The view isn't bad, but as a game show, The Race Megaways lacked the vitality found in Who Wants to Be a Millionaire Megaways or Wheel of Fortune Megaways.The Race Megaways slot - base gameTickets to the show, as such, start at 20 p/c per spin before topping out at $/€20 per paid game round. Very highly volatile, the game comes with an overall return to player value of 96.27%, or when buying a bonus, the RTP increases to 96.36%. Individual spins can drop different numbers of symbols on the main reels, producing up to 117,649 ways to win.Hitting matching symbols on adjacent reels from the leftmost side of the panel triggers a reward. The value of which varies from 0.5 to 0.9 times the stake when consisting of six low pay 9 to A symbols, or 1 to 12.5 times the bet for six of the four high pay gemstone tiles. Wilds are one of The Race Megaways' key components, where their duties include substituting for any pay symbol and tying into some of the features.The Race Megaways: Slot FeaturesThe Race Megaways slot - Heart bonusSpecifically, when reels stop spinning, a wild symbol may duplicate. When a Wild Duplication occurs, all symbols on the vertical reel are replaced by wild symbols. In addition, during free spins, each wild that is added to the reels by the Wild Duplication process gets a multiplier of up to x5. Wilds do not hit on reels 1 or 6.ReactionsA classic Megaways extra, the reaction mechanic removes all winning symbols except scatters from the reels, replacing them with symbols from above on the main reels or the right on the extra reel. Reactions end when no new win is created.Heart Bonus RoundWhen at least 3 scatter symbols land in the base game, they trigger the Heart Bonus Round (or you can buy direct access for 100 times your stake). Here, 3 respins are awarded on special reels that only land Hearts or blanks. Heart symbols lock to the reels and reset the respin count when they land. When no more respins remain, or all positions are filled, the round ends, and free spins begin.The Race Megaways slot - free spinsUnlimited Free SpinsThe number of Heart symbols in view at the end of the Heart Round Bonus award lives, which carry over to the free spins round. Here, the win multiplier starts at x1 and increases after each reaction. When a Terminator symbol lands, 1 life is lost. When all lives are lost, the free spins feature ends. Scatters are not present during free spins.Win Exchange and Bonus BuyWhen players win 100 times the stake or more, they have the option of buying entrance to the Heart Bonus Round for the cost of 100x the bet. If a win worth between 25 and 100 times the stake occurs, players can swap the win for a chance to win entrance to the Heart Bonus Round.The Race Megaways slot - bonus buy optionsThe Race Megaways: Slot VerdictNot so sure about this one. Technically, The Race Megaways is alright, it's got some wild duplicating action going on, free spins with an 'unlimited' element and a pre-feature bonus round where the life collecting takes place. For a game that refers to or alludes to a race, it felt strangely lacking in adrenaline. A baffling slot in many ways, actually, since there's little racing going on unless we're missing something achingly obvious, making it hard to tell quite what The Race Megaways is trying to get at. Dragged-out bonus rounds often had the tendency to end in great disappointment and with nothing much happening other than watching the win multiplier grow.As a game show style event, it pales in comparison to the previous game show slots Big Time Gaming has made. To be fair, those ones (like Who Wants to Be a Millionaire and Wheel of Fortune Megaways) were built off the back of actual real-world shows, so they possessed strong brand recognition. The Race Megaways, by comparison, feels like some producers made a pilot episode which ended up being canned by the powers that be at the network, thereby remaining anonymous. Nothing wrong with going for a non-branded game show angle, of course, but The Race Megaways, while lacking killer excitement, also lacked depth, personality, or whatever you call that certain 'je ne sais quoi' which elevates a tv show from obscurity to household name.Perhaps it's because Big Time Gaming has produced some of the most memorable slots of all time, as well as one of gambling's most popular gaming mechanics, that expectations run high when facing a new release. However, even if The Race Megaways had come from a new up-and-coming studio yet to make its mark, it's questionable if our reaction would have been much warmer. It simply lacked the drama, ingenuity, the passion one typically associates with a Big Time Gaming production. Put it this way, if The Race Megaways did pop up on the telly, it would be hard not to quickly switch the channel.

When no new winning symbols appear, the number collected is multiplied by the individual value to calculate the payout.The paytable consists of 10 regular symbols and several specials we'll look at below. Making up the low pays are J-A royals, then three glowing gems, followed by three exotically carved heads. Values range from 0.05 for each lowly Jack up to 0.6x for red Hindu-looking masks. A golden 'W' is the wild, which substitutes for any normal symbol.Monkey’s Gold: Slot FeaturesNoLimit City layers on more complexity and winning opportunities through a bunch of extra features. The hottest one is free spins with a progressive multiplier, joined by colossal symbols, symbol multipliers, and symbol upgrades.Symbol upgrades tie directly to xPays. When a row is filled during a spin sequence, all winning symbols in view are upgraded to a higher paying version. The highest paying symbol gets upgraded with an added multiplier.At random, 2x2 or 3x3 colossal symbols may land on any free drop. Not only do they contribute their bulk, they also come with a multiplier of x4 to x500. Let's be clear; this multiplies the number of symbols collected, not the total win. If colossal symbols drop, forming empty positions beneath them, any gaps become wilds. Any symbol with a multiplier on it gets counted as multiple symbols rather than just a single. Moreover, when substituting for other symbols, wilds inherit any active symbol multiplier.Monkey's Gold pulls all this good stuff together and sprinkles on a win multiplier during free spins. To get there, you need to land 3 or more scatter symbols - this will award you 10 free spins whilst +3 extra spins are added for any additional scatter symbol.Before free spins commence, a dice is rolled to reveal how much the win multiplier increments by; +1, +2 or +3. Whenever a row is filled during free spins, as well as upgrading symbols, it increases the win multiplier by the respective amount.Last up is the feature buy where for 73 times the stake at least three bonus symbols land on the next drop.Monkey’s Gold: Slot VerdictIt's funny, playing Monkey's Gold xPays caused flashes of half a dozen slots to bubble up from the subconscious. First, there is an ELK's Gold feel to it, stemming from both features and mechanics. There's even a bit of Yggdrasil's Pirate 2: Mutiny worming its way in due to the way the winning symbol collection system works. Despite the melange of memories, Monkey's Gold has its own individuality. Features that might have been seen elsewhere have been twisted, and arguably improved. You have to hand it to Nolimit City; even when they might have allowed themselves to be inspired by others, they can't help put an individual stamp on them.Nolimit has done a superb job of integrating the features, so when they fire together, the experience can only be described as thrilling. Collected winning symbols, triggering full row upgrades, capped by the progressive multiplier during free spins is sublime in practice.Nolimit City might have taken inspiration from other sources, or appeared to, yet it really doesn't matter. What they've crafted here is a highly playable slot with some appealing features. They work best in tandem, yet even in isolation they can raise the roof. Take the symbol multiplier as an example. Okay, this isn't going to happen often, but in testing, a colossal Ace landed during free spins, packing an eye-watering x250 multiplier. In a heartbeat, what was shaping up as an average bonus became an instant heart racer. At full tilt, solid wins of up to 12,693 times the bet are possible. And as we all know by now, Nolimit City stated win potential is actually achievable, something that cannot be said for some of their competitors.Nolimit City has further cemented their creative credentials by designing a game that reminds you of others while transcending them at the same time. It's not as brutal, or as rewarding, as some heavyweights in the feature on feature category. It nevertheless is an absolute joy to play when it's stacking on features and wins like there's no tomorrow. Fans of straight forward gaming may struggle to appreciate the complexities, but for those who like the multi-layered wedding cake angle, Monkey's Gold piles it on with best of them.

Title: Wild West Gold Megaways
review: Wild West Gold Megaways: Slot OverviewSaddle up, y'all, software provider Pragmatic Play heads back West, by squeezing a few extra miles out of their highly successful slot Wild West Gold. To do so, they've given the previous game a Megaways makeover, boosting the core mechanics while leaving the original features largely untouched. So, will the resulting game delight fans or add fuel to the righteous indignation felt by critics of the Megaways upgrade factory line? Grab them thar leather chaps and join us to find out.The first few noticeable changes are mostly cosmetic. Naturally, the game grid has been stretched to accommodate 6 reels, holding anything from 2 to 7 symbols each. Ways vary as they do when using this system, maxing out at 117,649 when all reels are full. The main initial difference, though, is the change of music. This time, Pragmatic Play's sound team have dialled up the 'gritty West' setting on their synthesiser, compared to the lively saloon piano sounds of before. The track change isn't better or worse for our money, just different. So far, it was a case of 'will there be any deeper alterations?'Well, the grid might have grown in size, but many of the numbers have shrunk. One is RTP, where the highest value is 96.44%, or 96.41% when the Ante Bet is activated. Normal stakes vary from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, while the Ante Bet adds 25% to the cost to have extra scatter symbols added to the reels. Volatility has remained high, rated at 5 out of 5; potential, on the other hand, has not, and to be honest, is one of the weakest things about Wild West Gold Megaways as you will see.Wins are awarded when at least three matching symbols land in adjacent reels, starting from the leftmost reel. In spite of being a Megaways game, cascades do not occur when wins hit, whether in the bonus or base game. Instead, players receive a one-off win worth 0.25-0.3x the bet when made of the 10-A low pay symbols, or 0.4-1x the bet when made up of the higher value pistols, gold bags, or four character symbols. Wilds are critical to pounding out better value wins in Wild West Gold Megaways. They land on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5 to substitute any paying symbol. In addition, wilds can have random multipliers of x2, x3, or x5, and multiply each other if more than one is used in a win.Wild West Gold Megaways: Slot FeaturesAs well as wild multipliers, the other feature in Wild West Gold Megaways is its free spins bonus round. This is triggered when 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters symbols land to award a payout of 4x, 20x, 100x, or 500x the bet plus 7 free spins. During free spins, whenever a wild symbol hits, it gets a multiplier of x2, x3, or x5, and remains on the reels until the round ends. This being a Megaways powered grid, wilds change size as the number of symbols on the reels change. Lastly, when 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 gold star overly icons are in view, players win an extra 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 free spins.Bonus BuyEligible players are able to buy free spins rather than trigger them organically. For the cost of 100x the bet, a spin occurs, which lands 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols. Buying the bonus has an RTP value of 96.45%.Wild West Gold Megaways: Slot VerdictIt's doubtful you need us to tell you how prevalent Megaways has become. From humble beginnings under the watchful eye of Big Time Gaming to one of the most successful licences in online gambling. The growth has been phenomenal, and it's not without its detractors. When the upgrade process significantly improves the experience of an older slot, fair dues, it can be a win-win situation for all involved. At other times, though, the Megawaysification of an already established game can come across like a cynical, if not lazy, cash grab. Not saying that Wild West Gold Megaways falls into the latter category, but Pragmatic Play has done little to massively justify the Megaways re-release. Quite the opposite, really.In terms of audio-visuals and gameplay, Wild West Gold Megaways is as solid as ever. If you've ever daydreamed about Dead or Alive Megaways, this, along with Desperados Wild Megaways, is about as close as it gets, although when directly compared it is more of a The Dog House Megaways sibling than anything else. It might have been nice if cascades had been wedged in there somewhere, yet the wild multipliers make up for their exclusion. More so when wilds are sticky in free spins - then they can be a riot.And yet, the stench of disappointment lingered throughout the review. Not because of anything Wild West Gold Megaways does, but what it isn't allowed to do. What continually drove home the feeling of 'why did they bother?' is the decreased potential. From the 6,750x of the previous version to the 5,000x of this one. Imagine if NetEnt ever released Dead or Alive Megaways with a 5K win cap slapped on, the thing would be run out of town tarred and featured before noon.To sum up, Wild West Gold Megaways could have been a genuine badass. However, it's not, and that's a shame. If fans of the first were screaming out for a Megaways version, they've got it, but it's hard not to wonder why Pragmatic Play went with the low (for Megaways) max win. Had they backed it with a more impressive figure, Wild West Gold Megaways could have been that outlaw who saunters into town and causes everyone to stare at the ground to avoid making eye contact. Never mind a knife; at this level of potential, there was a feeling Wild West Gold Megaways brought trongs to a gunfight.

Title: Age of Huracan
review: Age of Huracan: Slot OverviewBefore the year 2012, whenever you heard about the Mayans, prophecies about the end of the world probably weren't far from your mind. It had to do with the Maya Long Count, pointing to December 21 (or 23), 2012 as some sort of end date. Fortunately for humanity, the cataclysm many had predicted, feared or hoped for, passed by as uneventfully as the Y2K scare did. Computers didn't get confused, there was no planetary collision, and the sky didn't rain down destruction. It was a pretty standard Friday like any other where people got up, went to school or work, then unwound after a hard week, and life went on.Then again, perhaps the apocalypse is a drawn-out event that only kicked off in 2012? Time will tell. Until then, we've got Age of Huracan from Kalamba Games to give players a taste of what might come to pass. Huracán (Spanish for "hurricane") was the Mayan God of Storms, and he brings plenty of those to one of Age of Huracan's bonus games. As well as free spins, players seek glory via a K-Cash feature or hit the Hyper Bonus to shortcut to either.Unless you've been following Kalamba Games like a Facebook stalker, you might not know Age of Huracan is the studio's 50th slot. The game does look like it was designed by an experienced provider too, where a 5-reel, 1,024 pay ways grid is embedded in a nicely drawn jungle, full of verdant plant life and moss-covered temples. Age of Huracan looks nice, but hold out for free spins if you're interested in the premise because Kalamba steps up the show when they hit.Any device is fine for dodging the downpour, where stakes range from 50 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Mathematically, Kalamba has chosen to design a rather high-performance slot for their 50th release, marrying solid potential to a highly volatile game engine they've rated as 9 out of 10. Hit frequency is a tad lower than might be expected at 16.7%, though most players will be satisfied with an RTP of between 96.62% and 96.75% - the bonus buy options accounting for the variety.On to the paytable, which throws up a few minor oddities around how symbols pay. One is the lowest symbol, and the two highest symbols pay out on two of a kind or more, while the rest need at least three to do so. Symbols start with 9-A card suits, then daggers, glowing green things, and four Mayan characters are used. The three least profitable characters pay 2 to 10x the bet for five of a kind, yet the top one stands out since it's worth 100x for five. One final symbol before we head into the storms is the Mayan Calendar looking wild, substituting for all other symbols except the Bonus or K-Cash.Age of Huracan: Slot FeaturesKalamba has made a few adjustments to a hold & win feature, titling it K-Cash, and bolted on a round of free spins for a few more thrills. During the base game, blue or orange K-Cash symbols may land on any reel; Blue ones add a cash amount to the meter on the top right, orange ones fill a meter on the left with every 5 increasing the multiplier by 1, up to x5.When 3 or more K-Cash symbols appear, they lock in place, and 3 K-Cash Spins are triggered. Each new K-Cash symbol locks and resets the number of remaining spins to 3. As before, orange symbols increment the multiplier meter. At the end, when spins run out or all positions are filled, the monetary amount collected is increased by the multiplier and paid out. In addition, full grid wins award a prize equal to 10x the bet, times the value of the multiplier meter.The mysterious figure standing before a tornado is the scatter symbol. Landing 3, 4, or 5 in the base game award 3, 8, or 15 free spins plus a payout of 2, 5, or 10 times the stake. Nothing new is added for free spins, aside from a dramatic stormy background, though the bonus can be retriggered when 2, 3, 4, or 5 scatters land to award 3, 8, 12, or 15 free spins.The final extra is the HyperBonus, provided feature buys are permitted where you live. Players get three choices. One is 3 Cash Spins with a starting x5 multiplier for 21.2x the bet, or 8, or 15 free spins for 35.4x or 66.3x the total stake.Age of Huracan: Slot VerdictThere are good things in Age of Huracan, but the features could have been jerked a bit harder to boost the game's appeal. Up first, the way the K-Cash collector lets you build value before K-Cash Spins actually trigger is quite interesting. It adds a new dimension for hold & win fans to experiment with. What lets it down is the values aren't amazing. For instance, the multiplier meter tops out at x5, while K-Cash symbols can be worth 4 times the bet at the most. Busting out a calculator means a full screen of symbols, with absolutely everything maxed, is worth 400x the bet. There is the Full Grid prize, yet still, don't expect a gigantic total.Other game phases don't suffer the same underwhelming fate in regards to potential; tornado chasers will be pleased to know. Age of Huracan has a max win figure of 10,240 times the bet, which happens to be the same value as a full grid of the top pay symbol. Again though, free spins would have benefited from a modifier to make them more exciting than the base game. They're utterly devoid of any extra interest; you can't even collect K-Cash symbols when they are active. It's almost a relief once free spins are over so you can get back to the base game and pick up where you left off.As a 50th release, Age of Huracan in many ways sums up the Kalamba journey so far - great visuals, plenty of atmosphere, respectable stats, but head-scratching features. It wouldn't have hurt if extra thought had gone into free spins and extra dough into K-Cash Spins.
