Three RTP options have been designed, where the most optimal value is the 96.05% version.Royal Nuts' low pay symbols are 10, J, Q, K, and A playing card ranks, while its high pays are three Royal Nut character symbols. Wilds are a prominent part of Royal Nuts, and they are able to substitute for any of the regular paying symbols.Royal Nuts: Slot FeaturesRoyal Nuts slot - free spinsOne mission of Royal Nuts is to transform those Royal Nuts symbols into Golden Wild Nuts, which come in three varieties. This happens randomly in the base game or via a collection feature in the free spins round.Golden Wild NutsIn the base game, the Golden Wild Nuts feature may randomly trigger, activating different kinds of wilds. Next to the grid, the 3 Royal Nuts high pay symbols on display highlight and indicate the Golden Wild Nuts transformation for each symbol. These three possibly wild types are:Regular Wild - A Royal Nut transforms into a wild.Stacked Wild - A Royal Nut transforms into a Stacked Wild, able to land in random stacks of 2 to 4 symbols high in the base game or up to 5 symbols high in free spins.Expanding Wild - A Royal Nut transforms into an Expanding Wild, which expands to cover all positions on its reel.Free SpinsIn the base game, landing 3, 4 or 5 scatter symbols anywhere on the grid awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. In free spins, gem symbols may land on the reels. These are collected by their respective meters when they do. Next to the grid, the Royal Nuts collect these blue, red, or green gems according to the colour of each Royal Nut symbol. A white gem increases all 3 Royal Nuts meters by +1. When a collection meter accumulates 2 gems, the Regular Wild is activated. Collecting a further 2 gems upgrades the wild to Stacked Wild, and another 2 collected gems upgrades to Expanding Wilds. Scatters do not appear during free spins, so the feature cannot be retriggered.Free Spins BuyIt is possible to use the bonus buy option to buy entrance to the free spins round for a cost of 65 times the bet.Royal Nuts slot - free spinsRoyal Nuts: Slot VerdictAround the time of Royal Nuts' review, NetEnt's release schedule had been pretty inconsistent. Some decent stuff, such as Casino Nights, had been mixed in with some less intriguing stuff, like Ticket To Wild, though overall, there hadn't been anything hugely standout-ish for a while. Royal Nuts wasn't a major standout either, but it was one of the better slots, and several factors contributed to making it so.One positive factor was Royal Nuts' affable presentation. Fruit you get a lot of in slots; nuts, though? Not so much. As such, it was hard to draw thematic parallels with many other games, but one that did spring to mind (it's not about nuts) was NetEnt's own Bee Hive Bonanza. The two games share a cutesy look, regal characters, and fairly uncomplicated, yet enjoyable, gameplay. The nut characters and their nutty world do well to draw you in, and neat moments such as the musical touches help slap a smile on the face while there. Royal Nuts' sights and sounds have been ideally matched with the uncomplicated gameplay, where random Golden Wild Nuts sprinkle salt on the base game while the progressive gem hunt adds flavour to the free spins round. Not a lot that is extraordinary, yet good for a few laughs when all is going well and for producing wins of up to 5,774x.So, is the time of the nut's overthrow of fruit as the dominant online slot culinary delight upon us? Probably not, because while fruits are bold, bright, and colourful, nuts are arguably a bit drab-looking by comparison. Title: Gorilla Mayhem

Title: The Magic Orb Hold & Win

Title: Christmas Megaways
review: Christmas Megaways: Slot OverviewUK based Iron Dog Studio decorate their Branded Megaways concept in tinsel and wrapping for punters looking for something to spin during the holiday season. This one, Christmas Megaways, is a wholly Iron Dog affair, perhaps released in an attempt to show what the software can do as much as cash in on Xmas. Christmas Megaways shows how easily the format can be configured, yet is also reveals limitations, thus resulting in a final product that gives some mixed feelings.The layout is classic Branded Megaways with the four-star free spins meter located on the right and company brand-name, or in this case title, on the left above the Megaways counter. In the centre sits the 6-reel game area, capable of randomly producing between 64-117,749 ways to win on each spin. Surrounding the slot is a winter scene, all snowy mountains, gift packages, and starry skies. When 4 or more consecutive tumbles occur, 8 free spins are awarded. For each tumble past 4, an additional 2 free spins are added to the total, up to a maximum of 14. If on the triggering spin, or any free spins, there is a reel holding 7 symbols, it is locked at this height for the duration of the bonus. If reels are locked on the final free spin, then one more spin is added. The bonus round also uses a win multiplier that increases by +1 after a win with no upper limit. Also, should four consecutive tumbles in the bonus game occur, players win 4 extra free spins - each extra tumble past four adding 2 up to a max of 14.Finally, where applicable, players may buy a batch of free spins. There are several price options, starting from 30x the bet for 6 free spins, up to 130x the bet for 10 free spins and one already locked reel.Christmas Megaways: Slot VerdictLet's start by acknowledging Christmas Megaways' gameplay isn't bad, it's actually quite good from a technical standpoint. In saying so, it's the same as Branded Megaways or Pirate Kingdom which came before it. If you liked those, and the pirate one was a something of a hit, then chances are you'll appreciate this. Then again, repeat performances in slots often fall flat, especially on the third outing. Mix in the sterile treatment of one of the jolliest times of the year, and Christmas Megaways struggles to be very exciting.In many ways Christmas Megaways feels like exactly what it is. Someone, possibly the Grinch, thought it was enough to just fill in a few gaps on a template, and boom, there's a slot. The problem is it has ended up being as unimaginative as the title. Technically, players could find thrills here, but why would you when there are so many other Christmas themed slots that actually come across as a little heart-warming. This one feels about 100 degrees icier than Iron Dog's 1 Million Megaways BC which was set in the actual ice age when eggnog by a roaring indoor fire was a far off dream.The Branded idea is an intriguing one, but judging by this effort, it seems operators are getting a better deal. It's great for them since they can customise games by bunging logos and whatnot on there. Not so hot for players, since what emerges is a soulless, cut and paste job. Slot painting by numbers if you will. Maybe we are being too harsh. Some players might like the toned-down Christmas approach, not to mention potential is massive at 40,000 times the bet.Hey, it's early days with the Branded thing so who knows where it will go next. What's clear at the moment is that if Christmas Megaways doesn't outshine the cookie-cutter issue for you, then it's about as fun as being blazing hungover on Christmas Day in the company of annoying in-laws.

Title: Buildin’ Bucks

Title: Towering Pays Excalibur

At the end of the round, prize values on the locked shield symbols are awarded. If shield symbols display a Feature Wheel, this is awarded when the Hold & Spin ends. For dynamic gaming that can't sit still, it might be worth a whirl; otherwise, it just seems rife with redundancies.One of the issues is a large number of named features that do essentially the same thing. First clicking through the paytable, skim reading headlines makes it seem like Towering Pays Excalibur is an absolute feature fiesta. When you start drilling down on the details, you realise a lot of them are similar and it perhaps might have been more effective if there was just one or two really good extras rather than a bunch of average ones. There is a lot of stacked symbol action going on, but also strange situations when, say, the 5x8 grid is active with loads of matching symbols, but just one winning line. Excalibur might have worked better if some of the excess had been trimmed away into something streamlined rather than the overabundance of too similar extras? Just a thought. Towering Pays Excalibur might lose its point then, though, which is presumably to be a feature-fest on a dynamic set of reels.After a while, there are so many moving parts in Towering Pays Excalibur they tend to blur together, making it tough to see what was used before and what wasn't. The result ends up feeling less like a progression over what came before, than just more complexity with an Arthurian bent.

Then again, squeezing in some last-minute shopping on Christmas Eve amongst throngs of panicked shoppers might well be some peoples' idea of horror. But we digress. Title: The Big Dawgs

Revealing one of the DAWG words triggers Dirty Dawg free spins. Revealing both DAWG words triggers Double Dawgs free spins.Dirty Dawg Free SpinsThis round begins with 5 free spins. During it, a total multiplier is applied to all wins in the sequence. The multiplier starts at x1 and increases by +1 for each winning tumble. At the end of a free spin, the multiplier returns to x1. Revealing one of the DAWG words during the feature awards +5 free spins. Revealing both DAWG words triggers Double Dawg free spins when the current round ends. The rules are the same as Dirty Dawg free spins, except the win multiplier does not reset at the end of each free spin.Buy Free SpinsFrom the bonus buy section, players can buy a spin that triggers Dirty Dawg free spins for 80x the bet (RTP 96%) or a spin that triggers Double Dawg free spins for 250x the bet (95.95%).The Big Dawgs slot - feature buy optionsThe Big Dawgs: Slot VerdictThe Big Dawgs is an absolute mongrel of a game which pulls in influences, echoes, and repeats from all over the place. From the graffiti stylising of a punk Hacksaw Gaming slot, Top Dawg$ from Relax Gaming, Play'n GO's Moon Princess range as well as Golden Ticket 2, East Coast vs West Coast… take your pick, it's got DNA strands from across the iGaming spectrum. One slight letdown is The Big Dawgs' 5,000x the bet max win, which, while nothing to cock a leg at, is outshone by some of its competitors/influences.We could be cynical and say The Big Dawgs is too close for comfort to too many other games. The point is... sorry, got lost in a haze of dog affection there; the Big Dawgs might not be the most original, heck, it might have blatantly nicked other studios' ideas, but it's still a playable game, bitey, with plenty of slobbery affection to give, if you're in its good books.

Title: Gator Gold Gigablox

Title: Firefly Frenzy
review: Firefly Frenzy (Play'n GO): OverviewThe light of a firefly is the most efficient light there is. Nearly 100% of the energy in the chemical reaction is emitted as light. Starting with 8 free spins, the value of the lowest multiplier appearing during the free spins will be the same as the firefly that activated it.In practicality, this means that if the feature was triggered by a 2x firefly wild, the multiplier wilds will be either 2x or 3x. The feature can also be retriggered in the same way, with the firefly that retriggered it now replacing the previous firefly to become the lowest multiplier that can land.Firefly Frenzy (Play'n GO): VerdictVisually and mechanically, Firefly Frenzy follows every convention you can imagine and ticks many of the boxes already established by other providers. Furthermore, we can't help but feel there should have been more of a twist to the free spin feature, maybe by boosting the multipliers or by offering enhanced reels with stacked wilds.With that said, Firefly Frenzy is still a decent game and a must try for those who are into high variance slots. The potential here is outstanding as well, but don't count on landing the max win of 10,000 times your stake as you only have about a 1 in a 43 million chance to do so. As is the case with any volatile slot, most of your bonuses will be quite mediocre (which is necessary as the slot needs to collect cash for the jackpot payouts), but with the massive potential distributed across both the base game and the free spin feature, the chance of landing a colossal win is there from the very first spin.

Moving up to the more valuable symbols we see gazelles, cheetahs, rhinos and elephants on the reels - the latter being the most lucrative one giving you 20 times your stake for 5 of a kind as well as being the only symbol appearing fully stacked on the reels.King of the feline family and top predator of the savannah, it's the lion that is the centre of attention here. Now, every bonus symbol that appears on the reels during the bonus adds one more free spin to your total with no limit to how many times you can retrigger the feature.As you've likely already figured out, the combination of retriggers and added wilds makes for quite an exciting bonus as the potential for landing the 1000x max win (full-screen elephants/lions) increases with every spin played.Safari King (Pragmatic Play): ConclusionSafari King makes no attempt to come across as anything other than the simple, rather ordinary, slot that it is. It's not bad mind you and the 1000x per spin win potential undoubtedly makes it worth a shot. With that said, there's that generic feel to it, made worse by its uninspiring savannah theme that we've seen too many times before.This is not Pragmatic's proudest moment, and maybe it was never meant to be. Title: Game of Gladiators Uprising
review: Game of Gladiators Uprising: Slot OverviewAfter a glance at Game of Gladiators, an online slot from Play'n GO released back in 2019, the urge to express some righteous anti-revisionist history rhetoric began to stir, but before launching into a tirade, we took a step back and launched into some Wikipedia trolling instead. And you know what? Back in the day, there were indeed both male and female gladiators doing battle on the sand for audiences' entertainment. The female version of a gladiator is called a gladiatrix, and they fought animals as well as each other, like their male counterparts. They weren't as numerous as male gladiators back then, though, nor are they as numerous in pop culture now. Perhaps Game of Gladiators Uprising will help rectify the situation.You know, going out on a sports pitch or court to play a game can be a nerve-racking experience, so it's hard to imagine how it would feel when a portcullis cranked open then running into an amphitheatre with a group of armed adversaries. Hashtag shudder. Fortunately, doing so is no longer really an option, though one way of getting a taste, a minor one, of what it might have been like, is via games like Game of Gladiators Uprising. Okay, maybe not so much, but Play'n GO has created a pretty neat scene, being completely serious about it without a hint of humour. In the middle of an arena sits a 5x4 game grid while the gladiator Spartacus is locked up on the left, Bellica on the right, as Emperor Gaius sits up top in his special emperor box seat. A fairly unique view that tees things up for the battling, literally, between combatants to come.Game of Gladiators Uprising slot - base gameA little surprising, perhaps given the life and death subject matter, but Game of Gladiators Uprising runs on a medium volatile math model (6 out of 10), with a bunch of RTP models from 84.2% to 96.2%, market-dependent. Playable on tablets, mobile, or desktop devices, it takes bets of 5 p/c to $/€100 per spin, making it suitable for almost every gambling budget. Running across the game grid is 30 fixed paylines where winning combinations of three to five of a kind can hit. For the low pays, we find angular J-A royals worth 1 to 1.4 times the bet for five-of-a-kind or 5 to 30 times the bet for five of the shackles, chisels, morning stars, or helmet premium symbols.Game of Gladiators Uprising: Slot FeaturesGame of Gladiators Uprising slot - Emperor Strike featureGladiator symbols are present on any of the reels and act as wild and scatter. There are three wild types, Spartacus, Bellica, and Emperor Gaius. All three can substitute for any pay symbol and trigger a feature. Game of Gladiators Uprising's other extra is its battle-filled round of free spins.Gladiator's OathWhen a single type of gladiator symbol lands on the reels, a respin is triggered. Depending on the gladiator, the respin also comes with a modifier extra:Legion Slash – Spartacus adds 3 to 5 wilds on the reels.Full Strike – Bellica adds 1 or 2 full reel wilds to the reels.Emperor Strike – Emperor Gaius adds 2 or 3 x2 multiplier wilds to the reels.During respins, any gladiators landing on the grid will not trigger another respin.Champions of the ArenaLanding 2 types of gladiator symbols on the reels triggers Champions of the Arena free spins. Before the round begins, players pick which gladiator will win in the Guess the Victor section. If the pick is correct, at the end, 5x the bet is awarded as a result. Now, during this feature, free spins continue until a gladiator wins or loses the battle, with up to 100 free spins at the most. Each gladiator starts with 3 lives. Collecting 5 of the same gladiator symbols reaches a collect point on the meter above the reels, triggering a respin with the gladiator's respective modifier, plus a random multiplier of x2, x5, x10, or x50. Each triggered respin decreases their opponent's life. When a gladiator has lost 3 lives, free spins end. If the maximum number of spins is reached, the battle is considered a draw and the Guess the Victor reward is not awarded. However, if both gladiators reach the third attack point at the same time, the Guess the Victor is awarded.Game of Gladiators Uprising slot - free spins paytableGame of Gladiators Uprising: Slot VerdictIt's not too hard to see Game of Gladiators Uprising offering a decent level of entertainment for the right folk. Play'n GO hasn't just tossed a few warrior symbols on a reel matrix in the middle of an amphitheatre and called it a day, but has taken the time to work in a more cinematic battle element for free spins. This selling point for some might be anathema to others, yet it is different, and if Ancient Rome slots appeal, then Game of Gladiators Uprising's uniqueness might raise pulses amongst certain members of its target audience.That's good because when coldly dissecting the three modifiers on their own, they aren't particularly special. Although, full reel wilds, wild multipliers and added wilds do have the ability to link up into something pretty handy at times. And they can be more potent in the bonus round, too, since multipliers of up to x50 are theoretically possible. In numerical terms, this translates to a game which can hit up to 6,000 times the stake when it's going full force. Factor in up to 100 free spins, though one wonders how often that cap will be called into use, and Game of Gladiators Uprising might well offer a significant bang for buck quotient.All up, Game of Gladiators Uprising might not be as potentially lucrative as NetEnt's Rome The Golden Age or heroic as 300 Shields Mighty Ways (nor arguably as brutal); it may lose the fight against other well-made classically themed slots. However, bring everything together, and there's something unique about Game of Gladiators Uprising, so for those who like to combine gambling with gladiators, it's not a bad option.

Title: Free Reelin' Joker
review: Free Reelin' Joker: Slot OverviewA glance at the title and screenshots is all it takes to recognise Free Reelin' Joker as another entry in Play'n GO's popular Joker line-up of slots. The only exception to this rule is mixed wins; they do not expand. For example, if you land a plum, a lemon, and a joker – a reel will not be added in this case.If the added reel increases the win, another one is added, and so on up to 6 reels wide at the most. For players after some light, single payline action in a joker-focused game, Free Reelin' Joker would make a pretty good option. Visually at least, it's one of the more attractive joker themed games to come from this studio.Moving from there on to gameplay, where the Free Reelin' Fun feature chugs the game along while building larger wins in the process. However, Free Reelin' Joker isn't anywhere as unique or as potentially profitable as Seven 7's was.What you want to happen in this one is to land jokers on all 6 reels, including a golden joker, to crack the games top prize. Do so, and a win worth 1,000 times the stake is coming your way. For players who like to know the odds, the chance of that happening is one in 735,917. In other words, max win isn't going to occur often, but the lower volatility means regular wins for players who like constant, albeit diminutive, hits to keep them engaged.It's fair to say hardcore gamblers will find little about Free Reelin' Joker to get hyped about. On the flip side, it would be ideal for a casual one line distraction, as long as massive wins aren't a requirement. Title: Tricks And Treats
review: Tricks and Treats: Slot OverviewAll Saints' Day eve must be just around the corner because, at the time of review, a couple of creepy-themed slots had crept out of the woodwork in time for Halloween. Largely thanks to North American tradition, Halloween is synonymous with collecting free candy, and not dishing any out will result in some sort of dastardly trick. This leads us to today's game, an online slot from Red Tiger titled Tricks and Treats, which mixes several highlights of the spooky season with Trick symbols, Treat symbols, and Halloween Spins.A question, is Halloween meant to be actually, like proper, scary? You know, shivers down the spine, cold sweat, questioning what is going on, or is it all just fake cobwebs, pumpkins, and sweets? Maybe it's best not to know. Anyway, Halloween Spins certainly isn't a game that's going to keep you awake at night, questioning reality. It has a faint Nightmare Before Christmas look going on and is set in one of those mysterious olde towns, where half the buildings are semi-straight while the others lean at impossible angles without toppling over and crushing each other. On the streets, carved pumpkins line porch steps, lights hang on strings, while ghosts and bats flutter about the place. Visually, Tricks and Treats has a certain level of charm, PG charm, but charm all the same.Tricks And Treats slot - main gameJust as Tricks and Treats is unlikely to shock your socks off, neither will is likely to break any numerical records. However, players not too fussed about scooping the biggest possible treats out there can do so on any device, selecting a stake of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Mathematically low volatile, wins occur when at least three matching symbols land left to right from the leftmost side, feeding into a theoretical return to player value of 95.73%.The gaming part of Tricks and Treats takes place on a 5-reel, 4-columned panel covered in 25 paylines. The pay symbols certainly get into the spirit of the season, including the low-pay J-A royals, which have little witch hats on them. For the highs, we get a candle, a spider on a cupcake, a ghost, and a moody-looking cat wearing a witch hat. Landing a five-of-a-kind winning line awards 0.4 to 1.2 times the stake for the royals, or 2 to 10 times the stake when made up of high pays.Tricks and Treats: Slot FeaturesTricks And Treats slot - random trick symbolIf you've made it this far without getting freaked out, brace for some of the better bits. This is where the Treat and Trick parts come into the game, as goes a triggered bout of Halloween Spins.TreatTreat symbols are special scatters that award instant cash prizes when they hit of 1x, 2x, 3x, 5x, 10x, 15x, 20x, or 25x the total bet. Treat symbols cannot be used to create winning lines, and up to 4 of them may appear after a spin.TrickTrick symbols are also special scatter symbols. These ones turn into wilds when they land, and occasionally they reveal multipliers of up to x3 in value. These multipliers are applied to all wins on the current spin - both line wins and Treat prizes. If more than one Trick multiplier lands in view, the values are added up before they are applied to any wins. Like Treats, up to 4 Trick symbols may land after a spin.Halloween SpinsGetting 3, 4, or 5 Halloween Spins scatters on the board at once triggers 10, 12, or 15 free Halloween Spins, respectively. When Halloween Spins are active, Halloween Spins scatters do not appear on the reels, so the feature cannot be triggered. However, when Trick symbols hit during free spins and reveal multipliers, the values are accumulated until the bonus round ends. The maximum possible multiplier in Halloween Spins is capped at x15. When free spins end, the multiplier is reset.Tricks And Treats slot - free spinsTricks and Treats: Slot VerdictSo, would you be dishing out candies if Tricks and Treats came-a knocking, or slam the door in its face and risk having your front garden covered in toilet paper? For our money, Tricks and Treats wasn't an amazing experience, so we might go for the latter option and save the candy for something a bit more special. On the plus side, the atmosphere is Halloween-y; Red Tiger has stacked the screen with all manner of 'spooky' spectres, cheeky pumpkins, and a multitude of other miscellaneous seasonal images to build a playful scene.The gameplay kind of suits too, but it feels geared toward a certain audience who isn't too demanding in terms of massive potential and freaky features. Okay, the two Trick and Treat symbol features are a little freaky at times, though they are limited in what they can ultimately do. There is a chance they open up a bit in free spins since the multiplier is progressive, to a point, yet even at full whack, with everything it's got chucked into a bubbling cauldron, the most Tricks and Treats can muster is 1,696.8x the bet. It's a figure that matches what Tricks and Treats seems to be setting out to achieve, which isn't dominance of the Halloween-themed sector of the market, but more of a sort of humorous version of 'horror', like the Scary Movie franchise – 'Wazzup'.So there you have, Tricks and Treats ended up being a quirky game which elicited a few amusing moments but didn't rise up much further than that. If lightly enjoyable Halloween-ing is what you're pining for, you might well find it in Tricks and Treats. There's fun to be had for the right punter in the right circumstances, just don't expect to metaphorically ransack the town's entire supply of candy while doing so.

Title: Multifly!
review: Multifly! (Yggdrasil Gaming): OverviewAside from herpetologists or those with singular tastes, lizards are usually pretty low on favourite animal lists. They lack the cuteness factor that pandas, or dolphins, or puppies have. Lizards, however, are the star of the show in Yggdrasil's latest slot Multifly! and a few spins is all it takes to boost their appeal. It helps that they are chameleons with that cool colour-change ability that they have. Their main attraction though is that they can pile on multipliers which have a major effect on the outcome of a game. With a name like Multifly!, you would expect there to be plenty of that sort of action going on. Yggdrasil has created a slot with features that build on, and play off, each other. Time to jungle up and see how it works.You don't come across too many games stacked with lizards and Yggdrasil has pulled it off in their typically stylish way. The icning on top is that Multifly! offers some hefty rewards to go with such a cute looking game.When it comes to the rules, Multifly! uses a conventional 5 reel, 3 row setup with 243 ways to win. As long as 3 or more matching symbols land consecutively from the first reel, you have a winner, no matter the row. The math model can be fickle, one minute it's humming along happily feeding on coins, the next it is doing its best snowball impression. These dips and dives come coutesy of an RTP of 96.3% combined with high volatility and a rather low hit rate of 17%.The symbols are a colourful bunch and are split in to high and low pay groups. The low pays are 9-A royals, while the high pays all creatures such as a lizard, a frog, a toucan, and a parrot. An eclectic mix to be sure, with the parrot worth the most at 4 times the stake for five of a kind. That might not sound like a lot, but Multifly is a game that can pile on the wins. Part of the reason is that when winning combos land, they trigger a reel multiplier which we will take a look at below.Multifly! (Yggdrasil Gaming): FeaturesFree spins round in action with multiplier reel lit up above the reels.As well as those win multipliers there are a bunch of other features. The most common is the Dropdown feature. This is essentially just a typical cascading win system where winning symbols are removed from the reels to let new symbols fall into place. This mechanic provides additional chances to win, and it also adds a wild symbol to the reels whenever it occurs. The Dropdown feature will continue to run until no more winners land.On top of that, whenever a wild enters the game it triggers the Reel Multiplier feature. This occurs whether the wild lands randomly on a spin, or is added via the Dropdown feature. Each reel has its own multiplier which starts at x1. When a wild appears, the reel it is on has its multiplier increased by +1. Thanks to the Dropdown feature, multipliers can build up over several reels which are applied one by one to any winning combination. Only reels that have winning symbols on them will apply their multipliers. During the base game, multipliers are reset back to x1 with each fresh new spin.The final feature is a round of Free Spins - when 3 scatters land simultaneously on reels 2, 3 and 4 they award 10 free spins. The rules are the same as in the base game except that the Reel Multiplier feature is not reset during free spins. This means that Dropdowns, wilds, and multipliers, can add up nicely by the time the round is over.Multifly! (Yggdrasil Gaming): VerdictMultifly! is one of those slots that can go from zero to hundred, and back again in an eye blink. Its high volatility and low hit rate are partly responsible, but that effect is largely due to the way its multipliers can shake up a game. For example, even if your free spins round starts off poorly, a streak of cascades can turn the tables on the very last spin. This roller coaster of frustration can go in a different direction as the build up of huge multipliers across all five reels do not guarantee big wins - you will still depend on landing five of a kind winners.Multifly’s main drawback is that the gameplay can get a bit repetitive at times. This is partly because the bonus game is basically the main game, albeit with multipliers that don't reset. Because of that, a session can get a little pedestrian after a while. Moreover, for those who enjoy fast-paced slots, Multifly! can be perceived as rather slow as it insists on playing through its animations on every single win which you cannot skip.On the whole, Multifly is an entertaining game with the type of clever features and potential to overcome any aversion to lizards or jungle creepy crawlies. It's one of those slots with meandering patches of not much going on, interspersed by intense bursts when it's suddenly all go. A real volatile experience – with potential of up to 10,000 times the stake available.

Title: Sidekick Jack
review: Sidekick Jack: Slot OverviewWhen you think about it, the sidekick concept is pretty popular, but how popular is it amongst sidekicks themselves? Forever just out of the main frame, getting some but never the bulk of the love, glory and adulation heaped on the main character. Then again, other people are more than happy not being in the spotlight, not having the full burden of responsibility resting on their shoulders. If the hero massively messes up, bye-bye, they're done, but it's arguably easier for the sidekick to slink away and hook up with another hero to play second fiddle. Heroes, villains, and sidekicks are what this here slot Sidekick Jack is all about. Another eye-catcher was poor old Jack, whose face looks like it had a close encounter with a cheese grater - courtesy of the game's resident wolf creature. Amazingly, Jack seems totally unfazed by his "rugged" look, like he's auditioning for the role of a pirate in a low-budget movie. In any case, Sidekick Jack is set in London: in one of the city's many parks in the base game, then its mean streets in the free spins round. The theme is a little bit confusing, not necessarily in a bad way, and the background artwork, with its 60s comic book style, adds a nice touch. While it may not come across as a cutting-edge production, it gets the job done.Sidekick Jack slot - base gameJack does his sidekicking on a 6x4 game grid. Given all the blood and slashing on show, Sidekick Jack's low-medium volatility was a slight surprise, though few will be let down by the 96.10% RTP or the wide 25 c to $/€250 bet range - increasing to 35 c to $/€350 when the Sidekick bet is switched on.Embedded in the gaming matrix is 50 paylines. They are used to award wins left to right from the leftmost reel, and there are 10 regular pays in the game. The list includes 10-A card rank lows, then a policeman's hat, bullets, a slashed warning sign, a bus, and a lady character with big bulging eyes. The wolfie chap is wild, substituting for all regular pay symbols. Wilds land on reels 2 to 6.Sidekick Jack: Slot FeaturesSidekick Jack slot - free spinsSidekick Jack's features are the Sidekick Bet optional extra, free spins with sticky wilds, and a bonus buy called the Superbet.ScattersThere are 2 different types of scatters available in the game - the moon scatter and the Sidekick Jack scatter. Both appear on the leftmost reel, plus reels 2 and 3. However, Sidekick Jack scatters are only activated when players turn on the Sidekick bet. More on these below.Free SpinsLanding 3 moon scatters awards 10 free spins. During free spins, any 3 moon scatters awards an additional +5 free spins - once only, for a maximum of 15 free spins. During free spins, wilds landing on reels 2-6 are sticky and are held in place till the feature ends.Sidekick BetActivating the Sidekick bet increases the bet by 1.4x. This activates Jack scatters. Activated Jack scatters can trigger a 10 free spins bonus round when 3 Jack symbols land. Hitting 3 moon scatters during this feature awards +5 free spins once. In addition, any 3 Jack scatters during the bonus round retriggers +5 free spins once, for a maximum of 20 free spins.SuperbetThe Superbet is where players can buy the free spins bonus round for the cost of 66 times the bet. It is possible to retrigger free spins by landing 3 moons for +5 spins and +5 spins for landing 3 Jacks - one time each.Sidekick Jack slot - free spinsSidekick Jack: Slot VerdictNot trying to be a villain, but Sidekick Jack did give off sidekick rather than main event vibes. On a positive note, it is unusual; that's one way for a debut to stand out. The theme is somewhat out there, somewhat confusing, a sort of Dr Jekyll/Mr Hyde meets An American Werewolf in London B-movie bonanza. Jack's unusual, too. The game docs mention the wolf bowing to his sidekick, Jack, yet it looks like the wolf has tried to tear him to pieces. Or did the big-eyed lady on the highest-paying symbol do that using her fingernails? So many questions.One question is whether to engage the Sidekick bet. There's no major reason why not; it provides an obvious on-screen difference when using what is effectively an ante bet feature while adding personality and all. More importantly, it increases your chance of barrelling into the free spins round; plus, the activated Sidekick scatter makes it possible to squeeze out an extra 5 free spins, bumping the maximum possible total from 15 to 20. Odd that Wicked Games capped the number of max free spins in this way, but hey, such was their choice. As for max win, the game docs mentions 10,400 credits per spin, which is a little vague, as well.On the gameplay side, apart from the Sidekick ante bet effect, Sidekick Jack isn't exactly a flowering garden bustling with new ideas. The main event, well and truly, is the sticky wild free spins bonus round, and you know, this is a proven mechanic. It performs well enough in Sidekick Jack, though a lack of multiplier prevents things from going nuclear. Have to say, there were high expectations going into Sidekick Jack, given some of the studio's background, which weren't exactly met, but hey, it's a debut, so onwards and upwards and all that.

Title: Lost Vegas

Like its Survivor counterpart, there is no set number of Zombie Free Spins. Instead, the feature continues to play until all five reels are infected, with a set upper limit of 50 free spins. Should players make it all the way to survive 50 free spins, they receive an extra cash prize on top of any winnings.Lost Vegas: VerdictTechnically, Lost Vegas might sound like fairly standard stuff, but the excellent aesthetics give the game some oozing x-factor, pushing it onto uncommon ground. It’s not every day you get to run from a Zombie Elvis lookalike along the Vegas Strip, and Microgaming has pulled it off in a slickly comedic style. Giving players the chance to play the game from the zombie and survivor angle is another clever twist, in a game full of them.The features have their moments. Title: Shields of the Wild
review: Shields of the Wild introductionNextGen is the Kinder Egg of iGaming; you never know what you're going to get. It could be a surprisingly good game (rarely), or downright awful. This means that after 2 spins you will have 2 full stacks of the same symbols on reels 4 and 5. Now, if a scatter symbol lands on the reels, the stack does not move and an upgrade of the stacked symbols takes place. The symbol update progression can be seen below the reels. The Marching Stacks free spins game ends when stacked symbols fill all 5 reels.At the completion of the free spins, a retrigger may be awarded and the whole process starts over again but starting with your already upgraded symbol. Title: Sweet Kingdom

Title: Nice Catch 2 DoubleMax

Title: Mental
review: Mental: Slot OverviewAfter the run Nolimit City's been on, a game titled 'Mental' is going to have players either running in fear or dashing to their laptop to pick up the gauntlet. For players in the latter group, Mental presents a hefty challenge. The studio has experience designing slots that have a relatively complicated set of rules and features. Mental takes this to the extreme in many ways by jamming in dynamic reel action, splitting symbols, transformations, symbol multipliers - the whole shebang. We'll try to break it down, but it will be difficult to rely much of what happens in Mental on paper. Something else hard to convey is how downright creepy Mental is. But hey, we're as keen on a challenge as we are for a big brutal slot so let's plough in and see where we end up.Let's just say, the first place we end up isn't the most pleasant spot to spend a Friday night. The first impressions are a collage of old-fashioned asylums, Victorian-era anatomical sketches, therapy verging on torture, and Hannibal Lecter. If you're waiting for the punchline, there isn't one. Mental takes the topic of psychiatric care very seriously. From the flickering lights to the sepia tones to the slithering soundtrack, Mental has been put together to spook as much as entertain. It might not scar you forever like certain slasher flicks do, but it gets as close to doing so as a slot ever has.Mental is played on a 5-reel game grid, a little like Tombstone's though arranged in a 3-2-3-2-3 layout, providing 108 ways to win, though the reels can expand up to a maximum of 20 rows. Wins form when three or more matching symbols land on adjacent reels from the left-hand side of the grid. Default RTP comes in at 96.08%, rising when buying the various features to a maximum of 96.47%. Volatility, well, we probably don't have to say this, has been rated 'Extreme' by the studio, so prepare yourself mentally for that reality. Playable on any device, Mental offers stakes of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin.The atmosphere gets denser when going over the symbols, starting with five body parts as the lower value tiles – skeletal hands, kidneys, hearts, brains, and eyes. If that wasn't enough, five patients are used for the high pays, anonymously referred to as Patient 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Landing five matching patient symbols is worth a payout of 1.5 to 5 times the stake. Deep breath, time for the features.Mental: Slot FeaturesMental - free spinsListing the features will give us a logical way of working through them, so in Mental, you'll come across extras as Fire Frames, Dead Patients, Enhancer Cells, Mental Transformations, Autopsy Free Spins, Lobotomy Free Spins, Mental Free Spins, !!! This is Mental !!!, and 4 feature buy options.In the main game, on every spin, 1 to 13 positions are randomly surrounded by flames. These are called Fire Frames, and any symbol landing within one splits into 2 parts.The ominously titled Dead Patient feature triggers when 2 Dead Patient symbols hit. It reveals 1 of the premium patient symbols with a random multiplier of x5, x10, x15, x30, x50, x100, x300, x500, x1,000, or x9,999 attached. The multiplier value equates to the number of that symbol on the reel rather than a win multiplier.At the bottom of reels 2 and 4 are the Enhancer Cells. Reel 2 and reel 4 are activated with 4 or 6 Fire Frames, respectively. When active, Enhancer Cells reveal one of these effects:A wild symbol.1 of the 5 patient symbols.A regular Dead Patient symbol.xWays – reveals three identical symbols, but not Scorpion, Spider, or Dead Patient symbols.xSplit – splits one symbol on each reel into two, then splits itself into 2 wilds.xNudge Wild - nudges so it is fully visible on the reel. Each nudged step increases a win multiplier by 1. More than one wild multiplier adds the values.Landing spider symbols on reel 2 or 4 triggers the Mental Transform feature. Spiders transform into either xWays, xSplit, Dead Patient, Wild, or Patient symbol.Autopsy Free Spins Next up is free spins. The first one, 8 Autopsy Free Spins, is awarded when 3 Scorpion symbols land on reels 1, 3, and 5. Each Scorpion symbol landing in a Fire Frame awards +1 spin. In this bonus game, up to 5 positions are randomly given a Fire Frame. Once landed, Fire Frames stick throughout the feature. It is possible to upgrade Autopsy Spins to Lobotomy Spins by landing a Spider Symbol.Lobotomy Free Spins Landing 3 Scorpion Symbol + 1 Spider Symbol in the base game awards 9 Lobotomy Spins. In addition to Autopsy Spin rules, any Spider Symbols that hit are sticky, triggering Mental Transformations on each spin. There is also a Dead Multiplier rule. The highest Multiplier value from Dead Symbols is collected with a count. When new Patient symbols hit, their collected multiplier is applied to it, then 1 deducted from the count. Landing 2 Spider Symbols upgrades to Mental Freespins.Mental Free Spins The most lucrative bonus is triggered from the main game if 3 Scorpion Symbols and 2 Spider Symbols hit, awarding 10 spins. What changes here is both Spider Symbols are sticky, triggering Mental Transformations on each spin. Also, the Dead Multiplier count does not decrease after its multiplier is transferred to new Patient symbols.If bonus buys are an option where you live, then paying 80, 200, or 1,000 times the stake gets you 8-11 Autopsy Free Spins, 9-13 Lobotomy Freespins, or 10-15 Mental Free spins, respectively. Paying 220x the stake is a lucky dip option with 50% chance of getting Autopsy, 40% for Lobotomy, or 10% of landing Mental Freespins.Finally, !!! This is Mental !!! is the name given to the scenario when players hit the max win figure of 66,666 times the base stake.Mental: Slot VerdictWell, Mental certainly lives up to its name, no arguments. There are scant few games like this floating around. None actually, yet is there a reason for that? Mental is a grim slot, one not designed to make players chuckle unless they have an unusual sense of humour. It means Mental doesn't have the same fun factor as other hits Nolimit has churned out this year. There's none of the joyous East Coast vs West Coast bounce, the rib-tickling of xWays Hoarder xSplit, or the dark humour found in El Paso Gunfight xNudge and San Quentin xWays. This is a serious subject, dealt with in a serious manner. Perhaps when picking this topic, you've got no choice other than to go heavy. When the gaming's done you might need to do something to clear your mental palate, like putting on an episode of Keeping up with the Kardashians after watching a horror movie. It's funny, going back to play slots like Immortal Romance, A Dark Matter, or Mysterious is like watching Barney the Dinosaur sing the four times table.Another possible concern is the complexity of the bonus games. No one's questioning Mental's ability to go wild when the right symbols are hitting, but it does teeter on being a tad too convoluted at times. Demoing is a requirement, and even then, it requires a good playthrough to pick up on all the various nuances. Some players are sure to lap up the complexity, others will flee the asylum to find the nearest fruit machine.When tackling Mental's paytable, it's not hard to picture a group of bearded Victorian gentlemen with pipes dissecting the rules, trying to figure out what's going on before giving up and inventing natural selection instead, because it's more obvious. Jokes aside, Mental's not so bad when you take the time to go over the rules, yet it's nigh on indecipherable otherwise. There's just so much cutting, slicing, transforming, locking, and whatnot that Mental is initially overwhelming. It's very clever, no doubts there, but Mental skims the limit on complex kitchen sink gaming.To sum up, sure, we've been goofing around a bit, but Mental is about as dark as it gets in a slot. If you're down with the subject matter, the unsettling visuals, and unwieldy rules, there is a one-of-a-kind game here that pushes the envelope as much as anything Nolimit City has released.

A slot that utilises such a well-used theme needs at least one amazing feature to make it stand out from the bunch, and the Pharaoh has missed a trick here.Pharaoh’s Dream (Bally): VerdictPharaoh’s Dream is not the first time Bally has taken players on an Egyptian odyssey. Title: Book of Shadows
review: Book of Shadows: OverviewDeveloper Nolimit City gets all bookish in their occult flavoured slot Book of Shadows. It seems there is an unwritten, gentleman's type agreement that all developers have at least one' Book of' slot in the catalogue. An eerie, almost Arabic, soundtrack wafts away like the fireflies floating across the screen, punctuated by howling wolves, and hooting owls. It feels like a headless horseman could come bounding through the leafless trees at any moment.Book of Shadows - free spinsBook of Shadows is playable on any device from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. In all cases, volatility remains the same – 10/10, or as Nolimit classes it 'Extreme'.Core rules are pretty standard. Land matching symbols left to right from the first reel for a win. As you'd imagine, more rows mean more paylines, so 3, 4, or 5 rows provides 10, 15 or 20 Shadow Rows, as they are called. Ten regular symbols make up the paytable, starting with 10-A royals, followed by an eyeball, a butterfly, a goat's skull, a purple cat, and a female goth. As is standard in most 'Book of' slots, the scatter doubles as a wild symbol here.Book of Shadows: FeaturesFree spins with expandable symbols remain the most desirable moment here, but there are a couple of extra features including Lucky Locks, Gamble 50/50, and the Gamble Wheel of Bonus.Let's tackle the Lucky Locks first. Up to five gambles can take place in a row, as long as the winning amount is less than €500,000.The Wheel of Bonus allows you to gamble for the chance to win free spins – as long as the winnings do not exceed 60x the bet. A wheel with a highlighted segment spins, the size depends on the amount of your win. Land in the segment to pick up 10 free spins at the current row height.What it all comes down to is the free spins game, triggered by landing 3 or more book symbols in view - 3 scatters award 10 free spins at the current row height, but you can increase or decrease the number of rows to receive more or less free spins.Before the round starts, a golden symbol is randomly chosen. If you're not pleased with the one offered you can reshuffle once in hopes of an upgrade. It can work the opposite way though, so beware.During free spins, golden symbols expand to cover full reels after any win lines have been evaluated. Expanded golden symbols pay all win lines from any position; they do not have to be adjacent. The ultimate result is five goth girls on a 5 row grid for a 10,000 times the stake win. Also, landing 3 or more book scatters on a free spin retriggers the feature.The bonus game is triggered every 154 spins theoretically, yet if you can't wait, there is a feature buy option. If available in your jurisdiction, The Nolimit Bonus, as it is called, costs 60x, 90x, or 120x for 10 free spins with 3, 4 or 5 rows respectively.Book of Shadows: VerdictWhen designing their take on the Book thing, most developers tweak one aspect to help justify the game's release. Nolimit City, on the other hand, has bravely taken the popular genre and turned it on its head. Aside from expanding symbols (which admittedly are the core feature), almost everything else has been altered. The result is a ‘Book of’ slot which is genuinely new. Such a bold approach won't be to everybody's liking. Some may find it fiddly, bloated, and possibly annoying. It's certainly not your typical Ra-style imitator.Instead, it's a real gamblers tool. Locking reels, for example, are fun when they go your way. Say, locking two books and landing the third one to trigger free spins. However Lucky Locks are not cheap. For example, locking a book on the first and third reel boosts spin costs to over 40x the stake. Many will contend it's better to just fork out for the feature.The same dilemma rears up when confronted by the Gamble features. Picking the right card, or winning free spins is brilliant when it works out, a flaming pumpkin in the head when it all goes wrong. The same can be said for Shadow Reels. It's hard to stick to three rows when you know five is available - especially when you see hordes of scatters land on inactive rows. Some may argue it would have been better if Nolimit had just used the 5x5 setup, and be done. Still, the whole game revolves around player's choice.It is possible for Book of Shadows to grow on you, the deeper you delve. There is a lot to take in, and plenty of options to experiment with. You might hit on a combination you love, or, all this fannying about might just get in the way. It's a game that could annoy the heck out of Ra purists, while others may love the multiple opportunities to try their luck, not to mention the unusual theme.Book of Shadows has been cleverly designed, and there are plenty of options for players who like to dig in, have a punt, or play around with settings. Once again Nolimit has demonstrated their creative bent by crafting something unique with one of the most well-worn slot formats around.

Title: Moon Princess
review:

This spin allows Love, Star, and Storm’s to trigger their powers one at a time to create more chances at winning.The main goal of Moon Princess is clearing the whole grid to trigger the main Free Spins feature. When this happens, players choose either Love who awards 4 free spins, Star brings 5, while Storm awards 8 free spins. All this talk of princesses, love, and moons might be off-putting for some, but hopefully not, because Moon Princess is a top-notch slot that has been superbly designed.These types of games are all about getting on a roll, and Moon Princess can certainly roll with the best of them. Combos lead to filled meters, to modifiers, to free spins, and beyond. Chains of winners can pop along seemingly without end, when they are going well. It is highly volatile keep in mind, so not every spin is going to be an epic ride to glory.When it goes, it can certainly go nuts, although the stated max win potential of 5,000x seems like a bit of exaggeration. More realistic is a max win half of that number. In any case, couple that figure with the high-performance math model and you’ve got a game that overcomes any aversion you might have for the theme. Often when Moon Princess gets going, you have no idea what is happening – even if you’ve fully read the rules. But it doesn’t matter at all. Moon Princess is a riot of activity where it’s best to just sit back and enjoy the anime madness.Don't MissIf Moon Princess ticks all the right boxes for you, you'll probably want to check out the Christmas version titled Moon Princess Christmas Kingdom or, alternatively, the Egyptian themed Sisters of the Sun version - both offering wins of up to 15,000 times your stake.

Title: Rainbow Riches Cluster Magic

Free spins can be retriggered, and the difference between them and regular spins is the Multiplier Trail upgrade.Lara Croft Tomb of the Sun slot - free spinsLara Croft Tomb of the Sun: Slot VerdictTo nutshell Lara Croft Tomb of the Sun, it seems closer to a do-over than a full reboot when compared to the slot which preceded it. On paper, much of the gameplay is the same - Rolling Reels, Multiplier Trail, free spins, and Jackpots triggered by landing wild symbols. It's not bang on the same, though. Title: 5 Families
review: 5 Families: Overview’As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster', so said tough guy Henry Hill in the film Goodfellas. In Red Tiger's mafia themed slot 5 Families, players get a chance to live out some of those mob fantasies. Despite all the violent crime, The Mafia is one of those topics that has a perennial hold on our imagination repeatedly showing up in books, tv shows, and films. Red Tiger has captured some of the spirit, yet 5 Families turns out to be a sparse experience, lacking much in the way of depth, excitement, or potential.The game starts quite well, thanks to the smoky, opulent setting, all plush chairs and candlelight. This is a place for those who have worked their way up the crime ladder to relax and play a few hands of high stakes card games. The laid back music is cosy at first, nicely complementing the lux environment. After a while, the soundtrack does drag on the eyelids though. It turns into an assault on your concentration and motivation levels, not helped by the low key gameplay. Still, from a visual standpoint, Red Tiger slots are typically lookers and 5 Families is no exception to the rule.Playable from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin, the action takes place on a classic 5-reel, 10-payline grid. Not uncommon from Red Tiger nowadays, RTP is down slightly on 95.69%, which doesn't help the cause, while volatility sits in the medium range. Hardcore gamblers will find little to get excited about over the math model. Indeed, there is little about the whole game to get too enthused over.Like the rest of the game, the symbols are well-drawn, capturing the dapper side of the Mafia theme. There are nine symbols used in 5 Families, period. All are pay symbols, there are no wilds or scatters around here.The four low pays are mob paraphernalia such as pistols and papers, bullets and liquor, casino chips, and a suitcase full of dollar bills. In the base game, five of the low pays on a line are worth 1 to 2.5 times the stake. On to the high pays which are a who's who of real and fictional mob characters. There are five of them in total, including a Junior Soprano and an Al Capone lookalike. This lot of toughs are worth from 6 to 20 times the total bet for a line of five.5 Families: Features5 Families - free spinsThe name of the game around here is simplicity, meaning the base game is uncluttered by many features. In fact, there is just one extra to be aware of - the VIP Room feature.Whenever a winner lands, a bullet is added to a revolver's chamber sitting above the reels. When a non-winning spin hits, the bullets are removed. However, if you get 5 consecutive wins and fill the chamber with bullets, then the VIP Room feature is activated.When spinning in the VIP room, all winning combinations have their values multiplied by 5. This means the premium symbols are now worth 30 to 100x for a line of five. The feature does not come with a set number of spins. Instead, if 5 non-winning spins occur, players are ejected from the VIP Room back to the main game.5 Families: Verdict5 Families comes off as one of those filler slots that rolls easily from the Red Tiger production line in between their more superior gambling machines. During testing, there were times when 5 Families felt a little half-finished. What it does do is alright, there just isn't enough of it to hold much long term interest.5 Families looks good, there no doubts in that regard. Red Tiger can't help but make an attractive game, but it's all a bit thin. No wilds or scatters, plus a so-so bonus game makes 5 Families feel incomplete. It’s as if Tony Soprano was the project manager who didn't like the way the game was heading so he whacked the team and sent the game out half baked.Other than players who simply cannot get enough of Mob movies, it's hard to think who else to recommend 5 Families to. Okay, the aim is straight forward gaming, but the snail's pace can be a real killer, not to mention tediously repetitive. After a while, even the music doesn't help.The track would go down well in a speakeasy while taking your time over an expensive whisky or savouring the smoke from a hundred dollar chubby. But because there is little other excitement, the plinking piano piece is in constant danger of sending players off to sleep. Don't count on the potential to stay motivated either. The game maxes out at 1,000 times the stake per spin during the bonus, which isn't terrible, but probably won't get too many hearts racing as it's more of a 'win collector' game rather than one which hits fast and hard.Initially, fans of Red Tiger will be drawn in by the good looks and interesting theme. Unfortunately, there is little beyond that to hold any long term attention. If 5 Families worked for the Mob, it'd be an associate who hasn't been made yet. A grunt who smashes open parking meters for small change to help make up their captain's quota.

Title: Divine Riches Helios
review: Divine Riches Helios: Slot OverviewMicrogaming associates Just For The Win appear to have a definite interest in all things 'riches'. So far, there's been Neptune's Riches, the studio's first grid slot Odin's Riches, and now they take to the sky with Divine Riches Helios. Helios, of course, is the Ancient Greek God of the Sun. In Divine Riches Helios, he's been depicted as a real beefcake, all bulging arms and popping pecs, while starring alongside features such as jackpots and free spins with premium symbol upgrades.Helios might be the God of the Sun, but the slot made in his honour is not quite so dazzlingly bright. In addition, a helping of charm is provided by the uber-ripped Greek God, yet apart from that, Divine Riches Helios is a little plain looking. Last but not least, wild symbols are used in Helios to replace anything except the free spins symbols.Divine Riches Helios: Slot FeaturesJust For The Win has kept a lid on innovation in Divine Riches Helios, choosing instead to go with features titled the Blazing Bonus and Free Spins with the Hand of Helios.Blazing BonusEvery time special bonus tokens land in the game, there is a chance of triggering the Blazing Bonus feature. In free spins, when a Helios symbol lands, it is collected. Every time 12 Helios symbols have been collected; the Hand of Helios feature is activated. When triggered, the Hand of Helios feature upgrades a high pay symbol to the next more value one on the paytable. In addition, whenever the Hand of Helios activates, +2 extra free spins are awarded. If all upgradeable symbols have been upgraded to Helios symbols, no more Helios symbols are collected.Divine Riches Helios: Slot VerdictUnless you're absolutely gagging to take to the reels with one of the buffest dudes in iGaming, you aren't losing much by giving Divine Riches Helios a miss. Just For The Win is good at coating their slots with a glossy outer layer, which Divine Riches Helios sort of has, but dig beneath that, and the gaming is a bit shallow. A fairly pleasant, plain-looking game (though the cartoon hero has a certain charisma), Divine Riches Helios comes stacked with several rather plain features on board to match.Perhaps plain isn't the right word, but there's little in Divine Riches Helios that hasn't been used to as good if not greater effect elsewhere. From the jackpot picks to the Pink Elephants style symbol upgrading free spins. To be fair, going through the full upgrade process and having Helios as the only high paying symbol on the board could be interesting, though we never made it quite so far during the review to verify. The pay both ways symbol gives Divine Riches Helios a smidge of individualism, though it wasn't enough to draw attention away from the shortcomings. These largely being gameplay which failed to stimulate much imagination and feelings of insecurity after constantly self-comparing to such a muscle-bound alpha with an epic jawline. To experience the same theme with more unique gaming, Relax's beast Helios' Fury might be the go. Or, if you're feeling sentimental, old classics such as Kronos or Zeus III might fit the bill as Divine Riches appears to have been modelled after these old iconic WMS titles.Ironically, given the visuals, Divine Riches Helios doesn't possess as much of the blue sky thinking that went into Neptune's Riches or Odin's Riches. This could be for better or for worse, however, as some players might prefer the straightforward thrills offered by a simple pick 'n click jackpot bonus. The top prize of 5,000x is decent enough, but it was hard to shake the feeling Divine Riches Helios is destined to take up space on a shelf as much as anything else.

Title: Das xBoot
review: Das xBoot: Slot OverviewDas Boot is a movie released in 1981, which received a glowing critical response and is viewed by many as one of the greatest and most expensive films Germany has ever produced. It was based on a book of the same name published in 1973 by Lothar-Günther Buchheim, describing his experiences aboard German sub U-96, in the hazardous waters of the Atlantic Ocean during World War 2. U-boats sinking Allied ships during WW2 might not be the first topic that springs to mind when developers brainstorm new ideas. If there is one thing Nolimit City has taught us, it's they are no regular studio, taking Das Boot, and transforming it into Das xBoot, a complex slot jam-packed with an arsenal of extras.Das xBoot is a real amalgamation of features and mechanics from previous Nolimit slots all rolled into one. The graphics and effects are full-on Das Boot, the action located in a murky grey sea next to the sub's starboard side. Paradoxically, since Das xBoot is based on the Kriegsmarine, it feels a little tame, coming so soon after Mental. However, it packs in plenty of atmosphere, with come book style looks offset by a brilliant Jaws meets Klaus Doldinger meets Blade Runner 2049 soundtrack, which adds a layer of lurking menace to induce an enjoyable tense feel.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, the base game is played on a 6-reel panel arranged in a 2-3-4-4-3-2 formation, which chops and changes depending on the game phase or if certain symbols are present. In its most basic form, there are 576 ways to win, though this can balloon to 75,712 under the right conditions. It kind of goes without saying that Das xBoot is a highly volatile slot, rated 10 out of 10 by its maker. RTP is variable, so be on the lookout for the 96.03% version as it is the most generous one. Wins occur at a frequency of 22.07%, while free spins trigger every 211 spins on average - there are two bonus round levels, depending on how many scatter symbols hit to activate them.Diving down further to the symbols, we come across ten of them as the regular pays, plus various special symbols. On the low pay side are 10-A card ranks, then five crew members as the premiums – chefs, radio guys, engineers, periscope operators, and captains. The most valuable is the Kapitanleutnant, worth 20 times the stake for a six of a kind winning combination.Das xBoot: Slot Features﻿Going to sea for any length of time requires plenty of stores to tie you over, and Das xBoot comes with loads of extras such as xNudge Wilds, xWays, xBomb Wild Multipliers, Silent Hunter Spins, and Wolf Pack Spins.Starting with the wilds, the xNudge Wild is a 4-row high wild symbol that always nudges to be fully visible. Each nudge increases its wild multiplier by +1. xNudge Wilds land on reel 3 or 4 only, except in Silent Hunter Free Spins, where it only lands on reel 4. All multipliers add to each other, and wins are evaluated using the total multiplier.The xWays symbol lands only on reels 2 or 5 to reveal 2-3 instances of a regular random symbol. If more than one xWays symbol lands on the reels, they all reveal the same pay symbol.When an xBomb Wild lands, the global win multiplier increases by +1, then it explodes, removing all non-winning symbols from the reels. Exploded xBombs convert to wild symbols after exploding. The remaining symbols after the explosion drop to the bottom of the grid, and new ones tumble in. If free spins trigger on the same spin, the win multiplier is carried over to them.Keep an eye out for the sonar display, it's the scatter symbol, appearing on reels 2-5. Landing 3 of them triggers 8 Silent Hunter Free Spins, or 4 of them in view activates 8 Wolf Pack Free Spins.For Silent Hunter Free Spins, reel 3 grows to 8 positions high (like a periscope), and a new Periscope Wild may land on it. If matching symbols land on reels 1 and 2, with a Periscope Wild on reel 3, a torpedo launch sequence occurs, and the win multiplier increases by +1. This is a short boat attack animation, and if the boat is sunk, the Periscope Wild covers reel 3. Also, for each position, the stack of Periscope Wilds nudge down to cover the reel, the multiplier for that reel increases by 1. This value is added to any global win multiplier. If the attack misses, the Periscope Wild remains a single wild. Finally, any scatter in view adds +2 additional free spins.For Wolf Pack Free Spins, a torpedo tube appears beneath reels 2-5. When new torpedo wild symbols hit on these reels, they drop an xWays symbol onto the torpedo area. These xWays symbols start on x2, increasing by +1 for each following torpedo wilds that hit from then on, up to a maximum of x9. When all 4 positions of the torpedo are filled, it launches out of the way to reveal xWays symbols. On reels 2 or 5, these revealed xWays transform into the respective number of regular symbols; on reels 3 or 4 they become the applicable number of wild symbols. A torpedo launch also increases the win multiplier by +1. Like before, scatter symbols award an extra +2 free spins.The last feature is the Nolimit Bonus feature buy option where players can buy either bonus game. Silent Hunter Free Spins cost 75x the bet possessing an RTP of 96.57%, while Wolf Pack Spins cost 350x the bet while having an RTP value of 96.58%.Das xBoot: Slot VerdictDas xBoot has a higher than usual complexity, though it's nowhere near as confusing as the previous game Mental was. It will probably take a few bonus rounds to completely clock what is going on, yet there is no residual confusion left once everything falls into place. It's funny, after Mental, Das xBoot feels rather light by comparison, which is an odd thing to say about a slot based on one of the most dangerous battlegrounds of World War 2. Comic book graphics soften the theme to an extent, but sinking enemy ships and the menacing soundtrack do a great job of building tension.The features are a who's who line up of Nolimit City classics. Limiting special symbols to certain reels was a good idea, adding variety while also amplifying each other's effects should they trigger in unison. Silent Hunter Free Spins would usually produce 1 or 2 Periscope Wilds per round, giving you the chance of filling reel 3 with wilds. Get an xWays symbol or xNudge in there at the same time, and results can be exciting. Das xBoot is a volatile slot, though, so brace for plenty of 'Scheisse' moments, too (the game's word here).As we've seen in previous Nolimit City games, all it takes is one stunning spin to change everything, and Wolf Pack Free Spins are where this is most likely to happen. Here is where you want to build as high a collection of xWays symbols on the torpedo as possible. Then, if you manage to launch the torpedo, the following spin can be absolutely crazy with all those potential wilds, multipliers and additional ways in play. Prepare for some major teasing, however. One time during testing, the very last Wolf Pack spin launched the torpedo, jacking ways, alongside wild stacks, xWays, the whole works… with absolutely nothing connecting on the first reel. That produced a humorous yet frustrating 'Nein, nein, nein' animation as the game tried to commiserate with the close but no cigar outcome.Das xBoot's gameplay is so all or nothing it's like a metaphor for a fruitless or successful submarine hunt. On a darker note, some estimates put the chances of U-boat sailors surviving the war at 20%. By comparison, the odds of hitting Das xBoot's max win are even slimmer. However, do so, and a colossal haul worth 55,200x the bet is coming your way, triggering the Das Gold Des Roter Teufel feature as the round shuts down.Having memories, or nightmares, of Mental fresh in your mind may diminish Das xBoot's impact, but this doesn't stop it from being another big, volatile juggernaut from Nolimit City. Once again, the team has picked a theme most others would shy away from and stacked it with the sort of gameplay that has no qualms torpedoing starry-eyed players out of the water as much as reward them.

Title: Outlaw
review: Outlaw: Slot OverviewThey say two's company, three's a crowd, but when it comes to books, movies, or online slots, there's something satisfying about a good trilogy. Regular symbols pay when they land on consecutive reels starting from the left, and at least three are needed to do so, except the highest value symbol which pays out for two of a kind. Hitting a six-of-a-kind winning way awards 0.3-0.4x the bet for the royals or 0.5 to 10x the stake for the four premiums.Outlaw: Slot FeaturesFor features, it's a case of old and new components merged and twisted to form something different. Landing 3 or more scatters awards free spins, and if one of the triggering scatters is a Gold Megascatter, Enhanced Free Spins are awarded. When either bonus round type is triggered, players can choose Fallen Angel Free Spins or Dizzy in the Head Free Spins (or the enhanced versions). When heading into the bonus rounds, not only do the visuals change, but The Cult launches into their song 'Outlaw' while it is in play.Fallen Angel Free SpinsOutlaw slot - Fallen Angel free spinsThis one comes with 7 free spins. For Enhanced Fallen Anger Free Spins, the rules are the same, plus one of the high pay symbols is also chosen to be the second Sticky Wild on reels 2-5. Scatters do not appear in either version of this bonus round.Dizzy in the Head Free SpinsOutlaw slot - Dizzy in the Head free spinsA total of 8 free spins are awarded for this feature. During it, a full reel Ladder Wild appears on each free spin, highlighting a multiplier up to x77. Any wins passing through the Ladder Wild have the multiplier applied to it. Silver Scatters remain on the reels for this feature, and landing 3, 4, or 5 of them awards 4, 6, or 8 extra free spins. In Enhanced Dizzy in the Head Free Spins, whenever the Wild Ladder substitutes in a win, the multipliers on the ladder are increased for the rest of the feature, up to x777.Win ExchangeWhen winning 100 times the stake or more, players can pay an amount worth 100x the bet to buy free spins. Or, if the winning total is 25-100x the bet, you can elect to stake the win for the chance to win free spins or Enhanced Free Spins on two segmented prize wheels.Bonus BuyAlternatively, players with access to the bonus buy can buy the regular bonus round for 70x the bet or the enhanced version for 300x the bet.Outlaw slot - bonus buy optionsOutlaw: Slot VerdictFor the final instalment in The Cult trilogy, Big Time Gaming has resisted the urge to freak fans out with something wildly innovative, choosing instead to largely stick to what made the previous games so great. Or punishing, depending on your viewpoint and past experiences. Make no mistake; Outlaw is potentially a rough ride like either game which preceded it – or lucrative, depending on how luck is fairing on the day. The base game coasts along, bolstered by a lot more ways to win than previous games and the two full reel wilds. Although, the Outlaw Wild is a bit of a let down when you realize it counts for a single symbol rather than the number of symbols that would have landed on its reel. So does The Sheriff, but it's got the x7 on board.Once free spins or Enhanced Free Spins hit, it is freaking game on, though, and there are several ways of possibly getting your butt there. Unlike previous incarnations, applicable players have no need to sit patiently (or impatiently) through the base game for the requisite number of scatters to hit. Indeed, one of the first semi-organic triggers came from a circa 31x the bet base game win, leading to a successful Win Exchange spin, then onto Enhanced Free Spins. It can happen. Lil Devil has the honour of being first, Wild Flower is famous for its volatility, and Outlaw kinda mixes and matches elements of both while injecting a few things all of its own. Title: Wicked Kitty

As it turns out, "Grimoire" is really only a fancy name for a witch's diary and is a book of magic with instructions on how to formulate magical objects, namely amulets and talismans.In the world of online gambling, Golden Grimoire is a 5-reel, 4-row slot with 40 fixed paylines of low to medium volatility. Accepting bets from between 0.20 up to 400 EUR a spin, the game comes shipped with an RTP setting of 96.44%. Initially, Golden Grimoire may come across as slightly confusing, but is actually a rather simple creation with heavy focus on symbol transformation that applies in both the base game and bonus.As you would expect from NetEnt, much effort has been invested in the visual appearance and the result is just as stunning as ever. Set inside a sorcerer's chamber, there are plenty of subtle details and animations to stimulate your cerebral cortex - Secret scripts and occult markings magically appearing as the reels spin, a starry sky revealing the orbit of the Earth and a scatter tease that makes objects diabolically float in the air. It all graciously exposes the incredible talent available to Netent. If only the mathematicians were given such freedom of expression as well.Golden Grimoire (NetEnt): Symbols, Paytable & FeaturesThe standard symbols are 8 in total and appear fully stacked on the reels in both the base game and bonus. Symbols on the reels include hearts, spades, clubs and diamonds as well as beetles, snakes, cephalopod molluscs and spiders holding on to gemstones. The spider is the most rewarding symbol giving you 1 time your stake for 5 across a full payline.Central to the game is the Mystery symbol that comes in the form of a spellbook with a question mark. Just like all other symbols, it appears fully stacked on the reels but may only appear on reels 3, 4 and 5 in the base game. When it lands, a random symbol is selected, transforming all instances of the Mystery symbols into that symbol. Now, if the Mystery symbol matches the leftmost symbol in the same row, all symbols in that row will transform to the same symbol. If the Mystery symbol turns into a wild, however, the same things happens only this time all symbols in that row turn into wild symbols regardless of the symbol on the first reel.The wild is represented by a golden skull and can only appear as a result of symbol transformation.Golden Grimoire (NetEnt): Free SpinsFree spins feature with sticky mystery books8 free spins are on offer if you land 3 scatter symbols on reels 1, 3 and 5 respectively. It's all about the Mystery symbol here, but while the basic functionality is the same, it comes with a couple of additional benefits. The stacked Mystery books are now extended to appear on reel 2 as well. More importantly, any Mystery symbol landing on the reels will stay in place throughout the bonus session.Unfortunately, as the bonus cannot be re-triggered, it's of outmost importance to land as many sticky books as possible early in the bonus in order to get anything out of it at all. Even if you should be lucky enough to land a full-screen top paying symbol, it will payout no more than 200 times your stake. Unless our calculations are way off the chart, don't expect more than 1000x from this bonus, and even that would be extremely unlikely.Golden Grimoire (NetEnt): ConclusionIt's a bit shocking to see NetEnt stick to this kind of low potential nonsense, especially considering the hailstorm of criticism the company has had to endure in recent times for this exact reason. With the NetEnt CEO herself very candidly putting the cards on the table, hinting of self-awareness and giving quite a sober reflection, we really did expect a fresh start with the arrival of a new year.Unless for some reason you're specifically into medium variance slots with little to no potential and willing to waste your time running in circles, we cannot give you any justifiable reasons to play this drivel from a gambling point of view. If all you look for in a slot is to kill some time and keep yourself entertained, you're better off matching your socks. Please NetEnt, give your design team a raise and take good care of them. They may be the only reason you still have a fighting chance.

Title: Neon Villains

However, in practice, the two remain very comparable. It certainly didn't deviate as hard as Florageddon! did. Interestingly, 243 ways to win are a lot more than the 25 paylines of the older game, but this system has a lower hit rate than before. Statistically speaking, the hit rate in Neon Villains DoubleMax is roughly 10% points less than its dino predecessor. Kind of ruins the point of transition to a ways system? Title: Mayhem
review: Mayhem: Slot OverviewFresh off reviewing ELK Studios' post-apocalyptic slot Nitropolis 3 comes Mayhem, another dystopic thought experiment, this time from software provider Red Tiger. From then on, the multiplier grows by +1 after each subsequent respins sequence, up to a maximum value of x10. Lastly, each free spins symbol landing in the feature adds +1 extra free spin to the remaining amount.Mayhem: Slot VerdictPlayers intrigued by future visions of a planetary reset can add another solid slot to the pile.
