Make it all the way up on the jackpot ladder and you'll get to spin the wheel to win either win a bet multiplier or one of the jackpots.Pots O'Riches (Blueprint Gaming): VerdictPots O' Riches is a game with a cultural identity that is more likely to strike a chord with UK players than the rest of the market. Either way, despite being well-executed, it's not the most unique or exciting game you'll ever play as the potential is too low and most of the features have been recycled from other Blueprint slots. If it's the jackpot game you're after, there are far better Blueprint games to play that are also connected to it, such as Slots O' Gold Megaways (which also features a leprechaun).On the positive side, Pots O' Riches is undoubtedly a charming game that offers balanced gameplay of medium volatility and a whole batch of features to chase. Regardless of our opinion, many players will surely enjoy it even though we did not.

Title: Fruit Combinator
review: Fruit Combinator: Slot OverviewTime for some healthy eating folks and a metaphorical chance to consume 1 of your 5 a day thanks to Yggdrasil Gaming partner studio ReelPlay in a video slot titled Fruit Combinator - a fruity-themed slot which uses a multi-faceted mechanic ReelPlay has called a 'reverse cascade'. As well as this 'revolutionary' feature (again, ReelPlay's words), Fruit Combinator comes with other extras like Explosive Reactions, Symbol Morphs, and Win Boosters.Fruit slots aren't exactly famous for creating intricate worlds full of depth, hidden meaning, and elaborately rendered scenes. Fruit Combinator takes this idea to an extreme and is played from a pilot's eye view of the world, as if staring out of a cockpit window, watching the world go by in a swirl of clouds and blue skies. Seriously, Fruit Combinator's background is animated as if the three-fifths full game grid is hurtling through the stratosphere. Four static prize values sit on the left-hand side of the screen, the UI on the right. It's either super clean or super boring; take your pick, and let's move to the numbers.Fruit Combinator slot - base gameSo, numbers, and arguably the most important of them all is up first, where the default theoretical return to player comes out at 96.1%. It's driven by a low volatile math model and hosted on a game grid which has 6 reels, each reel possessing 5 positions. However, base game spins always begin with 3 rows of active symbols and 2 rows of blank spaces. How those empty spaces can be filled is explained below in the features section. Till then, bet selection varies from 20 p/c to $/€40 per spin, without a bonus buy or ante bet in sight.Loads of fruit are in sight as the pay table is full of them. However, the low pays are actually 10-A card royals, while the high pays are where we come across a strawberry, watermelon, orange, plum and a bunch of grapes. Landing 6-of-a-kind winning way awards players 0.5 to 1 times the bet for the low pays and 1.2 to 10 times the bet for the highs. Wilds appear in Fruit Combinator, too, on all but the leftmost reel. Wilds substitute for all symbols except the scatter.Fruit Combinator: Slot FeaturesFruit Combinator slot - free spinsHere's how Fruit Combinator works. Winning combinations are created when matching pay symbols land on 3 or more adjacent reels from the left side of the grid onwards. When this happens, the non-winning symbols are removed (except scatters), and the winning symbols drop to the bottom of the grid. This is known as the Explosion part of the sequence.Next in the sequence are Morphs. If there is more than one symbol type in view sitting at the bottom of the grid, all pay symbols morph into the highest value pay symbol in view. Wilds and scatters are excluded from morphing.Up next is Boosters. If, after Explosions and Morphs, any previous winning symbol is not in a winning position anymore, additional matching symbols are added to make it a winning symbol.Following Boosters is Drops. Here, a new symbol is dropped onto the top of each reel that has less than 5 symbols. Any dropped symbols which do not match or substitute the current paying symbol explodes. Any dropped symbol that does match or substitute but does not land in a winning position also explodes. Scatters are always kept, as are any symbols that match or substitute in paying positions. If the total kept symbol count is higher than the count of the previous Drop, then an extra Drop occurs (or in the base game before any Morphs or Boosters if it is the first Drop). Wins are paid when no more Drops are activated.Free GamesFree games are triggered when at least 3 scatter symbols land and after base game Drops have been completed. The prize value on each scatter symbol is paid, and 3 free games are awarded. Landing a new scatter symbol resets the spin count to 3. At the end of any free game, the prize value on any scatter is paid. Scatter symbols have values of 1-100x the bet or have the Mini, Minor, Major, or Grand bonus worth 10x, 50x, 250x or 2,000x the bet, respectively.Fruit Combinator slot - free spinsFruit Combinator: Slot VerdictFor better or for worse, fruit is one of those things that gamblers are likely to bump into sooner or later at regular intervals when playing online slots. Fruit seems to have been around since practically the dawn of the slot phenomenon and is likely to be there until the curtains close on them if this should ever occur. The good thing is software developers have really widened the net to encompass a huge range of topics as time has progressed so that players have hundreds if not thousands of non-fruit options to choose from.Bringing it back to the topic at hand, fruit lovers are spoiled for choice, yet Fruit Combinator might not be at the top of a huge number of fruit fans' lists. For the most part, it is basically a clone of another ReelPlay's Professor Clank's Combinator. Perhaps the earlier game struck a chord with enough players to justify a reskin. With the popularity of fruit, you'd imagine Fruit Combinator might well reach a broader audience than Professor Clank's Combinator was able to. If fruit isn't the be-all and end-all, though, Fruit Combinator's theme isn't as original or as interesting as Professor Clank's Combinator. It's just fruit, clouds, and recycled gameplay. Hardly rip-roaringly exciting stuff to be screaming off the rooftops about.And so the review comes to a close on a game which was okay to play around with for a bit but one possessing little that was very remarkable. In fact, and we're not trying to be mean or anything here, but Fruit Combinator sort of just came across as basically what it was. That is, essentially, a clone which is more generic and less original than the slot it was ported over from.

Title: The Equalizer
review: The Equalizer (Red Tiger): ReviewGet ready for a burst of faux-nostalgia with a groovy retro futuristic-inspired slot from Red Tiger. Taking more than a few cues from the likes of Hotline (NetEnt) and Banana Rock (Play'n GO), The Equalizer is a blisteringly intense game packed with action that's an absolute adrenaline rush. It wears its inspirations in the hex code of its colour palette, but The Equalizer refines formulas in a manner that makes it feel innovative, exciting and fresh in surprising ways.Red Tiger drops you off in a city that could either be from a 1984 Atari game, or some distant future, whatever you prefer. With a 5x4 reel set in default mode, it comes with a feature that can expand both the reels and the rows, increasing the number of paylines from 15 up to a maximum of 60. You also get stacked wilds, which too can expand, as well as a free spins bonus where expanded reels and wilds remain in place for the entire duration of the bonus session. You can play this eccentric slot from 10 cents to 40€/$ per spin.Visually, it looks quite spectacular and is built around a theme that is different from the usual Red Tiger stuff. What sticks out most profoundly maybe, is the giant equalizer below the reels that reacts to the music and certain events in the game. On a side note, the background music is not bad in any way, but it's also not as distinct and catchy as we would expect from a slot that seems to revolve around music. Although it does intensify in the bonus, some more work on the beat could probably have enhanced the experience. Either way, on the semi-transparent reels, which are set against a futuristic metropolis neon backdrop, you'll see lower value card suit symbols alongside stars, bars, dice and diamonds. The top payer is the yellow Lambo which is worth 25 times your stake for 7 of a kind.The Equalizer (Red Tiger): FeaturesFree spins feature in playThe Equalizer is not a particularly feature-heavy slot, but those that are on offer are well integrated and activate quite frequently. Included in the game is the Expanding Slot feature which triggers randomly. In play for the current spin only in the base game, it expands the reel set to a maximum size of 7 reels and 6 rows. You also get an Expanding Wilds feature where wilds can increase in size up to 6 symbols high.Although the main game has potential to generate some decent wins, it's all about the bass...sorry, the Free Spins here. To trigger it, you need to land 3 scatter symbols simultaneously anywhere on the reels - this will give you 10 spins. In the free spins you get all the features that are available to you in the main game but with a few significant advantages.Any wild that appears on the reels will remain in play for the remainder of the bonus and can move left or right on the reels on each spin. You get the same benefit with the Expanding Slot feature - if the reels and rows expand, they will remain expanded for the duration of the free spins round. Furthermore, every +scatter symbol that lands on the reels will add 1 extra spin to your total, without limits.The Equalizer (Red Tiger): VerdictSeeing that Red Tiger recently acquired the Megaways engine, we're a little bit surprised to see them release a shape-shifting game built around a concept developed by themselves. Although it's not as sophisticated as Big Time Gaming's celebrated design, it does offer plenty of action and variety. The Equalizer has what it takes to keep you entertained in the main game, but it is the free spin feature that carries it all the way to the goal. The combination of expanding reels, rows and wilds along with the sticky feature and retriggers is simply outstanding and possibly one of the best Red Tiger bonus games we've ever played.Due to its volatile nature, you have to be a bit careful. During our test sessions, bonuses could drop at a rate of 1 in 50 spins, but there were also plenty of dry spells where it would take us hundreds of spins. However, with 10,000 xbet potential, a lucky few will undoubtedly dance to the beat of The Equalizer.

Title: Frozen Gems
review: Frozen Gems: Slot OverviewDeveloper Play'n GO turns the temperature down once again for an icy themed slot titled Frozen Gems. The name relates in part to the shiny stones making up half the paytable, in part to the way bonus symbols thaw their way enter the action. When they do, players benefit from wilds and splitting symbols which expand reels as well as the default 243 win ways up to 8,748. Play'n GO has tinkered with this idea in several slots in the past that haven’t exactly lit the iGaming world alight, will Frozen Gems fare any better?Bringing back memories of Ice Joker, Play'n GO has stuck to the wintery theme, surrounding the default 5-reel game area with plenty of icy imagery. It’s a little difficult to make out exactly where you are. Obviously, it’s some sort of cave, like a mine, but there is an underwater feeling as well which adds a touch of claustrophobia. Gemstones litter the screen, stuck to walls in a raw form while the refined versions turn up on the reels. A bit of gold trim adorns the grid, yet these aren’t exactly Play'n GO’s best graphics - we’ve definitely experienced more visually impactful slots from the studio.Gem collecting takes place on mobile, tablet, or desktop devices, by selecting a wager from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. The game isn’t exactly a hugely volatile one, but a medium/high rating of 7 out of 10 means it can throw the odd curveball or two. Potential is unusually high for Play'n GO, so there are rewards when the game goes on one of its positive benders, growing reels, tossing in multipliers and whatnot. Beware of a floating RTP which fluctuates at the individual operator’s whim. The default version is the one you want where the RTP is 96.34%, dropping to 94.34% or even less depending on jurisdiction and casino.Wins hit in Frozen Gems when at least three matching symbols land left to right from the first reel onwards. When this happens, the cascade system kicks in, possibly snowballing into several other features. You’ll appreciate any help you can get too since individual wins are lower than usual. Pay symbols begin with 10 to A card royals where five of a kind will win you 0.3 to 0.5 times the bet. Better, though not a much better, value is found in the four gemstones coloured green, purple, red, and orange - five of these symbols are worth a payout of 0.65x to 1x the bet. The wild symbol is worth a bit more at 2.5x the bet for five of a kind. It also substitutes for any regular pay to pull together a combination.Frozen Gems: Slot FeaturesKey to Frozen Gems is the frosty horizontal reel running across the top. Five bonus symbols are held there which come into play as players land winning combinations. On each spin, the bonus reel will carry the following combinations:Two x2 splitting wilds, along with one wild and two x3 splitting symbols.Two x2 splitting wilds, along with two wilds and one x3 splitting symbol.Now, if 3 consecutive winning symbols appear on a reel in the same sequence, then the respective bonus symbols above them thaw and apply their modifier, like so:Wild – turns all positions on the reel into wilds, except scatters.x2 Splitting Symbol – divides all symbols except scatters on the reel into 2 symbols.x3 Splitting Symbol – divides all symbols except scatters on the reel into 3 symbols.At most, there can be up 8,748 ways to win when the maximum number of symbols have been split with the help of the splitting modifiers. Moreover, every win triggers the cascade feature which removes winning symbols from the grid, letting new ones in for another chance. The game also comes with a win multiplier starting at x1, in all phases of the game. Following each cascade, the multiplier increases by +1 where there is no limit set on how high it can get.The final feature is 9 free spins, awarded when 3 scatters are in view, along with an x5 bet win. Any extra scatter on the reels awards an additional 5x prize, keep in mind these scatter wins are not affected by the win multiplier. Whatever the win multiplier was on the triggering spin is carried over to start the round off. The key benefit here is that the win multiplier never resets as it does during the main game. Should scatter symbols land, each one awards +1 free spin. Like the multiplier there is no limit.Frozen Gems: Slot VerdictIn a sense, Frozen Gems takes over where Perfect Gems left off. While the splitting mechanic is entertaining, it seems the developer hasn’t quite pulled off a major game changer using them. It should be mentioned that the competition in this particular category is fierce, and many providers have been experimenting with various approaches on how to present expanding reels and win ways to players for quite some time now.Frozen Gems is neither worse, nor significantly better than its predecessor. The gameplay is kind of interesting, but the splitting symbol/expanding reel concept is being done elsewhere to better effect. Avatar UX’s PopWins range instantly springs to mind as a competitor who is blazing away in this field as do Yggdrasil's Splitz mechanic. Not trying to disparage Frozen Gems here, some may prefer the more traditional looking setup. Yet if its big thrills and even bigger potential you’re after, then slots running PopWins blows it out of the water.Speaking of potential, Frozen Gems come with one of Play'n GO’s higher rewards. They’ve doubled the usual figure to provide payouts of up to 10,000 times the stake. When symbol values are this low, an obscene number of x2 or x3 splitting symbols will need to come into play. In saying that, the ever-present win multiplier is a surprisingly welcome addition. It’s not a freak occurrence, but it’s not every day you see one outside of a bonus game.When you sum everything up, Frozen Gems manages to come across as something a little different. It doesn’t feel like a breakthrough slot though, more of an oddity which may delight some players as much as it leaves others feeling cold.Don't MissIf you enjoyed playing Frozen Gems, be sure to check out the next release in Play'n GO's dynamic reel splitting series of games. Titled Prism of Gems, it offers significantly higher wins of up to 30,000 times your stake.

Title: Lil' Devil
review: Lil' Devil (Big Time Gaming): OverviewYou know how Big Time Gaming likes to build their games around famous hit songs? Well, if you happen to be a fan of British rock band The Cult, you probably already have an idea of what's coming your way. So far, Big Time Gaming has embellished our gaming experience with music from the bands Electric Six (Danger! High Voltage), Europe (The Final Countdown), and Dio (Holy Diver). Now looking to further expand its collection of these popular concept games, Lil' Devil is to be added to that list.The Cult (not to be confused with The Cure) is a hard rock band formed in Bradford, England in 1983 that gained a following in the UK with singles such as "She Sells Sanctuary" before breaking through in the US in the late 80s. The track "Lil' Devil", which appears on the album Electric (1987), was produced by Rick Rubin who has become known for his work on massively successful releases from the likes of Red Hot Chili Peppers, Metallica and Linkin Park."Be My Angel" Free Spins in actionAlthough it has not officially been advertised as such (at the time of writing), Lil' Devil shares enough similarities with Danger! High Voltage and The Final Countdown to establish it as the third installment of the series. Just like the former two, it's not a Megaways offering but is built using 6 reels, 4 fixed rows and 4,096 ways to win. Extremely volatile, as Big Time Gaming slots are typically known to be, it has a RTP of between 96.31% - 96.43%. In case you're wondering, the variation in RTP is the result of the newly introduced Heartstopper™ feature that gives you enhanced free spins and which you will read more about further below.Visually, Lil' Devil has an apocalyptic feel to it. With a backdrop dominated by yellow and orange colour grading, it looks as if the world has been set ablaze or a sand storm of epic proportions has swept over. As a tribute to the gold-rush themed slot Bonanza, you'll see a wooden shack in the background, and just below the reels, poppy flowers sway gently in the wind. It may not be the best looking slot we've ever seen, but there's still something very intriguing about it as it has plenty of that Big Time Gaming personality that fans love.Going through the paytable, we can conclude that its dominated by six lower-value symbols that are represented by the usual 9, 10, J, Q, K and A royal values. More rewarding are the picture symbols of the alligator, the lizard in a bottle, scorpion and the locked purple heart. The latter is the most lucrative, giving you 10 times your stake for a six of a kind combination. The female devil is the wild - it appears on all reels but the first and substitutes for all symbols except the scatter. There is also an Angel Wild that appears fully stacked in the middle section only (reel 3 and 4). Moreover, it comes with multipliers that carry values of between 4x - 12x. Land two of these on the middle reels and they can combine to give you multipliers of up to 144x.Lil' Devil (Big Time Gaming): FeaturesLil' Devil comes packed with features, including a newly trademarked one that makes its first appearance in this slot. First, however, we begin with the Free Spins features. To trigger the bonus, you will have to land 3 or more scatter symbols anywhere in view - landing two of them will launch The Cult's song Lil' Devil and award a heart (more on that later). Upon doing so, you will be faced with two options:Be My Angel Free Spins - Starting with 7 free spins, one of the regular symbols is randomly chosen to act as the sticky wild. If it hits anywhere on reels 2 through to 5, it will transform into a sticky wild and remain in position for the rest of the round. If you manage to get a full reel of sticky wilds, you will be awarded 3 additional spins. Better yet, if it happens on reel 3 or 4, it will transform into an Angel Wild that will set you off with a multiplier of 4x and increase by 2 with each spin up to a maximum of 12x. With two of these, you could potentially be playing with multipliers of up to 144x.Dynamite Lover Free Spins - Starting with 12 free spins, all symbols part of a winning combination, except scatters, are part of a reaction and are replaced by symbols dropping in from above. Dynamite Wilds may also appear on the two central reels - these increase by 1 on each cascade that they're part of and multiply each other. You can also retrigger this feature by landing 3 or more scatters which will give you 6 extra free spins (additional scatters award an extra 6 spins each).Rewinding things a bit, remember that we mentioned how 2 scatters in the base game will award a heart? Well, once you've collected 40 of these, as indicated by the meters on both sides of the reels, the Heartstopper™ Enhanced Free Spins feature activates. Once again, you get to chose from the same two free spins features, although this time, they come with additional benefits:Enhanced Be My Angel Free Spins - The top paying symbol (purple heart) is now also designated a sticky wild.Enhanced Dynamite Lover Free Spins - The multiplier of the Dynamite Wild starts at 5x as opposed to 1x in standard mode.Lil' Devil (Big Time Gaming): VerdictAs you have probably figured out already, Lil' Devil is a slot with a strong resemblance to Danger! High Voltage, which is not a bad thing by any means. In fact, we're relieved to see Big Time Gaming go back to something more straightforward and dumbed-down after a couple of slightly more intricate releases that have required a bit more brain activity from players. Whether it's an improvement to the other two games in the series is up for debate, but Lil' Devil is undoubtedly another step forward for the provider and a welcomed addition that will offer players plenty of tense gameplay and thrilling sessions.Moreover, the Heartstopper™ feature also serves the game well, acting as a little side game that gives you something extra to put your hope into every time that scatter tease gives you the middle finger. In that sense, Lil' Devil follows in the footsteps of Kingmaker, another slot where you don't want to trigger the feature too soon. To conclude, Lil' Devil is another outstanding release from the Australians and a worthy follow up to Danger! High Voltage and The Final Countdown. Insanely volatile, it also comes packed with huge potential that will make sure to keep everyone and their mother on the edge.Don't MissCurious to explore other high potential Big Time Gaming titles? Be sure to try Beef Lightning (56,000x potential), Spicy Meatballs (44,000x potential), or Wild Flower which is a continuation on Danger! High Voltage and Lil' Devil.

Title: Le Bandit
review: Le Bandit: Slot OverviewYou might have heard of the action comedy film Smokey and the Bandit starring Burt Reynolds and Sally Field, now get ready to meet cartoon bad guy Smokey Le Bandit. Well, we say guy, but Smokey is a raccoon, and he's the star of Le Bandit, an online slot from busy developer Hacksaw Gaming. He sounds like a bit of a rogue; as the game info puts it, Smokey 'won't hesitate to fleece you for all you're worth by using every trick in the book and then some!' It's not all bad news, though, because Smokey can be 'persuaded to share some of his ill-gotten gains' if you can get on his good side. This may occur through features like Super Cascades, Golden Squares, plus three bonus rounds – Luck Of The Bandit, All That Glitters Is Gold, and Treasure At The End Of The Rainbow.A sepia-lit backstreet location is the setting for Le Bandit, where a 6x5 gaming panel sits next to Smokey himself, who might not come across as a super friendly chap at first. With a crowbar in hand, twirly moustache, and clenched fists, he looks like he's just about to get up to nefarious activities, though he does cheer up from time to time. Based on the visual cues and the game's title, it would seem we have gone back in time to an earlier part of France's past. The Polaroid camera FS symbol (despite being first released in 1948) throws a spanner in the works, but wherever we are is amusingly presented, with an edge.Le Bandit slot - base gameThe math model isn't as edgy as it can be from Hacksaw Gaming, as the volatility has been classed as medium (3 out of 5) whilst generating an RTP of 96.34%. At the default RTP level, Le Bandit has a hit frequency of 32.47% and creates wins when 5 or more matching symbols are connected to each other anywhere on the gaming grid. Le Bandit uses what it calls a Super Cascade wins system, so when a winning cluster hits, all regular paying symbols of the same type as the winning symbols are removed from the reels, and new symbols drop down to fill the gaps. When picking a stake, the options are 10 p/c to $/€100, and four options are available from the feature buy menu.Ten regular paying symbols may land on Le Bandit's grid. These are 10 to A card ranks as the low pays, then a trap, cheese, a mug of beer, a bag of baguettes, and a top hat are the highs. Hitting a 5 OAK winning cluster pays 0.1 to 1 times the bet, rising to 15 to 100 times the bet for a 13+ cluster. The wild reward poster is able to substitute for any regular pay symbol.Le Bandit: Slot FeaturesLe Bandit slot - free spinsAs well as Super Cascades, Le Bandit serves up features such as Golden Squares, special symbols, three bonus rounds and bonus buys.Golden SquaresAfter a winning combination occurs, the squares behind the winning symbols are highlighted and known as Golden Squares. If a Rainbow symbol is on the grid, it activates any Golden Squares after all winning combinations have been awarded. Activated Golden Squares reveal either Bronze, Silver, or Gold Coins and have the chance to show Pot of Gold or Four-Leaf Clover symbols. All Coins have values as multipliers of the bet. Bronze Coins have values of 0.2x, 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 3x, or 4x. Silver Coins have values of 5x, 10x, 15x, or 20x, and Gold Coins have values of 25x, 50x, 100x, 250x, or 500x. Once all of the Coins and special symbols are revealed, any Four-Leaf Clover symbols activate, multiplying all Coins and Pot of Gold symbols on adjacent squares with values of x2, x3, x4, x5, or x10.Pot of Gold symbols, when in view, activate after Four-Leaf Clovers by collecting all Coin values and other Pot of Gold symbols, storing the total value. When the last Pot of Gold has activated, all other Golden Squares activate again, revealing new symbols and the process above repeats until no new Pot of Gold appears. Then, all Coins and Pot of Gold symbols award their values. Golden Squares are then removed.Luck of the BanditLanding 3 FS scatters in the base game triggers this feature with 8 free spins. In this bonus, all Golden Squares remain highlighted between spins until they are activated by Rainbow symbols. Landing 2 FS scatters awards +2 free spins, landing 3 FS scatters awards an extra 4 free spins. Hitting 4 FS scatter upgrades the bonus to All That Glitters Is Gold, plus 4 extra free spins are awarded.All That Glitters Is GoldOr, you can activate this feature by landing 4 FS scatters in the base game to win 12 free spins. In this round, all Golden Squares remain highlighted till the end, even after being activated. Landing 2 FS scatters awards +2 free spins, landing 3 FS scatters awards an extra 4 free spins.Treasure At The End Of The RainbowThis round is triggered by landing 5 FS symbols in the base game to win 12 free spins. In this bonus, all Golden Squares remain highlighted till the end, even after being activated, and a Rainbow symbol is guaranteed to hit on each spin. Also, Bronze Coins do not appear in this feature.Bonus BuyThe bonus buy lets players activate these modes/features. The first is highly volatile; the rest are medium volatile.BonusHunt FeatureSpins – 3x the bet where each spin is 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game. RTP 96.28%.Rainbow FeatureSpins – 50x the bet where each spin is guaranteed to land a Rainbow symbol. RTP 96.36%.Luck Of The Bandit – 100x the bet to buy 8 free spins. RTP 96.3%.All That Glitters Is Gold – 250x the bet to buy 12 free spins. RTP 96.4%.Le Bandit slot - feature buy menuLe Bandit: Slot VerdictChalk up another playable slot from Hacksaw Gaming that delivers new ways for players to potentially collect a few coins. Thanks to studios like Push Gaming, Slotmill, or Pragmatic Play, coin win features are hot, and Le Bandit's unique way of loading them on the board, then augmenting their values with various special symbols, is worth a look for coin fans. The amusing urban animal RIP City/retro Disney style of presentation is fun, and the feisty racoon with his speech bubble quips help make Le Bandit as personable as it is playable.Speaking of playable, Le Bandit is one of those cluster-paying slots which works best when it gets on a major roll. You could say that about pretty much all of them, but still. Instead of how it often is in some cluster games, this doesn't mean collecting winning symbols in a meter, then injecting features on the grid at set collection points. Instead, the goal is to plaster as many Golden Squares onto the reels as possible, with a Rainbow symbol in view to start activating them. Then you want to get locked in a Pot of Gold collection loop, with a few multipliers thrown in for good measure. At full capacity, Le Bandit can generate wins up to 10,000x the bet, and while it might be medium volatile, the game did seem to have quite a swingy temperament at times.Due to some of Smokey's disguises and several of the symbols, Le Bandit arguably leans towards being an Irish-themed slot as well, sort of. If so, then it's hard to think of any other Irish/leprechaun slot that looks like this. Or plays like this, for that matter. So, for something unique in the thematic as well as gameplay departments, Le Bandit could be just the rascally racoon-populated slot you never knew you wanted.

Title: Frogs & Bugs
review: Frogs & Bugs: Slot OverviewHope you like creepy crawlies for this one, folks. Frogs & Bugs is an online slot built by prolific software designer Pragmatic Play. Built might not be the best word to use in this situation, as Frogs & Bugs is a reskin of an earlier release called Tropical Tiki - a game that didn't pull off anything especially wow at the time of its review. In other words, hopes weren't exactly soaring high up there in the clouds when the Frogs & Bugs test run began. But optimism is an inherent human trait; if we didn't think the future could be better than it is today, who knows where humanity might have ended up? In that spirit of optimism, let's see what Frogs & Bugs can do.First up is the Frogs & Bugs setting and sensory impact. The game takes place in a lily pad-coated pond, all vines, lotus flowers and such like. Visually, the game has a Wild Hop & Drop look about it, which makes sense as both slots have a froggy focus. A cute, cartoonish, friendly look got Frogs & Bugs off to a pretty positive start, though nothing completely shrugged off the doubts it would perform much better than the original slot did once in motion.Frogs & Bugs slot - base gameFrogs & Bugs do have a fairly unusual grid set-up, consisting of 6-reels, holding 3 rows each, in the base game, and is able to expand further in the bonus round. The locked symbols drop to the lowest possible positions on their reels, and new symbols tumble in from above. If more winning symbols appear, they lock as well, as do any extra scatters. This process continues until no new winning symbols or scatters land, or all positions are filled, then a win evaluation occurs, and the next spin can take place.Free SpinsLanding at least 4 scatter symbols (on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5) triggers the free spins round, where players get 8 free spins. During free spins, the game grid grows to 6-reels, 5-rows in size where at best, 6,400 ways to win may become active. However, in the beginning, the top 2 rows have all of their positions locked. At most, 8 positions can be unlocked in a round.Buy Free SpinsPlayers may buy their way into the free spins section for some of that grid expansion/unlocking action for the cost of 100 times the bet. When buying free spins, the number of triggering scatters is always 4, and no tumbles will occur.Frogs & Bugs slot - free spinsFrogs & Bugs: Slot VerdictThere you have it; as far as enjoyment levels go, Frogs & Bugs was about on par with its template slot Tropical Tiki. Title: The Sword and the Grail Excalibur

Title: Jin Chan’s Pond of Riches

Title: Mega Flip
review: Mega Flip: OverviewDeveloper Relax Gaming drags players onto the dance floor in their classically inspired slot Mega Flip. Relax Gaming use a dice icon to rate volatility, and Mega Flip earns the full 5 out of 5 in that regard. Hits come at a rate of nearly one in four, or 24.79%, so fairly frequent, though standard symbol combos aren't exactly massive. RTP is good at 96.2%, making it slightly above average so no issues in the stats department.Depending on how you view these kinds of games the paytable is enough to make you laugh or cry. Those down for some fruity fun will enjoy the plums, oranges, and cherries making up the low pays. Classic symbols reign supreme for the high pays too, including bells, shamrocks, stars, and sevens. You really need those features bopping on the dance floor if you want to get anywhere.Mega Flip: FeaturesMega Flip - free spins in actionMega Flip has two features brightening the party - respins, which pop up relatively often, alongside a free spins round which is far more elusive.Just below the main reels is an additional reel rotating horizontally. If this reel lights up saying 'Respin' in conjunction with a win, then a respin is triggered. During the respin feature, winning symbols lock and respins keep on coming as long as new winning symbols land.Also, filling a reel with winning symbols activates the multiplier above it. However, multipliers are activated in sequential order, meaning the 1st reel must be filled first, then the 2nd and so on. Let's say reels 2, 3, and 4 are filled, but the first is not, then no multiplier is awarded. If the 1st reel is filled on the next respin though, then the 4th reel multiplier immediately becomes active in this example. During the base game, the multiplier ascends through values of x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, and x7.You probably don't need us to tell you to keep an eye for the diamond symbol. Landing 3 in the main game triggers the Free Spins feature. Exactly 3 awards 8 free spins with every additional diamond in view awarding 2 extra free spins.During free spins, the reel area is flipped horizontally lining the reels up in a 4-4-3-3-2-2 fashion to increase hit rate. The respins reel gets locked, so respins are awarded on any initial winning combination. Multipliers no longer have to be activated by filling the first reel onwards either. For example, if the 6th reel is full, it activates the x2 on the first reel, even if the first reel is not.Lastly, landing 3 Diamond symbols retriggers the feature and award 4 more spins, with each additional diamond adding 2 extra spins. For every free spins retrigger, the potential multipliers are all increased by one.Mega Flip: VerdictMega Flip can be a bit of fun at first. Its unusual reel setup is intriguing and hitting a decent respin early on can leave you wanting more. You get tantalisingly close to full grids relatively often too, which provides motivation to keep trying for the next one. It can get frustrating when a significant proportion of the grid is filled with winning symbols, but not get two in the first reel, preventing you from activating any multipliers.The situation improves during free spins as it usually does since having respins on every winning combination is a major help. The scenario you want is a full grid of sevens, which is worth 1,512 times your stake with the x7 multiplier active. At full capacity, however, Mega Flip comes with potential of up to 5,495 times the stake.For players looking for another classically Twin Spin inspired hit, Mega Flip isn't a bad option. It's got a few things you might not have seen before, predominantly the grid arrangement, so there's that. If you're up for more fruit in jazzy surrounds, that's a little bit different, sure why not? If not, then Mega Flip can come across as a local DJ struggling to warm up a crowd before the international headliner takes command of the room.

Title: Lost Boys Loot
review: Lost Boys Loot (iSoftBet): OverviewWith regulators growing increasingly concerned over the use of graphics that could appeal to kids, it's a bit surprising to see there are still developers out there who create video slots that look more like something that came with your children's Fruit Loops box rather than a virtual gambling machine. Why have one wild when you can have four? The two 1x1 Hook wilds are standard and substitute for the base game pay symbols. Tinkerbell appears magically at random during the main game to turn 3-5 symbols into Tink wilds.There is also a Fully Stacked Hook Wild that not only substitutes for pay symbols but when it lands and covers the middle reel, it triggers the Treasure Trap Free Spins. To start this bonus game, players spin the Captain's wheel to win 5, 8, 10, or 12 free spins. During these free spins, the extended Hook wild remains locked on the middle reel. When winning combinations land, Hook locks the symbols into place for the remainder of the spins by tossing a net over them.Peter Pan is the bonus symbol and 3 or more trigger the Dueling Free Spins feature - 3, 4, 0r 5 Peter Pan bonus symbols will give you 10, 20, or 30 free spins respectively. They get the name 'Dueling' because if Pan and the extended Hook symbol land at the same time, they get into a brawl. If Hook wins the battle, he increases the bonus round multiplier, and if Pan wins, he awards more free spins.The last symbol is the treasure chest and just one is needed to unlock the Lost Boys Bonus feature. The screen changes to one covered in chests, and players get to open 3 of them that can contain either cash prizes or the two free spins rounds.To cap it all off, the crocodile that bit off Hook's hand also leaps into the action from time to time. Known as the Tick Tock's Wild Chomp feature, how it works is that the croc lurks beneath a reel, and if a Hook wild lands on that reel the croc leaps up to grab him changing all symbols beneath it wild as well.Lost Boys Loot (iSoftBet): VerdictYou might need a moment or two after all of that to absorb everything. The gameplay contains a lot of different elements, and a demo is certainly worthwhile to learn how they all work. A fast-flowing, highly volatile slot this is not, but its bright theme and smorgasbord of extras do make Lost Boys Loot intriguing.Where it lags is that Peter Pan and Neverland were all about magic, about being young forever, and about flying. Sure, there are battles between Hook and Pan during the game, but it's all a bit down to earth – it doesn't soar to the heights that the movie and stories achieved. A bit more enchantment, or maybe a more emotional soundtrack would have engaged fans of the Pan fable a bit more.As it is, Lost Boys Loot is an above-average slot that is certainly easy on the eyes. Perhaps we were a little hard on it during the previous paragraph as it does possess a charm that makes spinning its reels enjoyable. The number of extras iSoftBet has managed to ram in is impressive and fun to discover. The result is a slot that is suited to casual gamers who will enjoy the mix of features and the gentle volatility. Those looking for a stronger hit won't be impressed. A top prize of 500x the bet is technically possible on one spin, and when you factor in multipliers this could conceivably reach solid amounts. However the top prize has been capped at 48,190 coins, or around 2,410x the total bet.The vibe, the theme, and the numbers are aimed at a certain section of the gambling community, and that's fine. If it sounds enticing, you will have a pleasant time on your trip to Neverland. If you are recoiling over the numbers, however, then not even a sprinkle of Tink's fairy dust will win you over.

Title: Bulldozer
review: Bulldozer: Slot OverviewCock-a-doodle-doo! Get ready to cultivate some exciting wins with a new slot offering from Iron Dog Studios (1x2 Network).  The game takes us to the pasture of farmland where we find a farmer, bales of hay, roosters, rams and most importantly, bulls. This cheery mixture of animals and farmers alike provide for a gaming experience that will surely find an audience in the gaming world, especially fans of classic hold-and-win style slots.Bulldozer slot - base gameBulldozer is a medium volatility slot with a standard RTP of 96.07% but is also available in lower RTP versions (94.02%/88.03%). The action itself takes place on a 5-reel, 3-row active panel with 20 fixed paylines to land winning combinations on. playable stakes are €/$0.20-€/$50.00, available on both mobile and desktop devices. For those who want to jump straight into the more potentially rewarding parts of the game, a bonus buy option is available, allow you to buy 10 spins for 71 times your stake, alternatively 20 spins for 142 times your stake, or a whopping 30 free spins for 214 times your stake. The Hold and Win feature itself cannot be purchased, but in testing, the hit frequency appeared not too brutal.Bulldozer: Slot FeaturesBulldozer slot - Hold & Win Respin featureThis farm-themed slot is akin to Play'n Go's recent 2022 release Animal Madness although the setting for the slot is the only thing that is not a typical hold-and-win type slot. Iron Dog has added extra features into the mix to differentiate it from the rest, including Spreading Wilds, Coin Collection, Free Spins, and a hold-and-win round.Bull WildThis is where the bulldozer comes in.  Bull Wilds can appear on reels and substitute for all non-special symbols. If you land a Bull Wild and a Bulldozer symbol on the same spin, the Bull Wild will charge towards the nearest bulldozer to replace the symbol, leaving a trail of Wild Bulls behind it - a feature reminiscent of ELK Studios' successful Toro series of games.  Landing a full line of Bull Wilds will result in 250 times your bet. This feature is available in both the base game and the free spins.CoinsCoins can appear on all reels, and landing 5 or more coins will trigger the hold-and-win feature.  If you trigger the feature during the free spins round, a "W" Coin will substitute for all non-special symbols. When the coin lands on the reels, it will flip to reveal a multiplier which will affect any win line it is a part of.  If you are lucky enough to get two multipliers on the same win line - they will multiply each other.Free SpinsLanding 3 or more scatters triggers the free spins feature; 3, 4 or 5 scatters give you 10, 20, or 30 free spins, respectively. During free spins, the Bull wild and coin features are in play, with an added +1FS coin. Moreover, the wooden cannon is more frequently active than in the base game. This cannon fires coins onto the active panel for an increased chance of triggering the hold-and-win feature.Hold-And-WinDuring the base game or in the free spins feature, if you are lucky enough to land 5 or more coins, this will trigger the hold-and-win feature. Jackpot coins are also available, and landing one will result in a prize ranging from 50 times your stake for the Mini Jackpot all the way up to 750 times your stake for the Major Jackpot. Fill the screen with paying coins, and a prize of 2500 times your stake is awarded.Bulldozer slot - free spinsBulldozer: Slot VerdictThe opportunity to review another hold-and-win slot is usually not the most exciting task, though, in the case of Bulldozer, there are enough modifiers and features to keep casual slot players interested. The hardcore gamers, on the other hand, might not be too impressed with getting their hands dirty doing some farming here. Sure, Bulldozer will not produce epic wins like previous Iron Dog Studio slot hits like Pirate Kingdom Megaways or 1 Million Megaways BC. However, the fairly high potential might be incentive enough for even more experienced players to go give it a try.Speaking of potential, spreading wilds meeting the bull wild can result in significant wins during base game play given the fact that a full screen of wilds will produce the coveted 5000x payday. To sum things up, fans of hold-and-win slots are quite likely to enjoy Bulldozer to some extent seeing there is potential for some decent wins. The gameplay itself isn't terrible either though, if you're not a fan of this type of gaming, Bulldozer won't convert you.

Title: Lucky Lemons
review: Lucky Lemons: Slot OverviewIs casino game maker Snowborn Games into Feng Shui? That was a question which arose when reviewing its online slot Lucky Lemons, since according to what some have said about the Chinese geomancy, having 9 lemons in a bowl purifies energies while also being evidence of good luck and fortune. Hopefully, players manage to rummage up those last two things since good luck and fortune are two of the most coveted outcomes in online gambling. Not sure how coveted Lucky Lemons will be, though. It's a pretty vanilla slot, ultra-light on theme, while possessing elements recognizable from earlier Snowborn releases.Lucky Lemons sits on a different branch of the same family tree as slots like Pile 'Em Up and, by extension, to a lesser degree, Tippy's Tavern. It's a low personality fruity slot, blue backgrounded in the base game, orange in the bonus, and red in free spins. There's not much else to say about the audiovisuals other than they are pleasantly innocuous to the point of being uninteresting. Like calming elevator music.Lucky Lemons slot - base gameThe bet selection in Lucky Lemons is 20 c to $/€50 per spin, and players are able to buy the free spins round from the feature shop. Operating on a medium volatile math model, of the three available RTP configurations, 96% is the default return value. A 5-reel grid is where the symbols land in 3 rows, forming winning combinations along the 20 paylines.Awarding up to 1 to 2.4 times the stake are the low pay J-A card ranks, then we've got grapes, plums, watermelon slices, and cherries, worth 7x to 17x the bet for 5 OAK. Wilds pay 100x the bet when a winning line of 5 of them land on the grid. Wilds appear on all reels and can substitute for all regular pay symbols.Lucky Lemons: Slot FeaturesLucky Lemons slot - bonus gameLucky Lemons' features carry on from Snowborn Games' prior slots, where they include money symbol collects, a Lemon Booster multiplier, free spins, a hold 'n win bonus round with jackpot prizes, and a feature buy.Collect Wins & Lemon BoosterLanding a Collect symbol on the rightmost reel awards the total amount of all Lemon symbols in view, multiplied by the value of the Lemon Booster. Lemon symbol values are 0.2 to 50 times the bet. The Lemon Booster starts at x1. It increases with each 1UP symbol collected up to x10. After the multiplier has been applied to Lemon symbols, it resets to x1 in the base game. The Lemon Booster is available in the base game and in free spins.Free SpinsHitting 3 scatters on reels 1, 3 and 5 awards 10 free spins. Each 1UP symbol increases the Lemon Booster multiplier, and in free spins, the Lemon Booster does not reset. Moreover, +5 free spins are awarded when the Lemon Booster multiplier reaches x4, x7, and x10.Bonus & Prize SymbolsThe Bonus is randomly triggered when landing a Lemon symbol on reels 1, 2, 3, or 4. When activated, the feature starts with 3 bonus spins on an empty grid. A Lemon or Prize symbol landing anywhere resets the 3 bonus spins. Lemons are sticky. If Lemons and Prize symbols fill all of the positions, the Mega Prize is awarded. The feature ends when there are no empty positions left, or all of the spins run out.During the Bonus feature, the four possible Prize symbols are the 30x Mini, the 100x Minor, the 500x Major, and the 5,000x Mega. Prize symbols are collected by their corresponding meters, and are removed from the reels. Symbols that trigger a win remain on the reels until the feature ends. If 3 of the same Prize symbols land, the corresponding prize is awarded.Buy Free SpinsAt Lucky Lemons' feature shop, players can buy 10 free spins for 50 times the total bet.Lucky Lemons slot - free spinsLucky Lemons: Slot VerdictIt was hard to know where to begin with Lucky Lemons. The game was so vanilla, so lacking in character it struggled to spark many trains of thought. This led to some internet noodling, along the lines of 'Are lemons lucky?, and a number of beliefs popped up in the search results, including the Feng Shui info. Maybe that's where Snowborn got the idea for Lucky Lemons from, maybe not. Snowborn didn't have to look far for the gameplay ideas since many of them have either shown up in the studio's earlier work or are common features that return in various incarcerations again and again, and again. Same goes for the local jackpots which Games Global studios clutch onto like a drowning man to driftwood. They remain a polarizing feature: some revel in the chase, while others bemoan the allocation of RTP towards seemingly unattainable pots.Couple the so-so gameplay with the soulless presentation, and Lucky Lemons was a game that was hard to fall for. It wasn't dislikable either, however; it just didn't really elicit any strong emotional response either way. The game does its thing, you collect Lemon symbol cash prizes, increment the Lemon Booster multiplier, maybe trigger a bonus or two, ho-hum, on it goes. The action is okay, but any edge, any angle, any hook, was sorely missing. Snowborn has shown in the past it is more than capable of creating slots with character such as Cat Clans, or those with punch like the two Masters slots, yet Lucky Lemons displayed neither of those qualities.Lucky Lemons does have a max win of 5,000x, and given it's similar in some ways to one of Snowborn's more successful slots, Pile' Em Up, who knows, it might be a hit with a certain audience. Great if it does, but equally great if we never end up crossing paths with Lucky Lemons again.

Title: Beef Up the Bonus
review: Beef Up the Bonus: Slot OverviewIn the words of software provider High Limit Studio, their game Beef Up the Bonus is its 'meatiest slot ever'. The good news for vegetarians and animal lovers is that Beef Up the Bonus is not a study in modern-day meat production, which sees hundreds of millions of cattle slaughtered each year. No, no, it's more a celebration of mighty bulls roaming the range, looking intimidating, snortin' and stampin' their hooves. It also has features like a prize wheel, a hold 'n win round, and free spins that are pretty standard on the surface, but there are one or two tweaks that may cause flutters of intrigue.Powered by Games Global, Beef Up the Bonus' visuals, referred to by the studio as part of an Art 2.0 concept, manage to be both minimal and brightly eye-catching at the same time. One eye-catcher is the seriously expressioned bull on the side of the screen, looking like one of those big black bull billboards dotted around Spain, while the hot desert background conjured memories of the untitled yellow Mark Rothko painting with the white line through the middle. That or a Wile E. Coyote chasing Road Runner through the desert scenario. As mentioned, Beef Up the Bonus looks a bit basic, but it is cleanly presented, so it is eye-pleasing in its way.Beef Up the Bonus slot - base gameTaking up a chunk of the screen is a 5-reel, 3-row gaming grid with 20 paylines for line win calculations. Running the game is a medium volatile math model, with a default RTP of 96.01%, though lower values are available in certain markets. Players pick stakes of 20 c to $/€40 per spin, and on the highest RTP model, hits occur at a rate of 26.95%.For low pays, Beef Up the Bonus has J-A card ranks designed in a Western style, paying 2.5x the bet when hitting a line of 5 of them; then, as highs, there are cacti, boots, hats, pistols, and vultures worth 3.75 to 12.5 times the bet for a 5 OAK result. Hitting on all reels expect the leftmost one is Beef Up the Bonus' wild symbol, substituting any regular pay symbol.Beef Up the Bonus: Slot FeaturesBeef Up the Bonus slot - free spinsBeefing up the game are a Link&Win feature, a Link&Win Upgrade Trail, free spins, and a wheel feature.Link&Win Upgrade TrailLink&Win symbols land in two forms – regular Coin symbols on all reels or Coin Wild symbols, which only appear in free spins. Beef Up symbols may land randomly on regular pay symbols in the base game. Beef Up symbols are collected when they do show up by the Link&Win Upgrade Trail, which has 3 levels.Link&WinPlay begins at level 1. Landing at least 6 Link&Win symbols triggers the Link&Win feature – this feature can also be triggered from the wheel feature, where it begins with 6-14 randomly generated Link&Win symbols. A total of 3 respins start the round, and all Link&Win symbols are held. Newly landed Link&Win symbols are also held, and the respins count is reset to 3. Each Link&Win symbol displays a cash prize of up to 50x the bet, all awarded when the round ends.Collecting 20 Beef Up symbols in the base game upgrades the Link&Win Upgrade Trail to level 2. The rules of Level 1 remain; however, Level 2 adds multipliers to all initially blank positions. One of these is a 50x, 60x, or 70x multiplier held on one of the random blank positions. Others are 2x, 3x, and 5x, multipliers held on all other initially blank positions. All multipliers are applied to their respective cash prizes at the end of the feature.Collecting 40 Beef Up symbols in the base game upgrades the Link&Win Upgrade Trail to level 3. All rules from level 2 apply, plus landing Link&Win symbols increases the multipliers on positions without Link&Win symbols. A 50x, 60x, or 70x multiplier is active on a random blank position and can increase to 1,030x. Other 2x, 3x, or 5x multipliers are active on all other initially blank positions and can increase to 145x.Free SpinsHorseshoe scatters are present on all reels. Hitting 3, 4, or 5 scatters pays 2x, 15x, or 100x the bet, while also awarded 10 free spins. Hitting 3 or more scatters in the free spins round grants an additional +3 free spins. Coin wilds are stacked in free spins, appearing on one reel at a time, and move from the leftmost reel to the rightmost reel, then from the rightmost to the leftmost reel, from free spin to free spin. Coin wild symbols substitute for all symbols except scatters. The Link&Win feature can be won during free spins at the same Upgrade Trail level as in the base game.Wheel FeatureWheel symbols appear on reels 1, 3, and 5 in the base game. Hitting 3 of them triggers the Wheel feature, where a wheel spins to award free spins, the Link&Win round, or the Mini, Maxi, Minor, Major, or Mega prize worth 5x, 10x, 50x, 500x, or 5,000x the bet, respectively.Beef Up the Bonus slot - bonusBeef Up the Bonus: Slot VerdictPhew, that was quite a meaty set of features to chow through. A lot, if not most, are fairly standard extras one might find in any number of Games Global studio slots (as well as from other designers), but High Limit Studio has made a few adjustments to make Beef Up the Bonus relatively more entertaining than it might have been. What's interesting is that according to the documentation, some of what's ended up in the game has come about from feedback over High Limit Game's first year or so of developing slots. Therefore, in certain circles, Beef Up the Bonus should be quite warmly received if these were the sorts of tweaks commentators were hoping for.For one thing, the Link&Win feature can receive quite a beefing up. This comes in the form of position multipliers, which can theoretically be quite large – up to x70 at level 2 or up to x1,030 at level 3. It's a nifty idea, works with the beefing up concept, and one good thing is that progress doesn't go back to level 1. However, the Link&Win round is a bit of a one-trick pony, with no special symbols or anything similar in the mix. Simply land Link&Win symbols, hopefully with the biggest multipliers as possible, then cash in when the round ends. Some may like the simplicity. Others may be bored. Helping flesh Beef Up the Bonus are its free spins round and bonus wheel. The wheel is where the game's 5,000x the bet max win may be instantly won, while free spins have the coin stack thing.If your idea of an enjoyable hold 'n win slot is something brutal, with a massive max win and an intricate web of special symbols, then Beef Up the Bonus is unlikely to be beefy enough. In fact, it might come across as a plant-based meat substitute. On the other side of the coin, though, Beef Up the Bonus is pretty flowey, keeping the action going with fairly frequent Link&Win triggers, and has a prize wheel and free spins on the side, meaning it should be a match for gamblers who go in for this Games Global Link&Win style of play.

Title: TikiPop
review: TikiPop: Slot OverviewIf there is one bunch of games finding its stride, it's the PopWins range from independent developer Avatar UX. The 5th release in the series, TikiPop uses one of the more mainstream themes so far, aside from its fruity filled sibling CherryPop perhaps. As the name makes mention, we're off to the Pacific Ocean for some Tiki-themed action alongside expanding reels, PopWins, multipliers and free spins.When you go Tiki, it's customary to go bright, which Avatar UX has most assuredly done. Tiki symbols on the reels are as flashy as you could want them, while laced around the grid is plenty of Pacific fauna. TikiPop's soundtrack is just as bouncy, with pleasant auditory effects when combos hit or wins count up. It gets moodier during free spins, where the action shifts to a blazing red temple and where every element of TikiPop is enhanced. Suffice to say, TikiPop does the genre justice with an explosion of colour.Players get their totem on by selecting bets from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin, across all devices. So far, PopWins has been about highly volatile math models, which is what we find here as well, chaining wins together and blowing out the reels when it's firing. RTP, meanwhile, is decent and close to what the other PopWin slots have offered, producing a value of 96.10%.Central to the range is the PopWins mechanic itself. Whenever a combination lands, the winning symbols pop and are replaced by two new ones so more wins may occur. This pushes the default 5x3 sized grid up to 5 rows in height at most during the main game. If all reels fully extend, an x2 multiplier is applied to the round win. As you'd expect, expanding rows has an effect on win ways as well, boosting them from a starting figure of 243 up to 3,125 in the base game and stretching even further during free spins. Keep in mind that TikiPop pays both ways – left to right as well as right to left, doubling the number of functional win ways to 486 – 6,250.Tikis abound on the paytable, making up the five high pay symbols, worth 2.5 to 6 times the stake for five of a kind. There is a more valuable symbol, the jewelled Super High which is worth 10x the bet for five of a kind. Rounding out the bottom of the paytable are tribal patterned J-A card icons. There's no wild, but the pay both ways system and other features mean you don't really miss it.TikiPop: Slot Features﻿Hitting 3, 4, or 5 scatters on the reels, awards 7, 11, or 15 free spins, or as they're referred too; Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 free spins. Before the round, players may gamble to win more spins. Level 1 can be gambled for Level 2, or Level 2 for Level 3. There is a 50/50 chance of winning. However, be warned that losing will dump you back to the base game. Alternatively, you can collect free spins and head straight to the bonus.Free spins start on an altered grid arrangement from 4-3-3-3-4 up to 5x5 in formation. A couple of changes occur in the bonus. A major one is the progressive multiplier which enters the fray, starting at x1, and incrementing by 1 following each PopWin - with no set limit on how high it can go. Also, the grid does not reset to its original height between spins. Instead, it drops down to the shortest reel height. If players unlock 7 positions on all 5 reels, then the game remains locked at that height for the rest of the round where 33,614 win ways are available.In addition, when all reels are unlocked, the multiplier increments by 2 instead of 1, while 2-4 free spins are also added to the total. Basically you want to open the grid as early as possible to pick up a host of benefits.TikiPop also provides a bonus buy for those looking to skip the base game. 100x the bet gets you 7 free spins which can be gambled or collected as if they were triggered naturally.TikiPop: Slot VerdictTikiPop is another solid entrant in the PopWins range, and more evidence the series is going from strength to strength. It's got a bright yet conventional look that most players can enjoy, as well as high volatility, big reward combination to satisfy the harder crew. It's not the deadliest beast in the PopWins stable, nor the highest paying. Although we're yet to see evidence of its claimed potential, none have so far matched the first one, PopRocks, in that regard, where brutal punishment could flick to insanity in a beat.Nevertheless, the series has improved as it has progressed, and TikiPop has a better flow, landing wins at a rate that makes it easy to stay motivated. The other incentive to keep spinning is a bonus game which can go mental when the full grid is unlocked. TikiPop's bonus game is one of the less complicated ones in the range, though all the better for it. Its free spins are where the pay both ways system really shines in conjunction with a multiplier which can hit some pretty high levels. When the multiplier is increasing by +2 a pop, it's capable of turning even low pay wins into something special each time. Then there's massive potential of 32,000 times your stake up for grabs, putting the icing on a highly playable game.All up, TikiPop is another solid release in a range going through a refining process as it moves along. TikiPop might be a little garish for some, but if the fluro stylings don't burn your retinas, there is plenty to like about where PopWins is heading.Don't MissFore more PopWins action from developer Avatar UX, be sure to try the sixth slot in the range titled HippoPop. Expanding up to 65,536 ways during the bonus, it can dish out a whopping 48,150 times your stake in the best of scenarios.

Title: North Storm
review: North Storm (Rabcat): OverviewRabcat is an up and coming gaming company based in Austria that works alongside gambling titans Microgaming and Yggdrasil. They are a group of developers that certainly enjoy a mythological/fantasy slot as their back catalogue testifies. Some examples are gods in Legend of Olympus, fantasy in Dragons Myth and Forsaken Kingdom, among others. Their latest slot North Storm follows this tradition, with more than a little inspiration from other well-known slots and TV shows.Let’s just come out and say it, the game bears heavy resemblance to NetEnt's Asgardian Stones. It even uses a similar game mechanic, which here is known as the Rolling Reels feature. Then there is the background, is that the Fist of the First Men, where the Night’s Watch fought off the Army of the Dead? Maybe that’s a coincidence, but that wild also looks freakishly similar to House Stark’s emblem, and the scatter like a White Walker. Whatever, chalk it up to coincidence and roll with it for now. Because the game is a looker, no doubt about that and Rabcat has captured the look, sound and feel of the fantasy genre nicely. Fans of the theme will find plenty of visceral appeal.First things first - players get 25 fixed paylines spread over 5 reels and 3 rows. Bets start at 0.25 p/c and go all the way up to $/€50 per spin. Not exactly a heroic amount, but more than enough for most brave warriors to get fired up. With a respectable RTP of 96.13% and medium volatility, those who like more consistent, ongoing rewards may find that here. The great thing about the game mechanic means that wins can multiply, which keeps the action rolling. Still, it doesn’t mask the imitative nature of the game though, it actually highlights it.Symbols offer decent value throughout the paytable. On the lower side, we get runic style 10, J, Q and K symbols worth from 0.2x to 4x the stake. The three top base game symbols are Celtic patterns worth from 0.8x up to 100x the wager. The dire wolf is the wild and takes the place of any paying symbol. It is also worth 100x the bet if 5 of a kind land in a winning combination. Mix in the Bonus Falls feature, and these symbols can build up into satisfying amounts. Though, with the game’s top prize of approximately 500-1000x per spin in the bonus, jackpot fans may prefer juicier hunting grounds to get a hit.North Storm (Rabcat): FeaturesFree Spins feature in actionBonus Falls is the most common feature you will come across. When a winning combo lands, it disintegrates to let existing or new symbols fill in the gaps. This can lead to more winners off one spin and so on. What makes things even more interesting is that consecutive wins are subject to a multiplier that increases by x1 up to a maximum of x4 with each win.The glowing-eyed bad guy is the scatter and ties into the Bonus Falls feature. If 3 land on a payline, 8 Free Spins is awarded. If they land on other paylines during that spin or on consecutive Bonus Falls spins then they result in 2 more free spins - capped at 20. During the base game and free spins, the multiplier increases like so:Default – x1 during bonus game, x2 during free spins.1st Cascade – x2 during bonus game, x4 during free spins.2nd Cascade – x3 during bonus game, x6 during free spins.3rd Cascade – x4 during the bonus game, x8 during free spins.Like many new slots at the moment, North Storm is at its raging best when its extras combine in that fashion.North Storm: VerdictIf imitation is the sincerest form of flattery then North Storm will be make a few people blush right now. As well as Asgardian Stones, it has gameplay ported right from Jungle Jim, and if we go back a few steps, even the ghost of Gonzo’s Quest can be felt. No big deal, the entertainment industry is rife with borrowing ideas and finding inspiration in each other's work. As long as the new product isn’t an exact copy, from a legal standpoint, and builds on past endeavors to offer something new, we can live with it.Then again, imitation might be flattery, but it also rarely leads to greatness. What we get with North Storm is an entertaining game with decent potential, though one that will neither shake up the slots world nor win awards for originality. In Rabcat’s defense, it is unlikely they were aiming for either of these goals when they developed North Storm. Instead, it feels like they have leapt on a theme and game mechanic that are both super popular at the moment.Many could see this as a cynical cash grab, but Rabcat’s previous game history proves that this is a company that clearly enjoys creating fantasy themed slots. With that in mind it is easy to be a bit more lenient with the criticism, but still, this is the slots business and we all want bang for our buck. Taking all of that into consideration, North Storm has plenty of ticks in the pro column. The graphics are outstanding, symbols hold ok value, and the dynamic action of the Bonus Falls are dynamite when they roll together. Overall, it's a great looking game with strong appeal, but hardcore gamblers and veteran punters will be harder to please.

Title: China River
review: China River (Bally): OverviewWhen a slot comes along that is part of a progressive jackpot it raises a question. Does it rely solely on its prize to pull in players, thereby meaning the game itself is just an afterthought? When you see that Barcrest is the developer behind the latest placeholder game for the jackpot network, a cold sweat starts to break out over what might be in store. You never know what to expect. Like ripping off a Band-Aid, the best thing to do is just dive right in and see what we have to contend with.The original China River slot dates back to around 2014. Why Bally has decided to do try and revive such a bland and generic slot by releasing a remake we will never known. Either way, the first encounter with China River 2.0 elicited a surprisingly mild response. The graphics are okay-ish, nothing ground-breaking of course, but not an insult to the eyes. The 5x3 reel setup is located in a somewhat pleasant looking carnation bush. The music has that Chinese dizi flute, floating down the Yangtze River at dusk admiring the Three Gorges vibe to it. Aesthetically it has a certain level of tastefulness going on; it’s relaxing even. If first impressions are anything to go by, then China River is not going to be one of those high-octane, rip-roaring, slots. Hit spin, and so it proves to be.Before that though, bets need to be selected, and players can choose from 30 p/c to $/€30. Quick spin would have been a nice option because the reels are slower than Chinese internet download speeds thanks to all those firewalls. There are 30 paylines on which to land winning combinations of three or more of a kind. Perusing the paytable reveals a split between 6 low and 4 high. The low pays are 9-A royals which if you look close have delicate little Asian prints on them. The high pays are comprised of a frog, a golden bowl, a lotus flower, and a Chinese character. The character only needs two to be a winner, and if you land five the game will reward you with 33.33 times the stake.A couple of extras include a cute wee yellow bird symbol which is the wild. It can land on reels 2, 3, 4, and 5 and substitute for any of the pay symbols. When it does, you are treated to a nice animation of flowers and a boat on a river.Mathematically, the game has a theoretical RTP of 95.87% which is the new standard and what we've now come to expect following all the regulatory changes that have significantly impacted the industry. In terms of volatility, there is no official word on it but the game appears to run on a medium variance model.China River (Bally): FeaturesMain gameMost players will probably fire up China River to have a crack at the jackpot so let’s start with that. Mega Drop has 3 progressive jackpots which must be won before they reach set levels, these are Minor, Major, and Epic which are progressive and must drop before they reach 1,500, 20,000, or 200,000 credits respectively.There is no telling when they will be won, the process happens at random at any moment. When a jackpot has been won, it is reset to a seed amount of around 25% of the amount paid out. 2% of each bet goes to feed the three jackpots, and the process continues again. All three jackpots can be won while betting at any stake level; there is no restriction. But, the higher the stakes, the greater the chance of winning will be.The paytable mentions a mysterious Mystery Stacked Reels feature.
