What also contributes to this shift is the winding down of the math model and potential. It's an unusual move given the tendency for developers to go in the opposite direction on a sequel. While the previous two slots could hit 10,000x, Blinged makes do with just half the amount, so 5,000 times the stake max.At the end of the day, the changes mean Blinged plays to a different crowd, possibly a female audience. Put it this way; if the two slots were rappers, one would have grown up in Compton and released tracks from a Cell Block 8, while the other one cut their teeth on an X-Factor stage lip-syncing Vanilla Ice's solitary hit.

Title: Gods of Rock

Title: Book of Fusion

Title: Fortunes Of Ali Baba

Title: Nitropolis
review: Nitropolis: Slot OverviewIt’s easy to bemoan an apparent lack of original ideas when it comes to slot development. It sometimes seems there are a handful of studios out there blazing a trail while the rest are copying or adapting like wannabe clothes designers soaking up a fashion show. One studio boldly going where it hasn’t been before is ELK Studios in their unusual slot Nitropolis. In this world, four clans: the Dirty Dawgs, the Gritty Kitties, the Pug Thugs, and the Rouge Rats fight it out for green Nitro to fuel their cars. Quite what category operators will slide Nitropolis into will be interesting to see. Like Billy Corgan said about post-modernism ‘it is whatever the [heck] you want it to be.’Firing up the game for the first time it quickly dawns on you it's not your typical ELK offering, the 6-reel, 4,096 win way game area located in the industrial environment of Nitropolis. This is a city of the future, populated by animals, with sensational music that sounds like a Britpop/electronica potpourri, graduating to punk during the bonus game. A soundtrack so good it gives Nolimit City's Punk Rocker a run for its money, although that's from where Nitropolis most obviously draws most of its inspiration, both in terms of audiovisual design as well as its main mechanics. Either way, the genuinely eclectic mix of themes, ideas, and concepts works, coming together to form a unique game all the same.Nitropolis is playable on any device by setting bets from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, or by activating one of the betting strategies – Optimizer, Leveller, Booster, or Jumper. As to math model, the gaming is highly volatile, suiting the level of reward and type of features on offer. This is a thoroughly busy slot that can provide quite a lot of playtime, even if free spins can take time to trigger. It’s hard to tell statistically though since ELK rarely releases free spin frequency like they used to. Hit rate, on the other hand, is available, so at 19.8% you’re getting a win every five spins or thereabouts. Capping off stats is the agreeable figure of 96.1% for the RTP rate.Twelve regular symbols make up the paytable, divided into low, medium, and high pays. Combinations may be three to six symbols long, in any row from the first reel onwards. Since there are so many potential win ways possible in Nitropolis, the values of single combinations are much lower than usual. Six mid pays are worth 0.24x to 0.36x, while six high pays dole out 0.6x to 1x the stake. So yeah, not a whole lot. Fortunately, the features do allow plenty of room to go berserk. Lastly, we get a suspicious mushroom cloud wild, substituting for anything except the bonus symbol. During free spins, the wild also substitutes for the scatter symbol in a scatter win.Nitropolis: Slot FeaturesAt first, the features may seem confusing, but are actually more straight forward once you’ve read up on them or better yet, seen them in action a few times. First are Winning Respins which trigger after every win in the base or bonus game. All symbols involved in the winning combination spin again, potentially leading to new combinations. Respins continue until no new wins appear.Next are ELK's newly introduced and trademarked mechanic known as Nitro Reels™ which may appear in any reel. These symbols cover two positions and may contain 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12 symbols, affecting the number of win ways. The default 4,096 can get as ludicrously high as 85,155,840 at the most. Moreover, Nitro Reels can randomly upgrade win ways in between Respin and Free Spins. Also, there is a chance Nitro Reels will randomly spin again for a second chance when there are no additional wins.The highlight is the bonus game, triggered when 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols land in view during the base game to give you 10, 15, 20, or 25 spins respectively. Three or more bonus symbols in the feature retrigger the same number of spins.Now, before the feature starts, one symbol is randomly chosen to be the scatter paying symbol. Three or more scatter paying symbols on three or more different reels triggers a win. The main benefit, however, is the fact that Nitro Reels are sticky, remaining locked in place way for the full duration.Nitropolis: Slot VerdictAt first Nitropolis can be a little confusing. Without scrutinising the paytable first, it’s hard to tell what is going on. Even worse is triggering free spins before absorbing the rules, then you’re left wondering why you’re getting paid. The good news is Nitropolis isn’t as complicated as it initially comes across and nothing a few rounds won't overcome. Once you’ve mastered how Nitro Reels and Respins work, it becomes clear, not to mention fun.Of course there’s no way a slot like this won’t offend some people. Not everyone will be jazzed by the complex mix of Respins, Nitro Frames, and scatter pays symbols. Nitropolis is the antitheses of straight forward and classic gaming. It’s certainly not a slot you pop on to unwind with at 4 am. Even the theme was a daring choice, setting an adorable bunch of critters in a dystopian future where humanity appears to have been being wiped out, allowing other species to evolve intelligence, and thumbs. Or some such.While the gameplay has a healthy dose of originality, there are ghosts of other slots here too. Special symbol scatter pays have a Book of Ra/Danger! High Voltage feel to them, and Nitro Reels are undoubtedly reminiscent of Nolimit’s xWays mechanic. Still, as a whole, Nitropolis provides something new. It also provides solid potential, to the tune of 10,000 times the bet. You might think it would’ve been more though, given that over 85 million ways to win are possible, probably leaving some asking what the point of a gazillion win ways is when there are 9 payline slots that offer 10x the potential. Having said that, the potential is still enticing enough and higher than we're used to seeing from ELK, so no real complaints there.So after an excessive bout of deconstruction (Nitropolis is a game which inspires a level of critical analysis ), what’s left is a well-made, fun game with banging tunes. Strangely though, the bonus game feels weaker than it should as the scatter symbol approach just didn't add enough excitement and explosivity. A multiplier in its place could possibly have worked better.The features might not be as original as they first appear to be, but that doesn't stop the Nitropolis from being entertaining. They all come together to form a unique game, boasting big potential, genuinely entertaining moments, drenched in an industrial post-punk attitude, and pugs.

Title: Mahjong 88

Triggered randomly on a losing spin, here's what you can expect:Spring - can give you up to 12 wilds randomly appearing on the grid.Summer -  can give you up to 5 wilds while also destroying adjacent symbols.Autumn -  can give you up to 11 wilds with symbols destroyed from edges or turning wild.Winter -  can give you up to 4 wilds that stick even if part of a winning combination.Each season will last between 25 and 99 spins and go from spring to summer to autumn and then finally winter before starting over again. Consequently, the result is a slot with a rather dull and cluttered theme with eye-straining tiles along with a backing track so shooting there's a real risk of falling asleep. Title: Jolly Dicers
review: Jolly Dicers: OverviewJolly Dicers is a quirky online slot brought out by Dice Lab, the company that cannot get enough of the six-sided gaming objects. This is their second slot to be featured on our site, following on from the oddly playable Sugar Cubes. That charming wee game was a little different, but not a bad alternative for some light entertainment. Their second release, Jolly Dicers, is an even more acquired taste than the debut. Safe to say, it's probably unlike anything you've ever seen before.Jolly Dicers is definitely not without its intriguing aspects with a massive potential possibly the central plank in its allure. If you’re ready to discover the delights of rolling dice on a rolling ship at sea, all aboard.Deciding whether you like Jolly Dicers or not begins with the game’s look. Graphics and animations have a sort of bobbing effect, reminiscent of noughties PC games like Tales of Monkey Island, or Age of Booty at a stretch. Play takes place on the deck of a ship, and there is a lot going on. To start with, symbols tumble into a 4x4 inner grid which is surrounded by a 1x1 outer grid containing special symbols. Below this 6x6 matrix, a captain and his mate turn wheels on each spin to get the symbols moving. It’s kind of neat and bears some resemblance to NetEnt's Finn and the Swirly Spin, but it's also easy to see how it might annoy people as well. There is so much moving on screen it would have been nice if players had the option to switch off animations. Just a suggestion, others might love the extra atmosphere it all provides.Before ordering the pirates to animate reels, setting bets is up. Hit the coin icon to do so and choose between 10 p/c and $/€100 per spin. Auto spin is available, but keep in mind that even when activated, free spins must be played manually. While we are on stats, there are a few to get through. RTP is interesting and comes in at 96.39% during the base game, which isn't too bad to begin with, but gets a massive boost to 97.5% during the Gamble Game (which we will look at below). Finally, volatility is quite high as well getting a 4/5 rating on Dice Labs Richter scale, so be prepared for some cold swings in between the hits.Winners are formed when 4 or more matching symbols are touching vertically or horizontally. When a cluster hits, it is removed from the grid to let new symbols fall into the spaces for extra chances to win. Regular pay symbols are the six sides of a dice 1-6, designed in different coloured bits of wood. The bigger the number, the bigger the reward, and payouts range from 4 ‘ones’ at 0.4x the stake to 16 ‘sixes’ at 9.6 times the stake. There is also a wild that moves along the Orbiting mechanism during the base game. It can stand in for any dice symbol to complete a cluster.Jolly Dicers: FeaturesFree spins gameJolly Dicers rely heavily on its extra modifiers to provide the entertainment and action. During the base game, there are 4 different of them that can help boost your winnings:Magic Potion - When two magic potion symbols sit directly opposite each other horizontally or vertically, the dice symbols in between them are changed into the highest value symbol.Bombs - When two bomb symbols appear directly opposite each other the dice symbols in between them are destroyed, and the value of each symbol is added up and paid out.Cutlass - Two cutlasses opposite each other destroy the low pay dice symbols 1, 2, and 3, causing a payout of their combined values.Pistol - Two matching cutlasses opposite each other destroy the high pay 4, 5, and 6 dice symbols triggering a payout of their values.The highlight is the Free Spins bonus game, however. When 2 scatter coin symbols land opposite each other on the Orbiting Reel they award 6 free spins. This bonus game consists of a 4x4 grid using the same dice symbols as the base game. At the start of each spin, two dice are rolled, and the numbers they reveal are removed from the next spin to increase the chances of winning. If a double lands, say 2 sixes, the six symbols are removed and one additional spin is added. The bonus game also comes with a multiplier that starts at x1 and increases by +1 for each cascade. The multiplier resets with each new spin.The last feature is the Gamble Game and the place where it things can go nuts. It is unlocked when 6 consecutive cascades occur during the base game or free spins. The action shifts to a poor soul walking the plank. Players roll dice and can win up to 6x the gambled amount with up to three consecutive gambles being the maximum.Jolly Dicers: VerdictJolly Dicers was a tricky game to review. The whole package takes time to get to grips with and form a solid opinion about what’s on offer as it comes across as a bit of a mess in the beginning. It’s clear the game was a passion project for the team and the extra bits and animations can take a while to warm to. One example is the clunky way the Orbiting Reel moves special symbols around. No doubt, it was made that way to simulate a rickety rope system, but it can be a bit distracting initially. The same goes for the two pirates turning the reels. So far both of Dice Lab’s slots take a demo or two to get a real feel for them.If you’re on the fence about whether to try the game, then the potential might help sway you. Then again, it might not. Like a lot about Jolly Dicers, there is a twist involved. To explain, the max win via the base game + free spins won’t get hearts fluttering at 533 times the bet. Yet, like RTP, the potential gets a major boost in the Gamble Game. Max out the Gamble Game and winnings from the base game + free spins can be multiplied by up to 216x (6x6x6). This works out at total wins of up to a staggering 115,528 times the bet. An astronomical amount, probably only matched by astronomical odds. As impressive as those numbers may be, it's very likely that the max payout will be capped.To sum up, Jolly Dicers has it's not so great aspects - it can come across as too complex, like it's trying too hard, which may put some players off. But, there are positives to Jolly Dicers that take longer to appreciate. For one, gamblers that want to go large might get a kick out of the Gamble Game. Jolly Dicers is different, and conjures up some nice pirating atmosphere, though it's harder to fall for than Sugar Cubes was. Good on Dice Lab for trying something different though and the end result will definitely appeal to some players more than others.

Title: Duel At Dawn
review: Duel At Dawn: Slot OverviewIn the battle royale that is the online slot Wild Western category, many enter, few make it to the top. One Western slot which did make an impact on the genre was Hacksaw Gaming's Wanted Dead or a Wild. Moody oil painting visuals, exciting breadth of gameplay, and a powerful x-factor helped make it stand out from the rest. The studio revisited the dusty Ol' West again in 2 Wild 2 Die, and like a persistent hombre hopped up on sarsaparilla that just won't stay down, the studio is back for more pew-pew on the frontier action in Duel At Dawn.Duel At Dawn don't make the friendliest first impression. That would be on account of the Outlaw pointing his pistol directly at the player, on a downward angle, as if the viewer is on their knees in the dust pleading for their life. The visuals are closer to 2 Wild 2 Die than Wanted, being more realistic than stylistic, and are in some ways less striking because of this art direction. Then again, the visuals are solid enough, and that gunman brings the menace as he accompanies players through all phases of the game.Duel At Dawn slot - base gameA total of 19 ways to win are built into Duel At Dawn's 5-reel, 5-row gaming matrix. With a medium-high 4 out of 5 rated volatility to be aware of, Duel At Dawn's highest available RTP clocks in at 96.3%.Literal J, Q, K, and A playing cards are Duel At Dawn's low-pay symbols. They all award 1x the bet for a 5 OAK winning line. After the cards are cartwheels, skulls, hats, pistols, and sheriff badges, worth 3 to 10 times the bet for a 5 OAK win. Wilds may appear on any reel to replace any of the regularly paying symbols in a winning combination. An all wild 5 OAK pays 10x the bet.Duel At Dawn: Slot FeaturesDuel At Dawn slot - Wild Wild West featureThe heat Duel At Dawn is packing is DuelReels, The Outlaw Feature, a Wild Wild West bonus, a Dusk 'Til Dawn bonus, and bonus buys.DuelReelsWhen a VS symbol hits, it expands into a wild DuelReel if it would become part of the win once expanded. After expanding, a duel takes place on each reel. Each DuelReel has two multipliers of x2 to x200 connected to the Outlaw and the Sheriff. Whoever wins the duel applies their multiplier across the whole reel, affecting any wins the DuelReel is part of. If more than one DuelReel is part of the same win, their multipliers are added together before being applied. Only one VS symbol may land per reel, and DuelReels are wild.The Outlaw FeatureWhen an Outlaw symbol lands, it expands to become a full wild Outlaw reel, displaying a revolver with 1 to 6 bullets in the chamber. The number of bullets represents the number of wild symbols the Outlaw shoots onto the grid. If more than one Outlaw is on the reels, they cannot shoot wilds onto the same positions, and they can't shoot each other. Up to 2 Outlaw symbols may appear on a spin, one per reel. Each Outlaw reel also has a multiplier of x2 to x200, which applies to any win they are part of. If more than one Outlaw reel is part of the same win, their multipliers are added together before being applied.Wild Wild WestLanding 3 FS scatters in the base game awards 10 free Wild Wild West spins. This feature has the same mechanics as the base game, but there is an increased chance of getting high-value multipliers on DuelReels and Outlaw reels. There is also a greater chance of landing VS and Outlaw symbols. Hitting 2 scatters grants a further +2 free spins, while 3 scatters grant an extra +4 free spins.Dusk 'Til DawnLanding 4 FS scatters in the base game awards 10 free Dusk 'Til Dawn spins. In this feature, it is possible to earn 4 DuelSpins with guaranteed VS symbols. Each DuelSpin is unlocked by landing Outlaw symbols and shooting 6 wild symbols onto the grid. This doesn't have to be at the same time. Each DuelSpin is awarded after the spin it was unlocked on and doesn't count as one of the awarded free spins. Up to 2 DuelSpins can be unlocked on one spin.Moreover, multiplier DuelSpins are awarded in sequence before moving to the next free spin. Each subsequent DuelSpin awards more guaranteed VS symbols. The first guarantees at least 2 VS symbols, the second guarantees at least 3 VS symbols, the third guarantees at least 4 VS symbols, and the fourth guarantees 5 VS symbols. Each unlocked DuelSpin also awards +3 free spins. VS symbols do not appear in this bonus, except during DuelSpins.Bonus BuyDuel At Dawn's arsenal of bonus buys includes the following: BonusHunt FeatureSpins (3x the bet) - Each spin is 5 times more likely to trigger free spins, Deadly Duels FeatureSpins (60x the bet) - Each spin guarantees at least 2 VS symbols land. FS scatters do not land in this mode, Lone Outlaw FeatureSpins (60x the bet) - Each spin guarantees at least 1 Outlaw symbol with at least 2 bullets lands. FS symbols do not land in this mode, Wild Wild West Bonus (100x the bet), or Dusk 'Til Dawn Bonus (200x the bet).Duel At Dawn slot - Dusk 'Til Dawn featureDuel At Dawn: Slot VerdictWell, pardner, Hacksaw Gaming sure does know how to craft an engaging Western slot, no doubt. Looping back for a bit, one reason Wanted Dead or a Wild stuck out is because, till that point, Hacksaw Gaming had mostly pushed out cutey games like Cash Compass or Hop 'N' Pop. Since then, the studio has turned to the dark side on numerous occasions, Hand of Anubis and Rotten being two memorable examples, and the team has shown it is equally adept at making dense slots as it is at pushing out easy-going Pocketz stuff. Another thing the developer excels at is coming up with a good idea then finessing that idea over subsequent releases, which is something we've seen numerous times in the past and we see again in Duel At Dawn.This is no bad thing because features like the return of VS symbols and shooting wild bullets can be quite a thrill. They're able to play their roles rather well in the base game, for starters, where the full reel wild multiplier Outlaw symbol, in conjunction with shooting wilds, can lead to a lot of wildness on the reels. If 2 Outlaws happen to land, which probably won't be a super regular occurrence, you best be diving for cover. VS symbols have proven their worth since Warrior Ways dropped them on the scene, and they work every bit as well here. The Wild Wild West bonus round stirs the pot by theoretically upping the chances of landing better stuff, while Dusk 'Til Dawn pushes things even further along the idea-finessing track. Key to keep in mind is that while 6 shot wilds are needed to win a DuelSpin, you don't have to fire all 6 in one go, but rather, the chamber-emptying progress is saved as it goes. No need to mention how desirable getting all 5 VS symbols on the reels would be.A 15,000x the bet win cap is one of the final layers of icing on Duel At Dawn, but equally exciting is the way the game can drop into full shootout mode at any point. There is no guarantee it will do so, of course, but Hacksaw, being Hacksaw, has imbued Duel At Dawn with the sort of quick or the shot to bits features the studio is famed for.

Title: Animal Madness
review: Animal Madness: Slot OverviewPlay'n GO might be well known for creating darkly themed slots, rock games, big freaky grid slots, or joker games (amongst others). However, Animal Madness marks at least the third time the studio has headed out of town to make a farm-themed slot. Animal Madness might be mechanically different from its forebears since it's a cluster paying grid slot, yet it's as heavily steeped in farm life, perhaps more so.A sweeping orchestral score opens the game, revealing a pastoral setting which is both inviting and a little intimidating at the same time. Animal Madness is a cute game full of cute characters, yet the sky is ominously dark, and is that a storm forming in the background? Hitting spin drops 25 symbols onto a 5x5 game panel, forming a win when at least 4 matching symbols are connecting in vertical or horizontal directions. Not a massive game, though a medium volatile one, which can hit its full winning potential on a single spin due to the inclusion of a cascade feature. This removes winning symbols from the reels and lets new ones drop down to close the gaps. Cascades continue until no new wins hit, feeding a math model that has a theoretical return value of 96.20%.Players get eight pay symbols to make wins with, split between low pay crops and high pay livestock. A variety of wild symbols may be added to the reels via the features; all wild types are able to substitute for any of the pay symbols to help build clusters.Animal Madness: Slot FeaturesWhen a winning cluster is removed from the game board, it zooms into the mouth of a sunflower sitting next to the grid. After a certain number of cascades have been collected, a modifier is added to the board, like so:3 consecutive cascades trigger Wild Chickens – three 1x2 wild symbols are added to the reels.6 consecutive cascades trigger the Wild Goat – a 2x3 wild symbol is placed on the grid.9 consecutive cascades trigger Wild Sheep – two 2x2 wild symbols are added to the grid + symbols are upgraded.12 consecutive cascades trigger Wild Cow – a 3x3 sized wild is placed on the reels.One more feature is Rabbit Mayhem, awarded randomly on any non-winning spin. When active, random symbols are removed from the play area, triggering a cascade.Animal Madness: Slot VerdictFew studios have as much expertise at designing grid slots as Play'n GO has, and Animal Madness is quite different to most others they've done. It doesn't follow the usual template of collecting winning symbols to charge a meter, though when you think about it, collecting consecutive cascades to trigger features is pretty much the same thing. The difference between this and most Play'n GO grid slots is the lack of an ultimate bonus round. Even a relatively toned-down grid slot like Lordi Reel Monsters fired off a potentially devastating free spin when a collection sequence was complete. As the saying goes, variety is the spice of life, and some players may actually prefer this method.Without a long-term goal like triggering a bonus round, Animal Madness does have a treadmill-like quality made up of sprints when the features trigger and jogging on the spot for much of the rest the time. What makes it entertaining, for a while at least, is that the hits do come pretty thick and fast. This led to quite frequent feature triggers, though getting past the second level wasn't easy. Also, the Rabbit Mayhem feature wasn't super rare either, which clears a few pesky symbols out of the way while feeding the sunflower in the process. What's good about the wild symbol placement features is they pretty much guarantee a win when they are added to the grid. This means two things - you get some cash, and the cascades roll on. What's also good is that at the upper end of the paytable, payouts can be substantial. At best, it's possible to win up to 2,250x the bet when playing Animal Madness.To use the treadmill analogy again, after pounding out the miles, eventually, you just want to step off, whether from exhaustion or boredom and there comes a time when Animal Madness' frenzy starts to wear thin. Till that happens, though, there's some carefree gaming to be had for the right player, amidst a flurry of cute animal antics.

Title: Super Lion Megaways

Title: Knight Fight
review: Knight Fight: Slot OverviewSwedish software provider ELK Studios has turned out bundles of excitingly innovative online slots over the years, from the Gold games, the Nitropolis series, to the Toro lineup. One popular set of slots from the studio stars a gaggle of feisty avian entities in the team's Pirots range - to date, three of them have been released. When you're on to a good thing in the gambling industry, it makes a certain business sense to ride it out until the wheels fall off before abandoning the project for something new. In the spirit of squeezing extra mileage out of an entertaining concept comes Knight Fight, a revival of ELK Studios' CollectR mechanic and a reskin of Pirots 2.Knight Fight is not the first time ELK Studios has tangled with the medieval world. An earlier example was the cluster pays slot Micro Knights, and if you go back to take a look, the characters in both games are rather similar to each other, particularly that purple dragon. The same eccentric spirit has returned, gelling perfectly with the already eccentric nature of the Pirots games. Like Print Studios' Holy Hand Grenade, Knight Fight has a look and feel that isn't a million miles away from something Monty Python might have done if they'd been in the business of making slots. There's even a goat in this game, too.Knight Fight slot - base gameHitting the spin button, after picking a stake of 10 c to $/100, drops symbols and 4 collector knights onto a 6x6 gaming area. Knight Fight does not use lines, ways, scatter pays, or clusters to make wins. Instead, it relies on its CollectR mechanic and its 4 knights to travel around the board, where able, to collect pay symbols, feature symbols, and the like. As before, volatility is high, and the RTP is 94%, even when using the X-iter feature buys.Knights collect crest pay symbols to award their values. There are four types of crest symbols; each type may be collected by a knight of the same colour. Crest symbols come in 7 value levels. The lowest levels are worth 0.05 to 0.1 times the bet; the highest is 10 to 50 times the bet. Wilds substitute for pay symbolsKnight Fight: Slot FeaturesKnight Fight slot - free spinsKnight Fight has 4 knight collector symbols that move around the reels in descending order of symbol value. Each knight is linked to a crest symbol of the same colour. Knights collect adjacent crest symbols of the same colour and feature symbols by moving orthogonally around the board. After all possible symbols have been collected, new symbols are dropped in to fill the gaps, pricing another chance for collecting. This means knights can move more than once on the same spin, including before a refill. Collecting a feature symbol triggers the symbol's feature.Symbol Collection MeterThe symbol collection meter keeps track of collected crest and wild symbols. The meter keeps collecting until the knights can't collect any more symbols. When the meter is full, one pending feature symbol release is added. Up to 3 feature symbol releases may be stacked at the same time. All stacked feature symbol releases are awarded at the same time. Feature symbol releases are awarded just before the goat turns evil, before the dragon flame strikes, as part of the first free spin, or when knights can't collect any more symbols. A feature symbol release converts a number of random crest symbols into random feature symbols. Aside from Scatters and Wilds, feature symbol types are:Coins - a collected coin symbol pays its displayed value. The MAX WIN coin awards the remaining amount needed to hit the maximum win.Upgrade Symbols - upgrades by 1-3 levels the payout level of crest symbols of the same colour as the knight that collected the upgrade symbol, up to 7. Collected upgrade all symbols upgrade all four crest symbols.Goat Symbols - when collected by a knight, it turns evil at the end of the spin when no more symbols can be collected. The knights are scared away from the grid, dropping them in new places.Transform Symbols - when collected, it transforms a cluster of crest symbols next to the knight into the same colour as the collecting knight. It may convert a random number of crest symbols into feature symbols.Golden Apple Basket Symbols - places Apples in empty spaces when collected. Knights can then cross these empty spaces one time each to reach symbols.Dragon Egg - a dragon egg or a dragon flame symbol collected by a knight triggers a dragon flame strike at the end of the spin when no more symbols can be collected. It removes knights and any symbols except feature symbols in close proximity to it, causing a redrop to fill the gaps. The dragon flame strike expands the grid up to 8x8. A collected Goat will trigger before a collected Dragon Egg.Adjacent knights may perform a Switcheroo where they swap places vertically or horizontally when they can collect more symbols. It may only happen if new clusters of symbols can be unlocked. If 3 or more knights end up horizontally and/or vertically next to each other, they fight on a random area of the grid. Scatters, coins, goats, and dragon egg symbols in the fight's path are collected, while crest symbols are removed. Knights redrop when the fight is over. A symbol drop refills the empty spaces.Free SpinsIf 3 scatter symbols are collected on a spin, 5 free spins are awarded. Free spins start with the current active number of rows and reels. The current collection meter progress is brought over, and any pending feature symbol releases are triggered on the first free spin. The grid size, progress on the symbol collection meter, payout level of crest symbols, and collection of scatter symbols are persistent in free spins. Collecting 3 scatter symbols awards additional free spins.X-iterKnight Fight's X-iter offers these bonus buys:Bonus Hunt - one spin with 4x the chance of triggering free spins for 3x the bet.Golden Apple Feast - one spin with the Golden Apple Basket feature triggered from the start for 10x the bet.Maximum Grid Size - one spin played with the maximum grid size for 25x the bet.Bonus - 100x the bet.Super Bonus - 500x the bet. All free spins are played with the maximum grid size, and all upgrade symbols upgrade all crest symbols.Knight Fight slot - free spinsKnight Fight: Slot VerdictNot sure what the initial expectations of Knight Fight were, but they weren't of a Pirots 2 reskin. ELK Studios isn't particularly big on clones and reskins, preferring to let their prodigious talent for taking players to new and exciting players pour forth in uniquely individual games. Oh sure, ELK has no qualms about running a series out over the course of years or making twists and turns to successful gameplay, but rarely do they bring back the exact same set of mechanics covered in a game world it's arguably explored before. This is not a complaint, a rage into the wind over the unfairness of life, but rather just an observation, ruminating on Knight Fight's family tree.Knights, after all, could pull out family trees called pedigrees to show who was the first in the family to attain a coat of arms. Knight Fight relies heavily on its 4 knights to drive the action, and the chaps here have about as much personality as the 4 parrots of the Pirots game did, being humorous to watch in action, darting about the grid, collecting stuff, getting into fisticuffs. As before, symbol upgrades are critical to getting solid wins. As are coins. So much so that there is a wonder how (or if) Knight Fight's 10,000x top prize is achievable without collecting the MAX WIN coin.As it often is, the second time around wasn't as thrilling as the first, but Knight Fight was at least almost as entertaining as Pirots 2. You could say that technically, it is almost impossible not to be since the same features and gameplay have been brought over. The end result is a slot that's about on par with the game it was made from, not as must-see, let's say, but still a charming romp through the Middle Ages, collecting stuff along the way.

Title: 10,000 Wonders MultiMax
review: 10,000 Wonders Multimax: Slot OverviewLike the grand old Duke of York and his 10,000 men, developer ReelPlay has trundled out its favourite 5-digit number for the online slot 10,000 Wonders Multimax, a descendent of 10,000 Wonders 10K Ways. The total multiplier for use in a winning combination is the product of all multipliers above reels containing winning symbols. The win for the combination is multiplied by the total multiplier.Bonus RespinsThe bonus respins round is triggered by landing at least 6 Lamp symbols. The round completes when no more respins remain or all possible positions are filled by Lamp symbols.When complete, each Lamp symbol awards a prize or a bonus prize. Possible bonus prizes are the 10x Red Diamond, 50x Pink Diamond, 250x Green Diamond, or the 2,000x Blue Diamond, while the non-bonus prizes range from 1 to 100 times the bet. The prize or bonus prize per Lamp is multiplied by the Multimax Multiplier of the reel it landed on. Lastly, if all reel positions are filled with Lamp symbols, players are awarded a 10,000x the bet 10K Bonus.Feature BuyPlayers may choose to buy the Bonus Respins feature, where a spin is played that results in 6 Lamp symbols. The choices are 50x the bet for Bonus Respins with 0-3 multiplier upgrades (RTP 96.7%), 75x the bet for Bonus Respins with 3-6 multiplier upgrades (RTP 96.8%), or 100x the bet for Bonus Respins with 6-10 multiplier upgrades (RTP 96.9%). Each upgrade adds 1 to the multiplier for a random reel.10,000 Wonders MultiMax slot - bonus buy options10,000 Wonders Multimax: Slot VerdictFrom memory, this is the first time Multimax has gotten jiggy with a hold 'n win, streak respin, style bonus round. One interesting result of this is that because ReelPlay has shrunk the grid and ways to win down, the 10,000 from the title no longer links to the number of ways to win but to the 10K bonus prize instead. To activate that Alladin's cave of loot requires filling the grid with Lamp symbols, and since the grid has shrunk to a 5x3 number, it doesn't seem like a monumental challenge - in theory. In practice, well, good luck if you decide to take up the 10,000 Wonders Multimax chase.Why would a wide-eyed, hopeful gambler choose to do so? One reason might be to sample what a Multimax slot with a streak respin feature has to offer. In some ways, this is a relatively unique coming together of features; in some ways, it could also be argued that a game like iSoftBet's Aztec Gold Megaways provides similar, though not exactly the same, sort of action. Perhaps a big number was a requirement so as to not dilute the Multimax reputation.That's a reputation built predominantly by MultiFly! since following releases haven't really wowed as the original did. 10,000 Wonders Multimax didn't hugely wow either, but there are certain creative ideas attached, and it is arguably a more desirable game than 10,000 Wonders 10K Ways was.

Title: Gems of Adoria

Title: Wild Frames
review: Wild Frames (Play'n GO): OverviewWild Frames is the latest addition to Play'n GO’s collection of grid slots. This one combines the modern features and gameplay we have come to expect from the series with a classic fruit slot vibe and symbols. Previous grid slots from Play'n GO had the ability to get some great rolls on when the cluster system did its thing with the cascading wins mechanic. Mix in a bunch of features and modifiers such as the Charge Meter and the volatility is matched only by the payout potential. Wild Frames might look and feel different, but fans will be relieved to hear that, at its core, it retains everything that made previous grid slots so successful. On paper this is a promising prospect indeed, let’s see how it plays out.Graphically, Wild Frames is not quite as instantly appealing as previous versions such as Honey Rush or Black Mamba. Its 7x7 grid is full of classic slot symbols which sit against a fairly plain background made up of various purple tones and geometric shapes. It’s pleasing, in a minimalist way, but once the action kicks off in earnest you won’t even notice it. The horizontal bar along the bottom lets players select bet levels from 20 p/c up to $/€100 per spin, and like other similar slots, there aren’t paylines as such. Instead, winning combinations are formed when similar symbols land next to each other horizontally or vertically in clusters.Key stats include volatility which is as high is it gets with a 10/10 rating from Play'n GO. Slots providers have some control over the RTP which can vary from casino to casino, but will usually be set to either 94.5% or 96.5%. This being the case, make sure to check the paytable at your local online casino to find out which one you are using for best value.As mentioned, symbols come straight out of the old school fruit slots play book. There are 8 base game symbols – big bright card suits, diamonds, clubs, hearts, and spades, followed by equally bold bells, stars, diamonds and lucky 7’s. At least 5 of a kind in a cluster are needed to spark a payout, and when they do, they vanish off the screen. New symbols tumble into the gaps which can spark of cascades of clusters and wins from a single spin. This is a common enough mechanic at the moment and one that suits this 7x7 grid style perfectly. The most valuable pay symbol is the ‘7’ - get 30 or more of them in a cluster and you’ve scored a solid 500 times the stake right there.Wild Frames (Play'n GO): FeaturesHelping with the rollercoaster gameplay are several features that work off of each other. The first is the glitzy golden ‘W’ Wild symbol. The game isn’t called Wild Frames for nothing, and the Wild is a critical element of the game. When Wilds turn up they create a sticky frame on that specific position. If they land where there is already an existing frame they upgrade it with a Progressive Multiplier that starts at x1 and goes up to x9. Keep in mind that all of these frames build up but they remain inactive until the Wild Frames feature is triggered. Another key point, is that after a non-winning spin, 4-6 Wild symbols can be randomly added to the grid.Like other Play n’ Go grid slots we get a Charge Meter next to the play area. Whenever a winning symbol lands it adds 1 charge to the meter. When the meter hits 20, 40, or 60 charges, then each of these levels triggers the Transform, Wildcard, and Shatter features respectively. They modify the grid like so:Transform changes all high pay symbols (the non-card suits) into one common high pay symbol.Wildcard sprinkles 3-6 Wilds onto the grid at random.Shatter removes all the card suit symbols from the grid.If the Charge Meter reaches the full 80 charges then the Wild Frames feature is triggered. Now all frames on the grid are activated, including multiplier frames, and symbols that were sitting in one become wild. When winning clusters with multiplier frames form, the highest multiplier will be applied to it. For every 10 charges over 80, 2 additional frames are randomly added to the grid. The Wild Frames feature ends when no more winning clusters fall.Wild Frames (Play'n GO): VerdictVisually, Wild Frames is not all that exciting although its well put together. The theme is generic and not nearly as original as some of the other grid slot offerings from Play'n GO. From a marketing point of view, the classic look might of course win some new fans over that are otherwise put off by this type of 'modern' gameplay. Mechanically, on the other hand, it's everything you've come to expect from these grid slots.To get the most out of Wild Frames you will need the game to prolong cascades as long as possible. Strike it lucky and a major snowballing effect occurs. The Charge meter fills up, more features are unleashed on the grid, and more frames are added. Hit the main Wild Frame feature when the 80 symbols clear and some insane wins can pop along - there are plenty of online videos demonstrating this phenomenon with previous grid slots. There is plenty at to play for too, with the ability to hit up to 7,000 times the stake. Action Spins are another way of playing Land Of The Free at a brisker pace than usual.Land Of The Free slot - Titan SpinLand Of The Free: Slot VerdictNolimit City is no stranger to controversy, but they have really outdone themselves this time. Land Of The Free is either the funniest sh*t you've seen on the reels in a long time or the most offensive. Reactions may vary depending on what part of the world players reside in, maybe not. Title: Monsters Unchained
review: Monsters Unchained: Slot OverviewIf there were monsters in the world, in the fantastical sense of the word, the last thing anyone would want to do is unchain them, right? That is unless the person in question is bent on world destruction or at least terrorising portions of the general population with creatures with big pointy claws and supernatural powers. Where were we? Oh yeah, in Monsters Unchained, an online slot from Red Tiger, players will want to unchain these beasties as much as possible. The reason why is because the three monsters in the game each bring a different modifier to the table, and unchaining them as much as possible can lead to greater potency in their effects.The setting for Monsters Unchained is a dank, heavy location, a sort of oubliette, where people, things, or… monsters are put and forgotten about. Like a mediaeval dungeon set deep in the bowels of a castle, all metal grating, thick stone walls, flaming torches, bones, and unsavoury sour water. An ideal spot to host a game where the monsters are the Minotaur, Medusa, and Cerberus, the 3 headed dog. Three characters from Greek Mythology who are no strangers to the iGaming realm. Each one sits next to the game grid with a meter that is filled when certain Chain Breaker symbols hit; the full process will come clear very soon.Monsters Unchained slot - base gameFirst, a bit of bookkeeping and Monsters Unchained is a highly volatile slot with a higher than usual RTP for Red Tiger of right on 96%. It's played on a dynamic reel set, which utilises 5 reels, 3 rows and 243 ways to win by default, but it can grow when the Minotaur is unchained. Bet selection begins at 10 p/c and rises to $/€10 per spin.Winning ways are created when matching symbols land anywhere on adjacent reels, from the leftmost reel onwards. Monsters Unchained has 9 regular paying symbols; 5 of them are 10-A card rank low pays, the rest are a shackle, an axe, a lamp, and a chest of gold. Hitting a 5-of-a-kind winning way puts a win of 0.4 to 0.8 times the bet for the lows or 1 to 3 times the bet for the highs in your pocket. Wilds only appear as a result of the Medusa modifier, substituting for any paying symbol.Monsters Unchained: Slot FeaturesMonsters Unchained slot - Chainbreaker Dog feature in actionMonsters Unchained has a base game which is played in cycles of 10 spins. For the first 9 spins in the cycle, when Chain Breaker symbols land, they are collected in their respective Monsters' meters. Meters contain 3 steps, and breaking a monster's chain completes 1 step of the meter. On the 10th spin, the monsters with at least 1 of their chains broken will trigger their corresponding feature on that spin. The more broken chains, the more potent the monsters' features will be. After the 10th spin, the meters are cleared for the next cycle of spins.Three types of Chain Breaker symbols may land – red, green, and blue, and they appear on all spins except the 10th. Only 1 Chain Breaker may land on a spin, and up to 3 Chain Breaker symbols of a specific type may land in a cycle of 10 spins:Minotaur - The Minotaur's chains are broken by the red Chain Breaker symbol. On the 10th spin, the reels expand to 5x4, 5x5, or 6x5, with 1,024, 3,125, or 15,625 ways to win for 1, 2, or 3 destroyed chains, respectively.Medusa - Medusa's chains are broken by landing the green Chain Breaker symbol. On the 10th spin, Medusa adds 2 or 3, 4 or 5, or 6 or 7 wilds to the reels for 1, 2, or 3 destroyed chains, respectively. Wilds will not be placed on the first or last reels, regardless of grid size.Cerberus - The blue Chain Breaker symbol breaks Cerberus' chains. On the 10th spin, Cerberus adds a win multiplier of x2 or x3, x4 or x5, or x6 or x7 when 1, 2, or 3 of its chains have respectively been broken.Monster SpinsHit 3 Monster scatters on reels 1, 3, and 5 and 10 free spins are triggered. Scatters do not land on the 10th spin of a cycle, nor do they land on free spins. Any broken chains in the base game are not carried over to the bonus round.When a chain is broken in the free spins round, its effect begins from the next free spins onwards. The reel expansion and win multiplier remain active, while Medusa will add wilds on random positions on each spin till the feature ends. Breaking all of a monster's chains awards +3 free spins, meaning it is possible to win 19 at the most. When the feature ends, players return to the base game and continue the chain status where it was left off.Monsters Unchained slot - free spinsMonsters Unchained: Slot VerdictFor a dip into mythology's scarier side, Monsters Unchained has a few neat things to offer gamblers in a mood for monsters. Naturally, it'll be a better fit for those who like games that roll over set batches of spins, storing up modifiers for use on the final spin of the cycle. It's not a hugely numerous mechanic, but it's one that rears up from time to time and which Red Tiger has put to good use here - for a number of reasons. One is the monster angle, which ties neatly into the unchaining idea, and the whole look of Monsters Unchained has been done to the typically high Red Tiger visual standard.Another nifty thing about the setup is that it's got three distinct features rather than one. For example, the 9 nine spins don't just frame positions where certain symbols hit, then drop a wild onto them for the 10th spin. Instead, it may be possible, with a bit (or a lot) or luck, to have 3 very useful modifiers unchained on the last spin of a cycle - expanded reels and ways, win multipliers, as well as added wilds. Quite intoxicating when you think of the possibilities, adding a compelling element to the base game. As usual, free spins are where the game is most likely going to really flex due to the persistent nature given to the features. All on a ways to win gaming grid which is nice, too, and good for wins as high as 10,500 times the bet.With features that can get better the more they are unchained and a sweet interplay of gaming components, Monsters Unchained delivered an entertaining adventure through the bowels of a dungeon with three terrifying yet potentially rewarding monsters on our tail. On the other hand, those who are not into progression/collection-type slots of any kind are unlikely to be won over by this game either.

Title: Fruit Smash
review: Fruit Smash: Slot OverviewAs far as first impressions go, a name like Fruit Smash is unlikely to get too many players hot with anticipation – unless they are hardcore fruities. However, Slotmill's Fruit Smash is far from being a run-of-the-mill old school slot machine. Instead, Fruit Smash serves up solid, if slightly copy-cat, scatter paying action in an Avalanche-style slot with big potential multipliers that just happens to use fruit for most of its imagery.It wouldn't be a major surprise to find out Slotmill had been playing one or two Hacksaw Gaming slots when they developed Fruit Smash. The game just has that feel to it. When its natural delights load, players find themselves in a glowing green bush next to a 6x6 sized panel, covered in all manner of healthy snacks. Initially, Fruit Smash gave off a sort of coy innocence through its disarming visuals and extremely chipper soundtrack, though it can be anything but once the fruit starts tumbling. One nice touch is the interesting facts that pop up on the home screen. For example, did you know strawberries are the only fruit with seeds on the outside? You do now.One reason for Fruit Smash's capricious mood swings is a highly volatile math model, which generates a theoretical return to player value of 96.19%. The game is available on any device and lets players select stakes of 10 p/c to $/€50 per spin - that is if you choose to play Fruit Smash in regular mode (or don't have a choice) because it may also come with Burst Mode and three Fast Track options, covered below.Landing eight or more matching symbols anywhere on the grid creates a win, which then gets removed from the grid by the Avalanche mechanic. New or remaining symbols fall down into the gaps, and if a new win is created, another Avalanche is triggered. Normal pay symbols are all fruit (coconuts are technically fruit despite their name) and include blueberries, plums, apples, watermelons, coconuts, spiky yellow fruit, spiky purple fruit, strawberries, pineapples, and dragon fruit. Eight symbol scatter wins are worth 0.3 to 0.8x the bet, rising to 15 to 60 times the stake for a 16+ sized scatter payout. There are no wilds used in this system at any time.Fruit Smash: Slot FeaturesAs well as the Avalanche feature, other extras of note are Giant Fruit symbols, win multipliers, free spins, Fruit Frenzy Free Spins, Fast Track, and Burst Mode.Win MultiplierA win multiplier is used in all phases of the game. Following each Avalanche, it increases by +1. The win multiplier reset between paid spins, yet not between free spins.Giant Fruit SymbolsOn each spin, a 2x2, 3x3, or 4x4 sized Giant Fruit Symbol can randomly appear on the reels. Giant Fruit Symbols aren't just big; they can also carry win multipliers of up to x100, which is applied to any win they are part of. If two Giant Fruit Symbols of the same type appear, their values are added together.Free SpinsLanding 3 scatter symbols in the base game awards 10 free spins. If 3 scatter symbols hit in the bonus game, +5 spins are awarded. As mentioned, the win multiplier does not reset in free spins, and the active win multiplier is added to Giant Fruit Multipliers before being applied to scatter symbol wins.Fruit Frenzy Free SpinsThis feature can randomly be awarded instead of regular free spins when 3 scatter symbols land. During this bonus, Giant Fruit symbols are guaranteed to land on each new free spin.Fast TrackIf the Fast Track menu is present, players can play Fruit Smash in the following three modes:Giant Fruit – costs 5x the bet for a spin with guaranteed Giant Fruit, RTP is 96.28%.Free Spins – buy a regular round of free spins for 100x the bet, RTP is 96.45%.Fruit Frenzy Free Spins – buy a round of Fruit Frenzy Free Spins for 500x the bet, RTP is 96.53%.Burst ModeIn Burst Mode, players select a stake level and a number of spins which is then played out without the game grid being present. Any wins are simply displayed on the screen if and when they happen.Fruit Smash: Slot VerdictAfter glancing back through Slotmill's catalogue, the studio shows encouraging signs of creating steadily better games. Despite the general progression, there is, at times, a slight lack of the major individuality required to really make their games pop from the bunch. This was more pronounced in Fruit Smash, which felt like something Hacksaw Gaming would have produced. We've noticed a similar phenomenon while testing other games they've done, but perhaps the use of such common items as fruit exacerbated this impression.Familiarity hasn't damaged Fruit Smash's chances of being a fun slot to play, though, it must be said. Scatter paying slots aren't hugely numerous, so they possess an inherent desirability factor, and the use of massive multipliers is always a plus. When adding both of these elements together, Fruit Smash also caused memories of Sweet Bonanza to come bubbling to the surface. It's like Slotmill is going through an adolescence stage and hasn't quite found the conviction or self-confidence to completely follow its inner voice and is looking at the cool kids for cues.Still, any player after a scatter paying fruit slot with masses of multipliers and a decent max win could do a lot worse than pick Fruit Smash for some grid-based entertainment. There are no major faults we can point at to say otherwise. To push the point home, while Slotmill is good at crafting polished slots, to really make a mark, they might want to dig deeper into their personalities or bravely go where no one's been before. So far, though, the studio is ticking along nicely, and Fruit Smash is a smartly designed scatter paying slot, which might not be a long-term classic, but has everything it needs for short term success.

Title: Dead Man's Fingers
review: Dead Man's Fingers: Slot OverviewThe last time we caught up with independent developer G Games was in the jungle-based Fishin' Frenzy-style online slot Tiger Tiger. If that one underwhelmed you as much as it did us, then prepare for a repeat. Dead Man's Fingers is an oddly titled online slot which essentially does the exact same thing as Tiger Tiger, with a few peripheral changes, most being cosmetic. Released in partnership with Yggdrasil, the name of the game refers to a skeletal hand of a pirate captain. His bony digits appear on a collection symbol, scooping up instant cash symbols when they land at the same time, either in the base game or in an enhanced free spins bonus round.Due to the buccaneering theme and similarly coloured reels, Dead Man's Fingers brought to mind Yggdrasil own slot Pirates 2: Mutiny when it first loaded. A pleasing view greets players, where a pirate ship is located offshore of a beach covered in a locked treasure chest, a skeleton in a cage, palm trees, all set beneath a moody Caribbean sky. Dead Man's Fingers is quite handsomely presented; no major issues there. Once the reels start spinning, it didn't take long to clock that the gameplay comes straight from Tiger Tiger, which curbed our enthusiasm.Played using 5 reels and 4 rows, Dead Man's Fingers uses 25 paylines to land combinations of winning symbols across. Officially, volatility has been classified as medium-high, whilst RTP comes in at 95.2%. As before, hit frequency weighs in at 17.69%, which is on the low side, so prepare for a lot of dead spins. If it still sounds pretty hunky-dory, then Dead Man's Fingers may be played on any device, allowing stakes of 25 p/c to $/€100.The biggest thrills occurred when those fingers are reeling in Quickhit money symbols, but in between that happening, players collect coins when matching symbols land left to right across the reels. At least two are required in the case of the premium pirate symbol, which pays 80x the bet for five of a kind and can land up to four positions high. At least three are needed for the remaining symbols where we find four higher value gems worth 12 to 32x the bet and five lower value skull tokens worth 2.4 to 8x the stake for a line of five. The final regular symbol is the octopus adorned wild, landing on reels 2, 3, or 4, substituting all symbols except Quickhit Money symbols or the Cash Collect symbol.Dead Man's Fingers: Slot FeaturesIn the base or bonus game, Quickhit Money symbols and Collect symbols may appear on any spin as part of the Money Collect feature. Now, each Quickhit symbol displays a cash value or one of the Mini, Minor, Major, or Grand prizes. Cash values range from 1x to 20x the bet, while the four larger prizes are worth 50x, 100x, 200x, or 1,000x the bet. When Quickhit Money symbols are present on reels 1 to 4 at the same time as a Collect symbol on reel 5, players win all prizes in view.Compass scatters appear on reels 2, 3, or 4 and landing 3 of them awards 10 free spins. During free spins, there are more Quickhit Money symbols and Collect symbols on the reels, presumably increasing the chance of scoring instant cash wins. Hitting 3 scatters prolongs the round with another 10 free spins, with no limit to the number of possible retriggers.Dead Man's Fingers: Slot VerdictNot much has changed between Dead Man's Fingers and Tiger Tiger, including our response. The key alterations are the increase in volatility and the new theme, which takes players far from the jungle to a sea-based setting. The graphics are arguably better than before, making Dead Man's Fingers slightly more enjoyable than its slightly older sibling. Though, much of the goodwill was dashed to bits when it dawned on us that we'd basically played it all before in Tiger Tiger.To put a positive spin on it, Dead Man's Fingers might be everything a cash symbol collector enthusiast needs to have a right old time. Yet, Dead Man's Fingers comes up short against other games using this system like Big Bass Bonanza or the Megaways versions, for example – both of which have an enticing multiplier upgrade feature in free spins. The same goes for the pirate theme, where there are loads of swashbuckling slots to choose from, many of them superior to Dead Man's Fingers.Perhaps if G Games had sweetened the deal and expanded Dead Man's Fingers' winning possibilities, it might have upped the allure. On an interesting aside, the in-game help docs actually mention a 100,000x win was achieved during simulated spins, and a big stack of potential cash might have helped cut through the mediocrity. However, G Games' has stuck with a 2,740x the bet win cap, and while this is on a par with other cash collection games, it's not enough to really tip the balance in Dead Man's Fingers' favour.Dead Man's Fingers might look and feel like an improvement over Tiger Tiger, yet after a playthrough, it ended up being a case of more of the same. To sum up, Dead Man's Fingers is a so-so game, competing against similarly featured games that often do it better. Whether the theme is pirating or the goal is collecting cash symbols, it doesn't take much effort to find bigger, better, more exciting alternatives to what Dead Man's Fingers has to offer.

Title: Hit It Hard
review: Hit it Hard: OverviewELK’s latest neon-drenched extravagance is the sixth slot in their Classic Series. It has been about six months since the previous one, Win Win, and while both are classic fruit slots at their core, the extras are satisfyingly different. Hit it Hard has a unique dice game that has players move around a board full of mini-games with the ultimate goal of breaking the bank. Like the fast-paced slot in question, let’s skip the pleasantries and get right to the point of spinning reels.What initially hits you hard is the soundtrack the blows through the speakers. It’s like every 90s sitcom and game show theme music rolled into one. ELK Studios has gone for the big band vibe with a full horn section and an axeman wailing over the top. The sound effects are quite good too with classic slot bleeps and clicks. Just as successfully as any other game in the Classic Series, ELK has reproduced the modern flat top slot right on your device. The Equalizer like visuals cap off the effect and the result is a retro slot that is a lot more viscerally exciting than many in the genre.The aim of the game is to get the dice rolling, but first thing is first – selecting bets. Players can stick with stakes of 20 p/c - $/€100 per spin, or pick one of the four pre-programmed bet strategies. These strategies can be activated and deactivated at any time and are an acquired taste. When they go your way they’re amazing, if not, they are the most annoying feature ever created. Player preference for sure. The base game is super simple and involves spinning a 3x3 reel arrangement with just 5 paylines that are worth learning from the paytable.Continuing the simple rules, winning combinations are made up of 3 symbols only. All symbols are classic icons of the industry and are split into three groups of three symbols each. First up are the low pay cherries, lemons, and watermelons. The mid-table contains green, blue, and red BARS. Finally, the premiums are trios of green, blue, and red 7s worth 10, 25 and 50 times your stake respectively for a 3 of a kind combination. The final common symbol is the wild which only appears on the third reel. If it lands and is not used in a winning combination then that reel is held while the other two are respun for a second chance. Even better, the wild can also come with a multiplier of x2, x3, x4, or x5 attached to up the win rate.Players will appreciate every multiplier they can get to offset a low hit rate of 15.9% while the volatility goes in the other direction with a high rating of 8 out of 10. RTP is respectable with a figure of 96.3%, and the resulting math model felt quite well balanced overall. It allowed the bonus game to be triggered a number of times during testing which is the main point of this colouful trip back to the 90s.Hit it Hard: FeaturesBonus game triggeredAlong with the Wild Respin which we looked at, the other feature is the bonus board game which sits above the reels. First, you will need to trigger it, and this is done when the dice symbol lands on the mid position of reel three. Before starting the bonus game, the dice symbol turns into a x10 wild first, and any wins are paid out. There are 23 game spaces on the board which offer different mini-games, and the dice is rolled randomly to move the player around. The spaces are broken down into these categories:Stacked Wilds: get a spin with Stacked Wilds on reel 2, then on reel 3. Then a final spin with Stacked Wilds on reels 2 and 3 simultaneously.Wild 10 Spins: get 10 spins with multiplier wilds guaranteed to land on reel 3.Quantum Leap: players make a leap around the board which can be much bigger than a dice roll.Power Run: this awards every feature you pass on a move. So roll a 6 and playout 6 squares rather than just the final space from the roll.Lucky Ballz: a game of pachinko with 4 ball drops to collect multipliers up to 500x the stake.Super Ballz: the same as Lucky Ballz except balls continue to drop until 2 land on the same multiplier.The key: players collect a key symbol.The vault: land here with two collected key symbols to Break the Bank with the maximum win.The remaining symbols award free spins with or without multipliers.Players continue to move around the board as long as each batch of spins that are awarded has at least one winner. If you land on something like Super Ballz where there are no spins, you automatically get another roll of the dice.Hit it Hard: VerdictSo will fans of ELK’s Classic Series appreciate what they’ve done with Hit it Hard? Sure will, with its familiar looks and feel, yet brand new features, it is another worthy addition to the Series and will undoubtedly entertain fans. ELK’s stated aim with Hit it Hard was to take players back to the neon-filled 90s. And they have nailed that objective. It has that Equalizer vibe to it, but with toned down rules and gameplay. The extra features are well executed, not to mention being as fun as they are tense when in play. Speaking of features, the board game triggered surprisingly often, and its rounds lasted good lengths of time too. Winning combinations seemed to land more frequently when the dice game was in operation, which helped extend its duration. So yes, there is plenty for fans to get excited about.As well as its good points there are a few criticisms to go along with them that let Hit it Hard down. For one, potential is half of what is possible with Win Win on 2,500 times the stake. The hit rate is also down by around 3%, which is surprising since this game is all about hitting it hard, although with a higher volatility rating that is to be expected. On the positive, the RTP is slightly higher this time around.To sum up, Hit it Hard is a fine addition to the Classic Series and it showcases everything that the range is all about. Simple, retro gaming married with modern aesthetics and features. The result is a pacey slot that is capable of doling out plenty of fun moments. Just a shame that it is outperformed by other slots in the series when it comes to key stats.

Title: Bar-X Safecracker Megaways
review: Bar-X Safecracker Megaways: OverviewIt all started back in 2016 with the release of Big Time Gaming's Bonanza. Bar-X Safecracker Megaways features a mix of stylish and sleek design with a visually pleasing deep red colour palette. On the reels you'll see lower value 9 to A royals alongside more rewarding bars, lucky sevens, diamonds and X-symbols. The wild symbol, designed in red and black with the word "wild" written on it, appears on the extra horizontal reel only and substitutes for all symbols except the scatter.Bar-X Safecracker Megaways: FeaturesThe free spins feature in action with 8 Mystery Symbols in viewBar-X Safecracker Megaways comes with the usual set of features seen in the majority of Blueprint's Megaways slots. Now, with the free spins round initiated, each cascading chain reaction will increase your win multiplier by 1x with no limits. Moreover, you can also retrigger the feature by landing another 4+ scatters.Bar-X Safecracker Megaways: VerdictIn spite of having churned out a ridiculous amount of reskins and Megaways clones, Blueprint Gaming has managed to navigate around the pitfalls, skillfully avoiding the trap of making their games feel generic or unambitious. Mathematically, these are all excellent medium variance slots that offer good value for any gambling budget if you're looking for some play time as well as a chance to land massive wins whether in the base game or the free spins.Ultimately, the game has little new on offer for those already familiar with the concept, but if you're a fan of Megaways, and a proponent of freedom of choice, you surely won't mind trying your luck on Bar-X Safecracker Megaways.

Title: Finn and the Dragon Tales
review: Finn and the Dragon Tales: Slot OverviewIt's no secret that leprechauns abound in online gambling, but one of the more recognisable examples of these magical entities is a chap named Finn, who first hit the scene in NetEnt's 2017 slot Finn and the Swirly Spin. As the name says, Finn slots are famous for gaming grids which spin symbols in a swirling direction rather than the usual top-down motion. The last installement reviewed, Finn and the Candy Spin, was a letdown, but Finn and the Dragon Tales is shaping up to be an improvement, helped by things like a stronger max win and an innovative, transformative, scatter win free spins round.As mentioned, Finn is famous for his swirly, whirly gaming grid, which Finn and the Dragon Tales possesses. Symbols on the reels appear in a clockwise pattern, starting at the bottom left corner and ending at the centre. Title: Boom Pirates
review: Boom Pirates (Foxium): OverviewFoxium, for those of you who don't know, is one of many independent studios recruited by Microgaming as part of an ongoing project in which Microgaming supplies the platform and know-how while its partnering studios focuses on creating exclusive content. With that said, some of them are slowly but steadily starting to mature and grow into their shoes as proper slot makers. As a matter of fact, with the release of Boom Pirates, Foxium has taken a giant leap forward.For whatever reason, and we can only speculate, Boom Pirates has been delayed by nearly a year. Just by the look of it, you can tell it's quite an ambitious undertaking for such a small studio, but seeing that it comes with a new mechanic called Wonderways™, there could possibly have been some legal issue to sort out, as we've seen in other cases. Utilizing a default setup of 5-reels, 4-rows and 1024 ways to win, it piggybacks on the Megaways hype by offering up to a staggering 10,077,696 ways to win in fully extended mode. There are also plenty of unique features to benefit from such as the Boom Pirate feature that randomly activates extra rows and reels, as well as the Mary's Swashbuckling Attack that can randomly turn a non-winning spin into a five of a kind win. So, if you're up for some swashbuckling action, you can join the pirate crew from as little as 0.10 up to €30 per spin across all devices.The pirate topic never ceases to fascinate us. It's a well-liked theme that reflects our passion for adventure, mystery and travel - in Boom Pirates, we get a little bit of everything. On the wooden reels, symbols include 10 to A royal values as well as 5 more valuable picture symbols represented by gunpowder barrels, canons, colourful parrots, a tattooed pirate named Ben and, finally, Captain Mary. And nope, no wild symbols available here.Boom Pirates (Foxium): FeaturesFree spins featureThe first decision you'll have to make before embarking whether you want to play with the Foxify™ feature activated or not. If you do, it will increase the odds of triggering the free spins but will also increase your current bet size by 50%. If you want to skip waiting for the bonus to drop altogether, you can opt for the Buy Feature by clicking the gift button. This will cost you 100 times your stake.Before we attack the free spins, there are a couple of base game modifiers to wade through. First, there is the Boom Pirates feature which can come into play randomly on any spin. When activated, you'll hear a pirate call out "boooooom pirates" as the strategically parked pirate ship starts firing cannon balls onto the reels. As a result, this can extend the reel set up to 10,077,696 pay ways for that spin. Also randomly triggered, you may see Mary swing in on a rope following a non-winning spin to award a five of a kind win. This is known as Mary's Swashbuckling Attack.While it's possible to unlock the maximum pay ways in the base game, the Free Spins feature comes with a few added benefits. It comes into play when you land the 3 scatter symbols that together spell YO-HO-HO on reels 1, 3, and 5 simultaneously - this will give you 10 free spins (alternatively you can also buy the feature). During the round, additional tiles (paylines) can be randomly activated on the full 6x9 grid if hit by the bombardment of the pirate ship (it's more active during the free spins). Once these tiles (paylines) are activated, they remain active until the end of the round.Boom Pirates (Foxium): VerdictSo, was Boom Pirates worth the long wait? Indeed it was. It's undoubtedly fun to play, it looks fantastic, and there's an adequate amount of thrill and tension to keep you on your toes. Few games come without any downsides, however, and Boom Pirates has a few of these as well, although not everyone will be bothered by them.For such an "open" game with millions of possible paylines, it's surprisingly limiting on the player. The first demo we tried had a max win of 5000x which, even at that number, could be considered low for a game that aims to stand alongside the likes of Megaways. Offering up to 10 million ways to win but capping the game at 3,800x doesn't make much sense.  There are other limitations as well, such as the removal of wilds and the fact that you're required to land scatters on fixed reels as if it was some 9 payline slot.Overall, Boom Pirates is an excellent game, and if you're not provoked by its limitations, there's a good chance that you'll enjoy it a whole lot. The scenery is phenomenal, there's some comical elements to make you chuckle at times, and it can even offer you satisfyingly long sessions at times. In spite of its flaws, it's a confident yes from us.

Title: Wild Mantra

Title: 10,001 Nights Megaways

Players pick one of three cards to have an x3, x5, or x8 multiplier applied to the next win.Mega Wilds – unlocked by collecting 30 magic lamps. Up to four full reel wilds appear on the grid, each carrying a multiplier of x2 to x7.Progress is locked to the stake level, so changing your bet starts the collection process all over again. These four features can also be combined so more than one can be in effect at the same time.Destiny Free SpinsTo enter the bonus round requires landing at least 3 Destiny Spins symbols; 3 awards 8 free spins, plus 2 free spins for each scatter from four onwards. It's not unlimited, though, and is capped at x20.10,001 Nights Megaways slot - mega wilds10,001 Nights Megaways: Slot VerdictIn stories, genies typically grant three wishes, yet some people say they'd get around this limitation by asking for an unlimited number of wishes. The reason why we jumped to this conclusion is because the progression between this and the previous game has been kind of subtle, rather than a massive change request brought about by having a low number of wishes. There's nothing particularly negative to say about 10,001 Nights Megaways, but some may be wishing Red Tiger had been a bit braver for the overhaul.One of the main reasons is that the max win has stayed the same as before, at the albeit respectable level of 10,347x the bet. You might think with the addition of cascades, an extra reel, and a ton of extra possible ways, the upper winning total could have been higher. In its defence, would it have been weird calling a game 10,001 Nights Megaways and having potential of 20,001x? Then again, 10,347 isn't 10,001 either. Instead, players have to put in a bit of time to unlock them one by one. Title: Chilli Heat Megaways

In their place, the studio has focused more resources into the respin feature, adding new ways of cobbling together bigger wins. As well as the respins game, Chilli Heat Megaways has tumbles, an Ante Bet, and a buy respins feature.The tumble feature triggers after base game wins, removing the winning symbols and tumbling new or remaining symbols into the gaps. This can lead to new wins lining up, keeping the tumble feature firing until no more wins appear.The Ante Bet is an optional extra, accessible at any time in the base game. For the extra cost of 25% on top of the bet, players can double their chances of winning the respin feature.Money symbols are the key to the respin feature, appearing on any of the main reels. The bonus round starts with 3 spins, where reels 1 and 6 are initially locked.If new money symbols hit on the main grid, they are held in position and reset the respins counter. Above them, on the horizontal reel, special symbols may land, producing the following effects:Padlock leaning to the left – unlocks reel 1.Padlock leaning to the right – unlocks reel 6.Up and down arrows – Extends the number of possible symbols on the reel below it to 7.Circular down arrow – collects all money symbols below it and adds it to the total win.Square down arrow – collect all money symbols in view and adds them to the total win.Circular 'X' – multiplies the money symbols below it by x2, x3, x5, or x10 randomly.Square 'X' – multiplies all money symbols in view by x2, x3, x5, or x10 randomly.If you don't want to wait for money bags to land naturally and are able to access bonus buys, Chilli Heat Megaways offers a buy respin feature. Paying 100x the base bet gets you a spin that is guaranteed to trigger the respins feature.Chilli Heat Megaways: Slot VerdictChilli Heat Megaways is kind of a strangely unsatisfying game when seen as either an upgrade or as a standalone. As a remake, the respins feature has obviously been expanded, the graphics are better, potential is higher, plus players get the benefit of Megaways and tumbles in the base game. However, some players who dug the laid-back attitude of the first, not to mention the free spins and jackpots, might feel they're on unfamiliar territory spinning this Megaways version.Since there is nothing but tumbles fleshing out the base game, let's head straight to the respins feature. Pragmatic Play themselves went larger not long before in a respin focused slot with arguably just as much charm in a game called Empty the Bank, also offering twice the potential at 10k.What's leftover then is the warm Mexican vibe. Otherwise, Chilli Heat Megaways fails to really ignite the taste buds, since there are better places to dip your tortillas.

Title: Thor's Vengeance

Volatility, on the other hand, weighs in at medium/high which matches the potential and features well for those who prefer a harder edge. When it does, one of three modifiers come into play:All of the low pay symbols are removed.A random number of symbols are swapped for matching symbols.A random number of symbols are turned into wilds for a guaranteed win.Next, mighty Mjolnir makes an appearance in the Thor’s Hammer feature by being smashed against the reels. It either appears as a 2x2 sized wild in any position, or nudges rows and reels. Whatever is chosen, a winner is the guaranteed outcome.If the Thor’s Multiplier is randomly triggered, he sees the big man summon lightning once again. This time he directs it at the multiplier shield to award a multiplier of up to x20.The last modifier is Thor’s Generosity which may appear when two scatter symbols are in view. If it does, Thor blasts one random symbol with lightning turning it into the third scatter to trigger the feature.Whenever 3 scatters appear on the reels they award 8 free spins. Each additional scatter over 3 adds another +4 to the total. During the feature, free spins may be retriggered in the same way. Once in, a growing multiplier comes into play. The other modifiers may appear, so when Thor’s Multiplier activates, it increases the current multiplier by up to x20.Thor’s Vengeance: Slot VerdictIt seems Red Tiger has broken the drought by making a pretty fun game. To be fair, Thor’s Vengeance is not quite as thrilling as Thor’s Lightning, though the higher potential might sway players over. It appears Red Tiger has taken on board some of the criticism that’s been slung its way. The result is a decent slot.There are a few niggles. Why RTP couldn’t be on the sunny side of average for a change, or why they had to cover two positions on the middle reels, almost halving the number of win ways? Still, these are more technicalities rather than an aversion to the total package. Even potential is up significantly over their recent releases.
