The multiplier applied to picks is obviously the sweetener when a higher number of consecutive wins happen. At best, the 25x prize meets the x100 multiplier, which wouldn't be too bad at all. It was a little surprising to find out the Cannonball Bonus was absent from the free spins round. The merging wild feature is okay, but would it have made more sense to integrate/boost the Cannonball Bonus instead of completely dropping it? Guess we'll never know.When the wind really gets into Cannonball Cash's sails, it is good for wins as high as 7,465.7x the bet, totalling a sizable potential haul. So, whilst Cannonball Cash is unlikely to conquer the Spanish Main, sack Cartagena, or anything like that, it offers a few interesting diversions for pirate-minded players.

Title: Robber Strike
review: Robber Strike: Slot OverviewIt seems like a lot of people out there appreciate a good heist (from a safe distance), as attested by all the movies, books, and online slots consistently being released. Software provider Pragmatic Play appears to favour the theme, too, as the topic of crime has appeared in the studio's past work already. Well, it's time to add another one to the swag bag. Titled Robber Strike, it boasts several intriguing features, though, by the time you're done reading about them, you might think they've been nicked from elsewhere.On with the show, and if you ever see a masked man holding a bulging bag with a dollar sign imprint over his shoulder, there's a good chance he's up to no good. One of these bandit types greets players on Robber Strike's home page, and in the game proper, he appears on the wild symbols. With a pretty sweet bongo-driven soundtrack jammin' in the background (it gets livelier when the reels are spinning), Robber Strike is located in a swanky banking spot, the kind of place that caters to high net-worth individuals rather than any old stiff off the street. Behind the gaming grid sits a vault door, and when triggering free spins, players enter it to mingle with stacks of gold coins and bundles of banknotes.Robber Strike slot - base gameOn to the game grid, where Robber Strike's has 6 reels holding 4 symbols each, providing 4,096 ways to win. Wins are awarded for landing matching symbols left to right from the first reel and on. Volatility is high in this game of smash and grab, with a 96.51% maximum theoretical return to player, or 96.5% when buying free spins. The stake selection begins at 10 p/c, rising to $/€100 for the high rolling heisters out there, while buying the bonus round has a cost of 100 times the bet.All pay symbols award wins for 3 to 6-of-a-kind winning ways, and 10 different pay symbols grace the table. The first five are low-pay 10-A card royals, worth 0.4 to 0.8 times the stake for a 6 symbol win, whereas a 6 premium symbol win awards 2 to 50 times the bet. The high-pay symbols are bank notes, a crown, a dog, a copper, and a big boss-type character. Robber Strike's wilds are a bit special. They appear on all but the leftmost reel, replacing any regular pay symbol. When a wild hits in the base game, a chance exists it will randomly expand to cover all positions on a reel, and when it expands, it has a random multiplier of x2 to x10, which applies to all winning combinations it is part of.Robber Strike: Slot FeaturesRobber Strike slot - free spins optionsNo other features appear in the base game, but like a guard posted outside a vault, be on the lookout for Robber Strike's scatter symbols. Landing 3 or more scatter symbols triggers the bonus round. Furthermore, if triggered by 4, 5, or 6 scatters, players also collect 20x, 200x, or 2,000x the bet, respectively. When triggered, players choose Free Spins with Expanding Wilds or Free Spins with Sticky Wilds.Free Spins with Expanding Wilds10 free spins come with this feature. During it, whenever a wild hits on reels 3 or 4, it expands to cover the entire reel, and a respins session is triggered. The game keeps respinning, awarding wins after each respins until no new win hits. Each time a respin occurs, the multiplier increases by +1 on the expanded wild, which applies to all wins that it is part of. If, during respins, 2 expanded wilds are present at the same time, their multipliers are multiplied before awarding the win. Landing 3 or more scatters retriggers the round without limit.Free Spins with Sticky Wilds8 free spins are awarded with this feature. Before the round begins, a random symbol is picked. Whenever picked symbols land on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5, they transform into wilds. All wild symbols landing in this bonus, either naturally or from a symbol transformation, will remain on the reels until the round ends. When filling one or more reels on the same spin with sticky wilds, +3 more free spins are awarded.Buy Free SpinsWhen buying the bonus round for 100 times the bet, 3 to 6 scatters will land to trigger the feature. Then, players are able to pick their preferred feature of the two options.Robber Strike: Slot VerdictWe used the word nicked in the intro, but even if the features here exactly weren't straight lifted from elsewhere, they did ring bells as if they have been used before. In one form or another, at least. No big surprise why these sorts of features are popular either, because Robber Strike does some pretty sweet stuff with expanding wild symbols. Maybe inspired by games like Beast Mode, Danger High Voltage, or some of the expanding wild features Hacksaw Gaming has been tinkering with recently. Pragmatic Play itself is no stranger to expanding/spreading wild action; see games like Wild West Duels, Excalibur Unleashed, or Power of Thor Megaways, amongst others, as examples. The point is expanding wilds are hot and can get better (potentially) with a juicy multiplier tossed in there, too.Robber Strike ups the ante further since when more than one wild multiplier is in play on a respin, the values multiply each other, providing the chance for spicy heisting to occur. Factor in the 4,096 ways to win pay system, decent symbol values, and who knows, lucky armchair robbers might just crack the vault. At 5,000x the bet, Robber Strike's win cap is a decent enough target to aim for, all things considered. It could have been bigger, perhaps, but it at least feels achievable given what players have to work with.Perhaps one of Robber Strike's criticisms is that the theme use is a little bit on the unoriginally unexciting side. Pragmatic Play itself has used this kind of thing more than once in the past; Reel Banks, The Great Stick Up, and Cash Patrol sprang to mind as distant relations of one sort or another. No biggie, and while Robber Strike doesn't strike one as a Pragmatic Play flagship release (do they do those anymore?), it's got the sort of features that can pull off a good pilfering when they're doing their expanding and multiplying thing.

Title: Bompers
review: Bompers: Slot OverviewBompers is the third slot from ELK Studios to use their gravity mechanic, and they've combined it with classic slot imagery this time around. In the previous two, Cygnus and IO, ELK went all cosmic, so utilising a sort of disco pinball theme takes things into a completely different direction. Here, the team has dialled up almost every element. Audio is a standout, as are features, including a new trademarked one called X-citer which is like a menu of feature buys. Let's see how it stacks up.Of the three gravity slots so far, Bompers is the least busy one visually speaking. A pinball table displaying a couple of bumpers makes up the background, so you can see how ELK possibly came up with the Bompers concept. On each new spin, 24 symbols drop into a 6x4 grid where columns are staggered rather than flush - this means symbols randomly fall to the left or right in new drops or avalanches. While visuals are decent, the tune is banging indeed, and a lot heavier than your typical fruit slot jazzy number. When the action heats up, so does the tempo, mixing in a bit of dubstep, voice-overs, and makes a major contribution to the overall enjoyment of the game.Bompers is available on any device, offering the usual ELK bet range of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin - or drop, as they are called around here. Highly volatile, drops can just as easily lead nowhere or blow up, avalanching into special symbols, extra rows, and more ways to win. At the start of a drop, 4,096 ways are in play, rising to 262,144 when all 8 rows are active. The RTP, meanwhile, has dropped ever so slightly compared to the previous offerings in the range, now coming in at 95.8%. As most will have noticed, this is in line with the overall current trend.Regular pay symbols are made up of classic icons such as cherries, lemons, oranges, watermelons, 4-leaf clovers, horseshoes, and bars. The most lucrative is the lucky 7 - land 3, 4, 5 or 6 of these for an award of 2, 4, 6 or 20 times the stake. The final regular symbol is the wild, substituting for any of the pay symbols.Bompers: Slot Features﻿Bompers is the name of special wild symbols which appear throughout the game - up to 5 during the base game. When other symbols bump them, either from dropping in or by the gravity effect, they fill the Bomper's meter. When it is completely filled, the Bomper turns into a sticky wild. In the base game, Bompers are sticky throughout wins or avalanches.Mystery bombs trigger when avalanches end, transforming itself and all connecting symbols into one matching symbol type. If 2 or more mystery bombs overlap, then all overlapping symbols become wild.It's the job of the shooting star symbol to travel upwards on the grid. When it gets to the top, it creates a mixed group of up to 7 symbols, out of which up to 3 are guaranteed to be wild.The 'B' symbol is the scatter, and 3 in view trigger 7 free drops which can be retriggered during the course of the round. Before free drops commence, up to 5 Bompers are randomly placed on the grid. Moreover, during the bonus sticky wilds remain in place for the full duration.Lastly, the X-iter is a list of features you can activate for different prices. First is the normal mode, where you hit spin for the regular stake. For 25x the bet you can guarantee 3 symbol drops with an increasing number of Bompers. The first drop starts with 1 Bomper, and each subsequent drop adds one extra Bomper. 50x the bet gets you 5 symbol drops using this method, while 300x the bet gets you 10 symbol drops with an increasing number of Bompers. Finally, for 100x the bet, you can guarantee 3 bonus symbols will appear on the next drop.Bompers: Slot VerdictIt might not sound like it on paper, but in practice, Bompers can get pretty manic when it winds up. Audio is a large piece of the puzzle. Bomper's music was made in the same spirit as the manically good tune used in Nitropolis. If anything, it's even more maniacal, mixing in a bunch of genres over its relentless house beat. If Bomper's visuals seem a little light at first, the music more than makes up for any sensorial shortfall - big count ups are especially enjoyable. If Willy Wonka was tasked with making a fruit slot, it would probably be a lot like this.Onto gameplay and Bompers is similar to previous gravity-driven slots, or Gold Series games, in that it needs several components working together to provide best results. One thing about Bomper symbols themselves worth reiterating, is they are not wild until their meters fully charge. If you're unaware of this, they can be disappointing at first, particularity if you've forked out for a bunch of them and they're just sitting there dividing regular symbols. Fortunately, the wait can be worth it, and having several wild Bompers in action causes all manner of mechanics to come into play.Elk's new X-iter feature is an interesting addition providing several bonus buy options for all wallet types. The increasing number of Bompers can turn into a real Bomper-fest, and it is nice to have a cheaper option to get a taste without hammering your account. One thing to consider is Bomper symbols often need quite a bumps to turn them wild, which can be tricky to achieve in just three drops - though it can happen of course. The ten drop option gives you more room to manoeuvre, but it is pricey. At best, Bompers can produce wins of up to X,000 times the bet.All up, Bompers is a genetically modified fruit themed slot, like none other out there. It's got the gameplay to match when it goes off, just make sure you've turned the sound up.

Title: Towering Fortunes
review: Towering Fortunes: Slot OverviewMoney, money, money, it's surely one of the key reasons players try their luck with online slots, and if you like visual reminders of wealth in your games, here's an option from developer Pragmatic Play. It's been dubbed Towering Fortunes and sits comfortably in the genre of slots that likes to flaunt the so-called finer things in life. Or, if not finer, more expensive, at least. If that sounds pretty neat, feel free to join us as we well and truly get our 'bling' on. Sorry, we'll try to tone down the gauche setting a notch or two from now on.In Towering Fortunes, players find themselves in a built-up part of town, with skyscrapers blazing across the horizon. The setting could be made up, but there's a ring of Hong Kong to the view, with what could be the Observation Wheel on the right and the International Commerce Centre to the left. While musing on this part of the world, we found out that the name Hong Kong means 'fragrant harbour', and apparently around 40% of the territory consists of nature reserves and country parks, despite being drenched in high-rise buildings. Anyway, this might be Hong Kong, it might not, yet it's somewhere dynamically urban where it feels like fortunes can potentially be made.Towering Fortunes slot - base gameTowering Fortunes is played on a 5-reel, 3-row grid, which has 20 fixed paylines for landing winning combinations across. Players should be prepared for a highly volatile math model, which the studio has rated 4.5 lightning bolts out of 5. As is typically the case, RTP is variable, with the highest value coming in at 96.5% before dipping to 95.5% or 94.5% at the lower two settings. Playable on any device, users have bet levels of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin to choose from.A rather singular Hold & Spin feature is Towering Fortunes' main event, but until it activates, regular payouts occur when matching symbols land across a payline in adjacent reels starting from the left. The first four are J-A card royals with diamond decorations, paying 2.5 to 5 times the stake for a five-of-a-kind hit. Next are glasses of liquor and cigars, sports cars, yachts, jets, and a lady as the premium tiles, awarding 7.5 to 50x the bet for five of a kind. Assisting with creating winning lines are the wild symbols, which land on all reels to substitute any pay symbol. When the dashing wild tile makes wins of itself, it pays up to 250x the bet for five-of-a-kind.Towering Fortunes: Slot FeaturesTowering Fortunes slot - mystery symbolsThe two extra bits lighting up Towering Fortunes' reels are Mystery Symbols and the Hold & Spin feature. Mystery Symbols are straightforward. When they land, they all transform to reveal the same matching random pay symbol.Hold & Spin FeatureLanding 3 or more Money symbols anywhere on the grid in the base game triggers the Hold & Spin feature. The normal grid is removed and replaced with one consisting of 5 reels, with each reel having 11 positions. Triggering Money symbols fall to the bottom of their respective reels where they sit for the feature. When the reels spin, only blanks or new Money symbols hit - when Money symbols land, they stack at the bottom of the reels or on top of any symbols already there. Now, each reel has 3 lives. When three spins occur where a reel has not landed a new Money symbol, it is blocked, and no more spins take place on it. When a Money symbol lands on an active reel, it resets the reel's lives back to three.At the top of each reel, a multiplier is displayed starting at x1 and which applies to Money symbols sitting beneath it. When Money symbols stack to certain heights, the multiplier increases. If the stack reaches 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, or 11 symbols high, the multiplier becomes x2, x5, x10, x20, x30 or x100, respectively. When all 5 reels are blocked, and no more spins remain, the round ends. Then, the Money symbols in view are awarded.Towering Fortunes slot - respin bonusTowering Fortunes: Slot VerdictHow you feel about money slots, in general, is probably how you'd feel about putting Towering Fortunes through its paces. It has a bold, almost retro look in parts, as if the game came out a few years ago with a sort of The Finer Reels of Life look and feel about it. Instead of detracting from the experience, the design, in some ways, just adds to the 'Check me out, I swim in a pool Benjamins' attitude. In other words, the dated-looking symbols amplify the charm, if that's the right word, like a billionaire CEO wearing pyjamas to a meeting where everyone else is in business suits because, well, they're rich, and they can.If the livin' large thing invokes feelings of ambivalence, but you're the sort of player who favours a bit of hold 'n win action, Towering Fortunes actually has a pretty nifty bonus round to try out. Simply designed, though quite clever at the same time, it's unique enough to warrant a look, even if the rest of the game might come across as a bit garish. The Hold & Spin feature offers action that can get quite interesting when enough Money symbols start stacking to awaken reel multipliers. Multipliers can grow quite nicely when the going's good, too, from single digits to double, and with a bit (or a lot) of luck, bag the x100. At full blast, Towering Fortunes is kept under wraps with the specific figure of 6,422x the bet as its win cap.A respectable amount, yet if that isn't enough to get you out of bed in the morning, but you like Towering Fortunes' look, something like Dream Drop Diamonds might be a better option. Both games use a similar stacking symbols concept in their main bonus rounds, with the difference being Relax Gaming's slot is wired into a progressive jackpot network. Towering Fortunes dangles less potential lucre, but it ticks the right boxes for one of these expensive consumer item-themed games while tossing a fairly unique bonus round into the mix.

Title: Blirix Workshop
review: Blirix Workshop: Slot OverviewIt took a brief Google search to confirm Blirix isn’t in some up and coming animated film, book, or tv character, but rather, someone Iron Dog Studio has dreamt up to star in one of their slots. Blirix Workshop is based on a quirky scientist engaging in a spot of alchemical transformation. He’s got a handy spell book conjuring up a bunch of modifiers when it appears, as well as awarding free spins when he himself shows up on the reels. Yeah, it is one of those quirkily themed games that’s cute, yet one where features often frustrate as much as they thrill.Blirix’ actual workshop certainly is a cosy place to hang out and try your luck. A bubbling blue cauldron projects a 5-reel, 15-payline action area on the screen, making it look like it is floating in mid-air. Around it, a cat lounges in an armchair as a mouse keeps his distance on the opposite side of the screen. Beneath him, potions brew, while skulls, books, and parchments litter the rest of the room. A magically minded soundtrack lays a bit of fantasy on to the scene, which ends up being a rather warm one.Mixing up a potion is possible on any device, from mobile to desktop, by selecting stakes from 20 p/c to $/€20 per spin. Blirix Workshop is not one of Iron Dog’s high power slots by any stretch, let’s get that out there now. Medium volatility plays a part, as do low-performance features and meek wins. We’re used to a bit more grunt from Iron Dog to be honest, but they can’t all be whimsical brutes. Blirix is a lot lighter, suiting a different sort of audience than those who appreciate Iron Dog’s more tightly wound Megaways slots, for instance. On the other hand, the 96.0% RTP should be acceptable for most.Winning combinations of three to five matching symbols are possible, left to right from the first reel. Opening up the paytable we find red, green orange, and purple pieces of jewellery as the low paying symbols, while lanterns, hourglasses, a potion tub, and a pipe are the highs. Landing a line of five high pay symbols is worth a payout of 4 to 15 times the stake. Keep an eye for the symbol which bears a resemblance to Audrey Junior from the Little Shop of Horrors. This one’s wild, substituting all non-special symbols and expanding to cover all positions if it lands on the bottom row. If the wild is awarded via the Book of Spells (covered below), it also brings an x2 multiplier into play.Blirix Workshop: Slot FeaturesBlirix Workshop - free spinsOne integral symbol is the Magic Book, appearing only on the third reel. It’s wild for one, while also triggering the Book of Spells feature when it lands. When active, a book overlays the screen, and a modifier is randomly selected from its pages. This could be a symbol transformation, extra wilds, or a multiplier up to x5. When spells are awarded, they come with a strength rating of 1-4, where higher ratings lead to greater rewards.Despite the modifiers, nothing really happens until free spins are triggered. This occurs when 3, 4, or 5 Blirix scatters land to award 10, 15, 20 free spins, respectively, or by using the bonus buy option which also increases the RTP to 96.4%. In free spins, symbols on the third reel get collected in the cauldron. Collecting 15 symbols triggers the Cauldron Combo Bonus. Here, the symbols in the pot are placed on the reels for a new win evaluation.During the feature, book symbols have a bunch of extra spells they can produce. These can convert low pay symbols in the cauldron to highs, add wilds to the cauldron, add more free spins, or introduce a global multiplier. Don’t forget, spells available in the main game are available here too. Lastly, if 3, 4, or 5 scatters land, 5, 10, or 15 free spins are added to the total.Blirix Workshop: Slot VerdictWell, it’s a shame Blirix couldn’t have perfected his modifiers and features more because they feel like they’re still in the prototype phase. Extra eye of newt or toe of frog might have added a bit more pep. Let’s start with the modifiers which have two inherent issues, or annoyances might be a better word. The most concerning is that they don’t do a lot of modifying when called into action. The other irritant is triggering a modifier which doesn’t do anything at all.For instance, when receiving a multiplier for a certain symbol type, yet having no combination on the reels to apply it to. Yet you still have to sit through an animation to find out you’re not getting anything. It’s a shame because Blirix Workshop’s endearing looks crate a warm environment, yet any goodwill quickly erodes after waves of ineffectual features wear away at your patience. Free spins do increase the pace, there are more spells, and better returns are possible, but they require next level patience to trigger. When activated, you better hope they go some way to restore your battered balance.Blirix Workshop could have been better if the features were more potent, free spins triggered more often, or the base game wasn’t such a drag. However, the crowd this is aimed at may very well lap it up anyway. If spinning reels in an adorable environment is the only goal, then Blirix makes an ideal choice. If however, slowly animated features leading nowhere makes your blood curdle its best to give Blirix a miss.

Title: Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win
review: Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win: Slot OverviewAnyone out there daydreaming of visiting a far-off distant land to soak up the sun and kick back in the sand with a cool beverage while taking a punt? If so, then stir up a piña colada or grab a tropical juice of choice and join us as we take a trip to the sunny shores of Stakelogic's online slot Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win, a cluster paying grid slot, with free spins, wheels, and as you might be expecting from the title, a hold 'n win feature.Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win is also a slot which features feisty, charismatic birds that brought to mind ELK Studios' Pirots and Pirots 2 slots. However, the birds in Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win are mostly pay symbols, so they don't wander around the joint eating symbols, bopping at discos or anything like that. In other words, Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win isn't as avant-garde as its Pirots pals, but it is a slot that made a very amiable first impression. The artwork is exceptionally pleasing to the eye, very tastefully laid out, and expertly coloured, creating the sort of dream holiday destination Instagram influencers would be all over like a rash.Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win slot - base gameThe active gaming area in Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win is a 5-reel, 4-row cluster paying grid, awarding regular wins when 4 or more identical symbols are connected to each other in horizontal or vertical directions. Behind the scenes, mixing the drinks in the background stirs a medium-high volatile math model, pushing out a default RTP value of 96%. As far as tackling the game goes, players can choose a wager of 20 c to $/€50, and bonus buys are an option as well.Cheerfully patterned J to A card ranks are the lower value symbols, while the higher value ones are 4 avian characters. Landing clusters made up of 4 matching symbols is worth 0.1 to 1 times the bet, going up to 10 to 200 times the bet for hitting a 15+ cluster win. Winning clusters trigger a hold and respin feature, which holds winning symbols and respins non-winning positions until the win can no longer be improved. Multipliers also appear on any new winning symbols when this happens, starting at x2 and going up to x17 max. Respins end when no winning symbols land or all positions are winning. Wilds substitute for all paying symbols and have the same values as the highest-paying bird when making an all-wild winTiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win: Slot FeaturesTiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win slot - Fortune wheelMoving on to the remaining features, we come across a Coin symbol collection element, Fortune Wheels, free spins, a Hold 'N' Win Bonus Game, and bonus buys.Scatter SymbolsScatter symbols appear on all reels. Hitting 3 of them triggers the Fortune Wheel while 4 scatters trigger the Mega Fortune Wheel, and having 5 scatters in view triggers the Epic Fortune Wheel.Coin and Treasure Chest SymbolsCoin symbols are present on all reels, showing values of 1x to 50x the bet. Landing 5 Coin symbols triggers the Hold 'N' Win Bonus Game, which is possible from the base game or from free spins. The Treasure Chest symbol appears on rightmost reel. When it lands, it pays the value of all Coin symbols in view on that spin.Fortune WheelSpinning the Fortune Wheel awards free spins or the Hold 'N' Win Bonus Game. The Mega Fortune and Epic Fortune Wheel have better chances of triggering the Hold 'N' Win Bonus Game or free spins with higher values.Free SpinsFree spins can only be won through the Fortune Wheel, where it is possible to attain 8 to 15 free spins. Free spins can be retriggered by landing 3 or more scatter symbols, thereby activating the Fortune Wheel. No special new rules were listed in the game info section for the free spins feature.Hold 'N' Win Bonus GameThe Hold 'N' Win Bonus Game starts with 3 respins, and only Coin symbols may land. Every time a Coin symbol lands, the number of respins is reset to 3. When 4 or more Coin symbols connect to form a cluster they merge into a Treasure Chest symbol, displaying the accumulated value of the cluster of Coins which created it. If 4 or more Treasure Chest symbols form a cluster, they merge into a Golden Tiki Idle symbol. This symbol displays the accumulated value of the cluster of Treasure Chest symbols which created it.Buy BonusVia the buy bonus, players can get the Fortune Wheel for 100x the bet, the Mega Fortune Wheel for 200x the bet, or the Epic Fortune Wheel for 300x the bet.Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win slot - bonus gameTiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win: Slot VerdictOne persistent thought while reviewing Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win was if and/or how much inspiration Stakelogic garnered from ELK's Pirots slots. Maybe some, maybe none, hard to say, but given how 'inspired' Stakelogic has been in the past by other studios' work (see Money Track 2 for one particularly ludicrous example), it's a question that stuck in the mind as Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win played out. Speaking of playing out, Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win does not function like a Pirots slot, though. It's actually kind of closer to something like Hula Balua in some ways, which incidentally is another tropical island-style slot from ELK Studios. Perhaps Stakelogic's design team was on an ELK binge when it was making Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win? Perhaps not, moving on.Whatever the case, Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win hasn't turned out too badly at all, quite alright, in fact, though it might help to view the game in a bubble as if free from any possible outside influences. The respins/cluster combo is not a common one and plays well in the base game and free spins, joined as well by the Coin collection feature, not to mention multipliers. One of Tiki Tiki Hold 'n' Win's twists, a relatively minor though positive one, is the way Coin symbols can cluster together to form Treasure Chest symbols, which can, in turn, cluster together to form Golden Tiki Idle symbols. It's a game that, when firing on all pistons, may cluster together to form wins of up to 10,000 times the bet.Add all of the parts together, and you've got a neatly packaged cluster pays slot that looks excellent, plays well, and can flip from lying on a reclining beach chair mode to a flurry of feathers in a moment, making for a potentially enthralling tropical getaway slot.

Title: Raven Rising
review: ﻿Raven Rising: Slot OverviewOne of the neat things about online slots compared to other forms of gambling is the astonishing range of themes they are dressed up with. The variety is so great it's like loading up your favourite streaming service and not knowing which series or movie to watch. At the highest RTP setting, Quickspin has classified the volatility as 4.5 out of 5, and the game splits RTP into 64.12% for the base game, the rest going to free spins.Making their way across the game board are 20 fixed paylines, awarding a win when at least three matching symbols land on consecutive reels from reel number one. J to A runic royals make up the low pays, with axes, hammers, Freyja, and Odin bringing up the high pays. Landing a line of five matching symbols triggers a payout of 1.25 to 70 times the stake. Moreover, wilds come in handy here by substituting for any of the above-mentioned pay symbols. Wilds also pay up to 125x the bet for a five wild winning line.Raven Rising: Slot FeaturesRaven Rising slot - free spins gambleRaven Rising is accompanied by a simple but sturdy set of extras which includes tumbles, increasing multipliers, Ragnarök Free Spins, and a buy feature.TumblesThe tumble feature removes winning lines from the game grid and replaces them with symbols falling down from above. If another win lines up after the symbols have tumbled, the feature is triggered again. When no new wins appear, the tumble sequence ends.Increasing MultiplierIn the Midgård base game, the win multiplier increases by +1 whenever a set of winning symbols is tumbled off the board. When no more tumbles occur, the multiplier resets to x1 for the next base game spin.Ragnarök Free SpinsWhen getting 3, 4, or 5 Raven Scatter symbols in the base game, 7, 10, or 15 free spins are awarded, respectively. While the bonus round is active, landing 3, 4, or 5 Raven Scatters awards an additional 3, 5, or 7 free spins, respectively. Before free spins begin, players can take part in the Ragnarök Gamble if they choose to do so. A successful gamble moves players to the next highest free spins level (up to 15), while unsuccessful gambles lose all of the free spins. If there is one studio we can thank for the TV to slot crossover, it's got to be Blueprint Gaming. Blueprint has taken the show by both hands and squeezed every last drop they can wrangle out of it. Clearly, there is plenty of blood left in the stone, too, because now we've got Deal or No Deal Banker's Bonanza, an online slot that justifies its existence in two ways. One is the use of a Sweet Bonanza style scatter pays system. The second is pretty massive if you're a fan of the show. For the first time, the legendary Noel Edmonds has lent his voice to the game, showing up in the bonus round.Players who like the 'if it ain't broke, don't fix it' approach will be happy with how Blueprint has handled the audio-visuals. A show-inspired throbbing soundtrack beats away in the background, while upfront, players interact with a game grid surrounded by glowing orange lights and a bonus game trail. It's all very familiar, a little same-same, but banker-philes should be pleased with the look.DONDBB is a medium-high volatile game utilizing a 6-reel, 5-row grid matrix in combination with a scatter pays system rather than ways or lines. Basically, if 8 or more matching symbols are in view anywhere on the board, you've got a winner on your hands, and the cascade feature is triggered. Any device is suitable for taking on the Banker, allowing you to pick a stake from 10 p/c to $/€20 per spin.Appearing on the reels are nine regular pay symbols split into low pay commons and higher value symbols from the show. Starting things off are cherries, lemons, plums, watermelons, and bells, which are worth 2-8x the bet for 12+ in view. Then we get question mark mugs, letters, seals, and boxes as the premiums, paying 10 to 25 times the stake for 12+ on the grid. No wilds appear at any time, but there are mystery symbols which always transform into the same identical symbol.Deal or No Deal Banker's Bonanza: Slot FeaturesLand a win, and the cascade feature removes the winning symbols from the board. Symbols above them fall into the gaps, which can lead to extra wins. When enough repeat cascades occur, the bonus game is triggered.Bonus TrailWhen 6, 8, or 11 consecutive cascades occur on a single base game spin, players gain access to the Deal or No Deal Bonus round, the Super Deal or No Deal Bonus Round, or the Mega Deal or No Deal Bonus Round, respectively.Once triggered, the screen displays cash prizes on the left side of the screen and free spin prizes on the right. The difference between the three bonus tiers is the lowest one displays cash and free spins prizes, the Super Bonus displays fewer cash prizes, while the Mega Bonus only displays free spins.Players start by picking one box, which is saved till the end. Then, the round commences by opening the rest of the boxes one by one. Each time a box is opened, it reveals one of the prizes, which is removed from the screen. At set intervals, the Banker calls to make an offer. You can accept the offer and return to the base game or reject it to open another round of boxes. If you go all the way to the end, you open the box you initially picked and take the prize.Free SpinsIn free spins, a golden box multiplier symbol becomes active, bearing values of x2 to x100. After winning cascades end, any multipliers in view are added up and applied to the total cascade win. If 3 or more bonus symbols land during the round, +5 additional free spins are won.Deal or No Deal Banker's Bonanza: Slot VerdictIt's easy to lose track of how many Deal or No Deal slots Blueprint has released now, and the steamroller continues to power on. If anything, the DOND behemoth appears to be picking up speed, and the partnership between Blueprint and Banijay Brands, the license holder, seems as robust as ever. While the scatter pay system is one of Banker's Bonanza's attractions, bringing Noel Edmonds onboard is near enough a revolution. If there was something missing from previous DOND games, it was the conspicuous Noel sized hole, which Banker's Bonanza has effectively filled. The only way this could be topped is by having Noel's mug inserted into future DOND slots or getting him to guest star on Deal or No Deal Live.Let's plant our feet back on earth for a bit and go over Banker's Bonanza. It's alright. Nothing special if DOND means little to you. The box opening bonus game can be kind of fun. With a smidge of imagination, you can pretend you're in the hot seat, opening boxes, accepting or rejecting the Banker's offer, and enjoying the suspense. There are issues, though. The main one is the Banker's offers are pretty lame. On the show, contestants wrestled with offers reaching into the thousands of Pounds, making the decision to accept or carry on an extraordinarily tough one. In the slot, the decisions rarely get anywhere near as intense. Because the Banker's offers are often so unappealing, and the cash prizes themselves so low, there is very little incentive not to open all of the boxes. Sure, you get a taste of the show, but bonus rounds generally ended up as a race to the finish line to see what we had in the original box, making the whole procedure feel a bit drawn out and redundant.In certain gambling circles, another DOND release will be celebrated like a Eurovision after-party, and it won't matter a jot to them what a critic might have to say. Deep down, this is pretty predictable stuff, but the new bits should be received warmly, especially the inclusion of Noel Edmond's dulcet tones.

Title: Aurora Beast Hunter

In ascending order we get J-A royals, nunchucks (supposedly pretty useless in a fight but a quintessential 90s weapon), ninja stars, handguns, a freaking Gatling gun, and Aurora.Our heroine can land stacked while offering the best returns at 12.50 times the stake for five. On any base game spin, there is a chance of being awarded a random cash prize, a random wild, or a sticky wild stack.If it’s the cash prize, then at least one expanding wild or stacked wild is guaranteed as well as an extra payout of 1.5x or 2x. The random wild feature sprinkles 1 to 5 wilds on reels 1, 3, or 5. Lastly, the sticky wild stack feature awards expanded wilds with respins.Things heat up during the free spins which comes into play when 3 monster truck scatter symbols appear on reels 1, 3, or 5. Once triggered, players get to choose one of three options - The Sub, Danger Zone, and Sandstorm.Sandstorm comes with 12 low volatile free spins. Here, expanding wilds and stacked wilds award a cash prize of 1.5x or 2x respectively. Maximum wins from Sandstorm is 2,000x.Danger Zone comes with 8 medium volatile free spins. On every spin, 1 to 5 wilds are sprinkled over the reels in random positions. The most you can win from the Danger Zone is 3,000x.The Sub starts with 5 highly volatile free spins. On each spin, one reel is randomly marked. If there is stacked wild or an expanding wild on that reel, it becomes a sticky wild stack for the remainder of the feature. When a sticky wild stack appears, one more free spin is awarded. Payouts from The Sub max out at 5,000x.Aurora Beast Hunter: VerdictSometimes a developer busts out of their regular pattern to come up with something which may surprise a lot of players. The retro vibe and effects play a big role in making Aurora Beast Hunter one of Just For The Win’s better productions.Sure, the look won’t please everyone, it is an acquired taste perhaps. Those not into bright, silly sci-fi, dipped in nostalgic veneer may find it hard to stomach. For anyone into classic video games though, or the 1990s, or a slot that doesn’t take itself too seriously will have a ball.Like a lot of action movies, it pays to suspend disbelief and buckle in for the ride. Just For The Win has nailed the trip back in time well via bright graphics, heroic symbols, heavy metal sounds, and animations. In a pleasant twist, the gameplay and potential complement the looks. The three variable volatile free spins, along with the rest of the features broaden the game’s appeal, making Aurora Beast Hunter one of Just For The Win’s more likeable slots.For some old school styling, Aurora and her bevvy of beasts are well able to serve up some wholesome fun. On a side note, if you dig the era, it might pay to check out the chunkily rendered Hellcatraz from Relax Gaming.

Title: ThunderCats Reels of Thundera
review: ThunderCats Reels of Thundera: ReviewThe '80s animated cult show ThunderCats holds a special place in the hearts of many. The series follows a band of catlike humanoid aliens by the name of Lion-O, Tygra, Panthro, Cheetara, Wilykat, and Wilykit. Having escaped their destroyed planet for another world, they must find a way to make it their new home while thwarting various evildoers. Originally produced in Japan using American voice actors, the show was bought up and folded into Warner Bros in 1989 who still owns the right to the franchise.Having sealed the deal with Warner Bros, Blueprint Gaming now expands its already extensive portfolio of branded slots by adding ThunderCats Reel of Thundera to the list, a game built on the same template as other titles in the studios nostalgic collection of branded slots such as The Goonies, Mars Attacks!, and Beavis and Butt-Head. If you've played any of said games, you'll know what to expect. Utilising 5 reels and 20 paylines, it comes with plenty of random base game features, loads of bonuses and a feature gamble only for the bold. ThunderCats Reel of Thundera can be played from as little as 10 cents up to 200€ per spin, which makes it suitable for low-rollers, high-rollers and everyone in between.The overall production quality here is outstanding. The game comes with cartoon style artwork in line with the original series that will make any fan of ThunderCats wet themselves. With a sea of molten lava in the background and with catchy high-tempo music to set the right mood, on the reels you'll see J, Q, K, and A royals along with surfboards, nunchakus, ThunderTanks, swords and the ThunderCats logo. The latter, which appear super stacked on the reels, is the most rewarding giving you 50 times your stake for 5 on a full payline. The wild symbols substitutes for all other symbols bar the scatter and is of the same value as the top symbol.ThunderCats Reels of Thundera: FeaturesCheetara Lightning Dash featureIn the base game, the Awaken the Eye if Thundera can trigger randomly during any spin to give you 1 of 6 reel modifiers. This is what you can expect:Lion-O - applies wilds to the reels, significantly increasing the chance of a winning combination.Tygra - swipes the reels with a chance to turn them wild, any winning combination retriggers the feature.Panthro - strikes the reels linking between 2 to 5 reels together to deliver the same symbols.Cheetara - dashes over the reels and shuffles all symbols in view to new positions. This feature can retrigger up to 5 times.Wily Kit and Wily Kat - will apply Mystery Symbols onto the reels which all transform into the same symbol.Snarf - will apply scatter symbols to the reels, significantly improving the chance of activating the bonus.Moreover, four additional reel modifiers can trigger following a losing spin which can give you five of a kind wins, upgraded symbols, and symbol removals.Keep an eye out for the ThunderCats logo which is the bonus scatter symbol - 3 or more in view will trigger the bonus wheel which will eventually stop on 1 of the 6 bonus features. Worth noting is that we found the wheel to be disproportionally weighted, usually stopping on the two lowest ranking bonuses. Either way, once your bonus has been awarded, you're now offered the opportunity to gamble it in hope to win a better one with the risk having to walk away with a cash prize instead, or accept what you've been given. Once underway, this is what you can expect in the bonuses:Sight Beyond Sight - Pick an Eye of Thundera to reveal one of four outcomes: Lion-O (Cash Multiplier is increased); Thundercats Logo (Cash Multiplier values are upgraded); Mumm-Ra (will end the feature); Thundertank (takes you to another bonus). You can trigger any one of the five other bonuses if the ThunderTank comes up three times.The Black Pyramid - Here you get to select from emblems to reveal one of three outcomes. Lion-O (will move your marker along the pyramid); Thundercats Logo (upgrades the bonus at the top of The Black Pyramid); Mumm-Ra (will end the feature). Landing on an arrow will move you up The Black Pyramid - reach the top to trigger another feature.The Ever-Living: Free Spins - A multiplier visible on screen selects a random value on each spin between x2 - x5, multiplying any winning combination by the chosen value. During any spin, if two or more Special Mumm-Ra symbols appear in view, additional Ever-Living Spins will be awarded. During the retrigger, the multiplier randomly selects a value between x6 - x10 on each spin.Hear The Roar: Free Spins - During any spin, if a special Lion-O symbol appears in view, it will upgrade another symbol indicated by the image next to the reels. This can happen up to four times. When the free spins come to an end, you'll have a chance to win extra spins. Picking an Eye of Thundera will either end the feature or award additional spins.Thundercats Hooo! Free Spins - Any wild that appears in view will be held until the feature ends. Five extra spins are rewarded if you fill a whole reel with wilds.Ancient Spirits of Evil - Triggered by landing 5 scatter symbols, gambling to, or if the bonus wheel stops on the Ancient Spirits of Evil segment. The player selects from emblems to reveal one of five outcomes. Lion-O (will spin the wheel); Thundercats Logo (will move you to the next ring); Mumm-Ra (the feature ends); Red Arrow (more red arrows are added to the wheel); Upgrade (values on the wheel are increased). Landing on a cash value will replace that section of the wheel with a red arrow. Landing on a red arrow will move you to the next ring. Reaching the centre of the wheel will award the Ultimate Thunder bonus.Ultimate Thunder Bonus - Your total winnings from Ancient Spirits of Evil will be transferred to the Ultimate Thunder bonus. Here you will get to pick one of the ThunderCats to reveal a multiplier which will then be applied to your winnings.ThunderCats Reels of Thundera: VerdictWe'd be lying if we said we weren't disappointed when realizing ThunderCats Reels of Thundera is merely a reskin of The Goonies and other branded slots released by Blueprint. If those games didn't win you over, neither will this one. If, however, you're not too bothered by the obvious similarities in gameplay, and if you're particularly fond of these multi-bonus, feature-heavy slots that Blueprint has learned to master so well, you will undoubtedly get a kick out of playing this one.The various modifiers are well designed, the soundtrack is impressive to say the least, and the bright colours and inviting animation make it an all-around thrilling slot to play. A superb adaptation, ThunderCats Reels of Thundera accurately captures the fast-paced action of the series while also offering great potential of up to 10,000 times your total stake.

Title: Superstars
review: Superstars slot by NetEntSuperstars: Slot OverviewQuestion, have you ever watched an awards ceremony, like the Oscars and been enraptured by the star power and talent on display or repulsed by a perceived phoney backslapping look at us we're famous attitude? Bringing together five colossal characters has got to be easier when they are from casino games compared to real life. Some drew the conclusion that none of the three male leads wanted to come off weaker than the others. Fortunately, there's none of that going on in Superstars, where the characters happily share space on a 5x5 game grid, backgrounded by a big rainbow for this NetEnt family reunion.Superstars has been designed to run on any device, and lets players pick stakes of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. If the token lands on one, the values of multiplier prizes on the reels increase.Random – awards one of the Finn, Gonzo, Miss Banks, Space Wars, or Starburst features.Replay – replays the next Bonus feature if one is triggered.Final GameIf all of the spaces on the reels are filled with multiplier prizes, the Final Game is triggered. The squares on the game board are given values of 25x to 1,000x except the top right and bottom left corners which award Dice if landed on. Players enter the Final Game carrying the number of Dice they had in free spins. The maximum number of free spins plus the number of hearts is transferred into Dice for the Final Game. At times, when tv shows do an episode made up of snippets of past episodes, they can come across like wafer-thin filler, but Superstars, fortunately, doesn't feel like that. Instead, you get the impression that the NetEnt team might have had a bit of fun making this, running through their extensive back catalogue, trawling for popular characters they could rope into a single all-star slot and see what might happen.The result is a game that should be rather appealing to players who can name the stars. It's not mandatory to know all of them to enjoy the game, of course, but it might help. The base game is a little so-so since there really isn't anything special to it; NetEnt has saved the creative juices to pour them into a fairly elaborate bonus round. In a nutshell, the bonus round is a hold 'n win feature with a stack of extras to work your way through, depending on how Dice are won and rolled. As alluded to before, Superstars isn't a massive game, but when the stars are performing and the multipliers are adding up, it can go all the way through to 4,596 times the stake. Bigger than some of the games its characters are drawn from, smaller than others.Add up all of the bits, pieces, and characters, and you've got a pretty fun game on your hands. If you consider slots like Money Train 3 to be the acme of hold 'n wins, then Superstars may come over a bit lite. Still, Superstars isn't trying to compete in that division, aiming instead for a more general audience or players nostalgically warmed by the thought of having so much online slot star power brought together in one place.

Title: Rabbit Garden

Title: Phoenix Paradise

Title: Giza Infinity Reels

Title: Wild Wild Riches
review: Wild Wild Riches: Slot OverviewIt's been a while since an Irish slot passed our way, though for some reason these games tend to come in waves. Premiums are more in touch with their Celtic roots, including mushrooms, pipes, horseshoes, harps, and mugs of beer. This rule applies to the jackpots and multipliers symbols as well – there must be two wilds plus pots on reels 3 and 4 to activate them.Next are free spins which technically increase your chances of triggering the Money Collect Bonus. It starts by landing wilds on reels 1 and 2, as well the bonus symbol on reel 3. This gives 10 free spins, with additional wilds and pots of gold added to the reels. You are certainly never in doubt as to the type of slot you're playing even without the jolly chap present.One slightly new aspect is the Ante Bet option which wasn't as effective as it was hoped to be. During testing, the additional stake cost produced no noticeable change to the frequency of features. Pragmatic claim wins of 4,600 times the stake are possible, so any help cracking it is a bonus though. 20% extra for double the chance of features sounds like a bargain and it appears to affect the RTP positively too.The altered grid is alright, it means more gold pots can appear on reels 3 to 5, though it does feel a tad gimmicky. If Wild Wild Riches played out on a 5x4 grid, it wouldn't be much, if any, different to how it is now. Then again, perhaps we shouldn't complain too loudly when a developer attempts creativity, especially in a category as saturated as the Irish one is.As far as these types of slots go, Wild Wild Riches manages to stand out, to an extent. Title: Pirates Party
review: Pirates Party: Slot OverviewHere's a little thought experiment, no Googling; if someone mentions the words 'pirate party', how do you visualise it going down? Maybe there'd be casks of rum being consumed at a prodigious rate, a lot of cussing, maybe a punch up or two, depending on how friendly the pirates are, before a late night to bed, and a powerful hangover the next morning. Then again, maybe other pirate get-togethers were no more boisterous than a couple of half-pint shandies by a crackling fire after months at sea. If you'd like to see developer NetEnt's interpretation of a buccaneering shindig, come take a look at the online slot Pirates Party.The funny thing about Pirates Party is that at no time does it ever feel like an actual party. NetEnt has used a light-hearted cartoonish method to present buccaneering in the sort of salty slot where the sun always shines, loot lies around just waiting to be picked up, and the governor's offspring throws themselves at you for your hand in marriage. Matching symbols landing on three or more adjacent reels beginning from the leftmost side of the grid make a win. Helms are split into segments, each segment possessing a prize. Helm wheels cost a certain amount of tokens to spin:Blue Helm – costs 1 token to spin where there are prizes of 2x to 15x the bet.Green Helm – costs 3 tokens to spin where there are prizes of 5x to 50x the bet, plus free spins.Purple Helm – costs 5 tokens to spin where there are prizes of 10x to 100x the bet, plus free spins.The round ends when all tokens have been spent, and the wheels stop spinning. Once activated, players choose the free spins round they would prefer from these options:15 free spins with a win multiplier of x5 applied to all wins.10 free spins with up to 5 wild symbols may be added to the reels for the current spin.5 free spins with up to 2 wild symbols of 2x2 in size may be added to the reels for the current spin.Pirates Party slot - free spins with colossal wildsPirates Party: Slot VerdictPirates Party might not be an outrageously debauched event at a seedy dockside tavern of all-night alcohol consumption and wall-to-wall regurgitation, but it is a rather spirited event. This is a game where free spins take place beneath the water, and the human character symbols (as well as the animals) pack snorkels so they can breathe down there. Unrealistic, sure, not that we are calling for historical accuracy, just pointing out the sort of hilarity angle the game's shooting for. The feel-good factor is one of Pirates Party's selling points, creating the impression it is aimed at a casual, general sort of gambler, one which isn't fussed by a 3,046x max win figure. Dropping two 2x2 wilds onto a pay ways game board has promise, but getting more than one in view could be a challenge.And so wraps up Pirates Party, which was not by many measures the wildest soirée ever witnessed by humankind. It's not hard to see it appealing to certain gamblers, though, what with the popular pirate theme, its bright, cheerful theme use, injections of humour, and fairly wide range of features, even if many of them are old hat.

Title: Hell's Hogs 2 Squelin' Wheels

Title: Hula Balua

Title: Bankin' Bacon

In fact, our porcine friends have represented prosperity and wealth in Germany for centuries and is where some people say the origins of pig-shaped money boxes originated. Wherever they came from, they are prolific in slots, and Bankin' Bacon is another contribution to the pile of piggy, money, wealth themed games - this one from developer Blueprint Gaming.Blueprint has set Bankin' Bacon in an area that looks a little like Big Time Gaming's Royal Mint Megaways. This one is more cartoonish, though, which the studio probably felt obliged to do since it goes with the piggy bank theme. The game area sits at the top of some stairs leading to a plush bank with a nice glass-domed roof. It looks like a financial institution that does not welcome the regular populace in to deposit their monthly paychecks. This is the sort of place doing business with the aristocracy or high net worth individuals. Regular Joes get to admire the architecture from the outside. When Banker Spins trigger, however, players are let inside for a more democratic scramble for cash from the bank vault.Gaming is held on a 6-reel, 4-row game grid, which pays left to right on adjacent reels, producing 4,096 ways to win. It's unclear what the hit rate is, but in testing, either you scored from the collection system or were punished due to the low number of ways wins. It doesn't help that Bankin' Bacon has a noticeable low return to player value of 94%. As for the other numbers, the game runs on a medium/high volatility setting while offering stakes from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin.Having a snuffle through the paytable turns up a selection of 9 regular pay symbols. The first five are a bunch of bright 10-A card royals; then, there are bags of coins, stacks of banknotes, scales, and old-fashioned cash registers. There's a common theme here. For one, they pay out a conciliatory prize of up to 10x the bet when six of a kind hit. Secondly, when they appear in Banker Spins, their individual values are collected.Bankin' Bacon: Slot FeaturesIf you are familiar with the iconic slot Fishin' Frenzy, you'll quickly recognise the connection as the two games use a similar collection feature during free spins. Landing 3, 4, 5, or 6 gold coin scatter symbols awards 10, 15, 20, or 30 Banker Spins. Or, instead of collecting the awarded number of free spins, players can try their luck with the Mystery Choice. If the latter, a prize wheel spins to award either more or less spins than was originally won, and one cheque value for the full duration of Banker Spins. Set cheques means only one specific value will appear on the money scatters, which can be a benefit or a curse.Next, it's on to free spins where cheque and piggy bank symbols appear in any position. When both are in view at the same time, the cheques are collected by the pig, and their values are added to the free spin win total. If more than 1 piggy bank wild lands at once, all cheques in view are collected by all wilds one at a time. When Banker Spins end, the total value of line wins and scatter wins is paid.Bankin' Bacon: Slot VerdictOnce you realise Banker Spins are basically a copy of Fishin' Frenzy's, Bankin' Bacon ends up being pretty predictable. The base game knocks on in a jaunty manner thanks to the jazzy tune that proliferate in these sorts of slots, and the bright cartoon graphics. This part of Bankin' Bacon is quite good, giving the game a bouncy good nature. A few spins in, and the bounce starts to deflate as it turns into a case of sitting back through a feature free base game and waiting for Banker Spins to trigger.Bankers Spins are where players cast off their metaphorical fishing tackle and attempt to reel in cheques. Does anyone still use cheques outside the USA? Well, you'll want them to show up in great numbers during Banker Spins, which they do, but the piggy bank wild isn't anywhere near as numerous. It wasn't unheard of for Banker Spins to pass by without collecting a single cheque. Then again, other bonus rounds hoovered up cheque scatters like they were quite literally going out of style.One thing separating Bankin' Bacon from Fishin' Frenzy is the Mystery Choice feature. As you can imagine, this is one of those rolls of the dice that can go heavily in your favour if you're lucky – or, not. Get it rolling, and numbers around 2,000x should be possible. What spoils things is Bankin' Bacon's disappointing RTP, which unfortunately is low enough to be a deal-breaker. 94% is just downright tight and probably more than enough to send players into the arms of other piggy bank/wealth themed games. There are plenty of them out there, after all.Add it all up, and you've got a Fishin' Frenzy follow on which could've been a strong contender for anyone who likes the scatter collection feature these games are famed for. Yet, Bankin' Bacon went and put a trotter in the goodwill by that poke in the eye RTP value.

Title: Thor's Rage

Scatter wins of 8-9 OAK are worth 0.3 to 10 times the bet, while 12+ OAK hits pay 3 to 100 times the bet. Wild symbols substitute anything except scatters. After taking part in a win, wilds do not disappear in the chain reaction but transform into multiplier symbols instead.Thor's Rage: Slot FeaturesThor's Rage slot slot - free spinsOn top of wilds and chain reactions, Thor's Rage has multiplier symbols and a free spins bonus round with a persistent Total Multiplier.MultipliersMultiplier symbols have values of x2 to x1,000. At the end of a chain reaction sequence, the total win is multiplied by the sum of all multipliers to calculate the final winning total.Free SpinsLanding 4, 5, or 6 scatters awards 15 free spins on top of a payout of 5x, 20x, or 100x the bet, respectively. Hitting 3 or more scatters awards an extra +5 free spins.Thor's Rage slot slot - free spinsThor's Rage: Slot VerdictGates of Olympus was released a few years ago, in 2021, so Thor's Rage is a little late to the party. No matter, Red Tiger has come out with a competitor, which largely follows suit while making a few adjustments to help it stand on its own two feet. To an extent. First, there's the deity switch, where one was Zeus of Ancient Greek belief, this one is Thor of Norse belief. The wild mixes things up to a degree, and the way it reverts to a multiplier symbol after substituting in a win rather than just tumbling out of existence is a nice touch.The wild symbol on its own isn't enough to hide the fact Thor's Rage is very close in just about every other way to one of the most popular slots out there. But it's hard to judge Red Tiger too harshly for this since casino game makers regularly 'borrow' ideas from each other like kleptomaniacal magpies. Scatter pay enthusiasts were probably already well served by the slots already at hand, but well, for a Thor version with a wild to multiplier alternative, you could do worse than Thor's Rage.

Title: Turtle Paradise

We really do excel at destruction sometimes.Shame, because, amongst the other benefits turtles bring to the planet, they're pretty cute, especially the baby ones. Title: Aztec Wilds
review: Aztec Wilds: OverviewFans of Aztec themed slots are having a great year. There has been a good number released so far, and we now have Iron Dog Studios wading into the fray with their latest offering. What is it about the Aztecs that make them such fertile grounds for slot developers? It is probably the exotic imagery and the legends of gold that motivated European explorers and players alike. Whatever it is, the Aztec themed slots production line powers on. Let’s see how Iron Dog’s latest effort measures up to the competition.The first impression of Aztec Wilds is a game that hasn’t run with the theme like some of its competitors have. Yes, it looks exotic and jungle-y, but we could be anywhere – South America, Tahiti, even South East Asia. The game uses 50 coins per spin, so stakes start at 50 c/p and go up to $/€100 a pop. As you would expect with the tumble feature, winning combinations are removed to make space for new symbols to fall into and potentially create consecutive wins. Land at least four consecutive combos in a row to unlock the bonus round like so:4 wins in a row result in 14 free spins.5 wins in a row result in 16 free spins.6 wins in a row results in 16 free spins and a x3 starting multiplier.7 wins in a row result in 20 free spins and a x3 starting multiplier.8 wins in a row result in 20 free spins and a x6 starting multiplier.During the free spins round, each tumble increases the multiplier by x1 and applies it to the current spin win. No sticky wild or expanding wilds appear during the free spins round.Aztec Wilds: VerdictAztec Wilds is an okay game that feels like it hasn’t reached its full potential. For one, the theme is underutilised. If you replace the word Aztec in the tile with something like Tahiti you wouldn’t notice the difference. Yes, some of that stonework and the gold symbols have an Aztec touch, but it feels underdone. The three face mask symbols look like they are on loan direct from ELK's Tahiti Gold.Perhaps this sounds like nit-picking over small details. But there have been so many Aztec themed slots released this year that developers need to do something special to stand out from the bunch. We don’t quite get that with Aztec Wilds, neither in look, or gameplay. Players into the Aztec thing will feel short-changed by the lack of imagination used with the theme. Think of the inventive use of symbology and colour used in Phoenix Reborn for example. That one might not have been a classic but it sticks in the memory with its full reel flaming Phoenix’s. There is nothing overly memorable about Aztec Wilds. Almost every element has been seen somewhere else.What happens if we put all that aside and concentrate on Aztec Wilds as a standalone game? It fares slightly better. One saving grace is the attractive 6000 times the stake potential which will get players spinning. And the way tumble wins unlock free spins when four or more occur can be very tantalising. For example, when three cascades occur nerves pop as you cross your fingers for that elusive fourth win to fall. But still, we’ve seen that concept before as well. It is okay for slots to imitate other slots, to an extent. It isn’t unusual and is the most sincere form of flattery. Yet, if the slot in question is missing at least one major original aspect it runs the risk of falling flat.In contrast, Iron Dog’s previous release Pirate Kingdom Megaways used a well-worn theme as well. It didn’t have super amazing graphics, but it delivered gameplay that cut through all that to make it a solid entertainer. We’ve seen Iron Dog pull off compelling slots action, just don’t expect to find it with Aztec Wilds. If you are interested in this theme you might want to give the new Aztec Gold Megaways slot a crack instead.

Title: Troll Hunters 2

Title: Freaky Friday
review: Freaky Friday: Slot OverviewBack in 1976, Barbara Harris and Jodie Foster switched bodies in a comedy film called Freaky Friday, which returned to the big screen in 2003 when Jamie Lee Curtis and Lindsay Lohan reprised the roles. Bearing absolutely no relation whatsoever to either movie is an online slot also called Freaky Friday from software provider Stakelogic. As well as possessing a recognisable name, Freaky Friday is a Book of Ra spin-off, where expanding symbols appear in free spins, alongside an innovation called the Fixed Symbols Feature.While Freaky Friday might have a familiar name and core game mechanics, it looks nothing like the movies or slot previously mentioned. In this game, players find themselves in a laboratory with a scientist who appears to have nefarious hypotheses in mind. As well as appearing as the highest value symbol, the scientist stands next to the reel-set holding a syringe containing a fluorescent green substance, making one wonder where he plans on sticking it. Random paraphernalia litters the rest of the lab as a suitably eccentric soundtrack caps off what is quite a diabolically devious scientific scene.Freaky Friday is not what you would call a total Ra rip-off as Stakelogic has taken the time to push, prod, and pull at certain aspects of it in an effort to make something more original. One way they've done so is by adding an extra row to the reels and a few additional paylines. The result is a game board made up of 5 reels, 4 rows, and 20 fixed paylines. There are also two ways of playing the game, vastly different in both cost and opportunity. One is the regular mode, where stakes vary from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin; the other is by activating the Super Stake, which doubles the cost. The benefit of activating Super Stake is you get a Fixed Symbols Feature in free spins, though both ways of playing appear to generate the same return value of 95.82%.Before getting all giddy at the prospect of having twice the standard number of paylines, Stakelogic has toned down symbol values as a compensator. For instance, landing a full line of the top premium scientist symbol is worth 125x the bet instead of the customary 500x. Following him down the chain are electrified hats, face masks, brains, and pill bottles, worth 50x to 10x the bet for five of a kind. Next are chaotic looking 10-A royals as the low pays, paying out 2.5-5 times the stake for a line of five.Freaky Friday: Slot FeaturesAs is usually the case in these sorts of games, the wild/scatter symbol is crucial. As wild, the book symbol can complete winning lines by substituting any pay symbol. As the scatter, landing 3, 4, or 5 book symbols awards 2.5x, 25x, or 125x the bet, plus 10 free spins.Free SpinsBefore free spins start, one pay symbol is randomly selected to be the expanding symbol. After regular evaluations have taken place, if the expanding symbols in view can make a win, they expand to cover all positions on their reels. Bear in mind that expanding symbols can form wins from any reel and do not have to be adjacent to each other to do so. Ten free spins will be awarded whenever three or more scatter symbols hit during the feature, and the expanding symbol remains the same for any retrigger.Fixed Symbols FeatureIf the Super Stake is active when free spins are triggered, then the Fixed Symbols Feature will be available. How it works is when a Golden Wild Scatter symbol lands on reels 2, 3, or 4, that reel becomes a Fixed Symbol Reel. This means whenever an Expanding Symbol win can occur; the Golden Reel fills with the expansion symbol – even if one did not land on the Golden Reel. For example, let's say 10s are the expanding symbols and reels 2 and 3 are Golden Reels. If a 10 symbol lands only on reel 5, then reels 2, 3, and 5 will fill with expanded 10 symbols for a payout.Freaky Friday: Slot VerdictWhether Stakelogic was unaware of the previous films or were banking on a bit of name recognition, we'll probably never know, but the game is somewhat freaky, as far as 'Book of' slots go. It's not majorly out there like Book of Shadow, on the cutting edge of science where the line between reality and illusion blur, yet it's got one or two innovations worth checking out if this is an area of interest. Yet, there is a case of one hand giveth, the other taking away going on, as many of the new elements have some sort of counterbalance going on that limits their overall effectiveness.For example, the extra row and ways could've blown Freaky Friday up if Stakelogic had left the symbol values alone. Gone is the 5,000x (or more) full screen win these games are legendary for. In its place, a screen of scientists is worth half, at 2,500x the bet, even with double the paylines – some might consider the actual bet multiplier to be half that again when Super Stake is activated. It might be hard to play Freaky Friday without using the Super Stake, though, because the Fixed Symbol Feature is one of the game's main selling points and proved to be quite amusing during our test sessions.Paying extra for a feature you don't get when betting normally isn't something every player will be hugely excited to do. The problem is that without the Fixed Symbol Feature, Freaky Friday is a pretty regular expanding symbols game, albeit one with a few numeral shifts and a new theme. At times it felt like a little too much shuffling went on to balance everything out, and Freaky Friday might have made more of a mark if Stakelogic had loosened the leash to really get freaky. However, if you can stomach coughing up extra for a chance to see all that Freaky Friday has to offer, it does provide something of a unique experience, as far as 'Book of' slots go.

Title: Akiva: Claws of Power

Title: Gems Gone Wild Power Reels
review: Gems Gone Wild Power Reels: OverviewDeveloper R7 in conjunction with Red Tiger expands the Power Reels range in a Starburst(ish) slot titled Gems Gone Wild. While nowhere near as risqué as other 'Gone Wild' genres some might be accustomed to, it's not a super exciting game in general truth be told.Other slots in the Power Range have tended to employ some form of selling point, to boost their appeal. Something a little out of the ordinary to make you think, 'well the rest of the game might not be amazing, but at least it's got X'. It's not obvious from the outset what that might be in Gems Gone Wild, so let's have a dig to see what we can find.The first look isn’t bad, perhaps a touch plain, but there is a nice swirl in space effect going on. Visuals are backed by a housey/jazzy/funk track which you often come across in an outer space slot. The music is nice, not overly memorable, but a pleasant wee foot-tapper to accompany the game.If you've never played a Power Reels slot before the first glance can be a bit overwhelming. The first thing to know is that three or more adjacent matching symbols create a winning combo.The magic, if you will, is that combos can land anywhere on a line to payout. They must be adjacent though - it's not 'Book of Gems Gone Wild' after all. But, a paying combination could sit on reels 3, 4, 5 for example, or reels 6, 7, 8 let's say. Also, due to the number of reels, it is perfectly fine to have more than one winner on a pay line. So multiple symbol types can cause payouts from a single payline.Medium volatile, players can select stakes from 10 p/c at the lower end, up to $/€20 per spin for the higher rollers. RTP, meanwhile, has slipped since Zeus Lightning back into the sub 96% zone at 95.68%.The say size doesn't matter, but on the Gems Gone Wild paytable, it does appear to be the case. The eight regular pay symbols are all gems and the higher up the paytable you go, the bigger and more valuable they get. It maxes out with the circular golden one, where eight of a kind reaps a reward of 75 times the bet. The only other symbol in the game is the wild. Its core role is to substitute for any other pay symbol to create a win. Since more than one symbol combination can land on a payline, wilds will only connect with the highest paying type in that situation.Gems Gone Wild Power Reels: FeaturesGems Gone Wild - base gameGems Gone Wild is light when it comes to features which all revolve around wild symbols - the Super Wilds and Locked Wilds. Super Wilds appear at random on any spin, creating a block of wild symbols. Super Wilds may show up in 2x2 or 3x3 size.On any spin, random wilds may appear to trigger the Locked Wilds mode. In this mode, if new wilds appear on the next spin, the old ones are locked to the grid and connect for new wins. Otherwise, the old wilds disappear from the reels and the game goes back to normal mode.Gems Gone Wild Power Reels: VerdictGems Gone Wild is possibly the least exciting slot in the Power Reels range so far. There just isn't much to do or cross your fingers for. No sort of bonus game, no free spins; just like the great void of space where it all takes place, there isn't a whole lot of anything really.Other slots in the Power Reels range have had at least one sweetener to draw in a wandering eye. Zeus Lightning had the high RTP, Five Star some impressive potential, while Phoenix Fire the looks. Gems Gone Wild is the standout, managing to break with tradition by setting everything to 'meh'.Sure, there's the big reel set up, but the limitation of its low paylines don't help, and there is scant else taking advantage of its size. Ok, so winning combos can start on any reel, but Gems Gone Wild ends up like a 10-foot basketball player who can't dribble or shoot. Unless players are really into the theme, they'll be catching zees in no time.And yet, Red Tiger clearly know their stuff, so there is no doubt a segment of the market ready to lap Gems Gone Wild up. It is fast, straight forward gaming, and potential of 3,000 times the stake can technically be achieved on any spin - provided the Locked Wild feature literally goes wild.Unless gems in space or locked wilds/respin style features rock your world like nothing else, it is hard to think of many compelling reasons to give Gems Gone Wild much serious consideration.

Title: Trigger Happy

Title: Midnight Thirst
review: Midnight Thirst: Slot OverviewWhen regular humans wake up in the middle of the night with a parched throat, they can easily get a glass of water from the kitchen or wherever. Reaching a new multiplier level awards +3 free spins. On a winning spin, the progress bar resets to the last multiplier level reached.Level 1 – x6 multiplier.Level 2 – x13 multiplier, +3 free spins.Level 3 – x24 multiplier, +3 free spins.Level 4 – x41 multiplier, +3 free spins.Feature BuyThe bonus buy guarantees entry to the free spins round. Instead of just bashing away in the hopes of racking up as many wins as possible, Midnight Thirst is a balancing act of not winning for a while in order to start working through the multipliers and maybe end up with free spins. Then, when a win does appear on the reels, fingers crossed it's a significant one to make up for the wait, hopefully, made better by a multiplier that has patiently accrued.It's a tightrope act, in other words, that won't be to everyone's taste. Then it's back on the treadmill, starting the process from scratch all over again. The sitch perks up in free spins because the multipliers there are far weightier than those found in the base game, offering arguably the best chances of snatching glory – all the way up to 5,000x the bet at best.For something a bit different, Midnight Thirst could be worth a demo spin or two to see what's up. Title: Wishbringer
review: Wishbringer: Slot OverviewPrepare to do a bit of rubbing players; we're taking a genie-themed online slot from developer Hacksaw Gaming for a whirl. On a magic carpet? Entry to the bonus round can be bought as well for 110x the bet, granting 10, 20, or 40 free spins.Wishbringer slot - free spinsWishbringer: Slot VerdictThat was unexpectedly odd. Wishbringer did not seem like a typical Hacksaw Gaming slot but rather something a junior partner studio might have produced instead of the big daddy of the group. Then again, it's not so odd, considering this is a remake of Beam Boys, pulling in pretty much all of the features and mechanics of the laser-eyed cat game for reuse in a genie-themed one. Title: 7 Gold Fruits
