If 3 or more Gold Fruit Bombs land, they each explode to form a stack of Gold Fruit symbols with cash prizes filling their reels. After any line wins are awarded, players win all cash prizes in view, even if they are not on winning lines.RespinsDuring this feature, each position on the grid lands either blanks or Gold Fruit symbols holding cash values. To begin with, 3 respins are awarded, and when a new Gold Fruit symbol is locked to the grid, the respin count is reset. The total of all cash prizes in view is awarded at the end of the round. First, though, if a line win is created, any cash prizes on that line are multiplied by x2. A symbol can be multiplied more than once if more than 1 line win forms through it. Also, filling 15 positions guarantees a Big 7 prize in the final position.Big 7 PrizesFour Big 7 prizes may appear on '7' symbols on the rightmost reel. A Big 7 prize is awarded by creating a line with other '7' symbols in the base game or in free spins or by locking them in place during the respins round. The 4 prizes are the Big, Super, Mega, and Ultra, bearing values of 100x, 250x, 1,000x, and 5,000x the bet, respectively.Buy FeatureFrom here, players can buy a Bomb Spin, which is a guaranteed win with 1 or more Cash Bomb symbols for 40x the bet (RTP 96.5%), or access the bonus round for 80 times the bet (RTP 96.1%).7 Gold Fruits slot - respin bonus7 Gold Fruits: Slot VerdictThere was a thought that 7 Gold Fruits might have been related to 7 Gold Gigablox, also by 4ThePlayer, but aside from the glitzy classic slot exterior, both games are quite dissimilar from each other. The free spins round is more or less another altered run-through of the base game, with extras, which leaves the respins feature. Can't say it really does so, but if the brief was to design a mightily bright, glitzy slot with fruit, respins, new bits and more, then 7 Gold Fruits achieves its mission.

Title: Martian Miner Infinity Reels

This is because the default 3-reel, 4-row grid has been crammed into a tiny area in the centre of the screen, within a futuristic drilling device. The Teleport Reel Modifier occurs randomly in the base game only. When triggered, players are teleported to a random depth to complete the spin. During the spin, the high-paying gem symbols come into play to replace metal symbols.Access to free spins is granted when 10 or more reels are added. Fuel cell symbols land during this process and the number collected equates to the number of free spins for the bonus round. When the digger reaches certain depths in free spins (every 10 added reels), high pay symbols are unlocked and replace lower paying symbols. Also, 3 new symbols appear in free spins:Treasure chests award instant cash prizes.Fossils award additional free spins.Ankhs increase a win multiplier.Instead of waiting for free spins, you may be able to buy them if the option is available. There are three choices – 12, 16, or 20 free spins costing 50, 75x, or 100x the total bet, respectively.Martian Miner Infinity Reels: Slot VerdictWell, it's different, and some players might love the experimental off-world adventure. In an industry rife with copying or rehashing the same old format, themes, and features over again, originality is to be recognised. In saying so, Martian Miner could be so far ahead of the curve it's hard to relate to. One concern is players used to reels spinning up and down might need time to get accustomed to the sideways action. However, it's an acquired taste that will thrill or induce motion sickness.It's nice BB is trying new things, yet a few aspects of Martian Miner fall flat. For one, the grid feels squished. A lot of room is taken up by a static wallpaper-like background image, which sets the scene, then it just sits there doing nothing except use space. As well as the general strangeness, some of the smaller details don't quite fit either, such as the bonus game icons. What do Ankhs have to do with Mars? Is BB suggesting ancient Egyptians travelled the stars, leaving evidence of their mysterious journeys in their wake? Who knows, perhaps the team just liked the graphic.Moving onto gameplay, Martian Miner suffers the usual pros and cons inherent in most Infinity Reels games without doing anything to change haters’ minds or put the mechanic off for supporters. In some ways, the Infinity Reels concept has been put to good use for the bonus game, emphasising the mining theme as the machine burrows under the Martian surface. If you can trigger multipliers via Ankh symbols, they can make all the difference between a lousy round and a good one.Martian Miner Infinity Reels is one of those games so unusual, a demo is needed to form a concrete opinion about it. Who knows, it could be the game you never knew you needed in your life? Or, an annoying oddity that should be blasted to the red planet aboard the next probe and left there to ice over.

Title: Mega Pearl Gigablox
review: Mega Pearl Gigablox: Slot OverviewMega Pearl Gigablox is an online slot from developer ReelPlay, that is not only powered by Yggdrasil (via GATI) but is built around their Gigablox mechanic. It got us thinking, is there such a thing as a mega pearl? After some scouring of the web, we came across a treasure called the Pearl of Puerto. Now, you know, if someone has gone to the bother of naming a piece of jewellery, it's going to be something special, or expensive at least. Both apply to The Pearl of Puerto, which was found in the Philippines in 1996, is 67cm in length, and weighs a preposterous 34kg. It's basically a pearl the size of a small child. As to its value, some have priced it as high as $100 million…This brings us back to Mega Pearl Gigablox, which isn't going to fire off a win worth anywhere near that amount but does feature plenty of pearls as a consolation. It's also a game heavily steeped in Asian culture. In fact, Asian-ness literally oozes from every orifice. It starts with location, and the game grid has been plugged into the side of a dragon draped pagoda at the top of a mountain, while other mountains trail off into the misty distance. A blue, hazy clouded sky somehow gives the game a timeless quality, though this could be because looking at Mega Pearl Gigablox is like looking at countless other Asian themed slots offering the same sort of view. It's not unattractive, far from it, but pretty formulaic all the same.Digging deeper into Mega Pearl Gigablox's workings, we find a real mix of big and small numbers. On the weaker side, for some, is a low volatile math model churning out wins at a frequency of 21.1%. Potential, on the other hand, is well respectable at 16,297x (on paper, at least), while the RTP sort of hovers in between with a fairly average value of 95.03%. Playable on any device, landscape mode offering a better view on mobile, stakes of 40 p/c to $/€14 per spin may be set.The strong Asian-ness is just as prominent on the game grid as well, where all of the symbols possess a very cultural look. First on the paytable are four Chinese characters worth 1.25 times the stake for six of a kind, then there are flowers, lanterns, coins, and sycees, paying 2.5 to 5x the bet for a line of six. Speaking of lines, Mega Pearl Gigablox has 40 fixed paylines crossing across its 6-reel, 4-row game grid to land winning combinations on. At least three matching symbols are required to create a winning line. The dragon symbol helps here since it is wild, thereby substituting all symbols except the scatter.Mega Pearl Gigablox: Slot FeaturesGigablox itself is the most common feature in Mega Pearl Gigablox, which ReelPlay has complemented with a respins bonus game and a buy feature.GigabloxGigablox functions on every spin in the base game. It creates blocks of symbols from 2x2 to 4x4 in size anywhere on the grid. For example, one spin might join reels 1 and 2 together to create 2x2 sized blocks and reels 3-6 together to make 4x4 sized blocks, or any combination besides. You just never know what you are going to get, and a neat animation occurs when reels are spliced together. Larger blocks count for as many 1x1 symbols makes them up. Gigablox can be any symbol in the game, including wilds or scatters.Respins BonusLanding at least 6 pearl scatter symbols in the base game triggers the respins bonus round. Triggering symbols are locked in place and given individual values of 1-1,000x, then 3 respins are awarded. If new pearl symbols hit, they lock in place and reset the spin count back to 3. If pearl symbols exist in a square formation of 2x2 or larger, they combine to create Mega Pearl symbols. The value of the new Mega Pearl is twice the sum of the pearl symbols that combined to create it. The bonus ends when spins drop to zero or all positions are filled with pearl/Megapearl symbols.Buy BonusIf the option presents itself, players are able to buy the bonus round for the cost of 80 times the total stake. Once bought, a spin occurs, which lands at least 6 pearl scatters symbols to start the feature.Mega Pearl Gigablox: Slot VerdictMega Pearl Gigablox absolutely drips Asian culture from the moment it loads until the curtain is pulled on its pearl-encrusted bonus round. Sights, sounds, and atmosphere are about as Asian as it gets. This is a game designed with a certain appetite in mind, and the Asian market should be in slots Nirvana when firing up Mega Pearl Gigablox. To achieve this goal, however, ReelPlay has pulled out a number of cliches, meaning you won't see much here that you haven't seen before from a purely graphical perspective. The scenery is very familiar though quite pretty for what it is, and the soundtrack fits like a charm too.On the gaming side of things, the story is just as generic as the choice of visuals. Gigablox chugs along in the base game and might have benefited from a side modifier to help keep things interesting. Yggdrasil's mechanic does hold its own quite well, and its random nature keeps you on your toes to an extent, but a little something extra mixing things up wouldn't have hurt. The same can be said about the bonus round, too. What it does is okay - land pearls and hope they create Megapearls to level up their value. Again, a little something more wouldn't have hurt the game's appeal. The relative basicness doesn't hold back Mega Pearl Gigablox's potential, though, which tops out at 16,297x the bet.Add it all up, and you've got an ideal game for Asian-themed players looking for a low volatile yet high potential game with straightforward gameplay and cosy audio-visuals. Of course, anyone not in that category will find it tough to extract much joy from Mega Pearl Gigablox. For us, the standard looks, feels, and relatively basic features made Mega Pearl Gigablox more a soggy lone wonton of a game than an Asian feast.

Title: Hugo Goal
review: Hugo Goal IntroductionHugo Goal is a 3-reel video slots played on 5 fixed paylines. It's playable on all devices from as little as €0.05 all the way up to €100. Title: King's Mask Eclipse of Gods

Perhaps a lucky player, somewhere out there, in the real world, will strike King's Mask Eclipse of Gods on its best day, and we'll be able to see just how it happens - though given how rare those sorts of mega wins from Play'n GO seem to be, don't hold your breath.Without the big number, King's Mask Eclipse of Gods is a pretty average game. Title: Get The Gold InfiniReels
review: Get the Gold InfiniReels: Slot OverviewIn the Infinity Reels vs InfiniReels match up, there has been a clear winner when it comes to uptake and sheer number of releases. ReelPlay's Infinity Reels concept has soldiered on, through the ups and downs, a new slot powered by the mechanic dropping on a regular basis. InfiniReels from NetEnt, on the other hand, seems to have been pushed to the back of the features rack to gather dust. Kind of strange in a way because both releases to use it so far, Gods of Gold (NetEnt) and Dragon's Fire (Red Tiger), were decent games. Perhaps the two studios have been biding their time, cooking up something extraordinary to blow the InfiniReels series wide open.If you had a suspicion that innovation and attention to detail were to blame for the long wait between InfiniReels slots, here comes Get the Gold to destroy that hypothesis. Get the Gold InfiniReels is one of those games you can't even rib a studio about; it's so bad you just sort of wonder what happened. Whether a Red Tiger slot is good or not, it is usually hard to fault them when it comes to aesthetics. Their games generally have a polished, gleaming look that is easy on the eyes. Again, Get the Gold destroys this idea as well. Have you ever played an old point and click game or a text-based game where you typed in instructions and at some point had to play a budget mini-game within the game? Get the Gold InfiniReels gives off those vibes. It looks like Marty McFly when 1955 Doc Brown dressed him up to go back to the Wild West.The troubles continue when we get to the gameplay. InfiniReels are all about growing the grid, right? Adding reels when wins occur, drawing out ridiculously long winning combinations in order to make bank. Not so Get the Gold. Three of a kind triggers a win, and that's it. On to the next spin. Reels do get added at a later stage, but only when the Gold Rush phase is activated. Until then, the odd mining themed action is restricted to a 3x3 game grid, set in a body of water, with a hint of gold at the corner of the screen.Playable on tablets, desktops, and smartphones, players can set bets from 10 p/c to $/€10 per spin. A highly volatile game, max win is impressive at 10,000 times your stake, yet it does feel something of a challenge when you see what there is to work with. Default RTP is 95.72%, though Dragon's Fire's return was variable, so be on the lookout for this should you for whatever reason decide to have a blast on Get the Gold.Here's a quick look at the win information on the paytable. Six regular symbols appear here – fish, a water jug thing, hats, boots, pans of gold, and a shovel and treasure map. Landing 3 of these symbols left to right is worth a payout of 0.1 to 0.7 times the stake. Pay ways longer than three have their values added again for each reel added in Gold Rush mode to active win way combos.Get the Gold InfiniReels: Slot FeaturesLanding at least 1 Gold Cart scatter symbol on each of the 3 reels triggers Gold Rush mode. Each Gold Cart displays a prize value that is collected during Gold Rush mode and paid when the phase ends. During Gold Rush, each spin adds a new reel to the right-hand side of the game panel and continues to do so until no scatter symbols land for 4 consecutive spins, or the max win is reached. There are three types of Gold Cart scatters:Regular prize bearing Gold Carts displaying values of x2 to x50.Double scatters which double the amount collected so far.Triple scatters which triple the amount collected so far.Keep in mind, Gold Rush spins cost the same as regular spins, and when they end, the grid returns to its default 3x3 size.Get the Gold InfiniReels: Slot VerdictThere are a lot of these InfiniReels, or Infinity Reels slots filling line-ups now, and sorry to say but Get the Gold InfiniReels is one of the worst. It's hard to know where to begin, so let's start in the base game. When players pick this sort of slot, they presumably want to see reels build like there is no tomorrow. That's because extra reels extend winning combinations and often build a symbol multiplier at the same time. For some reason, and it is impossible to think of a positive one, Red Tiger has stripped this functionality from the base game. It's like ordering a cheeseburger and asking them to hold the cheese – what's the point? Without the key InfiniReels function, the base game is reduced to a dull-looking 3x3 slot.Land the requisite number of gold cart scatters, and the game does improve to a degree. Here the added reels feature finally comes into play, and it becomes possible to collect some gold (symbols). A fair number of carts tended to stack up in Gold Rush mode; even the doubler symbol cropped up on rare occasions. However, when four consecutive non-wins hit, going back to the base game was a major downer. Unbelievably, Get the Gold boasts massive winning potential for a Red Tiger game at 10,000x the bet. No one's doubting the statisticians, but scoring a payout even remotely close to 10,000x the bet feels like a titanic feat of fortune would be required.Red Tiger has a solid reputation for designing great looking slots, even if the rest of the game ends up lagging. Get the Gold can't even say that. InfiniReels/Infinity Reels slots have a bumpy track record. Sometimes they come together to produce something of value; Money Mariachi Infinity Reels, which came out around the same time, is a good example. Get the Gold, on the other hand, seriously weakens the bell curve.

Title: Pack & Cash
review: Pack & Cash: Slot OverviewIt's hard to believe, but not that long ago people had to order items by mail, phone, or maybe fax if the company in question was high tech. Once again, Play'n GO's busy schedule has pushed the team to conjure up a unique topic to make their game stand out from the bunch. Still, Play'n GO has picked some good ones to drive the action, so they certainly don't let the game down. Other positives include getting the win multiplier in all phases of the game, not just during free spins, which isn't always the case. Potential is a highlight too, where wins of up to 10,000x the bet are possible, with a probability of 1 in 100 million spins of occurring.You might not learn a lot about the intricacies of logistical planning while spinning Pack & Cash, but you'll find plenty of entertainment in its place. Like a well-oiled delivery outfit, Pack & Cash is the picture of efficiency. Everything runs as it should, stats are solid, and features are all high functioning favourites.

Title: Wolf Power Megaways

Title: Diamond Fruits Megaclusters

A good number of them strung together, the wild cannon fired, and we just missed out on free spins, yet the reward was relatively meagre. Like Relax Gaming's Cluster Tumble, the long yet low-value cluster wins were a regular source of amazement. Some might find this a total turn off, yet it's hard to look away as well. Like constantly tonguing a wiggly tooth, you kind of want to see what will happen next.Manage to push Diamond Fruits to free spins, and they play out in a fairly predictive manner. To this end, the most you can win in the base game is around 250x, increasing to 6,650x the bet in free spins. Whether players are down with this cuddlier side of Big Time Gaming will be interesting to see.After the initial dazzle wore away, Diamond Fruit came across as a collection of peripheral fireworks rather than a true paradigm shift. Title: Fat Rabbit

Title: Serengeti Gold

Title: Warrior Graveyard

Title: Deadwood
review: Deadwood Slot (Nolimit City): OverviewThe American Wild West has brought fame to countless actors and made writers wealthy. In other words, there's a chance to upgrade the feature to Shoot Out Gunslinger Spins here as well.The highlight and the key to the biggest wins is the Shoot Out Free Spins feature. If triggered during the base game, the player gets to choose between 10 Shoot Out Gunslinger Spins or 10 Shoot Out Hunter Spins.During this mode, the sheriff badges remain locked in position whilst activating the Shoot Out feature on each spin which transforms all low value symbols appearing on the three middle reels into wilds.Finally, for those who don't feel like waiting for the bonus to drop organically, there is always the choice to use the feature buy option. It might share some similarities on the surface, in particular in terms of the base game features, but the fact is that Deadwood is a completely different game in almost every aspect. For one, the base game might appear more forgiving due to the increased hit frequency and that extra chunk of RTP. It's a much busier slot altogether where features appear more frequently, even if triggering the bonus can be a bit of a challenge as the bonus seems to come in, on average, at a rate of around 1 in 200 spins.Surprisingly, the one area where things haven't changed much is the maximum win potential which, at 13,950 times your stake, doesn't stand out much from the 11,456x on offer in the original. Where NetEnt went all in with Dead or Alive 2 by raising the win potential from 10,000x to 111,111x, Nolimit City took a more cautious approach. Then again, it's significantly harder for smaller developers to "sell" their games to operators with extreme payout potential without the option to limit the bet size.Overall, Deadwood is an outstanding slot that manages to live up to most of our expectations. The most obvious of upgrades is in the visual department, but we're glad to see that the developer has avoided the lazy route of cloning the old math model. With a fresh approach, it allows for an all-around more unique and interesting gaming experience. As it stands, Deadwood is an excellent alternative to Tombstone and not necessarily a complete replacement.Don't MissThere's also a third instalement in Nolimit City's western-themed series of slots titled El Paso Gunfight xNudge. If Mode 1 or 2 is revealed, then the Pick & Click ends, and the free spins mode starts. If the other modes are revealed, the free spins mode plays out, then you return to the Pick & Click for more picking.Hot Dog Heist slot - bonus roundHot Dog Heist: Slot VerdictThe last lot of Play'n GO slot reviews before this, Lion Saga Odyssey, Sobek's Godly Spins, and Boat Bonanza Christmas, for example, have leaned on the meh side, and much due to its Wild North cloning status, so does Hot Dog Heist. Title: Katmandu Gold
review: Katmandu Gold: Slot OverviewIt might be a small step for adventurer Kane, but ELK's fifth instalement in their Gold series is a giant leap for the studio, and the first from them to offer a bonus buy option. Some go cautious when they try a new feature for the first time. Others just shut their eyes and leap into the unknown with reckless abandon. Possibly taking inspiration from Nolimit City, what it means is a two option bonus buy approach. It's not just a massive buy-in that makes Katmandu Gold stand out. It also offers some sweet features, a gorgeous location, and the highest potential found in a Gold slot so far.Before the grammar police come out to batter the title, 'Katmandu' is a legitimate way of spelling Kathmandu; it's just an older English version. It refers to the capital city of Nepal, located at the foot of the Himalayan Mountains. It's here our hero Kane has come to find solace. The poor chap is exhausted from his globetrotting ways in search of hidden gold and has come to the mountain kingdom to find inner peace. Kane being Kane, always falling backwards into success, has stumbled on ancient rumours of temple gold. Hopefully, he's not planning on ripping off artefacts from a local shrine.So far, ELK has done a fantastic job of setting games in the Gold Series in unusual locations, and Katmandu Gold is no exception. The familiar 6-reel, 4,096 win ways action area is flanked by two Buddhist inspired pillars, while an exotic temple can be seen in the far distance backlit by a low hanging Himalayan sun. You don't actually see the temple until the bonus game is triggered. Until then it lies hidden by a massive Oriental door. Like other slots in the range, the view dynamically zooms in and out as rows are added or removed from the stack. ELK is to be commended for creating a unique scene which melds perfectly with the audio to make a solid impact.Available on any device, Katmandu can be played from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Complementing the attractive visuals is an equally pleasing set of statistics. Three RTP levels are produced depending on whether the bonus buy is activated. It starts on a default rating of 96.2%, rising to 96.3% for the entry-level feature buy, and 96.4% during the Buy Super Bonus. ELK has raised the roof on the potential, as much to silence the critics as anything else, while the volatility of 7 out of 10 is high, though not savagely so. Keeping the action ticking along are about as many features as there are chakras, on top of a hit frequency of 22.4%.At the start of each drop winning combinations are formed when three or more matching symbols land left to right. There is quite a few of them too, starting on J-A as the lows, earth, air, fire, water, as the mids, with turtles, tigers, dragons, and Kane as the high pays. Values for six premiums range from 2 to 4 times the stake. The wild rounds this section off, substituting for anything except the bonus or the Ice Climber symbol.Katmandu Gold: Slot FeaturesOne great thing about the Gold Series is you always get something new, not to mention exciting when it comes to features. They aren't always a home run, but ELK puts in the effort each time, and it shows. In Katmandu Gold, players benefit from Avalanches, Big Symbols, Ice Climbers, Expanding Wins, Multiplier Free Drops, and of course, the brand new Buy Feature.Avalanches are at the core of it all, triggering after every win and removing the winning symbols in order to allow new ones drop for another chance to win. An extra row is also added to the grid, up to a maximum height of 8. Avalanches continue as long as wins keep landing.As seen in previous instalments, ELK loves Big Symbols, and have included them here as well. Big Symbols are pretty much just what you suspect - super, mega, and epic symbols of 2x2, 3x3, or 4x4 size that may appear on any symbol drop.Keep an eye out for the Yin & Yang looking symbol known as the Ice Climber. If 2 land, the Ice Climber feature is triggered. All symbols above the Ice Climbers are replaced with wilds or high pay symbols, while any empty positions beneath them turn wild. If the Ice Climber is triggered on the 8th row, then an extra row is added, taking win ways up to 531,441.Pay symbols or wilds may land with a gold arrow attached above, below, or both. This is the Expanding Win Symbol. When these symbols are used in a win, they expand in the direction of the arrow, replacing all symbols in their path.The main event is free drops, triggered when 3 or more bonus symbols appear on screen during a drop sequence. The number awarded is 10, 15, 20, or 25 drops when 3, 4, 5, or 6 bonus symbols are in view. Free drops can be retriggered too. The bonus game is a little different from Gold games of the past. This one comes with a win multiplier that starts at x1. Each time a bonus symbol marked with an 'X' lands, the multiplier increases by +1.Finally we have the bonus buy, where there are two options. The first is a typical 100x the bet outlay to buy 3-6 bonus symbols on the next drop. Then there is the Buy Super Bonus, which also gets you 3-6 bonus symbols, but where the win multiplier starts on 10x. This one doesn't come cheap though. You're looking at 500x the bet to activate the Super Buy Bonus.Katmandu Gold: Slot VerdictJudging by Katmandu Gold it appears there is a ton of gas left in the Gold Series. Not only has the team found an interesting new location to take players, they've designed some great features to pair with it. Katmandu Gold certainly adds a new dimension to the series, ending up being the best one so far.Crucially, Katmandu Gold does what the Gold Series is renowned for, namely piling on rows and win ways when consecutive combos roll in. Getting to the eighth row always produces a little rush, plus having a ninth one tucked away to blow up should you make it so far is an additional thrill. The game is full of little details like that which pop from nowhere to pull a bunch of wins in such as Big Symbols or Expanding Win Symbols. There can be runs of dead spins, but there is always the anticipation that just around the corner, is the drop to change everything.It's the win multiplier in free spins which is going to lead players to the best of what Katmandu Gold has to offer. In numerical terms, the best works out to be 10,000x the stake – the highest in the range to date. Some may rue the decision not to use the safety level mechanism, yet the inclusion of a multiplier more than makes up for it. This leads to possibly the most controversial aspect of the game, the new ELK Bonus Buy feature. Forking out 100x for free spins is pretty standard, but 500 for the Super version? Sure the multiplier starts on 10x, and the first time we triggered it 6 bonus symbols landed for the full 25 drops. Still, its hefty price tag puts it almost in Deadwood territory and really needs to be handled with care.In a nutshell, ELK has taken most of what made the previous four Gold games great, added some new features, improved the audiovisual experience, and upped the potential to produce a hugely playable game. In almost every respect this is the biggest one from the highly successful range. Katmandu Gold radically heightens the anticipation for what ELK will possibly do in the sixth instalment. The key question being, where on earth will we find Kane next?

Title: Cubes
review: Cubes: OverviewMaltese developer Hacksaw Gaming, the scratch card guys, are back with another slot in their Pocketz Series to while away some spare time. Continuing the approach used in Om Nom, Cubes is another minimalists dream using stripped-down visuals paired with simple, yet compelling gameplay. The resulting package is certainly unique, and while it won't appeal to everyone, Cubes has the potential to fill the void for certain player types or gaming moods.The first impressions raised half an eyebrow. Picture the result of a successful Tetris/Rubik's Cube Tinder hook up, and you're not far off the mark. A 5x5 grid of plain coloured squares sits before a greyed out cuboid background that lights up white from time to time.Accompanying the simple visuals is a relaxing tribal beat, rather soothing to the ears. If you close your eyes, you can effortlessly picture some guy in dreads busking on the street for loose change, tapping away on his Bali Steel Pan drum.Hitting spin sets the grid in motion, yet you can't really call it a spin. Instead of tumbles, or spinning reels, the 25 blocks leap into the air and land in a rearranged pattern. If 5 or more similarly coloured symbols appear connecting vertically or horizontally, then extra squares are added to the grid, expanding it to 7x7 in size.Now, if the original combination increases in size, or new winners land, the process repeats up to a maximum grid of 11x11 in size. Chain reactions continue until no new clusters or expanded combos appear; then the win is calculated and paid out. That is unless, a particular set of clusters form, triggering free spins – more on this in the features section.Playable across all devices from 20 p/c up to $/€100 per spin, , and particularly optimized for mobile devices, the math model players get is a medium volatile one with a default RTP rating of 96.35%. The hit rate is theoretically quite high at 31.94%, but it didn't always feel like that. During testing, swathes of dead spins would occur until something interesting happened. At least the soundtrack is a relaxing one in those moments.The symbols used in the game are as basic as it gets. There are six different squares, coloured green, yellow, red, light blue, purple, and dark blue. Interestingly, the squares all have the same value from 0.10x for a 5 square cluster up to 40x for clusters of 25+. So that's it for the symbols, there is no fussing about with wilds or scatters around here. However, there are a few features padding out the tetragonal gameplay; it's not all shuffling cubes about.Cubes: FeaturesKeeping play interesting, there are three features to look out for. These are the Middle Multiplier, Free Spins, and the Colour Blast! (their emphasis, not ours). Every spin during the base game has an 'X' on the middle cube. If this cube is part of a winning cluster, the X reveals a multiplier that is applied to the win. The number of cubes involved in the win adds 1 to the multiplier up to a maximum of x22.Free spins are triggered by landing a number of different coloured clusters. Whenever a uniquely coloured cluster lands, one letter from the word CUBES above the grid lights up. If you manage to illuminate the whole word, then 10 free spins are awarded along with a random colour. All wins in that colour become sticky for the duration of the free spins feature. During free spins, the size of the grid is also sticky, so it does not reset between spins.The final feature is the Colour Blast which is only possible to hit on free spins. Should players reach a cluster of 70 cubes during the free spin mode, then they are awarded an instant win of 2,500 times the bet.Cubes: VerdictWell, it's safe to say that Hacksaw Gaming is the scratch card guys no more. Cubes once again demonstrates the team's knack for developing highly playable slots. While Cubes is not a high impact game offering anything particular unmissable, there is an allure to it. Like Hacksaw's previous slots, Cubes has a certain x-factor that makes it easy to justify having one more spin. Like Tetris, there is something thrilling about getting shapes to line up in a pleasingly geometric fashion - even more so when those shapes payout.Not that we are talking about huge wins when they do. At full power, Cubes can produce rewards of up to 3,167 times the bet. So no, not massive sums of cash, but possibly enough to satisfy those that dig the unusual gameplay and math model.The Colour Blast is a nice touch if you can make to the free spins. That in itself proved to be an almost Herculean task during testing. If it's all-time wins you're after, it might be worth taking a look at Hacksaw's fixed jackpot slot The Haunted Circus for potential multi-million Euro payouts.To sum up, Cubes is a thoroughly modern game for the smartphone generation. Easy to play, light-hearted, while still offering the odd decent win. Clearly, Cubes isn't one of those massive, high volatile, high potential slots you make it a personal mission to crack. But, that's not its intention, nor that of the series. Cubes is a game you can easily envisage players firing up on their phones to kill a bit of time with – which is pretty much the definition of the Pocketz Series right there.

Title: Beat The Beast: Mighty Sphinx
review: Beat the Beast: Mighty Sphinx: OverviewThunderkick returns with the second slot in their Beat the Beast series. Five are planned, and each one is aimed at 'brave players’ – Thunderkick's words. Number one in the series took these brave players beneath the sea to take on the mythical Kraken in Kraken's Lair. The follow up heads in the opposite direction to the heat and dust of Egypt and all the symbology this popular theme offers. So, after grappling with a multi-tentacled horror from the deep, players move back to much more well-trod ground in Ancient Egypt.The first you'll probably notice is that Mighty Sphinx looks very much the same as Kraken's Lair did - aside from the background, and a few symbol and colour changes, of course. As expected, the setup is the same too, 5 reels, 3 rows, and 9 paylines on which to line up winning combinations. The bet range too remains the same as always when it comes to Thunderkick slots allowing you to choose to play as low as 10 p/c per spin, or as high as $/€100. Interestingly, whilst Thunderkick's stated aim with the series was to produce a line of classic slots with modern twists, there doesn't seem to have been much twisting for the sequel.The pleasingly classic, yet modern, graphics with Kraken's Lair lose some of their charm the second time around being so analogous. But it is nothing too detracting. When it comes to the paytable, similar styled symbols are used as before and are split into low, medium, and high pay tiles. Low pays are 10-A royals, while medium pays are the Sphinx statuette, the scarab, Ankh, and Khopesh Sword. The high pay is the winged Sphinx who is worth 250 times the stake for a line of five – half what the Kraken was worth, as a comparison.As to forming winning combinations, low pays need at least three of a kind; the mid and high pays only two. The final symbol is the Sphinx Emblem, which is the scatter and the wild. As a wild, it can substitute for any other symbol.Being a beast of a slot, or at least part of the Beast series, means a highly volatile math model powering the game. Another critical figure is RTP which clocks in at 96.14%, or 0.02% higher than Kraken's Lair for the statisticians out there keeping score.Beat the Beast: Mighty Sphinx: FeaturesWild upgradeAiming for an old school slotting experience, the game is somewhat light on features although that doesn't make it less of a game. During the base game, the Mystery feature may trigger randomly on any spin. When activated, up to 3 Sphinx Emblems wilds/scatters are randomly placed on any reel at the beginning of a spin. Keep in mind too that Sphinx Emblems pay out 2x, 20x, and 200x for 2, 3, and 5 of a kind.The highlight is the Free Spins feature which starts with 10 spins when 3 golden Sphinx Emblems appear in view anywhere on the reels. At the beginning of every spin, 1-3 golden Emblems are placed randomly on the reels. If 3 Emblems are in view they award 5 extra spins - half of what Kraken offered if you were wondering. When free spins are retriggered, they activate the Wild Upgrade feature. This feature transforms one mid pay symbol into a wild symbol.Beat the Beast: Mighty Sphinx: VerdictLet's begin the verdict by acknowledging that as a standalone, Mighty Sphinx is a decent enough game with nothing particularly bad about it. As a continuation of the Beat the Beast series, it might be something of a disappointment for some though. You typically expect sequels to be a bigger experience, as producers feel the pressure to outdo the original. This applies across the board, from movies, games, books, and slots. Mighty Sphinx is one of the few that dares to go smaller. Kraken's Lair kicked off the Beat the Beast Series well, with a fearful character, some interesting features, and nice potential. The sequel is a bit of a lightweight in comparison, with most aspects having been copied or toned down. This includes, looks, features, and one of the most important aspects for many players – max payout.At 4,444 times the stake, the potential is significantly lower than Kraken's Lair was. There are no major reasons why not to play Mighty Sphinx but none super compelling either, unless you have completely fallen for the beast beating concept.Thunderkick churns out well made, fun games on the whole, but you get the impression something held them back when making Mighty Sphinx. It's a shame because the hyped Beast series is a great opportunity to really cut loose, throw the gauntlet down to the big guys and stake a claim. Hopefully, Mighty Sphinx is a case of shifting into a second gear coast for a spell before injecting the nitrous oxide. Perhaps, the Beast series is on the cusp of taking players somewhere weird and wonderful that knocks socks off and gets the community talking. We live in hope.

Title: Starburst Galaxy
review: Starburst Galaxy: Slot OverviewStarburst is one of those iconic slots that gamblers tend to sort of bump into or hear about sooner or later on their travels. Designed by iGaming veterans NetEnt, it was a popular slot on release in 2012 and has lingered in the gambling consciousness, or unconsciousness, ever since. The game's maker returned to the cosmos for Starburst XXXtreme around 9 years later, and for whatever reason, the team has made a sequel. The original Starburst slot was an ultra-simple game, and the initial expectations were that Starburst Galaxy would follow suit. Spoiler alert: it's not simple, being rammed with the sort of features the first Starburst wouldn't have dreamed about 12 years ago.The original slot was held out in the cosmos far from our beautiful blue planet, and so is its little bro (or sis) Starburst Galaxy. The graphics have been updated, but the familiar symbols and trippy sound effects hearken back to the earlier slot. There's not much more to say about the front end than that, really, other than mentioning the pleasant way Starburst Galaxy manages to be both strangely new yet cosily familiar in the same instance, like swapping hands for, well, never mind.Starburst Galaxy slot - base gameStarburst Galaxy pushes the gaming grid so its 5 reels hold 5 symbols each and has removed paylines from the equation. To win you some loot and get the features moving along, at least 3 identical adjacent symbols in vertical or horizontal lines must land - winning combinations can begin from any position on the reels. Volatility has been rated as medium-high, and the most desirable RTP is registered at 96% no matter how you play - regular 20 c to $/€28 per spin or using the "Elevate" feature buys.The pay symbols are purple gems, blue gems, orange gems, green gems, yellow gems, a 7, and a BAR symbol. Five OAK wins are worth 2 to 20 times the bet, though when the reels expand, 7 OAK wins pay 10 to 250 times the bet. Any win triggers the Avalanche feature, as do 3 scatters when they disappear from the reels. Winning symbols are removed and replaced by symbols dropping, repeating like this until there are no more wins.Starburst Galaxy: Slot FeaturesStarburst Galaxy slot - Galaxy Star feature in playAs for features, Starburst Galaxy is the polar opposite of Starburst, brimming with Avalanches, wilds, Feature Generator features, a Galaxy Star, a Galaxy Meter, a Mega Star, a Multiplier Collect Meter, and feature buys.Wild SymbolsWhen a win without a wild in it is removed, a wild symbol is placed in the centre area of the vanished combination. If 2 winning combinations intersect, a wild for each win is placed - unless they intersect at their centres, then one wild is placed. Wild symbols substitute for all symbols except scatters.Feature GeneratorIn the base game, each winning combination progresses the Feature Generator. Every 5 winning combinations in a row randomly awards one of these 5 modifiers, one by one:Destroy - removes 1 or more random symbol types from the grid.Random Wilds - replaces 3 to 9 pay symbols with wilds.Expanding Wilds - turns all wild symbols on the reels into vertical stacks of 3 wild symbols.Line Transform - fills a row or reel with a random pay symbol type.Upgrade - upgrades 1 or more random symbols of the same type on the reels to a symbol type with a higher value.Galaxy Star Feature and Galaxy MeterThe Galaxy Star feature is activated when the fifth feature on the Feature Generator is awarded. The gaming area expands to 7x7, and a 3x3 wild is placed on the reels. After wins are calculated, winning symbols vanish, and 4 to 8 wilds appear Reactoonz style. When there are no more wins, all awarded features left in the Feature Generator are activated.The Galaxy Meter activates when the 3x3 wild appears on the reels. Each winning combination is added to the Galaxy Meter. Each time it reaches 50, the Galaxy Star feature is awarded, activating when there are no more wins. After reaching 50 on the Galaxy Meter, it starts from the beginning, and the rest of the wins contribute to it.Mega Star Feature and Multiplier Collect MeterEvery 3 scatters on the reels in the same spin award the Mega Star feature. After the Avalanche, when there are no more wins, a 2x2 wild is placed on the reels where there are no wild symbols already. When wins are evaluated, winning symbols disappear, and 2 to 5 regular wilds are placed on the reels during the next Avalanche.The Mega Star activates before the awarded and not activated features in the Feature Generator do. When the Mega Star triggers, 1 or more scatters may have multipliers of x2 to x25. The multipliers start the Multiplier Collect Meter, which shows all added multipliers that apply to all winning combinations till the end of the game round.Elevate FeatureIn-game features can be activated by the Elevate feature. The choices are:Bonus Boost - 3x the bet, increases the chance of reaching the Galaxy Star.Mega Star - 10x the bet to activate the Mega Star feature. One free main game spin is guaranteed to have 3 scatters.Boosted Mega Star - 50x the bet. Activates the Mega Star and the Multiplier Collect Meter. When the feature is activated, 1 free main game spin guarantees to have 3 scatters to activate the Mega Star. At least 2 scatters will have multipliers.Galaxy Star - guarantees reaching the Galaxy Stay for 100x the bet.Galaxy Star Bonanza - 500x the bet. Activates the Galaxy Star with 5 awarded features in the Feature Generator and a random multiplier of x2 to x75.Starburst Galaxy slot - Galaxy Star Bonanza feature in playStarburst Galaxy: Slot VerdictThe shift from Starburst to Starburst Galaxy is like that moment in a rom-com when the bookish nerd who sits at the back of the room avoiding attention dramatically removes her glasses and lets her hair flow free (in slow motion), transforming from someone none of the hunks would look at twice at to uber babe that everyone suddenly wants. The two games are like night and day. Mechanically, at least. Audiovisually, Starburst Galaxy has a sweet acknowledgement of the past going on, but with upgrades to make it more energetically modern.Gameplay-ise, it feels like NetEnt took a leaf out of Play'n GO's handbook, as echoes of slots like Moon Princess and Reactoonz reverberated through the review. Starburst Galaxy has the recognisable task of landing horizontal or vertical line wins anywhere on the board, removing them, dropping a wild, and collecting various items to charge up collection meters for feature releases or progression. Quite a mouthful, and quite a lot of new things (new for Starburst) to try to trigger. Make sure you're belted in for the winning potential reveal, as Starburst Galaxy's 25,000x is like the Saturn rocket that powered the Apollo program compared to Starburst's less explosive Big Tom Thumb.Starburst Galaxy really did not turn out the way it was initially expected to. There were expectations that NetEnt would stick closer to the original than it has done. While links to the previous game exist, such as the looks, sounds, and certain wild trickery, Starburst Galaxy has a shed load of extras to experience, offers far greater winning potential, and manages to successfully blend the old and the new, nostalgia and forward-thinking, to create a sequel 12 years after the original dropped which actually feels relevant rather than a needless trip down memory lane.

Title: Risqué Megaways
review: Risqué Megaways: Slot OverviewRisqué Megaways is a Moulin Rouge style cabaret-themed online slot from Red Tiger, powered by Big Time Gaming's popular game engine. Picking a word like 'Risqué' for a title is a perilous move. If the game doesn't live up to its claim, there's a danger of coming across a bit hollow. On the other hand, few things silence jaded critics like nailing a big boast. Risqué Megaways falls somewhere between these two extremes, being neither outrageously risqué nor overly puritanical. Let's take a look.'It's Showtime!' is the game's catchphrase, and the visuals have no trouble living up to their end of the bargain. Risqué Megaways' game grid takes centre stage, literally, as if you're seated in a darkened room at a live show. Players waiting for a lewd performance to commence may be a little disappointed. Risqué Megaways is 'burlesque' in the way a PG film might use the word. Good clean fun, rather than anything particularly racy. The flashy looks are nicely done, though, and are the sort of ostentatious display Red Tiger excels at.As for the game's math model, it's not quite as 'risqué' as some hardcore gamers might hope for. I may be highly volatile, and the RTP a tad below the 96% mark, but the max win potential isn't exactly wild and crazy at 5,250 times the stake. If you're ok with the numbers presented, Risqué Megaways can be played on any device and allows users to set bets of 10 p/c to $/€20 per spin.Getting technical, the main game grid is made up of 6 dynamic reels holding between 2 to 8 symbols, plus there are 2 bonus reels holding 4 symbols each above and below the main panel. When each reel is full to capacity, players are furnished with 321,489 ways to win, much more than the typical Megaways set-up in other words. To win, landing at least three matching symbols from the leftmost reel is needed, of which there are nine regular pay symbols - these are four card suits, paying 0.4x the bet for six of a kind, then boots, cocktail glasses, hats, perfume bottles, and microphones. Six of a kind premium wins are worth 0.6 to 2 times the stake. Also, chain reactions trigger after every way win, removing winning symbols and letting those still on the reel drop down into the gaps. If a new win forms, another chain reaction is triggered.Risqué Megaways: Slot FeaturesWhen it comes to features, the main events are Fan Symbols, Wild Super Symbols, free spins, and a gamble option.Fan SymbolsFan symbols appear on the upper or lower bonus reels. If a fan symbol on the top and bottom reel are aligned, they unfold to cover the whole reel and display either a random pay symbol or a Wild Super Symbol. Whatever symbol is revealed it comes with a win multiplier of x4 to x9. In the base game, these full reel symbols lock and reveal a new random symbol on each spin until it participates in a win. If it is Wild Super Symbol, it remains in this state until used in a win. If more than one pair of fan symbols hit, they reveal the same symbol when they unfold.Free SpinsLanding 3 scatters in the base game awards 10 free spins. While free spins are active, any scatter in view awards an additional +1 free spin. A win multiplier appears in the bonus round, starting at x1, and increases after each win by +1 - up to a maximum of x20. Any fan symbols that reveal a symbol in free spins stay locked until the end of the feature, revealing a new symbol on each spin. Like before, full reel wilds remain wilds until they are used in a win.Risqué Megaways: Slot VerdictRisqué Megaways isn't tremendously risqué. There's the leggy Wild Super Symbols, but players signing on for some smutty reel action might be unfulfilled. While Risqué might not have been the word we'd have used, the game is glitzy, in an Off-Broadway theatre type way, so there is plenty of glam going on. Red Tiger tends to fill their games with glossy imagery anyway, so they were probably right in their element when designing Risqué Megaways.The headline here is arguably the wild multiplier, a feature that has turned up in quite a few Red Tiger slots by now, most notably in games such as Piggy Riches Megaways, What the Fox Megaways, Hustling, and Doggy Riches Megaways to new a few. Title: Monopoly Heights
review: Monopoly Heights (Bally): OverviewMonopoly Heights is the latest instalment in the ongoing Monopoly franchise which continues to expand. Title: Ark of Mystery
review:
Ark of Mystery - IntroductionQuickspin has some seriously talented artists at hand. Central to the game is the special multiplier symbol and the wild respin feature which both can come together to award quite decent wins as you will see.
Ark of Mystery is comparably simplistic in design, yet classy and arty at the same time. The somewhat stereotypical quintessence of ancient Egypt is captured with a backdrop illustrating what appears to be a treasure tomb flanked by two pillars. They have always produced entertaining slots of high quality, but were slow to recognize the demand for high variance and massive potential. Title: Poison Eve
review: Poison Eve (Nolimit City): OverviewPlayers looking to spin reels in a fantasy world have the new slot Poison Eve from Nolimit City to try. The vibe might be peaceful and calm at first, but the math model can produce gaming sessions that are anything but. When you see Poison Eve do its thing, the high volatility and low action base game makes more sense.Poison Eve is quite an entertaining slot, it’s not as gripping as Nolimit’s last one Dragon Tribe was (in our humble opinion), but definitely has its good moments. Potential wise, being able to hit 2,000 times the stake on one spin is an attractive proposal. That is easier said than done though as you would expect - five Poison Eves is all it takes though which is a tantalising proposal and adds some compulsion to the gaming. Get the Flower Power feature on a good roll, and you might be able to tap into even higher potential.If you are looking for a bit of enchantment, and can put up with some staggering runs of go nowhere spins while tracking down bigger wins, you might find something of value with Poison Eve.

Title: Anna Van Helsing Monster Huntress

Title: Samurai Code

Title: Banana Odyssey

The music injects plenty of cheer, though, providing the perfect counterbalance to the unorthodox visuals.Saint Nicked slot - base gameAs for the technical side of things, pressing the bet menu button gives you betting options ranging from between 20 p/c to $/€40 per spin. Any device may be used to get the 'bad' Santa experience, occurring on a grid that starts at 5-reels, 3-rows in size, though this can expand during free spins.At the default grid size, players have 243 ways to win by landing matching symbols from the first reel onwards across consecutive reels. 10 through A card royals make up the low pays, worth 1x the bet for five of a kind, while the highs are fluffy handcuffs, pressies, glasses of liquor and gingerbread men, and Rudolph. Sub Symbols have values which are collected by the Bar Meter. The Bar Meter also displays a trigger value and may display a safe point. When enough Sub Symbol values are collected on a single spin to reach or exceed the trigger value, the next Advent Calendar prize is awarded. The Bar Meter resets on the following spin, either back to zero or to a Safe Point if the Safe Point value was reached or exceeded on the current spin.Happy HourAt random, Happy Hour may trigger on any base game spin, adding a number of Sub Symbols to the reels.Advent CalendarWhen the Advent Calendar is triggered from the Bar Meter, players click the lowest available number (from 1 to 25) to reveal a prize. We're used to the usual hose-down of Xmas-related slots as the end of the year draws near, which are often older games sprayed in snow or have had a skin change to be set in a scene of domesticity. Title: Christmas Tree
review: Christmas Tree: Slot OverviewDeveloper TrueLab Games gets their Christmas spirit well and truly on in the unimaginatively titled slot Christmas Tree. Released through Yggdrasil’s YGS Masters program, the slot celebrates the most recognisable icon of Xmas, the humble tree. TrueLab has plonked one on screen to host a grid slot offering an elves workshop of features.Due to the similar shape, Christmas Tree is vaguely reminiscent of Play’n GO’s slot Gold Volcano since both are arranged in a triangular shape. TrueLab has gone for the full Winter Wonderland look, lavishing on purple-hued snow, a snowman, a warm cosy house in the background, and even a star like the one that led the three wise men to Bethlehem. It’s hard to think of much else Xmas related the studio could have stuffed in. It’s so in-season will anyone want to play this on boxing day (or later) when they are stuffed with roast meat, eggnog, and their presents have failed to live up to expectations?Christmas Tree may be played on any device by first selecting the appropriate stake from 40 p/c up to $/€40 per spin. Christmas Tree packs a surprisingly high potential, and while attempting to crack it, players theoretically enjoy a win every three spins or so where the hit frequency has been rated 31.6%.Played using a 6 row high grid in a 2-3-4-5-6-7 formation, each ascending row has one less symbol than before until the top one holds just two. When five or more matching symbols connect diagonally, you have a win on your hands, and the cascade feature is triggered.Things stay festive for the paytable too, starting with three decorations in green, blue, and purple as the low pays, followed by candy canes, sweets and bells as the mids. Next, come two premium symbols – Santa and an Angel. The final regular symbol is a snow globe wild which substitutes for anything except the Mystery Symbols.Christmas Tree: Slot FeaturesCascades are the most common extra that can lead players onto most of the features if enough of them occur. On the side are two random extras popping off the odd win or two every so often.Starting with the randoms, one is the Blizzard feature which appears when no more wins in a cascade sequence occur. A cold wind blows across the grid, dropping 3-9 mystery symbols in random positions. These mystery gift boxes then transform into the same symbol – pays or wilds. Infectious good cheer makes Christmas Tree an apt option for the season. Title: Ghost Glyph
review: Ghost Glyph: OverviewDeveloper Quickspin deepens their crush on the grid slot format with the spooky(ish) game Ghost Glyph. This one is concerned with gaining entrance to a haunted house where the free spins phase of the game is located. While camped out on the driveway, players get a bunch of integrated features driven by a host of friendly ghosts.The paranormal activity takes place on a 7x7 grid at night in an expensive tree-lined part of town. Visually, the studio has struck a tone that matches the gameplay well, with cute little symbols covering the game area while big bright ghosts weave in and out when brought to life. At the end of the day, stats will possibly determine whether the game is your cup of tea or not. For one, this feature can create consecutive winners on a single spin. Two, after a winning cluster has been removed, a Ghost Glyph is awarded in one of the empty spaces.A Ghost Glyph is a 1x1 symbol which acts as a wild, substituting for any pay symbol. When a Ghost Glyph is removed as part of a winning cluster, it flies up to activate one of the Ghost Urns. If the Blue Urn is activated, all unused Ghost Glyphs are turned into wilds whilst no new Ghost Glyphs appear on that tumble sequence.Before each spin, 5 Ghost Urns are randomly selected and displayed above the grid. The last one is always a Blue Urn (Key). When there is a non-winning tumble, any activated Ghost Urns are awarded in the order they were triggered:Yellow Ghost Urn – randomly places 4-10 wild symbols in the game area.Green Ghost Urn – selects a low pay symbol type and turns all instances of it into another low pay symbol type.Red Ghost Urn – targets one low pay symbol type and removes them from the grid.Blue Ghost Urn – activates the bonus game, or adds 3 spins to the bonus game.Players receive 8 free spins when all Urns have been activated, leaving the Blue Ghost Urn to activate last. Once in, every tumble sequence in the bonus game increases the gauge on the Paranormality Meter. It takes 8 tumbles to fill the meter completely. When the meter is filled, it levels up, unlocking the Massive Wild feature. Once the Massive Wild has been awarded, the meter resets.The Massive Wild feature is activated at the end of the last free spin if the meter has reached level 1 or higher. Massive wilds land in 2x2 size at level 1, or 3x3 size at any higher levels. At level 1 or 2, Massive Wilds are removed when part of a win. At level 3 or higher, Massive Wilds move position during each tumble sequence. Basically, you want the meter to fill as many times as possible so larger persistent Massive Wilds are added to the final free spin.Ghost Glyph: VerdictQuickspin took to the grid slot format like a duck to water and Ghost Glyph is another solid example. The build quality is high, the ghostly characters are charming (if you're into that kind of style), and the gameplay flows well. Nice consecutive chains of wins are possible, triggering feature after feature, culminating in free spins if your luck is in. Don’t expect miracles when you are let inside the mansion, though. Ghost Glyph is fun, but it’s far from being a high paying slot since potential maxes out at 2,260 times the stake.However you feel about the rewards, Quickspin has put a lot of thought into each aspect of the game. From winning cluster/Ghost Glyph animations to the way each of the modifiers works together. Ghost Glyph is another high-quality Quickspin grid slot and no corner appears to have been cut during production. Like Wild Cauldron, Ghost Glyph has a charm that is easy to warm to; partly from its inhabitants, partly from the atmosphere Quickspin has created.As alluded to, the main showstoppers for the harder-edged gambler will be the game engine and potential. If you identify with this group, then hearing the words ‘balanced math model’ in the blurb will probably give you pause. It is certainly balanced, no objections there, it’s just balanced in favour of those who like a fright, but not too much of a fright. Say, those who prefer Slimer from Ghostbusters to the head-spinning scene in The Exorcist.That’s all good though, some people like to sleep soundly at night rather than worry about what’s lurking under the bed. Bottom line, if you’re happy with the math model and stats, then there is no reason why you won’t enjoy what Ghost Glyph has to offer.

Title: Oasis of Dead

Title: Eye of Atum

The number of free spins you can win is capped at 150.Eye of Atum: Slot VerdictIt kind of feels like Play'n GO phoned this one in. Eye of Atum's straightforward gameplay might appeal to players after something simple and easy, or at a stretch, Egyptian slot veterans might appreciate a different version of Merkur's Eye of Horus slot (which was probably the point with this release). However, there are several issues here that you don't usually encounter in a Play'n GO game, which might be off-putting for both old and new players. Namely, poor potential and flat looks. Usually, it's the opposite when reviewing a Play'n GO release - sizing up a big win number while being dazzled by glossy graphics. By contrast, Eye of Atum did nothing to catch our eye and stayed stuck in low gear for the rest of the review.If we are being generous, perhaps players enchanted by Eye of Horus style gameplay will be intrigued by Eye of Atum's expanding wild/upgrading symbol antics. The wild is far and away the highlight of the show. What kills the mood is the fact max win in Eye of Atum has been limited to 2,000x the bet. Title: Flaming Fox

Title: Fruitopolis Fortune Play
review: Fruitopolis Fortune Play: Slot OverviewAdding to the countless number of fruit slots available pretty much everywhere comes another one from Blueprint Gaming titled Fruitopolis. It's the sort of name which may well elicit frissons of delight amongst fans of the format, or fearful cold sweats, depending on your thoughts on these sorts of games. As the name suggests, Fruitopolis is an online slot dripping with fruity icons that splits itself into two game modes. One is Standard Play; the other is Fortune Play, which is radically different in terms of rules and spin cost. As well as two game modes, players can enjoy a pay adjacent system, Golden Chip mystery symbols, and Money Spins.Typical, boring, magnificently traditional, all are terms that could be used to describe Fruitopolis depending on the sort of mood you are in. In Standard Mode, a single 5-reel, 4-row game grid sits front and centre before a crimson, diamond-patterned background, like a thickly padded wall in a club. There's not much to say about Fruitopolis from an aesthetic standpoint. It's a seen one you've seen them all type deal.Fruitopolis is playable on any device, and when it comes to bet selection, there are a few considerations to make. The first is whether you wish to play the game in Standard Play mode, where bets range from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Or flip it over to Fortune Play mode by clicking the colourful square button sitting below the reels. This is a big bet style option, ratcheting stakes up to $/€2 to $/€200, and the exact details of what it entails are covered in the following section. Before we go, be aware that Fruitopolis is a highly volatile slot, while RTP swings between 95.06% and 95.38%.In total, 20 fixed paylines are attached to the game grid, creating winning combinations when at least three matching symbols land in adjacent reels across them. However, unlike most games, winning combinations can begin from any reel, not just the first. In ascending order from the least valuable side of the paytable, we find 10-A playing card symbols, cherries, lemons, plums, and 7s. Card rank wins are worth 5-10 times the stake for five of a kind, rising to 15-25 times the bet for the remaining premium symbols. Fruitopolis might have plenty of fruit, but it does not use wild symbols at any time.Fruitopolis Fortune Play: Slot FeaturesThere are a couple of other special symbols to look out for, though; these are diamond scatters which trigger Money Spins and Golden Chip mystery symbols.Money SpinsThe Money Spins bonus round is triggered when any number of diamond scatter symbols hit. Once in, 3 respins are awarded in what is a rather basic hold and win game. Diamond scatters are sticky, so they lock into position and reveal a cash prize. When new diamonds hit, they reset the spin counter back to three. At the end of the round, all cash prizes in view are added up and awarded.Golden ChipsWhen Golden Chip symbols land, they all transform into the same pay symbol type. Then a win evaluation takes place. Golden Chips can also transform into Money Spins symbols.Fortune PlayFortune Play is possibly the most intriguing thing about Fruitopolis as, so far, it has been pretty standard. Flicking the switch below the grid activates this game mode. Roughly speaking, Fortune Spins cost 20 times what regular spins cost. So, on a €20 Fortune Play spin, pay symbols have the same value they would have at a €1 Standard Play spin. So what do you get for the extra cash? For one, this mode is played on four grid sets rather than just one. Each grid has a turn of spinning before the next one does. Once all four matrices have been activated, the Fortune Play spin is over.Where Fortune Play gets interesting is when Golden Chip mystery symbols land, they are transferred to the remaining grids. For example, mystery symbols landing on reel set 1 are added to the same position on reel sets 2, 3, and 4. If on the same spin, more mystery symbols land on reel set 2, they are added to reel sets 3 and 4.Fruitopolis Fortune Play: Slot VerdictFor much of the test round, playing Fruitopolis was a tug of war battle between trying to stay focused on the reel-based action and the desire to do pretty much anything else. Maybe action is too strong a word. Anyway, the adjacent pays system is something, and it works with mystery symbols to create the odd thrill. For instance, a bunch of mystery symbols might land stacked on reels 3, 4, and 5 to create a win, which it wouldn't ordinarily do with a regular pay from the first reel setup. That's something, we guess.What made the struggle real is the fact Fruitopolis is basically a straight clone of Luck o' the Irish 2 Fortune Spins. Why the transition from one generic-looking slot to another, you might be wondering? We're not sure either, but the impression we got is that since the quad grid system hasn't quite taken off yet, Blueprint is hesitant to squander their really good thematic ideas on it. This is conjecture, of course, and it makes things tough for the Fortune Spins concept, which has merits, yet often flounders in a sea of thematic mediocrity.Winning potential is a funny one, too. As usual, Fruitopolis comes with the standard 50,000x or $250,000 win cap disclaimer (Blueprint really needs to be more transparent here), but it's unlikely the game will climb anywhere near such lofty levels. If the unspeakable occurred, and all four grids in a monumental Fortune Spin were covered in 7s, the result would be 2,000x the bet. Then again, not really, since 2,000x the regular bet equates to 100x the Fortune Spin cost. However you cut it, Fruitopolis isn't a massive xbet machine.In the end, we were left with the impression that Fruitopolis was a sort of beta tester for future slots. The way adjacent pays and mystery symbols gel together could see further use somewhere down the line, as could the Fortune Pays big bet idea. Heck, what are we saying? This is Blueprint Gaming, the masters of tweak, so players are sure to get a bunch of different iterations of these concepts in the future when they're squeezed into new games or merged with previous works. Mashing them into something with a more exciting theme wouldn't hurt.

Title: Age of Asgard

This wheel results in either 10 free spins, or a consolation prize of 50 times your stake, or it launches the Ragnarok free spins.Age of Asgard (Yggdrasil Gaming): VerdictAge if Asgard is a game that really grows on you. At first, it can be easy to dismiss it on the grounds of medium volatility and its so-so top prize, especially if you don't get many early wins in. However, we found the spins seriously fly by once the momentum began to ramp up. However, due to the company's name and country of origin, it does feel ever so slightly that Yggdrasil could have pulled the stops out and made this one a classic. It's just that with a bit of tinkering, Age of Asgard could have been a real contender.Perhaps by upping its top prize, or tweaking the volatility Age of Asgard could have been worthy of Valhalla. As it is, it remains a supremely playable mythological slot with gorgeous graphics and a brilliant interplay of extras. But hey, this is Yggdrasil, and we've come to expect nothing less.

Title: Legion X

The last few numbers, for now, are stakes which range from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, while the game may be played on any device.Winning combinations are formed in Legion X when matching symbols land on the grid from the leftmost side on adjacent reels. Making up the regular paying symbols are five stone cut 10-A card royals worth 1-1.1x the bet for five of a kind, then four menacing-looking barbarian characters and a Roman legionary as the five premiums. Landing a full five of a kind premium combination is worth a payout of 1.2 to 2.5x the bet.Legion X: Slot Features﻿﻿If you're tooling around looking for a feature-rich game, then be sure to put Legion X on the list. Or, if 2 special symbols land on reels 1 and 5, the feature is upgraded to an enhanced bonus mode.Legion X Equestris SpinsShould 3 bonus symbols land at the same time as 2 xWays symbols, then 10 free spins are awarded. Again, xNudge multipliers do not reset between free spins, except this time, xWays symbols are sticky, meaning Infectious xWays on each spin.Legion X Fretensis SpinsThis feature is triggered when 3 bonus symbols land along with 2 Infectious Wilds. Here, the 2 special symbols on the outer two reels are sticky, so players benefit from low symbols to wild conversions and Infectious xWays on each spin.Feature BuyThere is a lot to experience in Legion X, and Nolimit City allows players to go straight to each of the bonus rounds if they cough up the dough. Well, straightforward for Nolimit City, which still means it's worth spending a bit of extra time on the paytable to digest everything. They must feel a ton of pressure on their shoulders to keep this going, surely? Anyway, somehow, someway, the studio manages to knock it out of the park just about every time, and Legion X is no exception. It's got the mood, the 'tude, and most importantly, the gameplay to entertain players up for a volatile Roman Empire themed challenge.

When they do, they are collected next to the champion of the grid they landed on. Reset symbols may also appear on the reels. Hitting a Reset symbol resets the coin collection of the champion with the highest Coin count to 0, but not the champion chosen at the beginning. If two or more champions are tied, one is picked at random to reset. At the end of the round, if the chosen champion has the highest number of collected Coins or is tied for the most, then the wins from all grids are awarded to the player. Free spins cannot be retriggered, but they can be bought for 100x the bet.Chase for Glory slot - free spinsChase For Glory: Slot VerdictA bit of a game of two halves this one. However, activating free spins naturally wasn't the most herculean task we've undertaken, so soon enough, the champions were set upon each other to collect Coins and stare at each other a lot without ever doing any actual punching or kicking in the quad-gridded bonus round.It wasn't long ago we'd gone to war with another four grid online slot, so perhaps this specific tactic is on the up and up amongst software providers. What we do know is that when all is going to plan in Chase For Glory, players are able to collect wins of up to 7,887 times the bet.Chase For Glory's base game can plod, though its combination of ways and wilds helped inject some life at times.
