The Baphomet is the wild and appears on reel 3 only, substituting for all regular symbols except the scatter.Demon (Play'n GO): FeaturesHell Spins feature in actionAs you would expect from a slot based on a heavy metal band, it's loud and fast-paced with some intense features to go along. Central to the action is the Wild Mask feature - it appears on the middle reel only and will transform all instances of the singer symbol in view into wilds when it hits. That's all you get as far as the main game is concerned.The highlight of the Demon experience is the Free Spins game. It comes into play when wild amulets appear on reel 1 and 5 together with the wild mask symbol on the middle reel. You will get 11 free spins if the wild mask hits the centre of the reel or 6 if it lands on in the top or bottom position of the reel. During the feature, you'll benefit from a win multiplier - a multiplier value from 2x, 3x, 5x, or 8x will be randomly selected on each spin and applied to your winnings.Moreover, if you land both of the wild amulets on reel 1 and 5, you'll unlock the Hell Spins. Starting with a random number of spins ranging from 4 to 8, during the Hell Spins, the win multiplier is locked to the multiplier value selected for the triggering spin. Now, if the wild mask also appears on the middle reel, a random number of between 6 to 10 spins are awarded. If the wild mask appears in the middle position of reel 3 during triggering or retriggering of the Hell Spins feature, the win multiplier will be doubled for all remaining spins. The most you can win here is 5,000 times your stake, but given that a win like that only comes along once every 500 million spins, you should set the bar way lower in order to avoid disappointment.Demon (Play'n GO): Final VerdictDon't be misled - sale's pitch reviews of the game have been popping up on the web from the first day Demon was announced, all making big promises and hyping it as if it's the next best thing since sliced bread. It's not. The truth is that, even if you're a fan of the band, the slot is just an average Play'n GO release that involves high risk but not so much reward. For such a volatile slot (maximum Play'n GO volatility), the max win is unexpectedly low. Hopefully, it's mathematically designed to award wins of around 500x+ more frequently, but we'll have to see about that.Mechanically, Demon is a variation of Legacy of Egypt, which in turn was inspired by the iconic WMS slot Montezuma. Overall, it comes across as a half-hearted effort nowhere near as ambitious as Sabaton. If you're a fan of the band it's a no-brainer - you have to give it a few spins at least. Title: Razor Shark

Title: Wins of Nautilus Megaways

Title: Tivoli

Almost like shedding a few decades to relive a carefree youth. You can't escape reality forever of course, and after a few spins, it all comes crashing in. Blueprint Gaming has captured a strong dose of Tivoli’s magic by using popup book graphics that are genuinely captivating. The soundtrack is just as stirring, and animations such as the firework effects have been put to good use. It all combines to create a carefree look; some might say a little kiddy, with a carnival atmosphere to reproduce a golden age feel the amusement park is famous for. This is a place to forget about the outside world while discovering new wonders to lose yourself in. For a time at least, it's hard not to surrender and be sucked into Tivoli the slot's enchanting world.If you're not a major fan of Fishin' Frenzy, then the enchantment probably won't last all that long. Tivoli's fab new graphics elongate the playing time, though once the first impressions wear off, the slow pace plus a narrow range of features become apparent.The extras do make sense though. Above the reel set you'll see a 5-stage meter representing 5 reel enhancing features. The objective is to charge the meter by landing as many Battery symbols as possible. The more Battery symbols you land, the more features are combined in the subsequent re-spin.For example, landing only 1 Battery symbol will award you a simple re-spin, but landing 5 of them, on the other hand, will give you a re-spin with all features activated that includes the Swap symbol feature, random wilds, mega wild, random multiplier of up to 10x and more!Reactor (Red Tiger Gaming) - ConclusionReactor is an extremely volatile slot that is all about the Battery re-spin feature, which is also why the main game can get a bit tedious as essentially all potential is allocated to the re-spin feature. The reel enhancing extras on offer, however, can combine to dramatic effect with a max win potential of 5000 times your stake, so if you're a fan of high variance, you'll most likely enjoy this electrifying beast.
In writing, Reactor can come across as slightly complicated although it is not. In fact, it is a rather simple slot, and once you've triggered a couple of re-respins, you'll soon get the hang of what's going on.

Title: Wolf Call
review: Wolf Call: Slot OverviewYou'd imagine hiking through the majestic North American countryside and hearing an actual wolf call to be quite a scary experience, their haunting howl evoking a primal fear that must have given early humans the willies. Well, there's no need to get spooked when playing Wolf Call from Microgaming partner Spinplay Games. This game allows players to explore nature from a safe distance while spinning for things like multiplier wilds and free spins as they collect diamonds in hopes of triggering a jackpot pick me feature.If you're into nature, then the pleasantly drawn background and the triumphant sounding music make a rather stirring mix. The game panel is slightly see-through, and behind it lies a bubbling brook as it winds its way through a tree-covered valley. With the sun glowing in the distance, Spinplay has done a pretty good job of recreating those landscape portraits typical of American Romanticism, where artists sought to record the natural beauty before humans could charge in and tear up the place to extract resources. There's a sort of tacky look to the reel area, though, and the four jackpots above it cheapen the effect. However, the white dire wolf looking animal on the left-hand side is kind of cool.Played on a 5-reel, 4-row matrix providing 1,024 ways to win, wins occur when matching symbols land in adjacent reels starting from the left-hand side; any row height is fine. This system leads to a hit rate of 36.68% and an overall return value of 96.44%. RTP can be found at lower settings, though, so it pays to check. Medium volatile, Wolf Call is available on any device, accepting stakes of 10 p/c to $/€25 per spin.Moving on to the paytable, we find a mix of low-value 9-A card ranks and premium animals. These are eagles, deer, cougars, bears, and wolves. Landing five low pays results in a win worth 1x the bet, while premiums range from 2.5 to 10 times your stake. The diamond symbol is wild, replacing any normal pay symbol and also tying into a couple of the features.Wolf Call: Slot FeaturesWolf Call is a game of both long and short term goals. Diamond wilds are entwined with a Power Range feature that bestows multipliers and get collected to trigger a jackpot feature. Running alongside this is a free spins bonus round.Power RangeThe Power Range is the blue rectangle you can see in the middle of the game grid. Wilds that land inside the Power Range are awarded a win multiplier. In the base game, this is an x2 multiplier. In free spins, the Power Reel expands to cover all positions on the middle three reels and can create win multipliers of x2, x3, or x5.Diamond Meter and JackpotsEach time a wild symbol lands in the base game, it is collected by the Diamond Meter. When the meter is filled, the Diamond Jackpot feature is triggered. The screen is covered in diamonds, and players click them to reveal yellow, red, purple, or green diamonds. When 3 matching diamonds have been revealed, the corresponding jackpot is awarded. These are the green, purple, red, or orange jackpots worth 20x, 50x, 200x, or 5,000x the bet.Free SpinsWolves howling by the moon symbols are scatters and landing 3, 4, or 5 of them awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. During free spins, the Power Range expands to cover all positions on the middle three reels. On a final note, instead of triggering free spins naturally, players may be able to buy 10 of them for the cost of 50 times their stake.Wolf Call: Slot VerdictWolf Call is a game that kind of gets there; kind of doesn't. Bits of it aren't bad, while other bits lessen the experience. One of the positives is the Diamond Meter collection system. When changing bets, instead of starting from zero as most do, the game takes the equivalent value and transfers it to the new stake level. So, if you've filled half of the meter at €1, let's say, switching down to a lower stake may almost fill the bar completely. Some players may appreciate being able to fast track to the Jackpot Feature, in a way, though the prize values will naturally be reduced at the lower stake.The graphics aren't bad either, well the background imagery isn't at least, which is quite important in a North American nature game. The wilderness visuals are presumably high on the criteria list for players into this sort of thing. As mentioned, they are let down by the look of the reel area and the Jackpot display. Also, there's something a little tacky about the diamond symbols themselves, as if they just don't belong in this sort of game. Of course, such a seemingly small aspect isn't a deal-breaker, but the little things do count, and this fly in the milk detail did detract from the overall experience.The gameplay was okay, multipliers multiply each other, and appeared to land in larger quantities in free spins, though there is nothing mentioned about greater wild frequency in the paytable. Wilds are presumably more frequent since they are not collected by the Diamond Meter during free spins. Scoring the top prize from the Jackpot Feature is a headliner, yet technically, it is possible to win more elsewhere as Wolf Call advertises wins of over 10,000x the bet.In a well-stocked slot category like the wolf/North American nature one, Wolf Call stacks up fairly well. The stats are decent, winning potential is enticing, and the diamond collection mechanic leading to a guaranteed jackpot has merit. Sprucing up some of the graphics and livening the execution would have helped, but overall, players into this type of action should find some value here.

Title: Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash
review: Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash: Slot OverviewJust when we'd got the smell of fish off our hands from the last fish slot review, we get Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash from Games Global partner Gold Coin Studios. Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash is a follow-up to Fishing Floats of Cash (2022), which in turn appears to have been a reskin of Fiona's Fortune (2022). The recycling of bits and bobs and ideas and gaming components is evidently strong with this one. Never mind, time to grab a virtual rod and see what we can dredge up with Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash.To begin with, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash is cheerful if plain looking. Fishing slots tend to be upbeat affairs, and Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash certainly is that - largely thanks to its bouncy music. Sorry to use the same word twice so close together, but the visuals are plain, boring even, the base game background depicting some water and a hint of a cloudless sky. The rotating prize wheel is one incentive, perhaps, as are the three prize values displayed along the top of the game grid, though apart from the cheerful tunes, there isn't much about Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash that screamed to us, 'play me, you wanna be fisherperson.'Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash slot - base gameTurning our attention to Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash's inner workings, we find a highly volatile math model and four RTP configurations, 96.04% being the preferred one. The higher RTP model comes with a theoretical hit rate of 30.05% and bet limits of 20 p/c to $/€25 per spin. Sitting centre stage is a 5-reel, 3-row gaming panel with 25 paylines where regular line wins may land.While the main focus may be on winning elsewhere, regular wins begin from the leftmost side of the board, left to right across a payline on adjacent reels. For low pays, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash has 10 to A card royals, paying 2.4 to 3 times the bet for 5 OAK, then an anchor, a seagull, and a marlin are the high pays worth 6 to 8 times the bet for 5-of-a-kind. Appearing on reels 2 to 5, helping link wins together is the fisherman wild, which can substitute for any pay symbol.Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash: Slot FeaturesFishing Deeper Floats of Cash slot - WheelFishing Deeper Floats of Cash Not makes up for not having a heck of a lot of pay symbols by possessing a fair few features. These are the Express Collect, a Bonus Wheel, a Link&Win Respins feature, and free spins.Express ConnectExpress Connect prize symbols may land on reels 1 to 4, with values of 1 to 200 times the bet or displaying the Mini 20x the bet or Major 600x the bet prizes. When a Trigger symbol lands on reel 5, any Express Connect prize symbols also in view award their values.Wheel BonusLanding a Trigger symbol on reel 5 and a Wheel Bonus symbol on reel 1 triggers the Wheel Bonus. The Wheel spins to award 2x, 5x, or 10x the bet, the Link&Win feature, or the Mini, Major, or Mega Prize worth 20x, 600x, or 7,500x the bet, respectively.Link&WinThe Link&Win feature starts with 3 spins where only special symbols or blank spaces may land. Any new Link&Win symbols that hit reset the spin count. At the end, the values of all prizes are awarded. If all 15 positions are filled, the Mega Prize 7,500x the bet is also awarded.Free SpinsLanding 3 scatter symbols on reels 2-4 triggers 10 free spins. Whenever a Trigger symbol lands on the fifth reel, the Feature Trail is progressed by +1 position. Up to 3 Trigger symbols can land on a spin. Upon reaching each third position on the Trail, a multiplier applies to any future Express Collect wins and +5 additional free spins are awarded. The multiplier progresses like so - x2, x3, x5, then x10. The Trail has 12 positions to progress along.Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash slot - free spinsFishing Deeper Floats of Cash: Slot VerdictWell, it's a fishing game, alright, but it could be anything, really. When digging into Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash's past, it quickly became apparent how much recycling of gaming components and general reskinning went on to spawn the current game. Couple that with the plain visuals, and it was hard to fight off an overwhelming feeling of tedious boredom while playing Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash.For starters, there is a significant number of fishing slots already on the market, which is no bad thing in and of itself. And yet, if someone is planning to make yet another one, why not do something interesting with it? What's the point of churning out another reskin, or a Fishin' Frenzy/Big Bass Bonanza wanna-be? It doesn't mean the game has to light up the sky with incandescent innovation. Just something, anything to give the game an original spark. Not singling any one studio out here, by the way; just ranting into the wind. Fishing Floats of Cash kinda got away with it, maybe, since it was the first in this series, yet Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash is just a more volatile version with a higher max win. Perhaps the previous game was a hit? Fair dues to Gold Coin Studios if it was. But for non-fans, or if coming in for the first time, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash may well just fall flat, delivering a bunch of same old same old gaming, which was tiring to struggle though.Apologies for the bad vibes, but Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash just didn't float the boat. It's technically got the required parts to thrill players who strike it lucky, though with other more exciting fishing games on the market – the Big Bass range, Golden Catch, 4 Fantastic Fish in Egypt, and even iterations of Fishin' Frenzy, for example, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash was like ordering frozen fish from a restaurant rather than something freshly caught.

Title: Undead Fortune
review: Undead Fortune: Slot OverviewJust speculating here, but the act of grave robbing has probably been around for as long as people have buried with their riches. Perhaps it was people planning to be entombed with their wealth who came up with the idea of zombies in an attempt to scare off would-be tomb raiders? Whatever the origin might be, players get a taste of the undead in an online slot from Hacksaw Gaming titled Undead Fortune which is another slot that reveals the darker side of Hacksaw Gaming's personality. It follows a path laid down by prior slots such as Hand of Anubis and Gladiator legends, expanding on Hacksaw Gaming's DuelReels mechanic whilst combining it with a treasure trove of features such as Walking duels, Expanding DuelReels, The Curse bonus round, and The Tomb bonus round.Initially, Undead Fortune didn't make the same impact Hand of Anubis did which had a heavy atmosphere that felt like you'd been judged for your earthly deeds and been found wanting. Undead Fortune is chock full of horrifying images, including a huge, hooded cobra, but it didn't evoke the same level of despair. It's very lively, though, ironically, and soon enough, animated undead denizens will be lighting up the reels via the game's features and, hopefully, letting slip some of their fortunes.Undead Fortune slot - base gameHacksaw Gaming slots do tend to lean on the volatile side, and if our test sessions are anything to go by, Undead Fortune certainly warrants its 4 out of 5 volatility rating. As per usual, it comes in a variety of RTP settings with a maximum value of 96.29%, which at that level has a hit frequency of 26.77%. When playing regularly, stakes of 10 p/c to $/€100 may be selected, available on mobile, desktop, or tablet devices.Surrounded by hieroglyphically carved stone structure sits Undead Fortune's 5-reel, 4-row game panel. Running across it are 10 fixed paylines for landing winning combinations of three to five or a kind. For pay symbols, 10-A card royals are used as the low pays, while five monster/character symbols make up the premium tiles. Hitting a five-of-a-kind winning line awards 1-1.5x the bet for five royals or 4-10x the bet for five premiums. Wrapping this section up is the wild symbol, appearing on all reels to substitute any regular pay symbol. If five wilds hit along a payline, they award 10 times the stake.Undead Fortune: Slot FeaturesUndead Fortune slot - The Tomb free spinsUndead Fortune builds off slots that preceded it while doing its own thing at the same time. Features to be found in the game are Walking duels, Expanded DuelReels, The Curse, The Tomb, and several bonus buys for eligible players.Walking DuelsLanding Walk VS symbols activities Walking duels. Walking duels are wild symbols that expand to cover the whole reel. They reveal a monster and a multiplier value. If the monster is defeated, the multiplier is applied to the whole reel, boosting any wins that pass through it. Should more than one Walking duel be part of the same win, the multiplier values are added together before being used. Multipliers can have values of x2 to x200. Defeating the monster also awards a respin, and the expanded Walking duel symbol moves one reel to the left unless it is blocked by another Walking duel symbol or the edge of the grid. At the new position, another duel takes place, repeating the procedure mentioned above. New Walk VS symbols can land on respins.Expanding DuelReelsExpand VS symbols appear on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5, triggering Expanding duels when they hit. Expanding duel symbols are wild and expand to cover the whole reel, displaying a monster and a multiplier. If the monster is defeated, the multiplier is saved, and the Expanding duel expands one reel to the left unless blocked by the edge of the board. Once expanded, another monster and multiplier appear, repeating the process. If the monster is defeated after the expansion, the new multiplier is added to the current value. Multiplier values are x2 to x200. If the monster is not defeated or the Expanding duel cannot expand any further, any winning lines connected to it are multiplied by the multiplier. Walk VS and Expand VS symbols are not able to appear at the same time.The CurseGetting 3 Curse symbols on reels 1, 3, and 5 on a single base game round triggers The Curse bonus game. For The Curse, 10 free spins are awarded with a greater chance of landing Walk VS and Expand VS symbols.The TombLanding 3 Tomb scatters in a game on reels 1, 3, and 5 in a single game round triggers The Tomb bonus round. This round begins with multiplier values above each reel. Some reels are locked, some are active. Landing Tomb VS symbols on an active reel reveals a monster and a multiplier value of 2x to 200x. Defeating the monster adds the multiplier to the value above it. Losing the duel locks the reel. When all five reels are locked, the feature ends, and the values above the reels are awarded. However, it is possible to unlock reels. When 4 unlock symbols land on a locked reel, it is unlocked, or when the Golden Unlock symbol lands, all locked reels are unlocked.One more symbol which may land during the feature is the Epic Vs scatter. When hit, the whole grid becomes a duel, displaying monsters and a multiplier value. Win this duel, and all active reel values are either multiplied by x2 to x20 or have a value of 25x to 200x added to them. Losing this duel locks the reel the Epic VS symbol landed on.Buy BonusUndead Fortune's feature buy menu provides these five ways of playing the game:Bonus Featurespins – 3x the bet where each spin is 5 times more likely to award a bonus game. Very highly volatile.Walking Duel Featurespins – 10x the bet to guarantee at least one Walk VS symbol lands. Very highly volatile.Expanding Duel Featurespins – 50x the bet to guarantee that one Expand VS symbol hits. Extremely volatile.The Curse – 100x the bet. Very high volatility.The Tomb – 200x the bet. Very high volatility.Undead Fortune slot - feature buy menuUndead Fortune: Slot VerdictHand of Anubis came blowing onto our screen like a dread chill wind from the underworld and immediately grabbed attention with its bleak visuals. Undead Fortune has some of that effect, but it's not so pronounced. In part because Hand of Anubis was first, therefore stole its thunder, and partly from the sprinklings of neon giving the game an undead at a 90s retro party vibe. It certainly contains a lot of horrific imagery, though (for an online slot); the chaps with the big, stretched mouths are practicality vile. Maybe play the game during the day or with all the house lights on when the sun goes down if you happen to get night terrors. There are a few things here that may well feed them.On the gaming side, Undead Fortune is classic Hacksaw. It stands on the shoulders of slots the studio has released in the past while taking players' hands and leading them somewhere new. Walking Wilds might not be super new, but here, they get the chance to award multipliers when walking or, in the Expanding duel form, grow to cover parts of the grid while accumulating multipliers. Both are available in the base game or during The Curse, where they are technically more likely to trigger. Or, you can buy them from the feature buy, though getting repeatedly slapped down in consecutive losing duels can be irritating.The Tomb is something else altogether and could be outrageously unpredictable. Bonus buy results ranged from something like 4x the bet up to 4,651x. Others weren't quite so extreme, yet Hacksaw Gaming slots have a reputation for volatility which The Tomb certainly displayed during the review. At full strength, Undead Fortune can reach payouts up to 10,000x the bet. With the studio's track record and stacks of potential multipliers in Undead Fortune, it certainly seems doable.From an initial focus on online scratch cards, Hacksaw Gaming has become something of a darling amongst certain streamers, and it's not hard to envisage them (amongst others) destroying Undead Fortune's feature buy button, too. Fortunately, recreational gamblers should be able to extract entertainment from Undead Fortune as well, provided they're braced for a potentially rocky, volatile ride, and don't mind a horde of undead beings regularly trying to administer a beating.

Title: Rising Royals
review: Rising Royals : OverviewJust for the Win’s new slot continues their tradition of making gorgeous looking games that belie a medium volatility with low returns. Royal themed slots pop up from time to time but aren’t all that common. There is an opportunity there for developers to make a big impact and stake a claim in a fairly sparse category. Competition includes slots such as the LeoVegas original Royal Family from Yggdrasil and Play n’ GO’s Royal Masquerade. So, how does Rising Royals measure up?First is the royal theme which has a lot of promise due to the rich, overblown imagery that could be used. Where Royal Masquerade was based around the Italian upper classes, Rising Royals focuses on 18th Century France. As we know, the French Aristocracy famously came to a sticky end during the Revolution. The lower classes, tired of being oppressed by their self-proclaimed betters, rose up and took back control in a sea of blood and executions. In a way, Rising Royals has managed to capture the spirit of the age quite accurately in this new slot. After a few spins, players will get a glimpse of how an exploited French worker back then might have felt.The 18th-century upper class lived unbelievable lives of luxury. We are talking bling that continues to amaze even today. The huge palace on load screen is an example of such ostentatiousness. When the 5x3, 20-payline reel set, flanked by shimmering chandeliers grace the screen, it's hard not to produce an involuntary gasp. The graphics, typical of Just for the Win, are pretty indeed - bright and rich in colour. But don’t let them dazzle you. There is less to this game than initially meets the eye.The first let down occurs when you visit the paytable. For starters, there aren’t many symbols, and their values are pitiful. The low pay J - A symbols start things off with 0.8x to 3x the stake. There are four high pay symbols comprised of a curly-haired lesser noble, a duchess, a duke and the game’s logo. Payouts for these symbols start at 1x and go as high as 15 times your stake for five of the logo. Not exactly the princely sum you would expect from the cashed-up aristocratic set.Bets start at 10 c/p and can be set as high as $/€250 per spin. For that, players get a decent RTP of 96.01% and medium volatility. The game does tend to payout frequently, but wins are frustratingly low - even when locking in a good number of the high pay symbols. Usually, in this situation, you could count on a bundle of extra features to come swooping in to save the day, alas…Rising Royals : FeaturesRespins feature in actionRising Royals is surprisingly light on features. There are two that work in tandem - a Respin feature which can also trigger a symbol upgrade. How it works is that when a combination of high pay symbols land, they are locked in place and trigger a respin. If another high pay combination or more symbols from the first combo land, they are locked into place as well. This process repeats until no more appropriate symbols land, or the reels are covered in locked symbols, then the player is paid out.In addition, each time there is a symbol lock the chandelier meter on the side of the reels lights up. There are three sections, and when they are all lit, the locked symbols get Upgraded to the next highest on the paytable. The process can be repeated. So if the meter is filled again then the symbols are upgraded once more to the next highest level.As far as features go it works quite well. In combination with a multiplier, or higher value symbols, it could have been pretty potent. As it is, it does get a tad repetitive, and the returns just aren’t enough to keep you hitting the spin button. It’s not mandatory that a game offers a wild or scatter of course, and slots can achieve greatness without them. But, in the case of Royals Rising they would not have gone amiss.Rising Royals: VerdictOnce again Just for the Win has produced another pretty yet unexciting low-value slot. It begs the question, who is playing these games? Because there must be a lot of satisfied punters lapping these games up to justify the steady stream that are churned out. The answer must be recreational gamers happy with regular low value wins to keep the spins ticking over.Low symbol values aren’t necessarily a cause for concern - as long as a slot’s features are able to work with them to create decent wins. Sadly, that is missing, and Rising Royal’s features don’t come anywhere close to providing much intensity. With a top prize of around 300 times your stake why bother? The respins/upgrade feature is okay, but the game is screaming out for more. Multipliers, free spins, or a wild at the least could have provided more thrills. But, the French Aristocracy was never known for its generosity, so let them eat cake we guess. In that way you could say Just for the Win have captured the essence of 18th Century French Aristocracy nicely.In the royal/aristocrat slot category, Rising Royals has come up short against the competition. Royal Masquerade, for example, keeps things to the point with a solid top prize and extreme volatility, not to mention a lot more extra features. The bottom line is if you are in the mood for gambling with royalty, there are better options out there.

Title: Cat Wilde and the Doom of Dead
review: Cat Wilde and the Doom of Dead: OverviewRich Wilde, the debonair scholar gentleman, is back in this… Hold up, wait a minute. Scratch that. Doom of Dead stars his daughter Cat Wilde who takes centre stage in another ‘Book of’ styled slot from developer Play'n GO. Will we ever reach the stage when every pair of words in the English language has been wrapped around 'of' to name a slot? Perhaps, but that day is still a long way off, as is the seemingly insatiable appetite for this style of gameplay. If you’ve played one, then the chances are excellent you will know what to expect. However, the lead character change is new, is anything else?Doom of Dead - base gameWell the theme is not, so prepare for another journey to Ancient Egypt in a 5-reel, 10 payline slot. Your eyes get to feast on temples, pillars, snakes, and deities, all done to the typically high Play'n GO standard. The expanding wild's, in particular, are eerily well-drawn. Set within an ancient Egyptian burial chamber, the recognition factor is high if you've played other slots in the same genre. The visuals are crisp and the animations superbly designed.Playable from the usual Play'n GO range of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin, players are sent off to explore with the boisterous Cat Wilde. Those who appreciate high volatility will be stoked with the game’s 10 out of 10 rating, which is as volatile as you could possibly want. Default RTP is good on 96.29%, but can be lower depending on where you play. For example, it is possible to find Book of Dead wallowing in the mid to low 90s, so be sure to have a look at the paytable before launching.Complementing the dusty background is a host of Egyptian themed symbols. Well, maybe not so much the 10-A low pays, though a touch of styling helps them fit in with the bunch. The rest are the premiums, consisting of scarabs, Anubis, a Sphinx, and our heroine Cat Wilde. ‘Book of’ slots usually offer pretty good symbol values, and Doom of Dead is no exception. For example, five premiums vary in reward from 7.5x for the humble scarabs up to 100x for the tenacious Cat.On a slightly unusual note, the game comes with a standalone wild, as well as a scatter. Whenever the standard 1x1 wild lands, it expands into a full reel wild displaying an Egyptian god. Wilds substitute for any other pay symbols and are worth 100 times the stake for a line of five.Cat Wilde and the Doom of Dead: FeaturesAs well as expanding wilds, temple raiders have the fabled ‘Book of’ free spins game to look forward to. This legendary feature is triggered when 3 compass scatters land on reels 1, 3, and 5 at the same time. 10 free spins are awarded, but before they begin, one regular symbol from the low or high end of the paytable is randomly selected to become the special expanding symbol.When possible for the special symbol to create a winning combination, they expand to cover full reels. The special expanded symbols pay from anywhere – they do not have to be adjacent. So should you land them on reels 1, 3, and 5, as an example, they will pay out as if they landed on the first three reels. The best-case scenario is a landing five wilds, or five expanded Cat Wilde symbols, for the game’s max single spin payout.Scatters continue to turn up during free spins, so the feature can technically be retriggered without limit - though Play ‘n GO has built-in a win cap, should that happen.Cat Wilde and the Doom of Dead: VerdictIt’s been a while since Rich Wilde first burst onto the scene, and he has been running strong ever since. The series has sent him to all manner of far-flung destinations and now sees his daughter take over the family business.So how did she do? Not too bad at all, though copying a guaranteed winning formula has certainly helped her chances. For a first solo outing, a 'Book of' copy is a fairly safe bet, so it would be nice to see Cat branch out if Play n’ GO choose to use her again in the future.Fans of this style will be pleased to know that despite a switch-up in characters, the gameplay and potential remain bang on point. You might think after all these years of looting Ancient Egyptian tombs there wouldn’t be much left, but Cat’s clearly got other ideas.Actually, it didn’t take long for the vivacious Cat to splinter off from her dad. It only feels like yesterday the dynamic father/daughter archaeologist combo were doing their thing exploring watery ruins in Rich Wilde and the the Shield of Athena. Perhaps Cat felt pressured to step out from her famous father’s shadow and prove her worth?Well, her solo debut is worth a fair bit, with potential capped at 5,000 times the stake which came in once every 1 billion spins during Play'n GO's simulation of the game. One thing to bear in mind is that due to the somewhat limited symbol values, it isn’t possible to land 5,000x on a single spin as you can in other ‘Book of’ slots. As always, it’s the bonus round supplying the opportunity for magic to flourish. This time it’s not just from expanding special symbols, but from full reel wilds adding more opportunities to win.At the end of the day what can you say? Cat Wilde and the Doom of Dead is another attractive and highly entertaining ‘Book of’ style slot. Will the community ever have their fill of these? Maybe, but it’s impossible to see Cat sealing the lid on them.

Title: Mayan Eagle Nobleways
review: Mayan Eagle: OverviewMicrogaming partner All41Studios is the mastermind behind the Central American driven slot Mayan Eagle. The theme might not be new, but the game is the first to use the in-house designed Nobleways mechanic. Sounds pretty, well, noble, but in effect, it's not the most innovative device you'll come across - nor the most sophisticated.It plays well with the other features though, Rolling Reels in particular, but don't expect to be dazzled on the whole. On that note, buckle up for a trek through the steamy Yucatan Peninsula for some Mayan infused gaming.Step Pyramids, temples, and carvings great players once the game loads. It's a classic Mesoamerican view, and quite a nice looking one indeed. Not so pleasing to the eyes is the 6 reel, 5 row game area, unfortunately. There is something a little off about the symbols. Encountering a dry spell can be a killer.Mayan Eagle's centrepiece is the trademarked Nobleways mechanic. In essence, Nobleways is 15,625 fixed win ways over the game's 6 reels. Should any more scatters be present, then they add +2 free spins each. During free spins, players benefit from a progressive win multiplier, starting at x2 and increasing by +1 on every Rolling Reel. The multiplier does not reset between spins but continues ever upwards with no set limit. Should another 4 scatters land in view during the round, then 12 more free spins are added to the total.Mayan Eagle: VerdictWell, no one said slashing through deep bush would be a walk in the park. The earlier explorers or conquerors, if you prefer to call them, didn't have it easy, and neither do players. Catching Mayan Eagle on a down patch is like having the jungle hack you with the machete. What kills it is the free spins frequency - 1 in 434 is no joke and is demoralising enough on paper. In practice, it felt like a full revolution of the Mayan Calendar had passed before free spins finally eventuated. An approach like that might work with a complex slot like Bonanza, not as well here.Strangely, the bankroll remained more or less neutral throughout, helped by the high hit rate and the features. Not just Rolling Reels, but Mystery Symbols popped up often enough to keep the interest level somewhat high. If we weren't conducting a review though, it would have been easy to give up after the first 500 spins lead to a whole bunch of tail chasing. It's hard not to doubt your tenacity when faced with jogging on the spot for another aeon of regular spins.The new-fangled Nobleways mechanic doesn't really offer anything new. All up, it’s perhaps better suited to wannabe Hernández de Córdobas who enjoy exploring this part of the world.For even more win ways we also suggest you have a look at All41 Studios' first ever Megaways release Shamrock Holmes Megaways.

From Relax Gaming's Dead Man's Trail to Yggdrasil's Pirates 2 Mutiny to Foxium's Boom Pirates. Shoot, look at the Branded Megaways franchise that followed on from Iron Dog's Pirate Kingdom Megaways. Not always, but there is something about the salty tang, warm wind on skin, or the sniff of treasure in the air that inspires certain studios to get creative.Some blue sky thinking certainly went into Shifting Seas' list of features, growing reels, rows, and ways. Doing things this way creates a snowballing effect which works hand in glove with the Avalanche mechanic as well. Shifting Seas brings everything together to create a next-level interplay of several different parts. Title: Holiday Spirits

review: Three Star Fortune: OverviewDeveloper Pragmatic Play plant themselves firmly on familiar ground with the Asian styled slot Three Star Fortune. The three stars in the title refer to the three jolly star gods Fu, Lu, and Shou, who represent wealth, status, and longevity. Most people would be happy with abundance of those three things, and in Chinese culture, these attributes traditionally denoted a good life. As such, the trio turns up regularly in the slot world. In Three Star Fortune they trigger the only feature, so yeah, they are just as desirable, if not more so in when spinning its Eastern-themed reels.Pragmatic Play has certainly created a game world for fans of the genre to feel comfortable in. Depending on how you feel about this style, Three Star Fortune will come across as generic and clichéd or familiar and homely. For the background, Pragmatic has practically recreated the Zhangjiajie National Forest with its misty mountains and covered them in traditional buildings, bridges, and waterfalls. It's dreamy, and it has been used in dozens of other similarly themed slots, but yeah, if you like the subject matter, you'll love the look.Reels dominate the view and are located in a green-tiled structure with the obligatory peaked corners. Their deep red tone helps contrast the bold colours of the symbols, which includes plenty of gold for good measure. Three Star Fortune uses a conventional 5 reel, 3 row set up with 10 paylines on which all symbols pay right to left, as well as left to right. The good thing about the pay both way dynamic is that it actually comes in quite handy with the way the feature works.Before delving in too deep is the matter of setting stakes. This can be done by altering the number of coins per line, and their value, and boils down to total bets of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. To understand what you're up against, it might be good to know that Three Star Fortune is a highly volatile slot with a industry standard RTP of 96.27%. The RTP, however, is adjustable, which means operators can set a lower number if they feel like it.Pragmatic Play has squeezed the theme hard when it came to designing the symbols too. On the low side, the three names Fu, Lu, and Shou have been used and appear in the form of Chinese characters. Then, we get a gourd that looks like Egg Shen's potion bottle, a scroll, and something that looks like a pink fruit. The premium symbol is one of those gold sycees that is worth 25 times the stake for a line of five. All symbols need at least three of a kind to trigger a payout. Another nice touch is that 5 of a kind wins are paid twice - once for each direction.Three Star Fortune: FeaturesThree Star Fortune - free spins featureThree Star Fortune keeps it ultra-simple with little in the way of features to interrupt the game’s flow. The one it does possess involves all three gods as expanding wilds. Each god has their own reel with Lu on reel 2, Fu on reel 3, and Shou on reel 4.Known as the Expanding Wilds feature, when one of the wilds appears, it expands to cover the reel and wins are paid out. Then, it is held for a free Respins in its expanded form. If another wild lands on a respin, it expands and triggers another respin. When respins have concluded the wilds are removed for the next new spin.Three Star Fortune: VerdictIf you are looking for some straightforward slots action in a well presented, attractive environment, Three Star Fortune can be quite good. For a while, at least. Ironically, despite featuring the god of longevity, the shelf life is likely quite short due to the repetitive and stripped down nature of this slot. Once you've seen the expanding wilds do their thing a few times, that's pretty much it. If you can get on a good roll, you'd be forgiven for sticking with it. If not, there isn't much else to keep grinding Three Star Fortune out long term.Still, for those with a deep affinity for Asian slots, Three Star Fortune is quite a good example with a ton of exotic imagery throw in for good measure. With a back catalogue bulging with Asian themed slots, Pragmatic Play certainly knows a thing or two about crafting them. Players that are into dreamy, cloud swirled mountains, a bit of divine presence, and gold and burgundy style, will probably be all over it.Without bonus games or free spins, however, it's just the three wild gods keeping players company and the wins ticking along. They can be quite effective when working together and Pragmatic Play has claimed potential of up to 5,000 times the stake. Yet, it is a little hard to see how that is possible. With pay both ways doubling full lines, a grid of wilds and sycees is worth 500 times the stake. Even in the unlikely event of landing that on consecutive respins, it will be nearly impossible to even come close to hitting the stated figure.In the end, Three Star Fortune is really one for fans of the genre. It has a good pace and the pay both ways mechanic has been paired perfectly with the expanding wilds feature. But its lack of originality, low payouts, and repetitive nature will make it hard to win over those that don't love this style.

Title: Hot Spin Deluxe
review: Hot Spin Deluxe (iSoftBet): OverviewThe original Hot Spin isn't exactly an old slot, but developers iSoftBet felt it was time to jazz it up and release a deluxe version. Not a lot has changed; we still get the same flashing lights and classic symbols of a retro Las Vegas-style slot - with a few extras. In fact, take a quick glance at a screenshot, and you would be forgiven for thinking you were looking at the original Hot Spin. Two key additions have been made, however, and they have drastically improved the game's potential for larger wins.The soundtrack can't be described as anything other than groovy. It's a sweet 70s disco flavoured piece of EDM and suits the game well - old school gaming with a modern twist. The visuals are nice, with a lot of bright gold, and touches of shimmer along the trim. Sticking with the retro theme, the gameplay is fast and simple, in the base game at least. When it comes to extras, there are a whole lot more than you would find on a fruit slot back in the day.The setup is the same as before, with 5 reels, 3 rows and 20 fixed paylines which flow fast. Located above the grid is the Hot Spin Reel turning lazily, just waiting for the right moment to completely flip the game. The overall sensory effect is pleasant and produces a mellow, relaxed state, conducive for a solid gaming session. The first thing to do is slink a bit lower into your chair and pick a bet level from 20 c/p up to $/€20 per spin.Symbols come straight from the fruit slot manual with cherries, lemons, plums, and watermelons starting off the paytable. Next up are the high pay symbols – bells, stars, 7, and the diamond as the most valuable base symbol at 25 times the stake for a five of a kind combination. The big gold 'W' is the wild which can replace any of the paytable symbols except the Bonus Symbol to form winning combinations. Stats are also similar to the first Hot Spin, with medium-high volatility and an RTP rate of 96.0%. Without doubt, what made the original slot interesting was its Hot Spin Wheel and the 6 features it was able to bestow. Fortunately, we get that, and then some, with the Deluxe version.Hot Spin Deluxe (iSoftBet): FeaturesBonus wheelThe bonus symbol appears on reels 1, 3, and 5 and when 3 land the Hot Spin Wheel springs to life. When the Hot Spin Wheel comes to a stop, it awards up to 15 Free Spins which includes one of these special features:Mystery Symbols - a golden question mark appears on the reels in 6, 8, or 12 positions. When the reels stop spinning they all turn to reveal the same symbol.Random Wilds - as the name suggests 5, 7, or 10 tiles are turned into Wild symbols.Mega Reel - this feature turns either reels 1-3 or 2-4 into one mega-sized symbol.In-Sync Reels - no, not a Justin Timberlake throwback, unfortunately. Instead, 2 or 3 reels will synchronise and land the same symbols on each one. Super In-Sync Reels can drop which synchronises either 3 or 4 reels at once.Wild Reels - the feature turns up to 3 reels completely stacked with Wilds. Again, Super Wild Reels can also land to provide 3 – 5 reels stacked with Wilds.Ultra Reel - turns the entire grid into one ultra-symbol.Now to the two features which added the word 'Deluxe' onto the title and warranted a remake; the first is Hot Spin Deluxe. This triggers the Hot Spin Reel at random during any normal spin to bring in one of the features mentioned above. The second upgrade is the Hot Spin Deluxe Multiplier. This is the one that will light player’s fire as it reveals a multiplier of up to x10 which can applies to any Hot Spin feature.Hot Spin Deluxe (iSoftBet): VerdictHot Spin Deluxe is what the first one could have, or should have been. The original was alright, and the Hot Spin Wheel with its set of features was a draw for many players no doubt. What it lacked was decent payouts to really set it up as a favourite. Perhaps iSoftBet has been out canvassing the gaming community for opinions and ideas? However the inspiration arose; they spotted an opportunity for a quick and easy remake. The upgrade will draw in both fans of the original and new players for several reasons. Hot Spin Deluxe is certainly a more enticing slot, and a lot of that is down to the new max potential. It is now capable of hitting 5,000 times the stake thanks to the inclusion of those extra multipliers.So no, Hot Spin Deluxe is not hugely different, but it is a step up from its predecessor. These minor tweak upgrades can be a double edged sword though. Hopefully, this doesn't turn into a major trend, with other developers taking an older game, bolting on one or two additional features and flooding the market with ‘Deluxe’ versions. Ah well, as long as prizes drastically increase along with the renovations then it is hard to complain too loudly about things like unoriginality.All in all, Hot Spin Deluxe is a compelling slot that is made all the more exciting by the random features. Knowing that they can drop at any time keeps the game fresh and your finger poised on the spin button. This game will inevitable spell the end of the original Hot Spin slot - why would anyone bother to play that anymore? Anyone in the mood for some retro-themed gaming with a bunch of extras thrown in for good measure will find plenty to be satisfied with here.

Title: Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God
review: Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God: Slot OverviewThe intrepid explorer, Cat Wilde, is back for another adventure in a slot with a real mouthful of a name. Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God takes the adventurous lady to Central America to find fortune and glory. It’s not the most original of locations to set a slot, and to be honest, a lack of originality permeates many aspects of the game. As you can see, there is a strong whiff of Gonzo's Quest about the venture – the original more so than the Red Tiger Megaways reboot. Still, Gonzo didn't become a classic for nought, so with Play'n GO's dependably high graphic standard accompanied by an attractive leading lady, expectations were running high.The connections to NetEnt's classic are apparent the moment the game lights up. Above the 5-reel, 20-payline game area are the familiar progressive multipliers which spring to life when wins hit – larger than before it should be added. A step pyramid looms over a thick verdant rainforest behind the reels, while a jungle rhythm jams in the background. Pay close attention to the sun in the centre of the sky; you'll be hoping the moon comes to blot it out, signifying a shift into free spins.Since we are dealing with Play'n GO, players can expect a well-built math model, generating an RTP value of 96.22%. This is the default value, of course, so make sure to check the version you plan to fire up as it can be found at lower levels. Bushwhackers should be prepared for medium volatility which can be experienced on any device offering stakes from 20 p/c to $/€100.Big chunky symbols make up the paytable, divided between low pay 10 to Aces, followed by high pay sundials, keys, skulls, and Cat as the most valuable. Five of a kind wins are worth 6 to 37.5x the bet for premium combinations, though values drop sharply for four of a kind. At least three adjacent symbols from the first reel are needed to form a winning combination. Sun God wilds are handy for this, landing on reels 2, 3, and 4 in the base game to substitute for any symbol except the scatter. They are also worth 100x the bet for five of a kind – the only length of combination they pay out on by the way.Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God: Slot Features﻿Gonzo on roids is a pretty accurate description of Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God, and that assessment is a fair one of the features. They start with cascades, lead to progressive multipliers, and both get a boost when free spins trigger.Starting with cascades, which activate after every win, removing winning symbols so new ones can drop in, potentially leading to more combinations. This mechanic is available in all phases of the game with the cascading effect continuing until no new winners appear.While this is going on a win multiplier is in play. It starts at x1 for the initial win, then rises through x2, x4, x6 then x10 following consecutive winning cascades. When a sequence ends, the multiplier drops back to x1.Keep an eye out for the Moon Goddess scatter symbols - 10 free spins are awarded when they appear on reels 1, 3, and 5 simultaneously. The multiplier remains in use in free spins, only this time the top-level becomes x70. Scatters also become wild as well and are collected whenever they land. Collecting 5 scatters awards 5 extra spins, up to a maximum of 40. Also, the win multiplier is upgraded when 5 scatters are collected, though the highest remains x70. A final point is that wilds land on any reel during the bonus round.Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God: Slot VerdictAs mentioned, expectations were high and the game is fun, but it can also get kind of bogged down and struggle to find the energy to recover. It doesn't stop Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God from being a reliably good looking Play'n GO release that produces a strong set of stats. The gameplay isn't bad either - of course being lifted out of the Gonzo playbook helps. Play'n GO has expanded multipliers which make a huge difference. Yet, despite its many positive points, unless you get it to go off, Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God isn't an all-around exciting game.The main problem is how slow it can be. It's like the game expects you to provide the energy rather than be a high-octane, or even medium-octane slot that gets you pumped. If it were any more laid back, it'd be lain flat, fast asleep. There's certainly none of Gonzo's amiable antics. In his place, we get Cat, who is easier on the eyes than Gonzo (sorry bud), yet she's such a non-event in this slot as to be virtually absent giving the game an almost generic feel. If Play'n GO had dropped Cat altogether and replaced her symbol with a can of paint, it wouldn't have made any difference. Here, she comes across as someone who has gotten by just fine on their looks so never needed to develop a personality or a sense of humour. It’s as if she thinks her smile is enough to deactivate booby traps in a hidden tomb or make the locals lower their bows.For a different take on the Gonzo thing, it's worth a look. Potential is up thanks to bigger multipliers and free spins which can go mental to produce significant wins. However, while Cat Wilde in the Eclipse of the Sun God is capable of satisfying moments, and hosts a bonus round that can go nuts, it is also noticeably lacklustre a lot of the time.

Title: Cursed Crypt
review: Cursed Crypt: Slot OverviewIf you're going to go tooling around in a crypt, maybe do a bit of raiding, or what have you, it might pay to do so in a crypt which is not cursed. But, some people can't help themselves, huh, because here we are, gripping a torch alongside software provider Hacksaw Gaming as we descend into the online slot Cursed Crypt, an Egyptian-themed adventure that spreads random symbols along reels while looking spooky as it does so.If Cursed Crypt has a family member it is related to in the Hacksaw Gaming lineup, it has to be the dread fest that was Hand of Anubis. Both have a dark, dark feel to them, shunning the stereotypical Ancient Egypt vibe often served up in slots to craft one which looks like the robotic species Necrons from the Warhammer 40K universe landed on planet Earth. A gloomy, ominous spirit dominates, split through with glowing green hues, to create a deliciously dark gaming world.Cursed Crypt slot - base gameClicking those up and down buttons next to the spin button is how players can pick a stake of 10 c to $/€100 per spin, while further along to the left is where the bonus buy can be found. When gambling in the normal manner, Cursed Crypt's default RTP is 96.22%, while its volatility is medium-high, rated by its maker as 4 out of 5. To make winning combinations, matching symbols must land from the leftmost side of the grid on at least 3 consecutive reels, and 1,024 ways to win blast the 5-reel, 4-row matrix.If you haven't been scared away yet, here are the pay symbols. The lower values are a set of 5 hieroglyph-style symbols, whereas the higher pays are 5 character/animal symbols. All low pays award 1 times the bet for a 5 OAK result, boosting up to 3-15x the bet for a 5 OAK high pay win. Wilds are present on all reels. They substitute for all regular pays and sling out 20 times the bet for landing a 5 wild winning line.Cursed Crypt: Slot FeaturesCursed Crypt slot - free spinsThere is a ring of familiarity to Cursed Crypt's features as certain symbols spread along reels, bestowing goodness when they go your way. However, instead of springing multipliers or anything like that, the spread brings random symbols instead, both in the base game and in the two bonus rounds. A suite of bonus buys are also available for players who prefer skipping to their favourite parts.Cursed ReelsWhen the Curse symbol lands, it spreads the Curse upwards to the top of the grid, creating Cursed Positions. Cursed Positions are replaced with a random symbol.Wrath of SobekIn the base game, landing 3 FS symbols triggers this feature with 10 free spins. In the Wrath of Sobek round, there is an increased chance of landing Curse symbols. Hitting 2 FS symbols awards +2 free spins while hitting 3 FS symbols awards +4 free spins.Tomb of TutankhamunIndulge your Howard Carter fantasies by landing 4 FS symbols in the base game to trigger 10 free spins in the Tomb of Tutankhamun bonus. In this bonus round, the Curse symbols will only fill Cursed Positions with high-pay symbols or wild symbols. Hitting 2 FS symbols awards +2 free spins while hitting 3 FS symbols awards +4 free spins.Bonus BuysCursed Crypt furnishes players with these bonus buys:BonusHunt FeatureSpins - 3x the bet, each spin is 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game. RTP 96.35%, very highly volatile.Curse of Three FeatureSpins - 40x the bet, each spin guarantees at least 3 Curse symbols land. RTP 96.34%, highly volatile.Curse of Five FeatureSpins - 150x the bet, each spin guarantees at least 5 Curse symbols land. RTP 96.34%, very highly volatile.Wrath of Sobek - 100x the bet, highly volatile. RTP 96.3%.Tomb of Tutankhamun - 200x the bet, very highly volatile. RTP 96.34%.Cursed Crypt slot - bonus buy menuCursed Crypt: Slot VerdictA twisty, turny path was trodden down before reaching a conclusion on Cursed Crypt. Spoiler alert: the final impression was favourable. In the beginning, reading about special symbols that spread upwards to the top of the reels, dumping identical symbols, just sounded too close to other Hacksaw Gaming slots that perform a similar role, like, oh, dunno, how about Beast Below? Admittedly, from memory, previous slots tended to do so with wild multipliers, so it is tough to accuse Cursed Crypt of doing the exact same thing. However, the spreading upwards effect was close enough to elicit a jaded wee sigh of 'here we go again' before plunging into the action.Good we did, though, because Cursed Crypt's action turned out to be not bad at all. Rather good, actually, for several reasons. The first reason is the high production values and the heavier, spookier, more menacing interpretation of Ancient Egypt than the vast majority of slots making up this genre have. We know Hacksaw Gaming can do light-as-a-feather slots like Om Nom, but it can certainly pull off haunting thrillers like this one. Secondly, the spreading symbols effect might not sound as exciting as spreading wild multipliers, but the potential power play was the way Hacksaw Gaming has jammed a ways to win system into Cursed Crypt instead of going for the usual paylines setup. Like Beam Boys, significant damage can ensue when Curse symbols really do their thing. Demoing Curse of Five FeatureSpins was one fun way of seeing what Curse symbols could do.The features are such that 10,000x the bet winning potential is achievable in all of Cursed Crypt's game modes. There is not much else to say other than Hacksaw Gaming has done it again, pooling its design skills to make another moody, tightly wound slot which stands proudly on the games that preceded it.

Title: Ivory Citadel
review: Ivory Citadel (Just For The Win): OverviewJust for the Win’s latest slot Ivory Citadel is located in a part of the world that doesn’t usually get much slot traffic - Western Asia. Asian themed slots abound but are usually set in China, Japan, or somewhere in the East. A quick Google search revealed that Western Asia includes countries such as Iran, Iraq, Pakistan and India. Not exactly countries that are used as slot themes too often. Judging by the scenery and the symbols involved, it feels like Ivory Citadel is based in the western parts of India perhaps? Wherever it is, Just for the Win has put a heavy emphasis on just how wild, and exotic this slot world is.It’s always nice to try something new, and Western Asia possesses its fair share of exotic locations to be sure. We get one as the background to the game which looks like the flying mountains from the movie Avatar. Rocky outcrops thrust into the sky surrounding the Ivory Tower with an entrance guarded by stone elephants. Throw in some mist and a jungle beat and the mood is set.Intrepid explorers can take on the wildlife with bets from 10 c/p to $/€100 per spin of its 5 reels. The gameplay favours the more laid back player with 20 paylines, and a decent RTP of 96.03% combined with medium volatility. With a low max potential and a hit rate of 1/4.45, wins are steady if a tad on the lower side, generally speaking.The 8 base game symbols are made up of J, Q, K and A Royals crafted in a muscular stone style. Next are three wilds beasts that do not look happy to see people on their patch - a snake, a buffalo, and a tiger. The developers have made them look more spirit-like than realistic looking, in bright, bold colours. The Ivory Citadel logo is the most valuable base game symbol which is worth 40 times the stake for five of a kind.Ivory Citadel (Just For The Win): FeaturesFree spins game in actionJust for the Win has added a couple of extras to help provide better payouts. You can’t miss the wild symbol, which is pink and gold with the word WILD written over it. It can land anywhere and pays out 5x, 16x, and 40x the stake for 3, 4, and 5 of a kind on a payline. It also substitutes for any symbol except the free spins and mystery symbols.The Mystery Symbol can appear in both the base game and during free spins and acts slightly different in each. In both games, when the spin has finished, the mystery symbol turns into any symbol except the free spins symbol for potential more wins.The Ganesha-like elephant is the Free Spins symbol and the key to unlocking the bonus round. Land 3,4, or 5 of them to score 8, 10, or 12 free spins respectively. When the Mystery Symbol lands during free spins, it becomes a sticky Mystery Symbol which can change into a different set of symbols which each free spin. If a reel contains only Mystery Symbols, they all turn Wild, and that reel remains locked as Wild for the remainder of the free spins. In this way, it is possible to stack multiple reels with wilds can guarantee wins on every successive free spin.Ivory Citadel (Just For The Win): VerdictJust for the Win has put the theme to good work in an attempt to emphasize just how wild and mysterious this slot world is. While it never quite reaches expectations, in many ways it does succeed. It looks good for one, no one ever accused Just for the Win of making an ugly slot. The bonus features are quite good too, particularly the stacked and sticky wilds which can leads to runs of satisfying wins, and jumping on the Mystery Symbol bandwagon will probably work in its favor too.Yes, Ivory Citadel is a pleasing looking slot, with a suitably pleasing soundtrack, and pleasing bonus features. It does what it says on the tin, but not much more than that. It's middle of the road gaming that doesn’t rock the boat and put people off, nor does it possess much x-factor to wow players either. This is game development that plays it safe.Ivory Citadel is bound to attract a fair share of punters due to its theme, graphics, and features. It has the modern aesthetics that sit it comfortably in any casino line up to tempt the odd player looking for a something a bit different. Will it pull in more dedicated gamers? Unlikely. It’s just not that exciting and the features would have benefited from more intensity. The real deal breaker for many will be the games potential though. With a max win of 1,968 times the stake it won’t satisfy players looking for high returns on their wagers. Add everything up and we have a typical Just for the Win slot on our hands.

Title: Totem Guardians Dream Drop
review: Totem Guardians Dream Drop: Slot OverviewWouldn't it be great if each one of us was assigned a spirit animal, a guardian, a guide that we could commune with, who could offer advice, teach us the ways, reveal hidden knowledge as we traverse the perils, pitfalls, and joys of life, before shuffling off to continue the journey in a new physical form? Maybe reality is actually like this, but the constant demands of modern life, too much TV or getting lost in the social media black hole have gummed up our third eyes. Who knows. For now, we can celebrate any potential connection to the spirit realm while spinning for the chance to win sizable piles of cash in software provider Relax Gaming's slot Totem Guardians Dream Drop – as well as a non-jackpot variant.Totem Guardians Dream Drop is a slot that gets away from it all, fleeing the city to connect with nature, possibly on a physical as well as mental and spiritual level. Mix the components together, and Totem Guardians Dream Drop offers a mix of the mundane physical dimension with other realities that lie beyond the ken of our five bodily senses.Totem Guardians slot - base gameStakes from 20 c to €/$100 may be placed in what is a highly volatile slot, possessing an RTP of 94%, or 96.1%, when playing the non-jackpot version. Diamonds, clubs, hearts, and spades are the low-pay symbols found in the game, awarding a win of 0.25 to 0.4 times the bet for a 6 OAK combination. Hitting 6 premium symbols, of which there are 4 totem-styled animals, pays 0.8 to 3 times the stake. Wild symbols are able to help connect wins by substituting for any regular pay symbol, and wilds land on all reels except the leftmost one. Wilds do not contribute to Totem Multipliers.Totem Guardians Dream Drop: Slot FeaturesTotem Guardians slot - jackpot gameNaturally, Dream Drop is the main event around here, but milling about in the wings are rising Totem Multipliers working with a cascade-type feature and a free spins round.Totem MultiplierEach symbol has a multiplier value associated with it, displayed on the totem pole next to the grid. Winning symbols and all matching symbols in view are removed from the reels, and the respective multiplier is increased by +1 for each symbol removed. Multipliers apply to all wins of the same symbol type and can be as high as x100. Each bonus scatter symbol landing in view boosts the rate that the symbol multiplier increases by, displayed as a multiplier value on top of the Totem Multiplier meter. In addition, one locked row is revealed for each scatter symbol that lands. Symbol multipliers can randomly increase at the start of any spin.Free SpinsWhen landing 3 scatter symbols, players are awarded 5 free spins. All values on the Totem Multiplier meter are transferred from the base game to the free spin round, and the values do not reset between free spins. All rows on the gaming grid are revealed during the free spins round, and +1 additional free spin is awarded for each scatter that lands. In the non-JP Totem Guardians, players may buy free spins for 60 times the bet. When buying free spins, the RTP is 96.87%.Dream DropThe Dream Drop feature may randomly trigger at the start of any regular spin. Make it to the jackpot game, where filling a column with DD symbols awards its corresponding jackpot prize. This could be the Rapid, Midi, Maxi, Major, or Mega, where the starting values of the progressive jackpots are €1, €5, €100, €25,000, or €500,000, respectively.Totem Guardians slot - free spinsTotem Guardians Dream Drop: Slot VerdictWhile reviewing Totem Guardians Dream Drop, a few prior Relax Gaming slots bubbled up as reminders. The game was like a mix of Volatile Vikings/Volatile Vikings 2, a bit of Wild Hike, and sprinklings of Banana Town. Only in some ways, as Totem Guardians Dream Drop is by no means a copy of them or anything like that. There was just something about the look of the Volatile Vikings slots and a familiar Wild Hike vibe crossover, not to mention a connection to the multipliers linked to the winning symbol action of the Banana Town games. Here, Relax Gaming has deviated from the scatter pays system of Banana Town by using a connected ways pay system instead. However, one of the main goals remains collecting winning symbol types to increment the respective multiplier in the hopes of getting further wins with the same kind of symbols in order to trigger a snowballing sequence of events.Not a super common occurrence, perhaps, but it can happen, and the max multipliers in Totem Guardians Dream Drop are potentially higher than they are able to get in Banana Town. Overall winning potential is not higher, though, as it maxes out at 5,000x here compared to 10,000x in the banana-related slots. Does it matter in the Dream Drop version? Probably not so much, as the big deal there is the Mega Jackpot, which has a maximum growth value of €3 million. That'd buy a lot of woodland retreats.As for gamblers who don't win the big one, which means the vast majority, Totem Guardians Dream Drop offers some decent action to accompany any DD-induced anticipation. Linking multiplier values to wins can be fun, and the leaving the rat race behind theme adds a blanket of chill to the chase. Totem Guardians Dream Drop isn't one of Relax Gaming's biggies, but it evolves the symbol multiplier feature, this time with connected ways, and the totem, spirit, guardian angle has been presented quite nicely.

Title: Piggy Luck
review: Piggy Luck: Slot OverviewDid you know that saying the word 'pig' on a boat is considered by some people to be bad luck on account of pigs not being able to swim? Dropping the p-word on a boat could lead to a smack on the nose since drawing blood is believed by some to be one way of reversing the curse. In the gambling world, it's quite the opposite, where pigs are commonly associated with cash and high living. Hopefully, our porky pals are lucky as they take centre stage in an online slot from Microgaming partner and independent developer Gong Gaming Technologies, titled Piggy Luck.Pigs are no strangers to the reels and are often portrayed as upper-class members of society. Piggy Bank Bills and Piggy Riches Megaways are two examples of pigs living it up in mansions, surrounded by the finer things in life. Piggy Luck isn't like that. It's more about bright colours, simply laid out to exude a positive attitude. Sad to say, a few spins in, our positivity crumbled fast. Essentially, players get a 5x3 grid matrix, a glowing logo down below, plus three pigs with meters up top.Possibly to help distract players from the lack of visual cues, Piggy Luck has a high hit rate of 49.19%, so nearly every second spin will theoretically be a winner. This flurry of hits is combined with a low volatile math model and a maximum return to player value of 95.12%, with 58.62% allocated to the base game and the rest to the features. Piggy Luck is available to play on any device and has bet choices of 20 p/c to $/€25 per spin.In the spirit of minimalism, just six pay symbols are used in the game, forming wins when matching tiles land on one of the 20 paylines, beginning from the left side of the panel. The three lower pay symbols are Q, K, and A, while the higher pays are crowns, stars, and diamonds. Landing five of a kind awards players 5x the bet for the low pays, or 7.5-12.5x the bet for the three high pays. Wilds are worth even more, up to 50x the bet for a line of five of them, plus they can be used to replace any normal pay symbol to complete a winning line.Piggy Luck: Slot FeaturesThe three piggy personalities displayed above the reels represent the features triggerable in Piggy Luck – Golden Path, free spins, and Cash Collect. In addition, players can activate a Wheel of Luck feature to gamble their way to the three bonus rounds.Golden PathLanding 3 Piggy King symbols on reels 2, 3, and 4 triggers the Golden Path feature. A ladder of prizes appears, as does a 6-segment wheel with the numbers 1-6 on each segment. The wheel spins, showing players how many steps they move along the prize ladder. After every spin, the lowest number on the wheel turns to Collect. The feature ends when the arrow on the ladder lands on Collect. Where players are on the ladder is the prize amount awarded.Free SpinsA total of 3 Piggy Queen symbols in view on reels 3, 4, and 5 awards 15 free spins. While the feature is active, landing 3 Piggy Queen symbols retriggers an additional +15 free spins. That's pretty much all there is to the free spins game.Cash CollectHit 3 Piggy Joker symbols on reels 1, 2, and 3 to trigger the Cash Collect feature. Here, 20 coins are placed on the screen. Players pick them one by one to reveal multipliers of the bet. The feature ends when a picked coin reveals a cash value and a tick. Then the sum of all multipliers is awarded.Wheel of LuckOn top of the grid in the base game are 3 wheels, each one corresponding to the free spins, Cash Collect, and Golden Path features. Each wheel has 2 segments – a trigger area and a non-feature area. Players collect Joker, King, and Piggy Queen symbols to increase the respective trigger area on the wheel. Each wheel can be spun for the cost of 10x the bet, and if the wheel arrow stops in the trigger area of the wheel, the feature will begin. Filling in the trigger area of a Wheel automatically starts the feature. One more thing to look out for is the wolf's paw symbol. This symbol resets the trigger area of the wheel it lands beneath.Piggy Luck: Slot VerdictPiggy Luck looked kind of brightly fun, to begin with, but this perception quickly morphed into one of exasperated tedium in a short space of time. The low volatile math model and low bonus round award values meant relatively fast feature triggers that tended to go nowhere. In some cases, not nowhere fast. For example, the first free spins trigger produced three further retriggers, and the total was 60 of the dullest free spins we'd ploughed through in a while. The end result wasn't exactly a kick in the teeth, but 60 spins to mount a 79.6x the bet win felt more like work than fun. As mentioned in the game sheet, free spins can theoretically be retriggered 'infinitely', which is a frightening thought.The Cash Collect felt just as pointless. You do know you are going to win something; however, you also know you are going to win something small. Go all the way to max The Cash Collect out by successfully picking all of the coins, and you're looking at a top prize of 39x the bet.Lastly, we've got the Golden Path, which does have a decent top prize. Yet, something doesn't sit right when you do the maths. The ladder has 36 steps, yet when adding all the numbers on the wheel, the total comes to 21. Perhaps filling the Golden Path meter in the base game helps players progress, but this wasn't the way the demo functioned, and by then, it was sort of a moot point anyway.Have you ever been driving along a straight piece of road and felt like you were going backwards when the car was, in reality, moving forwards? There was a similar sense produced while playing Piggy Luck. If you don't like its light, frequent style, it's hard to throw off the impression Piggy Luck is a waste of time.

Title: Beheaded
review: Beheaded: Slot OverviewShipwrecks, ay? There are a lot of reasons why you wouldn't want to find yourself in that situation. For example, one nightmare shipwreck scenario plays out in software provider Nolimit City's online slot Beheaded.
