A sleepy Arabic soundtrack meanders away producing a relaxing feel, as the onscreen exploits unfold.Ramses gets his revenge on any device, offering bets from 10 p/c to $/€20 per spin. While RTP is slightly above average on 96.15%, in the short term the high volatility ensures anything can happen. From base game grinds to bonus games that occasionally fire off a big one out of nowhere, the game can swing in all directions.Relax made the agreeable choice of using a 4,096 win ways system for players to form combinations. Rows are irrelevant, so as long as three or more identical symbols are adjacent from the leftmost reel you’ve got a winner. In another nice touch, when symbols start to line up, they become indented by sinking into the floor, so you can see exactly which ones are winning or not. A small thing, but handy nonetheless and much cleaner than the way Red Tiger handle things for example, who completely clutter the screen with their payline count-ups.The symbols used have a compact icon-y look reminiscent of collectable game tokens. There are eight regular pay symbols, split into four low pay patterns, and high pay gods. The high pays include Anubis, Sobek, Horus, and Ramses at the top. This four are worth payouts of 1.5 to 4 times the bet in combinations of six of a kind. Not huge, yet the pay mechanic helps, as do wild multipliers during the bonus.Ramses’ Revenge: Slot FeaturesFor the majority of the time, not a whole lot happens in regards to features. Mystery Sandstorms punctuate the base game, but the jewel of the Nile is far and away free spins with their roaming multiplier wilds.On any base game spin, the Mystery Sandstorm feature may randomly trigger. If it does, 2-6 waves occur, where 1-4 mystery symbols per wave are dumped on the reels. All mystery symbols change to reveal the same matching symbol type.The most exciting moments are reserved for the round of free spins. The explorer symbols are what you want here and it takes 2 in view trigger 6 free spins. Before free spins begin, two mummies wander out of the tomb and take the place of the two triggering explorers. These mummies are wild, replacing any other symbol to make a combination. Note that wilds only ever appear during free spins.When new explorers wilds land, the closest mummy moves to take its place. In doing so, one extra spin is awarded, and the multiplier of the respective mummy increases by 1. If more explorers land than there are mummies in view, additional mummies are added to the reels. Also, if more than one mummy is used in a win, the values are multiplied rather than added. There can be, at most, four active mummies on the reels at once.Players not in the mood to wait through the base game for the bonus to hit, may have the option to skip them altogether. Where available, Relax has bolted on feature buy functionality, costing 80 times the stake. When activated, two scatters land on the next spin, triggering the free spins feature. On a technical note, the RTP remains the same this way is as in the default mode.Ramses’ Revenge: Slot VerdictRamses’ Revenge is a game that contains few surprises. The first is how rough the game can be, belying its cute sprite-based appearance. It can be tough going, requiring patience to get to the good parts, or you can leap into the bonus buy to fast track things along - though this is no guarantee of success.Not a lot happened for the first 300 spins or so. There were a couple of circa 30x wins to help stay alive, yet the rest was pretty so-so for a while. The first bonus game was an eye-opener though. Even just two wandering multiplier wilds proved to be quite effective, providing they wandered into the right positions. Overall, bonus rounds proved to be as temperamental as the rest of the game. Some were weak; some were unexpectedly good. During one of our bonus buys, however, we managed to score a win of almost 1,000x.What makes the free spins round particularly interesting is the way mummies multiply each other, giving it a strong resemblance to Jammin' Jars in a strange way. An x4 and an x6 for example, in the midst of several high pays, can cause some serious mayhem. Drop a third wild multiplier in and things can really get hectic. This dynamic well suits the 4,096 ways to win system. Ramses’ Revenge can be unforgiving enough as it is, with fixed paylines, it might have been heart-breaking.In some ways, Ramses’ Revenge ended up playing out like Relax Gaming's Marching Legions. Like that one, free spins can go nuts, piling on multipliers and wins like there's no tomorrow. Then again, it can be equally as frustrating. Ramses’ Revenge is an enjoyable game, a little different, provoking emotional responses which seem out of odds with its lightweight looks.

Title: The Catfather
review: The Catfather: Slot OverviewIn the spirit of a Coolidge painting depicting dogs playing poker is The Catfather from developer Pragmatic Play. Not only do players get a slot dripping in the flea-ridden beasts, but they also get them dressed like gangsters ready to do a bit of crime. Anyone care to wager what these dastardly mousers might be up to - scratching the rug, or just peeing on it? Anything is possible in a game run by cats impersonating criminals. Then again, perhaps not exactly anything, since The Catfather is about as lethal as a big sleeping furry feline stretched out by the heater on a cold winter’s morning – that thing isn’t going anywhere. Still, put this many cats in one place, and wacky things are bound to happen, right?The Catfather - base gameLet’s start by saying The Catfather isn’t a complicated game, made up as it is of 5 reels, 3 rows, and 9 fixed paylines. For a slot at least partly mob-related, the background is as strangely humdrum as it gets. Instead of some speakeasy, or hideout, we get a couple of lamps and drapes next to the grid - an image of staid homely domestication if ever there was one. Clearly, these cats are gangstas in thought rather than deed. For your listening pleasure, a wicked bass lead 70s Bond era soundtrack adds some much-needed drama.The most remarkable thing about The Catfather, aside from its bonkers theme, is a whopping default RTP value of 98.1%. As equally mystifying, for other reasons, is an absence of a volatility rating, usually prominently displayed in a Pragmatic Play slot. Here one can speculate, but judging by the rest of the game, don’t expect a highly volatile machine, quite the opposite. Due to the number of paylines, bets can be placed from 9 p/c per spin up to $/€45 for the higher rollers.On the topic of paylines, The Catfather pays both ways as long as three or more symbols line up from reel 1 or 5. Symbols are made up of sparkling Q-A royals, then five kitties with distinctive looks and get-ups from Zorro style masks to monocles plus Bowler Hats. As to values, five of a kind premium wins are worth payouts of 3.33x to 22.22x the stake. Everything is ever so slightly unusual in this game. Take wilds, for example. They substitute for regular pay symbols like normal but pay out when just one lands (1.11x the bet), up to 555x the bet for five of a kind. Wilds gain an extra ability during one of the base game features too.The Catfather: Slot FeaturesThe Catfather - It's a Wild Night feature in actionNestled in with the multitude of cat pimps, crooks, and goodness only knows what else, are two bonus features. One is random wild stacks, the other free spins where all wins are subject to a fixed multiplier.Wild reels pop up completely at random on any base spin. Well, not all reels, only reels 2, 3, and 4 are eligible for this effect, but since the game pays both ways they can be surprisingly alright. Don’t expect to retire after playing The Catfather under the best of circumstances though; it’s not a dream maker of a slot.The other feature, free spins, is triggered when 3 or more mouse scatters land anywhere on the reels. Players pick up a payout of 0.22, 0.56, or 2.22 times their stake as well as 10, 15, or 25 free spins, when 3, 4, or 5 scatters are in view. Like the rest of The Catfather, free spins keep things simple. There are no convoluted rule changes or anything innovative either really. Basically, all wins have their values multiplied by 4. Scatters continue to show during the bonus game too, so free spins can be retriggered up to 50 at the most.The Catfather: Slot VerdictThe Catfather is one of those ludicrous games a small segment of the population will utterly fall for while everyone else shakes their head in disbelief. Cat devotees may well love the playfully mesmerising bunch of oddball felines in various guises all over the reels. Players who find entertainment value in animals pretending to be humans might find The Catfather amusing at a push as well. Okay, we are clutching at straws here, but there is a bit of an old school charm to the features, if you want to put a positive spin on it. Wild reels and free spins with a multiplier is about as old school as it gets, and a little beguiling with their simplicity.Beneath the plain, cat-filled exterior is a pretty domesticated math model hacking up modest wins like annoying hairballs. Those who like wallowing around on the spot might appreciate the gentler volatility, yet what lies beneath the fleabag exterior might appeal to a wider range of players in the right circumstance. For instance, the higher than average RTP might come in handy for working through wagering requirements perhaps. It’s actually hard to think of another game that comes close to such a figure for a good long while. Of course, RTP isn’t enough to make you look past the rest of The Catfather’s shortcomings though. Not least is a max win of 2,251x the stake, which suits the cuddly gaming, yet is hardly exciting.Add it all up, and you’ve got a game which might suit certain situations due to a high return to player value, but little outside of that - unless you live in a house where you can’t take a step without putting a foot on a fur ball. In that case, The Catfather’s abundance of felines will extend its furry little paws to draw you in. If you’re more of a dog person, then The Catfather ‘s math model and rewards have about as much drive as a spayed moggy.

Title: Dragon Hopper
review: Dragon Hopper: Slot OverviewPush Gaming's Dragon Hopper takes players on a journey to the Orient, blending familiar mechanics with inventive features designed to add depth and unpredictability. Following in the footsteps of the 2021 release Fire Hopper and borrowing inspiration from titles like Crystal Catcher, Dragon Hopper looks to evolve the grid slot experience. While it doesn't shy away from using proven elements, it introduces new features, such as the Dragon feature and the Bubble feature, as well as the Mystic Flare feature.Visually, Dragon Hopper captures a tranquil, almost dreamlike atmosphere, with the reels suspended high up in the clouds. Traditional Asian architecture and vibrant lanterns dot the background, while soft, glowing lights add a touch of mysticism to the setting. The audio complements the visuals with a laid-back, classic Asian-inspired soundtrack that leans into soothing melodies and subtle tones. It's a relaxing backdrop that avoids being overly dramatic, adding a sense of calm to the gameplay while maintaining the thematic consistency Push Gaming is known for.Dragon Hopper slot - base gameDragon Hopper operates on a 7x7 grid and employs a Cluster Link mechanic where wins occur by landing clusters of at least five matching symbols, connected either horizontally or vertically. Cascading symbols follow every win, clearing successful clusters and allowing new symbols to drop into the empty spaces for potential chain reactions. It's a highly volatile experience, backed by a configurable RTP of up to 96.33% at its optimal setting, with a minimum bet starting at €/$0.10 and climbing to a hefty $/€100 for high rollers.On the paytable, the symbols are split into higher and lower-paying categories, all thematically styled as colorful lanterns befitting the festive vibe of the game. The top-tier symbols include red, gold, and pink lanterns, offering payouts up to 50x the bet for clusters of 17 or more. Meanwhile, the low-paying symbols, represented by hues of blue, green, and purple, cap out at a more modest 10x the bet for equivalent cluster sizes.  As a cluster slot, winning clusters are removed via the cascade mechanic, allowing new symbols to drop in and potentially create additional wins.Dragon Hopper: Slot FeaturesDragon Hopper slot - Mystic Flare featureThe features in Dragon Hopper showcase a mix of familiar mechanics and fresh ideas. Push Gaming has included some of its signature elements, such as the Instant Prize symbols, while introducing new concepts like the Bubble feature and the Dragon feature. Here's a detailed breakdown.Wild symbols and Dragon featureThe Dragon and Golden Dragon symbols serve as wilds, substituting for all symbols except the Fire Cloud and Bonus symbols. These wilds come with an initial multiplier ranging from x1 to x10, which increases by +1 whenever the Dragon moves during the Dragon feature. When a Dragon symbol is in view alongside a Fire Cloud symbol, the Dragon Feature is triggered. The Dragon symbol flies to the nearest Fire Cloud, leaving a Golden Dragon behind with its multiplier intact, creating new win opportunities.Instant Prize SymbolsA Push Gaming hallmark, these symbols act as bet multipliers, with values ranging from x1 to x1,000. Clusters of 5 or more Instant Prize Symbols trigger payouts. These symbols can appear in both the base game and free spins.Mystic Flare FeatureTriggered randomly on non-winning cascades, this feature introduces Mystic symbols onto the grid in sizes ranging from 2x2 to 4x4. These symbols then break down into 1x1 symbols, which can transform into regular symbols, Instant Prize symbols, or even bonus or Dragon symbols.Free Spins FeatureWhen 3, 4 or 5 bonus symbols land on the reels, 6, 9 or 12 free spins are awarded, respectively. Once in, the Dragon, Golden Dragon, Fire Cloud and Instant Prize symbols from the base game will remain in the same position and carry over to the free spins feature with the respective values. During the round, each empty symbol position will spin through to land either Fire Cloud, Instant Prize, Extra Spin or Blank symbols. Each Instant Prize symbol that lands will remain in its position throughout the feature. All instant prize symbol clusters are evaluated at the end of the round.Bubble FeatureDuring the free spins feature, Bubble symbols randomly appear on the grid before the first spin begins and remain in place until the next spin. These symbols are non-paying but come with assigned values of 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, or 500. The Bubble symbol moves one grid space per spin, either vertically or diagonally. These symbols can appear individually or as stacks of up to five and interact with key game elements such as the Golden Dragon symbol, Fire Cloudsymbol, and Instant Prize symbol.When a Bubble symbol lands on the Golden Dragon symbol, it activates and adds its value to the Golden Dragon symbol's multiplier. If a Fire Cloud symbol lands beneath a Bubble symbol, the Bubble activates and transfers its value to the Fire Cloud symbol. The Golden Dragon symbol then follows the Dragon feature, transferring the Bubble's value to its multiplier. When an Instant Prize symbol lands beneath a Bubble symbol, the Bubble activates, adding its value to the Instant Prize symbol. Similarly, if a Bubble lands on an Instant Prize symbol, it activates and transfers its value to the Instant Prize symbol.Dragon Hopper slot - free spinsDragon Hopper: Slot VerdictPush Gaming has a well-established reputation for delivering vibrant, feature-packed games, and Dragon Hopper feels like a continuation of this ethos - though with a sense of déjà vu that's hard to ignore. The game borrows heavily from Push's playbook, layering classic mechanics like cascading reels and Instant Prize symbols with fresh elements such as the Dragon and Bubble features. The result is a slot that delivers pretty much what you would expect of a new Push Gaming release. Nothing more, nothing less.The Instant Prize symbol feature, a staple for Push Gaming since its debut around 2019, once again takes center stage. While it's undeniably effective at driving gameplay and engagement, its ubiquity across recent titles like Big Bamboo, Razor Returns, and Boss Bear has started to feel overly familiar. In Dragon Hopper, it's once again been integrated well, but just like the Dragon feature, with its hopping multipliers, it doesn't quite elevate the experience beyond what we've seen before.Ultimately, Dragon Hopper is a polished addition to Push Gaming's library, but it doesn't quite have the bite or originality to stand out among their more innovative offerings. For fans of the studio's formula, it's a dependable choice, but for those looking for something groundbreaking, it might feel like hopping on well-trodden ground. Solid, fun, but not unforgettable.

Title: Arthur's Gold
review: Arthur’s Gold: OverviewLaunched in mid-2018, Gold Coin Studios release their first slot, Arthur’s Gold, in partnership with one of the titans of the industry Microgaming. Led by an ex-IGT Vice President, this Reno-based studio brings with it plenty of experience, though details are still light. For now, let’s content ourselves with their new slot based on the old tales of Arthur, his knights, the round table, and apparently, his bags of gold.Scribes of yore must have glossed over this, but Arthur was pretty cashed up as evidenced by the mountain of coins onscreen. Most people will probably recall Arthur’s search for the Holy Grail rather than amassing a fortune, but that’s okay, coins it is. Someone at Gold Coin Studios clearly has a thing for them so let’s roll with it.The influence of land-based slots at IGT appears to have leaked into the development of Arthur’s Gold which has a slightly classic vibe to it. Booting up the slot instantly made us think of Edict’s Dragon’s Treasure. The rest of the background is taken up by an old hall which can be seen on the edges of the 5-reel, 3-row grid. The user interface is kept neatly out of the way, where stakes can be set by hitting the +/- buttons for spin costs of 20 p/c to $/€50.You never feel lonely playing Arthur’s Gold because so many characters appear on the grid. Double premium symbols amplify the effect, so instead of having one Arthur on a symbol, you can have two like a twin or a doppelganger. Along with Arthur, players spin Merlin, Guinevere, Lancelot, and Viviane as the high pays, with J-A royals as the low pays. All symbols need to land least three of a kind on one of the 20 paylines to trigger a payout.As mentioned, the high pays can appear doubled up which has a dramatic effect on the value of a win. For example, all of the high pays are worth 2.5x the stake for a line of five. However, when doubled to 10 of a kind, their values increase to 50x - 125x the stake. It is similar to the effect Just for the Win used with Tweethearts and the clone Double Lucky Line, but in Arthur’s Gold, double symbols can land in any position.The game also comes with two wilds - a standard wild and a special wild that only appears in the bonus game. Wilds not only substitute for any regular pay symbol, but 2, 3, 4, or 5 of them on a payline are worth 2x, 6x, 30x, or 500x the stake. Critically, wilds count as double symbols when they substitute for the high pay symbols.Some positive numbers are called forth from the math model to do Arthur’s handiwork starting with an RTP of 96.19%. Hit frequency is quite high, at 30.21%, or a little shy of 1 in 3, so wins do turn up on frequent basis. You’ll need them to do so since the majority of winning combinations are low value unless double symbols are involved. The math model is highly volatile and the game is capable of dealing sizeable wins when it’s on, which generally happens during the features.Arthur’s Gold: FeaturesArthur's Gold - free spins featureThe best way to get your hands on some of those coins is by triggering the Arthur’s Gold Free Spins Bonus. This occurs when 3, 4, or 5 treasure chest scatters land to award 2x, 5x, or 10x the stake plus 10 free spins. During free spins, a new special wild enters the game which may land on reels 2, 3, or 4. When it does, it expands to cover a full reel and triggers a respin.If another special wild lands on a respin, it expands and is locked for another respin. Up to 3 consecutive respins are technically possible and do not reduce the number of free spins. The final rule is Scatters appear only in the base game, so it is not possible to extend or retrigger the bonus game.Last is the Double Up feature where players can guess the result of a coin toss to double (or nothing) any base game win or the total amount won during free spins. The Double Up is available once for each win as long as the current win does not exceed $/€5,000.Arthur’s Gold: VerdictSo does Arthur’s cup runneth over to reward those he deems worthy? To an extent, it does. Expanding wilds aren’t exactly new, but they work well with the double symbols to produce larger than usual combinations for agreeable results. Thankfully, since wilds count for two high pay symbols they are convenient for not only putting together 5+ combinations, but knocking out plenty 3 or 4 symbol combos that keep the action and bankroll ticking along.Casting your eye to the immense pile of treasure onscreen leads to one question - what’s the potential in Arthur’s Gold? At over 4,000 times the stake, decent wins are possible, though not quite the hall of gold coins alluded to.All told, Arthur’s Gold is a fairly solid first release to be featured here from Gold Coin Studios. Effort has gone into most aspects of the game without the developer explicitly favouring one element over another. One possible sticking point could be the target audience not getting too exciting about the potential.Those that identify as ‘high volatility players’, as Gold Coin calls them in their sales pitch of the game, might give pause to max wins some may perceive as modest, although the volatile swings are undoubtedly there to offer both thrill and excitement.

Title: Ashoka
review: Ashoka: Slot OverviewTime for a history lesson team. Cast your minds back a few thousand years to the 3rd century BCE when a chap called Ashoka, otherwise known as Ashoka the Great, ruled a significant portion of Asia and is said to have played an important role in helping spread Buddhism back in the day. Hey, who said online gambling is all fruit and flaming sevens, huh? That brings us to Ashoka, an online slot from developer ELK Studios, a scatter-paying game incorporating several mechanical tricks into one exotic place.Exotic might not be a strong enough word to describe Ashoka. With its many armed statue, rhythmic chanting soundtrack, and secretive atmosphere, Ashoka has a sort of mystical vibe going on. Its thick, heavy natural world setting possesses echoes of some of the Gold slots, such as Voodoo Gold, Ecuador Gold, or Pacific Gold, for example. It's like one of those places people don't go to much or haven't been to in a long while, which plants have reclaimed, and the spirit of the natural world is almost tangible as if visiting the spot at a certain time on a certain day would allow communion between the noumenal world and the one that resides unseen behind the veil. Something like that.Ashoka slot - base gameFlanked by a skull and statue is Ashoka's gaming grid made up of 6 columns holding 8 positions each. On each spin, not all positions on the reels are filled with active symbols; some spaces are taken up by valueless blocker symbols. Should 8 or more matching pay symbols be in view anywhere on the grid, a win is formed, and the respective symbols are cleared from the grid. Vertically adjacent blocker symbols are removed as well. After the symbol removal, new symbols Avalanche down to fill the gaps. Highly volatile, players select a base bet of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin and may choose to activate bonus modes from the X-iter menu. No matter how Ashoka is played, its theoretical return to player value is 94%.For symbols, Ashoka has J-A ranks displayed on stone blocks as its lows, then a blue gem, green gem, orange gem, red gem, and a white tiger as its highs. Landing an 8-matching scatter win pays 0.1 to 5 times the bet, while a 15+ matching scatter win is worth 3 to 100 times the bet. Ashoka also makes use of several kinds of wild symbols, all of which can replace any regular pay symbol. These are regular wilds, Big Wilds of up to 3x3 in size, and charged wilds. Charged wilds stay on the reels for up to three wins, and if spaces appear beneath a big wild, they are filled with 1x1-sized wilds.Ashoka: Slot FeaturesAshoka slot - free spins triggeredAs well as the wild variety and Avalanche mechanic, Ashoka also has a multiplier symbol, super multiplier symbol, Bonus Game, and the X-iter.Multiplier and Super MultiplierMultiplier symbols add their values to the win multiplier when there is a winning scatter in view. The win multiplier multiplies all wins when it is active. The multiplier symbol is removed along with winning symbols by Avalanches. The super multiplier also adds its value to the win multiplier when there is a winning scatter in view. However, the super multiplier stays on the grid, reactivating for each Avalanche. It is removed when no more wins appear.Bonus GameSkull bonus symbols may land amongst the blockers. These inactive bonus symbols become active when they are vertically adjacent to a winning symbol, and getting 3 active bonus symbols in the base game triggers 10 free drops in the bonus game. Any super multiplier symbols carry over to the bonus game and persist between free drops. Extra free drops are awarded where having 2 or 3 active bonus symbols awards +5 or +10 free drops, respectively.X-iterThe X-iter feature buy menu gives players the chance to buy various game modes. These are:Bonus Hunt – 3x the bet to buy a game round with a greater chance of triggering a bonus.Charged Wilds – 10x the bet to buy a game round where all wild symbols are charged wild symbols.Super Multiplier – 25x the bet to buy a game round with a guaranteed super multiplier symbol.Buy Bonus – 100x the bet to buy the bonus game.Super Bonus – 500x the bet to buy the bonus game with a guaranteed super multiplier.Ashoka slot - free spinsAshoka: Slot VerdictBy no means a simple game, Ashoka didn't produce the same sensation of overflowing features or rules as they sometimes do when reviewing an ELK Studios game. Often, by now, it can feel like the typing version of a 10K jog just to get everything down. Anyway, we made it to the final section, so how did Ashoka fare? For the most part pretty positively, and while we are used to seeing slots from ELK Studios boasting mind-bending numbers in terms of ways to win, i.e. the Nitropolis range with its millions and millions of ways, maybe billions, scatter paying systems are much rarer. In fact, Ashoka might well be the studio's first. Being the creative team they are, ELK Studios has avoided following in the success of other pay-anywhere slots like Sweet Bonanza or Pragmatic Play's Gates games and has done something more original with it. The result felt like a mix of the previously mentioned Kane slots, a bit of Dropz, a dash of Cluster Tumble, and plenty of its own magic.Like Cluster Tumble, one of the primary base game goals is smashing blocker symbols to enter the bonus game. Flicking on the Bonus Hunt turned out to be a highly enjoyable way to take on this quest, as drops turned into a tantalising skull chase. Pricey, though, at 3 times the regular bet. Multiplier and super multiplier symbols were not exactly plentiful, but wilds popped up every so often, so kudos to the ELK Studios math team for incorporating them into a scatter-paying slot which often isn't the way.No surprise that the super bonus round was the more exciting of the two. The persistent win multiplier and persistent super multiplier have the ability to jack the game's excitement levels. Again, pricey, though, when bought from the X-iter, perhaps. At full charge, Ashoka can produce wins of up to 25,000 times the bet. There will no doubt be things that players aren't overly fond of here; no need to bang on about the sub-95% RTP which is practically ELk Studios' MO by now, and Ashoka can be tough going. Had the RTP been upped a notch it would have been a top scorer by any standards. Having said that, Ashoka is undoubtedly another high-quality ELK Studios release that takes the scatter-paying online slot format in an exciting direction.

Title: Elemental Princess
review: Elemental Princess: OverviewYggdrasil Gaming partner studio Dreamtech journeys to their favoured corner of the slot market – the Asian theme section. Elemental Princess is based around four princesses, each one unleashing a unique power and reward during modifiers or free spins. Players can look forward to floating wilds, sticky wilds, spreading wilds, and win multipliers.Elemental Princess has a gentle look, its background changing to match whichever princess is active. This could be anything from cherry blossoms, rolling hills, light green trees, or bamboo stalks. When the four ladies are brought together, the gang looks like an Asian version of Alphonse Mucha’s Art Nouveau illustrations of the four seasons. The action takes place on a 5 reel, 3-row game area set within a tastefully decorated wooden structure. Players get 25 fixed paylines to hit winners on, occurring when three or more land adjacently from the leftmost reel.Playable from 30 p/c to $/€150 per spin on mobiles, tablets, or desktop devices, the game produces a range of stats - some solid, some not so exciting. Let’s start with one of the better ones – the RTP which is comfortably above average at 96.46%. Wins land quite regularly to keep the pace up too. Officially 34.21% of spins will return something, paired with medium volatility. Overall, the potential is pretty disappointing though, in fact, it’s possibly the least inspiring aspect of Elemental Princess. But we'll get to that.Before the big reveal takes place, a quick look over the paytable where there are 10 pays, and a bunch of special symbols. Pay symbols start with 9-A card royals, followed by 4 high pays designed in an earth, air, fire, and water style. Premium values aren’t bad, at the upper levels at least, ranging from 6 to 40 times the stake for 5 of a kind.Helping form combinations are not one but five wild symbols. While they might look different, they all essentially do the same thing – substitute for the regular pays. They are the most lucrative symbols in the game, where a line of 5 is worth 80 times the stake. The most common is the standard wild, the remaining four wilds appear during the features.Elemental Princess: FeaturesElemental Princess - free spinsThere are shades of Play’n GO’s Moon Princess going on here, and not just in the title. Each princess can modify the reels in their own unique way when activated, while the four free spins features are based around them. However, it doesn’t get anywhere near as chaotic as Play’n GO’s slot.On any base game spin, there is a chance a Princess Spin modifier may be awarded. There are 4 types:The Earth Princess Spin turns all standard wilds into Earth Princess Wilds. Any high paying symbol next to an Earth Princess Wild is also transformed into an Earth Princess Wild.On a Water Princess Spin, all standard wilds turn into Water Princess Wilds, and 2, 3, 5, or 10 of these symbols are placed in random positions on the reels.Fire Princess Spins change standard wilds into Fire Princess Wilds, plus a multiplier of x2, x3, x5, or x10 is applied to any wins.If the Air Princess Spin is awarded, all standard wilds change into Air Princess Wilds, and a Floating Mega Wild appears over the reels, up to 3x3 in size.Next is the Free Games feature which is triggered in two different ways. One is when 3 or more scatter symbols are in view; the second is the Lucky Feature Trigger and Re-Trigger. This latter method can trigger the Free Games feature from the base game, or retrigger it if it's already active.After the trigger, a selection screen chooses one of the four Princess features. Each one starts with 10 free spins and can be retriggered when 3 or more scatters land, or the Lucky Feature Retrigger occurs. Depending on which Princess feature is triggered, this is what you can look forward to:Earth Princess free spins use Spreading Wilds. Wilds become Earth Princess Wilds, which then turn any adjacent high pay symbols into Earth Princess Wilds as well.Water Princess free spins come with Held Wilds. Any Water Princess Wilds appearing are locked and remain in position for the remainder of the feature.Next are Fire Princess free spins which use a Win Multiplier. During this feature, any Fire Princess Wilds in view increase the win multiplier by +1.Lastly, are Air Princess free spins and Floating Mega Wilds. The round starts with a 1x2 Floating Mega Wild on the reels in a random position. On each free spin, it moves to a new position. Also, whenever an Air Princess Wild appears, it is collected. Triggering free spins with a minimum of 6 scatters might seem a lot, but they appear in stacks of threes on the reels, so not as tall an order as you might think. During testing, they landed in threes, so two reels were usually enough to launch the bonus game. Plus, you get the locking respins feature, lending a helping hand.That just leaves winning potential, and this is one thing about Savanna Roar which doesn't disappoint. During a billion simulated spins, Jelly managed to get the game stampeding and recorded a win of 10,459 times the stake.Jelly's aim with Savanna Roar was to produce a slot for players who prefer simplicity over complex games, using a familiar theme and proven mechanics. Job done in this case, as Jelly has nailed its objectives; however, Savanna Roar is so familiar as to be forgettable. Now the cherry's popped, hopefully Jelly can let more of their individual creativity shine next time.

Title: Marlin Catch
review: Marlin Catch: Slot OverviewFishing is a highly popular pastime, spilling over from lakes, rivers, and seas to the reels in abundance. Pragmatic Play's hit Big Bass Bonanza is one of many to strike the right note with armchair anglers, and its success must have caught the eye of rival studio Stakelogic. Stakelogic is no stranger to riding the coattails of others, and this time they've come up with a fishing-themed slot that feels very similar to BBB. However, the resulting slot Marlin Catch isn't what you would call a direct port, since there are no money symbols, ergo, no money symbol collection which was a hallmark of Big Bass Bonanza and others like it. Instead, Stakelogic has tinkered with several elements to produce a much gruntier slot all around. Time to cast off?Marlin Catch either takes players beneath the waves or gives them a birds-eye view of some very clear water, where fish meander and coral sits there doing its thing. Like other similar fishing slots, Marline Catch is big, bright, and friendly-looking, with chunkified symbols all over its reels. Reels happen to be transparent, so players keen on the great outdoors get a better view of the aquatic life bubbling away down there.As fishing is for anyone with a rod, Marlin Catch is suitable for playing on any device, where stakes of 10 p/c to $/€20 are available. A medium/high volatile game, rated 4 out of 5, the RTP comes in different configurations, as high as 96.5%, though there is no mention of whether the return value changes whether you play in the default mode or when activating one of the four possible bonus buy options.Played on a 5x3 sized game panel, with 10 fixed paylines, the job is to hit winning combinations of three or more from the lefthand side across them. The first five symbols on the paytable are puffy BBB-style 10-A card royals which pay 1-5x the bet for a line of five. Then there are hooks, rods, coral, and life rings as premiums, paying out 10-200x the bet for five of a kind. Wilds have the same value as the top premium and substitute for any normal paying symbols.Marlin Catch: Slot FeaturesInterestingly, Marlin Catch does not feature a money symbol collection, which came as a surprise. What it does have is free spins with sticky multiplier wilds, a collection bar system, a gamble feature, and feature buys.Gamble OptionEach winning combination may be gambled or the prize money collected. To gamble, picking the correct suit or colour of a face-down card quadruples or doubles the amount, while picking incorrectly forfeits the winnings.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 marlin scatter symbols awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. A few new rules come into play here. One is that when wilds land, they stick in position for the next spin. If new wilds land on the new spin, all previous wilds get a +1 multiplier increase – up to a maximum of x7. If no wilds land on the next spin, the previous wild multipliers are reduced by 1, or if they have no multiplier, they are removed from the reels.A collection symbol and collection bar also appear during free spins. Whenever the fisherman symbol lands, it is collected on the bar, even if it lands behind a sticky wild. Each 3 fishermen symbols collected awards more spins and increases the win multiplier:3 collectors award +10 free spins and an x2 win multiplier6 collectors award +8 free spins and an x3 win multiplier9 collectors award +6 free spins and an x5 win multiplier12 collectors award +4 free spins and an x10 win multiplierBuy FeatureIf you are able to, Marlin Catch offers four ways to buy the bonus round. Shelling out 100x, 500x, or 1,000x the bet gets you 10, 15, or 20 free spins. Or you can try your luck by paying 375x the bet for a lucky dip option.Marlin Catch: Slot VerdictAfter the positive reception Big Bass Bonanza and its follow-ups received, there are no surprises to see copycats creeping out of the woodwork. The fact that it comes from Stakelogic, who has no qualms borrowing other people's ideas, just adds an extra layer of inevitability. Well, no ethical qualms perhaps, but Avatar UX's legal challenge over their PopWins mechanic saw Stakelogic paint themselves into a corner where the only way out was to licence it.It feels unlikely the same thing will happen over Marlin Catch between Stakelogic and Pragmatic Play. Partly because Big Bass Bonanza itself was strongly influenced by outside sources. Perhaps Stakelogic has learnt their lesson because the similarities between this and BBB are more tenuous. For one, the money symbol collection has been axed and replaced by a sticky wild multiplier feature which can actually, really go off. Clever the way existing wild multiplier values increase when new wilds hit or are reduced when none do.Having the chance to buy free spins right away is sure to appeal to certain impatient anglers out there, too. It's as if Stakelogic took the bits they liked, gutted the bits they didn't, and went wild with what was leftover. One of the biggest differentiators is the vast difference in the two game's potential. Where BBB topped out at 2,100x, Marlin Catch heads for much deeper waters where players can technically haul in catches worth up to 25,000x the bet.Marlin Catch does things differently enough to sit side by side the slot it resembles rather than just push it completely out of the limelight. There is a place for both slots, in other words. The things that Stakelogic have added, moulded, or changed have made Marlin Catch a more original experience than first suspected. There's the same getting out on the water spirit as before. Just this time, players can buy their way to the bonus, gamble wins if they want, and snag sticky wild multipliers in free spins, meaning much bigger fish on the menu.

Title: Dawn of Egypt
review: Dawn of Egypt (Play'n GO): OverviewIf there is one developer who digs the Egyptian theme it is Play’n GO. What’s the tally up to now? Hard to say but there is quite a selection for fans of the genre to fire up. The latest to come off the production line is Dawn of Egypt which is a sequel to Legacy of Egypt. A danger with pouring forth similar games is that they start to blur together and produce diminishing results. What is Dawn of Egypt’s impact to be?As we’ve so often come to expect from Play’n GO the game is certainly easy on the eyes. Symbols are gorgeously high-def, and the background brings Ancient Egypt to roaring to the screen. The 5x3 reels are located in a temple at the base of a pyramid which is backlit by blazing sunlight. Play’n GO has a fair amount of practice building these types of slots, and they have certainly become dab hands at recreating the magic of the era. Once players are done admiring the scenery, they can select appropriate bets from 10 p/c up to $/€100 per spin and play begins. The reels are crossed by 10 paylines on which to form combinations of three matching symbols or more for a payout.Symbol values are rather high right across the board. First up are the low paying J – A royals, all well-styled according to the theme. Next up are the high pays where we get a lotus flower, Ankh, scorpion, snake, and the gods Bastet and Horus. The falcon god Horus brings in a solid 100 times the stake when five appear on a payline. The standard wild, which is a shiny scarab ornament, will give you 100 times the stake for five of a kind while also performing its usual duty of substituting for any other standard pay symbol.Hardcore players will be pleased to see a high volatility rating here (7/10), albeit not as high as Book of Dead for example which comes in at 1o out of 10 in terms of volatility score. Keep an eye on the RTP, which is comes in at 96.23% by default but which can vary by market.Dawn of Egypt (Play'n GO): Features﻿Alongside decent returns during the base game, the developer wizards at Play’n GO have put together a real mash-up of features. It is nice to see that more though went into developing them then it did with choosing the genre. Like exploring ancient ruins, the key feature is a two-tiered level of Free Spins. Initially, free spins are triggered by three or more scatter symbols which can land on any reel. The mysteriously blue pyramid scatter also brings top returns with it. Get four of five on a payline for 5x or 20x the stake. However, get lucky, and score 5 scatters then you are looking at a 1,000x payout.The free spin round begins by spinning the Wheel of the Gods to determine how many spins there will be. The wheel can produce 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 15, or 20 free spins in total. On every single free spin, one high paying symbol is randomly selected. Any lesser value high pay symbols that land on that spin are automatically upgraded to the chosen high pay symbol.Not only that, but during free spins, the pyramid scatter changes into a wild scatter. On the one hand, the wild scatter acts like a normal wild and can substitute for any of the pay symbols. Also, if 2 or more wild scatters land on a free spin they pause the round and trigger Pyramid Spins. Each wild scatter is worth up to 4 Pyramid Spins. This means up to 20 Pyramid Spins are possible and they can also be retriggered indefinitely. What makes Pyramid spins special is that they retain the chosen high pay symbol from the free spin the feature was launched from. This can mean a run of just the chosen symbol, wilds, and royals in play. Once Pyramid Spins have run out the game returns to the free spins round.Dawn of Egypt (Play'n GO): VerdictAs mentioned in the intro, Play’n GO has a soft spot for Ancient Egypt flavoured slot. The benefit for players is that they pull them off well, which you’d expect after all that practice. The interesting thing is that they are starting to kind of look alike. Symbols and backgrounds vary from slot to slot, sure, but they have a familiar ‘quality’ to them. You just know when you are playing a Play’n GO Egyptian themed slot.That’s not a bad thing though as their quality is typically good. On a positive note, Dawn of Egypt’s parts all add up to a dependably enjoyable slot. Potential is equally juicy and is the familiar 5,000 times the stake that Play’n GO like to go with. Dawn of Egypt’s high volatility rating means that when it goes off, lucrative rolls are possible. This is more likely to happen during free spins naturally. The way free spins can lead to Pyramid Spins is not only a great idea but adds an extra dimension to the nerves as well as well as to winnings. The game is not just all about its free spins though. Decent symbol values during the base game prevent it from being a snore-fest. Of course, lines of the highest paying symbols are rare, but they are there lurking should Horus feel the urge to bestow some coins on his acolytes.If you don’t mind a little unoriginality, players will find an entertaining slot with Dawn of Egypt. It ticks all the right boxes, and there is nothing glaring with it in the slightest. Of course, five minutes after playing it can blur into obscurity along with a score of other Ancient Egypt slots. But while its reels are spinning, Dawn of Egypt is more than capable of doling out gratifying gaming.

Title: Jelly Slice
review: Jelly Slice: Slot OverviewDepending on which side of the Atlantic you reside on, the word 'jelly' can have different meanings. Broadly speaking, on the American side, jelly is close to the British equivalent of jam, while on the other side of the pond, jelly is usually the jiggly gelatinous substance otherwise referred to as Jello. It's this jiggly stuff which wiggles about in software provider Hacksaw Gaming's slot Jelly Slice, a relatively simple slot that dials up the cuteness factor while easing back the complexity.In fact, the cuteness quotient has been cranked so high for this one it veers dangerously close to almost too sweet for certain tastes. However, some people can't get enough sweetness in their lives, and those appetites might be a better fit for Jelly Slice. To the right-hand side of the screen, we've got a flowing pink-haired, almost anime-style female character, clipboard in hand, while adorable little jelly people land on the reels in a pink and cyan-heavy game world. If your teeth or eyes aren't throbbing in pain yet, that's a positive signal to keep the investigation going.Jelly Slice slot - base gameNext on the list, or clipboard as the case may be, is picking a stake, and the options go as low as 10 cents or as high as $/€100 per paid spin. When pressing the spin button, symbols drop out of shoots onto a 5-reel, 4-row active gaming area where there can be anywhere from 1,024 to 1,048,576 ways to win. When symbols start getting sliced, that's when the ways to win increase. When regular betting, Jelly Slice's volatility is medium, and the default RTP is 96.24%.The tumble mechanic removes winning symbols from the reels after they have paid, then drops symbols to fill the vacated spaces. Tumbles keep triggering as long as new wins keep appearing after the drop. Winning combinations start from the leftmost reel, and matching symbols must land on adjacent reels. The low pays are jelly-ish 10 to A symbols, while the highs are 5 jelly creatures in various colours. Hitting a 5 OAK royal win pays 1 times the bet for all of them, rising to 2-10 times the bet for a 5 OAK high pay win. Rainbow star wilds substitute for any regular pay symbols from any reel. A 5 wild symbol hit pays 20 times the stake.Jelly Slice: Slot FeaturesJelly Slice slot - free spinsSlice by name slice by nature, as Jelly Slice has a Slice Mechanic that chops symbols into bits, as well as tumbles, a Razor-Sharp bonus round, and feature buys.Slicer MechanicDuring the game, it is possible to activate 1 Slicer per reel before the drop starts. The Slicer slices all symbols passing through it into 2, 3, or 4 pieces, depending on the value displayed on the Slicer. Each sliced part counts as one symbol for any potential wins. Slicers persist through tumbles, and any symbol dropping through a Slicer due to a tumble also gets sliced.Razor-Sharp BonusLanding 5 to 20 FS scatter symbols in the base game activates the Razor-Sharp bonus round. Each FS symbol that lands awards 1 free spin for the bonus. During the bound round, there is an increased chance of activating Slicers. The number of FS symbols in view translates to the number of free spins awarded after the scatters have or have not been sliced. For example, 1, 2, 3, or 4 FS symbols in view awards +1, +2, +3, or +4 extra free spins, respectively.Bonus BuyJelly Slice's feature buy section comes with these choices:BonusHunt FeatureSpins - 3x the bet for a spin that is 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game. Highly volatile, RTP 96.39%.Slicer FeatureSpins - 20x the bet for a spin, which guarantees at least 1 Slicer. Very highly volatile, RTP 96.33%.Razor-Sharp Bonus - 100x the bet. Highly volatile, RTP 96.37%.Jelly Slice slot - free spinsJelly Slice: Slot VerdictJelly Slice has an interesting feature, but it is packaged within a slot that doesn't punch as forcefully as it might have. Some people may argue otherwise, fair enough, and if sweet, adorable, faux anime environments are the absolute bee's knees, then Jelly Slice could be just the thing. Jelly Slice felt light for a Hacksaw Gaming slot and not in the same charming way as, say, a Canny the Can game. It seemed closer in spirit to anomalies like Bouncy Bombs or Vending Machine. As when reviewing those two, Jelly Slice didn't create the impression it was going to be one of Hacksaw Gaming's top performers, but there are points of interest.One is the Slicer feature. It combines perfectly with cascading wins since if a winning symbol or symbols are removed from beneath a Slicer, any symbol tumbling through the Slicer will be sliced in turn. This system has the makings of sweet cascade runs, potentially, not to mention a monstrous number of possible ways to win, provided a bunch of symbols on the grid cut through the Slicer. As a flow-on effect, winning potential of 10,000x the bet is a sizable shake of icing on top and is achievable in all game modes.To wrap up, Hacksaw Gaming has bravely taken a break from the multiplier reel effect to experiment with alternative ways of entertaining gamblers, which is appreciated. The resulting feature has promise, and as is often the studio's way, if the team tinkers with it in future releases, this wouldn't be a bad thing.

Title: The Bowery Boys
review: The Bowery Boys: Slot OverviewDeveloper Hacksaw Gaming rewinds the clock to the 19th century and heads to one of the most infamous parts of New York City, Hell's Kitchen, in an online slot titled The Bowery Boys. The Bowery Boys were one of New York's earliest gangs, noted for their anti-immigrant, anti-Catholic leanings, and based in the Bowery neighbourhood. They probably weren't the sort of chaps a respectable person would want to associate with, but which make interesting characters in popular culture from movies, books, to online slots.In The Bowery Boys, Hacksaw Gaming has taken a graphic novel approach, dropping the usual cutesy angle for something more cinematographic. It's nothing like the paper mache, fruit 'n veg, cute form their games often take, making The Bowery Boys closer in look to Wanted Dead or a Wild. It's also close in spirit too, as both games delve into a grittier side of life. Played on a 6x5 sized game panel, players find themselves in a dimly lit part of town, possessing a strong Watchmen type vibe. It's all moody skies, yellow moon, cobblestones, with a hint of violence about to explode at any moment. This being Hacksaw Gaming, the action on the reels can pop and bubble just as violently.From a mathematical perspective, The Bowery Boys is a highly volatile game, available in a number of RTP models. The most generous has a value of 96.41% and can be quickly checked by opening up the paytable information. Available on tablet, mobile, or desktop devices, armchair gangsters can load up stakes from 10 p/c to as high as $/€100 per spin.One of The Bowery Boys surprise moments was finding out it does not use cluster pays, which is a Hacksaw Gaming speciality. Instead, makes use of a so-called All-scatter wins system similar to the one used in Joker Bombs and Pragmatic's Sweet Bonanza. Here, all symbols in the game pay like scatters, so as long as at least 8 matching symbols are in view, they create a win. The paytable starts off with 10-A card royals, worth 0.1 to 20 times your bet for landing 8-15+ identical symbols. This increases to 1-100x for landing 8-15+ of the premium boys, fighting men, guns, couples, or lady tiles. Interestingly, there is a wild symbol, landing in the form of a powder keg to substitute any regular pay symbol.The Bowery Boys: Slot FeaturesOne thing The Bowery Boys is not short of is features. Extras to cover here include cascades, Strongboxes, Blasting Bomb Multipliers, and three bonus games.CascadesWhen winning symbols hit, they are removed from the grid, and the gaps are filled by new symbols dropping down from above. This may lead to another win, and cascades continue until no new win appears. Prize money is collected and displayed above the reels as the pending amount. When cascades end, the total pending win amount is awarded and reset to 0.StrongboxesIf a Strongbox symbol lands at the same time as a key symbol, it is opened, and its contents awarded. The three Strongbox types available are small, medium, and large, each awarding a prize worth 2x-5x, 10x-25x, or 50x-250x the bet, respectively. These prizes are added to the total pending win amount above the reels.Blasting Bomb MultipliersThese are bombs that carry values of x2 to x100 and are applied to the current pending win amount. If more than one bomb lands, the values are added together before being applied. Multipliers will only activate if there is a pending win amount currently displayed.Bonus GamesLanding 1, 2, or 3 bonus symbols in the base game awards the Strongbox Storage, Daisy's Dynamite, or Bowery Savings Bank bonus games, respectively:Strongbox Storage comes with 10 free spins. Here, you can store up to 5 Strongboxes in a storage space if they land without a key. When a key does land, it opens any Strongbox on the reels and any in the storage. Each bonus symbol landing in view awards an additional free spin.Daisy's Dynamite awards 10 free spins where Dynamite Multipliers and Detonator symbols come into play. Dynamite Multipliers have values of x2 to x100 and are stored in a Dynamite Box until a Detonator lands. The Detonator triggers all stored Dynamite Multipliers, which are applied to the pending win for the current round.In Bowery Savings Bank, which also comes with 10 free spins, for every win, the same amount is stored in a separate Vault. Keep in mind the original win is always paid. Landing Dice symbols multiplies the value in the Vault by x2-x12. If a Police Officer Badge hits, the police will have to be paid off with 10-50% removed from the current Vault value. When a dollar sign symbol hits, the money in the Vault is won.Bonus BuyIf available, players can buy their way to the Strongbox Storage, Daisy's Dynamite, or Bowery Savings Bank features for 80x, 200x, or 300x their total stake.The Bowery Boys: Slot VerdictIt sometimes feels like Hacksaw Gaming has a real Jekyll & Hyde thing going on. One minute they're producing games full of things like personified food; the other minute, the team's getting about as bleak as it gets in an online slot. Obviously, The Bowery Boys leans towards the latter side of the spectrum. The good news is Hacksaw is as adept at creating gritty games as it is at exploring the adorable side of life. One of their major talents is crafting insanely playable slots, of which The Bowery Boys is another excellent example.This time around, they might not have been as completely original as they usually are, as The Bowery Boys' gameplay has a strong Sweet Bonanza hangover. Scatter win systems aren't super common, though, so it makes a nice change from clusters and can definitely go mental with a solid multiplier onboard. One thing different is the inclusion of a wild symbol which most developers have shied away from when using the scatter pays system, so it's worth a look if you're curious to see how it pans out.Where The Bowery Boys also breaks away from a game like Sweet Bonanza isn't just the inclusion of a wild but is in its set of three bonus games. Each one of them is typical Hacksaw Gaming too. Meaning they're capable of epic teasing when the game is running against you. For example, not getting the Detonator when you've got a few Dynamite Multipliers stored, not getting the key to unlock Strongboxes, or watching your profits evaporate to paying off the cops, oof. Hacksaw games are well equipped to reward, too, though, and if you find yourself on the positive side of The Bowery Boys' volatility, you can win up to 10,000x the bet.Often, Hacksaw builds a game around one or two clever features that get expanded upon in free spins. In The Bowery Boys, players benefit from several compelling features, a trio of tantalisingly good bonus rounds, and a rich world to enjoy them in, or not; these games can be hugely volatile after all.

Title: Africa X UP
review: Africa X UP: Slot OverviewMicrogaming partner Alchemy Gaming transports players to the warm African continent, once again, for an exotically themed slot titled Africa X UP. If you're a relatively young studio, taking on a generic topic runs the risk of being overlooked unless you can do something special with it. To that end, Africa X UP uses a scatter collection system to build win multipliers which then get unleashed when free spins are triggered. Taking a page out of White Rabbit's playbook, players can buy free spins at a reduced cost if they have already collected a few scatters.At first glance, you'd be forgiven for thinking Alchemy Gaming has gone down the 9 Masks of Fire imitation route, with the collection meter and all the cultural touches. But, at closer inspection, the meter actually awards multipliers rather than cash prizes. Alchemy has also delved into the African imagery in more depth, so players get a rich view of a dusty plain, all tussock grass, acacia trees, and distant mountains. A Lion King-like soundtrack completes the scene as players spin a 5-reel, 3-row game grid using 243 ways to win.Highly volatile and playable on any device, Africa X UP offers a range of stakes starting at 30 p/c on the lower end, going up to $/€37.50 per spin. Wins hit when at least three matching symbols land left to right from reel number one. There are 10 pay symbols to work with - five are 10-A card icons; the rest are buffalo, rhinos, elephants, a warrioress and a warrior. Landing a winning combination of five symbols in length is worth a payout of 3.33 to 4.67 times the stake. Moreover, wild symbols appear anywhere and expand to cover all positions on their reel whenever the land. They substitute any pay symbols to complete wins and are worth payouts up to 50 times the bet for five of a kind.Africa X UP: Slot FeaturesAfrica X UP - free spinsThe goal of Africa X UP is to collect X UP scatter symbols to increase a win multiplier which is available when free spins are triggered. X UP symbols land on any reel, and when 2 are in view, they are collected on a multiplier trail located to the left of the reels. The more you collect, the bigger the multiplier becomes, starting at x2, going through x3, x4, x5, x7, x10, x15, and finally x25. Multipliers are stored at each bet level, so changing the stake starts the trail again. If you move back to previous stake levels, you continue from where the trail left off.If three X UP symbols land, then 8 free spins are awarded, and whatever multiplier is active on the trail is applied to all wins during the round. In free spins, landing 2 scatters awards +2 additional free spins and helps increase the free spins multiplier.Africa X UP is a game that may reward patience, yet players not in the mood for some base game collecting can buy the bonus game instead. There are several options here though all award 8 free spins. What changes is you can start them with an x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x7, x10, x15, or x25 multiplier for 18.67, 26.67, 38.67, 50.33, 61.67, 86.33, 120, 181, 300 times the base stake. Or, you can pay 80 times the stake for a random starting multiplier of x2 to x25. If you've already collected a few X UP symbols, then the cost of buying the feature decreases.Africa X UP: Slot VerdictUp until now, we've been used to seeing mainly jackpot style slots like Goldaur Guardians or Wheel of Wishes from Alchemy Gaming. For a young studio forging an identity, the encouraging thing about Africa X UP is that while the team has selected a common theme, the game is relatively imaginative. There's an interesting Wakanda thing going on, coupled with a quasi-spiritual representation of Africa's big animals. It might have been cool if the studio had explored the mystical side even further, but as it is, Africa X UP has several individual touches to help it stand out from the crowded African slot genre.The gameplay is as erratic as a high potential, highly volatile slot can be. Africa X UP dangles a pretty big carrot in the form of an x25 win multiplier but getting there isn't a straight-line process. Instead, prepare to dip 'n dive, being rewarded or punished along the way. If patience is required to get to the best bits, you want to know there will be a payoff for waiting around. Fortunately, there is, and Africa X UP has winning potential of up to 30,000 times the stake. No doubt it will help if you've got the biggest multiplier on board, though lesser multipliers can be pretty effective as well. It's not a matter of just hitting the spin button and sitting back until you've got the x25 locked in, though. There is a good chance you'll trigger free spins long before that happens, and you'll have to make do with something less potent.To give you an idea, it took around 500 spins to trigger the first bonus game, and by then, an x5 multiplier had been achieved. That put into perspective the chance of triggering free spins with the x25 multiplier, and the realisation made buying the bonus instead real tempting. Especially so when a few X UP symbols have already been collected to drop the price.To sum up, Africa X UP is a nicely designed game from Alchemy Gaming with several interesting elements. It's arguably their best looking slot to date, showcases some individual handling of a commonplace theme, provides challenging gaming, and has a big ol' cherry of a max win on top.

Title: Dragon Chase
review: Dragon Chase (Quickspin): ReviewNo other provider has made such a radical change to its core DNA as Quickspin, and though few have ever questioned the company's creative talent, the paytables, on the other hand, have historically been rather disappointing. This changed quite drastically after the release of Dwarfs Gone Wild, a slot that was to be Quickspin's "flagship" title but instead quickly fell into oblivion. With a multitude of features and lots of eye-candy, it made big promises but ultimately failed to deliver. In a time where extreme volatility and massive payouts is the trend, Dwarfs made little (no pun intended) sense.In the wake of Dwarfs, Quickspin decided it was time to grow up, and a few hard-hitting, highly volatile beasts down the road, the company had managed to work its way up to become relevant again by today's standards. While monsterous 5000x+ Quickspin wins still appear to be relatively rare (possibly because they're not played as much as other providers or because the win frequency is lower), the change has been a welcomed one, offering players a broader variety in terms of volatility. With its new Asian-themed Dragon Chase slot, Quckspin takes another important step forward as it marks the release of the studios first jackpot game. Playable from 20 cents to 100€ per spin across all devices, this 5-reel, 3-row, 20-payline slot comes with a Wildfire feature where symbols move downwards with each spin. There's also a Free Spins Bonus where you'll benefit from extra Wildfire symbols as well as a Dragon Pearl Respin feature that can lead to potentially life-changing wins should you trigger the progressive jackpot.Set in the heavenly realms of the dragons, Dragon Chase is designed with a warm colour palette almost entirely made out of red and gold. With fireflies swirling in the background and a fierce dragon resting on the reels, symbols include A to 10 lower value royals as well as more lucrative gold rings, Chinese ingots, frog and dragon statues - the latter being the most rewarding giving you 50 times your stake for a full payline. Of the same value as the dragon statue is the flaming ball which serves as a wild, substituting for all symbols except the scatter.Dragon Chase (Quickspin): FeatureTriggering randomly in the base game, when a Wildfire symbol lands on the reels, it remains in place and move down 1 position each spin until falling out of view. Up to 5 of these can land in one spin and up to 10 Wildfire symbols can appear on the reels together.Dragon Chase also comes with a Free Spins feature which activates when 3 scatter symbols appear on the 3 middle reels. Starting with 10 spins, you can re-trigger the feature with 3 extra spins if you land 2 scatter symbols on reels 2 and 4. The bonus is not too different from the base game, but you'll benefit from extra Wildfire symbols to increase the winning potential. At the end of the bonus, any Wildfire symbols present on the reels will be carried through to the base game. There is a chance to land wins of up to 1170 times your stake here.The Dragon Pearl Respin feature is where the big bucks can be won. Activated when 3 jackpot symbols appear in view, you get 3 spins played on a grid with 15 sparately spinning positions. Whenever a Dragon Pearl symbol hit the reels, it sticks in place while the number of spins resets to 3. Title: Bust the Bank

Title: Temple Frenzy Lightning Chase

Title: Twisted Lab RotoGrid

Title: 8 Golden Dragon Challenge

Likely helped along if you can it make all the way to the Envelope Bonus with a decent multiplier, and 8 Golden Dragon Challenge's max win is 8,800x the bet. Not only is this a respectable amount, but Pragmatic Play was also able to squeeze a couple of extra '8s' in there for good measure.It might not look it at first, but 8 Golden Dragon Challenge manages to add something new to the Asian-inspired list of slot choices. Title: Bookie of Odds

The lack of originality, however, makes it a rather pointless release, unless you're a great horse racing enthusiast that also happens to be into online slots.For players who were around when Book of Oz came out, there's really nothing new to explore or discover here. Bookie of Odds only really feels like a hasty re-skin, released with the sole purpose of cashing in on the horse racing hype NetEnt promoted over the past few weeks. How do you rate a clone? Title: Gates of Valhalla

Free spins weren't smooth sailing, though, far from it, and completely wild-free bonus rounds did occur. Needless to say, those didn't accomplish much, and the global win multiplier on its own didn't go very far without a bit of wild assistance. However, up to five wilds appeared simultaneously on-screen, and since the global win multiplier is applied to the total win of all tumbles, results can be quite good. During testing, this meant payouts of 500x+.Norse mythology slots are one of the most numerous genres around, yet Pragmatic Play has designed another one that warrants a look. RTP 96.31%, highly volatile.So Many Toads FeatureSpins - 40x the bet, each spin guarantees 8 Toads and 1 Prosperity Pot symbols land. RTP 96.33%, medium volatile.Toad Bonus - 100x the bet. Title: Aloha! Christmas

Christmas Edition - free spinsWhen looking at features, the demarcation between the two Aloha slots starts to widen. Christmas Edition: Slot VerdictCalling this a Christmas slot might seem like a teensy bit of a stretch. Title: Luchamigos

The 3 possible Hot Amigos features are:Gran Chico – creates a 2x2 sized mega wild.Roco Elastico – creates a wild stack.Muchos Salvajes – creates 4 random wilds.Power Chile SpinsLanding 3 Power Chile symbols on reels 1, 3, and 5 awards 7 free spins. In free spins, Hot Amigo features can be triggered without the need for a Power Chile. Also, landing Hot Amigo wilds progresses the Chile Meter. Reaching the +2 on the Chile Meter awards an additional +2 free spins, up to a maximum of 15 free spins.When reaching fire icons on the Chile Meter, the Hot Spin is triggered. Title: Egyptian Tombs

Title: Arctic Magic
review: Arctic Magic (Microgaming): OverviewMicrogaming titles don't come along all too often these days. Scatters are also worth a fair amount of money as well with 5 returning 500 times the stake before the free spins even start.All wins during the bonus round are subjected to a x3 multiplier. Scatters continue to appear during the round so free spins can be retriggered. Scatters and wilds are so handy that they only need 2 of a kind on a payline to payout a small number of coins. When either land, a nice animation of the aurora borealis plays on the screen too for a touch of winter magic.Arctic Magic (Microgaming): VerdictThere's nothing magical about Arctic Magic. In fact, there's not even the slightest bit of originality to it or any other sort of quality that will make you come back for more. And as it turns out, the game is a reskin of Microgaming's 2019 Christmas contribution Festive Indulgance. Whilst the developers managed to give that game some charm and character, Arctic Magic lacks all of that. The theme feels generic, the symbols sort of melt together into a mess and the gameplay is far too weak to make up for the dull appearance.Arctic Magic is not an entertaining slot and it doesn't take many spins for its average gameplay to show through. Yes wilds and scatters can be worth a stack of coins, but they suffer the same fate that symbols in a game like A Dark Matter did. Namely, 5 wilds or scatters are highly valuable but rare, and payouts for 4 of a kind or less drop significantly. Title: Divine Showdown
review: Divine Showdown (Play’n GO): OverviewFans of mythologically themed slots never have a hard time finding something to play. Most software developers give this genre a crack sooner or later, and the category is bulging with options. The latest company to let their champion loose in this competitive arena is Play'n GO with the ambitious slot Divine Showdown. Most mythology slots focus on one religion or belief system. There is a ton of Thor/Norse god slots, Greek and Roman, and of course, the otherworldly gods of Ancient Egypt. Play'n GO have gone down a slightly different route. Instead of keeping the religions cordoned off, why not combine several of them in one place? What could go wrong?Well, the gods are not exactly known for sharing. They don’t want their supporters wandering off to follow other divinities. So get four of them in a room, and you have a recipe for some titanic struggles. Play'n GO have cleverly incorporated this competitive spirit into Divine Showdown where the four different gods literally battle during special features. Us mere mortals want this to happen because when we choose the winning deity, the rewards are there for the victor.Divine Showdown is a good looking game, although, it could be prettier and we will come back to that later. Its 5-reel, 3-row, 20-payline grid sits in front of a mash-up of swords, arenas, temples, and cliffs. It certainly looks like the kind of place gods would duke it out. Below the grid is a bar that scrolls horizontally to allow bets to be placed from 20 p/c up to $/€100 per spin.Click the paytable to view the 9 base game symbols starting with 9 to A royals. These are followed by the Chinese monkey god Wukong, Anubis the Egyptian god of the underworld, Greek Athena and Norse god Thor. Steely-eyed Thor, who bears a striking resemblance to the Hemsworth brothers, tops the base game table at 16 times the stake for five of a kind. The golden wild is worth more at 20 times the stake for a five of a kind combination, and it also substitutes for any other pay symbol. Other key stats include the volatility which Play'n GO list as very high. RTP can fluctuate between 94.5% and 96.51%, or even lower actually, so always be sure to have a look in the paytable.Divine Showdown (Play’n GO): FeaturesFree spins roundSome gods are notoriously fickle, and as such several extra features can trigger on any spin at random. The first is a Multiplier Reel which pops up to award multipliers of up to x10 at any time. The gods themselves can also show up at any time, each with their own special ability. Wukong creates Wild Reels where an entire reel is wild, Anubis turns 1 or 2 symbols into Wilds, Athena Synchronises 3 reels to spin with the same symbols, and Thor turns all god symbols into Thor Symbols. During any one of these features, the Multiplier Reel can also drop as well.With the word 'showdown' in the title, you would expect some fighting to take place. We get this in the bonus round. The quad embossed symbol is the scatter, and 3 are needed to trigger Free Spins. When the bonus round launches, players choose which god they will enter with - considering the individual abilities mentioned above.Before each round or spin, the Battle Reel is spun. If it lands on 'Spin', then the reels spin once as normal. If it lands on a god symbol, then a fight is initiated between the player’s champion and that god. During battles, Power Symbols cascade on the screen instead of spinning reels. Whichever god has the highest amount of Power Symbols is the winner. If this is the enemy, then the player loses a life. There is no set number of free spins to the bonus round. Instead, it continues indefinitely until the player loses all three lives at which point the action returns to the base game again.Divine Showdown (Play’n GO): VerdictWhen a developer goes this large with a theme, the rest of the game really needs to step up. In some ways, Play'n GO have achieved this symbiosis, in others ways Divine Showdown falls a little short. Some criticism first. The graphics, while being above average, don’t quite do enough to convey the awesome coming together of four mighty gods. The symbols have a Street Fighter 2 vibe to them that are a little flat. Don’t get us wrong, the graphics overall are good, and convey action, but an injection of more flair and life would not have been missed.The positive news is that the theme, on the whole, works well. The idea of bringing a diverse range of gods together, rather than focusing on one pantheon is an intriguing one. Developers often hype battle sequences in slots, but we aren’t playing full-blown video games here, so they are usually point and click at best. Despite that natural limitation, the battles here make sense and tie the features with the theme together well.Over all though, while being an entertaining game, Divine Showdown feels like a slightly missed opportunity. You don’t get the impression that Play'n GO have completely poured their heart and soul into it. A slot with a theme this epic could have been massive, instead, it has settled for above-average status. Perhaps we are being too hard on it. There is plenty to enjoy here, especially for fans of the theme who will be able to loose themselves in some intense gaming sessions. The high volatility will sort out the truly dedicated from the long line of wannabes, and there is up to 5,000 times the stake on offer if the gods find you worthy.

Title: Fire Forge

Title: Rome Supermatch
review: Rome Supermatch: Slot OverviewIn the online slot world, at least two paths exist for up-and-coming game designers – follow the herd or kick the hornet's nest by doing something no one else has ever seen before. For this one, the matching symbols become sticky, and all other symbols respin for the chance of improving the win.Buy BonusIf present, the Bonus Store has two buy choices – Second Chance and Always Match. The Second Chance costs 20x the bet, guaranteeing the Second Chance Bonus will activate, while the Always Match guarantees at least three matching symbols on the first row – costing 5x the bet. Only one can be bought at a time.Rome Supermatch slot - Mega Respin feature triggeredRome Supermatch: Slot VerdictNo doubt, a fair whack of creative juices flowed into the making of Rome Supermatch. There's just nothing really else like it on the market, so kudos to Nailed It! Games for boldly trying something new rather than playing it safe by regurgitating proven crowd pleasers. Of course, living dangerously on the edge of the creative envelope means some may not quite grasp what you are getting at, therefore risking commercial success. On the other hand, who knows? You might have a hit on your hands by producing something players never knew they wanted. Who would have predicted how thoroughly mobile devices and apps would have taken over our lives before just about everyone seems to have one in their pocket? Cast your mind back. What did we use to do on the train to work, pass the time in a queue, or when using the facilities? Read magazines, daydream?Bringing a more serious focus back to Rome Supermatch, there is a good chance its unique brand of entertainment will appeal to certain players out in the iGaming realm. Title: Wild Corral
review: Wild Corral: OverviewUK based studio and SG Digital partner Core Gaming cranks out slots on a regular basis in partnership with SG Digital, but this is the first in their range to go fully Wild West. At the end of the round, any multiplier wilds left on the reels are added together and applied to the total stake.Wild Corral: VerdictWild Corral is a game where the features seem promising, but fail to hit the mark a lot of the time. On the upside, the west has been presented well, and Wild Corral isn't a game you have to wait an age for free spins to hit like in Core Gaming's now cancelled Viking Hoard slot. Beginners luck of course, but the feature appeared at a fairly constant rate throughout testing. It seems Core Gaming has made some positive adjustments to the math model after our criticism, making it more player-friendly.The team could have improved Wild Corral if they had tweaked other aspects too. The sticky(ish) wilds In the Wild Zone is quite a good idea, but could have been better. For one, if they stayed sticky for the duration of free spins, the game might have been devastating. Though accusations of copying the Dead and Alive series probably would have arisen. As it is, wilds can build up pretty impressive multipliers, x12+ wasn't uncommon, and do multiply each other. Then, once wilds are used, they are gone with the wind and the bonus feels pretty much over and done.All up, Wild Corral has its moments, and there are some interesting aspects for sure even if they're tugging on a tight leash. With some fine-tuning, maybe more win ways to take advantage of the sticky wilds, it could have been more effective though.

Title: Pineapple Pop
