Hit the little gear button on the top right to open up the paytable which is light on details - not because Inspired is economising on content, but because there isn’t a whole lot you need to know.First up are the symbols - oranges, plums, watermelons, grapes, blackberries, and strawberries make up the lower end of the table. Then there are blue, red, and white lucky sevens which are worth 100 times the stake for five of a kind. The other pay symbols are white cherries which come with a credit amount on them. During the base game, they form winning combinations, but the credit amount comes into play during the bonus game. The highest paying symbol is the Logo which pays out 200 times the stake for five across a full payline. All five of a kinds offer quite good value; the issue is that even four of a kind is very rare, even of the lowly fruit. RTP is above average on 96.5%, and the official volatility rating is low (according to SG Digital). Though with the mega runs of dead spins interspersed with the odd poor win the volatility feels a lot higher than that. The math model must be an absolute beast.Mega Cherry (Inspired): FeaturesDon’t come to Mega Cherry if you are looking for a feature-heavy slot. The two extras included here are unlikely to satisfy that requirement. Either way, the main event is the Cash Collector Bonus - 6 white cherry symbols need to land in conjunction with the Bonus symbol to trigger the Cash Collector Bonus and 5 free spins. The cherry symbols used to launch the feature are locked on the reels while every other position is spun. The only symbols that can land are more cherry symbols, blank spaces, or golden coins. Any new cherry symbols are locked in place for the remainder of the feature. If a golden coin lands, it turns the cherry symbols red and gold. This means that at the end of the free spins, their credit values are added together and paid out along with any win line combinations.Running out of cash? The Spin Chance feature is your second chance of a comeback. It's triggered automatically if your balance is reduced below the current stake, yet is still greater than zero. It essentially offers you an opportunity to wager the remaining balance in an attempt at winning an additional spin at the current stake.Mega Cherry (Inspired): VerdictRumour has it that Zen monks play this game to test their patience. All jokes aside, Mega Cherry is one tough slot that puts in no effort to make friends. It is possible to come out positive with Mega Cherry, but you will need to wade through an unbelievable amount of dead spins to get there. Strike this game on an off day, and you’ll have the pleasure of watching your account evaporate slowly but steadily before your very eyes. If the action was entertaining, you could just shrug your shoulders and write that off as a bad day and better luck next time. The sad reality is that you are just watching fruit spin endlessly while this thing eats away at your bankroll.So who is Mega Cherry’s target audience? Diehard fruit fans, ex-kamikaze pilots, people who vote tax cuts for billionaires? Seriously, this thing can be tough. Even the soundtrack, which was so soothing in the beginning starts to drive you up the wall and force the mute button. Then it’s just you, some dead spinning symbols, and the odd bleep when reels stop spinning. Oh, and your sanity eking out of your physical form until all that’s left is a husk repeatedly hitting spin in the hopes of getting somewhere, anywhere. Low volatile games should be a lot more gentle than this. If you can stick it out and land the Cash Collector Bonus, you might get lucky and win your money back. The best you can hope for is a 12 or so cherry symbols during the bonus round. A 50 credit showed up once so technically 12 of those and a golden coin could net you 600 times the stake.It’s just not enough to compensate for the racked nerves. Players who are hanging out for fruit flavoured slot would be better off spinning something like Joker Troupe, or sticking to their old favourites. Even if Cherry Mega was less stingy with the wins, its repetitive gameplay and limited features quickly get boring. Next.

Title: Primal Megaways
review: Primal Megaways IntroductionThere's no doubt about the fact that Megaways has helped bring new life into Blueprint Gaming, we're sure most would agree. With that said, the reverse is true as well. Blueprint Gaming, while having had the tendency to focus heavily on the entertainment aspect of slots, often is achieved with the help of its much appreciate random features, many of the pre-Megaways era games have remained somewhat old-fashioned due to their limited paylines. This has changed, and the combination of the intriguing features in combination with Megaways has worked out exceptionally well for the provider.Without context, the premise of Primal Megaways might not stop you in your tracks. It's a Blueprint slot at heart with the familiar setup presented against a prehistoric backdrop along with a soundtrack that reacts to the action generated by the spinning of the reels. Undeniably, Primal MegaWays does bear a resemblance to the likes of Buffalo Rising and other Blueprint Megaways slots, but what we get to experience here is a new twist to the Megaways mechanics. What is true is that Blueprint does not waste time reinventing the wheel here.Primal Megaways, just like most other slots of the MegaWays family, is a 6-reeler with win ways that can span up to a staggering 46,656 lines. Now, wait a minute, is what seasoned players might be thinking, there are 70,993 win ways missing here. We've come to know MegaWays slots as the 117k win ways beasts that they are, but what Primal lacks in paylines, it makes up for in retriggers as you will see. Make no mistake; this is a high variance fire-breathing dragon irrespective of the cartoonish characteristics of the slot.Set in the Paleolithic ice age, the game boasts impressive visuals far above the current standards of the industry. With crisp graphics and warm colours, it's undoubtedly an attractive creation with the capability to enthrall and captivate players. In terms of features, there's some new and old to be found. The Mystery symbols, which we know from previous releases, have been included here as well. A new addition, on the other hand, is the Free Spin Guarantee feature which means no one will leave the bonus empty-handed. Although the main game is packed with potential, central to the game is the free spin feature with its multiplier symbols and unlimited retriggers.Primal Megaways Symbols & PaytableOn the reels you will find 10 to A royal values plus a quintet of prehistoric animals, out of which the Mammoth is the top paying symbol giving you 50 times the stake for 6 across a payline. As mentioned before, you can expect to see the Mystery symbol feature come into play every now and then. When dropping on the reels, these fiery symbols will reveal a random symbol bar the multiplier and scatter symbols.Primal Megaways Free SpinsFree spins feature with multipliersTo trigger the bonus, players have to land 3 or more scatter symbols anywhere on the reels. Free spins are awarded accordingly:3 Scatter Symbols in view awards 10 Free Spins with wild multipliers of x2 and x3.4 Scatter Symbols in view awards 15 Free Spins with wild multipliers of x2, x3 or x4.5 Scatter Symbols in view awards 20 Free Spins with wild multipliers of x2, x3, x4 or x5.6 Scatter Symbols in view awards 30 Free Spins with wild multipliers of x2, x3, x4, x5 or x6.During the bonus, 2 or more additional scatter symbols will award extra free spins and there is no limit to how many times it can retrigger, although it should be noted that the outcome, just as with most slots, has likely been decided before the bonus is actually played out.Although the vast amount of win ways by itself enables the opportunity to land big wins, players rely heavily on the wild multipliers for the truly insane payouts. The wild multiplier can appear in reels 2 to 6 and multiply by each other (for example 2 x 2 x 2 = x8). In other words, there's massive potential here, something we got to experience first hand as we managed to land a x120 multiplier during our test round!Whatismore, a free spin win guarantee will make sure you won't leave empty-handed. Should your bonus end with less than 10 times the total bet, the free spins feature will automatically retrigger and off you go again.Primal Megaways ConclusionThe fact that Primal Megaways stands up so well mechanically against more recent games is undoubtedly the most pleasant surprise of the package, and we're happy to sacrifice the thousands of Megaways here for what we receive in return in the bonus game. In our humble opinion, it's one of the best Megaways-franchise slots produced as of late, although proceed with caution as the volatility is extremely high, even more so than what you may be used to.Primal Megaways undoubtedly holds its own, and we have to say it's an incredibly refreshing take on the Megaways concept that further strengthens the position of the franchise. Granted, we can't wait to see all the insane big win videos and hear the primal screams that this slot surely will produce.

Title: Fortunes of Sparta
review: Fortunes of Sparta: OverviewThis is Sparta! So goes the immortal line from the epic loincloth movie 300 which retold the Spartans’ most famous battle. And so goes the war cry from the anonymous hoplite that kicks off Blueprint Gaming's slot Fortunes of Sparta. It's a far cry from the contemporary handling of their recent Megaways extravaganzas. Instead, Fortunes of Sparta follows in the tradition of Napoleon and Revolution: Patriots Fortune by taking a classic approach to gaming, with a historical theme.The first slot that sprang to mind oddly, was swords and sandals slot Plataea from WMS, though with a crisper, more modern look. There isn't a whole lot happening visually in Fortunes of Sparta, with no background image other than a stone wall, but the graphics we do get are high quality.Each ab and striation has been brought to life through the on-screen warriors, as has their accoutrement. The sounds are pretty epic too and give the game some additional oomph. Along with the slashing, slamming effects is a choral piece floating away, adding depth to the proceedings.Playable across all devices from 25 p/c per spin or as high as $/€125, the gaming area is set between two Greek columns and is made up of 5 reels, 3 rows, crossed by 20 paylines. Players look to land combinations of three or more matching symbols on a payline from the first reel onwards to receive a reward.Prying open the paytable reveals the symbols we get to defend Sparta with which are 7 regular pay symbols that are all newly crafted for the game. On the low side are jugs, swords and shields to start. These are backed up by three different warrior poses, and one white-clad queen figure.The warrior holding the stabbing spear is the most valuable from the regular symbols, worth 20 times the stake for a line of five. The wild is the one you want, though. As well as being able to substitute for any symbol bar the scatter, 5 of these profitable symbols are worth an insane 4,000 times the stake.Another generous figure is Fortune of Sparta's RTP, which at 97.04% is comfortably on the positive side of average. The game has a rather high volatility, and with the way features work, sessions can very much be all or nothing. Testing went through some disheartening patches populated by waves of dead to barely living spins. Then all of a sudden something big would hit, and all would seem right with the world.Fortunes of Sparta: FeaturesFortunes of Sparta - free spinsFeatures are somewhat, well, Spartan since there aren't too much to get to grips with. Like the Spartans though, they get pretty wild when wound up. It all revolves around the Spartan Streak feature, which comes into play when the Spartan Streak symbol appears on the middle reel and forms a win with any regular symbol in the base game.When triggered, it expands and transforms into a sticky stacked wild. Moreover, the winning symbols are locked in place while the remaining reels respin - any new matching winning symbols that turn up are held in place. Reels continue to respin until no new winning symbols land or the reels are stacked.Keep an eye out for the flaming Omega scatter - when 3 of these appear, they trigger the Spartan Spins and become locked in place while the other positions are respun. Reels continue to spin in this manner while new scatters land until no new ones appear or the grid is covered. The resulting 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8-9, or 10+ scatters award 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 50, or up to 100 Spartan Spins respectively.On top of the sheer number possible, Spartan Spins come with a couple of tricks concealed up their sleeve making them highly desirable. The first is the middle reel which is turned into the Spartan Streak wild helping increase the hit rate whilst also triggering the Spartan Streaks on every winning spin.Fortunes of Sparta: VerdictAs it turns out, this game is a re-release of an older title called Legend of Sparta, and for some good old fashioned gaming, Fortunes of Sparta isn't too bad at all. The base game has little more than regular spins going on, but the bonus game can be something else. When it works out, it is definitely worth sitting through all of those drab 'death by a thousand cuts' that occur during the main game. What also helps are the sweet visuals and the excellent sound effects which make waiting around for the bonus game easier to battle through then they might have been.As with a lot of Blueprint games, the stated maximum win from a single game is $250,000 or 10,000 times the stake, whichever comes first. Full grids of the premium symbol are worth 1,000 times the stake and hitting the high number of free spins can be lucrative indeed. The game is quite volatile though, so no guarantees as usual. Some bonus games went well, others were like running into a Spartan shield wall and getting a dory thrust to the face. Such are the whims of fortune.Yes, the theme's been done before, as have the features to certain degrees, but the overall product is quite satisfying. For simple gaming with above average looks, generous RTP, and an excellent bonus game, Fortunes of Sparta could be a good fit. In a sense, Fortunes of Sparta is the Napoleon sibling that Revolution: Patriots Fortune failed to be.

Title: Atlantean GigaRise
review: Atlantean GigaRise: Slot OverviewAfter the tour de force that was Hades Gigablox, there was some excitement when Atlantean GigaRise landed on the desk. Unfortunately, apart from the 'Giga' in the title, the two games have nothing in common. Atlantean GigaRise doesn’t even use developer Yggdrasil Gaming’s unpredictable Gigablox feature. Instead, it’s a gentle dip beneath the waves to the underwater kingdom of Atlantis, where jackpots, rising reels, and free spins reside.If you’ve spent more than five minutes playing slots, it’s likely Atlantis has been crossed off your bucket list already. The mythical city that sunk to the bottom of the sea is a hugely popular game location. In Atlantean GigaRise it plays host to a 5-reel grid that looks a little lopsided at first. Each reel holds 3 to 8 rows which grow in height, changing the win ways in the process when the right symbols land. To either side of the reels, marble columns support a structure holding 5 amphorae which crack open to reveal prizes when reels grow to reach them.More Greco-Roman structures appear in the background as fish lazily swim between them and weeds ruffle gently in the current. Speaking of gentle, it feels like the soundtrack’s main job is to send players off into a peaceful slumber. The problem is that it isn’t a counterbalance to some rip-roaring action. Quite the opposite, and a lot of the time it’s a dual battle between trying to score big, and stopping yourself from nodding off.Atlantean GigaRise’ jackpot hunt is possible on any device, offering bets from 20 p/c to $/€40 per spin. To keep the jackpots satiated, 3.8% of each bet is siphoned off to feed the pot. A medium volatile math model awaits intrepid explorers, and quite a few features accompany it. Don’t get your hopes of winning too much outside of the jackpot though. Atlantean GigaRise isn’t one of Yggdrasil’s high performers. It’s more of a middle ground option more concerned with experimenting with new reel forms than showering lucky players in riches. Jackpots aren’t bad, nor is the RTP value, generating a figure of 96%.As reels rise, so do the number of win ways, climaxing at 32,768 when each has the full 8 positions in play. Wins occur left to right when three or more matching symbols land, regardless of row height. A bunch of cute icons have been used for the pay symbols, starting with 10-A card royals, topped by high pay amphorae, lyres, swords, helmets, and some jewellery. Values are depressed to compensate for rising reels and ways, so when a win consisting of five premiums lands, expect a win worth up to 2 times the stake. The last symbol to cover before deep-diving into the most promising parts is the wild. The wild is a golden column and stands in for any pay symbol type to complete a winning combination.Atlantean GigaRise: Slot FeaturesBe sure to keep an eye on those trident symbols which trigger the Rising Reels feature. When they land, their respective reel is increased by 1 position while also expanding the paylines. Each reel stays raised between spins, and when a trident lands on a fully expanded reel 8 rows in height, the bonus game is awarded. There are 3 prize sets available here – bronze, silver or gold, offering ascending values.The bonus game uses 1 highlighted horizontal payline and every symbol that lands on it awards either free spins sessions of up to 80 spins, cash wins up to 200x, or jackpots. The round starts with 3 lives, deducting 1 when no prize lands on the payline. However, spins are reset when prize symbols do hit. Now, landing a jackpot symbol in the highlighted area awards its corresponding value. These jackpots are progressive, possessing seed values of €40, €200, €600, €1,500, and €15,000 for the Forgotten, Rare, Mythical, Ancient, and Legendary Jackpot respectively.If free spins have been won, they play directly after the bonus game ends. Alternatively, landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters in the base game award 20, 40, or 80 free spins. Rising reels remain in play during free spins, so the bonus game described previously can be triggered as before. Moreover, retriggers are possible when 2, 3, 4, or 5 scatters land to award 5, 20, 40, or 80 additional free spins.Atlantean GigaRise: Slot VerdictThere is a time and place for everything, as they say, so for a lazy dazy jackpot hunt beneath the waves, Atlantean GigaRise might be alright. Don’t expect a high thrills experience when you are there, though. It comes across as a jackpot game better suited to casual gamblers, and a somewhat bloated and over-complicated one too. Lower rollers especially will be able to make more out of the top rewards. As an example, hitting €15k when max betting is only worth 375x the total stake. Of course, jackpots are progressive, so the rewards could theoretically be a lot higher.The whole theme treatment and low energy gameplay reinforce the impression of a game happy coasting in second gear. There is a metaphorical third gear, where non-jackpot wins can reach as high as 4,370x the bet. Not hugely exciting, but if you’re cool with the laid-back environment as a whole, then that amount is probably more than enough of a motivator to paddle around in Atlantean GigaRise’ aquatic world.

Title: Golden Ticket 2
review: Golden Ticket 2: OverviewSequel season continues at Play’n GO as they release a follow up to their 2014 circus themed slot Golden Ticket. The studio has stuck to the core spirit of the game while fine-tuning the looks, features and potential. Actually, when you put it like that, there does seem to be quite a lot of changes. Let's take a ringside seat to go over what's new in Golden Ticket 2.Visually, there is a lot linking the two games. It's certainly not a complete disconnect like Jolly Roger 1 and 2 was. Playable from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, players get the same 5x5 setup along with 20 fixed paylines located in a tent surrounded by clowns, ringmasters and other characters of the big top. One minor cosmetic change is the action predominantly took place outside in the first, this time we've moved under the canvas. The spirit remains the same though fortunately, which was one of the major selling points of the original. Play’n GO absolutely nailed the look and feel of an old-time circus, nicely reviving it for the sequel.As you likely know by now, Play'n GO makes use of flexible RTP which means you can face different RTP-settings depending on wh ere you're playing. The default RTP, however, is set to 96.5%. The math model has definitely been altered, so be prepared to go up against a totally different beast if you've played the original. That one was a medium volatile slot whilst the sequel is as volatile as Play'n GO slots come.In terms of the actual gameplay, it works as follows: on each spin 25 symbols tumble into the grid. Wins are achieved by landing 3 or more matching symbols connecting either horizontally or vertically. Winning combinations are cleared from the grid after they have been paid, and any remaining symbols drop to fill the gaps, potentially creating new wins. With each new drop, the win multiplier is increased by one, resetting to x1 on a new base game spin.The paytable is full of circus icons consisting of 5 low pay, 3 high pay symbols. The low pays include a monocycle, juggling items, a target, knives, and a ringmaster's hat. Hit a line of 5 low pays for rewards of 2 to 4 times the stake. The high pays are three characters from the show - a clown, a blindfolded knife thrower, and a ringmaster. A 5 of a kind combo here rewards 10 times the stake no matter the symbol. Players also get a consolation prize of up to 5x for lines of three or more mixed premiums landing horizontally or vertically.Finally, the golden tent is the wild, substituting for any pay symbol to make a combination. It is also worth a fair amount on its own with 5 in a row worth 50 times the stake. Wilds are created in the middle position when a winning combination of three symbols is removed. If there are only wilds left on the grid, then they are removed.Golden Ticket 2: FeaturesGolden Ticket 2 - free spinsPlay’n GO has given the features a vigorous shakeup and now revolves around multiplier wilds, Win Spins and free spins.To the left of the grid is a 3 segment meter that is filled when premium wins occur. Wins consisting of 3, 4, or 5 symbols fill 1, 2, or 3 segments of the meter respectively. Completely filling the meter triggers the multiplier wilds feature where 1 or 2 multiplier wilds are added randomly to the reels.On the right, one of the three characters is displayed, influencing which wild multiplier it will be. An active clown, knife thrower, or ringmaster, awards the x1, x2, or x3 multiplier wilds respectively. The multiplier wilds feature can only trigger once per game round; then the character changes for the next trigger.Like the original, lurking behind the symbols on the grid is the word BONUS. Clearing the BONUS row triggers free spins which comes with three options. The less free spins, the higher the multiplier and the volatility, so players choose their most suitable option:5 highly volatile free spins with an x3 multiplier wild.7 medium volatile free spins with an x2 multiplier wild.9 low volatile free spins with an x1 multiplier wild.During free spins, filling 3 segments of the meter triggers a Win Spin using a 2x2 version of the multiplier wild. A new grid of symbols appears, and the multiplier wild is randomly placed on the board. The win multiplier is reset between free spins and Win Spins.Filling 5 segments of the expanded meter on a Win Spin retriggers another one – keeping in mind the win multiplier is not reset between consecutive Win Spins. Finally, should you manage to clear the full grid, a bonus prize of 500x the bet is awarded.Golden Ticket 2: VerdictWhether the sequel will appeal to the same fans of the first will be interesting to see. On the one hand, the two games look quite similar, both handling the circus theme in style, creating bags of big top atmosphere. On the other hand, the volatility and potential are much higher, which may suit a more dedicated attitude.For some, the removal of the target shooting bonus game will be a blow. Not that it was highly lucrative, but it was fun, and worked perfectly with the theme. The new bonus games are a lot more sophisticated though, capable of producing more intense moments and larger payouts. Now, Golden Ticket 2 offers wins of up to 5,000 times the stake, or double the first.All up, it's a case of Golden Ticket looks and base game meets Moon Princess with elements of Pimped (Win Spins) tossed in for good measure. The result of this mash-up can be as enjoyable as a day out at the circus. That is, one of those delightful disasters of a show which constantly threatens to slip from a state of barely controlled chaos into total mayhem.

Title: Infectious 5
review: Developer Nolimit City must have had so much fun with the Infectious xWays feature designed for East Coast vs West Coast that it's back for round two. This time, the team has moved away from the fluro, graffiti, hip hop, beat ridden urban areas of downtown 1990s to a world of the not too distant future where only superheroes can thrive in a toxic environment. The studio has tightened its focus on the Infectious xWays feature in Infectious 5 xWays, which is accompanied by a variety of free spin bonus games, and of course, substantial returns.Welcome to a vision of the future where morality, survival, and humanity have blurred under the strain of just getting by in a world turned upside down. A Marvel/DC vibe is injected by superhero character symbols as they land on the 5-reel, 1,024 ways to win game grid. An industrial setting is where Nolimit City has laid the scene made up of cranes, chains, sparks, and blurred towers in the background, hinting at some industrial hive world. Along with that, we get an epic, bombastic soundtrack to enrich the heroic atmosphere.  It's not the riot of living colour East Coast vs West Coast was, but it's a well atmospheric scene and not something Nolimit has really done before.The comic book ethos is reinforced by the use of Harvey Dent's ominous words, 'You either die a hero, or you live long enough to see yourself become the villain'. That's a nicely poetic way of describing the all or nothing nature of Infectious 5 xWays' 'Extremely' volatile math model, rated 10 out of 10 by the maker, so gear up for that. As per usual, the RTP is variable, where the value comes in two forms - 96.02% is the most desirable, though it can be found lower at 94.27%. Other important numbers are a hit rate of 31.43%, while stakes from 20 p/c to $/€50/100 per spin may be selected – on any device.Players score a win in Infectious 5 xWays when three or more identical symbols connect left to right from the first reel. Higher value symbols are the character tiles, named Havoc, Mind Flayer, Torch, Misery, and Toxicity, worth from 1.50 to 4 times your stake for 5 of a kind, followed by 10-A low pays which are worth from 1 to 1.25 times your stake for 5 oak combinations. Three more symbols comprise the paytable, two of which are covered in the next section, leaving the regular wild symbol. This one appears as a chunky yellow 'W' tile that replaces any regular pays to complete a winning combination.Infectious 5 xWays: Slot FeaturesAs mentioned, xWays and Infectious xWays have popped up famously in East Coast vs West Coast, where they play the central role in Infectious 5 xWays. Complimenting these two extras are three free spin bonus games.When xWays symbols hit, they transform into any symbol except wilds or scatters. When they do, they reveal 2 or 3 of the same symbol type, expanding the reel height and increasing the number of win ways. At the most, it is possible to have up to 110,592 ways in action.If an xWays symbol lands simultaneously as a wild symbol, the Infectious xWays feature is triggered. As well as the xWays symbol splitting to reveal more symbols, any other instance of that symbol type on the grid is infected, expanding them in the same way.Landing 3 or 4 scatter symbols triggers the free spins round where you can pick one of two options;Toxic Hazard comes with 9 or 10 infectious spins, where 1 to 5 random wilds are placed on the middle reels for every spin. This means that xWays symbols instantly trigger Infectious xWays every time.Lock n' Load comes with 7 or 8 infectious spins and is the more volatile option. Here all wilds lock in place for the duration of the feature while also awarding +1 free spin when they appear on the reels. Wilds may also be awarded an x2 or x3 multiplier, and landing an xWays symbol means guaranteed Infectious xWays.Should 5 scatter symbols land in the base game, or be collected during the previous two bonus games (by collecting a total of 5 scatter symbols), then Infectious Spins: Mayhem mode is launched.Toxic Hazard Mayhem: comes with 12 infectious spins - all infectious 5 symbols will turn into 1 golden infectious 5 symbol. Any infectious xWays during this mode only reveal the golden infectious 5 symbols.Lock 'n Load Mayhem: comes with 10 infectious spins - all infectious 5 symbols will turn into 1 golden infectious 5 symbol. Any infectious xWays during this mode only reveal the golden infectious 5 symbols.Infectious 5 xWays also offers players a list of bonus buy options. Players can go straight to any of the three bonus games, with price tags ranging from 75 to 555 times the total base bet.Infectious 5 xWays: Slot VerdictFrom a lesser studio, reusing the same feature in another game while the new smell hasn't worn off the previous one yet would feel like a cynical move. Not so with Nolimit City, who somehow blast out a game of the year slot on a monthly basis. Instead of feeling like a rehash, focusing on the one feature has given the studio a chance to push it into new and exciting areas not seen previously. There are already great clips of Infectious xWays popping off solid wins in East Coast vs West Coast. In Infectious 5 xWays, we are sure to see a repeat, and then some.If you thought Infectious xWays were potent before, combining them with locked wilds, or better, locked multiplier wilds are next level. Doing so adds a crazy level of volatility and reward to Lock n' Load spins, even more so to Mayhem Mode. The game doesn't have the fabulously rich theme use of East Coast vs West Coast, which tore you out of reality and plonked you into the best parts of the 1990s, but it was going to be hard to match that. To compensate, Nolimit has ratcheted the winning potential up to 55,555 times the stake, occurring once every 28 million spins, which is relatively frequent compared to many games. Big numbers get thrown around in slots all the time, yet Nolimit City games are some of the few we've seen repeatedly smash their win cap. From Bushido Ways xNudge to Fire in the Hole xBomb, to the mind-melting 200k of San Quentin xWays, all are proven big win games.They're also extraordinarily volatile machines, and Infectious 5 xWays is no different. Like its siblings, it will infuriate, exasperate, and torment, especially when what would have been an all-time Infectious xWays hit doesn't manage to connect. But, when it does, it's exciting as anything else Nolimit has done this year and almost guaranteed to pop up on a highlight reel sooner or later.

Title: King of Sweets
review: King of Sweets: Slot OverviewIf there are people who just can't get enough candy in their lives, then being ruled over by a sovereign called the King of Sweets would probably be pretty, well, sweet. King of Sweets is also the name of a Play'n GO candy game made in the time-honoured tradition of slots that hurt your gums just by looking at them. In an interesting twist, it's also a reskin of a game that could not be further from sugar, spice, and all things nice. The original in question is the freaky, tentacled, green and purple glowing monstrosity Rich Wilde and the Tome of Insanity, which has lent practically everything but the skin to King of Sweets.With a name like King of Sweets, what else can you expect to see on the screen other than a candy-coated paradise for sweet-tooth gamblers? An actual king shows up on the reels as one of the wild symbols, and his castle sits on the right while the foreground is littered with confectionery, cupcakes and the like. As far as candy slots go, King of Sweets' screen doesn't utterly ooze sugary items, but make no mistake, this is a saccharine slot that grates on the teeth if you're not totally on board with the subject matter.King of Sweets slot - base gameKing of Sweets' gaming area is a 5x5 space, creating winning combinations when at least four matching symbols are connected in horizontal or vertical directions anywhere on the grid. The symbols involved in a winning cluster get taken off the reels, causing symbols to drop down and new ones to come in from the top to replace them. Cascading continues as long as wins keep landing. When the bonus round is going, landing 2 scatter symbols awards +4 free spins, while landing 3 or more scatter symbols awards extra free spins in the manner they are originally triggered.During free spins, gold buffalo symbols are collected when they land before turning into regular buffalo symbols. For every 3 gold buffalo symbols collected, the lowest premium symbol on the reels is transformed into the buffalo for the rest of the feature. A maximum of 12 gold buffalo symbols can be collected.The rules are the same for the super bonus round, except for every 3 gold buffalos collected, Rampage Reels are triggered as well. Rampage Reels are reels that only contain buffalo symbols. When triggered, between 1 and the max number of Rampage Reels is randomly activated. The number of possible Rampage Reels is 2, 3, 4, or 5 when 3, 6, 9, or 12 gold buffalos have been collected.X-iterClicking the X-iter feature buy button displays five different ways of playing Buffalo Toro, though RTP is the same for all of them (94%):Matador Respin – 10x the bet buys 1 spin with a guaranteed Matador Respin.Toro Goes Wild – 25x the bet gets you 1 spin with a guaranteed Toro Goes Wild feature.Rampage Reels – 50x the bet buys 3 spins with guaranteed Rampage Reels on each spin.Bonus – buy the regular free spins feature for 100x the bet.Super Bonus – 500x the bet buys an entry to the Super Bonus game.Buffalo Toro slot - X-iter feature buy menuBuffalo Toro: Slot VerdictBuffalo Toro shows there's still no love lost between Toro and the Matador. This means hilarity ensues when the two characters hit at the same time, leading to the Toro Goes Wild features. Okay, it's not laugh-out-loud funny, the pair having duked it out for more than five years now, but their relationship continues to add personality to whatever game they appear in. And surprisingly, Buffalo Toro is the fourth time the two chaps have been brought together, cementing one of the more enduring relationships in slots. The symbol upgrade can work a real charm alongside those Rampaging Reels in an attempt to stack the grid with as many buffalo symbols as possible. It's tough to trigger naturally, however, since super scatter symbols only appear on the sixth reel. Buying it from the X-iter is another alternative, though it is pricey at 500x, not to mention challenging to recoup your outlay at times as well, a not uncommon ELK slots trait.Have you been on a commute to work in a crowded bus or train, and found a happy private mental place by blotting away the cramped conditions, pushing, shoving, passive-aggressive battles for a seat, and general irritation of being packed into a restrictive space, thereby making it possible to arrive at work, ready to bring it in the boardroom? Playing Buffalo Toro was kind of like that. If you can push the dismal brutality of the gameplay out of your consciousness, there's a rip-roaring buffalo-themed game here to enjoy.

Title: Skulls UP
review: Skulls UP (Quickspin): OverviewA pirates life was the very definition of volatility, especially when it came to glory. Either you took it all, or you got nothing. In spite of the hardships and the violence, and being chased by foreign government forces, pirating was an attractive proposition to certain types of (mainly) men. Instant wealth and instant glory, you just had to go out and get it. Men of that era could languish at home, or head out on the high seas, travel to exotic lands, and grab loot! Is it too much of a stretch to draw parallels between that life and playing slots? Nah, let’s run with it. The two must share common traits because pirate-themed slots pop up all the time. The latest is Skulls UP from Quickspin.Like the recent Golden Glyph, Skulls UP sees Quickspin tinkering with a conventional layout. Whereas Golden Glyph used a 7x7 setup, Skulls UP utilises reels that are expandable when certain symbols appear. The look is classic Quickspin with the familiar orange interface and 5x3 reel setup. Thanks to the extra features, this can quickly change, and we will detail how in the features section. When it comes to the pirate theme, developers tend to go down one of two routes – friendly cartoon-like, or grim baddie pirates. Quickspin have chosen the former, and the result is a cheerful mix of smiling pirates and cute animals.Don’t let the friendly vibe fool you though. This is one highly volatile game (4.5/5), so you can expect lulls or glory depending on how luck wants to play it. Just how much glory you will receive is slightly controversial, and we will go over that point when we wrap things up. As always with Quickspin, RTP is on the respectable side at 96.26% so no complaints there. Players pick bet levels that start at 10 p/c per spin and can be set as high as $/€100, and away they go. During the base game, the default 5x3 set up provides 243 win ways. Wins are formed by landing at least three adjacent matching symbols on any row from reel 1. Due to expanding rows, win ways can go as high as 1,944 at full power.When it comes to symbols, Quickspin has stayed more or less in theme, aside from the ubiquitous 10 – A card royals at the low end of things. On the high side, Quickspin has gone full swashbuckler, and we get parrots, monkeys, a pirate with an eye patch, and a lady pirate captain. This buccaneer-ess is worth the most at 20 times the stake for a five of a kind combo. Overall, symbols offer middle of the road value, nothing amazing or off-putting there. The paytable is rounded off by two different wilds which can land on reels 2, 3, and 4. There is also a scatter symbol that works together with the wilds to unlock the game’s best moments.Skulls UP (Quickspin): FeaturesFree spins featurePyromaniacs will be right at home with Skulls UP because the features all revolve around the burning stuff. Let’s start with the Flaming Respins which incorporates the Flaming Skull Wilds. The non-flaming Skull Wild performs the duties of a standard wild by substituting for any of the base pay symbols. When a Flaming Skull Wild lands, however, it triggers the Flaming Respins feature.Before the reels respin, any Flaming Skull Wild or Skull Wild will add an additional symbol to the grid above their position. The three middle reels can max out at 6 rows high, and if there is no more room above, then wilds stay in place. During a respin, if players score a win that includes a Flaming Skull Wild, the flame is extinguished, and it turns into a standard Skull Wild. As long as Flaming Skull Wilds remain on the reels, then the respins will continue to do their thing. All wins are tallied up, and the reels returned to normal height when no more respins occur.The scatter symbol is the treasure chest symbol. Land three of these to be awarded 8 Flaming Free Spins. The rules of the base game, including Flaming Respins, transfer over to the free spins round with two additions. The first is that if a reel reaches 6 symbols in height, then 2 additional free spins are added. Also, when Flaming Respins occur on a free spin, any increase in reel height will stay in place. That is, reels do not drop back to the normal height when a Flaming Respin is finished.Skulls UP (Quickspin): VerdictSkulls UP is a decent offering from Quickspin and has its entertaining moments. It’s good to see a developer trying new thing, though even with the nautical theme it doesn’t push the boat out as far as Golden Glyph did. What makes it work is the fact that features are kicked off every time a Flaming Wild Skull symbol lands, which helps maintain the flow. The expanding row feature is hardly new, but Quickspin has integrated it well with the pirating nature of the game. As you would expect the most exciting moments come when the features are working in tandem – especially during Flaming Free Spins where the rows stay in place after a Flaming Respin.The key drawback is the game’s potential, which at 3,650 times the bet isn’t exactly the Spanish Silver Train coming to town. It isn’t bad, but with the theme, the expanding reels mechanic and high volatility, we would have expected something higher. Still, fans of pirates or expanding reels will appreciate what Quickspin has produced. Get Skulls UP on a good roll, and it is capable of some satisfying gaming.

Title: Ancient Fortunes: Zeus
review: Ancient Fortunes: Zeus (Triple Edge Studios): ReviewIt's not a secret that we're no big fans of Microgaming. It has nothing to do with the fact that the company has been stacking up one trainwreck slot after another, in fact, the cut is much deeper than that. Following a series of bad games (plenty where those came from), and subsequently negative reviews, one Microgaming representative reacted childishly (they seem used to people rubbing their backs), calling us names and cutting all ties. With that said, our aim is straight and true and we stick to our policy of writing unbiased reviews no matter how bad the company we're dealing with.Alright, end of drama and on to more important things. In front of us, we have an online slot based on Greek mythology - more specifically, the thunder god Zeus. It's a popular theme that's been used countless times, most prominently in William Interactive's rendition, matter-of-factly entitled Zeus. Seen through a modern lens, Zeus was in many ways a peculiar god - he was married to his sister (Hera), he was repeatedly unfaithful to her, and he punished men by giving them women (quite a brutal deity). However, to those unfamiliar with Greek mythology he's just that cool, ripped, superhero hurling thunderbolts. Why he became a poster boy for online slots is a mystery though.In this 5-reel, 10-payline Microgaming powered slot developed by Triple Edge Studios, you will benefit from the Rolling Reels feature where winning streaks can lead to a 7x multiplier. Up to 70 free spins are on offer in the bonus where the previously mentioned feature also applies, but with a boost in the increasing multiplier that can reach up to 21x here. Play it across all devices from 0.10 to 70 Eur a spin.In regard to the design, there's little to complain about and it actually looks quite nice, which is more than can be said about most of Microgaming's other recent efforts. Ascending through the clouds, you're invited to the heavenly kingdom of Mount Olympus, home to the mighty Zeus.While spinning the reels you will come across a collection of low-value symbols represented by snakes, panthers, krakens and vultures. In order of value, the top ranking symbols are represented by the following greek gods: Dionysus (god of wine), Poseidon (god of the Sea, earthquakes and horses), Hermes (god of trade, heraldry, merchants, commerce, roads, thieves, trickery, sports, travelers, and athletes) and Ares (god of war). The latter is the most valuable and yields 62.5 times your stake for 5 appearing on a full payline. Replacing all other symbols, Zeus is the wild.Ancient Fortunes: Zeus (Triple Edge Studios): FeaturesAncient Fortunes: Zeus relies mainly on the Rolling Reels feature which allows you to win both ways (from left to right and right to left). Bonanza-style, it's essentially a chain-reaction feature that, upon landing winning combinations, removes the contributing symbols only to replace them with new ones. Furthermore, it comes with an increasing multiplier that can go up to 7x as a result of consecutive wins.Things get even better when you land 3, 4 or 5 lightning bolt scatters on a payline as it gives you access to the free spin feature. Starting with 10, 15 or 20 free spins respectively, you can retrigger the bonus with up to 70 free spins in total. Now, the Rolling Reels feature applies here as well, but with the added benefit of an increased maximum multiplier value of up to 21x.Ancient Fortunes: Zeus (Triple Edge Studios): VerdictWe might be going out on a limb here, but we can't shake the fact that Zeus comes across as a half-assed effort trying to jump on the Bonanza wagon. The 5x3, 10-payline setup is inherently limiting, something the attractive design cannot make up for. Furthermore, the gameplay is choppy and slow and feels more like a version of Gonzo's Quest.The medium variance action, in combination with the rather disappointing payouts, do little to evoke an emotional response, other than despair, and as such, Ancient Fortunes: Zeus is a game we just can't see ourselves spending much time on, especially with the alternatives available on the market if you're looking for cascading slots.

Title: Dragonfire Chamber of Gold
review: Dragonfire Chamber of Gold Hold&Win: Slot OverviewTime for swords and sandals, players, as we take on one of the most powerful creatures in any mythology – dragons. This time the scaly beasts have brought a bit of grandeur to iSoftBet's busy range of Hold&Win slots. The game in question is titled Dragonfire Chamber of Gold and adds one or two tricks to its streak respin bonus round while doing some nifty stuff with wild symbols in the base game.Dragonfire Chamber of Gold could have gone one of two ways. iSoftBet has added it to their Hold&Win collection, but it could have easily slotted into the Twisted Tales series if the studio had incorporated a few familiar faces. Dragonfire contains only custom-made characters, though, so the heroes and villains found in the game have a generic, homemade look to them. Not in a bad way at all, though, and as far as Hold&Win slots go, Dragonfire is one of the above-average ones. It's got a bit of thematic depth, decent graphics, and the soundtrack is especially uplifting, even a little chilling at times.The action occurs on a 5-reel, 5-row game panel, with 50 paylines for landing winning combinations of three to five of a kind across. It does this in a highly volatile way, splitting the action between a wild encrusted base game and a dragon egg money symbol bonus round. When suiting up for the adventure, players pick bets of 25 p/c to $/€25 per spin, and the dungeon questing has been made possible on any device.Checking out the paytable uncovers 10 regular pay symbols, split between low pay royals and higher value characters. Low pays award payouts of 2 to 4 times the stake for five of a kind, while the diverse character list is worth 6 to 40 times the bet for landing five on a payline. Wilds lend themselves to much of Dragonfire's thrilling sequences, where their basic function is replacing normal pay symbols to help complete winning lines. The rest of what wilds can do is covered next.Dragonfire Chamber of Gold Hold&Win: Slot FeaturesDragonfire Chamber of Gold slot - bonusWild symbols in Dragonfire Chamber of Gold aren't just wilds. Here they are known as Splitting Wilds. This is because when a wild symbol hits, it splits into two and triggers a respin. For the respin, one wild copy is placed one reel to the left; the other is placed one reel to the right. If a win occurs on the respin, any wilds involved in it move to an adjacent reel, and another respin is triggered. Wilds can also get win multipliers which increase by +1 each time they spread to a new reel. Alternatively, if a wild symbol lands on reels 2 and 4, a respin is awarded. For this respin, reel 3 turns completely wild, and the original wilds are moved to reels 1 and 5.Respins FeatureOne more important symbol in Dragonfire Chamber of Gold is the dragon egg scatter. Landing at least 5 of these symbols in the base game triggers the Hold&Win bonus round. As per usual, the triggering scatters symbols lock in place, and 3 spins are awarded. The bonus is played on a game panel where regular symbols have been removed. Now, whenever new dragon eggs land during the feature, they lock in place, reveal a cash prize and return the spin count back to 3. Should dragon eggs land on three consecutive spins, one of the gates next to the grid opens. When the gate on the right opens, all dragon egg values in view are collected, and dragon eggs are removed from the reels. This provides more space to land new ones.If the left gate opens, three multiplier frames are added to the grid. Multiplier frames move to random positions between spins, and if an egg lands in one or a frame lands on an egg, its value is multiplied. After a frame has been used to boost a win, it is removed from the reels. Frames remaining on the reels have their multiplier increased by +1 on each spin until they are used to increase a scatter symbol's value.Bonus BuyIf the Bonus Buy button is present, players can buy a respins bonus round for 100x the bet or a free spins bonus round with multiplier frames active for 250x the bet.Dragonfire Chamber of Gold Hold&Win: Slot VerdictIf there are two things that pop out at regular intervals from iSoftBet, it's dragons and Hold&Win features. It stands to reason the two elements would crash headlong into each other sooner or later. iSoftBet usually uses dragons in an Asian setting, with the exception of slots like Dragon Stone, so seeing them in a fantasy game makes for a nice change. On the subject of theme, iSoftBet has done quite a nice job. The graphics are good, the soundtrack borders on the sublime, and the action cuts nicely between the base game hall and bonus round dungeon. In short, fantasy players should be pleased with what they find.Dragonfire's features are fairly strong for a Hold&Win slot as well. Especially the base game, where the splitting, walking, multiplying wild respins are there to mix things up. It was a little surprising to find such a developed secondary feature in a Hold&Win game, actually. Usually, it's something like random wilds or a one-off win multiplier, not something so fully developed. Maybe we're making more out of the respin feature than it is, but it's a welcome accompaniment.On the other hand, the Hold&Win bonus round is pretty regular stuff, though it has a couple of extras chucked on top. The extras aren't part of some massive streak respin revolution, but they're something for hold and win experts to have a look over. Multipliers are one of the quickest ways of augmenting win values in a lot of games, but it was interesting to see how often multiplier frames stubbornly moved to empty positions during the playthrough. Not always. Sometimes they could be useful, just an observation.With all the experience iSoftBet has gained from making these sorts of games, it would be nice to see them channel their expertise into making one mammoth Hold&Win game. For now, they seem content with the quantity over premium quality approach, slinging out playable if slightly forgettable Hold&Win styled slots.

Title: Birthday!
review:
Birthday!: IntroductionELK Studios is certainly not a bad provider, but we are yet to see a game that has really been able to challenge the top providers. With ELK, it sort of feels as if we're waiting for something to happen that is not happening, and just like some of the other providers they have become a bit stuck in their way of creating slots. The element of surprise is not really there.The latest line of games - Wild Seas, Kaiju and Lake's Five are all decent games, but nothing that will win any awards. In fact, the game Kaiju turned out to be a scatter teasing son of a...Birthday is a 5-reel, 4-row slot with 178 fixed paylines. It is playable on all devices from €0.10 to €50 and features guest character's known from other ELK titles, such as the bull from Wild Toro (he's a sleezy looking bartender now apparently), the hot lady captain from Wild Seas, Electric Sam and the Blooper dudes.The layout itself is in typical ELK style, so those who know the games will feel at home right away. The soundtrack is what really stands out here with it's funky, R&B type of style! It's simply genious and certain to get stuck in your head. Another cool thing is how they have programmed for random celebrity birthday announcements to pop up.The symbols used in this game are not exactly traditional and there are actually only 6 regular symbols compared to most other 5-reel slots which usually makes use of at least 8. There are 3 low value symbols represented by red heart shaped balloons, green balloons and blue balloons.The 3 premium symbols are made out of birthday logos, roses and drinks, with the Birthday symbol being worth 15x across a line of 5 symbols. Birthday includes 3 different wilds - 1 regular (Birthday cake) and the other 2 only present in the Happy Spins feature and Free Spins bonus game.Birthday!: FeaturesFree Spins bonus game in actionHappy Spins are five different types of randomly triggered respins. The doorbell announces the start of every Happy Spins feature, and generates excitement about who the next guest will be and what particular feature he or she brings along.Spin until a given number of wins
The Camel gifts a respin that continues until a given number of wins (3 to 5) is achieved.Spin until 5 of a kind
Mr Lake's respin gift continues until a win with 5 of a kind is achieved on a payline.Electrified symbol
Electric Sam gifts a respin that continues as long as additional instances of a preselected symbol appear. The selected symbols get electrified and stay sticky throughout the respin.Spin until a given win
The sneaky Matador selects a symbol and gifts a respin that continues until a win with the selected symbol is achieved.Spin until a Big Win
Anne Bonny, the notorious pirate from Wild Seas, hands over a valuable respin gift that continues until a Big Win (15 x bet or higher) is achieved.Free Spins are triggered in a bit of an unusual way. Whenever Maggie, a cheerful little girl with a balloon, turns up to ring the doorbell, 10 free spins are awarded. She can also retrigger within the free spins generating a long chain of free spins and numerous of chances to win.What makes the free spins bonus game stand out from the main game are the two additional wilds:Sticky Wilds
The Soundtech may place up to three Sticky Wilds anywhere on the reels. All the wilds stay sticky during the remaining respins or free spins.Walking Wilds
The Soundtech Blooper hands out up to three Waiking Wilds anywhere on the reels. The Walking Wild move leftwards one reel for every spin until they leave the screen to the left.These wilds can also turn up in the randomly triggered Happy Spins feature.Birthday!: VerdictBirthday is quite high variance (7 out of 10 on ELK's volatility scale) with a max win potential of 5,000x, which is not bad at all and certainly makes it worth trying a few spins on. The game has a 96.3% RTP which is standard today and expected.It's not a game that stands out in any particular ways and it's certainly not a jaw dropping experience. With ELK you kind of know what you're going to get by now and this is no different. That doesn't mean it's bad, but it would have been fun to see them try something more out of the box.With that said, the Happy Spins feature keeps the game interesting in the main game which otherwise doesn't have much going for it. 5000x sounds nice and all, but it would require some sick hits that you are not likely to see of course, so expect 500-1000x on the best of days.

Title: Flying Hippo
review: Flying Hippo: Slot OverviewYou've probably heard the saying 'when pigs fly' to refer to something that just isn't going to happen, but have you ever heard of hippos flying? Due to their size, hippos are probably even less likely to find themselves airborne than their piggy counterparts. A terrifying thought, too, since hippos are one of the deadliest land-based animals; perhaps there's the makings of a movie here somewhere. We had Sharknado, so who knows? Anyhoo, bringing the focus back to the game at hand, we encounter Flying Hippo, a LeoVegas exclusive from software provider Pragmatic Play.Flying Hippo is a cluster pays grid slot that was odd from start to finish. To start, there's the theme's execution and Flying Hippo came across as low thrills, like it's not entirely sure what it's trying to be. The action is set in the sky, with clouds fluffing about in the lower part of the screen and a starry night sky in the upper part. With no bonus game transition, this is pretty much it. Playing Flying Hippo was like waiting for a punchline which never came.Flying Hippo slot by Pragmatic PlayOn the subject of stats, Pragmatic Play has rated the game five out of five for volatility, while the game churns out a return to player value of 93.99%. Clearly, Pragmatic Play has enough friends already. That might be enough for a lot of players to turn their attention aside already, but if not, then the game is available on any device, where players are free to choose a bet from 20 p/c per spin up to a maximum of $/€100 per spin.The gaming part of Flying Hippo takes place on a 7x7 matrix, with the goal of landing blocks of 5 or more matching symbols, connecting vertically or horizontally. Hit a winning cluster, and the tumble feature removes the winning symbols from the grid, replacing them with new ones from above. Before symbols drop, though, a wild is placed in one of the empty spots at random. Tumbles keep tumbling until no new win is created. As for pay symbols, we find fluffy J-A card symbols representing the low symbols, while the highs are a green star, a red star, a yellow star, and a hippo. Hitting a 5-6 symbol cluster pays 0.1 to 0.75 times the bet, rising to 5 to 50 times the bet for a 25+ sized cluster. Smiley clouds are the wild symbols, appearing on all reels to substitute for any other symbol. There are no other symbols in Flying Hippo.Flying Hippo: Slot FeaturesFlying Hippo slot - paytableThere isn't a whole lot happening in Flying Hippo to go through. Play mainly revolves around a tumble feature and a Spawning Wild feature, though the latter has quite a few rules attached. However, Flying Hippo does not have a bonus round or free spins phase to it.Spawning Wild FeatureWhen a wild symbol is created by the tumble feature, it may have a multiplier depending on the level of the current spin. This multiplier is applied to any future cluster wins the wild symbol is part of. When a wild symbol contributes to a winning cluster, it is collected by a meter. For every 6 wilds collected this way, the level of the spin increases from 1 to 2, then finally to 3. Before level 1 is hit, wilds appear with no multiplier or an x2;In level 1, they can have x2 or x3 multipliers.In level 2, this increases to x3, x4, x5, or x6.In level 3, they also appear with values of x3, x4, x5, or x6.After level 3 has been reached, the wild collection stops, and when tumbles end, 2 Colossal 2x2 wilds with random multipliers are added in random spots on the board. The value for these wilds can be x3, x5, x7, x10, x15, x25, or x50. If a Colossal Wild overlaps an existing wild, the smaller wild's multiplier is added to the Colossal Wild. If more than one wild is part of the same cluster, their multipliers are added together. After all tumbles in the spin end, the meter is reset back to level 0.Flying Hippo slot by Pragmatic PlayFlying Hippo: Slot VerdictWeird game. There's a floating, flying through-the-clouds effect, and one of the symbols is a hippo, but pardon the pun; the flying hippo concept never really got off the ground. It just felt odd. That wouldn't be such an issue if the gameplay and peripheral parts flew in to save the day, yet they just didn't. All in all, Flying Hippo felt incomplete, or not completely thought through, rushed. As if the designers forgot about the deadline and woke up at midnight of the day before the game was meant to be shipped and quickly threw some code together, tacked on a bunch of dull imagery and gave it a random name. Kind of like when Marge Simpson came up with 'Ghost Mutt'.That or someone at Pragmatic Play deliberately set out to punk LeoVegas. We would never suggest this was the case, but such was the reaction playing Flying Hippo provoked. Along with the casino, the game's stats would suggest it's setting out to punk players as well. With an RTP that would make the bean counters at ELK Studios jealous, who would want to play Flying Hippo after viewing the return value? It's not like there's a titanic progressive jackpot justifying the weak RTP, or gameplay so stunning players might look the other way. Flying Hippo's wild collection, multiplier building, and colossal wild dumping idea aren't a bad combo. They just get smothered into oblivion by the odd execution, stats, and lack of enthusiasm for the theme.With Flying Hippo, Pragmatic Play has proven it can certainly be capriciously erratic. The studio's prior game we reviewed was the excellently done The Dog House Multihold, which took a classic slot in a new and exciting direction, thereby reinforcing the team's reputation for being one of the best in the biz. Then, it followed up with Flying Hippo, a pointless release that did little but tarnish the studio's name.

Title: Spirit of the River
review: Spirit of the River: Slot OverviewDeveloper SG Digital moves on from exploring Native American culture in Yanaha's Rite to south of the border for a similar game titled Spirit of the River. We say similar, but it's basically the same, as SG Digital has simply reskinned Yanaha's Rite (a game conceived by LeoVegas and hosted on the SG Digital platform) by giving it an Aztec outer look instead. The rest is as it was mathematically and feature-wise, where players get a Dual Ways Pays mechanic, a Spin Tower scatter collection system, and free spins with 4-reel modifiers.The layout and general vibe of Spirit of the River is virtually the same as Yanaha’s Rite. On the left side stands a character with magical powers, in this case, a priestess type holding a ball of energy in mid-air. In the middle of the screen is the 4-reel, 6-row game grid, while the Spin Tower is located on the right displaying 4 different animals. If anything, the atmosphere isn't quite as rich as Yanaha's Rite was, maybe because it's kind of peculiar the priestess is chilling in a stream like nothing odd's going on. But hey, Spirit of the River packs in just as much magic as its predecessor for players who like to spin on the mysterious side of life.Getting started in Spirit of the River requires picking stakes where choices range from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin. Like before, the math model is medium-high volatile, generating a rather generous return value of 96.7% which does work in its favour as a selling point. As the name says, the Dual Ways mechanic pays left to right and top to bottom. Horizontal wins are determined when 3 or more matching symbols land left to right from the leftmost symbol, while vertical wins are formed by 3 identical symbols landing in consecutive rows starting from the topmost row.Symbol combinations have the same value no matter which direction they land in, and there are 10 regular pays to work with. The first seven are low and mid pay patterned symbols, while three characters appear on the trio of premiums. These are a warrior type, a chap who looks like the chief, and the priestess lady who is standing knee-deep in the river. Due to one of the reel modifiers in free spins, it is possible to expand the grid. At its larger size, an 8-symbol premium win is worth 10 to 20 times the stake. At the default grid size, a six-symbol vertical win is worth 2.5 to 5 times the bet. There is a wild too, replacing any pay symbol to complete wins, but it only shows up during free spins.Spirit of the River: Slot FeaturesSpirit of the River has two more symbols – a scatter which triggers free spins where a wild symbol may appear. When a scatter symbol lands on the grid, a segment is added to the Spirit Tower, and a spins counter is displayed above it. Players then get 20 spins to fill the Spirit Tower which has 4 segments in total. If the 20 spins run out without collecting 4 scatters, then 2 segments are removed from the Spirit Tower. If any segments remain, the spins counter resets; otherwise, the spins counter is removed.If the Spirit Tower is filled in time, then 8 free spins are awarded. Title: Kiss Reels of Rock
review: Kiss Reels of Rock: Slot OverviewThe rock group Kiss was colossal back in the day, the band famous for their face painting, eccentric costumes, fire breathing, fireworks, smoking guitars, and blood-spitting antics on stage, amongst other wacky things. Title: The Last Sundown
review: The Last Sundown: Slot OverviewAh, the future, no one has a clue what it will be like, but many people are willing to hazard a guess. At the start of free spins, one pay symbol is chosen to be a splitting symbol and one other regular pay symbol is selected for collection. Whenever the chosen collection symbol lands, it fills the collector by one. The more you collect, the more additional symbols can be turned into splitting symbols for the remainder of the feature. You will need to collect 6 for each weapon, 5 for each character, and 4 for the wild. Each time you complete a collection, you get +3 additional free spins as well as the new splitting symbol.The Last Sundown: Slot VerdictThe Last Sundown follows on from Play'n GO's Shimmering Woods, with several key changes to the gameplay. The other major difference is the choice of window dressing, and The Last Sundown has a far grittier theme than Shimmering Woods' crystals in the forest thing. Maybe this will broaden the appeal, maybe not, but it suits The Last Sundown's slightly higher volatility, and Play'n GO has presented it all in their usual attractive style.The gameplay and features are relatively simple yet very effective when the collection feature is going well. You don't get that in The Last Sundown, where collecting is all. Like the last precious well of water in the middle of a fought-over futuristic patch of earth. The Last Sundown can certainly deliver white-knuckle gaming when it fires up, and some players may welcome a more relaxed set of rules to enjoy the ride in.
