Where the last one, CherryPop, pushed the franchise closer to the mainstream due to its fruit styling, BountyPop returns to Avatar UX's Asian heritage for inspiration.At first, it will be hard to see what all the PopWins fuss is about. Upon firing the slot up, a basic 5-reel, 3-row grid sitting against a Northern Lights type image meets the eye, while a fantasy soundtrack drifts about in the background. It's functional, but pretty plain compared to what Avatar UX has done in the past.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€20 per spin, like others in the range, expect a highly volatile gaming experience which can go from nothing to prolonged sequences of pops with huge potential on offer. When spinning for the big one, wins come on average at a rate of 1 every 5 spins, while an RTP rating of 96% is right on average. The game uses a win-all-ways, pay-both-ways system meaning combinations from left to right as well as right to left are possible. This effectively doubles the 243 win ways possible in the default 5x3 mode. As the reels expand from the PopWins feature (covered below), so do the number of ways to win up to a maximum of 59,049.The paytable begins with four florescent card royals (J-A) designed in a flowing Gothic script, followed by a bunch of cartoon characters. The extras in BountyPop include free spins, and Mystery Wheel Multipliers.When a winning combination lands, each winning symbol pops to be replaced with two new symbols. This increases the size of the respective reels while boosting the number of ways to win. During the base game, reels max out at 6 positions high. When no more wins land, reels reset to their normal size.If all reels hit 6 rows high in the base game at the end of the win sequence, the Mystery Wheel feature is triggered. On the wheel's outer part, x2-x3, or x5 multipliers and arrows are present. Landing on an arrow spins the inner wheel which awards multipliers of x3-x5, or x10. Multipliers are then applied once to the current win.Landing 3 or more scatter symbols in view trigger the bonus game. Specifically, 3, 4, 5 scatters award 6, 9, or 12 free spins respectively. In the bonus game, reels can now expand to 9 rows in height producing up to 59,049 ways to win. Expanded rows do not reset to the base level between free spins either, but drop down to the lowest reel height.If all 5 reels reach 7 rows or higher a multiplier wheel is unlocked. This wheel spins when free spins are complete, applying a multiplier to the total round win:Bronze wheel (all reels 7 symbols tall): outer ring has Arrow, x2-3, x5. Inner ring has x3-5, x10.Silver wheel (all reels 8 symbols tall): outer ring has Arrow, x2-5, x7. Inner ring has x3-5, x7, x10.Gold wheel (all reels 9 symbols tall): outer ring has Arrow, x3-5, x7, x10. Inner ring has x3-5, x7, x10, x100.For the record, it takes 300 spins on average to trigger free spins. Where available, players can avoid the struggle by activating the bonus buy option, costing 100 times the bet to do so. Before the bonus starts players have the option of spinning a wheel to either win more free spins or lose the lot.BountyPop: Slot VerdictAfter reaching four deep in the PopWins range, players will have a sound idea of what to expect. Namely, getting winning symbols to pop, expand reels, and trigger multipliers. So far, each PopWins slot has used variations of these same components while playing around with the peripheral functions. BountyPop is the same, not doing anything out of the ordinary to put off fans or win over those not enamoured by the mechanic.After the slick styling of CherryPop, slightly more was expected from the follow-up. In fact, BountyPop comes across as less sophisticated too, as if less creativity went into the design than its predecessors. There just doesn't seem to be much new this time around. Unlocking reels on extended runs of pops is fun, yet the impact is watered down on the fourth run through. PopWins is a clever feature, but to keep using it requires pairing it with ever better themes, and features.BountyPop kind of misses the mark in that regard. The theme isn't very engaging, and the game boils down to hitting max rows to pull in a multiplier - fun when it happens, but it feels more repetitive than before. The bonus buy has never been quite so tempting, especially considering you need 300 spins on average to trigger free spins organically. Free spins can be quite a trip where everything gets bigger – reels, win ways and multipliers. It's here the game's eye-watering potential of 55,000 times the bet has a chance to be cracked. A big number, though none have trumped the 70,000x found in the original PopRocks slot yet.There was a feeling of progression in the last three PopWins slots, or they at least made sense from a business perspective. BountyPop, on the other hand, is neither as mainstream as CherryPop, nor does it push the series far along. BountyPop ends up being one for hardcore PopWins fans to enjoy, but it might not be the best entry point if you are new to the mechanic.Don't MissIf you like the PopWin series of slots, be sure to check out the next instalment titled TikiPop. It's played using a 96.10% RTP and offers wins of up to 32,000 times your bet.

Title: Playboy Fortunes
review: Playboy Fortunes: OverviewLads, prepare to get all hot under the collar in a bunny filled extravagance from Microgaming partner Gameburger Studios. The developer has taken their hit 9 Masks of Fire (or 9 Pots of Gold for that matter), stripped away the tribal graphics, slipped what’s left into a thong, and repackaged it as Playboy Fortunes. Apologies if that was a rather long-winded way of saying Playboy Fortunes is merely a reskin, but there we go. The original had a pretty heated theme already, so you might think the game could only get steamier by dropping in a few scantily clad ladies. Only one way to find out.Playboy might be famous for its media, especially its iconic magazine which has been enlightening the predominantly male mind since its inception in 1953. Fast forward to the modern era and around half of Playboy’s revenues now come from the licensing of consumer goods. This includes penetration of the slots market in part by Microgaming in Playboy and its follow-up, Playboy Gold Jackpots from Triple Edge Studios. The original was excellent, the other ones not so much, which goes to show that jamming on a pair of bunny ears is no guarantee of quality.Playboy Fortunes is built using a classic layout of 5 reels and 20 paylines with the grid located next to a scatter win prize ladder. As you would expect, the colour palette is heavy on the red and gold. When you combine the tones with the pattern on the background, the game has a palpable Asian touch, whether that was intentional or not is unclear. In any case, the action on the reels is accompanied by a funky soundtrack and a bunch of young ladies who appear at certain moments of the game. Playboy Fortunes gives off a gentleman’s club vibe, though not a strip club, which Gameburger has wisely avoided.Players can spin Playboy Fortunes on any device, setting bets from 20 p/c to $/€60 in the process. The math model stats are spot on the same as 9 Masks, providing an RTP of 96.24% coupled with medium volatility. Wins come just as frequently as before, thanks to a higher than normal hit rate of 39.75% contributing to the game’s positive flow.If there is one thing that has changed, it is the symbols. From the lows to the highs players get BARs, cocktails, keys, bow tie/cufflinks, sevens, double sevens, and triple sevens. As a value indicator, triple sevens are worth 37.5 times the stake for five of a kind. One thing about symbol combos is a mixture of sevens, such as 7+77+777, will also pay out, albeit at a reduced amount. Look out for the casino chips symbol; this is the wild. Five of them are worth 125 times the stake while being able to substitute for any regular pay symbol.Playboy Fortunes: FeaturesPlayboy Fortunes - free spinsThe jewel in Playboy Fortunes crown is the instant scatter win prizes, backed up by a round of free spins with a win multiplier on the side.Keep an eye out for the free spins scatter symbol which only appears on the middle three reels, as 3 in view awards a blast on the free spin wheel. The wheel awards 10 to 30 free spins, plus a multiplier of 2x or 3x. Multipliers are applied to any win during the feature except Playboy scatter wins. Free spins can also be retriggered with the amount of free spins awarded being the same as the initial trigger.We said to look out for the wild too, but it’s the Playboy scatter you really want - 3 or more of these anywhere in view award an instant cash prize. The amount up for grabs is f 1x, 5x, 15x, 40x, 100x, 500x, or 2,000 times the stake when 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9 scatters land respectively.Playboy Fortunes: VerdictIn spite of the rather lukewarm response from the casino community, 9 Masks of Fire proved to be quite successful for Gameburger. There was something in its mix of simple gaming, fiery/tribal theme, and instant 2,000x prize potential that struck a chord with many. So much so that Playboy Fortunes is the third clone of the original, which means the project comes off as an exercise in recycling. So, whilst Gameburger gets to recycle its well-proven game mechanics, Microgaming slings them an old Playboy license. It’s a win-win for the studios.And for players? Is Playboy Fortunes any good? Is it a worthy successor to 9 Masks? The answer kind of depends on your mood. In some ways, the game is a shameless bit of branding; a quick and easy reskin to cash in on past success. If you can’t see past the objectification of women issue, or the repetitive gameplay and modest potential, Playboy Fortunes is not quite so rosy.If you take it in good humour though, then the game can be a bit of fun. It strides off the mould more confidently than its predecessors did. The styling works quite well, the bunnies do their thing, and the gameplay is everything the first one was. All in all, sprinkling the latest one with Playboy bunnies is either the best thing ever or the most desperate, depending on your viewpoint.Usually, life is about middle grounds rather than extremes though, which is pretty much where Playboy Fortunes sits - smack bang mediocre. It has much of what players liked about 9 Masks and 9 Pots - the high hit rate, the chance for hitting 2,000x at any point, and nice design. There was a strong case of diminishing returns with the 9 Pots of Gold clone, yet Playboy Fortunes manages to pull things back into positive territory, to an extent.Still, Playboy Fortunes doesn’t have the innocent charm 9 Masks had, and the whole bunny thing will grate with some players - in which case it’s best sticking to the original. Overall, it feels like a lesser slot than 9 Masks was, yet Playboy Fortunes might be alright for a few laughs if you enjoyed what the original had to offer.

Title: Happy Riches
review: Happy Riches Slot (NetEnt): OverviewWell, the NetEnt reskin machine continues to chug on and churn out more and more rehashed slots for the Asian market. This time, NetEnt has dug up a cheerful older title called Flowers (2013) from their back catalogue for a remake. The aesthetics have been stripped away, they’ve kept the features and mechanics, and tarted it up with plenty of Asian imagery. It must be a formula for success because these types of slots are starting to pile up. No doubt it’s quicker and easier than designing a brand new slot from scratch. It's best to choose whether Happy Riches is worth playing by using that realistic figure to base decisions on. Title: Stone Gaze of Medusa 2

Bow in hand, this Medusa accompanies players as they brave her domain, set amidst a handsome ancient Greek scene, as she shrieks and laughs malevolently next to the 6-reel gaming grid.Stone Gaze of Medusa 2 slot - base gameWhere Stone Gaze of Medusa 2 deviates from the past is that it does not land a set number of symbols. If more than one Multiplier symbol lands, their multipliers are added together.Power SymbolsPower symbols may land anywhere on the grid to turn to stone and remove paying symbols. Stakelogic might have played with the number of symbols landing on each reel, in effect giving the game a semi-Megaways quality, but the rest of the slot is more or less the same as it was in the original. It does raise thoughts about a full-blown scatter paying slot on a genuine Megaways game engine - two enormously popular devices brought together in one spot could be lethal. At the very least, such an amalgamation would create quite an attention-grabbing headline, just saying.Stone Gaze of Medusa 2 is arguably less headline-worthy, but it gives scatter-paying folk something they might not have seen before. Alternating the number of symbols on the reels works about as well as you might expect. Potentially better when there are more of them, perhaps less so when the number of symbols is thinner. The concept might not be a game changer, but it's something new, and this effect helps push Stone Gaze of Medusa 2 even further away from Gates of Olympus than the first Stone Gaze of Medusa slot did - though the much slower-paced gameplay might turn some players off. Maybe if winning potential had increased, the sequel would have gained a greater oomph, but the top number has remained the same as before, at 10,000x the bet.As well as the dynamic reel height, there are other reasons why a scatter pays fan might want to pick this over, say, Gates. One is that Power symbols are able to remove more symbols than ever. Another is that the multiplier system is enjoyably straightforward. So, while much of this was available in the previous game, the faux-Megaways effect is something you don't really see in a scatter pays slot, making Stone Gaze of Medusa 2 one for the completists to tick off their list.

Like regular wilds, they never appear on the leftmost reel:Spawning wilds – creates up to 5 random multipliers from x2 to x5 in value.Expanding wilds – up to x3 expanding wilds are placed on the grid.Wild streak – offers several wilds on a single row or multiple rows of reels.Bonus Wheel & Super Bonus WheelLanding 3 scatter symbols on reels 2, 3, 4, and 5 triggers the Bonus Wheel, or landing 4 scatter symbols triggers the Super Bonus Wheel. For free spins, all low-value symbols are removed from the base reels. Landing 3 or 4 scatters triggers another Bonus Wheel.Bonus Trail & Super Bonus TrailThis feature is made up of a trail that players move around collecting multiplier values, starting with 3 lives. On each game round, a number is revealed, and the player's token moves that number of positions along the trail. Landing on a number adds that value to an overall bet multiplier known as the win bank. Landing on the same position twice or getting an X on the mini reel loses a life. When all lives are lost, the value of the multiplier bank is awarded. Landing on a mystery position triggers the Golden reel, revealing one of these:A number – this number is added to all values on the board. In the Super Trail, this value is added to each board position at the start of each new move.Three Hearts – one life is returned. Obviously, the impact has lessened the second time around, and the two game worlds could hardly be any different. The actors in Wild Hogs were like rascally piggy wiggies that grew up on the wrong side of the tracks and are determined to raise heck wherever they ride their choppers. The pigs in PigsVille, by contrast, are like the ones who studied hard, got a white-collar job in the city, made a bit of bread, raised a family in a neat middle-class pigsty in a respectable suburb, had a middle-aged crisis, then went out and bought motorbikes and joined a motorbike club for respectable middle-class pigs.Beyond the skin, players get basically the same thrills and spills as before. Title: Fruity Megaways
review: Fruity Megaways: Slot OverviewGiven the popularity of fruit and of Megaways, online slot Fruity Megaways has the sort of title that seems so obvious in retrospect you wonder why it hasn't been used before. The brains behind the release is UK-based outfit Iron Dog Studio, and it has made one heckuva delightful game right here. No matter how the rest of it plays out, if you'd like to come experience one of the more cheerful games reviewed in recent memory, then why not grab a healthy snack and let's take a look?The first thing that stood out about Fruity Megaways was its sweeping soundtrack. Seriously, play this game on mute, and it loses a massive whack of its charm. We'd say more about it, but we espouse the virtues of the tune in the verdict section, so let's hold off till then. Visually, Fruity Megaways is a warm game, too; its grid is flanked by smiling bananas, a fruit juice smiles up in the right-hand corner, and the reels are smothered in happy fruit, which, yes, are also smiling or looking friendly. One thing not looking happy is the chopped apple floating in the water beneath the reels, but we wouldn't be surprised if you flipped it over to find it was also smiling. Basically, if you want a quick positive snap from a slot in your life, fire up Fruity Megaways for a moment to soak in the amiable ambience.Fruity Megaways slot - base gameDespite the appearance, Fruity Megaways is a no-nonsense gambling machine, with a medium-high volatile math model producing a return to player of 96.06%. When you're ready to get the machine moving, bets of 10 p/c to $/€50 per spin may be selected.Cheerful characters of the predominantly fruit/fruit drink-related variety appear on Fruity Megaways' symbols. From lowest value to highest, there are blueberries, an apple, an orange, a strawberry, a banana, some grapes, a watermelon slice, and some sort of rainbow berry. Hitting a 6-symbol winning way pays 0.8 to 5 times the bet. A coconut, which is actually a type of fruit called a drupe, is Fruity Megaways' wild symbol. Wilds substitute for all non-special symbols.Fruity Megaways: Slot FeaturesFruity Megaways slot - pick me featureTumbles and scatters are the stepping stones to Fruity Megaways' features, such as the Pick Me feature, free spins, and Bonus Builder.TumblesEach symbol used in a win is removed from the board by the tumble mechanic. All removed symbols are replaced by symbols falling down from above. Following the tumble, if a new win is created, then the tumble feature triggers again until no new win appears.Pick Me FeatureIn the base game, five consecutive winning tumbles awards the Pick Me feature. For this, 5 fruits are presented on the screen for players to pick one. The picked fruit will reveal a cash prize of 5, 10, 15, or 20 times the bet, or 10 free spins.Free SpinsOtherwise, landing 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols awards 10, 15, 20, or 25 free spins, respectively. During free spins, getting 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, or 10 consecutive winning tumbles builds the Bonus Builder up. When free spins end, the highest level achieved on the Bonus Builder awards its prize.Fruity Megaways slot - free spinsFruity Megaways: Slot VerdictIf you ever feel a bit down, a bit mopey, life's getting to you, and you'd like a slot-based pick me up, then it might be worth putting Fruity Megaways on for a while. Even if you don't end up playing it, the game has one of the most charmingly upbeat songs we've heard in a slot for a good long time. Fruity Megaways' gameplay boils down to waiting for enough consecutive tumbles to hit to trigger the Pick Me feature or enough scatters to progress to free spins. Not a lot happened in between, which meant quite a lot of downtime. Once free spins trigger, again, it's largely a case of trying to get as many consecutive tumbles to occur to progress through the Bonus Builder feature.It means if you're gaga for games which perk up when enough tumbles have occurred, then Fruity Megaways might be right up your street. One slightly disappointing aspect, though, is Fruity Megaways' meagre (for a Megaways game) winning potential of 5,000x the bet. However, with everything else that's going on in Fruity Megaways, it doesn't feel like players will be sparking up this fruit game to chase down the biggest wins in online slots.

Title: Sleepy Grandpa
review: Sleepy Grandpa: Slot OverviewYou know, despite the huge amount of things to do on this planet, watch telly, read a book, ride a bike, drink a beverage, wingsuit flying, it's hard to beat a good old nap. When it's warm and cosy inside, there's nothing on your schedule, and your eyelids are getting heavy, what could be better than letting go of the waking world and drifting away to the land of nod? If you're a fan of slumbering, you're not alone because the main character of Backseat Gaming's slot Sleepy Grandpa, is partial to naps, too. Fortunately, he doesn't spend the whole game in siesta mode. He also takes part in digging up Coin symbols worth up to 1,000x each, potentially boosted in the bonus round where a Global Multiplier of up to x10 increases any win.If there is one location that almost always looks like a nice place to be in an online slot, it's down on the farm. Providers are keen to portray this side of life as sunnily as possible, almost as if there's no hard work involved, it never rains, food grows itself, and everything exists in wonderful pastoral harmony (Rabbit Royale from ELK Studios is one possible exception). So it is in Sleepy Grandpa, which packs in a red barn, some green green grass, happy animals, a windmill, and a cheerfully cloudy sky. The soundtrack is equally cheerful, and the finishing touch is Grandpa himself, happily snoozing on a bench with a mud-covered shovel in hand. So content does this man look, we might have to join him for a few zzz's…Sleepy Grandpa slot - base gameHmm, maybe later. For now, let's pick a bet instead where the options vary from 10 p/c to $/€100. Alternatively, players can choose the bonus buy, which provides one option – free spins for the cost of 100 times the bet. Playing in the usual mode attracts a default RTP of 96.23%, or when buying free spins, the return increases to 96.39%. With a medium volatile math model, no matter how you play, Sleepy Grandpa has a hit frequency of 37.5% and takes place on a 5-reel, 4-row grid matrix with 26 paylines.For symbol payout info, Sleepy Grandpa has nine regular paying symbols. The low-value lot are 10 to A card ranks, worth up to 1.2 to 1.8 times the bet for 5 OAK, while the high pay bunch are a chicken, a sheep, a pig, and a cow paying 6 to 10 times the bet for a 5 OAK win. Sleepy Grandpa doesn't have wild symbols in its base or bonus game, but it has a couple more special symbols to help inject excitement.Sleepy Grandpa: Slot FeaturesSleepy Grandpa slot - free spins intro screenSleepy Grandpa's features also revolve around aspects of farming and include the Dig feature, the Tractor feature, and a bonus game.Dig FeatureWhen at least 1 Farmer symbol and at least 1 Dirt symbol land at the same time, the Farmer digs up the Dirt. This reveals a Coin symbol bearing a value of 1x-3x, 5x, 10x, 25x, 50x, 75x, 100x, 250x, 500x, or 1,000x and is added to the Farmer. One Farmer symbol per reel can land at the same time. If more than 1 Farmer symbol lands, each Farmer will dig up each Dirt symbol one time. When all Dirt symbols have been dug up, all Farmer symbol values are added together and awarded.Tractor FeatureIf a Farmer symbol or a Golden Farmer land on the reels but no Dirt symbols land at the same time, there is a chance the Tractor feature triggers. When it activates, the Tractor ploughs the field and removes all symbols except scatter symbols or Farmer/Golden Farmer symbols already present. The Tractor will leave 1 to 10 Dirt symbols behind it, triggering the Dig feature. Tractors are present in the base and bonus game.Bonus GameLanding 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols in the base game awards 10, 12, or 15 free spins, respectively. Only one scatter symbol can land on each reel. In the bonus game, there is a chance the Gold Farmer symbol lands – only one can appear in a bonus game. The Golden Farmer is sticky, so it stays on the reels till the bonus game ends, triggering the Dig feature whenever Dirt symbols land.The bonus game also has a Global Multiplier with levels of x2, x3, x5, and x10. Each level has 4 empty slots that are filled by landing Farmer symbols. If a Golden Farmer is on the grid, it fills one slot on each spin. When 4 slots are filled, the Global Multiplier levels up to the next multiplier level. Each time the Global Multiplier levels up, +3 free spins are awarded. The Global Multiplier applies to all wins and to all Coins that are dug up.Sleepy Grandpa slot - free spinsSleepy Grandpa: Slot VerdictSo far, the partnership between Backseat Gaming and Hacksaw Gaming has been a rather fruitful one, as the slots the younger studio has been turning out haven't been bad at all. A bit on the simple side compared with its more established, dare we say more competent partner, but there's nothing wrong with starting somewhere modest, and finding your feet, before really going haywire. Sleepy Grandpa is a good example. It's a pleasant-looking and sounding slot with one or two interesting gaming elements to help you and Grandpa keep your eyelids open and stave off sleep.Not saying Sleepy Grandpa is a sleep-inducing game. It's a sort of mix of Fat Rabbit since tractors can turn up useful symbols in a similar vein to the Harvest feature and Fishin' Frenzy/Big Bass Bonanza. Really, it's like a farmyard version of a classic fish-themed money symbol collection game, so let's thank Backseat Gaming for using a different topic rather than sending players out to sea, again, for the millionth time. As such, for players in the frame of mind for a game that delivers Coin symbols, with rather large potential values, alongside a collection system but have had a gutful of fish, then Sleepy Grandpa could be the remedy. What makes triggering the bonus game attractive is not just the Global Multiplier (which applies to all wins, not just Coin collects) is the chance to hit a Golden Farmer, increasing the game's originality.If one was needed, the final incentive might be Sleepy Grandpa's winning potential of 10,000x the bet. Not a major eye-popping number in this day and age, but for a money collection game of this style, it's quite high. Certainly high enough to keep even the sleepiest gambler wide awake if they won it, or at least give them something to dream about achieving while dozing.

Title: Hugo's Adventure
review: Hugo's Adventure (Play'n GO): OverviewIn 1987, two Danish guys named Ivan Sølvason and Niels Krogh Mortensen came up with a groundbreaking idea - they were going to create an interactive video game TV Show that would allow viewers to interact with the live broadcast by controlling the character in the game with their telephones without delay. Having developed a fully functional custom-built system as well as the character of Hugo, the concept was eventually realized in 1990. Hugo went on to become a massive hit, eventually turned into a franchise and licensed to over 40 TV-channels around the world. Those of you who were around when it all unfolded can probably still remember all the frustrated kids trying to make the disobedient Hugo go in the direction they so badly wanted, frantically pressing those telephone buttons.Since then, media franchise Hugo has been included in numerous video games, apps, books, movies and even rap albums. Thanks to Swedish software developer Play'n GO, he's also the host of several casino games. While the first slot to feature Hugo was strictly based on the TV show, the follow-ups allowed us to see the friendly little troll in various other settings. In Hugo 2, for example, he was a locomotive driver, and in Hugo Goal, we got to see him as a rather useless goalkeeper. Out of these titles, Hugo 2 is the only one we can actually recommend, albeit none of them have been particularly good.In the fourth instalment titled Hugo's Adventure, Hugo's world has expanded. It comes with a bonus game where you'll see him dive to the deepest depths in search of treasures, and a free spins feature that takes him to dizzying heights. Highly volatile, the game is played using a layout of 5 reels and 10 fixed paylines while accepting bets from between 0.10 to $/€100 per spin.Every time a new Hugo slot comes out, debates arise regarding the childish theme which some feel is distasteful. In an age where the casino industry is slowly being choked to death by an increasing set of rules, it's either brave or crazy of Play'n GO to release a game like this. Regardless of all that, it's hard to deny that Hugo's Adventure looks fun. While the artwork is similar as in the other games, there are, of course, new settings to explore here. With a picture-perfect paradise backdrop, symbols on the reels include A to 10 card suits as well as the more rewarding monkey repairman, eagle pilot, and stewardess Hugolina. Hugo himself is the most lucrative, giving you 50 times your stake for a five of a kind combination.Hugo's Adventure (Play'n GO): FeaturesThe Underwater Adventure bonus in actionThere are two features included in Hugo's Adventure. The first one is the Underwater Adventure bonus pick game which comes into play when 2 submarine bonus scatters appear on reels 2 and 4 simultaneously. Next, you get to choose undersea treasures - these can reveal either cash prizes or take away one life. At the end of the bonus you will get one spin on the submarine multiplier for each life you have left. This gives you a chance to accumulate a multiplier of up to 20x, which is then applied to your total winnings from the bonus game.Things heat up when you land 3 airplane scatter symbols on reels 1, 3 and 5 which will grant you access to the Air Ace Free Spins feature. Starting with 9 spins and 1 life, keep an eye out for +1 heart balloon symbols as this will add an extra life to your total. If, on the other hand, Hugo is hit with an air mine, it will reduce his life by 1. There are also extra spins to be won up to a total of 20.There's more to the free spins feature than that, however. Finishing the free spins round with one or several lives left will automatically grant you access to the Underwater Adventure feature.Hugo's Adventure (Play'n GO): VerdictHugo's Adventure is the most volatile Hugo slot to date and also the best in the series, which isn't really much of an achievement we might add. As typically is the case with these slots, the bonus game is just a filler to spice things up a bit. In reality, it's all about the free spins game which is quite fun actually. Not only is it surprisingly entertaining, but the potential is also excellent, offering up a chance to pocket up to 5000 times your stake.If you enjoyed the other Hugo games, you will probably like this one even more. Even if you're not a fan of the ugly Scandinavian troll, the game is definitely worth a shot as the potential is good and the features well thought out. Unless you find the cartoon graphics disturbing, of course.Don't MissIf you happen to be a fan of the charming little troll, there are plenty of more entries in the Hugo series, such as Hugo Cart which comes bundled with 4 base game features and free spins in which you can unlock additional characters.

Title: PapayaPop
review: PapayaPop: Slot OverviewDeveloper Avatar UX invites players to get all glammed up for a night out in their Art Deco themed game PapayaPop. As the name suggests, this is another instalment in their popular PopWins driven range of slots, in collaboration with Yggdrasil Gaming. Scott Fitzgerald novel of the age. 'I was within and without, simultaneously enchanted and repelled by the inexhaustible variety of life' as expressed by the main character. PapayaPop certainly has a sparkle, and the choice to use exotic fruits for symbols instead of the usual cherries or plums lot was a wise move.Getting 1920s chic is possible on any device from smartphones to desktops, while bets range from 20 p/c to $/€40 per spin. This process extends reels upwards and increases ways to win. In the base game, reels can reach 6 positions high at the most, meaning up to 7,776 ways are in play, or 15,552 since it pays both ways. When no new wins appear in a sequence, the grid resets back to its regular size.However, if all reels reach 6 rows high in the base game, free spins with an x2 multiplier are awarded. Before they begin, players can collect or gamble them to potentially start with up to 6,250 ways and an x5 multiplier. To do so, you spin a Gamble Wheel, which will forfeit free spins if it stops on a non-winning segment.The bonus round does not have a set number of free spins, starting with 3 lives instead. Non-winning spins remove a life, while wins reset the counter back to three. Hit zero lives, and the bonus round ends. The grid can now increase up to 9 reels in height in free spins, boasting 118,098 ways to win. Also, the grid resets to the lowest reel height instead of its starting size between free spins. Therefore, if all reels reach nine rows high, the game will stay that way for the rest of the feature.In addition, the win multiplier increases by +1 after each free spin, whether there was a win or not. If the grid reaches its full 9-row size, the multiplier increments by +2 instead, with no enforced upper limit.One more feature before we go is the Bonus Buy option. Hit the button to pay 75x the stake to buy free spins. Players can gamble to improve the starting size and multiplier as before or collect to head straight in with the x2 multiplier/ 486 starting ways. For those who prefer to wait, or can't access the feature buy, free spins trigger every 197 spins on average.PapayaPop: Slot VerdictPapayaPop provides players with a conventional run-through of what PopWins is all about. In some ways, it feels like PapayaPop was hurried off the line not to further the series but just to keep the brand in the public eye lest it fades into obscurity. It's just that since PapayaPop does nothing to move the range on, it feels like padding rather than evolution.It's not to say PapayaPop won't entertain players up for a bout of PopWins in an Art Deco-styled game. In fact, PapayaPop's is one of the weakest when it comes to potential, not that there is an abundance of footage evidencing players hitting max wins on any of the PopWins games, though.To sum up, PapayaPop is capable of producing fine moments, and it's as slick as any other PopWins game. It is a little disappointing that Avatar UX didn't put a lot of thought into the features, relying on brand recognition and fancy styling to carry the game.

Title: Gold Volcano
review: Gold Volcano: OverviewDeveloper Play’n GO flexes its grid slot muscle in the lava flowing game Gold Volcano. Title: Wild Walker
review: Wild Walker: OverviewThere was a time, not too long ago when you couldn't open a magazine or switch on the telly and not see a zombie lurching towards you. The trend has cooled somewhat recently, though the decaying species still pops up occasionally. Developer Pragmatic Play attempts to revive the undead love affair in their slot Wild Walker. The title isn't just a clever name either, but one that describes the most regular feature in the game. Players also get extra reels during free spins, where the expanded wilds really come into their own.Pragmatic Play has gone to town on the graphics, particularly the animations. For one, the full reel zombies bob around like dancing Fortnite characters; it's a shame Pragmatic didn't sneak the 'Floss' in there somewhere. Wild Walker's 5-reel, 25-payline grid finds itself in the midst of the zombie apocalypse that authors and movie producers warned was just around the corner. It means burnt-out cars, lightning, rain, buzzards, the whole end of the world scene. The soundtrack is an interesting one too, alternating between laid back when not much is happening, revving up to a sort of late 80s/ 90s funk metal piece. The Faith No More-ish track adds just the right dash of weirdness to lighten the theme.Wild Walker may be played on any device, by choosing bets from 25 p/c to $/€125 per spin. Five lightning bolts on the homepage when the game loads warn players these zombies aren't here to play. Expect a highly volatile game that can be hard going. You might think a constantly roaming wild would offer some relief, but it often isn't the case. Overall, a decent default RTP rating of 96.55% evens things out in the long run. Things can get messy (in a good way) during free spins too, with the extra reels, longer combinations, and additional zombie wilds involved.Reels max out at 5 in the base game, rising to a possible 8 in the bonus, seriously affecting the symbol values. As to symbols, J-A royals make up the lows, while test tubes and needle guns are the two mids. Four character symbols are used for the high pays worth 4.8 to 20 times the stake during the base game. However, open up all 8 reels in free spins for game-changing payouts of 80 to 400x the bet.Wild Walker: FeaturesWild Walker - free spins with additional reels unlockedWild Walker comes with two features - expanded roaming wilds and free spins. The expanded wandering wild is a 1x3 full reel sized symbol that substitutes for anything except the bonus. This wild is present on every spin, switching to a randomly selected reel covering all three positions. Wilds also payout when adjacent – 1.2x for three or 6x for four in a row.As well as the wandering wild feature there are progressive free spins. The skull in gas mask image is the scatter which appears on all reels. When 3 or 4 are in view players win 8 free spins starting at the first or second level respectively.Players are treated to a cut scene between base and bonus game where several zombies mince past like a bunch of 'Thriller' extras. Free spins are held inside a lab, presumably where the anti-zombie juice is concocted. As well as the change in scenery, locked reels are added, in a 4 level bonus game:Level 1: 5 active reels + one expanded roaming wild symbol.Level 2: 6 active reels + one expanded wild locked on reel 1 and one expanded roaming wild.Level 3: 7 active reels + 2 expanded wilds locked on reels 1-2, and one expanded roaming wild.Level 4: 8 active reels + 3 expanded wilds locked on reels 1-3, and one expanded roaming wild.Every 3 scatters collected in the feature unlocks the next level and awards 2 free spins. When all reels are unlocked, players keep collecting scatters, so every 3 collected adds 2 more free spins, without limit.Wild Walker: VerdictWild Walker is an entertaining zombie slot from Pragmatic Play that has several compelling aspects contributing to the playability. Number one is the fab look. Pragmatic injected a nice video game quality, evidenced in the animations of the roaming wild and the thick atmosphere generated by the background image. There's plenty of life to it, odd considering the undead subject matter, and the soundtrack helps create an immersive game world to get lost in for a bit. It's well done, there is a sort of Lost Vegas vibe but a more industrial part of town thing rather than The Strip.The gameplay shines a lot brighter in some parts than others. The base game, for instance, gets a little tedious once the initial impact wears off. At first, an expanded roaming wild on every single spin feels quite generous. It's the type of feature you expect to see in a triggered phase of play. The problem is the wild doesn't seem to contribute much. If it wasn't there, and reels spun regularly, it's unlikely the hit rate would be much, if any, different.Occasionally the wild appears in just the right place for a decent win, yet more often than not it leaps around not accomplishing much. Also, its bulky size scatter-blocks a whole reel, reducing the chance of three landing to activate the bonus.However, once free spins are triggered, the expanded wilds come into their own. Not so much at the lower levels, though when wilds are locked, and longer combos are possible, things get pretty tense. Maxing Wild Walker out means wins of 4,900 times the bet are possible. Not an immense amount for a Pragmatic Play slot, yet one which feels more realistic, and achievable, than their oft-claimed and questionable astronomical figures.To sum up, Wild Walker is a nicely playable Pragmatic slot. It's got a great look, an eccentric soundtrack, and some epic moments on the reels. Well, in the bonus game at least. Does it do enough to knock Lost Vegas off the podium as best zombie slot? Probably not, but a fine effort all the same.

Title: Highway to Hell
review: Highway to Hell: Slot OverviewAccording to the Neil Young lyrics, 'It's better to burn out than to fade away', but is it, really? Perhaps the answer to that question depends to an extent on age, current life stage, and general temperament. When we're young, before the responsibilities of family, mortgage, and kids creep in, shoot, the sky's the limit, it's easy to throw caution to the wind and give in to peer pressure to impress the crowd. After all, if bones heal and cuts scar, it might be easy for someone to think they're bulletproof. However, few to none of us are invulnerable to life in the long run, so for a little taste of livin' on the edge, throwing it all away on a dice roll, how about we get our motors runnin' with developer Nolimit City's reckless slot Highway to Hell?The chaps in Highway to Hell look as though they may have broken out of hell as much as heading towards it. This is because instead of flesh and skin-coated human beings, the bike riders are skeleton characters instead. They're a bit like the flaming skull guy from Marvel's Ghost Rider, where Johnny Blaze made a deal with the arch-demon Mephisto to save his foster father's life. There's no Johny Blaze or Mephisto in this game, though, which centres on the MC Hellbound motorcycle gang as they raise hell on the open road in a back-of-nowhere USA-type setting while dodging the law. Though, what the cops are going to do with a group of undead hellraisers is anyone's guess.Highway to Hell slot - base gameHighway to Hell is played on a 6x4 gaming area with locked Enhancer Cells covering the bottom positions on the four middle reels. Symbols from winning combinations explode off the reels, allowing new symbols to drop in to replace them, repeating this way until no new win appears. By default, there are 1,296 ways to win, but this number increases as Enhancer Cells are unlocked and symbols on the grid are split. The volatility is high, and of the four RTP options, 96.03% being the highest. As is usually the case, Highway to Hell provides a wide variety of ways to gamble, though base bet selection is 20 c to $/€100.Flaming dice, a flaming playing card, a 13 of spades, a flaming skull, and a demonic face are Highway to Hell's low-pay symbols, while 5 skeletal character symbols are the premiums. Six-of-a-kind winning combinations are worth 0.3x to 0.6x the bet if made up of low pays or 1x to 2x the bet for the highs.Highway to Hell: Slot FeaturesHighway to Hell slot -free spinsThe features in Highway to Hells are its Avasplit Effect, wilds, xNudge Wilds, Enhancer Cells, Demon symbols, xWays, xSplit, Hell Spins, Extra Spins, Boosters, and bonus buys.Avasplit EffectWhen winning symbols explode, some remaining symbols are randomly selected for the Avasplit Effect, which increases their symbol size by +1.Wilds & xNudge WildsRegular wilds and xNudge Wilds may land on any reel, substituting any regular paying symbol. If just a part of an xNudge Wild lands, it nudges up or down until it's fully stacked. Each nudge increases the xNudge Wild multiplier by +1. If a nudged-over symbol has a multiplier, its value is added to the xNudge Wild multiplier. It will not nudge down on a locked Enhancer position. An xNudge may get a higher starting multiplier if it comes from a Hellevator Booster that already has a multiplier.Enhancer CellsWith each win, an Enhancer Cell position is unlocked from left to right, revealing a symbol when unlocked. If the revealed symbol is removed, a new symbol appears in its position on the next avalanche.DemonWhen a Demon lands, it removes a random number of symbols from the reels, though symbols larger than size 1 cannot be removed. The Demon then transforms into a random regular pay symbol holding a multiplier equal to the number of symbols it removed. If no symbol is removed, it transforms into a regular pay symbol with a multiplier of x1.xWaysAn xWays symbol transforms into a regular pay symbol or wild. It reveals 2 to 4 symbols of a matching type, thereby increasing the number of ways to win. If more than one xWays symbol lands, all of them reveal the same symbol.Highway to Hell slot - free spinsxSplitAn xSplit symbol splits all symbols on its reel, doubling the symbol size and converting itself into a wild. xSplits split all other symbols except scatters.Hell SpinsHitting 3 scatters or Hellevator Boosters in the base game awards 8 free spins. If a Hellevator Booster lands during the bonus trigger or during the bonus round, it persists on the reels throughout the round.The Hellevator Booster reveals a random symbol and cannot be removed by a Demon symbol. If the revealed symbol is part of a win, it is removed and a new symbol is revealed on the next avalanche. It appears that the Avasplit Effect increases the Hellevator multiplier, and when the Hellevator Booster gets a multiplier, its value is stored and progresses throughout the bonus feature. If an xNudge increases the Hellevator Booster's multiplier, the boost lasts for the current spin before returning to its previous value when the spin ends. Enhancer symbols reset on each spin.Landed scatters are collected during free spins to progress the scatter meter. When 3 scatters are collected, +2 spins are awarded, and a Hellevator Booster is added to the reels from the next spin. The scatter meter resets after collecting 3 scatters.Extra SpinWhen Hell Spins end, players may have the chance to buy an additional spin that keeps the Hellevator multiplier of the previous spin.Nolimit Booster & Bonus BuyxBet costs 2.4x the base bet, guaranteeing a scatter symbol on the leftmost reels, while Bonus Hunt at 15x lands valueless blank symbols, scatters, or Hellevator Boosters. Players may buy free spins triggered by 3 scatters for 60x or a free spins trigger including 1, 2, or 3 Hellevator Boosters for 100x, 180x, or 350x the bet, respectively. A 30%/20%/30%/20% Lucky Draw bonus costs 162x the bet. The other bonus buy is God Mode at 3,800x, which provides a chance to land the max win on a single spin.Highway to Hell slot - bonus buy menuHighway to Hell: Slot VerdictUnless you're a Marvel reader, skeletons riding motorcycles might not be something you see every day, but if you're a gambler, then a lot of the mechanics in Highway to Hell will probably seem familiar. The reason being, Nolimit City has stuffed a lot of its goto features into Highway to Hell. This includes favourites such as xNudge Wilds, Enhancers Cells, and xSplits. Doing so might not set the highway alight with ingenuity, but they're solid features which are able to enhance the slots they're a part of. Speaking of Enhancer Cells, while reading the rules, it was interesting to see there wasn't such a written focus on landing special feature symbols in them as there has been in previous slots like San Quentin 2 Death Row or Mental 2, for example, though you can still do so when the game is in play.Instead, one of the main focuses here seems to be on splitting or xWaying the deuce out of the reels to cram as many symbols onto the reels as possible in order to nudge closer to the game's 20,066x the bet max win. If you're lucky, splits and increasing ways take place alongside xNudge Wild multipliers, Demon multipliers, or multipliers on symbols in general. The Avasplit Effect is a new one (where that name came from might be interesting to know), and it amplifies Highway to Hell's ability to split symbols on the reels. It's totally random, so you never know where the chopping up of symbols may occur. When turning attention to free spins, obviously reels heavy with Hellevator Boosters racking up multipliers are what you want to see.Whilst Nolimit City might not have brought its freakiest innovations to bear in Highway to Hell, it's a slot full of good ideas, some of them worth a definite look-see for fans of the studio's output, such as the xZone-ish Demon symbol. The Extra Spin, too, the likes of which Relax Gaming used in Wild Yield, might interest players keen on testing their luck post-feature. On the whole, Highway to Hell felt like coming together of Nolimit City features in an arguably less-suspenseful Punk Rocker 2 type of game that scratches the splitting, waying, and nudging itch without necessarily revolutionising it.

Title: Wild Toro
review: Wild Toro: Slot OverviewBeing a Matador has to be one of the most daring occupations around. Stepping in the ring with a raging black bull, let alone getting up close enough to feel the wind rush through your hair as they rush past, takes a brave soul indeed. If you've ever wanted a taste of the action without the worry of being gored by a stray horn, then ELK Studios has you covered in their slot, Wild Toro. Wild Toro captures some of the energy found in the bull ring, funnelling it through three fun bonus features, putting players on the road to wins in excess of 2,000x the bet.You might think Wild Toro uses more than just 5 reels and 4 rows the way the grid completely takes over the screen. It is partly transparent, though, and beneath is a quant Spanish square where bullfights were known to take place as the inhabitants crowded around their hero to cheer them on. The big, bold symbols match the zest for life Spain is known for, while a sultry Iberian soundtrack provides the finishing touch on a rather festive scene.Players may set bets from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin when playing Wild Toro or activate one of four betting strategies pre-programmed by the ELK team. Any device is suitable for hosting the game, which possesses a math model running on a medium volatile setting, producing a return to player value of 96.40%.To win, players need to line up at least three matching symbols adjacent to each other from the first reel. There are 178 connecting win lines to land winning combinations on, lighting up successful symbols when they hit. Six symbols make up the regular paying tiles, starting with three lower value bronze, silver and gold coins worth 0.5 to 0.8 times the bet for five of a kind. Moving up, we find elaborately made fans, dagger thrusted oranges, and a rose as the three premium symbols. These ones are worth payouts of 2 to 10 times the stake for a five symbol winning combination. A couple of wilds appear on Wild Toro; one is a standard logo wild appearing anywhere on the grid to substitute all symbols except the Matador and Toro symbol. These we cover next.Wild Toro: Slot FeaturesWannabe matadors will come across three features in Wild Toro. Each one has the opportunity of overlapping the other, and are called Toro Walking Wilds, a Matador Respin Challenge, and the Toro Goes Wild Bonus.First up is Toro, the bull symbol, which appears on the rightmost reel, triggering the Toro Walking Wild feature when it lands. Toro moves reel by reel to the left, triggering a respin for every move. The feature continues until Toro falls off the leftmost reel, then accrued wins are paid out.If, during the Toro Walking Wild feature, a matador symbol lands (named Senor Diaz Jr), the Toro Goes Wild Bonus Game is triggered. When this happens, Toro gets mad and charges at all Matadors in sight, leaving a trail of wild symbols behind him for the next respin. When all of the Matadors on the grid have been defeated, Toro returns back to his Toro Walking Wild position to continue the feature. Only one Toro at a time can attack Matadors in this manner.Should 3 Matador symbols hit on the middle reels on the same spin, the Matador Respin Challenge is triggered. Matador symbols turn sticky during this feature, and a respin is awarded for each Matador. Senor Diaz Jr taunts the bull during this feature, increasing the chance of Toro hitting on the last reel. New Matador symbols award another respin, and the feature ends when respins are used, or Toro appears, launching the Toro Goes Wild Bonus.Wild Toro: Slot VerdictEven though ELK went on to design more complex slots, offering intricate features and big winning potential, Wild Toro remains one of their most popular slots. After a playthrough, it's not difficult to see why. The team has created a warm environment to dodge bulls in, painting an attractive village scene and filling it with big personalities. The connector pays is a good one too, being not quite paylines, not quite pay all ways, but a happy middle ground that does a good job of pulling together winning combinations.The interplaying trio of features is the star attraction of Wild Toro, however. Both leading characters are full of charisma, and ELK spent a lot of time getting them just right. For example, it took ten attempts to get Senor Diaz Jr's frightened look the way they wanted it. This attention to detail is obvious, making Wild Toro that much more enjoyable to play. It might take time for special symbols to hit to start piling up coins, plus there are no free spins, so patience is required at times to get to the good stuff.However, features can extend each other when the right symbols land at the right time, producing fairly lengthy bonus sequences. For example, Toro Walking Wild respins can lead into the Toro Goes Wild Bonus Game, and bulls end up chasing matadors, leaving wilds all over the place. Potential isn't huge by modern standards, but healthy wins of up to 2,250x the bet are achievable when Toro and Senor Diaz Jr really start to face off against each other.For a touch of sunny Spain that can turn up the excitement when bulls and matadors duel, Wild Toro is an enticing option. It oozes charm, is fairly easygoing despite being highly volatile, and has its moments when special symbols hit.Don't MissIf you enjoyed what the original Wild Toro had to offer, be sure to check out the sequel, Wild Toro 2 which comes with upgraded mechanics and crisp creatives. As well as the sequel, ELK has also expanded the Toro brand with Book of Toro and Toro 7s.

Title: The Wild Machine
review: The Wild Machine Slot: OverviewSlots from prolific developer Pragmatic Play have been a lucky dip of late. It’s not a holdout though, a generous default RTP of 96.52% and solid potential ensures that it is capable of decent payouts when it is warming up.The Wild Machine Slot: FeaturesFree spins screenThe Wild Machine is not the most busy of all slots in terms of features, but there is still a whole lot going on due to all the moving parts. When that happens, the 5x5 grid transforms into the 1-3-5-7-3-1 configuration with reels 1, 4, and 7 completely wild. This lasts for one spin and resets in preparation for the next.During the base game, scatters can appear on reels 2, 3, and 4. When 3 land, they trigger the Wonder Wheel feature. This wheel is split into 30 slices with batches of 5 cash prize segments separated by segments of free spins. If the wheel stops on a cash prize, it can keeping moving and collect up to five prizes with one spin. If it lands on Free Spins, then the Free Spins Feature is triggered. The wheel cannot award cash prizes and free spins on the same spin.If free spins are triggered, then players can opt to play one of the following two bonuses:Gold Foundry Free Spins – this round comes with 8 free spins and uses the 5x5 format. On every spin, between 2 and 5 reels are randomly selected to become completely wild.Diamond Forge Free Spins – this round has 5 free spins and uses the 1-3-5-7-5-3-1 format. During this round reels 1, 4, and 7 are always wild, and any new wild symbol that lands remains sticky for the duration of the feature.There is no information on whether or not one bonus is more volatile than the other, but the maximum potential is likely the same. Worth noting is that free spins cannot be retriggered in either of the two bonus games.The Wild Machine Slot: VerdictThe Wild Machine is a slot that ticks several of the right boxes. It's well designed and has a nice flow that makes it quite playable. What helps is that scatters are numerous and trigger the Wonder Wheel quite frequently. When the game runs hot, free spins rain down like candy in a lolly scramble. When it’s cold, the pointer only ever stops on the prize money. Either outcome helps keep enthusiasm, not to mention bankrolls, buoyant, extending the game’s shelf life.The Wild Machine isn’t one of those volatile Pragmatic slots that batter you into submission with endless waves of dead spins before deigning you worthy of a feature. Free spins are rarer than instant cash prizes, as you might expect, but still, you know you are going to win something with the Wonder Wheel which is always a nice feeling.So when free spins do tick over the question is which one to go for? The Diamond Forge comes with fewer spins but seemed to work out best. The key is to land a few lucky wilds in useful positions early and watch the repeat winners stack up with each consecutive spin. In saying that, the Gold Foundry could work well when several wild reels turn up in the right place too. How well? At full potential players spin for wins of up to 7,000 times the stake. Title: Mighty Stallion
