If it already has 7 symbols, no effect occurs.During the round, the 2 revealed modifiers are delivered when the relevant Bonus Coins fall onto the grid. Free spins have an unlimited win multiplier starting at 1 and increasing after each reaction. Landing 2 scatter symbols awards a further +2 free spins, plus 2 free spins are granted for each additional scatter beyond the second.Bonus BuyPlayers can fast forward the mission to the bonus round by buying 10 free spins for 100x the bet or 15 free spins for 200x their bet. The RTP when buying the bonus round is 96.36%.Max Megaways 3 slot - free spinsMax Megaways 3: Slot VerdictPlayers may well have mixed feelings about the return of the Megadozer. It might be great for anyone who likes the arcade references, Meh-gadozer for the haters. Since this feature is so central to Max Megaways 3, it could end up being a make-or-break moment. Its inclusion didn't exactly cause Danger High Voltage 2 to shine any brighter, after all. The Megadozer felt more relevant to the rest of what Max Megaways 3 does than it did in DHV2, though. Perhaps titanically unmet expectations over the sequel to the beloved Danger High Voltage contributed to much of the negative response to the dozer effect in that game.Whilst the mechanic is still unlikely to take over the world like a particularly successful supervillain, in Max Megaways 3, the dozer-dropping effect wasn't bad. During free spins, it helps deliver a similar set of modifiers as Bonanza Falls, with the addition of the Increase ways symbol. Dozing is available in the base game, too, which is no bad thing. It adds depth, especially since the features are not limited in number as they are in free spins. The overall gameplay fits the series quite well since the previous Max Megaways games were also all about base game bonuses and picking doors to reveal free spin bonuses. Just now the delivery system has been altered.What hasn't been altered is the chance to tap into some serious winning potential, though Max Megaways 3 is the least impressive of the trio. Still, 86,800x in the base game and 101,830x in the bonus round are impressive numbers (on paper, at least) that help give the 'Max' part of the title extra heft while providing wannabe secret agents with a big round target to aim at.

Title: Victoria Wild
review: Victoria Wild: OverviewDeveloper TrueLab takes players on an adventure with a dashing young explorer in the action-themed slot Victoria Wild. Powered by Yggdrasil Gaming courtesy of their YGS Masters program, Victoria Wild is decked out in three different wilds, a collection system, and several unique free spins locations.Before diving into the game, TrueLab provides a backstory to help broaden the experience. The hero of the tale, Victoria, has the task of conquering a drought-ridden desert, on her hunt for treasures. Okay, that’s about it, but despite the scant details, TrueLab has crafted quite an enjoyable world for players to immerse themselves in. Victoria is a likeable sort, while the map on what would be the sixth reel provides a certain sense of exploration.The game refers to ‘the desert’ though there are no clues as to where in the world it might be. A vulture bobs away on the right side of the screen, while the grid is surrounded by dead trees, bricks and old timber. One clue could be the buildings in the back which look like those mud structures in Mali with the sticks poking out. But still, we could be anywhere hot and dusty. Not that it really makes a whole lot of difference.The soundtrack is one of the game’s highlights. Players are treated to an orchestral piece that brought to mind the Sci-Fi film Stargate which was incidentally set on a desert world. The music piles on the drama, completing the action-adventure feel.Playable across all devices, its 5-reel, 3-row game area is glued together by 15 fixed paylines. Players choose the value of each line from 0.01 to 12 coins, resulting in total stakes of 15 p/c to $/€180 per spin. Continuing our investigation under the hood reveals a medium volatile math model and a fairly generous RTP rating of 96.55%.TrueLab has split the 9 regular symbols into 4 low, 4 medium, and 1 high pay. All are exploration-based, starting on the low pays which are the four points of a compass – N, E, S, and W. Each one has the same value of 3x the bet for five of a kind, rising to 15x for six. The mediums consist of a canteen, boots, a motorbike, and a handgun. This lot is worth up to 9x the bet for a line of five, or 45x for six of a kind.Lastly, Victoria is the high symbol worth 24x for five of a kind, 120x for six of a kind. We’re only mentioning both values since for the majority of the time five reels are in play, yet an extra reel is added during Oasis Free Spins to see the comparison. The standard tornado wild has the same value as the Victoria symbol, while also being able to substitute for any regular pay symbol.Victoria Wild: FeaturesVictoria Wild - free spinsVictoria Wild is built around a collection system that culminates in Oasis Free Spins. Along the way, players benefit from a Sandstorm feature, Tornado Respins, and Lost Temple free spins.Whenever 2 or more wilds are present on the reels during the base game, the Sandstorm feature is triggered. Here, 2, 3, 4 or 5 wilds in view award 5-8, 9-12, 13-15, or 15 Sandstorm spins respectively. On each of these spins, a jumping tornado wild leaps from position to position. Keep in mind these spins are not free.If a jumping tornado wild lands on a regular tornado wild the Sticky Wild Respin feature is triggered. During the respin, all wilds hold their places, including the jumping wild. If a new wild appears, it holds its place as well, and another respin occurs. The sticky wild respin feature ends when no new wilds appear.Next up is Temple Free Spins, triggered when 3 or more temple scatters appear on the reels. The more the merrier, so 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters award 8, 10, 12 or 15 Temple Spins respectively. What you want to see during this bonus round are wild lamp symbols. If 7 or more lamps are collected, the Secret Treasury bonus is activated when free spins end.In the Secret Treasury feature, a wheel spins, awarding one prize. This could be a 250 – 2,500 coin win, or a multiplier of x2 – x25 applied to the total amount won during Temple Free Spins. There is also a pretty lame booby prize on the wheel where you win nothing if you land on it.Lastly, is the Oasis Free Spins round. During the game, a map next to the reels displays Victoria’s progress. Each Oasis symbol that lands moves her one step closer to her goal. When 25 symbols have been collected, 10 Oasis Free Spins are awarded.A 6th reel is added for Oasis Free Spins expanding the grid to 6x3, though the number of paylines remains the same. During this feature, waterfall wilds appear on reels 2, 3, 4 or 5. When they land, they expand to cover the whole reel.Victoria Wild: VerdictThere is quite a lot to like about this heroine-led slot. Victoria Wild is a game with a lot going on from low-level wins to mid-grade modifiers to larger bonus games. This helps keep your mind off the map as you plod towards triggering the mythical Oasis Free Spins. To be honest, during testing we had more luck during Temple Free Spins due to a surprisingly good multiplier from the Secret Treasury bonus wheel. The multiple winning opportunities ensure solid wins are possible in Victoria Wild whichever way you cut it.Get Vicky swinging over ravines, fending off cobras, dodging tornadoes, or whatever it is an adventuress does and wins of up to 20,000 times the stake are possible. A figure most players will be able to get on board with, though the math model might be a less savoury prospect for some.As well as impressive numbers, TrueLab has made good use of the theme. It’s easy to bang on about going on a quest to build hype, but Victoria Wild does have a certain spirit to it. On a sensory level, the attractive graphics mixed with the stirring soundtrack imbue a healthy dose of adventure. From Sandstorms to respins and free spins, Victoria Wild offers plenty of sightseeing along the way.So while the volatility or the 15 payline format that TrueLab seems to favour may be off-putting for some, others will enjoy the visuals, the variety of features, and the quest-based nature of Victoria Wild, not to mention its massive potential.Don't MissThere is also an upgraded version titled Victoria Wild Deluxe, offering a bonus buy option as well as some feature tweaks.

Title: Masters Of Olympus
review: Masters of Olympus: Slot OverviewNordic studio Snowborn Games previously mastered Valhalla, or attempted to at least, and has now turned its attention from Norse Mythology to Mythology of an Ancient Greek nature. In other words, the follow-up to Masters of Valhalla is upon us in the form of Masters of Olympus, an online slot which borrows much from its predecessor while changing up one or two bits. Most has stayed the same technically, so players get Zeus Respins with expanding wilds, a Spartan Booster, and a hold 'n win bonus round with a bundle of special symbols flying about the place.High up on Olympus do we find ourselves when Masters of Olympus opens up. To the right are pastel-coloured mountain tops, and to the left stands Zeus holding a bolt of lightning before a Greco-styled structure. Snowborn Games has kept to the cartoonish style it used in Masters of Valhalla, imbuing Masters of Olympus with the same sort of lightness. Masters of Olympus does post some pretty impressive numbers, though, so while it might not look like a rugged Mythology slot, its features and stats are robust.Masters Of Olympus slot - base gameMore on the stats now, and one thing to look out for is Masters of Olympus' variety of RTP values. There are four, with the highest being 96.01%, so always check the paytable before hitting the spin button. Suitable for players that are into volatile gaming, players get a stake range of 10 p/c to $/€25 per spin. In the base game, Masters of Olympus' conducts business on a grid consisting of 5 columns of 4 symbols, with 1,024 ways to win.To create a win, three to five matching symbols must land from the leftmost side across adjacent reels. Doing so with five of the card suit symbols - diamonds, clubs, spades, or hearts triggers a payout of 1.1 to 1.2 times the stake. Hitting a five-of-a-kind premium win awards 2 to 3 times the bet when made up of Aphrodite, Apollo, Ares, or Athena. Lightning bolts also appear on the wild symbols, which substitute for all symbols except the bonus, to help create winning ways.Masters of Olympus: Slot FeaturesMasters Of Olympus slot - respin featureWhen wild symbols land, they are collected, granting a chance of triggering the Zeus Respins feature. When it is triggered, wild symbols on the reels expand the full reel down, and a respin takes place. On each new respin, the wild moves one position on the grid. If extra wild symbols land during this feature, they expand as well. The feature ends when no more wild symbols are in view.Zeus Respins – Coin CollectionCoin symbols landing during the feature are collected in a meter. Collecting 3 coin symbols during the feature awards the Olympus Bonus. However, if the Spartan Booster is full, the Spartan Bonus is instead awarded.Bonus SymbolAlternatively, another way of triggering the bonus round is by landing 3 bonus symbols on reels 1, 3, and 5. This will also trigger the Olympus Bonus or the Spartan Bonus if the Spartan Booster has been filled.Spartan BoosterBonus symbols landing on reels 1 and 3 are collected by the Spartan Booster. When filled, the next time the bonus is triggered, players will be awarded the Spartan Bonus rather than the Olympus Bonus. The difference is in the Olympus round, players get 3 respins; in the Spartan one, they get 4 respins.Olympus Bonus/Spartan BonusThis is a hold 'n win style bonus where the initially awarded number of respins are reset whenever a new symbol lands. Possible symbols are:Silver shield – possess a bet multiplier of 1-9x the bet.Gold shield – possess a bet multiplier of 10-50x the bet.Poseidon – has a multiplier value and also unlocks one of the two locked rows. Any symbols on unlocked rows are activated.Aphrodite – lands with a multiplier value which is used to multiply all symbols landing on that spin plus any following spin.Ares – lands with a multiplier value and collects the values of all symbols once on the spin it hits.Athena – lands with a multiplier value and collects the value of all symbols on the reels on that spin and each following spin.Zeus – lands with a multiplier value which gets added to all other symbols on the grid on that spin and each following spin.Apollo – lands with a multiplier value which is added to all other symbols on the grid once on the spin it hits.Hades – lands with a multiplier value and re-activates all Ares and Apollo symbols that landed on previous spins.Hot Spots – these randomly appear to indicate a higher chance of landing a non-silver or gold symbol.Buy BonusIf the bonus buy button is available in your region, clicking it lets you pick one of the three options. These are 50x the bet for the Olympus Bonus, 100x the bet for the Spartan Bonus, or 250x the bet for the Spartan Bonus with an Athena symbol on the grid from the first spin.Masters Of Olympus slot - free spinsMasters of Olympus: Slot VerdictPlaying Masters of Olympus was just as good as Masters of Valhalla was, if not a little bit better, for players who prefer to buy the most tricked-out bonus round they can. The Guaranteed Athena bonus buy is something that wasn't available in the previous game and proved to be quite fun during the review. Masters of Valhalla brought Money Train 2 to mind, whereas Master of Olympus feels more inspired by Money Train 3 as the Guaranteed Athena mirrored to a degree MT3's 500x bonus buy with the Persistent Symbol tacked on.Both are quite pricey but can be pretty darn entertaining when they prove their worth. Masters of Olympus never got as manic as it can get in the train games. It felt both outplayed by MT2 and completely pulverised by the follow-up MT3. It might be unfair, a bit harsh even, to compare Snowborn Games' slots to Relax Gaming's, as they would seem to suit different gambling circles, but it's hard not to when reviewing a game like this. eOn an anecdotal level, Masters of Olympus didn't seem as brutal or as volatile, maybe even a bit more forgiving than the Relax Gaming smash hit, which might make it a better match for players who don't want to feel like they've been levelled by a runaway goods train, repeatedly, when it all goes wrong. When it goes right, Masters of Olympus has the same max win figure as its predecessor, rolling in at 20,000 times the bet.Like before, Masters of Olympus didn't come across like it was made to tear up the hold 'n win scene and flex insane levels of novelty, but it's as solid as it was before and bound to scintillate the right player keen on this kind of entertainment.

Title: Regal Streak
review: Regal Streak: OverviewMysterious Red Tiger partners R7 go back to basics for their classically styled slot Regal Streak. Taking the less is more line; the game isn’t exactly stimulating in the theme or looks department. Regal Streak takes an unapologetically simple approach, padding out a straight forward base game, with a multiplier filled round of free spins which can drum up some surprisingly large wins.Regal Streak - base gameThe design of the game is plain, especially the visuals which use an emerald green, star-patterned background, similar to the felt top of a pool table. The grid isn’t much more elaborate. A gold bar wraps around a 5-reel, 3-payline slot, displaying a bunch of bright chunky symbols. Rounding off the experience is what sounds like a jazzy, disco version of Foster the People’s hit Pumped up Kicks. Okay a very jazzy version, while the remaining sound effects are the common bleeps that accompany this sort of game.Playable on any device, Regal Streak offers stakes ranging from 10 p/c to $/€10 per spin. Not exactly high roller friendly, but the potential is high, so bets have possibly been reigned in to minimise exposure. RTP is slightly below average on 95.71%, while volatility is high. A little surprising given the number of features hit during testing. Perhaps we caught Regal Streak on a good day, but it didn't appear to be as tight-fisted as other games in the Red Tiger stable can sometimes be.Despite essentially being a standard fruity-inspired slot, Regal Streak has one or two things which might surprise. The first is the pay anywhere mechanic - 3 or more matching symbols on a payline trigger a payout. Whether the combination starts from the first reel, or whether winning symbols are adjacent, or not, it doesn’t matter. Using this system squeezes more mileage out of the limited number of paylines and feels more dynamic than spending the majority of the time staring at just the first three reels.There are not many surprises on the paytable though where it’s generic icons from start to finish. 10 to Ace royals make up out the bottom end of the scale, followed by cherries, four-leaf clovers, bells, and lucky 7s. Full lines of premium symbols are worth 13.5 to 45 times the stake. There is no wild, and the only other symbol is the scatter, covered in the next section.Regal Streak: FeaturesRegal Streak - free spinsBesides the pay anywhere mechanic there isn’t much jazzing up the base game besides Regal Nudges. The bonus game, however, can go crazy if wound up tight enough. There you will find Regal Spins and several multiplier related features.During the main game, if 2 scatters land on a line, there is a chance the crown on the logo flies down to nudge the reels. This is the Regal Nudge feature, and when active, a third scatter may appear to trigger free spins.Keep an eye out for the regla spins symbols as 3, 4 or 5 of them anywhere in view award 15, 20, or 25 Regal Spins respectively. Before entering Regal Spins free spins, one of the pay symbols is randomly selected to be the multiplier symbol. This chosen symbol then has its respective multiplier bar placed above the reels. Higher paying symbols display larger values on the bar. For example, if the lucky seven symbol is chosen, the values on the multiplier bar are x7, x14, x21, and x28.Now, the round starts on x1, and each win involving the multiplier symbol moves progress along the bar, unlocking multipliers in the process. Any active multiplier is applied to each win line during the feature. The feature is further enhanced when 3 or more Regal Spins symbols appear on a payline - 3, 4 or 5 Regal Symbols on a line add 10, 15 or 20 free spins respectively. Also, they increase the Multiplier Bar values by +1 for each Regal Spins symbol on the line. For example, the lucky 7s multiplier bar increases to x10, x17, x24, and x31 when 3 bonus symbols land on a line.Regal Streak: VerdictWith Regal Streak, R7 has designed a game which isn’t really trying to be special or innovative in any way. The game does what it says on the label, and for the most part that’s about it. Things do get a little busier during Regal Spins when the win multiplier comes into play, but still, the gameplay remains uncomplicated throughout. What might prevent Regal Streak from being a write off is its potential, where wins of up to 9,545 times the stake are technically possible.When it comes to the overall design, Regal Streak is about as basic as it gets which might be a draw for some players after an older Reel King style vibe. The bonus game too has a vaguely ‘Book of’ feel to it due to the chosen symbol mechanic, though the rest of the rules are quite different. There’s not too much else to say about Regal Streak, either you dig the rudimentary gameplay, or it will bore you to tears.If you’re in the mood for a stripped-back classic slot with a quick pace and potentially big returns, then it might worth taking Regal Streak for a spin. Anyone else who prefers a bit more sophistication will feel like they’re dialling up a friend on a landline phone – one of those old rotary dial ones.

Title: Moon Spell
review: Moon Spell: Slot OverviewSoftware provider Red Tiger gathers some eye of newt and twirls its wand before setting a cauldron to boil in the witchy online slot Moon Spell. If you're the sort of person drawn to the occult or the unexplainable, maybe this will be for you. Red Tiger doesn't do wonders with the theme, though, or Moon Spell's features, really. Cash prize Moon symbols and an uncomplicated Hold and Respin bonus round aren't exactly wonders. Hmm, apologies for being a downer at the outset.Despite being visible in the daytime, the moon is more prominent at night, which is the hour that Moon Spell is played. 'Sometimes in the afternoon sky the moon would pass white as a cloud, furtive, lusterless, like an actress who does not have to perform yet and who, from the audience, in street clothes, watches the other actors for a moment, making herself inconspicuous, not wanting anyone to pay attention to her.' As Proust so poetically put it. There's not a ton of poetry in Moon Spell, however, as it's not the most richly magical scene ever to flare up an online slot. In general, the background is a bit plain, but the starry sky, audio jingles, and tree silhouettes are pleasant in their way. Aurora effects in free spins do improve the bound round. Possibly the biggest eye-catcher is the list of prize values on display above the reels, for good or for ill.Moon Spell slot - base gameBeneath the prize list, wrapped in ivy, is a 5x3 gaming grid evaluating winning combinations with the aid of 20 paylines. Players pick a wager of 10 c to $/€10 to start the casting, and as stats, they get a medium-high volatile math model and a top maximum RTP of 95.76%.For pay symbols, J, Q, K and A make up the lower lot, while jewellery, books, cats, and owls are the high pays. Winning 5 OAK symbol combinations gets you 5 times the bet for the royals or 10 to 40 times the bet for the picture symbols. Wilds pay an astounding 1,000x if a line of 5 of them happen to hit, and they can also be used to substitute any of the regular pays.Moon Spell: Slot FeaturesMoon Spell slot - instant winIt's pretty bread and butter stuff here, where Moon Spell slings out Moon symbol wins, a Hold and Respin round, plus Prize Ladder Bonus Prizes.Moon SymbolsMoon symbols land in any position, holding a cash prize of 0.5x to 100x the stake. Landing 3 or 4 Moon symbols awards the combined amount of their cash prizes.Hold and RespinLanding 5 or more Moon symbols on the reels activates the Hold and Respin bonus round with 3 respins. Moon symbols lock to the reels for respins, including the triggering Moons. Each new Moon symbol landed on the grid resets the spins back to 3. The round ends when no new Moon symbols land for 3 consecutive respins or all positions on the grid have been filled by Moon symbols. The combined total of all Moon symbols is awarded at the end.Prize Ladder and Bonus PrizesYou'll find 6 bonus prizes displayed above the reels on the Prize Ladder. During the Hold and Respin bonus, landing 10 or more Moon symbols awards a corresponding prize from the ladder - plus the combined values of all landed Moon symbols. The prizes on the ladder are: 10 Moons - 50x the bet, 11 Moons - 100x the bet, 12 Moons - 200x the bet, 13 Moons - 300x the bet, 14 Moons - 1,000x the bet, and 15 Moons - 5,000x the bet.Moon Spell slot - hold & respin featureMoon Spell: Slot VerdictHey ho, that was Moon Spell. Nothing special in many regards. Good for a bit of dipping into the witchy theme, perhaps, not to any great depth, though. The features hardly possess fathoms of depth, as well. Hit 3 or 4 Moon symbols, and get some coins. Alternatively, hit 5 or more Moon symbols and find yourself blasted into the bonus round. There's not much to the bonus round, either. Simply cross your fingers in the hope that loads of Moons land and lock, preferably 10 or more, to get an additional prize. Get 15 of them, and the top prize is yours. For the record, Moon Spell's max multiplier is 5,224x the bet.There's not a lot else to report on than that. Moon Spell has no twisted intricacies to untangle, no complex rules to decipher, not much of major interest in general. Red Tiger had been on a so-so/okay run around the time of writing, releasing slots like Savannah Pride, Roman Emperors, and Diamond Blitz 2, which hardly blazed, but Moon Spell was in several ways even less exciting. As for magic, the best the game managed to come up with were light novice-level cantrips, maybe sleep spells?

Title: Judge and Jury Megaways
review: Judge & Jury Megaways: Slot OverviewTrial by jury, the 'cornerstone of our liberty' as James Madison put it, has been around for rather a long time. According to certain sources, the Ancient Egyptians were first to use a form of trial by jury around 2,000 B.C.E., and the Ancient Greeks weren't far behind before the concept caught on amongst the Romans. Attempting to capture some courtroom drama on the reels is software provider Skywind in a slot called Judge & Jury Megaways. To reflect the veritable Gordian Knot of intricate legal loopholes and clauses, Skywind has loaded in a stack of features such as random wilds, symbol removals, cascades, free spins, progressive multipliers, an I.D. Parade, and Wanted Poster cash prizes.For the setting, Judge & Jury Megaways takes place in a location that looks part courtroom, part judge's office, what with all those books sitting on shelves in the upper right quadrant. A judge hangs out on the other side of the reels, banging his gavel, and occasionally saying judge-y things to thicken the atmosphere. Crime slots are popular, so good on Skywind for breathing a bit of fresh life into the genre by doing something different with it. There's a mishmash of all sorts here. Wanted posters, safes overflowing with cash, sirens, police officers, crims, the works. Skywind has chucked in the kitchen sink – both in terms of theme and features.On the mechanical front, Judge & Jury's game grid comprises 6 vertically spinning reels and a single horizontal bonus reel up the top. This being Megaways, the number of symbols on the main reels changes on each spin, producing anywhere from 324 to 117,649 ways to win. Players get multiple ways of representing themselves in court, meaning you can play in normal mode, where stakes vary from 20 p/c to $/€200 per spin or flick Double Chance on - this betting option increases the stake by 25%, doubling the chance of winning free spins. Either way, the game is fairly volatile (4/5) and comes with a solid return to player value.To the payable now, where 10-A card rank tiles appear as the low pays, and handcuffs, safes, robbers, policemen, and judges are used as the high pays. Landing a full six of a kind winning way results in a payout of 0.4-1x the bet for the royals, rising to 1.5-7.5x the bet for a premium win. Substituting for any of the pay symbols to help complete a winning way are 2 wild sirens – a blue and a red one. The special thing about the red wild is it appears on the top reel, and when it hits, it expands downwards to cover all positions on the reel beneath it.Judge & Jury Megaways: Slot FeaturesIf a stack of features is a must-have item in a slot, then Judge & Jury Megaways could be just the ticket because Skywind has jammed in quite a few extras, it must be said. It starts with the usual cascades, which remove winning combinations from the board when they hit, allowing symbols to drop down to plug the gaps. If this creates a new winning way, another cascade triggers.The JudgeThe judge isn't just there to look stern and commentate. Occasionally, he awards 2 random bonuses in the base game. For the first, he can remove royal symbols from the reels on a non-winning spin, where only non-royal symbols fall in on the resulting cascade. The other bonus is randomly adding 3-6 wild symbols to the reels.Wanted PostersOn each spin, a different wanted poster is displayed on the right-hand side. If a poster symbol appears on the reels which matches it, players win a cash prize of 2x, 5x, 10x, 100x, or 5,000x the bet. Once the prize has been paid, the poster is removed, and a cascade occurs into its gap. Wanted Posters appear in the base and bonus game but are not increased by the progressive multiplier.Free GamesLanding 4 scatters in the base game awards 10 free spins, plus 5 additional spins for any extra scatter in view – up to 20 at the most. During free spins, each win increases the progressive multiplier by +1 before new symbols cascade down. Lastly, landing 3 or 4 scatters during the feature awards an extra +5 or +10 free spins, respectively.I.D. ParadeWhile free spins are active, landing at least 3 cell symbols triggers the I.D. Parade feature. Getting 3, 4, 5, or 6 cell symbols in view awards 1, 2, 3, or 4 picks, respectively. For the parade, four suspects are displayed on-screen. Picking them uncovers prizes such as +3, +5, or +10 free spins, +3, +5, or +10 to the multiplier, or cash values of 5x, 10x, 20x, 30x, 50x, or 100x the bet.Buy In FeatureSome players may have access to the Buy In Feature button. If there, clicking it lets you pay 80x the bet to receive 10, 15, or 20 free spins.Judge & Jury Megaways: Slot VerdictSkywind has really taken to Megaways with gusto. The studio started with an older game upgrade called Big Buffalo Megaways and a clever 'book of' version in Book of Gems Megaways before moving on to be more creative with the format. Judge & Jury Megaways is another good example. It's not just a case of stuffing a ton of features onto a Megaways reel-set either, though there are plenty of extras to be found in Judge & Jury. What's neat is that games like Judge & Jury Megaways or Alive! Megaways bubble with a positive spirit, as if Skywind actually had fun while making them and dreaming up what sort of gameplay to include.Skywind has certainly gone to town with the features, as a lot of them have wedged their way into Judge & Jury Megaways. From the base game randoms to a free spins round with a progressive multiplier and I.D. Parade pick 'n clicks, to the universal Wanted Posters system, there is rarely a dull moment. For players who like a full list of extras, then Judge & Jury Megaways is one to check out. When you consider the solid entertainment value and a max win figure, Skywind has gone out of their way to make sure as many bases as possible are covered. One minor caveat is that the visuals have a slightly old fashioned Payday Megaways look to them, which, compared to many of the state of the art slots out there, may come across as rather dated. However, that's more of a personal issue rather than a deal-breaker since players value different aspects when playing slots.Needless to say, if you've got the slightest interest in Megaways, then putting Judge & Jury Megaways through its paces makes perfect sense. On the other hand, if stuffing a slot full of features Blueprint Gaming style is not enough to float your boat, what's left is a rather mediocre Megaways game which does look 5 years late to the party.

Title: Prime Zone
review: Prime Zone (Quickspin): OverviewIn Quickspin's latest offering, we're whipped back to Las Vegas during its glory days, a place of decadence and the sinful relinquishment of one's monetary reserves. Inside the smoky chambers and extravagant halls of any and every superstructure in the torrid, hot desert, there is a near infinite amount of entertainment. To some extent, Prime Zone delivers this home. But, there's also some deja vu to be experienced, for in many ways, what you'll find in Prime Zone is a rather typical old-school Quickspin slot.The structure of the reel set is a basic one. Utilising 5 reels, 3 rows and 10 paylines, Prime Zone comes with an industry standard RTP of 96.28% distributed to give you 38.36% in the base game and 57.92% in the free spins feature. The gameplay is quite straightforward as well and relies heavily on multipliers, which can combine to great effect, to provide all the action. As you get underway, you'll land multiplier wilds that will boost the multiplier value relative to the number of wilds on a payline. In the free spins round, these line-win multiplier wilds come to even greater use where they can be subject to multipliers of up to 4x. Ranging from medium to high variance, depending on the bonus game of your choice, you can play this game across all devices from 10 cents to 100€ per spin.Visually, Prime Zone has a classic Las Vegas feel to it. With an up-tempo version of the Joker Strike soundtrack playing on repeat, in the backdrop you'll see silhouettes of palm trees and skyscrapers against a neon purple sky. Encased in a golden frame, on the reels you'll see lower-value card suit symbols alongside bells, diamonds, blue sevens and red sevens. The latter is the most rewarding, giving you 50 times your stake for 5 on a full payline. The wild symbol substitutes for all other symbols bar the scatter and is the key to winning big as you will see.Prime Zone (Quickspin): FeaturesFree Spins feature - Mystery Mode option in actionCentral to the game is the Multiplier Wild symbol which can appear on all reels. The great thing about these wilds is that the multiplier increases relative to the number of wilds on a payline. So for example, 3 wilds appearing on a single payline will give you a 3x multiplier. Land a wild line (5x multiplier) and you're looking at a 250 times your stake max win in the base game.You'll find an even better use for these wilds in the Free Spins game which comes into play when 3 bonus scatter symbols appear anywhere on the 3 middle reels. With 7 free spins awarded, you're given the option to choose between four different bonuses ranging from lower to higher risk. These are your options:Option 1: medium variance and with all wins subject to a 1x multiplier, 3 wild symbols are randomly added inside the zone covering reels 1, 2 and 3.Option 2: medium variance and with all wins subject to a 2x multiplier, 3 wild symbols are randomly added inside the zone covering reels 2, 3 and 4.Option 3: high variance and with all wins subject to a 3x multiplier, 3 wild symbols are randomly added inside the zone covering reels 3, 4 and 5.Option 4: varying in volatility, the zone shifts between reels on each spin and will boost your winnings with a multiplier between 1x and 4x.Remember, these multipliers are added on top of the line-win wild multipliers, which means you can land wins of up to 1000 times your stake per single spin if you opt for the Mystery Shifting bonus. This, however, makes the game seem much more potent than it really is.Prime Zone (Quickspin): Final VerdictPrime Zone is undoubtedly a throwback to the classic Quickspin we know from before, both in terms of visual production and mathematical design. It's also a lot less intricate compared to many of the recent releases such as Ivan and the Immortal King, Divine Dreams and Hall of the Mountain King which have all been extremely ambitious titles. With that in mind, it's actually nice to see Quickspin go back to something simple again. What we found to be a bit disappointing, however, are the low payouts. While not bad enough to deter recreational players, who will be tied up in the engaging gameplay anyway, more experienced players might find the small base game wins off-putting and a bit of a drag.It doesn't actually get much better in the free spins feature either, as it turns out, where, during Quickspin's test runs of 100 billion spins, the best result the game could muster was a max win of 2685,5x. Now, it's not the worst number we've seen in a slot machine, and a lower max win should theoretically give you a more realistic chance to win big as the wins can be distributed over a larger number of players, but for hardcore gamblers that get a kick out of chasing monster wins, this won't suffice. As a consequence, Prime Zone is a game that you will either love or hate depending on what type of player you are.

Title: Carnival Queen
review: Carnival Queen (Thunderkick): ReviewIt's been a while since we've heard anything from Thunderkick, something that is not all too unusual for the Swedish developer that has a tendency to take good time crafting its slots. Having had the privilege to try Carnival Queen, the 3-month absence does make a bit more sense seeing how much effort must have been invested in the production. In a nutshell, Carnival Queen is a Bonanza-inspired slot involving cascading symbols, growing multipliers and excellent win potential. It draws inspiration from the Mardi Gras (French for "Fat Tuesday") festival that, although celebrated all over the world, is most widely associated with New Orleans and other traditionally French ethnic cities in America.Using 6 reels and 4096 ways to win in combination with the increasing multipliers, this bad boy (slaps hood of Thunderkick) can pay out a massive 22,700 times your stake! It is by far the highest paying slot to date released by the company. Carnival Queen can be played on all devices from between 0.10 to 100€ per spin and comes with an industry standard RTP of 96.1%.It's a cheerful slot using vibrant colours with the reels set against the backdrop of a crowded Louisiana thoroughfare. The cartoonish graphics and animations are excellent and quite typical of Thunderkick design-wise. On the reels you'll see gradient coloured A, K, Q, J, 10 and 9 royals as well as 4 high paying characters dressed in carnival-themed costumes. The king's crown and the wild symbol are the most lucrative of the bunch, however, giving you 20 times your stake for 6 across a payline.Carnival Queen (Thunderkick): FeaturesCentral to the game is the chain-reaction engine, or the Avalanche feature, as it's called here. You've seen it before in numerous slots - when a winning combination lands on the reels, the symbols involved are removed and replaced with new ones cascading from the top. Essentially, any win will set in motion a chain reaction that only stops when no more winning combinations appear on the reels. There is a twist to it, however. The Avalanche also triggers the multiplier feature. For each cascade, the multiplier increases by 1. You'll get the same in the bonus but with a major benefit as explained below.Landing 3, 4, 5 or 6 bonus scatters triggers 12, 16, 20 or 24 free spins respectively. You can also retrigger the bonus by landing 2 scatters, adding 3 more spins to your total. Furthermore, any additional scatter grants 3 extra free spins. Now, the bonus plays pretty much the same as the base game but with a few key benefits. Most importantly, the increasing multiplier will not revert back to zero on a losing spin, something that boosts the big win potential significantly. Furthermore, following a losing spin, a wild symbol will eliminate all standard symbols from its position, both vertically and horizontally, thus giving you a second chance to land a winning combination and trigger a cascade as well as the increasing multiplier.Carnival Queen (Thunderkick): ConclusionCarnival Queen is without question one of the better slots produced by Thunderkick, although it's quite obviously Bonanza-inspired and an attempt to keep up with current trends. With that said, it's undoubtedly a competent and entertaining medium variance slot capable of producing wins of up to 22,700 times your stake. Despite being a rather basic cascading-type slot, Carnival Queen does in no way come across as a clone or rip-off. With fine-tuned maths, outstanding visuals and a sprinkle of Thunderkick magic, Carnival Queen is a captivating and thrilling game worthwhile.

Title: Super Joker Megaways
review: Super Joker Megaways: Slot OverviewFor fans of fruity gaming, developer Stakelogic has filled a Megaways powered slot with the stuff, while condensing it down to a three-reel format. Despite the added sophistication Megaways inherently brings, Super Joker Megaways sticks to its fruit slot heritage by being a generally simple game. In saying that, there are quite a few features accompanying the action. Despite being streamlined in essence, complexity is provided by multi-mode gaming, cascades, instant prizes, and a gamble feature.There's no mistaking what genre you might have inadvertently wandered into when Super Joker Megaways loads up. A sort of 1970s diamond-patterned wallpaper makes up the background, behind a 3-reel grid covered in big bright symbols. Being a Megaways slot, the rows are dynamic and randomly change from between 2-8 rows on each spin, making the game capable of producing up to 512 ways to win. The soundtrack, meanwhile, has a Boogie Nights thing going on, helping produce an environment you dig daddio or you just don't.Highly volatile, the game is playable across all devices, producing an RTP of 96.5%. Choosing bets involves two levels of decision making. First is base, ranging from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Like many Stakelogic games, Super Joker Megaways comes with a Super Stake feature, so the second choice is whether to activate it or not. When engaged, more scatter symbols are added to the reels, increasing the chances of triggering the Super Win feature. There is a cost of course – it doubles the base bet. Symbol values are the same whether the Super Stake is active or not. There's no word on hit frequency in the game sheet, but being a fruit slot it's likely to be below 20% although it's just a guess from our side.As for symbols, there are only six regulars to form line wins with. From low to high are cherries, lemons, grapes, bells, stars, and lucky sevens, worth 0.20 to 5 times the bet for three of a kind. The only other symbols are scatters, covered next.Super Joker Megaways: Slot FeaturesWhat gives Super Joker Megaways more individuality than being a simple three reels Megaways slot is its two game modes. Most of the time, it chugs away in a default mode, alternating to Super Joker Mode when certain conditions are met. On top of this, players get cascades, a Super Win feature, and gambling options.Cascades in Super Joker Megaways work as they usually do in a Megaways game. When a win hits, it is removed from the reels to allow existing symbols to drop down and new ones to cascade in. More hits can line up, meaning cascades continue to function until no new winning combinations appear.The mischievous joker symbol is the scatter, landing on all three reels. When 3 or more are in view, they activate the Super Win feature. Next, a bunch of prizes appear on screen, and one is randomly awarded, paid, then you're back to the game. Reward size is partially dictated by the number of scatters triggering it. If 3 scatters flip the feature, the win could be anything from 2 to 600 times the stake. If 4 or more scatters triggered the feature, then you will always receive the 600x prize.Winning 2 times your stake or more triggers Super Joker Mode. In many ways, this is like another Super Stake option combined with a gamble feature. You'll know the mode is engaged because the background turns blue, and your win is displayed in a Super Meter located above the reels. You have the choice to spin in this mode which doubles the size of the total bet or collect your winnings. Super Joker Mode ends when the money in the meter is less than 2x the stake, or greater than 200x. The benefit of spinning in this mode is that landing two scatters awards 2x-600x the bet, while 3 or 4 scatters award 100-600x, or 600x respectively. Winning 100x from these prizes also ends the mode.For those who just can't have betting options is the gamble feature where you can double/quadruple or nothing your win by guessing the colour or suit of a face-down card.Super Joker Megaways: Slot VerdictFruity/Vegas-style slots continue their creep into the Megaways arena, with Super Joker Megaways furthering their advance. Stakelogic is no stranger to three-reel slots either, as Super Joker Megaways forms part of a whole line of Joker slots from Stakelogic.As for the features, the Super Stake option is standard by now, appearing in one form or another in a host of Stakelogic slots. It isn't cheap, literally doubling each bet, but when it works out it can be great. Taking the 'going large' concept one step further is Super Joker Mode. This one is a little more controversial and a potential deal-breaker. Like Super Stake, Super Joker Mode is great when it goes your way, yet it also has a tendency to chew through winnings like nothing else. It's a mode which fast tracks players to glory or ruin since each spin costs four times the base level.What makes Super Joker Mode slightly provocative perhaps is that it cannot be deactivated. Players who don't like the gamble feature popping up after a win have the luxury of switching it off. Not such an issue when manually spinning, but if you are using autospin, then when Super Joker Mode is in play there is no option to collect wins. You either hit the win caps or lose it all. Seeing a decent win take automatic hits you can't prevent is like jamming toothpaste back in the tube – super frustrating.If you like pushing your luck to the limit via extra gamble or stake options, then Super Joker Megaways should scratch the itch – especially if you enjoy doing so in a jazzy Vegas environment. If not, Super Joker Megaways kind of loses its point.

Title: Greedy Wolf
review: Greedy Wolf: Slot OverviewGet ready for some huffing and a puffing in Greedy Wolf, Pragmatic Play's retelling of the classic The Three Little Pigs fable. Many are probably familiar, but if not, it's a story that teaches a lesson about the benefits of hard work. Where the first two pigs rushed the house-building process so they could get back to playing around, the third one took his time to construct a brick house, thereby avoiding the wolf's jaws, who could not blow his house down. This is a tale that has been retold countless times in the past. Let's see how Pragmatic Play's version measures up.Heavily based on SG Gaming's land-based slot Huff n' Puff, Greedy Wolf is set in a fairy tale world of meadows, butterflies, mountains, a stream with a swan, a white fence, the works. Pragmatic Play has laid it on thick to create an idyllic location that evokes memories of the famous story. The little pigs can be seen running about in the distance, no doubt up to some sort of mischief, and at times, the wolf starts chasing them. In the middle of the screen is a 5-reel, 4-row game panel stuck to the side of what is presumably one of the pigs' houses.Greedy Wolf slot - base gameGreedy Wolf has been designed to be played on mobile, tablet, or desktop devices and accepts bets of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Or it may be possible to activate the Ante Bet, which increases the stake by 25%, thereby triggering the bonus round when 5 scatter symbols land instead of the normal 6. This affects RTP, which, when playing in the default mode is 96.48%, rising to 96.51% with the Ante Bet active. Be aware that Greedy Wolf also has two lower RTP models, while volatility has been rated at medium-high (3.5 out of 5).A total of 20 paylines cross the grid, and regular symbols pay from left to right. For the lower pays we get J-A card ranks and two tools, paying 3 to 5 times the bet for a five-symbol line, then there are three little pigs and the wolf as the high pays. Each looks about as happy as it gets, including the wolf who looks more like a lapdog than a fearful beast. Anyway, landing five premium symbols across a payline is worth 10 to 20 times the stake. Eking out a bit more is the wild symbol, as landing five wilds on a line pay 25x the bet. Wilds appear on all reels and can replace any pay symbol to help complete a win.Greedy Wolf: Slot FeaturesGreedy Wolf slot - free spinsGreedy Wolf comes with a bonus round, triggered when the required number of scatters hit, as well as three base game modifiers – Greedy Wolf Wild, 3 Little Pigs Wilds and Respins, plus Guaranteed Wins.Greedy Wolf WildOn the central reel only, fully stacked and expanded wolf symbols can randomly land. When this occurs, all pig symbols in view are transformed into wolf symbols. The game pays after the transformations have taken place.3 Little Pigs and RespinsOn random spins, wilds may be added to reels 1, 2, or 3, and a win evaluation occurs. Then, the wolf comes along to move wilds one position to the right and trigger a respin, or blow the wilds off the screen to end the feature. Respins continue until there is nowhere for the wilds to move or they have been blown away.Guaranteed WinOn random non-winning spins, the wolf can appear and blow all the symbols away. New symbols fall from the top, guaranteeing a win of at least 20x the bet or landing enough scatters to trigger free spins.Free SpinsLanding 6 scatters, or 5 when the Ante Bet is active awards 6 free spins. Triggering scatter symbols have straw frames placed around the position they landed, and if scatters land during the feature, they also get frames placed on their positions. If a cell already has a frame, it is upgraded from straw to wood, then bricks, then castle. Landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters awards an additional 1, 2, or 4 free spins, respectively. At the end of free spins, the framed positions are converted into houses. The wolf appears and blows the houses away to reveal money prizes. Prizes are higher based on the type of house.Greedy Wolf slot - free spinsGreedy Wolf: Slot VerdictWell, there's a bit of huffin' and a puffin' going on in Greedy Wolf, but not hurricane levels of air movement. It's got polish, bright looks, a ton of animations, several features, and there's an amusing interplay between wolf and piggies. However, it also feels like one of those games Pragmatic Play could design in their sleep with two hands tied behind their backs. The game makes good use of its characters, though, who climb ladders to add wilds or appear on screen to literally blow things away. When it comes to theme use, Greedy Wolf gives Quickspin's classic Big Bad Wolf a run for its money and does so in a charming manner.This made it easy to get caught up in the flow when the features were firing. At the beginning of the review, features were quite rare for a while, and the game lost some of its sheen. However, once they started popping, along with the cute way characters add some of the features, it was easy to settle back for a few rib-ticklers. Free spins were a letdown, though. We'd recently reviewed Wild Chapo Dream Drop, which uses a similar system of marking positions on the reels when scatter symbols hit. On the final free spin of Wild Chapo Dream Drop, the marked positions are filled with wilds and/or wild multipliers, which multiply each other. As such, the results can be quite startling. In Greedy Wolf, you just get cash prizes. That's fine, but they didn't tend to have major values, and even having a ton of marked positions just wasn't super exciting. Nor is Greedy Wolf's max win of 3,000x the bet.Greedy Wolf would probably fit the bill if a bubbly retelling of the Three Little Pigs fable is all you are looking for. However, if you want a bit more bite, a bit more huff 'n' puff, then a game like Big Bad Wolf Megaways and its ten times+ greater potential might be a better option.

Title: Star Bounty
review: Star Bounty: OverviewDeveloper Pragmatic Play does a spot of galactic bounty hunting in their sci-fi themed slot Star Bounty. Set in a nicely rendered alien environment, Star Bounty manages to get most things right with its mix of pay mechanics plus features such as Tumbles, Wild Multipliers, and Free Spins. The icing on top is its big potential, though how likely it is to hit might be an interesting question.So, as mentioned, make sure your rebreather is strapped on tight before hitting spin because we aren’t in Kansas anymore. Outside the viewport, spacecraft can be seen traversing the surface of a rocky alien planet. Then again, it could be a future version of earth where global warming has roasted the topsoil off. Wherever it is, Star Bounty has a strong sci-fi theme, as evidenced by the futuristic structures planet side, and the space ship bridge where the 6-reel, 4,096 ways to win hexagon shaped grid is found. Players also get a pretty sweet synth-heavy soundtrack to spin to. Overall, Star Bounty is one of the more convincing environments Pragmatic has conjured up in a while.Playable on any device from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, the game has a good flow to it made possible by the tumble's and pay system. These two mechanics make the nonaligned reels much easier to work with than they might appear in a screenshot. On the load screen, Pragmatic’s volatility meter displays a rating of 5/5, so, pretty much as high as it gets. RTP isn’t quite so high, but still a respectable rating of 96.6% - in default mode, that is.Despite the high volatility, the game is quite well balanced. The free spins feature triggered more often than was first expected, or feared. Of course, luck goes both ways, but during testing, a lot less time was spent gazing longingly at the feature buy button than is often the case.To get a win, matching symbols can land in any row as long as they sit adjacently from the first reel onwards. As to the symbols flitting across the reels, there is quite a collection of them, 12 in fact. We get four J-A royals, four space insignias, and four characters represented by two masked baddies, a female heroine, and a male hero. The male, who looks a little like Karl Urban from Chronicles of Riddick, is worth the most at 15 times the stake for six of a kind. Hitting lines of the other three premiums will get you 5 – 10 times the stake.A couple of wild types turn up to increase the chances of winning. In its basic form, the standard wild appears on reels 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 to substitute for any regular pay symbol. The other wild variations pop up during the features.Star Bounty: FeaturesStar Bounty - free spinsStar Bounty comes with plenty of extras to keep the game going. One is the Tumble feature which becomes active after every win. Winning symbols are cleared from the board, allowing new ones to drop into the empty spaces. Consecutive Tumbles continue until no new winning combination lands.A winged egg looking tile is the missile wild symbol, appearing on reels 2, 3, or 4. Whenever one lands on the reels, it fires missiles onto a random number of symbols turning them into wilds.The atom patterned hex is the scatter symbol and 3 or more in view at the end of a spin sequence triggers free spins. Before free spins begin, you have to work out how many you’re going to get. This is where the special respin feature comes in. This feature starts with the number of triggering scatter symbols locked to the reels. The remaining positions spin and each new scatter symbol that lands is locked, triggering another respin. When no new scatters land, the tally is added up and the number of free spins awarded – up to 24.During free spins, wilds may appear with a multiplier of x2 or x3. If more than one wild is part of a win, then their values are multiplied together. Free Spins appear to trigger quite regularly, but should players wish to cut straight to them, they can be bought for 75x the stake. When the feature buy is selected, the next spin guarantees 3 to 6 free spin scatter symbols.Star Bounty: VerdictGotta say, Star Bounty was a pleasant surprise from Pragmatic Play. The studio has matched excellent graphics with an ideal soundtrack to create a fantastic world to play in. The reel arrangement is a little different, yet it also works perfectly alongside the futuristic theme and the pay system. Pop on a couple of useful features, and it’s hard to find many faults with the end result.Tumbles keep the base game ticking along at a satisfying rate, though it might have been nice if they’d been paired with a win multiplier during free spins. As it is, wild multipliers in free spins feature are capable of creating decent wins on their own.During testing, wins during the bonus game were decent but nothing amazing, perhaps leading to question the game’s potential. Pragmatic claims 25,000 times the stake is possible. A massive number, but let’s say you triggered the full 24 free spins. You’d then need to average over 1,000x on each spin - realistic or science fiction? As we all know by now, Pragmatic's advertised max win potential is often far too optimistic.Aside from potential, the main criticism might be that Star Bounty doesn’t really offer anything new, features wise. It may look different, but it's really just a 6-reel, win-all-ways reel set. Yet what it has works well, each part integrating with the others to create a straight-up fun game. When it comes to sci-fi slots, Pragmatic’s Star Bounty comes out as one of the better ones.

Title: Blazing Bull
review: Blazing Bull Slot: OverviewDeveloper Kalamba Games usually tries to be clever when it comes to game design by using unusual features - for better or for worse. Blazing Bull is something of an anomaly in that regard, but still heads off-piste by getting players in touch with their spirit guides. At least, that’s what the game blurb says. However, Blazing Bull actually keeps its feet firmly on the ground in both a physical and metaphysical sense. It doesn’t get all new age-y, and even better, it's free of the frivolous "Hyper" features which often clog up a Kalamba title. That’s not to say that it’s devoid of features, it’s just that Kalamba have simplified the process and crafted an uncomplicated slot that will appeal to players who prefer more straight forward gaming.Blazing Bull is certainly a nice looking game. Vibrant is the word that springs to mind to describe it. The background has a misty manifest destiny era look to it, with wild mountains sloping down into rivers and a verdant valley where the grid has been placed. Creeping ivy surrounds the 6-reel, 4-row setup, and a light percussive soundtrack completes the scene. Symbols are crisp, bright, and the whole picture is one of the nicest to come from Kalamba’s studio so far. Gone are the cartoon zanies they often release to be replaced with a more realistic look, and Blazing Bull is all the better for it.It’s not completely realistic though. The high pay symbols have an etheric, glowing-eyed look, and the bull literally blazes with fire. The bull is also the highest paying symbol with 6 of a kind worth 5 times the stake - followed by a bear, an eagle, a cougar, and a wolf. These high pay symbols only need two of a kind for a winner. The low pays, on the other hand, need at least three and are made up of 9-A iron royals which also light up when they hit. Winning symbols can land on any row, consecutively from left to right, which adds up to 4,096 win ways. The wild, meanwhile, is represented by a dream catcher and substitutes for all regular symbols.Bets aren’t super friendly for low-rollers which start at 60 p/c and can be raised to $/€120 per spin. One good thing about Kalamba’s slots, however, is that you often get a good return to player rating with them. Blazing Bull is no different and offers an exceptionally generous RTP of 97.42%. Another high stat is the volatility which blazes away behind the scenes on a 10/10 rating whilst hit frequency isn’t bad either on 28.6%. The only thing that lets the side down is potential which we will get to shortly. For now, the features.Blazing Bull Slot: FeaturesFree spins feature in actionAbove the reels are two meters - one on the left for the Gold Bonus, one on the right for the Silver Bonus. Whenever a Silver or Gold Bonus symbol lands, it increases the respective meter, which adds more free spins to the bonus game when it's triggered. When 3 or more of one coin type lands, it triggers the corresponding bonus game. The Gold Bonus Game comes with at least 9 free spins and up to 30 max. The Silver Bonus Game has at least 7 free spins and up to 20 max.Both bonus games came with two added benefits; wilds are upgraded during Silver free spins to x2 multiplier wilds, and in Gold spins, they become x3 multiplier wilds. Both bonus games are padded out with a new bonus symbol adding an extra advantage. This symbol rewards players like so:Two bonus symbols award +2 free spins.Three bonus symbols award a 2x win +5 free spins.Four bonus symbols awards a 5x win +8 free spins.Five bonus symbols awards a 6x win +10 free spins.Six bonus symbols awards a 50x win +15 free spins.Once the bonus game has completed, the free spin meters start again from their original levels.Blazing Bull Slot: VerdictSometimes less is more, and this is certainly the case with Blazing Bull. Other titles from this developer to come our way were stuffed with intricate features that could sometimes get in the way of kicking back and enjoying the game at hand. That’s all been left on the cutting room floor with Blazing Bull. Kalamba Games has stripped it down to basics; there is no Hyperbet, no Hyperspins, which tremendously enhances the overall experience. Title: Sword of Khans

Title: Peaky Blindera

Hitting a 5 OAK cluster pays 0.1 to 1.5 times the bet up to 50 to 250 times the bet for hitting a 15+ cluster. Symbols come in sizes of 1x1, 2x2, or 3x3. Title: Celebration of Wealth

Title: Zeus II

Title: Demon Pots

When returning to free spins, the fully stacked are placed back on the reels. Activating the Free Spins pot during the round awards an extra 6 free spins.Buy Free SpinsPlayers may buy the free spins bonus for 100x the bet. When doing so, the Win Spins pot is activated, then at the end of them, the Free Spins pot is activated.Demon Pots slot - bonus gameDemon Pots: Slot VerdictIt's never a good sign when you're reviewing an online slot and recoil at the thought of suffering through more torment by scoring a retrigger during a bonus round. Title: Wicked Tales: Dark Red

If not, you will likely notice the unusual, and quite innovative we must admit, wheel layout. The Wandering Reels block is a group of 3 reels and 4 rows that spin together, moving randomly left and right with the majority of spins.More importantly, the Wandering Reels carry so-called Jumbo Blocks which essentially are full 3x4 sets of premiums as can be seen in the image above. Testing the game for this review we had a lot of trouble triggering the bonus wheel, and even if you manage to do so, you're not guaranteed activating the free spins.With that said, this is by far the best game to date to ever feature the Triple Edge logo, but does it really mean anything when the game is a clone of a bad Microgaming slot?

Title: Feeding Fury
review: Feeding Fury slot - base gameFeeding Fury: Slot OverviewPlayers! Don't be dipping your toe in the water around here; casino game maker Iron Dog Studio has unleashed the fish of war in an online slot going by the name of Feeding Fury - an aquatically themed slot that doesn't feature any angling, but it does feature a whole bunch of undersea critters. For the Feed or Die, a Collector Shark sits in the middle of the game board, eating all fish that land, thereby awarding a monetary value each time. As fish are eaten, they contribute points to a collection system; when the right number of points are gained in a single spin, the round moves to a higher level, of which there are three in total.At Level 1, The Collector Shark is a 1x1 symbol.At Level 2, The Collector Shark is a 2x2 symbol and a global multiplier of x2 applies to all values collected by The Collector Shark.At Level 3, The Collector Shark is a 3x2 symbol, and a global multiplier of x5 applies to all values collected by The Collector Shark. If a Hammerhead Shark hits in view, the global multiplier increases by x2 as soon as it is eaten.The Feed or Die feature continues until all lives have been lost or the win cap is reached.Feeding Fury slot - free spinsFeeding Fury: Slot VerdictAs far as fishing slots go, and there are a lot of them, Feeding Fury is quite unique. The base game's got Shark Attacks to add interest, though, in some ways, one of the most entertaining parts is the way Iron Dog Studio presented the fish, the animations, and the general humorous nature of the game. Title: Viral Spiral
review: Viral Spiral: Slot OverviewIn the entertainment biz, if a creator does something new, they often tend to do it in a bigger, more sensational way than what came before. In slots, this typically translates to things like outrageous themes, extra reels, more ways to win, and bigger potential rewards. Viral Spiral from Red Tiger is an anomaly. For Viral Spiral, Red Tiger has gone in the opposite direction to make one of the most minimalist games you'll come across.You might be thinking, okay, here comes another 3x3, 1-payline slot, but that setup is actually quite complex compared to what we find in Viral Spiral. This is a game which doesn't really have paylines, or reels and rows, in a traditional sense. Instead, in the centre of the screen sits one spinning reel, only ever displaying a single symbol. And in the case of symbols, it'll be either a losing symbol or a bonus symbol. The rest of the screen is just as simple, depicting a swirling pattern coloured in predominantly green tones, though it does shift colours during the Bonus Wheel segment of play.The first thing to do is pick a stake from options starting at 10 p/c, rising to $/€20 a pop. Hit spin, and you either land nothing, or you trigger the Bonus Wheel; it's as simple as that. Statistically, Viral Spiral's default RTP is 95.69%, and its math model is highly volatile. That is essentially all there is to say for now other than be ready for quite a number of dead spins before getting to the good bits.Viral Spiral: Slot FeaturesHow it works is players hit the spin button, and the reel spins to reveal one of two outcomes – a placeholder symbol which is worth nothing and does nothing, or the Bonus Wheel symbol hits. Landing the Bonus Wheel activates the Bonus Wheel feature, which takes over the screen. The bonus wheel contains 8 segments – 4 losing segments, 3 smaller prize segments, and 1 larger golden coloured prize.For the first Bonus Wheel spin, the winning segments are larger in size than the losing segments, offering a 75% chance of a win. Subsequent wheels have smaller winning segments, offering a 50% chance of winning. If the Bonus Wheel lands on a prize segment, all prizes are increased on the wheel and players are given the choice of collecting their win or gambling to respin the wheel. If the wheel lands on the golden big prize segment, the prizes on the following wheels are increased by a greater amount than when they land on a smaller prize segment.If the wheel lands on a non-winning segment, players lose and go back to the base game empty-handed. In all, players can gamble up to 3 times. The minimum reward offered by the wheel is 15x the bet, while the maximum is 5,000x. It is only possible to spin for the maximum 5,000x if the pointer has landed on the golden big prize segments for each spin.Viral Spiral also comes with a nudge feature, so if the Bonus Wheel symbol doesn't hit in the base game, the reel may be nudged, so it is pushed into view, triggering the feature. Finally, the game supplies a 'best gamble strategy' for interested players. If so, then according to Red Tiger, the best strategy is to gamble twice, then collect the prize.Viral Spiral: Slot VerdictWell, it's different; let's give Viral Spiral that. Will it actually live up to its name and go viral, though? It's a bit difficult to see that happening to be brutally honest. No doubt, in the wide spectrum of online gamblers, there will be some players who will lap Viral Spiral up, and the game has its merits. For one, it is the sort of slot a person could easily have running while they're watching telly or fiddling on their phone. Since most of the time there is nothing but dead spins occurring, you wouldn't miss much, if any, of the action if your attention was elsewhere.Others might be drawn to Viral Spiral's sheer simplicity. It's hard to think of a more pared-back stripped-down game. If one payline is still a little too much, then having one single symbol at a time appear on screen is just the antidote. HarleCoin by Red Tiger came up as a possible alternative, as did Crazy Tooth's Seven 7's, but both of those games are like 4D chess by comparison. Potential in Viral Spiral is good for what it is, and the game can be surprisingly good at hooking you into a seemingly endless tail chase while trying to score the top prize. Since you have to land the Bonus Wheel on the golden top prize segment every single time, actually making it to the 5K happy ending would be quite a trip to witness. Apologies, Viral Spial's downtime provided ample time to kick back and daydream.There may well be players out there who this game was literally made for, but after a bout of being hammered by losing Bonus Wheel gambles, low value wins, not to mention a flood of dead spins, the novelty of Viral Spiral inevitably wore off.

Title: Big Bad Wolf Christmas Special
review: Big Bad Wolf Christmas Special: Slot OverviewReleased in 2013, Big Bad Wolf was one Quickspin's first releases, and an instant hit for the up and coming studio. It could have been a risk using a kids' story to theme a slot, but Big Bad Wolf mixed just the right features, looks, and rewards to see past that to the playable game beneath. It's since garnered a cult status and is just as fun to play as ever. It's no high powered thrill ride, back then slots weren't generally quite as brutally volatile as they are today, yet it remains a guilty pleasure for many all the same. In a move many other developers have made, Big Bad Wolf has been converted into a holiday-friendly version. Like countless TV-shows before it, we now have the Big Bad Wolf Christmas Special.At first glance not too much seems to have changed. Players get the same timber framed 5-reel, 25 payline grid, set somewhere out in the countryside. Even the same barrel of apples sits next to it. This time, however, everything is covered in snow with sprinkles of the season here there such as gift ribbons and the like. One minor change is the payline numbers have gone to make way for decorative lights instead – perhaps the look was too old school. Birds chirp away in the background, making it all feel very familiar. At this point, we should warn players looking for new enhancements; the visual changes will be the only ones found in the game.When it comes to maths and stats, all remains untouched. That means a bet range from 25 p/c to $/€100, medium volatility, and the same excellent 97.34% RTP that played a major part in the success of the original. Again, the math model was one of the original's highlights, so players get the identical gameplay as before.To win, there are 11 regular symbols which pay left to right when at least three land on a payline. The five low win symbols are 10-A card royals, speckled in snow and still look like they've been nailed to the side of crates. Then there are what is termed the four medium win symbols – a soft toy and the three piggy stars of the story. Land 5 of these symbols to cause a payout of 8 to 12 times the stake.It is possible to have up to four different wild symbols in play, but to start with there is just one. This is the beehive wild which substitutes for all symbols except the Wolf Scatter and Moon symbols. The wild also carries a value of its own, paying out when at least two land in a line, or up to 40x the bet for five of a kind.Big Bad Wolf Christmas Special: Slot FeaturesBig Bad Wolf Christmas Special - free spinsPart of Big Bad Wolf's charm was its features. Not only were there a good number of them, but they worked together to enhance each other's effects well. The snowball roll starts with Swooping Reels, leading to Pigs Turn Wild, then Free Spins and finally the Blowing Down the House feature.Pretty common now, a little less so back in 2013, is the Swooping Reels style of feature (more commonly known as 'cascades'). All winning combinations trigger it, which starts by removing the winning symbols from the grid. Empty spaces are then filled by symbols dropping in from above, creating new chances to win from the same spin. Swooping Reels keep on swooping until there are no new winning combinations.Pigs Turn Wild does pretty much what the label suggests. Every 2nd win in a sequence turns a pig into a wild symbol. So the 2nd, 4th, then 6th win turns pig 1, 2, then 3 wild. When no more wins land the piggy wilds revert back to their normal state. This feature appears in the base game as well as free spins.You can tell you are playing the Christmas version because the wolf scatter now wears a Santa hat - 3 or more of these symbols on the reels activates 10 free spins plus pays out 3x the bet as well. Should three scatters land in the bonus game, then 10 more free spins are added to the tally.In free spins, a new moon symbol is introduced on the last reel, to be collected when they land. When 3 are collected, the Big Bad Wolf blows down the house to award +2 free spins. When 6 moons are collected, 2 more spins are added plus an x2 multiplier is applied to any win from then on in the feature.Big Bad Wolf Christmas Special: Slot VerdictIt's fair to say Quickspin has taken the quick and painless route when it came to designing this Christmas remake. Aside from a few graphical changes, everything even down to the second decimal place of the RTP is exactly the same as the original, meaning this is merely a reskin. Few fans of the original will be complaining too loudly though, as they now get the perfect excuse to blow houses down again in a re-release.Quite a lot of time has passed between the two games, yet the experience actually feels pretty contemporary. Cascades, reactions, swoops, or whatever you want to call them, are still red hot, appearing in countless games. What's interesting is with the proliferation of Megaways and the like, operating Swoops on a 25-payline grid should feel more restrictive than it does. On the contrary, the mechanic works just as well in Big Bad Wolf Christmas Special as anywhere else. Where the game might fail to ignite the fire of modern big win chasers is in potential, which tops out around 1,200 times your bet.But hey, it's nice to have a range of options to choose from, especially if you're stuck inside for the holiday season looking for something to play that isn't quite brutal enough to wreck your holiday spirit. For many, Big Bad Wolf Christmas Special is sure to be a pleasant trip down memory lane, a snowy one this time.

Title: East Sea Dragon King
review: East Sea Dragon King (NetEnt): OverviewAbout a year ago, NetEnt released Berryburst Max, a 5x3 slot that uses Cluster Pays and bright, fruity symbols. If you swap the theme from fruit to Asian and move the slot beneath the sea, you have nailed East Sea Dragon King to a tee. If you are familiar with Berryburst Max, then this will come as no surprise, but if you are used to (and prefer) a more elaborate slot then East Sea Dragon King feels like it is missing an extra or two. After all, we are dealing with a sea god here, something that really opened up the game and expanded the Dragon King's character would have been a welcome addition to the repetitive gameplay.The game is very volatile and usually involves a lot of dead spins. In turn, however, there is potential for wins of up to 6,000 times your stake which is not bad. Statistically, wins of over 2,500x occurs only once every 1 million spins. It might not sound very uplifting, but you should keep in mind that all players playing the game contribute to the spin cycle.East Sea Dragon King (NetEnt): VerdictEast Sea Dragon King is another strategic release from NetEnt looking to  further expand their market in Asia. This is done simply by giving some of their old games a makeover, which is not very exciting for those already familiar with these games. Despite giving developers, some leeway East Sea Dragon King still feels a little flat. The slot gets repetitive quickly and does nothing extraordinary to hold your interest.NetEnt's cluster pays system is great, but even that can't save a slot like East Sea Dragon King. A year can be an eternity in the entertainment industry, but Berryburst Max feels fresh and new in comparison. If you didn't know better, you would think it was the follow up to East Sea Dragon King. The soundtrack was epic, and the ripe fruit symbols looked like they were about to burst. In contrast, the graphics used on East Sea Dragon King, especially the symbols, are, well, not up to NetEnt's high standard. What it is really lacking is some x-factor, a unique or compelling feature that makes you want to keep hitting the spin button. This is NetEnt after all, a company with one of the best hit-packed back catalogues you will find in the business.So why play East Sea Dragon King? NetEnt fanatics or fans of Asian themed slots might find something to keep them going for a while, especially if you're into high high risk slots with a chance for high rewards. If you are not in either of these camps then it is unlikely you will find your slot fix here. Bigger audio, visuals, and thrills can be found elsewhere.

Title: Big Top Terror
review: Big Top Terror: Slot OverviewCircuses, in some ways like the clowns populating them, have this strange ability to be a canvas for both fabulous dream spaces where the wondrous may occur as well as hideous freak shows where terror reigns supreme. Perhaps they're a reflection of the human psyche, which has an enormous capacity for both love and hate. It's the scarier side of circuses that we're exploring today, courtesy of Yggdrasil Gaming's partner Hungry Bear. However, the game did trigger thoughts of Pragmatic Play's Zombie Carnival, Stakelogic's The Haunted Circus, as well as Play'n GO's 3 Clown Monty 2, amongst others, and Big Top Terror manages to forge its own place in the circus slot lineup.Big Top Terror slot - base gameTo roll up, roll up, in this game, gamblers are able to select a stake which suits them from 20 c to $/€5 per game round. Combinations may be up to 5 symbols in length, and all must begin on the leftmost reel.
