Title: Blade & Fangs
review: Blade & Fangs: Slot OverviewWith a name like Blade & Fangs, it's unlikely we're going to be dealing with candy, leprechauns, or fruit this time around. No, indeed, Blade & Fangs is a horror slot from software provider Pragmatic Play that possesses pointy objects of varying descriptions. Like horror movies tend to do, this one has a twist as well. The twist is that the gaming, for the most part, takes place on two separate gaming grids. However, land two knife-stabbing flower symbols on the outermost reels and the two grids merge to form a larger one during respins and free spins.Thematically, Blade & Fangs looks and sounds pretty decent, but it also felt like it lacked any sort of absorbing story. It's like a potpourri of horror images and audio thrown together into a vat of coagulating substances to see what might ooze out the other side. It's held in a room that looks like an altar part of a church, carpeted in skulls and lit by mysteriously shimmering light. Spooky sound effects are layered over the music, which occasionally goes all metal, sealing a horrific atmosphere – though one somewhat spoiled by the upbeat, celebratory tunes present in win counts. It's decent, but it also felt somewhat scattered as a story.Blade & Fangs slot - base gameWhile deciding what's best blades or fangs, spare a moment to decide what sort of wager you'd like to make. The choices are 20 c to $/€240 per spin, and a buy feature is available as well. The RTP comes out at 96.05%, no matter how Blade & Fangs is played, and runs on a highly volatile math model. Its USP is the split screen setup, so you've got one 5x3 grid up top and one 5x3 grid down the bottom – both with 243 ways to win.Both land the same set of symbols as well, which means pointy metal 10 to A card royals for the low pays, then a bat, a snake, a ghoul, a wolf, and a skeleton as the high pays. Hitting a 5-of-a-kind low pay win awards 1 to 1.5 times the stake, or 2 to 10 times the stake is awarded for landing 5 matching premium symbols. Interestingly, Blade & Fangs does not have wild symbols, but it has a scatter and two multiplier symbols.Blade & Fangs: Slot FeaturesBlade & Fangs slot - free spinsBoth gaming grids have their own specific multiplier symbol, which works together by joining the separate reel sets. As well as this are free spins with a general multiplier and a buy feature.Multiplier SymbolsThe +1x multiplier symbol may land on the leftmost reel of the top grid, while the x2 multiplier appears on the rightmost reel on the lower grid. Whenever both multiplier symbols land at the same time in the base game, the two sets of reels merge into a single 6x5 grid, and a respin is awarded. For the respin, a general multiplier of x2 applies to any wins. If an +1x multiplier symbol hits on the respin, the general multiplier increases by +1. If an x2 multiplier hits, the general multiplier is multiplied by x2. At the end of the respin, all wins are multiplied by the general multiplier, and the game splits back to two 5x3 screens.Free SpinsThe flaming skull scatter symbol appears on reels 2, 3, and 4. Hitting 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols awards 2x, 15x, 100x, or 500x the bet, respectively, plus 8 free spins. Free spins are always played on a merged 6x5 screen, and a general multiplier is active throughout, starting on x1. Every time a +1x multiplier symbol hits, +1 is added to the general multiplier, and every time an x2 multiplier hits, the general multiplier is multiplied by x2. Landing 3 or more scatter symbols awards an extra +4 free spins.Buy Free SpinsPlayers may buy free spins for 100 times the total bet. When buying free spins, 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols randomly land on the triggering spin.Blade & Fangs slot - free spinsBlade & Fangs: Slot VerdictLike a too-floppy pizza or one with not enough cheese, Blade & Fangs didn't quite hit the spot. As part of Pragmatic Play's heavy schedule, the developer is more than capable of firing off hits, but Blade & Fangs came across as more of a miss as if it was hastily put together or the team came up with some good ideas then floundered and weren't totally sure or couldn't agree on what to make of the prototype parts. Blade & Fangs felt sort of bitsy like the Prag bigwigs really wanted a two-grid game that merged but didn't have the side features to really make it all come together and pop. The theme, too. Blade & Fangs just didn't grip the way Darkness or Serial did and lacked the personality of, say, Hellvis Wild or even Demon Pots.Blade & Fangs, for most of the time (if not on a bonus buy binge), is basically two grids simultaneously spinning with not a lot actually happening. Multiplier symbols drop here and there to tease, and occasionally, two will hit, thereby bringing both reel sets together. Then, okay, tension levels do get the chance to spike on respins having so much more grid space and ways to work with. Respins are a taster for the free spins phase since the grids are stuck together for the duration of the round, not to mention the useful inclusion of a rising win multiplier. With a win cap of 5,000x the bet and decent stats, there is no doubt Blade & Fangs can technically shock (in a good way).Then again, pretty much any slot can shock when the right symbols hit and all. So, while a passable horror game possessing the usual Pragmatic Play pizzazz, Blade & Fangs wasn't one that caused much running off into the night in terror, or creeping back for repeat sessions.

Title: IO
review: Io Slot: OverviewThe cosmically named Io is the second slot from developer ELK Studios to use their Gravity mechanic. The first, Cygnus, was another mysterious slot based in Egypt, but with an eye towards the stars. Io takes it one step further by locating the action up there amongst the celestial bodies. As well as the Gravity mechanic causing symbols to tumble randomly left or right, players get a host of features to accompany them on their trip off-world.The voyage takes us to Jupiter where Io is one of its moons. This is no diplomatic mission to the stars though. It's actually a lot more amusing, described by ELK as a casino space station embarking on a journey to the frontiers of the solar system. Kind of like Captain Kirk on the Starship Enterprise, except the task here is to collect valuable minerals from the moon. It's all a bit of a laugh really, setting a jovial mode on the proceedings.On each spin, 24 symbols fall into a grid made up of 6 columns, 4 rows, and 4,096 ways to win. Winning combinations form when three or more matching symbols land consecutively from the first column onwards. They can appear on any row and yet be a winner, hence the large number of win ways. Before getting started, players choose regular bets of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, or plump for one of ELK's four betting strategies.Whenever a winner hits, the symbols involved in the combo vanish off the screen thanks to the Avalanche mechanic. When this occurs, symbols gravitate into the gaps, potentially creating more winning combos. Unlike most slots, the columns do not sit flush, so when symbols slink downwards, they can fall either left or right depending on gravity.Avalanches also add an extra row, maxing out at 8 in height. Should you reach this level, then an uncountable 262,144 win ways come into play. Avalanches also mean long chains of wins can occur as gaps are plugged by the appropriate symbols to keep the procedure going. Once no new winners appear, then the next new spin begins.As to symbols, the paytable has 8 regulars, divided into high and low pays. All are round disks, displaying classic slot icons such as J-A royals, stars, clovers, diamonds, and lucky sevens. Lucky sevens are worth the most at 5 times the stake for six of a kind, dropping to 0.20x for six Js. Helping cobble together combos, Io offers three wilds; one is a standard, the other are the Charged and Forge Wild covered below. Despite each one playing different roles, all wilds can substitute for any of the regular pay symbols.A minor case of déjà vu flashed up when investigating the math model since it is almost identical to the one used before. That's not necessarily a bad thing though, because it produces some solid numbers to back up the gameplay. Roll on volatility which has been rated at 8/10, putting it in the medium to high range. Hit frequency is slightly higher than before on 24.6%, though RTP takes a tiny nudge downwards to 96%. Overall, players who like a bit more variance in their gaming will be satisfied, as they will be by the equally solid potential.Io Slot: FeaturesIo - free drops triggeredAs mentioned, there are 2 special wilds working alongside the standard wild. First is the Charged Wild which starts with 4 lives. It remains on the game area throughout a full reaction sequence and each time a Charged Wild is used as part of a win, it loses a life. When all 4 lives are gone, it vanishes off the grid.Next, is the Wild Forge symbol eagle-eyed players may recognise in an altered form from Tahiti Gold or Voodoo Gold. In Io, when a Wild Forge appears, it fills an empty space below it with a multiplier wild. The value of the multiplier increases each time the Wild Forge is used with no set limit on how high it can go. If the Wild Forge falls to the bottom of the grid, it becomes a wild multiplier.Getting to the big bucks, or precious minerals as they are known around here, requires harnessing the features. To help you on your way, ELK has included the Laser feature. When the laser  symbols land, they shoot a beam of light, destroying itself as well as any regular symbols in its path, letting new ones slip into the empty spaces. If the beams from two laser symbols intersect, the symbols along the beams up to the intersection point become wilds.Keep an eye out for the bonus symbols - 3 or more in view trigger the free drops bonus game. At least 7 free drops are awarded, up to 15 for 6 bonus symbols in view - keeping in mind free drops can be retriggered too. During the feature, the grid expands to its full 8x8 size, and any Charged Wilds or Wild Forge symbols remain sticky at the bottom of the grid between spins for the full duration.Io Slot: VerdictWe might have traveled to the frontiers of space, but there isn't a huge amount players won't have seen before if they've played Cygnus. Aside from Jupiter out of the viewport, and some feature alterations, it's a whole lot like its predecessor. Even the math model is virtually the same as before, aside from a teensy drop of 0.1% in RTP. Potential has remained the same too on 5,000 times the stake, so no complaints there.Graphically, Io is not as striking as Cygnus, nor as atmospheric, so if that's a concern, then the original wins out as the best one to go for. Otherwise, it comes down to feature preference. Io doesn't have the progressive multiplier quite like the first, but Forge Wilds go a long way to making up for it. Not to mention sticky wilds during free drops which can do some serious damage.In a way, the Gravity mechanic series is looking like it might pan out like the Gold series. That means, retaining core stats and mechanics while making tweaks to features and scenery - and why not? It's a formula that has served Kane in the Gold series well, so there is no reason why it won't work in the Gravity range too.The biggest difference really is the general approach to the theme. Whereas Cygnus was all about the mysticism, Io has a more light-hearted back story, and it is kind of fun pretending to be on a space casino revolving around an exotic moon, collecting precious minerals. Of course, a nice story is nothing in a slot without the gameplay or potential backing it up. Fortunately, Io comes up trumps in those regards, so while it's not exactly a brand new experience, it's a satisfying one all the same.

Title: Big Bass - Keeping it Reel

Title: Dragonz
review: Dragonz: OverviewDragons in popular culture generally come in two forms - deadly beasts that lay waste to whole cities, or cutie pie monsters that would rather hug you than set you on fire. Developer Microgaming has chosen the latter option and filled their slot Dragonz with four friendly characters. The gang isn’t just for show either; each dragon livens up the reels and brings a different set of free spins with them. The uncomplicated, fast-paced gameplay of Dragonz makes the perfect accompaniment to the features which can fly free when triggered.Dragonz - Gobble sticky wilds free spinsA sweet animation opens up the game and introduces players to the four starring dragons. Microgaming has set the slot in the great outdoors on a deep green meadow against a clear blue sky. In the distance, floating rock structures add a subtle yet mystical dimension to the proceedings and the location shifts to reflect the various free spin rounds. The soundtrack is a good one too, with a fantasy rich vibe, spreading on an extra thick layer of atmosphere.To get the adventure going, players can choose a stake from 40 p/c up to $/€30 per spin. Other stats include an above-average RTP of 96.46% and a math model set to a medium/high level which provides a range of payouts from the small and frequent to the large and rarer.As mentioned, the game is pretty straight forward and consists of a classic Microgaming set up of 5 reels, 3 rows, and 243 win ways. Without paylines, winning combinations are formed when at least three matching symbols land consecutively from left to right on any row.The game includes 10 regular pay symbols with which to do so, divided into 6 low and 4 high pays. The low pays are standard 9-A royals, with little distinguishing characteristics to speak of. High pays are far more interesting and include the four dragons that are named Gobble, Frost, Switch, and Flint and offer payouts from 6.25x to 12.5x the stake for five of a kind. The base game avoids getting overly repetitive thanks to a beneficial wild symbol, not to mention the fine selection of bonus games.Dragonz: FeaturesKeep an eye out for the wild symbol during the base game, because should it land on the third reel on a non-winning spin, it adds additional wilds to the other reels for a guaranteed win. This feature has been named the Wild Deal and players will be glad to know that it pops up quite often to help soften the blow of landing non-winning spins. Wilds also payout when they appear in combinations of 3 or more, up to 15 times the stake for 5 of a kind.Clearly the wild, and the Wild Deal, is a boon, but the symbol you really want is the sparkling purple gem scatter. Should at least 3 appear in view, then one of the Free Spins features is triggered. Initially, one will be selected at random, but once free spins have been triggered 12 times, players can choose the one they would like to play from then on. Each of the four options comes with 10 free spins and the following modifiers:Gobble Free Spins with Winning Wilds. During this bonus game, Gobble spits wilds onto the reels at random which stay stuck in place as long as they are part of winning combination. This can lead to a substantial portion of free spins with the help of those sticky wilds in place.Frost Free Spins with Frosty Wilds. Frost flows across the reels and freezes any non-winning wilds in place until they contribute to a win. Free spins will continue until no frozen wilds are remaining on the grid, so there can be more than 10 spins in total.Switch Free Spins with Stashed Wilds. Switch collects any wilds that appear but do not contribute to a winning combination. When 3 or more have been collected, they are distributed on the reels at random to create a guaranteed win. Like Frost Free Spins, free spins with Switch will continue until all wild symbols are distributed.Flint Free Spins with Flaming Wilds. Flint likes fire, and each time he blows flames, he shoots wilds onto the reels at random. The number of wilds increases the more he does so with up to ten Flaming Wilds possible.On top of triggering bonus games, 2, 3, 4, or 5 scatters in view also award juicy payouts of 1x, 2x, 10x, or 100x the total bet staked respectively.Dragonz: VerdictDespite the subject matter, Dragonz isn’t a frightening monster of a slot. It fact, it’s one of those games that is just straight-up fun to play. Microgaming has struck a sweet balance by combining a pleasing look with charming characters and infectious gameplay via its features.This might be a world populated with dragons, but it is also the realm of the wild symbol. These useful symbols pop up all over the place and contribute to a nicely flowing base game with potential for massive payouts and bonus games that can transform into wild fests in a moment. Wins of 3,000 times the stake and more are possible from single spins, so Dragonz is also a slot that doesn’t come up short in the rewards department either.Dragonz might not be a game you fire up to be dazzled by cutting edge features or a brutal math model. Instead, it provides solid, entertaining gaming by covering the basics, adding in some great free spins options and piling on the appeal via its adorable characters. For something a little more light-hearted, and utterly charming, it doesn't get much better than Dragonz.

Title: Retro Tapes Cluster Link

Magnets land anywhere and pick a random pay symbol type, and pull them around its position to create a cluster win. Or, Magnets can also pull Instant Prize symbols if there are at least four of them in view, creating a cluster. Once the pay symbols or Instant Prize symbols have been attracted, the Magnet transforms into the same pay symbol type or an Instant Prize symbol of random value.Top Charts FeatureWhen at least 3 Wild Tape symbols are in view, the Top Charts feature is triggered. Landing 3, 4, 5, or 6 Wild Tapes awards 6, 8, 10, or 12 free spins, respectively. When triggered, the Wild Tape symbols and Instant Prizes on the board are carried over from the base game to the bonus round, stuck in their same positions. During the feature, each empty position spins to land a:Wild Tape symbol - as well as their usual duties, any new Wild Tape that hits awards an additional 2 free spins.Wild Multiplier symbolInstant Prize symbolMagnet symbol – highlights part of the grid and pulls in Instant Prizes around its position.Extra Spins symbol – awards 1 or 2 extra free spins, then transforms into an Instant Prize of random value.Blank Tape symbol – has no value and does not stick.Each Instant Prize symbol that lands remains in place until the feature ends, and wins are evaluated when the feature finishes. This occurs when spins run out or all positions are filled.Retro Tapes Cluster Link slot - free spinsRetro Tapes Cluster Link: Slot VerdictIt was easy to see Retro Tapes Cluster Link as an evolution of the iconic slot Jammin' Jars and its less iconic follow-up Jammin' Jars 2. Once immersed in the cheeky-eyed cassette tape world, the differences become more apparent, though, and on the whole, Retro Tapes Cluster Link offered quite a different gaming experience. There are similarities, however. One is mechanics, which can make it mercilessly tough to get ahead. It might pay to fortify yourself with ample lashings of fortitude, patience, and thick skin to weather what could be a full-frontal assault by those seemingly innocuous-looking yet potentially unsympathetic tapes. The same kind of thing goes for the bonus round, which has a hold 'n win element as certain symbols stack on the board but does not reset the spin count when new symbols hit as such. In other words, it's very different to the leaping progressive multiplier wilds of Jammin' Jars and more related instead to Jammin' Jars 2. As for potential, it's decent, clocking in at 10,000 times the stake. For those who like to know the odds, the probability of hitting the top prize is 1 in 1,248,439.Retro Tapes Cluster Link didn't quite create the same level of insta-affection as a game like Jammin' Jars did, but thanks to a blend of numbers, volatility, fun vibe, features, and flow, there is no doubt some fine gaming for the right player to discover. Weigh it all up, and cluster-paying grid slot enthusiasts have a solid cassette tape-filled option to pop on their to-try games list.

Title: Crystal Falls Multimax
review: Crystal Falls MultiMax: Slot OverviewBulletproof Games is a UK based studio located in the cathedral city of Lichfield, a few miles north of Birmingham. The studio has a few slots under its belt though none have made particularly large waves until Crystal Falls MultiMax - thanks to its association with Yggdrasil's YGS Program. A collection of gems land across a 5-reel, 3-row game grid, providing 20 fixed paylines to land winners on. Aside from a grim, dark cave and a low key ambient soundtrack, there's not much else to report on audio-visually.Available on any device, Crystal Falls MultiMax comes with two types of stakes – regular and Encore enhanced. Regularly priced stakes range from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, and when the Encore feature is activated, costs increase by 50%. For the extra charge, players improve their chances of winning free spins. Speaking of spins, around 1 in 4 (23%) will dole out some form of payment, contributing to a theoretical return value of 95%. Paired with medium-high volatility is mid-level potential at odds when seeing what the features are capable of.Players score coins when two or three matching symbols land adjacently from the left-hand side of the grid. It's precious stones all the way as single gems of various colours make up the low pays, while gem clusters are the high-value symbols paying up to 20x the bet for five of a mind. Wilds come into their own during free spins, though in all phases of the game, they are used to replace any pay symbols to complete a winning line.Crystal Falls MultiMax: Slot FeaturesCrystal Falls MultiMax brings together a Cascade+ feature, the aforementioned Encore ante bet, and free spins, making use of a MultiMax feature on loan from Yggdrasil. First thing to know is winning symbols are cleared from the grid when they hit, allowing symbols to drop into the gaps. Chains of winning cascades roll on in this way until no new combinations appear.While this is going on, players move along a progressive trail located to the left of the screen. The trail's position increases by one step for every cascade in the base game, and 4 consecutive wins trigger 7 free spins. Landing more than 4 consecutive wins leads onto 10, 12, or 18 free spins, before maxing out at 25.When no more winning combinations land and free spins are not won, the trail resets back to its starting level. However, if the Encore bet is engaged, two positions on the trail are converted to respins rather than losing positions. This means if you don't manage to trigger free spins, if the trail sits on a respin position, you get an extra chance to progress. The Encore feature increases the likelihood of triggering free spins from 1 in 140 to 1 in 62.During MultiMax free spins, multipliers starting at x1 sit above each reel. When a wild symbol lands, the multiplier above it increases by +1. Payline wins are multiplied by the multipliers on each applicable reel. For example, a three of a kind win would have the multipliers on reels 1-3 multiply the win - one after the other to build value. Moreover, the Cascade+ trail still applies during the bonus round, where three positions get you +3 extra free spins. From there, it is possible to win 7, 10, 12, 18, or 25 additional free spins if you progress far enough.Lastly, if you live in a country where bonus buys are allowed, Crystal Falls MultiMax offers one for 100x the bet. This starts the Cascade+ trail on the 10 free spins position for the next spin.Crystal Falls MultiMax: Slot VerdictHovering up every designer and their dog ensures a huge range of games are firing through the YGS Program. By sucking up every studio that isn't tied down has seen the quality become a bit of a mixed bag. There are the hits, to be sure, but lower grade games slip the net at ever-increasing rates. Sure, different strokes for different folks, and it's nice to have a range of options to please as many types of gamblers as possible, but at times it feels like quantity rather than quality is the overriding driver. Crystal Falls MultiMax stokes this response further, being a jumble of good and not so good elements.Let's hope Bulletproof lives up to their game because there are few constructive criticisms to make about Crystal Falls MultiMax. The first thing is the game is pretty average looking, and that is putting it politely. Looks are only skin deep, yet they are largely responsible for making the first impression, and Crystal Falls MultiMax doesn't exactly provoke much excitement when it first lights up your monitor.It's a missed opportunity because the features which follow are quite good. The Encore feature is a nice addition and slashes the wait time needed to trigger free spins. Respins don't always lead to free spins, of course, but they add an extra thrill when they trigger, adding to the experience. The bonus game is quite well thought out, too, though very close to Yggdrasil's own Multifly game. Then again, you'd expect so when borrowing a feature.As well as Crystal Falls MultiMax' decidedly average looks, its potential also lags when considering what the makers claim free spin multipliers can achieve. If so, then mission accomplished. However, this is unlikely to be the case. Still, when you trace Crystal Falls MultiMax' roots, it's hard not to come away with the impression it's a less attractive, less lucrative version of Multifly. It's a shame because Crystal Falls MultiMax could have been significantly better with a bit of spit and polish.

Title: White Wolf Moon

Only Bronze, Silver, and Gold Money symbols or blanks appear in the bonus round, and Money symbols lock in position when they hit.Bronze coins have possible values of 1x to 100x, or 1.5x to 500x, or 2x to 1,000x the bet if the feature was triggered by 3, 4, or 5 scatters, respectively.Silver coins have possible values of 2x to 500x, or 3x to 2,500x, or 4x to 5,000x the bet if the feature was triggered by 3, 4, or 5 scatters, respectively.Bronze coins have possible values of 4x to 1,000x, or 6x to 5,000x, or 8x to 10,000 the bet if the feature was triggered by 3, 4, or 5 scatters, respectively.The feature starts with 3 respins, which reset to 3 whenever a new Money symbol lands and locks. Title: Primal Spirits
review: Primal Spirits: Slot OverviewIf games are a reflection of the teams that make them, then whoever was behind Primal Spirits at Quickspin could well have been trying to get deeply in tune with nature. It was wondering whether Quickspin had poached an artist or two from competitor studio Peter & Sons. In Primal Spirits, things like the higher-value animal symbols, fonts, and general look, could easily pass for a P&S game. Whether there is a link or not, who knows? Wilds land on any reel to substitute all paying symbols and trigger out payouts of up to 5x the bet when making wins solely of wild symbols.Primal Spirits: Slot FeaturesPrimal Spirits slot - free spinsPrimal Spirits is not a complicated game, but it's not entirely straightforward either. It takes a few spins and a bit of paytable study to fully grasp what's going on.Tumbling ReelsThe first piece of the puzzle is Tumbling Reels, which removes winning symbols from the grid. Existing symbols drop-down and new symbols from up above fill the gaps.Totem TranceAfter a tumble, if the top part of the Totem on the left is blue, green, purple, or red, then any low pay symbols of this specific colour on the reels are transformed into its high pay counterpart. If the Top left Totem is golden, it upgrades all low-pay symbols in view. After the transformation takes place, if a new win is created, the Tumbling Reels is triggered.Colour MultiplierWhen the Totem Trance transforms a symbol and a win or free spin will follow, it adds +1 to its respective Colour Multiplier on the right-side Totem. Paying 150x the bet triggers the Thunder Free Spins feature.Primal Spirits slot - free spinsPrimal Spirits: Slot VerdictPrimal Spirits was a peculiar game to review. Subtly peculiar. When all was said and done, it was hard to tell whether the experience had been a fulfilling one or not. In some ways, more questions were raised after the test drive was complete than before it. The first puzzle was whether someone from Peter & Sons had had a hand in the game's development or not or whether it was a complete coincidence. The thing is, Peter & Sons' games are so distinct that if anyone copied them, whether by accident or design, a counterfeit would stick out like a sore thumb. Not pointing any fingers, just saying.The enigma flowed into the mechanics and features underpinning Primal Spirits. Are they good or not? We flip-flopped from one side of the question to the other, unable to definitively answer it. When Tumbles trigger Totem Trances, feeding Colour Multipliers leading to something decent at the end, then great, what an innovative trip. When it doesn't, the transformations and multipliers sort of meander. Perhaps it'll help if you're down with the subject matter? Not sure; Primal Spirits was a slippery one to pin down. There shouldn't be too many misgivings over the max win, though, Quickspin having recorded a win of 8,623x the bet during 100 million simulated spins.Hey, there's sure to be plenty of open-mind players out there, keen to sample the wide, varied, and at times downright weirdness served up by a creative industry. Title: Wild O'Clock
review: Wild O’Clock: OverviewCreative types go through patches where the proverbial writer's block sinks in. They sit down at their keyboard, or notepads, or whiteboards, or whatever it is to get the creative juices flowing, then… nothing. Other times, ideas are popping up left right and centre, as a geyser of creativity pours forth in an unstoppable tidal wave of expression. This seems to be the case with Red Tiger at the moment, releasing a floodgate of slots that is tough to keep up with at times.Coincidentally, time is the very essence of this review. While some claim time is merely an illusion, Wild O'Clock is built around the handy device used for measuring the stuff – the humble clock. It's ticking mechanism not only provides the theme but drives the tempo of the game. Some physicists argue time could just as easily have moved backwards as forward, yet since we are stuck with the latter, let's move on and delve into the abstract world of Wild O'Clock.The action takes place on a 6-reel, 4-row slot with 30 paylines to land winners on. If you've played these sorts of Red Tiger games before it will feel familiar immediately. There is plenty of gold trim, and the spacious grid is full of nice-looking symbols. The location of the game appears to be the inside of a clock or a clock maker's studio perhaps? It's not super obvious, but it's mysterious wherever it is. Adding to the scene is a music box soundtrack adding an extra layer of mystery.Players take part by selecting stakes from 10 p/c to $/€40 per spin, on any device. As noted in the Lord of the Wilds review, RTP appears to be on a downward creep in these Red Tiger fillers. In Wild O'Clock, players get a default rate of 95.69%, coupled with medium/high volatility. As is often the case, this can lead to extended bouts of base game naval-gazing before the slot deems you worthy of entry to the bonus. Like an exclusive club event, you haven't got an invite to.Before reaching the inner sanctum, here are a few base game rules. Land six of a kind from this group for payouts of 2.5x to 10x the stake.The standard wild looks pretty neat too, designed as an esoteric sun and moon worth the same as the highest paying symbol. There are two wilds; this one appears on any reel in 1x1 size to substitute for all paying symbols.Wild O’Clock: FeaturesWild O'Clock - free spinsWild O'Clock doesn't have a ton of features, but the way they are set up means something regularly happens, like, um, clockwork. This is chiefly due to the Lucky O'Clock feature, but Multiplier Wilds also pop up, while the game climaxes during the triggered batch of Clock Spins.Just as there are 12 hours on a clock, every 12 spins the Lucky O'Clock feature kicks in. A clock mechanism displayed above the reels increases by one hour on each spin. When it strikes 12 a random number of Super Wilds are added to the reels. Super Wilds are 1x4 sized wilds that always cover a full reel, substituting for all pay symbols. Up to 6 Super Wilds may appear for a full-screen win of 300x the stake.When wild symbols participate in a win, there is a chance they randomly become Multiplier Wilds. If they do, a multiplier of up to x8 appears and is applied to any combos on the win line.The coup de grace is the round of Clock Spins, triggered when 3 clock spins scatters are in view - 12 bonus spins are awarded with a global multiplier that is applied to all wins. Every time a wild is used in a win, it reveals a value which is added to the global multiplier. On the 12th Clock Spin, a random number of Super Wilds are added to the reels for a potentially final big win. This feature makes it easier to wait for Clock Spins, causing time to travel a little faster than normal. Still, when you study the stats, goodwill starts to eke away like sands in an hourglass as it often does in a Red Tiger filler.The bonus round isn't a bad one either, though it can be as temperamental as the rest of the game. Title: Joker Split
review: Joker Split: Slot OverviewPrepare for some potential side-splitting as we join Relax Gaming on a trip back to the Middle Ages to be entertained by jokers, those jesters of the court in the online slot Joker Split. Splitting is an apt verb, too, because Joker Split is all about splitting its joker wild symbols then flinging them back onto the board through respin sequences. It's also got free spins, a bonus buy, and a tightrope of a post-bonus round feature that can really make or break a day. And so, for a joker-filled peek at an earlier time period before mobile phones and penicillin, come take a look at Joker Split with us.Depending on the source, in the year 1,000, the population of Europe has been estimated to be approximately 40-60 million people. Whatever the exact number, there were significantly fewer people than now - a reality reflected by Joker Split's empty town square setting. The game's visuals reinforce the journey back to the Middle Ages, where a 6x6 grid sits in the middle of an urban location surrounded by charming Middle Agey buildings. It's hard to put a finger on, yet there was something a little retro about Joker Split. Not so much in the graphics, but some of the sound effects, perhaps, or the constant meandering of the music? It's nothing like Hellcatraz or Banana Town, obviously, but there's a touch. Maybe it's got something to do with the sound wild symbols make when they don't do anything and turn grey or some of the UI button sounds. A small touch, anyway.Joker Split slot - base gameJoker Split is a cluster paying slot which means wins are created when clusters of at least 5 identical pay symbols land, connected in horizontal or vertical directions. The joker wild symbol substitutes for all pay symbols on the gaming board. Wilds may have multiplier values which are applied to any cluster win the wild is involved in. On a respin, the wilds from the previous spin jump back onto the gaming area. If a wild jumps onto a position that already contains a wild, their multipliers are added together.Free SpinsScatter symbols are collected when they land. Collecting 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols awards 5, 6, or 7 free spins, respectively. Respins can be triggered in free spins. In free spins, any wild not used in a winning cluster is stored outside the reels. On the first respin of each free spin, all stored wilds become regular wilds and jump back onto the reels. This is possible as long as the total multiplier of the stored wilds is less than x200. When bought, one free spin is played where the stored wilds from the last free spin round remain and are reactivated by landing a new wild that forms a win. Any wilds stored from the bought extra spin are kept. The theoretical RTP for buying extra free spins is 96.5%.Joker Split slot - free spinsJoker Split: Slot VerdictIt's interesting, whilst total faith remains in Relax Gaming's ability to turn out some of the most frighteningly good slots ever made, the studio's releases have been a little patchy of late. Perhaps Money Train 4 looming on the horizon (at the time of review) was hoovering up the lion's share of Relax Gaming's resources and ideas, so supporting acts like Joker Split ended up getting less love than they might have done. Of course, this speculation might be way off the mark, but just a thought.Joker Split has its moments, though, when stacks of wilds are flying around the gaming board, landing on top of each other, increasing multipliers and creating winning clusters and so on. It's got some good ideas, and the action can get hectic at times. Joker Split is helped along in free spins since non-used wilds are collected off-screen, just waiting to be flung back onto the reels. Excellent when it all pans out, potentially expensive when it doesn't, and tempting to hit the 'Yes' button to buy it to see what happens in any case. Maybe tread carefully with it, as the price could quite quickly ratchet up, and the limit kick in rather soon, too.Gamblers who liked the way they could push their luck at the end of a round of free spins in Wild Yield might have their interest piqued by Joker Split, which offers a similar ride. Its splitting wilds idea has positives, and few would complain about the 20,000x the bet max win. And so, Joker Split has its upsides, but it also feels like it's struggling to step out of the shadows cast by Relax Gaming's finer stuff.

Title: Mighty Griffin Megaways

Title: Grand Melee
review: Grand Melee: Slot OverviewPlay a fantasy video game or RPG, and there's a good chance your character will be armed with a ranged weapon or a melee weapon, or a mixture of both. Ranged weapons, like a bow, for example, are good because you can pick enemies off before they get within striking distance. Unless, of course, they've got a weapon with a greater range than yours. But you also can't beat getting stuck in with a hearty melee weapon like an axe or mace and just cracking some pixelated heads. Today we're getting stuck into Grand Melee, an online slot from software designer Thunderkick. This is a sticky winning symbol respins-type slot that bends the rules of how these games usually go. Something new(ish) to sample then, so why don't we gear up for a bit of melee-ing and see how it fares?The first impression was surprisingly low-key for a Thunderkick game. Not that there's anything off-putting about Grand Melee's looks or sounds, but it didn't leap off the screen like a Thunderkick slot often does. Down the bottom, we've got a crowd of spectators watching the show, which takes place on a gaming matrix up on like a raised stage or something, with a couple of striped pavilions and trees to the sides of it. Even further into the background, a castle rises up, reinforcing the idea players have travelled back in time to somewhere like Europe in the Middle Ages to take Grand Melee on.Grand Melee slot - base gameDescribed by its maker as a highly volatile slot, Grand Melee produces a default theoretical return to player of 96.17%. Its game grid consists of 5 reels holding 4 symbols each, utilising an unusual connected pay ways system. Basically, wins begin on the leftmost reel and must be connected to each other across at least 3 adjacent reels, flush or corner to corner. If this sounds confusing, the paytable has a handy picture of how it all works.The paytable also has value information on its 10 regular paying symbols. The lower value 5 are 10-A card symbols, worth 1 to 1.5 times the bet for a 5 OAK win, while the 5 higher value bunch are characters of varying colours and looks. Hitting a win made up of 5 matching premium symbols pays 3 to 10 times the bet.Grand Melee: Slot FeaturesGrand Melee slot - respin featureGrand Melee does not have wild symbols, but it has a scatter, and several special symbols can land during the respins feature. The other feature to look out for is free spins.Sticky Respin FeatureWhen randomly triggered, the Sticky Respin feature picks an arbitrary symbol (though not Symbol Upgrade, Symbol Expansion, or Game Area Expansion symbols) and displays it above the reels. If at least 5 of these chosen symbols land anywhere on the grid, they turn sticky and lock into position. During the respin feature, landing new chosen symbols also locks them in place, while the other positions respin. When no new chosen symbols hit, a win evaluation of the sticky symbols takes place and the feature ends. During respins, special symbols may also land:Symbol Upgrade feature – this symbol may appear to transform all instances of the sticky symbols into more valuable sticky symbols.Symbol Expansion feature – this symbol may appear to transform into the sticky symbol type then expand to vertically cover the whole reel.Game Area Expansion feature – this symbol may land to transform into the sticky symbol type and add a new row to the top of the grid. At most, the grid can be 7 rows high.Bonus GameLanding 5 or more scatter symbols triggers the bonus game. This may also occur during the Sticky Respin feature if the scatter symbol is shown in the area above the reels, meaning it is sticking during respins. Respins continue in this case until no new scatter symbols land. The number of free spins awarded is equal to the number of scatter symbols in view when the round is triggered, and the bonus game can be retriggered. The bonus meter below the reels can be used to track progress. The meter resets between each spin and free spin. Presumably, symbols are chosen to be sticky more often, but this is not mentioned in the game info.Grand Melee slot - free spinsGrand Melee: Slot VerdictPat on the back to Thunderkick for trying something different with the sticky winning symbol respin device, but it probably won't be for everyone. Compared to, say, NetEnt's Jack Hammer, one of the originators of the feature, Grand Melee requires more patience. In some cases, a lot more patience. Since these sorts of games can blow up during their respin feature, there seems to be a greater number of dead spins compared to a 'regular' slot. Grand Melee seemed to push this further than normal and delivered a lot of dead spins. Like Homer Simpson sort of said, welcome to dead spin city, population you. Something along those lines.So yeah, not every win triggers the respins feature; that's important for players to wrap their heads around before tackling Grand Melee and worth repeating. You gotta wait for the game to randomly pick a symbol first, then land at least five of them. Even then, sticky symbols don't guarantee a win is going to result. They say every dog has its day, and patience might pay off, should fortune be smiling, as Sticky Respins could cobble together a lifeline that boosted the balance. What's strange is despite what felt like fairly low-action gaming much of the time, the balance remained surprisingly buoyant. Not saying Grand Melee can't go the other way, of course. Those special symbols are handy, too, and are a nice way of expanding the respins feature further. Then there are free spins too, where strangely, nothing new officially occurs, which is not in the base game. Still, despite this, Grand Melee is good for wins of up to 5,000x the bet.Grand Melee possesses an interesting and unique take on the winning respin feature that resurfaces every so often but is not super frequently used. However, after seeing how Grand Melee's version of it functioned a few times, clocking the nothing new in free spins aspect and the generally pleasant yet low-key vibe meant Grand Melee wasn't one that had us rushing back like charging into a virtual melee armed with a level 9000 bastard sword would.

Title: Beasts of Fire Maximum

Title: London Tube

Title: Lotsa Lines

On respins, only blank spaces or wild symbols may appear. If a new wild symbol lands, another respin is awarded, and the process repeats until no new wild symbols land, then a win evaluation takes place.The last symbol of note is the scatter, which appears in any position - 3 or more on the reels awards 12 free spins. During the Lotsa Lines Free Games feature the number of lines increases to 200, 300, 400, or 500. The bonus game can be retriggered if 3 or more scatters appear on a free spins.Lotsa Lines: Slot VerdictGood on Dreamtech for stepping outside their comfort zone in an attempt at creating something eye-catching. Ultimately though, Lotsa Lines failed to fully ignite the need to get up and cut a rug. The team is used to flamboyantly portraying fantasy themes, so it must have been tough to rein in that natural tendency to design futuristic minimalism. The compromise was to go wild with paylines since the visuals were toned down, resulting in a game that wrestles between being big and small at the same time.As the name suggests, Lotsa Lines does provide players with a fair few lines, but the term 'lotsa' is a subjective one. Maybe once upon a time, 500 paylines would have been impressive; however, in this day and age, that number of ways to win is a rounding error. Compared to a game like Nitropolis 2, which admittedly is an extreme example, Lotsa Line doesn’t have many at all. Other than as a catchy bit of marketing, you have to wonder why Dreamtech bothered with 500 paylines anyway when they could have piled on a pay all-ways system.Perhaps players who refuse to move on from a fixed payline format to more contemporary all ways systems might be impressed. For others, the whole game, its music, and lines feel state of the art - a few years ago. You can see what Dreamtech were angling for, yet it is like going to a dance party and finding out the ‘DJ’ is an iPod on shuffle hooked up to a sound system. Sure, you can boogie to it, but it feels a little hollow. In keeping with the dance floor analogy, after a while of playing Lotsa Lines, you get those end of the night vibes where the music has gone from being amping to irritatingly repetitive, and you have to push yourself to stay focused. Even potential fails to excite, and all those 500 paylines at full a power return the so-so amount of 3,500 times the stake.All up, Lotsa Lines might be an entertaining aside for players hooked on larger than normal fixed paylines in a modern setting. If so, then try not to expect the party of the century, and you could very well enjoy your time.

Title: Alice Cooper and the Tome of Madness

Title: 3 Devils Pinball
review: 3 Devils Pinball: Slot OverviewIt might be strange to know that Pinball machines - those seemingly innocuous devices which nowadays darken the corners of hipster cafes or retro bars - were once forbidden to play. After their heyday in the late 70s/80s, pinball machines were cast aside in favour of arcade games, proving much more profitable for business owners. Now, thanks to Microgaming partner Crazy Tooth Studio, players get a hybrid of all of these things. The music's nice too, a jazzy number to get you wiggling while hoping for the balls to run your way.Players can be pinball wizards on any device by selecting bets from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin. Mathematically, the game is slanted towards a laid back gambling mind-set, offering medium volatility and relatively modest potential. On the low side are pink, blue, orange, and green flames worth 0.75x the bet, then a pitchfork plus a green and a blue devil as the mids worth 1x the stake for six of a kind. The most lucrative is the big-eyed smiling devil worth 2.5x the bet for a line of six.Lastly in this section is the wild symbols which substitute for regular pays to complete a win. One is a random Pinball feature; the other is the triggered 3 Devils Bonus round - both using Crazy Tooth's Power Path mechanic.Any spin can trigger the Pinball feature. After a short animation, the grid is expanded up to 8 rows in height, using 50 paylines instead of the normal 25. Then, balls are fired into the game arena, rolling around the top of the table and knocked onto the reels. The ball's path across them turns symbols into wilds or x2 wilds. When no more balls appear, whatever remains on the grid is evaluated.The second feature, the 3 Devil's Bonus, is triggered when 3 scatter symbols are in view. The bonus comes with 4 rounds, serving up 4, 3, 2, and then 1 Power Path. At the start of each round, the 6x8 game board is covered in cash prizes or bumpers. A random Power Path is selected, and a ball travels along it across collecting prizes. Hitting a bumper may multiply the collected prizes by up to x5.3 Devils Pinball: Slot VerdictWe've come to expect something a little different with each Crazy Tooth release, and 3 Devils Pinball doesn't disappoint in that regard. It's not quite so out there or original as others they've released though. The game blurb describing 3 Devils Pinball as a 'red hot slot gaming experience like none other' is a little misleading since it's simply a clone of one of their earlier games called Queen of the Crystal Rays. Every feature, symbol value, and stat is bang on the same. The difference is the decorative layer, which okay, is a bit unusual.3 Devils Pinball isn't exactly an intense emotionally charged monster of a game aimed at dedicated gamblers, quite the opposite. It's more of a chilled, atmospheric mix of old cartoons like Steamboat Willy or Silly Symphonies Skeleton Dance with a Betty Boop devil sort of thing. In short, it has character, so those who enjoy the oddball factor Crazy Tooth brings won't be let down.What it doesn't bring is a whole lot of potential or big thrilling wins. Potential tops out at 2,597 times the bet, yet even that seems a bit of stretch. The problem is payouts aren't worth much. For example, most of the prizes on the grid during the 3 Devil's Bonus are 5c each (betting €1), so you might get a Power Path adding up to 0.5x the bet, or less. It is possible to find bigger prizes on there, plus multipliers, yet the bonus games failed to produce anything noteworthy.To sum up, 3 Devil's Pinball is another oddity that some niche segment of the market will lap up. Other players might be curious to see what the studio has rolled out of left field this time, but what it does probably won't keep them hanging around for long.
