Without it, the odd porcine/El Dorado mash-up would have been tougher to swallow, and the game would have likely even struggled to catch anyone's attention.

Title: Wanted Wildz Extreme
review: Wanted Wildz Extreme: Slot OverviewWild heavy Western slots have proven their worth over the years, with NetEnt's Dead or Alive 2 arguably the MacDaddy of them all. Around the mid to tail end of 2022, Red Tiger compadres Max Win Gaming laid down a gauntlet with the release of Wanted Wildz, a game which could produce some serious sticky multiplier wild action during its free spins bonus round. Wanted Wildz didn't manage to push DoA2 off the top spot, lacking the same level of firepower, but Max Win Gaming is back, and it has tightened the screws to come up with Wanted Wildz Extreme. For the most part, Wanted Wildz Extreme does indeed live up to its name, being a more formidable slot than the original. If you'd care to find out how, then it's Stetson time, y'all.For one thing, the theme has had a major reboot. Where the original served a traditional Wild West scene, Wanted Wildz Extreme has cyberpunk overtones, as if the Wild West took place in Shinjuku rather than the United States of America. Futuristic Wild West is no new thing, turning up in movies like Cowboys vs Aliens, series like Firefly, and slots such as Lucksome's 6 in the Chamber. The two different genres make for an entertaining synthesis, and Max Win Gaming has brought both together in an enticing mix of dust and neon.Wanted Wildz Extreme slot - base gameAs before, Wanted Wildz Extreme is a highly volatile online slot, though its RTP has risen to a default value of 96.21%. That is the value when wagering 20 c to $/€4 per spin, rising further to 96.25% when buying features, of which there are two to choose from. Technically capable of producing hails of bullets, Wanted Wildz Extreme is nevertheless an uncomplicated slot in most regards, played on a standard 5x3, 20 payline gaming setup.Line wins occur when matching symbols hit from the left side of the grid on consecutive reels. Western fonted 9-A card ranks are the low pays, giving players 1.5 to 2 times their stake when 5 OAK wins appear, or 5 to 25 times the bet for landing 5 boots, hats, bitcoins, or badges. The skeletal chap from the first game returns on the wild symbol, present on all reels. As well as substituting all normal pay symbols, the wild pays out 100x the bet for a 5-wild hit.Wanted Wildz Extreme: Slot FeaturesWanted Wildz Extreme slot - free spinsWanted Wildz Extreme's features shouldn't require too much mental input to get a handle on. They include the Random Wilds Multiplier, free spins, and bonus buys.Random Wilds MultiplierThis feature triggers at random in the base game. When activated, for the current spin, wilds multiply any winning lines they are part of by x2, x5, x25, or x100. If more than one wild participates in a winning line, the wild multiplier values do not accumulate. The total multiplier value is always equal to the current multiplier level shown on the Wild Multiplier Ladder, no matter how many wild symbols participate in a single winning line.Free SpinsGetting 3 or more scatters triggers the free spins bonus round. When wild symbols hit, they are locked in position for the entire round. Wilds multiply any winning lines they are in by x2, x5, x25, or x100, depending on the Wild Multiplier Ladder value. Each scatter that lands is collected on the ladder, activating higher multiplier values when certain levels are reached. The round starts with 5 free spins, and +5 free spins are awarded each time a new level is reached – the new higher multiplier values apply in the retriggered batch of free spins. In addition, hitting 3 or more scatters awards +5 free spins on the current level.Buy FeatureWanted Wildz Extreme has two buy features, both costing 100 times the bet. The first choice is a regular round of free spins, while the second choice is 10 spins, where the Random Wilds Multiplier is guaranteed to trigger on each spin.Wanted Wildz Extreme slot - free spinsWanted Wildz Extreme: Slot VerdictFirst off, there is a lot to like about Wanted Wildz Extreme. It's not a game that trips over itself trying to be ultra-innovative, but its features are interesting while possessing the ability to be highly effective. Part of the progression from Wanted Wilds to Wanted Wildz Extreme is its thematic makeover, which has worked like a charm. Max Win Gaming has crafted a neat futuristic Western for its skeleton cowboy to run amok in. To put it into terms gamblers should be familiar with, the shift from Wanted Wildz to Wanted Wildz Extreme is similar to Money Train's regular Western world transforming into the Steampunk environs of Money Train 2. It makes you wonder about the way fashions come in, float out, morph, and become something else, and it's not hard to visualise a world like Wanted Wildz Extreme, a sort of William Gibson's Neuromancer on the frontier free for all, fighting it out for cryptocurrency rather than bars of gold.Moving beyond the absorbing visual revamp, Wanted Wildz Extreme's gameplay has remained more or less faithful to the previous release, with little in the way of mechanical upgrades to bear in mind. Actually, the new bits mainly consist of the two feature buys, which should please buyers of bonus rounds. The rest is basically the same – wait till the Random Wilds Multiplier feature triggers in the base game for some possible multiplicative action or free spins for potentially even more multiplicative action. Like before, the way wild multipliers do not multiply or add to each other when more than one wild participates in a win might initially seem about as fun as wearing assless chaps on a cold day. But even though you get just the one multiplier value, no matter how many wilds are involved, Wanted Wildz Extreme comes with a sizable win cap of 25,000x the bet (compared to 15,000x before).So there are good things to uncover here for sure, yet Wanted Wildz Extreme isn't without one or two warts. We touched on the biggest downer, the non-accumulating properties of the wild multipliers, but in addition, the reel-spinning action felt strangely undramatic, especially in turbo mode (if available), and the count-up sequences could have been more exciting. Still, the numbers are strong, the theme has been nicely dealt with, and in a dusty street shoot-out, Wanted Wildz Extreme would be an intimidating opponent.

Title: Fire In The Hole
review: Fire in the Hole xBomb: Slot OverviewContinuing their unstoppable roll, developer Nolimit City set their sights on one of the more populous, some might say clichéd, slots themes - the humble mining game. Characteristically, Nolimit City was not content following someone else's script to do so. Instead, they've torn it up and let the team loose to conjure up something new. It might not seem wholly new if you only read the principle attributes on paper. In practice, however, Fire in the Hole xBomb is a big, gruff, no-nonsense machine that can blow sky high at any moment – much like a stick of dynamite, or the dwarven character who pops up at key moments throughout the game.Play begins on a game area set up using 6 reels, 3 rows, and 486 ways to win. You can see this is only half of the grid, as below the active area lie 3 dormant rows holding empty positions. At first, the location comes across as a little more subdued than usual for a Nolimit title. There is no prison scene, punk angst, or vicious wastelands setting the mood. A heavy plodding soundtrack layers on the atmosphere while glowing lanterns illuminate an old mine shaft propped up by timber support beams, betraying few clues of the intensity possible when Fire in the Hole xBomb is firing. If you close your eyes, it's easy to visualise caverns full of muscle-bound, sweaty dwarves going about the business of smashing rocks to reveal treasure or beating metal into blades.Offering stakes from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin, Fire in the Hole xBomb is another Nolimit City slot throwing around big numbers. One to be wary of is volatility, rated 10 out of 10 – not just high according to its maker, but extreme. As per usual, the RTP is variable; that's something to look out for before shouldering your imaginary pickaxe, where the preferred one uses a configuration of 96.06%. Other stats of interest include a hit rate of 1 in 4 and big potential - covered in the verdict.Fire in the Hole xBomb pays out on winging symbols left to right, irrespective of row, from the first reel. Symbols start with 5 boxed 9-K symbols, unorthodoxly dropping the usual A from the pile. Then we get the premiums consisting of pickaxes, rope, boots, a satchel, and a lantern - 6 of a kind premiums will get you a prize worth 1.75 to 7.5 times the stake.Fire in the Hole xBomb: Slot FeaturesFire in the Hole xBomb is the first slot to showcase Nolimit City's new xBomb feature. As part of the full package, players also get Collapsing Mine, Wild Mining, Lucky Wagon Spins, and feature buy functionality where these sorts of things are permissible.The Collapsing Mine feature is best to cover first and is more or less an elaborate cascade system. Each spin starts with 3 active rows, and when a collapse occurs, an additional row becomes active – up to 6 in total at the most. Collapses are triggered when winning combinations land, when an xBomb Wild explodes, or by the Wild Mining feature. Winning symbols are removed before triggering the next collapse, causing all symbols to fall downwards. This creates empty spaces for new symbols to fall into, possibly leading to consecutive wins. When all 6 rows are active, 46,656 ways are in play.Sadly, there is no connection between xBombs and the Tom Jones hit song. Anyway, xBomb Wild symbols substitute any symbol except scatters to complete wins. When xBomb Wilds explode, they remove all adjacent regular pay symbols and increase a win multiplier by x1 for the next collapse. xBomb Wilds explode when there is a win, even if it was not part of it. xBombs also explode to trigger a collapse if there is no win, as long as Wild Mining (covered below) is not triggered.Wild Mining triggers when 3, 4, or 5 of the same matching symbol type land in a horizontal line, but there is no winning combination. Triggering symbols are removed, and 1, 2, or 3 wilds, respectively, are added to the middle of the alignment. All other positions in the active area explode, except scatter or wild symbols; then, a new collapse is triggered.The highlight of the show is the Lucky Wagon Spins bonus feature. Played on a new grid, the number of starting rows correlates with the number of scatters that landed to trigger the bonus - so 3, 4, or 5 scatters gives you 2, 3, or 4 starting rows respectively. Now, you get 3 spins to start with, which reset back to 3 every time a coin symbol lands in the game area. Along the top of the grid, 6 carriages displaying different prizes and modifiers appear on each spin. When a coin lands, whatever prize or modifier displayed above it is awarded. This can be:A coin value ranging from x1-x100.A multiplier applied to all coins below it.Dynamite symbols, which add a value to the coin, unlock blocked row positions and activate collect chests on the bottom row.Bag symbols collect all coins on the corresponding reel and deposit them on the triggering coin.Chest symbols collect all values on the reel and clears all occupied positions in the reel area except the dwarf symbol.Dwarf symbols collect all values on the reel and place them on the triggering coin. It will do this on each following spin.When collect chests are active on the bottom row, they collect the value of all coins above them on each spin. There is a lot to take in, so just think of it as a completely overblown hold-and-win feature, with loads of modifiers.For players itching to skip the base game and get straight to the bonus, Nolimit has attached a feature buy to do so. There are 3 options costing 60x, 157x, or 500x the bet. For that, the game serves up 3, 4, or 5 bonus symbols, and ups the RTP to 96.07%, 96.2%, or 96.96%, respectively.Fire in the Hole xBomb: Slot VerdictAfter a huge start to 2021, which saw the release of San Quentin xWays and East Coast vs West Coast, Nolimit City has kept their foot on the gas by dropping another banger. We're talking about the extremely volatile, massive potential gaming that continues to cement Nolimit's reputation as a heavyweight studio in the gambling community. You might think the momentum has to give at some point, that it's just not feasible for a studio to keep knocking it out of the park.Judging by Fire in the Hole xBomb, that’s not an issue they have to worry about at the moment as the team's creative juices continue to bubble, laying down another challenge to their competitors. Hat's off to Nolimit City for breathing life back into the mining category, for one. Through a mix of pleasing audio-visuals, big potential, and cunning gameplay, Nolimit has designed a unique mining experience. It's a testament to a studio's design capabilities when they can reanimate a theme so prosaic, as well as craft unique settings elsewhere.As to the new feature, xBomb Wilds are ideal for a mining game and are similar to xNudge Wilds in that they produce multipliers while playing a major part in scoring bigger wins. As will be obvious to most experienced players, Lucky Wagon Spins have a dose of Money Train 2 about them. They might be less intense without all the gunfire going on, but Lucky Wagon Spins do come with a higher payoff to balance out the scale. You might only start with three spins, but they have the potential to snowball like a volatile freight train. Special symbols and Collect Chests play a crucial role in getting the most out of the bonus game, which, when strained to capacity, is as high as 60,000x the stake. Critically, max win is achievable in any game phase, including the base game, though it is more likely to occur in Lucky Wagon Spins triggered by five scatters.There's no reason why players won't take to Fire in the Hole xBomb in droves. There is a thriving market for mining themed games, as well as plenty of hardcore gamers itching to wave red flags at whatever raging beast Nolimit City unleashes. Best be clear though, Fire in the Hole xBomb is no laid-back roller coaster ride through a warmly lit mine shaft. This is one of those rickety old pits in danger of collapsing and crushing the unwary at any moment. There ain't no canary down here, let's put it that way. However, it's also a mine stuffed with rich stuff ready to be tapped by those who can withstand the pressure.Don't MissNot sick of mining yet? Then have a look at Nolimit City's 2022 sequel Misery Mining which is built to offer a phenomenal audiovisual experience and great potential.

Title: Out of the Ice
review: Out of the Ice: Slot OverviewBrrr, better put an extra layer on for this one players; Print Studios is getting all Arctic in an online slot dubbed Out of the Ice, which is a fantasy-themed game revolving around the people of the water - better known as merfolk. What's worth noting is that Print hasn't slapped a bunch of chesty mermaids on a grid and called it a day. No, they've gone deeper, more cultural, into the subject matter while coming up with equally singular gameplay, which involves things like expanding reels, random multipliers, respins, and free spins.According to NASA, the Earth's polar ice caps are melting at a rate of 9% per decade, which is a bit frightening. At this rate, the Arctic will be completely ice-free by the year 2040. If the planet ever reached Kamino status, it'd be hard for future generations to conceive of scenes like the one found in Out of the Ice. In this game, a 5-reel game grid, laid out in a 3-3-4-4-5 pattern, sits in a kind of icy floe scene decorated with some pretty winter flowers and frigidly cold water. If you've ever played the 2017 Quickspin classic Wins of Fortune, you will probably feel at home with the mechanic. Hidden, for now, are the game's most exciting parts, namely, expanding reels, and Merfolk multipliers, which are ready to break the calm serenity of the wintery scene at any moment.Serenity isn't quite the right word to describe Out of the Ice's math model, but Print Studios has in some ways dialled back the intensity compared to previous releases. However, once the bonus round is triggered, players are given the option to choose between three different bonus rounds, ranging from medium to highly volatile. When it comes to the return to player value, Print Studios have been forced to abandon their fixed RTP policy due to market factors, now offering three ranges at 96.55%, 94.X%, and one for the German market. On a positive note, players won't have to second guess which version they are playing as it will be clearly displayed on the splash screen, making them the first studio to ever do so.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, the game starts with 76 winning ways, which can grow to 259 when the grid is expanded by the Freezing Respin feature. All symbols have been custom-designed, and the pay symbols include green shells, purple shells, gold shells, blue crabs, green snails, purple fish, blue dragons, green dragons, and purple dragons, paying 0.5 to 10 times the stake for five of a kind.Out of the Ice: Slot Features﻿As for features, the first on the block is the Freezing Respin feature, triggered when winning combinations hit. The leftmost reel is removed, and a new 5 position reel is added to the right-hand side. The winning symbols are locked in place while all non-winning symbols respin. This process repeats until there are no more winning combinations or free spins are triggered.Merfolk MultipliersWhen a winning combination is formed, up to 2 Merfolk symbols may bust through the Ice and apply a multiplier. Multiplier values vary from x2 to x40 and are applied independently when more than one is used in a win.Free SpinsWhen 4 consecutive respins occur, the free spins bonus round is awarded. Here players can choose from 10 Multiplier Free Spins, 8 Sticky Multiplier Free Spins, or 4 Sticky Multiplier Retrigger Free Spins. All free spin options are played on a 5x5 grid. As before, when winning combinations land, the winning symbols are locked while the others respin. When no more winning symbols land on a respin, the payment evaluation takes place. Moreover, random multipliers may apply to any win during the free spins bonus. In Sticky Multiplier Free Spins, multipliers remain overlayed on their position for the rest of the feature, multiplying any winning symbol in that position. In Sticky Multiplier Retrigger Free Spins, multipliers also add an additional free spin the first time they are applied to a win.Out of the Ice: Slot VerdictAs readers are undoubtedly well aware, there is a tendency amongst many designers to create the biggest, chunkiest, in some cases scariest slots they can. The good news is, there is a stack of outstanding beasts out there in the wild to fulfil this itch. Even better, there is plenty of room in the market for the sort of niche Out of the Ice is aiming to occupy. Out of the Ice is by intention not the most brutal game, but it offers plenty in the way of thrills, spills, and chills. Pun sort of intended.So if not gunning to be the biggest, what is Out of the Ice's life purpose? For one, its set-up is exceedingly pleasant. As mentioned, mermaids might not be complete strangers to slots, yet they rarely, if ever, show up like this. It might not be the prettiest slot ever designed, that has to be said, but visually it does get the job done. Compared to Royal Potato, which completely blew our minds with its strong personality, rich visuals and excellent music, Out of the Ice, by contrast, comes across as slightly generic.Players who are not into hold & spin type gameplay are at risk of quickly growing impatient, but those keen on dynamic reels should be intrigued by Out of the Ice's version, which seamlessly melds respins and expanding ways. The frequency with which it does so is nicely balanced, but don't worry, there is bound to be plenty of teasing, almost triggering free spins moments to provide a challenge. Balanced is an excellent word for Out of the Ice, which dangles both decent potential of 6,000x the bet and a max win frequency of 1 in 282,000. When you're used to seeing one in a billion, or what can seem at times like one in a googolplex, these look like comparatively favourable odds.After Book of Destiny, the three slots which followed have all possessed fun fantasy elements, and Out of the Ice is arguably Print's dreamiest one so far. The mythical creature visuals and the gentle, almost trippy soundtrack create a really nice place to chill out for a bit and see how fortune fares.

Title: Diamonds of the Realm
review: Diamonds of the Realm: Slot OverviewDeveloper Play'n GO squeeze more mileage out of the Arthurian legends in their medieval themed slot Diamonds of the Realm. This one isn't just a follow up to the two previous releases titled The Sword and the Grail and The Green Knight; it practically is the same game, though with a few statistical modifications. We've lost count of the number of times Arthur and the lads have populated a Play'n GO release by now. Fortunately, they have a knack for being rather good, and if not always a raging inferno of innovation, can be depended on to deliver entertaining gaming regardless.A few paragraphs of text on the game sheet help set the mood. In this iteration of the Arthurian story, a dark shadow has fallen on Camelot in the form of Morgan and Mordred. In their drive for vengeance, or whatever it is that motivates them, the duo have nicked the Diamonds of the Realm. It's the player's job to get them back during free spins, which can provide substantial rewards for successful service.Whether the diamonds have special powers or just look pretty, getting them back is a good enough excuse to revisit Arthur and his knights one more time if ever there was one. Play'n GO has a soft spot for these sorts of games, and quite a number has built up in their collection by now. Diamonds of the Realm is one of the grimmer looking ones, which makes sense with all this talk of dark shadows and so forth. Mighty Camelot sits in the background behind a 5-reel, 20 payline game panel, while above it is the multiplier trail, ready to drop in the base game, and later, on every single free spin.Mathematically, there have been a few changes. The theoretical return, for one, has dipped slightly, now measuring 96.23% in the default configuration. The volatility, meanwhile, remains sky-high, with a full 10 out of 10 rating, making Diamonds of the Realm as unpredictable as its predecessor 'Grail' was. As before, bets range from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin, so no changes there.While you're trying to save the realm, regular wins occur when three to five matching symbols line up from the left-hand side of the reels. Symbols include coins stamped with J, Q, K, A, and T, as the low pays, while Mordred, Morgan, Queen Guinevere, and King Arthur are the 4 premium symbols. Hit a line of five premiums to collect a win worth 7.5 to 100 times your stake. A wild symbol also pops up in the game on any reel to substitute for all symbols except diamond scatters. In the same manner as the King, wilds are worth up to 100x the stake for a line of five of them.Diamonds of the Realm: Slot FeaturesDiamonds of the Realm has two closely related features, one which livens up the base game, the other, is a number of triggered free spins. At any point in the main game, the Win Multiplier feature may trigger. When it does, multiplier values of x2, x5, x10, or x100 appear over the reels. If a win occurs on this spin, its value is bolstered by whatever multiplier was randomly selected.To access free spins, you'll need at least 3 diamond scatters symbols to land in view. The reward is 5 free spins with the multiplier always active, so all wins during the bonus are subject to a starting multiplier of x2.Diamond scatters remain desirable symbols during free spins and are collected whenever they land. Gathering enough of them moves players through 3 more levels, like so:Level 2 – collecting 6 diamonds awards +5 free spins and increases the win multiplier to x5.Level 3– collecting 12 diamonds awards +5 free spins and increases the win multiplier to x10.Level 4 – collecting 18 diamonds awards +5 free spins and increases the win multiplier to x100. Once reaching level 4, diamonds are removed from the reels, so additional free spins cannot be won.Diamonds of the Realm: Slot VerdictIf you liked The Sword and the Grail, then you'll no doubt be up for Diamonds of the Realm as well, as it's the same game but with increased potential. In fact, if you went in for any of the Arthurian inspired slots from Play'n GO, you'd do well to give Diamonds of the Realm a crack as well. Each has something similar to offer, revolving around big multipliers in all facets of play. It's a little formulaic, though not a bad formula at all. These slots tend to look great, pack in loads of brooding atmosphere while doling out solid as a rock gameplay.The gameplay in question means a big bonus game that follows in the footsteps of 300 Shields while offering the occasional multiplier in the base game to balance things out and keep you alert. Play'n GO do like to toss the odd random multiplier into the main game, but they don't usually go as high as x100, which can do some serious damage, should it show up. Free spins are just as intense in Diamonds of the Realm as they ever were in The Sword and the Grail. It all starts with a short blast of just five spins to start cranking out diamond scatters in the hopes of progressing through the various levels to the fabled x100 round.The difference between this game and the previous one is that the rewards for successfully guarding the realm, or getting the diamonds, or whatever, are double that of what the two precious titles in the series had to offer at 20,000 times the bet. The probability of doing so is actually slightly better as well, though at 1 in 90 million or so spins, don't expect it to happen anytime soon.There is a feeling that we probably could have done without Diamonds of the Realm since it doesn't do much the original didn't do. However, players up for some more highly polished, highly volatile Arthur driven action are unlikely to be complaining, especially with the larger max win capabilities thrown into the bargain.

Title: Los Cuatro Esqueletos
review: Los Cuatro Esqueletos: Slot OverviewLos Cuatro Esqueletos, which, when translated to the English language, comes out as 'The Four Skeletons', is a Mexican-themed online slot from developer Relax Gaming. Getting even granular, Los Cuatro Esqueletos burrows into Mexican culture and comes up with one of the more popular aspects of it – the Day of the Dead holiday that takes place around the start of November. If you've played your fair share of online slots, there is a good chance you've bumped into this celebration before. It's become something of a goto amongst software developers looking to get a bit cultural, a bit colourful, and inject an upbeat Mariachi tune or two.After testing driving other Day of the Dead slots like Thunderkick's Esqueleto Explosivo 2, Play'n GO's Muerto en Mictlan, or Muertos Multiplier Megaways from Pragmatic Play, we come to Relax Gaming's interpretation of it. Los Cuatro Esqueletos is it, and spoiler alert, it's a 'book of' slot with an energetic Mexican exterior rather than Ancient Egypt. This means a game grid situated in the middle of a colourful town somewhere south of the Rio Grande, where the townsfolk hang flags on strings between buildings, which are all painted in eye-catching patterns and bright colours. It's pretty festive, not the most Day of the Dead-ish slot we've ever seen, but Los Cuatro Esqueletos ticks most of the boxes required of these sorts of slots audio-visually without doing anything majorly special. The same goes for the tunes. Adequate, with a bit of a horn section. On we go.Los Cuatro Esqueletos slot - base gameAvailable with or without Relax Gaming's Dream Drop jackpot network attached, the non-jackpot version has a surprisingly low RTP value of 94%. A medium volatile slot machine, the gaming is held on a 5-reel, 3-row grid with 10 paylines – a classic 'book of' set-up. Wins must start from the leftmost side of the matrix and contain at least 3 low pays or 2 high pay symbols. When placing a bet the lowest stake allowable is 20 p/c while the highest wager possible is $/€100.The name Los Cuatro Esqueletos makes a bit more sense after inspecting the paytable. Here is where we meet 4 skeleton characters as the 4 high-paying symbols, joined by 10 to A card rank symbols that look like they've been imprinted on coloured gravestones. Hit a 5 OAK win, and the rewards are 75 to 500 times the stake for the skeletons or 10 to 15 times the bet for the royals.Los Cuatro Esqueletos: Slot FeaturesLos Cuatro Esqueletos slot - symbol picking featureAs mentioned above, Los Cuatro Esqueletos is a 'book of' style game, so players can expect expanding full reel symbols in the free spins round, with a couple of twists adding a modicum of originality.Free SpinsPinatas are Los Cuatro Esqueletos' wild, and they're also the game's free spins scatter. As wild, they can substitute any non-expanded pay symbol to help complete winning lines. When used as the scatter, landing 3 or more of them awards 10 free spins. During the free spins round, hitting 3 or more scatters retriggers 10 additional free spins.Now, at the start of a bonus round, a bunch of pinatas are displayed on the screen, and players pick one of them. This will reveal which symbol is the special expander during free spins. At the end of a spin, after any wins have been awarded, if any, expanding symbols spread to cover all positions on their reel. If the expander is a premium symbol, it will need to be present on at least 2 reels or 3+ reels if the expander is a low-pay symbol. Expanded symbols pay all lines from any position.Super Free SpinsScatter symbols are also collected when they hit, and when 600 of them have been accrued, players are awarded 10 Super free spins. These are exactly the same as regular free spin, except 2 symbols are selected from the pick n click event before the round begins. Super free spins can be retriggered, awarding +10 free spins and an additional expanding symbol. The bet used in Super free spins is an average of the bets during the collection - extra info on this can be found in the paytable.Los Cuatro Esqueletos slot - free spinsLos Cuatro Esqueletos: Slot VerdictHate to be the killjoy around here, but did the planet really need one more expanding symbol in free spins, aka another 'book of' slots'? In the right circumstances, if the game in question offers something intriguingly new, is presented in an outstanding way, or possesses that 'I don't know what' x-factor quality, yeah, sure, why not? Unfortunately, Los Cuatro Esqueletos doesn't really have any of those things. Relax Gaming is a bona fide top-tier provider, producing world-dominating slots like the unstoppable Money Train range, so apologies for stating the obvious, but Los Cuatro Esqueletos is one of the studio's lesser releases.A couple of issues are obviously apparent. One is the sub-par RTP value. Perhaps if a slot blazes a white-hot trail, it would be easier to justify overlooking a lame return value, like with some of what ELK Studios does. But geez, Los Cuatro Esqueletos is entering a slot genre absolutely overflowing with choices for fans of the format. Most recreational gamblers may not be too bothered about RTP, but still, why pick a 94% one over the huge number of better-value slots? Even Los Cuatro Esqueletos' 'twist' is somewhat dubious. Collecting 600 scatters is likely to require a certain amount of commitment, and one wonders if this system has any sort of effect on the RTP. Make it all the way, and the reward is alright, without being super special, considering other slots already do this sort of thing. Not a ton, yet prior examples include Legacy of Dead, Sword of Khans, and Rise of Merlin (amongst others) if you're interested.On the plus side, a max win of 10,000x the bet is quite high for a slot like this, so that's something. Otherwise, Los Cuatro Esqueletos is a rather mediocre release from Reflex Gaming, a studio otherwise famous for consistently releasing slots which blow others out of the water. Los Cuatro Esqueletos, by contrast, sort of just treads water alongside them.

Title: Beast of Wealth
review: Beast of Wealth: OverviewBeast of Wealth is one of three games in Play’n GO’s trio of wealth based slots. Wealth by name, wealth by nature since all three have been designed as progressive jackpots. This game category is not exactly Play’n GO’s forte, so the studio has gone on the assault by dropping three at the same time. Is the thinking at least one will rise to the top as a player favourite? Or they just had a bunch of Asian skins and code lying around that found a good use? Who knows. What we do know is all three are Asian based, and are geared towards big win hunters spinning for four progressive jackpots.Compared to the other contributions in the trilogy, Beast of Wealth has a more traditional look to it. There’s no confusion at all when the game loads as to where you are. The 5-reel, 243 win ways game area is framed by a wooden temple-like structure with a tile roof that is classically Asian. Lanterns hang off it, while mountains and mist brood in the distance. As we said, a more classically Asian look.Players join the hunt by selecting bets of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin, on mobile, tablets, or desktop. The math model produces similar stats to Celebration of Wealth and Temple of Wealth too, such as a fairly high, but not brutal volatility, which the studio has rated as 7/10. RTP has taken a slight knock, dropping it to a default setting of 96.17%, though still an impressive figure for a progressive, which includes a contribution from each stake to the pot. Check the paytable before diving in though, like other Play’n GO games, the RTP is variable, so it may be found at a lower level.The paytable provides 10 regular pay symbols to work with - 6 low pay royals and 4 high pays. The highs are an abstract collection of beasts such as turtles, birds, tigers, and dragons. Five premiums in a row are worth from 2 to 10 times the stake. Lines of the wild are worth the same as the high pay dragon. Styled like a gong, the wild appears anywhere to substitute for any symbol except the scatter to line up winning combinations.Beast of Wealth: FeaturesBeast of Wealth - free spinsBeast of Wealth is as simple as its sister slots when it comes to features. The base game coasts in a pretty basic manner, until the features are triggered. There are two - free spins and the jackpot feature.The Yin & Yang symbol is what you need to unlock free spins. They appear on any reel, paying 5, 10, or 50 times the stake when 3, 4, or 5 are in view. At least 3 anywhere in view is enough to trigger free spins, and like before, there are five options for players to choose from:Turtles – 118 Turtle symbols added to the reels.Birds – 108 Bird symbols added to the reels.Tigers – 98 Tiger symbols added to the reels.Dragons – 88 Dragon symbols added to the reels.The 5th choice is a mystery option that awards 88-118 of any symbol type. Now, the dragon is tempting since it’s the most valuable icon on the paytable. However, there are less of them available making it harder to form combinations. In other words, players can expect a difference in volatility depending on the option chosen.During free spins, all other premium symbols are removed, so the chosen symbol is the only one to land in the feature. The round begins with 8 free spins which can be retriggered by three or more scatter symbols.Scatters are all well and good, but if it’s the jackpot you’re after, it’s Gold Reels you’ll want to see. On any base game spin, 1 to 5 reels randomly turn into Gold Reels. A wild landing on at least one of them triggers the jackpot feature. Once triggered, players are presented with 12 logo coins and asked to pick one by one to reveal jackpots – the Mini, Minor, Major, and Grand. Reveal three matching jackpots to win the corresponding prize. As before, 1.5% of each stake is skimmed off the top to grow the prize pool, and the bigger the bet, the better your chance of triggering a jackpot.Beast of Wealth: VerdictWell, it’s much of a muchness really since Beast of Wealth parallels the other two games in the series in so many ways. The bonus game has been tweaked, but it’s still a case of firing up for a crack at the progressive jackpot. Beast of Wealth is a slightly more Asian affair, though there isn’t a massive amount separating the three games. Tey all have similar stats, similar math models, and the non-jackpot potential remains the same as before.So how is a player meant to choose one over the others? To be honest, you can’t really. They're all wired into the same network, so players could be chasing the same rewards. Sure, free spins are different so demoing the three games is probably the only way of picking a clear favourite.

Title: Fruit Shop Frenzy
review: Fruit Shop Frenzy: Slot OverviewOne pivotal moment in the Robin Williams classic movie Hook was when Peter Banning, the mild-mannered lawyer, opened up his imagination and could see food on a table which was previously empty. What proceeds from there is a food fight of epic proportions, a frenzy of food throwing, if you will. It is in the spirit of frenzy-ness that we come to Fruit Shop Frenzy, an online slot from software provider NetEnt. Players who have been spinning reels for a while may well be aware of the original Fruit Shop, which the studio released back in 2011. A Megaways version followed a decade later, and 2 years on, we've got part 3 - Fruit Shop Frenzy.With all due respect, the original Fruit Shop slot is kinda looking its age by now, and the Megaways game, while possessing a visual upgrade, retained a lot of the first one's graphical simplicity. Fruit Shop Frenzy, by contrast, tells something of a story. What that story might be isn't explicitly expounded on, so players get to fill in the blanks as they see fit. The grid is locked within a shop, like a kiosk, or something, in a charming urban environment somewhere like Italy or Spain, let's say. What looks like delightful bistros or ristoranti line a cobbled street populated by scooters and pleasant plant life. You can imagine wandering around town baguette under one arm, whistling a tune, catching up with friends, living la dolce vita.Fruit Shop Frenzy slot - base gameAnd back to the game, which takes place on a 5-reel, 3-row gaming panel with 15 paylines awarding wins left to right from the first reel onwards. Despite the relaxed atmos, Fruit Shop Frenzy is a highly volatile slot, taking wagers of 10 p/c to $/€8 per paid spin. Fruit Shop Frenzy has a return to player value of 96.04% when playing 'normally', though the return figure increases a notch or two to 96.1% when buying the feature.Fruit is one of the things linking the 3 games together, as pretty much the same pay symbols appear in all. These are 10 to A card ranks paying 3 to 9 times the bet for a 5 OAK hit, then watermelon, oranges, a lemon, a plum, and cherries as the 5 premium symbols. Hit a 5 premium symbol win, and the payouts are 12 to 100 times the stake. Helping players pull winning lines together is the Fruit Shop Frenzy logo wild. Wilds appear on reels 2, 3, and 4, substituting for all paying symbols.Fruit Shop Frenzy: Slot FeaturesFruit Shop Frenzy slot - free spinsWhilst a simple-looking game, Fruit Shop Frenzy is slightly more sophisticated than you might suspect. Not in the base game as such, since it's basically feature free, but landing a fruit win kickstarts Fruit Shop Frenzy's chain of events.Free SpinsWhen one or more winning combos made up of fruit symbols hits, 2 free spins with increasing multipliers are triggered. The multiplier increments on the multiplier bar are x1, x2, x3, x4, and x5. Each winning round awards +1 free spin and moves the multiplier bar forward +1 step.Helper FeatureDuring free spins, a Helper symbol may land on the rightmost reel. When the Helper lands, it randomly activates one of these three modifiers – the multiplier values increase by +1, advancement to the next multiplier, or Frenzy mode is triggered.Frenzy ModeWhen Frenzy mode activates, 3 additional free spins are awarded, and the multiplier bar increases from 5 to 10 steps – so x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8, x9, and x10. The progress of the achieved multiplier in free spins is carried over to Frenzy mode. Each winning round in Frenzy mode awards +1 free spin and furthers the multiplier bar by +1 step. Now, while Frenzy mode is active, landing a Helper symbol on the rightmost reel randomly activates one of these features – the multiplier values increase by +1, advancement to the next multiplier, 1 to 6 random wilds are added to the middle three reels, or Double X triggers which doubles the values of the multipliers on the multiplier bar.Bonus BuyDue to the nature of Fruit Shop Frenzy's free spins feature, it triggers fairly frequently already, but if it's not frequent enough, players can buy direct access to Frenzy Mode for the cost of 20x the bet.Fruit Shop Frenzy slot - free spinsFruit Shop Frenzy: Slot VerdictIf you've been having images of NetEnt resting on its laurels, content squeezing extra mileage out of its back catalogue rather than flexing its creative muscles and dazzling a new generation of gamblers with its design talent and dazzling innovation, then Fruit Shop Frenzy is only going to reinforce those thoughts. A Megaways upgrade of an old classic made sense because, shoot, it seems like every studio and its dog are doing those, so why not get in on the action? Doing number 3 so long after the first might have seemed a bit dubious if NetEnt hadn't wedged in some new stuff to tempt players back for a third go.The new stuff isn't half bad, either. Where the previous 2 games triggered free spins and left it about there, Fruit Shop Frenzy pushes things to the next level should the game progress to Frenzy mode. A little tricky, perhaps, cos you'll need help from the Helper symbol to do so. But if you're not in the mood to peel fruit waiting for that to happen, Frenzy Mode can be bought for the reasonable cost of 20x the bet. After playing games like Bounty Hunters recently with its 850x Showdown Spins buy feature, 20x feels like small change by comparison. Totally different bonus rounds, of course, so we are admittedly not comparing apples with apples, as it were. What makes things interesting here is that while the feature is modestly costed by modern standards, Fruit Shop Frenzy's max win of 10,868x is nevertheless a substantial target to aim for, though about half of Fruit Shop Megaways, if you were wondering.As far as being the third slot in a series goes, Fruit Shop Frenzy is not a bad game by any means. It's got the spirit of the previous two slots while packing in extra personality and more features. Still, it might make one wonder whether NetEnt's heart is really in the game at the moment, what with all the remakes and so-so slots it had released around the time of writing, but that doesn't stop Fruit Shop Frenzy from being an amusing diversion.

Title: Lord Merlin And The Lady Of The Lake
review: Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake: Slot OverviewDeveloper Play'n GO follows up their 2019 Arthurian release Rise of Merlin with Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake. At the core of it all we once again get more ‘Book of’ style expanding symbols, though several additions make it a more than worthy sequel. Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake proudly continues the long tradition of these types of games, its premise thus making it a tempting option for players who like big volatility coupled with big potential to go with the expanding special symbol action.Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake moves the story from the original’s snowy confines to a picturesque outdoor setting. Here, the 5x3 grid shares screen space alongside twisted lakeside trees, loads of lily pads, and the clear blue sky of a gorgeous English day. Deep in the lake’s depths is where the mysterious Lady resided, providing Arthur with his sword Excalibur, a name also given to one of the new features found in the game.Available on any device, players can take part in the old legends by selecting bets from 1 p/c (one payline) up to $/€100 per spin, and, if they wish, playlines from between 1 to 10 in true old school fashion. Like paylines, RTP too is flexible, so make sure you’re getting the best deal, being the default setting of 96.2%. Volatility, meanwhile, is high, meaning Merlin can blow his lid at any time, playing well with the higher than average potential usually found in a game like this.Regular wins hit when three or more low pays or at least two high pays land on a payline starting from the first reel. As to symbols, low pays are made up of 10-A card royals, while the highs are a crest, a hat, a staff, and Merlin himself at the top of the table. Symbols values are big, where lines of five premiums are worth payouts of 75 to 1,000 times your stake. Merlin offers the same value as the Lady, who is wild. As well as being worth a stack of coins, she substitutes any of the regular symbols to complete a win.Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake: Slot Features﻿Naturally, expanding special symbols are the order of the day when free spins are activated. Triggering them occurs when 3, 4, or 5 scatters land in view. The prize is 8 spins as well as a win of 1x, 10x, or 100x your bet respectively. Instead of getting one special symbol throughout the whole feature, a different one is randomly selected on each free spin. Whenever enough special symbols land to form a win, they expand to cover all positions on their reel. Expanding symbols pay all active ways, from any position, regardless of whether they are adjacent or not.During free spins, sword scatters are changed into wild scatters which can substitute other symbols. When 2 or more wild scatters are in view, each awards 1 Excalibur Spin. A difference now is the special symbol from the triggering free spin remains set for all Excalibur spins. In addition, 2 or more wild scatters retrigger this feature, with no set limit on the number of times this may occur.Depending on the special expanding symbol awarded, here's the maximum potential of each symbol:Symbol(s)Max PayoutQ, J, 10100 times the betA, K150 times the betLion Crest, Merlin’s Hat750 times the betMerlin’s Staff2,000 times the betMerlin10,000 times the betThe final extra is a gamble option available after wins to boost their value. The goal is to pick the correct colour or suit to double or quadruple (or nothing ) your win. Players can gamble up to five consecutive times, or up to 2,500 coins.Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake: Slot VerdictIf there is something Play'n GO does well, and there are several things we could expound on here, it is ‘Book of’ slots. Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake continues this tradition, being another exceptional example in the genre. We all know, ‘Book of’ slots abound, yet Play'n GO releases generally manage to stand out - each one for a different reason. Of course, much of the hype comes down to their gold standard Book of Dead which has had a huge impact on the genre. When it comes to Lord Merlin and the Lady of the Lake, there are several arguments as to why players might want to choose this one over the countless others.Firstly it’s not an Egypt based game. Not that there is anything wrong with setting a ‘Book of’ slot in its country of origin, but it’s always nice to have options. The location Play'n GO has chosen is certainly idyllic, oozing mystery provided by the well-known story of Arthur, Merlin, and the Lady of the Lake. In typical Play'n GO style, they’ve made the visuals a treat to look at, full of smooth animations, and fitting effects.Then there is the gameplay, which is a significant cut above most in this category, despite being the same as Cat Wilde and the Lost Chapter. For players chasing massive wins, potential will be enough to encourage a spin a two. Due to double the value of the highest premium compared to games like Book of Dead or the original Rise of Merlin, single spin wins of 10,000 times the bet are possible. Incidentally, this figure is the games full potential. On another positive note, the max win occurred once in around 2.37 million spins, making it a far cry from the billions, or even hundreds of billions we usually see.Okay, it might be 'Cat Wilde and the Lost Chapter by a Lake', but that doesn’t stop Lord Merlin being another highly enjoyable game from Play'n GO. It makes an excellent follow up to the medieval styles found in Rise of Merlin, upping the ante in every respect. For players who enjoy a highly volatile ‘Book’ slot with monster potential and a great twist, you can’t go wrong taking this Lord or Lady on.

Title: Sisters of Oz
review: Sisters of Oz Jackpots: OverviewSisters of Oz is loosely based around the classic tale The Wizard of Oz, in particular its coven of four witches. Traditionally the witches of the north and south were goodies, while the east and west were the bad ones. In this slot version from Microgaming partner Triple Edge Studios, they’re all pretty much as dubious as each other. On the way to possibly winning one of four jackpots, players get jumbo blocks and free spins to look forward to.Sisters of Oz uses a 5-reel, 4-row grid, with 20 fixed paylines to land wins on. The location is Oz’s famous yellow brick road. The one Dorothy traipsed along, meeting three traveling companions on her way to the Great Wizard. The original movie was full of musical theatrics, and despite being released in 1939, it is still considered one of the greatest films ever. Good, family entertainment.Well, the slot version isn’t quite so wholesome. There are no green-skinned, wart nosed witches here. All four sisters in this rendition of the classic story look like they’re on loan from the Playboy mansion. Imagine Hustler magazine did an Oz-themed photo-shoot and you’ve kind of got the picture. Players will either go for the chesty, bedroom eyes or find it a cheese overkill. From time to time a breathy voice randomly says something like ‘Alluring’, in a final act of seduction.Sisters of Oz can be played on any device, by selecting bets from 20 p/c to $/€25 per spin. For a jackpot slot, the stats are quite user friendly, starting with an RTP rating of 95.83%. Hits come on a regular basis as well, so players can expect a win every 3.501 spins, or 28.56% of the time. Volatility has been measured as medium, though most of what we covered in this paragraph is probably of little interest to many jackpot chasers.Pay symbols come in two forms, 5 low-value potion bottles and 4 high pay witches. The witches come in different colours – red, green, purple, blue, occasionally winking flirtatiously. As to values, a line of five witches is worth from 2 to 18 times the stake. At least three of a kind is needed to form a winning combination, left to right from the first reel onwards.Sisters of Oz Jackpots: FeaturesSisters of Oz - Mega Jackpot triggeredNaturally, the fixed jackpots are the main showpiece in Sisters of Oz, but players also get jumbo blocks and free spins to help keep them entertained.First up, the four witch premiums appear on the reels in three sizes – 1x2, 1x3, and 1x4. At random on a base game spin, the middle three reels synchronise and spin together. Any high-value symbols then spin as 3x4 jumbo blocks, while low symbols or book scatters land as 1x1 between the jumbo blocks. Synchronised reels land first, to build a bit of anticipation, followed by reels 1 then 5.The golden book symbol has two jobs in Sisters of Oz – scatter and wild. As the wild, it substitutes for any pay symbol to help make a win. As the scatter, 3, 4, or 5 in view award 5, 7, or 10 free spins respectively. As well as award free spins scatters also payout 2x, 10x, or 100 times the stake on top.During free spins, the centre 3 reels are always synchronised, so only 3x4 jumbo blocks land on them. High or low pays can appear as jumbo blocks, though never the book scatter. However, book scatters landing on reels 1 and 5 add three free spins. Also, all line wins are doubled during the free spins feature.At any stage of the game, bonus symbol overlays appear at random on regular symbols. These are collected, granting a chance of triggering the jackpot wheel. When activated, players are presented with a 12 segment wheel, guaranteeing 1 of the 4 prizes - Mini, Minor, Majoir, or Mega jackpots worth 15x, 50x, 500x, or 10,000x respectively.Sisters of Oz Jackpots: VerdictThey say a scantily clad woman can sell anything. If that’s the case, Sisters of Oz should have no trouble pulling in the punters. The line-up of temptresses might be racier than the Playboy range of slots, but Sisters of Oz’s style outshines its substance most of the time. There is little game-wise to get excited about, and without the Mega jackpot attached the whole venture feels like a waste of time.On a positive note, Triple Edge Studios has created a nice looking slot. The animations are smooth, the graphics are super clear, practically photorealistic, and the sound effects add to the atmosphere. Well, apart from the cringy one-word voice overs. The studio has done a decent enough job of creating an attractive, adult version of Oz to spin in.The gameplay is average though. Jumbo symbols on the middle three reels are nothing new, and the low payline to grid size counts against it. However, players into the presentation of the theme and a possible 10,000x payday probably won’t be too bothered about that. Wins are frequent enough to keep the game moving, and free spins are there with their synchronised reels to display the full talents of the premium symbols.Sisters of Oz is an okay option for players keen on chasing a fixed 10,000x payout, possessing attributes that will charm some, while being completely over the top for others. If jackpots with cleave sounds appealing, Sisters of Oz pours it on like nothing else.

Title: Wings of Ra Megaways
review: Wings of Ra Megaways: Slot OverviewRa, the Egyptian god of the sun and sky, often isn't depicted with wings, but artistic licence being what it is, developer Red Tiger has seen fit to give players Wings of Ra Megaways. Not for the first time in that this is a follow-up to Wings of Ra (a non-Megaways variant), which came out about 4 years earlier. For Wings of Ra Megaways, the gaming grid has grown, and chain reaction wins have been included, but the nucleus of the original, its Mystery Coins and royal symbol removal in free spins features have been rounded up and returned.Red Tiger has expanded on the graphics when injecting the bigger grid, too, and Wings of Ra Megaways is a striking slot. Its base game takes place indoors in a fire-lit room of statues, hieroglyphs, and paintings, which is very pretty. As is the free spins location, which zooms outside, up at altitude, overlooking the Nile and a vista of pyramids bathed in golden sunlight. All very nicely done for the pleasure of Egyptian slot fans' eyes.Wings of Ra Megaways slot - base gameBetween 2 to 7 symbols can land on each of Wings of Ra Megaways' 6 reels, producing up to 117,649 ways to win. All wins begin on the leftmost reel and matching symbols must hit on adjacent reels. A medium volatile math governs the ride, while the highest RTP you will find in Wings of Ra Megaways is 95.72%. As for bet selection, wagers of 10 c to $/€100 are up for grabs.Card royals 10 to A make up Wings of Ra Megaways' low pay symbols, then an Eye of Horus, an Ankh, a bird, a lady and a man symbol are the high pays. The reward for landing 6-matching royals is 0.2 to 0.25 times the bet or 0.5 to 5 times the bet for hitting 6 matching premiums. Wilds substitute for all paying symbols and land on reels 2, 3, 4, and 5.Wings of Ra Megaways: Slot FeaturesWings of Ra Megaways slot - free spinsMystery Coins were central to the original Wings of Ra slot, and they're back for Wings of Ra Megaways. Accompanying Mystery Coins are chain reactions and free spins.Chain ReactionsChain reactions begin when a winning combination hits on the grid. The winning symbols vanish, leaving spaces that are filled by symbols dropping into them. Reactions continue like this without limit, ending when no new win is created.Mystery CoinMystery Coins cannot land from a chain reaction, only on an initial spin. All Mystery Coins in view reveal the same type of random pay symbol.Free SpinsFree spins scatter symbols are present on reels 2, 3, 4, and 5. Hitting 3 or 4 scatters awards players 10 or 15 free spins, respectively. During the bonus round, scatters cannot land.Mystery Coins can, however, and they are collected on a special progress bar when they do. Each time the bar is filled, the current lowest-paying royal symbol is removed from the reels for the remainder of the round. If a symbol is removed and a win is formed, any leftover symbols of the removed type on the reels disappear after the winning symbols do. After a symbol is removed, Mystery Coins no longer reveal the removed symbol.It takes 15 Mystery Coins to remove the 10 symbol, 30 Mystery Coins in total to remove the J, 45 in total for the Q, 60 in total for the K, and 75 in total for the A.Wings of Ra Megaways slot - free spinsWings of Ra Megaways: Slot VerdictIn the wide, wide world of Egyptian slots, there's room for a slot like Wings of Ra Megaways. It's a step up from the original while keeping a lot of the features as they were. The game is also easy to look at, and using Megaways is like inviting a quasi-famous friend of the family to a low-key event to give it extra gravitas. On the whole, though, there's nothing wow magic happening here, so even dedicated Egyptian slot players shouldn't feel too devastated if they miss it.One particular on-reels highlight was when a ton of landed Mystery symbols revealed one of the higher-paying symbols, triggering a chunky win. How chunky the wins can possibly get is a puzzle, though. The max multiplier noted on the help page was lower than hits that occurred during the review, so the 784.4x figure there is suspect. Stake range is relatively wide, which might be an indicator of winning potential being on the lower side for this game, so who knows.Will anyone really care, either? Okay, that was harsh since the mystery feature has its moments and Wings of Ra Megaways won't hurt your eyes for looking. Got a thrill from the first game? Then Wings of Ra Megaways should thrill just as much, if not more, than before, and imaginative players might have fun peering at the graphics and pretending they've gone through a bizarre time warp.

Title: Starburst XXXtreme
review: Starburst XXXtreme: Slot OverviewIconic is one of those words which gets thrown around a lot, but if ever an online slot was deserving of the term, it is NetEnt's classic Starburst. Released in 2013, Starburst remains an immensely popular go-to game for many. It is getting on in years, however, and comes across a little dated, not least due to a general shift towards more volatile, more rewarding games. In a drive to keep the brand relevant perhaps, or to thrill fans who have moved on to bigger slots, NetEnt has gone back to the classic in their 2021 release Starburst XXXtreme, kept a few things to retain a link while tearing out the innards and dropping in a vastly different set of maths.When it comes to visuals, you can spot the Starburst heritage a mile away as the remake looks very much the same. The cosmic inspired action takes place over a 5-reel, 3-row game grid with 9 rather than 10 fixed paylines. Players looking for major innovation will be happy to know, dropping a payline is the least of the changes found in Starburst XXXtreme. Audio visually, there's not much else to note; Starburst XXXtreme displays a travelling at light speed effect behind the reels at certain points, but fans of the first will feel right at home with the XXXtreme version.Playable from 10 p/c to $/€50 per spin, the math model has been completely revamped as well, with volatility now sitting at the opposite side of the spectrum, rated as 'high'. The pay-both-ways has been axed as well, so winning combinations only hit when at least three identical symbols land from the leftmost reel. If you're playing the game with XXXtreme Spins activated (more on that below), you don't notice this as much since there are constant fireworks going off, but the change is more obviously felt in the default betting mode.The game returns to familiar territory for the paytable, where the same 7 pay symbols have been used. This means 5 sparkling gems as the lower value symbols, topped by 7s and Bars. These latter two are worth a payout of 20 to 50 times the stake for a five of a kind combo. As before, wilds play a critical role in collecting coins; let's look at those below.Starburst XXXtreme: Slot Features﻿NetEnt has removed a bet line and restricted the others to pay in one direction only, so there must be something potent on board to justify the 'XXX' in the title? As it happens, NetEnt has added multipliers to the fray as compensation. That might sound a bit simplistic, but simplicity lies at the heart of the Starburst experience, and the effects can be extraordinary.First of all though, when booting up the game you will notice there are 2 XXXtreme Spins betting options available:One is 1 guaranteed Starburst Wild on each spin, increasing the stake by x10.The other is 2 guaranteed Starburst Wilds per spin, powering up the cost to 95x the base bet.If you're baulking at those numbers, know that it is possible to land just as many wilds on regular spins; they just won't show up as often. Betting strategy affects RTP slightly, where the return value hovers around 96.26-96.45%.As before, gameplay centers around the Starburst Wilds, which appear on reels 2, 3, or 4. When they land, they expand to cover all positions on their reel and award a respin. Wilds are locked for respins, and if a new one hits, it is also locked while awarding another respin.The new part is that each Starburst Wild also awards a multiplier of x2, x3, x5, x10, x25, x50, x100, or x150. If more than one wild lands, the multipliers are added together during a respin sequence, and the value is applied to any bet line wins from the current spin or following respins.One last extra is the Random Wilds feature. This can be randomly activated after a spin or a respin, adding 1-3 Starburst Wild symbols to the middle three reels.Starburst XXXtreme: Slot VerdictPlaying the two Starburst games is a real night and day experience. At first, the alterations aren't apparent since NetEnt has left the graphics and the soundtrack more or less intact. There is an upgrade, but the purpose wasn't to reproduce Starburst with modern visuals. It was to make a game which appealed to a completely different breed of gambler altogether, to fire a broadside at critics who might be claiming NetEnt's gone soft. In these regards, NetEnt has definitely met its goals. It's like the team took the old four-banger out of Lada then dropped in the sort of engine Koenigsegg would be envious of. It is possible to cruise as before and enjoy the starlit background when betting at regular levels, but XXXtreme Spins are a game-changer, drastically heightening the tension on every single spin – they are pricey, however, so beware.Starburst XXXtreme doesn't just provide outsized betting options for players who like to go large. The addition of multipliers which some readers astutely predicted provides a wholly different experience. If Starburst Wild respins were fun before, knowing that a total multiplier of up to 450x is possible adds a completely new dimension. It's not just increased thrills either, potential has blasted through the roof, reaching insanely stratospheric heights. NetEnt has slapped on a win cap of 200,000x the bet – technically possible with a combination of max multipliers, stacked Bars, and respins.Triple 'X' has certain connotations, and they might not be the most appropriate letters for a game title, but at least it's not a case of false advertising. Starburst XXXtreme is indeed extreme in many respects. While the spirit of the original remains, this one is for a totally different gambling temperament than the gentle, low volatile, 'stepping into online slots for the first time' of the original. Exploring everything Starburst XXXtreme has to offer doesn't come cheap, but for players after a challenge, they've got a new way of tackling an old favourite.

Title: Scarab Kingdom
review: Scarab Kingdom: Slot OverviewWith a name like Scarab Kingdom, it will be no surprise to know developer Just For The Win is shipping players to the warm world of Ancient Egypt on a quest for potential riches. For some reason, scarab beetles were all the rage in Ancient Egypt by 2,000 BCE, appearing on amulets, seals, and jewellery. The scarab hieroglyph was used to write the god Khepri's name, and it is this connection that probably accounts for its rise from humble dung beetle status to one of the most numerous amulets of Middle Kingdom Egypt. In Scarab Kingdom, scarabs are used to trigger both the Wild Scrolls feature and Cleo's Bonus. As well as these two extras, players also have free spins to contend with.Scarab Kingdom is played over a 5-reel, 30-payline game grid that doesn't have a pyramid in sight. The other two premiums can land anywhere from 1x1 to 1x4 in size and are worth up 10x the bet if a full line of five stretches across the grid. One is a Cleopatra type, the other, a Pharaoh. Also, each reel has a three-segment Scarab Holder located above it. Whenever a scarab symbol lands, it is added to both the Bonus Bar and its respective Scarab Holder.When a Scarab Holder is filled, a Wild Scrolls feature is awarded on the reel, turning it completely wild. Title: Jungle Gorilla
review: Jungle Gorilla: OverviewDeveloper Pragmatic Play takes players on a spot of wildlife watching in the nature-themed slot Jungle Gorilla. There are no guesses as to who the lead character around here might be. In the case of Jungle Gorilla, the 3/5 rating puts it in the medium spectrum of things whilst the default RTP is decent enough without being a standout on 96.57% - so no complaints there.The paytable includes 10 regular pay symbols, a golden gorilla scatter, plus a wild. These multipliers don’t rise forever though; each one is capped at x5 – even if a ton of gorilla scatters appear before it is used.Whenever a wild hits as part of a win, the respective reel multiplier is assigned to the symbol. If there is more than one wild multiplier on a win line, then their values are multiplied together rather than added. After the win is awarded, any used reel multipliers are reset back to x1. Moving to a new bet level starts the multipliers on x1, but any progress made will be saved when switching between the bet levels.Jungle Gorilla: VerdictPlaying Jungle Gorilla caused several older slots to flashback. Another NetEnt one, Gorilla Kingdom, also came to mind after a few spins. Of course, much of it due to the Harambe lookalike leading the action. Imagine if it could rack up an impressive multiplier while you waited, to be unleashed for a solid win.There were positive moments when the odd 100 to 250x hit would appear out of nowhere. However, a lot of the time testing felt like a relentless downward slide into bankroll oblivion. ‘Be fickle, fortune’, said Juliet, and satisfying rewards can be found in Jungle Gorilla. Single line wins are capped at 500x while Pragmatic Play quotes overall potential of up to 2,800 times the stake. An ok figure when you consider what you have to work with.If you are going to play Jungle Gorilla, then it might be best done so at a slow pace. On the other hand, if you’re the kind of player who wants to get on with things, or prefers more sophistication, then steer a wide berth around Jungle Gorilla.

Title: Thunder Hawk
review: Thunder Hawk: Slot OverviewArmenian software provider Peter & Sons heads out of doors for its Native American-themed online slot Thunder Hawk. First things first was working out what the title means, and when browsing the game info page and cross-referencing the words 'thunder hawk' online, we came across something called a 'Thunderbird', which Wikipedia describes as a 'supernatural being of power and strength.' Thunder Hawk the slot leans towards this mystical concept, and for features, it's got instant cash prizes, free spins with power-ups, Super Free Spins with power-ups, a Golden Bet and bonus buys.Thunder Hawk might not have the 'pure' Peter & Sons look we used to expect in each and every release, but it remains an attractive game with a distinctive look. Features are:Multiplier – multiplies the win amount with an x2 to x4 multiplier.Extra free spins – 1 to 3 extra free spins are awarded.Additional Thunderhawks – 1 to 3 Thunderhawk symbols are added.Super Free SpinsEach time the free spins round is unlocked, the meter beneath the reels progresses. When the meter is filled, Super Free Spins are triggered. For this bonus round, 5 free spins are awarded where only Thunderhawk symbols or blanks land. Thunderhawk symbols are sticky, and when spins end, a prize is awarded from the meter depending on how many Thunderhawks are in view. It is possible to receive 1 to 3 additional spins or extra Thunderhawk symbols on every spin.Bonus BuyClicking the Buy button opens up a menu with two bonus options. One is regular free spins round for 50 times the bet, and the second option is Super Free Spins for 150x the bet.Thunderhawk slot - feature buy optionsThunder Hawk: Slot VerdictYep, it's another 9 Masks kinda game, but coming from Peter & Sons means it manages to stand out from the crowded bunch to a degree. Being a Peter & Sons production means attractive artwork and pleasing sounds have combined to create a unique-looking slot. Not as striking as some of the studio's memorable works like Monster Blox to give an example, but still, Thunder Hawk looks like little else out there.The same can't quite be said about the gameplay, though, which revolves mostly around landing Thunderhawk symbols to scoop instant cash wins from the prize ladder. Or maybe it is altered this way on account of the multipliers to keep the game within its 5,000x the bet max win limit? Either way, 5,000x is Thunder Hawk's top prize. Also, Super Free Spins did not drop a feature on each spin. Either the demo needs a tweak, or the game rules do. Something to keep an eye out for in the future.So, did the world really need another one of these 9 Masks-style games? Title: Rainbow Riches Megaways
review: Rainbow Riches Megaways: ReviewThe first encounter we had with Barcrest's famous Leprechaun now seems like ages ago. Looking for something different to try, other than the usual 243 ways slots that we were playing with consistent regularity back in the days, Rainbow Riches seemed contrasting enough. Aside from having a fantastic session on it, which included a free spins round with a ridiculous amount of retriggers, what stuck to mind was the oddly primitive, but seducing sound effects and visuals. It wasn't until later that we became aware of the iconic status of the game, especially in the UK, where soon after its release it became one of the most popular slot machines in recent times.The time has now come for the Leprechaun to take a step into the modern era in a slot that preserves the classic feel of the original, but also benefits from the captivating action that the Megaways engine has to offer. Following a long series of Rainbow Riches games, this one utilises 6 reels and a random number of symbols per reel on each spin that can result in up to 117,649 ways to win when fully expanded. It comes with cascading reels, a Super Gem Bonus feature that turns all visible gems into matching symbols, and a Free Spins round with an unlimited win multiplier. You can play Rainbow Riches Megaways on all devices from between 20 cents to 20€ per spin.In terms of creative direction, the developers have made sure to keep the final design true to the original formula. This goes for all aspects of the game - sound, look and feel. With an Irish folklore theme, the reels are encased in gold coupled with a picturesque lush green countryside backdrop. Just below the unmistakable logo, a rainbow shoots out of a pot of gold filled to the brim with gold coins. On the reels you'll see the usual A to 10 royal values as well as blue, green, purple and orange gems. The most lucrative is the diamond with 6 of a kind giving you 50 times your stake. The wild symbol is represented by a horseshoe and substitutes for all regular symbols.Rainbow Riches Megaways: FeaturesMost people reading are likely already familiar with the Megaways game engine by now. Originally developed by Big Time Gaming, the concept of Megaways revolves around its shape-shifting reels that, in this particular game, can give you an outcome of between 2 to 7 symbols on reels 1 and 6, and between 2 and 6 symbols on the remaining reels, every time you hit the spin button. With some simple mathematical calculations, it means that each spin can bring about between 324 to 117,649 ways to win. Above reels 2, 3, 4 and 5, you'll also see a horizontal reel that delivers additional symbols, contributing to adjacent wins, as well as special symbols that only appear on this reel.Moreover, the Megaways concept is usually combined with cascading reels mechanics, which is also the case here - all symbols part of a winning combination explode to make room for new symbols. This chain effect repeats until no more winning combinations appear in view.Rainbow Riches Megaways comes with the Super Gem Bonus feature. It's quite similar to Blueprint Gaming's mystery symbols feature, but instead of appearing as a question mark across the reel set, it triggers when a Super Gem appears on the horizontal reel. When it does, all high-value gemstone symbols in view are transformed into one matching randomly chosen gemstone.Though offering excellent potential even in the base game, the Free Spins feature is the key to land the truly substantial wins. It comes into play when 4 or more scatter symbols land in view anywhere on the main reels and will give you 12 starting spins. For each additional scatter in view, 5 extra Free Spins are awarded. As is the case with all these Bonanza-type games, it's all about the unlimited win multiplier which increases by 1 on each winning cascade without ever reverting. During the free spins round, +1, +2 and +3 symbols may appear on the top reel to give you additional spins.If you don't want to wait for the free spins feature to drop organically, you can opt for the Buy Pass feature. For a cost of 100 times your stake, you'll gain direct access to the free spins. If you're feeling a bit more adventurous, you could go for the Take a Chance option instead. Hoping that the arrow lands on the green segment of the circle, you're odds of triggering the feature depends on the chosen stake - for a cost of 25, 50 or 75 times your stake, you will get a 25%, 50% or 75% chance of triggering the bonus respectively.Finally, there is the Bonus Bank feature, which reduces the price of the free spins bonus. 'Bank Off Wins' adds all wins to balance, 'Bank All Wins' adds all wins to the 'Bonus Bank', and 'Bank Small Wins' adds wins 3x stake or less to the 'Bonus Bank'.Rainbow Riches Megaways: Final VerdictAside from a couple of minor deviations, Rainbow Riches Megaways is a rather typical Megaways offering. For example, it's not too common for these slots to have different reel height settings as is the case here where the middle reels will give you no more than a maximum of 6 symbols as opposed to 7 on the first and last reels. Moreover, we found the RTP to be slightly lower than what you normally see in other Megaways slots, but being Barcrest, whose slots are usually around the 95% mark, we're not too surprised.Medium to high variance, it offers outstanding potential reaching well over 10,000 times your stake. High roller should take notice, however, that the game is capped at a maximum payout of 250,000€. Overall, it's a Megaways game as good as any other and will appeal to all players that enjoy these types of slots that are known, not only for their great potential, but also the extended and entertaining gameplay they have to offer. Rainbow Riches Megaways is, in our opinion at least, by far the best game in the Rainbow Riches series.If you're a fan of the Megaways game mechanic we suggest you take a look at Barcrest's second Megaways slot and their first ever branded release Beetlejuice Megaways. For more Big Time Gaming related mechanics, there's also Slot Vegas Megaquads.

Title: Dragon Horn

Title: Aztec Ascent

If you can get a great roll on, build a decent multiplier and knock out a few symbols for the mystery reveal, wins as high as 40,000x the bet are technically possible. It is quite a convoluted process and plays in a similar way to Yggdrasil's Valley of the Gods. Starting with the most common number of free spins, 8, doesn't leave a huge amount of time to accomplish much. It does get exciting when the collecting is going your way, yet it's generally not the hard and fast hit of adrenaline, something like Top Dawg$ is, by comparison.One slight downer is the base game is a tad sleepy. It's also interesting that Aztec Ascent doesn't have feature buy options, which would have come in handy for some since the base game isn't a major thrill fest, more a quiet Central American hike. Title: Tiki Fruits Totem Frenzy
review: Tiki Fruits Totem Frenzy: Slot OverviewDeveloper Red Tiger isn’t exactly massively renowned for grid slots, but there are a few playable numbers lurking in their back catalogue. Potential, however, has seen a clear increase, though it’s still nothing to go crazy over.Using a cluster pays system, you get a win in Tiki Fruits Totem Frenzy when 5 or more identical symbols connect vertically or horizontally. When this occurs, the successful cluster disappears, and symbols above fall into place, so consecutive wins on each spin are possible. When no new clusters form, the spin comes to an end.The fruit on offer in Totem Frenzy is pretty exotic, and most aren’t what you usually associate with a classic fruit slot. Higher value symbols include dice, stars, bells, diamonds, and 7s, worth 50 to 777 times your stake for a cluster made up of 25+ symbols.Tiki Fruits Totem Frenzy: Slot FeaturesDuring the base game, the extras revolve around the Tikis and the Totems. Title: 101 Candies

Feature Coins activate, then disappear from the reels in an Avalanche before a wild symbol moves from the Wild Conveyor to the reels.The Upgrade symbol increases the multipliers of all wild symbols by 1 up to a maximum of x101.The Destroy symbol removes 5 wild symbols from the Wild Conveyor.The Scramble symbol shuffles all wild symbols on the Wild Conveyor.The Transform symbol picks a random symbol on the reels and replaces all instances of it with another symbol.
