However, this method is clearly effective, and Pragmatic Play has stretched the win cap, pushing it out to 10,000x the bet. Gear up for some crazy tumbling, symbol collections to get to that level.In the end, Sword of Ares was a satisfying scatter-paying game to review. Pragmatic Play has married scatter wins to the tumble mechanic while tying in symbol collections and unlocking multipliers menagerie of mechanics quite well. Sword of Ares doesn't have the same level of fresh originality the first one had, which is understandable, being a follow-up, but the extended win cap and the new bits should be warmly received by players excited by this style of action.

Title: The Ultimate 5

Title: Banana Town
review: Banana Town: Slot OverviewIn the evolution of video games, some releases tower above others, providing inspiration, fuelling the industry, or being simply downright fun to play. One of the early video game titans was Donkey Kong, created by Shigeru Miyamoto and released in 1981. The game was a hit and went on to spawn numerous sequels, spin-offs, and franchises; and was the first time Mario appeared on screen before going on to find his own mega success. Tapping into the look and feel of an earlier Donkey Kong inspired age is an online slot called Banana Town from Relax Gaming. Banana Town is a game that uses a scatter pays system in combination with cascades, symbol specific progressive win multipliers, and free spins.Relax Gaming has evoked the spirit of an earlier age of video gaming by using an 8-bit approach to style Banana Town. This isn’t the first time the studio has done so, so we’re guessing someone on the team has a soft spot for classic video games. Similar releases from Relax Gaming have been the Christmas slot Santa’s Stack and the outstanding celebration of all things old-school in Hellcatraz, though the game that might actually have started the trend was Thunderkick with Flame Busters. It means chunkier than normal graphics, jerkier than usual animations, and bleepy sounds. Modern gamers might find it a tad old fashioned, but perhaps not, since games like the Mr Hopp’s Playhouse trilogy, and Baldi’s Basics are popular at the time of writing, all having an old-school flavour about them.Banana Town slot - base gamePlayed on a 6-reel, 5-column panel, Banana Town uses a scatter pay system to generate wins. As long as at least 8 matching symbols are in view, anywhere on the grid, a payout is made, similar to popular games like Sweet Bonanza. Wins occur at a frequency of 18.45%, leading to a total return value of 96.12%, or 96.16%, when buying free spins. Regular bets range from 10 p/c to $/€50 per spin, which should satisfy most players.Normal pay symbols consist of four lower value bananas coloured in blue, green, red, and yellow, plus five gangster looking monkey symbols. Landing 8-9 matching symbols is worth 0.5x for the low pays, rising to 1-4x for the high pays, while 12+ symbol wins pay 2-3x for the lows and 4-12x for the premiums. No wilds are used in Banana Town at any time.Banana Town: Slot FeaturesBanana Town slot - splash screenThe features in Banana Town are quite simplistic and include a progressive multiplier system in the base game, which gets a persistent factor when free spins are active. Firstly though, when a scatter win hits, the winning symbols are removed from the grid and symbols left on the reels fall down to close the gaps. If a new winning scatter is formed, the cascade feature is repeated again until no new win appears. In addition, wins are collected by a meter located on the right side of the grid. Each winning symbol type increases its corresponding win multiplier. The multipliers start at x1 and double after each symbol win, up to a maximum of x64.Free SpinsA total of 8 free spins are triggered when 3 dollar sign symbols land, plus an extra spin is granted for each additional dollar sign in view. While free spins are active, individual dollar sign symbols may add +1 free spins to the remaining amount. One important difference in the bonus round is that each symbol’s win multiplier is persistent, so they do not reset back to x1 as they do in the bonus round.Bonus BuyRather than wait for the requisite number of dollar sign bonus symbols to hit, applicable players can pay 100x the bet to trigger free spins right away. Before bought free spins begin, win multipliers can be randomly increased.Banana Town slot - free spinsBanana Town: Slot VerdictIf you’re keen on a bit of back in the day gaming, then Banana Town should be a delight when it opens up. It doesn’t have the immediate pull Hellcatraz had, and the gameplay isn’t as in-depth either, but the bright, sunny use of the limited colour palette is pleasing to the eyes and no doubt heart-warming as well if you grew up playing video games that looked like this. Donkey Kong is an absolute legend, being a platform-based paradigm shift that boosted both Nintendo and the video game industry as a whole. He sits up there alongside luminaries like Pac-Man, Ms Pac-Man, Mario, Sonic, Pikachu, and Link, as entertainment royalty.In many early video games, figuring out patterns can lead to glorious moments, but until then, the learning curve can be quite frustrating. Do you ever remember playing older games and feeling like they weren’t just difficult, but the console or computer was actively working against you to make you lose? How many controllers have been smashed on the ground in fits of exasperation…? We’re not saying Banana Town has much of a learning curve. On the contrary, it’s a simple game, really. Land wins, build multipliers, and hopefully land more wins to benefit from said multipliers. It can happen in the base game during better cascade sequences, though free spins are where the magic is probably more likely to happen since multipliers are persistent. Hitting the buy free spins option was where frustration was highest, as it seemed rather difficult to end a round with a positive result.Of course, we might have hit a poor run, fair dues, and there were times when a sizable multiplier met with a decent scatter win for a satisfying payout. Banana Town is not one of Relax Gaming’s massive slots, though, with a modest (for them) max win of 10,000x the bet. It also didn’t feel as explosive as other slots they’ve done. In Banana Town, landing 12 or more of the top premium symbols at the same time as an x64 multiplier leads to 768x the bet payout. Few would say no to a hit like that, but again, it’s kind of modest by Relax Gaming standards.The good news is that Relax Gaming standards are exceptionally high, and even if Banana Town might not be one of their key releases, it’s still an enjoyable, potentially exasperating, exploration of an earlier era of gaming with a simple yet at times thrilling set of features.

Title: PopRocks
review: PopRocks Slot: OverviewNo, this is not a slot based on the candy that pops in your mouth, PopRocks is the latest title from Hong Kong based studio Avatar UX. A collaboration with Yggdrasil’s Masters Program, PopRocks comes with an intriguing game design based on their new trademarked PopWins feature. It also boasts some pretty big numbers when it comes to both paylines and potential as you will see.Avatar UX creates Asian themed games for the European market, and it shows with PopRocks – more so than with their previous slot, Lilith’s Inferno, despite the characters and the martial arts fighting. Along with expanding reels and popping symbols is innovative game mechanic which plays out like a grid slot at times. Sounds confusing? All will be revealed.The game world is a little like the popular Netflix show Ice Fantasy. If you missed that one, it was a full-blown Asian good vs evil tussle, and PopRocks looks like it's set in the Fire Tribe’s kingdom. It’s a murky underworld with an ominous castle visible through the game’s transparent reels. If you like a high drama soundtrack while you spin, then PopRocks will appeal. It’s like a chase scene from a Disney action movie that will either entertain or annoy. It's worth mentioning, however, that the game still was in development during testing and that there was still some work to be done on the sounds.Visually, PopRocks doesn't exactly arouse awe but it gets the job done even if it has a slight generic feel to it. The grid is expandable and starts with a default 5 reel, 3 row arrangement along with 486 win ways - the game pays both ways which is why you get 243 win ways x 2. To get popping, stakes from 10 p/c up to $/€30 must be set first. One positive stat to mull over in the meantime is a rather generous RTP of 96.8%. Nice to see in a time when RTP is creeping downwards. PopRocks is insanely volatile though and sessions required sitting through stacks of dead and low pay wins until the expanded reels and features were unleashed.Moving on to the paytable, the symbols leave no doubt about the games origins and theme and are split into four categories – low, medium, high, and the appropriately named super high. The lows are a bunch of Asian infused 10-A royals which make up the bulk of the wins. Next up are the medium pays, which are four gems – green, blue, purple, and red. More personality has been injected into the high pays, which include gems clasped by dragons in blue, purple, green, and golden hues. Just one symbol earns the tile of super high and 5 of them are worth 100 times the stake.Low pay symbols are low value indeed, but when the features take off, they can have a huge effect on payout values. Wilds complete the paytable and can substitute for any other pay symbols. One thing to keep in mind is that high and super high symbols do not appear organically from spins, but only from Pops – let’s look at what that means.PopRocks Slot: FeaturesBonus mode in actionPopRocks is a slot that works best when the features are firing on all cylinders. Central is the PopWins feature which is similar to a cascade wins system with a few different rules. Firstly, symbols from winning combos are Popped off the reels, and each one is replaced by two new symbols. Obviously, more space is needed for the extra symbols, so the game extends reels to do so – each reel can expand 7 symbols high at the most.The right hand side of the reels displays the number of current win ways in play while the left-hand side has a multiplier meter that lights up when symbols are Popped. Each batch of 7 Popped symbols increases the multiplier by +1.When each reel has been expanded to 7 rows high, the Bonus Mode is triggered. In this mode, a wild is added to the game, the multiplier increases in increments of +2 rather than +1, and only one new symbol appears from each pop. Also, the win ways hit 33,614 – due to lines paying both ways.PopRocks Slot: VerdictPopRocks brings enough novel features to the party to make it worth checking out. If you like grid slots with high inertia, you might appreciate what PopRocks can do. It’s hard to get going, but once it does, it can power on and on, racking up wins in the process. Without free spins, respins, or any sort of bonus games, it relies solely on its big runs to provide the major thrills and rewards. Because these runs can be quite profitable, the rest of the game tends to putter along not doing a whole lot and when you hit that dry spell, the repetitive low win pop cycles can really test your patience. On the other hand, the fact that the game can skyrocket on any spin and go berserk undoubtedly adds a compelling element.If you don’t manage to get it on a good roll, not much else happens. Symbol values are so low that without a ton of consecutive winners blowing up all of the features, wins remain too small to do anything else expect drain accounts. Even when Pops chain together, you also need the high pay symbols to play their part in getting close to that fabled 72,188x potential. Of course, that is easier said than done.PopRocks is certainly worth a look, maybe a demo to get a feel for what it can do. Avatar UX has done a respectable job overall, it looks ok, plays well, and the features can be quite absorbing. Tread carefully though, PopRocks defines what all or nothing gaming is all about.If you enjoy the PopWins feature, take a look at WildPops which is the second slot from Avatar UX to utilise PopWins.

Title: 4 Fantastic Lobsters

(clone of Dead or Alive)Imperial Riches (original)If you've been around for a couple of years, it probably won't be too hard to guess which classic NetEnt game that has been cloned and re-branded as King of 3 Kingdoms. Title: Tropicool 3
review: Tropicool 3: Slot OverviewSwedish software provider ELK Studios is a creative lot, and one of the more out-there game worlds it has come up with is one originally populated by two birds known as Tony Toucan and Fiona Flamingo. Both were fed up with migrating each year, so they created their own little beachside paradise… in Antarctica. Not sure about the icy weather, but it would be a good place to go if you like avoiding crowds. Tropicool 2 introduced a sloth named Elmo, and we've now got part three in the series to contend with. Tropicool 3 is the name, and it keeps to the cold theme while bringing in a different set of mechanics.We say different, yet the tilted columns of symbols and the gravity effect have been lifted straight out of ELK's Cygnus range. The scene has changed too. There's still loads of snow about the place, and the overall sensorial effect is a chilly one, but it looks like we're in Las Vegas this time around rather than the southernmost parts of the world. No doubt there is a back story that explains everything, except it was not available at the time of review. Players are free to make one up. Maybe Tony and Fiona came to get hitched? Maybe Elmo snaked Fiona away from Tony, and the two of them eloped to Vegas for a shotgun wedding? Hey, feel free to go wild with the story.Tropicool 3 slot - base gameHitting the spin button drops 6 columns onto the grid, each column holding 6 symbols, where there are up to 46,656 connecting paylines. Wins pay when matching symbols are in at least 3 adjacent columns starting from the leftmost side, and an Avalanche feature triggers when wins appear. Tropicool 3 is a medium-high volatile slot, carrying ELK Studios' goto RTP figure of 94%. This return value remains the same whether activating bonuses from the X-iter or straight wagering 20 c to $/€100 per game round.Symbols time, and for low pays, Tropicool 3 has four fruits encased in ice worth 0.25x the bet for 6 OAK, then a lizard, a snake, a scarab, and birds icons as the higher paying symbols. Hitting 6 matching high pays awards 0.5 to 5 times the bet. Two wild symbols appear in the game – regular wilds, and locked wilds, both substitute any regular pay symbols. The difference is a locked wild lasts for 3 wins before it is removed by the Avalanche mechanic.Tropicool 3: Slot FeaturesTropicool 3 slot - free spinsTropicool 3's list of extras includes the Cool Reel, Elmo's Revenge, feature symbols, a free spins bonus game, a super free spins bonus game, and X-iter feature buys.Cool ReelThe Cool Reel on top of the grid has 3 rows with feature symbols, scatter symbols, and empty symbols. Feature symbols are activated when they drop into the main grid. A game round starts with new symbols dropping onto the main grid and new feature symbols sliding in from the right on the Cool Reel. Each winning combination on the main grid is paid, and the symbols (not unspent Locked Wilds) are removed from the reels; then, the remaining symbols drop vertically with gravity. The symbols from the first row on the Cool Reel above the winning columns drop onto the main grid and roll as far left or right as possible. Gravity also applies to the Cool Reel, which gets refilled from the right. Any new wins are paid, and the Avalanche process repeats until no more wins occur.Elmo's RevengeWhen an Elmo symbol reaches the leftmost column, the Elmo's Revenge feature triggers by dropping the complete Cool Reel onto the main grid. If the Elmo symbol ends on the bottom of columns 2-6, it is removed and dropped down again in the column one step to the left if possible.Feature SymbolsThe feature symbols available in the game are these:Multiplier Symbol – increases the win multiplier by x1 to x25 when dropping down from the Cool Reel.Row Swap – replaces payout symbols on a line with the same symbol.Mystery – all reveal a common pay symbol at the end of a drop.Bonus GameHitting 3, 4, 5, or 6 bonus scatter symbols awards players 6, 9, 12, or 15 free spins, respectively. During free spins, the Cool Reel is repopulated with new feature symbols for each free drop, and the win multiplier is sticky between drops. Locked wilds remain on the grid between drops till fully used. Getting Extra Drop symbols from the Cool Reel adds +1, +2, or +3 extra drops. In the base game, when 3 or more scatters are in view at the same time as an Elmo symbol, the super bonus game is awarded. In this round, 1 Elmo symbol is always in play on the main grid.X-iterFrom the X-iter menu, players have access to these bonus modes:Bonus Hunt – 3x the bet buys a game round with more than triple the chance of triggering the bonus game.Locked Wilds – 25x the bet buys a game round with 3 locked wilds dropping on the grid.Elmo's Revenge – 50x the bet buys a game round with a guaranteed Elmo symbol.Bonus Game – 100x the bet.Super Bonus Game – 500x the bet.Tropicool 3 slot - free spinsTropicool 3: Slot VerdictPretty much all of Tropicool 3's features have a familiar ring to them, but ELK Studios has made tweaks and alterations around the edges to bring something relatively new to the table. The gameplay, in general, feels like the studio has sewed together parts of the Tropicool line with parts of the Cygnus range into one odd, oddly good at times slot. Thematically, Tropicool 3 makes for an unusual break from the previous two games, adding quirk to a series that was already pretty out there. Frozen Vegas or a Vegas-like location with Ancient Egyptian overtones, huh? Okay, why not.Shame the animal characters don't really make much of an appearance on the screen or grid like they did in the original release, yet Tropicool fans are compensated by a new way of mechanically experiencing the game. It's not entirely new-new, obviously, since we've seen this mechanism power the Cygnus range. But it gels well with the Cool Reel and the goodies the feature reel is able to unload onto the grid. Elmo's Revenge becomes one of the most desirable outcomes then, and adds fire to the super bonus game since an Elmo symbol is visible the whole time. Yes, the gravity effect can be frustrating when it gravities in annoying ways, yet potentially highly satisfying when chains of symbols plop around the grid just the way you wanted them to. Hitting full satisfaction levels would mean achieving Tropicool 3's maximum winning potential of 25,000x the bet - this is a lot higher than it was in the first release, though the same as Tropicool 2.All in all, the meeting of Tropicool and Cygnus was, for the most part, a success. Each component brings its particular way of tantalising and/or rewarding to the mix, making for not exactly a raging hotbed of innovation but original in that the combination of mechanics gives players hungry for novelty an option to try. Tropicool was a fine game, though the blending of two forms rather than emphasising one or the other, at times, threatened to dilute rather than enhance the final product, losing some individuality in the process.

Title: KokeshiPop

Title: Build the Bank

Title: Candy Fall
review: Candy Fall: Slot OverviewThis game has likely been cancelledAlong with literature and manned space flight, one of the greatest things to come out of Russia has got to be the game Tetris. Title: Mystery of the Orient

Title: Lost City of the Djinn

This time it comes with an outer shell steeped in concepts such as magic, Djinn, and desert exploration.Whether exploring lost cities is preferable to avoiding fangs sinking into your neck, we'll leave to personal preference. Djinn Spins are where the desert heat gets a chance to ignite. As is usually the case with these sorts of bonus rounds, normal symbols can drum up and okay win, helped along by special symbols which can make a real difference.In terms of special symbols, Lost City comes up a little short when compared to the big hitters it's going up against, namely MT2 et al., since there are just two of them, and they are pretty basic. However, basic can still be effective; plus, when factoring in the Pattern Collect feature, Lost City of the Djinn can go bananas in the right set of circumstances. Like Baron Bloodmore, max win tops out at the impressive level of 25,000 times the stake.Lost City of the Djinn isn't as creative as they usually are from Thunderkick, seeing as it is basically a clone. It was a little surprising to find out the studio hadn't added anything in the way of innovation, so, no twists, turns, or clever new features. Title: Steam Squad

Game world is super important when doing a Steampunk slot, and Red Tiger has layered on quite a good one. A bizarre underwater realm greets players at the home screen before the camera pans up into the aforementioned cloud domain for the main game. If the win is improved, then the process repeats until no new winning symbols land.AmplifiersOn each spin, random multipliers of x2 to x100 appear above each reel. When a reel is filled with winning symbols, the respective multiplier is awarded and applied to the total of the win at the end of the spin. If more than one multiplier is awarded, the values are added up.Power UpAt random, after non-winning symbols are destroyed, a winning symbol may power up. When this happens, the symbol clones itself, filling the whole reel.Booster RowAlso at random, on a spin, a metal frame may appear on one of the rows. If this row is filled with winning symbols, a booster is activated. The booster triggers after no more winning symbols land after a winning wipeout. The booster may create a winning symbol in place of a non-winning one and continue the wipeout, or if a multiplier is activated, it will increase the multiplier by +1, +2, +3, +4, or +5. After the booster is applied, the metal frame moves to a higher row, which is not filled with winning symbols.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters on a base game spin awards 8, 10, 12, or 15 free spins, respectively. During the feature, landing 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters awards an extra 3, 5, 7, or 10 free spins, respectively. In free spins, the booster row is always active, and it may move between spins. In addition, when a reel is filled with winning symbols, all multipliers shown above reels are increased by +1. Multipliers are incremented until the end of the round.Buy FeaturePlayers may buy the free spins feature for 70x the bet, and doing so comes with an increased return value of 96%.Steam Squad slot - free spinsSteam Squad: Slot VerdictWith Steam Squad, do we have a studio holding two red hot tropes in their hands – Steampunk and scatter pays, then bringing them together to create something wildly experimental, or is this a desperate bid to leap on two separate trends at the same time? Debatable as the end result has its ups and downs. Scatter-paying mechanics have really taken off recently, helped along by slots like Pragmatic Play's Gates of Olympus, Gates of Olympus 1000 and its many follow-ons. Nowadays, it seems like every other studio is getting in on the act. Red Tiger itself has dabbled in the past; Sugar Monster is an example, and it has dabbled again for Steam Squad, where a number of features work alongside the scatter-paying mechanism.It's not a bad mix either. You can picture the boffins at Red Tiger, Steampunk goggles resting on foreheads, cogs flying about the place, sizzling bolts of electricity lighting up the workshop. It's a bit slow and sluggish at times, and the max win is a tad disappointing. In a game with so many sizable reel multipliers, topping out at 3,235.4x the bet seems a bit contradictory. Perhaps the game's maker was running on Victorian exchange rate values when it was coming up with win numbers. If that figure doesn't dampen your enthusiasm, then there's enough going on in Steam Squad regarding scatter-paying activity to warrant a look.If Steam Squad was a rickety airship cobbled together using cogs and dials and pistons and so on, a question remains over how reliable it would be for flying high above the planet through the clouds. Title: Sword Stomp

This approach really is Sword Stomp's main selling point though. For players in the mood for keeping it simple, a bit of old-school gaming with Viking imagery, then Sword Stomp ticks many of the right boxes. While the graphical standard is quite high, Sword Stomp managed to feel retro and has the sort of uncomplicated, some might say unsophisticated, gameplay which can literally slam down like a sledgehammer and do significant amounts of damage, when all's going well.It's interesting, the overriding comparison slot which kept bubbling up in the mind while reviewing Sword Stomp was none other than Thunderstruck 2. What's even more interesting is that even now, over a decade later, the Microgaming release felt like the fuller game. Maybe this is partly due to Thunderstruck 2's classic status. Not meaning to take anything away from Sword Stomp, though; it's a decent alternative for gamblers after a simple, old-school battler. The win cap isn't too shabby either, coming in at 10,000 times the bet.Sword Stomp is one of those love-it-or-leave-it situations. On the one hand, some players may love the simplistic savagery that sticky, full reel wilds with multipliers of up to x100 bring to the table, whereas others may find the whole venture a little too backwards for their tastes. Imagine a feast in Valhalla. Are you picturing delicate plates offering a wide variety of exquisite delicacies, brought in from across the nine realms, or a table covered in hunks of roast ox? Title: Gravity Bonanza
review: Gravity Bonanza: Slot OverviewJust like Vegas - 'what happens in a black hole stays in a black hole'. Thank you, Internet, for that side-splitting start to the review of Gravity Bonanza, an online slot from developer Pragmatic Play. No stranger to the outer limits of human travel, Pragmatic Play earlier ventured forth into the great inky unknown in the crash game Spaceman, but Gravity Bonanza, by contrast, is a more conventional online slot. It utilises a tumble mechanic in conjunction with a Black Hole symbol feature to hoover up certain symbols to potentially award a Gravity Bonus – possibly with a multiplier in free spins. When a Black Hole Symbol hits, a random type of symbol is chosen, and all instances of this symbol in view and on following tumbles are collected by the Gravity Bonus indicator. When tumbles end, the total number of collected symbols is paid according to the pay table.Free SpinsHitting 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7 scatter symbols in the base game awards 10, 15, 20, 30, or 50 free spins, respectively. In the free spins round, extra free spins are awarded in the same way. During the round, when the Black Hole symbol hits, it can do so with a multiplier of x2, x3, x5, or x10, which is applied to the Gravity Bonus prize when awarded.Bonus BuyPlayers keen to rocket into the bonus round can do so for the cost of 100x the bet. Once bought, 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7 scatter symbols will land to trigger the feature.Gravity Bonanza slot - free spinsGravity Bonanza: Slot VerdictFor a while, black holes existed only in theory, thanks to luminaries like Albert Einstein and Karl Schwarzschild, until the first one, Cygnus X-1, was identified in 1971. Fascinating phenomenon, one way black holes are formed is when a massive star collapses in on itself, its weight crushing in on all sides to compress the star into a singularity – a point of infinite density and zero volume that is exceptionally good at drawing in things which happen to float too close by. To push a metaphor, Pragmatic Play is rather good at drawing in all manner of ideas that cross its path for use in its games, as well. Simple yet fun, clever without being game-changing, but good for producing wins of up to 10,000x the bet.Being torn to bits as you're being dragged across the event horizon of a black hole where gravity is so crushingly powerful not even light can escape its pull would be pretty boo, right? Title: Dave Lame Bad Magician
review: Dave Lame Bad Magician: Slot OverviewHave you noticed when magicians perform their routines, they often spend a lot longer on the build-up than on the actual trick itself. All that swanning around a stage with attractive assistants, to a backing track of cheesy music getting everything in place. Then you have to make sure not to blink, or you might miss the actual magic. Fine, we get it, the dramatic ramping up is used to build tension, and as long as it leads to some form of payoff, the audience is generally happy to put up with the chichi showmanship.What happens when both the showmanship and the payoff never quite meet expectations? That's the question formed after playing Dave Lame Bad Magician from SG Digital: a magic-themed slot set on stage at a theatre, complete with drum rolls, big top music, and a look that makes you wonder if SG was going for some sort of retro thing. Yes or no, the game looks more dated than stylish, though it packs a lot of features in its various magician pockets.Played on a traditional 5-reel, 3-row game grid, which expands during one of the features, Dave Lame Bad Magician provides 20 fixed paylines to land winning combinations across. Dave might be a lame magician, but one thing that is not so lame is the math model driving the game. First up is an RTP figure of 96.10% combined with volatility officially classed as medium-high. Regular wins occur at a rate of 1 in 4.71 spins, while bonus games trigger on average every 153.9 spins, though they seemed more frequent during our testing sessions.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin, line-pays occur when matching symbols land on adjacent reels beginning on the far-left reel. Card royals J-A printed on actual cards are used for the low pay symbols while saws, bunnies in hats, flowers, and the game's logo are the high pays. Premium symbols payout 5 to 25 times the stake for five of a kind, bested by the wild, which is worth up to 50x for a line of five. Wilds land anywhere, though they are usually there to replace any of the pay symbols to complete line wins.Dave Lame Bad Magician: Slot FeaturesThere's no shortage of special symbols, modifiers, or bonus games in Dave Lame Bad Magician. Starting with the Dave Lame's Disappearing Act feature, during the base game, there is a chance that Dave Lame appears on both sides of the reels. When he does, win lines pay both ways for 2-5 respins, and wins on multiple lines are added together.Keep an eye out for the bonus symbol, it appears on reels 1, 3, or 5 in the base game, and landing 3 at once gains you entry to the Pick A Pot feature. Here, 5 red cups containing one bonus game each are shuffled around on a table. Players pick a pot to reveal one of the 5 bonus games.Then, you can either collect the feature or gamble it. When gambling, 2 pots are shuffled, and players pick one to move up or down the feature list. If the bottom feature was initially won, it is possible to pick a cup containing a consolation prize. If you get this one you win 10-15x the bet and go back to the base game.The following bonus games are available in the game:The Knife Throw bonus game displays a spinning wheel with an assistant tied to the middle and 10 balloons around the wheel's edge. Players pick 3 balloons for Dave to throw knives at, each one revealing a bet multiplier. The possible values are x2, x3, x5, x8, x10, x20, x30, or x50. When 3 balloons have been popped, the values are added together and awarded. If you were wondering, Dave won't throw the knife at the lady, only at balloons.Rabbits out of Dave's Hat awards 6 free spins. On each spin, rabbits or doves leap out of a hat and land on the reel in random positions, turning them wild. This feature cannot be retriggered.The Card Trick bonus game also awards 6 free spins on a grid where only special card symbols appear. Before the round begins, players pick one of these 5 cards – 2x, 5x, 8x, 10x, or 25x. If this card lands on a free spin, it doubles its value. During the feature, when cards land on the grid, they lock in place, then all values are added up and awarded when the free spins end. If a joker card lands, Dave reveals one of the multiplier cards – if it matches the card you initially selected, then it is increased by its original value.Winning the Escapology feature awards an unlimited free spins bonus game. During this one, whenever a special tap symbol lands, it adds an extra row, +10 ways to the existing grid, and increases the win multiplier by +1. Free spins end when the reel set reaches a total of 9 rows high.The final feature is the Sawing a Reel in Half bonus. When winning this one, Dave cuts the grid so players get either 2, 3, or 4 separate reel sets. When wilds land, they are transferred onto all other reel sets. Also, landing 3 bonus symbols on a reel set awards +2 additional free spins.Dave Lame Bad Magician: Slot VerdictLike The Shitty Beatles in Wayne's World, Dave Lame Bad Magician isn't just a clever name. If SG was going for a retro look they have done better to push the clock back a few extra years. Maybe if they'd worked the very early days of illusion, or used an Edwardian/Harry Houdini angle, or even done the 80s thing other studios are doing, it might have worked better than the Freddi Fish era looking game we got. Dave's got a friendly Mr Bean vibe, yet it’s hard to get past the feeling that, yeah, it is all a bit lame.This applies to other parts of the game too, the animations, for one, are pretty sluggish, the pace might have benefited from an extra push to get it going, and the features are amusing yet come across underpowered. Dave Lame Bad Magician follows on from other SG related slots like Cluedo Cash Mystery, being jam-packed with a large number of bonus games and features. Like Gremlins, SG has used a concept Blueprint Gaming has made famous of spinning a reel to win bonus games, which can then be gambled for potentially better ones. It shows you how much Blueprint Gaming has honed its craft. For example, The Goonies Return, to pick just one feature fest, is a master class in execution by comparison.As to rewards, Dave Lame Bad Magician isn't going to set the world of illusions alight, but they aren't bad. The slot's home page touts payouts of up to 5,000x the bet, though the game sheet lowers the 'Maximum Win' to 4,048x the bet. Interestingly, despite the name, Dave Lame's Disappearing Act provided the biggest win during the review. Not to say Dave can't step it up in the bonus games, but it didn't pan out that way for us during testing.To conclude, Dave Lame Bad Magician's title set the bar pretty low from the outset, which the rest of the game never really managed to lift it. To sign off with a cultural reference, the experience was akin to Gob's disappearing yacht act from the show Arrested Development. 'Where once there was a yacht, now there is not', he proclaims, before sinking the family's $700k boat to the tune of The Final Countdown.

Title: Hercules 10K Ways
review: Hercules 10K Ways: Slot OverviewHercules, son of the god Jupiter and the mortal Alcmena is the Roman adaptation of the Greek hero Heracles, who is probably most well known for his 12 Labours. You know, slaying the Nemean Lion, slaying the Lernaean Hydra, and slaying the Stymphalian Birds. He did do more than just slay, by the way, but the tendency to do battle is what drives much of Hercules 10K Ways, an online slot from software provider ReelPlay. Released in conjunction with partner studio Yggdrasil Gaming, Hercules 10K Ways' central feature is a hold 'n win round, which includes Hercules going toe to toe with a fearsome melange of monsters.One thing tying 10K Ways slots together is their Megaways-ish looking gaming panel. Hercules 10K Ways' matrix has 6 reels that spin vertically and a 4 symbols reel running side to side on the top. Unlike Megaways, the same number of symbols land on each and every spin producing the same number of ways to win - 10,000, hence the name. For setting, Hercules 10K Ways is held in a golden-hued land of Greco-Roman structures, mountains, sunbeams, and so forth. It's an okay view, nothing overly special, but when the bonus game triggers, be prepared to witness Hercules in all his raw pec-poppin' splendour.Hercules 10K Ways slot - base gameWhen it comes to ruddy great hold 'n win games, 10K Ways slots don't tend to sit in the upper echelons of the scale. More sort of mid-tier, technically speaking. Part of this assessment in the case of Hercules 10K Ways is due to a medium-high volatile math model, capped with decent, if not stunning winning possibilities. The game is available at four RTP levels; the highest is 96.1% which has a hit frequency of 24.52%. Wins pay from the leftmost reel onwards, provided matching symbols land on adjacent reels, and the bet levels are 20 p/c to $/€40 per spin.Hercules 10K Ways low pay 9-A card royals look like they've been recycled straight from Thor 10K Ways, though the 4 high pay beast symbols are new. Getting a winning line of 6 card rank symbols is worth a payout of 0.5 to 1.2 times the bet, rising to 2 to 100 times the stake for landing a 6 premium symbol win. Hercules appears on the top reel only during the base game, where he can be used to substitute for all symbols except Golden Apples.Heracles 10K Ways: Slot FeaturesHercules 10K Ways slot - free spins splash screenHercules 10K Ways' base game relies on cascades as its main feature, only really kicking up a gear when at least 5 Golden Apples land to trigger the Hercules Battle Spins Feature.CascadesEach symbol in a winning way is removed by the cascade mechanic and replaced by symbols from above or to the side (on the top reel). This process repeats until no new win is created after a cascade.Hercules Battle Spins FeatureEach triggering Golden Apple symbol awards its displayed value, and each one of them gives Hercules +1 life point, up to a maximum of 10. The first opponent appears on the opposite side of the grid to Hercules, and its life points are also displayed. The order of the opponents is Boar, Hydra, Cerberus, then Lion, each starting with 3, 4, 5, or 6 life points, respectively.Now, 3 respins are initially awarded, making up a Battle Round. Only the current monster's symbols, Hercules symbols (displaying a prize value), or blanks land during a Battle Round. When Hercules or monster symbols land, they are sticky until the end of the Battle Round. When a Battle Round ends (either spins run out or all positions are filled), symbols on the grid are processed left to right and top to bottom. When a Monster symbol is processed, it reduces Hercules' Life points by 1. When a Hercules symbol is processed, it reduces the monster's life points by 1 and awards its prize.If Hercules' Life points reach 0 before all symbols are processed, then the symbol processing ends, ending the bonus round. If the opponent's life reaches 0 before all symbols are processed, the remaining unprocessed Hercules symbols change to Golden Apples, which add Life points to Hercules and award their prize. Then the next opponent appears (up to Lion). If a Battle Round ends and Hercules still has life points, another Battle Round is triggered, awarding 3 more respins. At the start of a Battle Round, the grid is cleared.If the Lion is defeated, a Victory Prize is awarded, and the feature ends. The Victory Prize will be the Grand, Major, Minor, or Mini worth 2,000x, 250x, 50x, or 10x the bet, respectively. Golden Apples and Hercules symbols during the round display either a non-bonus prize of 1 to 100x the bet or the Grand, Major, Minor, or Mini.Hercules 10K Ways slot - free spinsHercules 10K Ways: Slot VerdictFirst off, a quick tip of the hat to ReelPlay for reaching into its bag of tricks and doing something different with the 10K range. It won't be to all tastes; players who prefer the Money Train side of the hold 'n win spectrum might find Hercules 10K Ways a bit slow-paced, a bit lightweight despite all the battling happening in the bonus round. Although, players who don't want to dodge runaway freight trains may prefer the video game slash cinematic quality that Reel Play has worked into Hercules 10K Ways.Not so much in the base game since there are no features other than cascading wins, meaning Hercules 10K Ways cranks along in a cyclical manner, churning out dead spins and ways wins. With its large number of ways, the base game is technically able to produce a decent result when the right symbols show up. This leaves the Hercules Battle Spins feature to pick up the slack, and this it does better than first presumed. After reviewing a few of these 10K Ways slots by now, the supposition was that Hercules 10K Ways would deliver another fairly dry bout of landing money symbols and then collecting them at the end. Instead, we were treated to a rather unique round of Hercules battling monsters instead. At times, the titanic struggle between two massive entities on either side of the game grid felt like Gods vs Gigablox or Monsters vs Gigablox from Hot Rise Games, another Yggdrasil Gaming associate. What's less titanic when compared to the bigger hitters in the hold 'n win game, though respectable enough, is an advertised max multiplier of 6,108 times the bet.While there have been ups and downs amongst the 10K series, as a whole, it has come across as a bit samey. Not always; there have been exceptions. Thor 10K Ways is one which sticks in the memory banks, as does Bucks and Doe 10K Ways with its unique hunting-centric bonus round. Hercules 10K Ways, too, is one that might not shake up the industry but does enough to raise its buffed, broad shoulders above the 10K Ways pack.

Title: Beat The Beast: Griffin's Gold

Fans who have been following the series might feel the heartstring tugs now it’s all wrapped up. The good news is Thunderkick have embarked upon a another series, the first of which is Crystal Quest: Deep Jungle, offering the same significant volatility and wins of Beat the Beast in a slightly more adventurous format.

Title: Euphoria

Title: Mysterious Egypt
review: Mysterious Egypt: Slot OverviewContributing another ‘Book of’ slot to the pile usually means one of two things. Title: Dragon Tiger

Title: The Mafiosi

Wannabe-wiseguys should be able to get a kick out of it, but The Mafiosi didn't stand out enough to really push it past mid-levels in the hierarchy.

Title: Massive Gold

Title: Golden Gods
review: Golden Gods: Slot OverviewGolden Gods is an online slot from Max Win Gaming powered by the more experienced software provider Relax Gaming. Title: Sabertooth
review: Sabertooth (WMS): OverviewOriginally, it was believed that sabertooth tigers died out long before humans came onto the scene. And at the game’s speed, we’ll probably be halfway into the next ice age before it drops.So why play here when there are better options elsewhere? Aside from the theoretical jackpot, prehistory buffs or nature lovers might be tempted to have a crack, other than that not much. Maybe players who want to pretend they are playing the land-based version at home? Yes, we are clutching at straws now. Title: Mochimon
review: Mochimon slot - base gameMochimon: Slot OverviewOnline slot Mochimon was the first game to hit the review desk in the year 2023, and it is none other than a clone from software provider Pragmatic Play. Let's answer that question up front and reveal the original was the gummy bear-filled candy slot Sugar Rush, a game that dropped about half a year before this one. Will Mochimon be better, will it be worse, or just more or less the same?Visually, the answer to that question will be whether you prefer cartoons or sweets. The first memories weren't just of Sugar Rush but of a prior game called Wild Beach Party. Like Mochimon, Wild Beach Party was, in turn, basically a reskin of Fruit Party 2, with an anime twist. This time, however, instead of hanging around in a skimpy bikini, she slipped into what appears to be a French Maid outfit. Classy or trashy? This all takes place with the help of a highly volatile math model, possessing a top return to player value of 96.5% - whether buying free spins or wagering 20 p/c to $/€100 per paid spin.It's hard to know what to call the symbols, being sprite-like characters of various descriptions. As mentioned, the tumble feature triggers after a win, plus there is no wild symbol to be found in Mochimon.Mochimon: Slot FeaturesMochimon slot - free spinsWorking hand in hand with the tumble mechanic is the Multiplier Spots feature. After the second time, a symbol explodes on the same spot, and a multiplier is added to the specific position. The multiplier starts at x2 and doubles every time symbols explode on that position, up to a maximum of x128. The multiplier applies to all winning combinations which land on top of it. If more than one multiplier is used in a win, the values are added together. In the base game, the multipliers persist until no more tumbles occur, then they are cleared for the next new spin.Free SpinsThe treasure chest is Mochimon's scatter, and landing 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7 of them awards 10, 12, 15, 20, or 30 free spins, respectively. What changes in free spins is that marked spots and multipliers remain on the grid until free spins come to an end. Players win an additional 10, 12, 15, 20, or 30 free spins when 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7 scatter symbols land during the feature, respectively. Also, where available, players can buy instant access to the bonus round for 100 times the stake. Buying free spins randomly lands 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7, triggering scatter symbols.Mochimon slot - free spinsMochimon: Slot VerdictIf you were wondering if the word Mochimon means something, 'Mochimon' is apparently a baby-level Digimon (Digital Monster) which we unearthed after doing some online digging. Digimon is a Japanese franchise which started in the late nineties and revolved around virtual pets before branching into a variety of entertainment forms, such as video games, TV, and movies. Not sure if Mochimon the slot has consciously tried to link itself to the popular franchise or not, but a tenuous association exists via the game's title. Will Bandai, Akiyoshi Hongo, or Toei Animation react? Let's wait and see.Even if any of Digimon's owners did step in to silence Mochimon, interested players do have a fall-back option in the form of Sugar Rush. Putting the sights and sounds aside, the gameplay and stats are identical. Not a terrible thing, really, since Sugar Rush and, by extension, Mochimon are capable of cobbling together some pretty compelling sequences of events. Marked multiplier spaces in the base game provide opportunities for some nifty action, which can be elevated to the next level by their persistent quality in free spins. So much so that hitting Sugar Rush's win cap of 5,000x the bet has been captured on film, meaning it's likely to be achievable in Mochimon, too, when the critters and multipliers are playing ball.It's not hard to see why Pragmatic Play made the executive decision to clone Sugar Rush. On the one hand, it sometimes feels like the studio is on a mission to recycle every game in its back catalogue, like some sort of hardcore slot eco-warrior. On the other hand, Sugar Rush came with some excellently replayable gaming, all of which is back, kicking as hard as ever, though the thrill of the new is naturally less in this anime makeover.

One spin is all it takes to kick start a chain of events that can get quite lengthy at times, building up decent Twisted Robot Credits and multipliers as it goes. For the most part, Twisted Turbine balances out quite well and doesn’t get too weighed down by all of the disparate elements. If you like spins to turn into long drawn out sequences of events, Twisted Turbine might be worth a look.

Title: Legend of Cleopatra Megaways

Title: Savanna Stampede

Play it on all devices, including mobile and tablets, from as little as 10 cents up to 250€ per spin.Screenshot of the main gameSavanna Stampede is no visual wonder but gets the job done. With a wallpaper-like backdrop of the African savanna at sunset, you will see the usual collection of royal values as well as a selection of wild animals. The max win from a single spin will come from a full screen of buffalos, which is worth 500 times your stake. Title: Dragon Tribe

The prehistoric background is filled with steaming volcanoes and flames that threaten to blow at any moment. It’s an apt metaphor for the game itself really. Volatility is set on medium-high, though it can feel higher than that depending on how a session is going. Of course, all sessions are different, so be prepared for anything to happen.Also be prepared for low symbol values. The way the game is structured means that decent wins are possible, but symbols need help from the features to give them any substance. There are 12 base game pay symbols altogether. When the xNudge Wild reaches the bottom row, it expands to cover the whole reel for one final flourish before leaving the game. Land 3 of these to trigger 10 Dragon Spins, with every additional bonus symbol worth an extra 3 spins. The feature begins by presenting the player with two options:Dragon Spins - more frequent wins, lower volatility, xNudge, and up to 11,000x potential.Dragon Spins Extreme - less frequent wins, higher volatility, xNudge and xWays, and up to 27,000x potential.No points for guessing which one we stuck to. And this is when the game went mental. During the feature, every third winning cascade turns one of the dragon symbols wild and adds 2 extra spins to the remaining total. During testing, Dragon Spins were triggered early on - before we had fully absorbed the rules, so it wasn’t 100% clear what was going on at first. Every dragon quickly turned wild which caused combos to line up at an insane rate. The overall result wasn’t all time, but it made a positive impression to say the least.Free spins (high volatile version)Dragon Tribe (Nolimit City): VerdictHit Dragon Tribe on a good day and it really is a fun game. Like a lot of slots at the moment, it’s all about piling one feature on top of another to get as many working in tandem. Do this, and the result is good old fashion slots action where tension builds along with the satisfying wins. Dragon Tribe is volatile though so don’t expect that to happen all the time. When it does it is a real hoot, and the 27,000 times the stake potential, of course, makes it all the more appealing for any hardcore gamer. After getting a taste of what it can do during testing, there is no doubt it is capable of some juicy payouts.Dragon Tribe was a pleasant surprise and a step up from Nolimit City. They have certainly raised the bar and what direction they go next is intriguing. Now the problem for gamers looking for a volatile dragon-themed slot with high potential is which one to choose - Dragon Tribe or Dragonfall? What do you think? Comment below.

Title: 10,001 Nights
review: 10,001 Nights: Slot OverviewMany readers are likely familiar with One Thousand and One Nights, the collection of old Middle Eastern stories which have been retold in various forms up to the present day. This being a slot and not a piece of literature; the 10,001 refers to winning potential, rather than adding more chapters to a book.Red Tiger has produced an attractive slot which makes full use of the theme. At first, the images of exotic women and sultans brought back memories of the recently reviewed Book of Kingdoms. After the frisson of dread past, 10,001 Nights turned out to be quite the opposite. Red Tiger has turned up the visual experience by setting the 5-reel, 20-payline action area in a palace-like environment, all expensive carpets, drapes, and starry night skies. Less titillating is a slightly lower than average RTP rating of 95.73%, while volatility hovers around the high end of the spectrum.The paytable is full of items every self-respecting Sultan should own. One the low side are gold-rimmed card suits – clubs, diamonds, hearts and spades. Next are the highs, consisting of genie shoes with curled toes, a spice jar, a camel, a tiger, and the Sultan himself. All need at least three to payout, except for the Sultan. He needs only two. As to payouts, 5 premiums on a line are worth from 3x to 40x the bet. The sultry deva in the Covid mask is the wild, which is worth more at 55x the bet. When she’s not paying out, she’s substituting for all paying symbols.10,001 Nights: Slot FeaturesInitially, 10,001 Nights offers four modifiers triggered by a collection system, plus a batch of free spins. As time progresses, the dynamic shifts, as you’ll see.The lamp symbol is the key to the four minor features, appearing at random on any spin. Each lamp is collected in one of four jars located on top of the reels. When a jar is full, it triggers one of four features in consecutive order:Stage 1 requires 6 lamps to be collected, unlocking the Imperial Spin feature. All low paying symbols are removed from the reels so only high pays will land during the spin.Stage 2 requires 7 more lamps, unlocking the Random Wilds feature. A random number of wild symbols are sprinkling around the reels.Stage 3 is achieved when 8 more lamps are collected, unlocking the Multi-Pick feature. Three cards are presented for the player to choose one. This reveals a multiplier which is applied to any win on the next spin. The highest observed during testing was x9.Stage 4 is achieved when 9 more lamps are collected, unlocking the Mega Wilds feature. One or more 1x4, full reel wilds are added to the screen.When a feature is unlocked it becomes active on the next spin. Once all four features have been unlocked, the lamp collection mechanic ends, and features instead trigger randomly from then on at that stake level. Changing bet levels starts the process from the beginning, and progress is saved if you go back. It is possible to have more than one feature active on a single spin if more than one is unlocked.10,001 Nights is a rather high paying slot, and solid wins are possible from free spins although strangely, they are no different from the base game. To trigger them, 3, 4, or 5 Destiny Spins Symbols in view award 8, 10, or 12 free spins respectively. During the feature, 3, 4, or 5 scatters add 6, 7, or 8 extra spins.10,001 Nights: Slot VerdictIs it the heat, the dust, the spicy food? Whatever it is, Red Tiger has found some inspiration in the Middle East and designed a pretty solid slot. It looks nice, sounds nice, the features aren’t half bad, plus potential sits on the high side. It’s got a classic Red Tiger look which some players might be wary of, but give it a chance as 10,001 Nights might surprise.One element of intrigue is that once the four modifiers have been unlocked by lamps they can’t be collected at the same bet level again. You can repeat the process by changing the stake if you really want to. Still, it's somewhat odd the lamp collection system doesn’t just reset. It does dampen the enthusiasm once you’ve seen all four in action. Unless you’re fine with mixing the bets up a bit, 10,001 Nights mellows to an extent once that point is reached. In its favour, features do trigger randomly from then on, and there are free spins, though the game does lose a little bit of its spark.The gameplay is fun, however, and the production values are high. The four modifiers can positively affect the balance but are nothing compared to the game’s max potential of 10,347.6 times the bet. A staggering figure from Red Tiger compared to the typical shelf filler slots they sling. Not exactly 10,001x the bet which would’ve been poetical, yet it’s unlikely anyone will be complaining about the extra amount. All up, 10,001 Nights is a decent game from Red Tiger. It’s got all the right elements for an enjoyable time in the Middle Eastern desert.

Title: Hall of the Mountain King

This Multiplier Meter feature is activated when one or more wilds appear on the reels - 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 wilds in view will award you a x1, x2, x3, x4 or x5 multiplier respectively. The bonus activates when you land 3 hammer scatters on the middle reels. Here's what awaits as you start your journey:Level 1It's all about collecting as many high-value symbols as possible here through the Symbol Upgrade feature. Either by random, or when you land a winning combination, the troll will smash one of the blocks in the upgrade meter positioned to the right of the reel set. The indicated low-value symbol is then removed from the reels and replaced with stacks of the corresponding premium symbol. Furthermore, the troll can also destroy the bottom block of the multiplier meter which upgrades all the multiplier values - the multipliers can go up to a maximum of x15. Progression to the next stage takes place once the top block has been destroyed.Level 2Entering the second stage, it now becomes a matter of collecting Whirling Wilds. When the troll destroys a Whirling Wild block, the wilds locked inside the block are collected and held in limbo above the reels for later use - it's possible to collect up to 6 wilds in total. The multiplier meter is still in use here as well and continues to upgrade as long as the troll keeps breaking the multiplier blocks. As in level 1, you move on to the next stage when the top block has been destroyed.Level 3The final stage and the very climax in the story of the Mountain King. Armed with your upgraded symbols and whirling wilds, you will see your collected features come together in great effect. Here you'll get 3 spins with the Whirling Wild Drop feature to help you create winning combinations - on each of the 3 spins, a random number of Whirling Wilds are dropped onto the reels.Hall of the Mountain King (Quickspin): VerdictThere are many elements, twists and layers that make this title worth enjoying, not to mention the carefully balanced equilibrium between the entertaining gameplay, volatility and massive potential. Admittedly, Mountain King is confusing at first and even after having played several bonuses, we weren't entirely sure of what was going on. Because of this, some players might feel it's a bit over the top, especially old school veterans who live by the motto less is more. However, with 7326 times your stake up for grabs, there is still a good chance that the game will appeal to all types of players.Hall of the Mountain King is an ambitious title, possibly one of the biggest to the date by Quickspin. Not only is it a piece of art where we see a memorable narrative being carried by a strong soundtrack and outstanding visuals, it also offers an out of the ordinary gaming experience where each bonus is unique and different from the others. The one big question mark is whether Mountain King can maintain the energy after launch, but so far the outlook seems promising.

Title: 9 Pots of Gold Megaways

Title: Hazakura Ways
review: Hazakura Ways: Slot OverviewIt's always interesting to learn the various ways different cultures name things that might not even make ripples on the consciousness of others. Much focus is given in Japanese culture to the cherry blossom phenomenon, and if you've played games like Sakura Fortune or Sakura Fortune 2, you'll probably be well aware. Following in this tradition is Hazakura Ways from provider Relax Gaming. In this example, the word 'hazakura' refers to the time when cherry blossoms have dropped their flowers and new leaves are starting to spring up. Into this harmonious part of the growth cycle, players are dropped, amidst feature offshoots such as expanding symbols, free spins, and a couple of extra betting options.The flowers haven't really begun to drop in Hazakura Ways as the game grid is framed by a structure covered in them. Like Plunderland, which was made available to us around the same time, Hazakura Ways displays a less exciting side of Relax Gaming from an aesthetic point of view, it has to be said. At first, it's easy to get caught up in the game's zen-like nature, like a stroll through a Japanese landscaped garden, admiring the way everything has been laid out just so. However, it doesn't take too many spins to realise that Hazakura Ways is as business-minded as anything else Relax has done. It's just got more flowers than usual covering the fact.Hazakura Ways might be a rather weak game on the outside, but underneath, it's as wild as it gets from Relax Gaming. Massive potential is paired with a highly volatile math model that swung wildly during our test sessions. From bonus buys which went nowhere, ending up crushed underfoot like a discarded cherry blossom, to other more satisfying outcomes, gear up for an unpredictable ride. RTP is dependable, starting with a standard value of 96.37%, rising to 97% when buying free spins. Stake range isn't huge, which is expected being such a potent slot, where options vary from 20 p/c to $/€20.Played on a 6-reel, 4-row game grid, wins happen when matching symbols line up left to right from reel one, regardless of position. This method provides 4,096 ways to win and is critical when combined with the expanded symbol feature. Inspecting the paytable, we find low pay versions of diamonds, clubs, spades, hearts, and stars worth 1-2x the bet for six, then swords, dagger pendants, a sensei looking guy, and a female heroine, furthering the Sakura Fortune-ish feel. Landing six matching premium symbols results in a payout worth 3 to 50 times your stake. A blooming, almost magical looking cherry blossom is the wild symbol, substituting all other symbols except the scatter.Hazakura Ways: Slot FeaturesTo sum up the features, there's a The Falcon Huntress thing going on, but it's not a copy by any means. Free spins and a random base game feature are where symbol expansions come into play, and these are joined by two betting options – where available.Random FeatureAt the start of any main game spin, one pay symbol may randomly be selected to be a special symbol. Any special symbols landing on that spin expand downwards, filling the remaining positions and paying out no matter what reel they are on.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, 5, or 6 lantern scatters awards 10, 15, 20, or 25 free spins. Before free spins start, one pay symbol is randomly chosen to be the special symbol for the bonus game's full duration. Like the previous feature, when the chosen symbol hits, it expands downwards to cover all positions and pays from any reel. Landing 3 or more scatters in the feature awards additional free spins.Mega BetActivating the Mega Bet increases the regular stake by 50%. In return, it also increases the chance of triggering free spins and the random feature. It also means that wild symbols expand to cover their reel as well whenever the chosen symbol expands.Buy BonusLastly, if you're done being zen in the base game, dishing out 80x the stake gains you instant access to free spins. This can be done with the Mega Bet on or off, so the cheaper option is regular free spins. The more expensive option is with expanding wild symbols.Hazakura Ways: Slot VerdictHazakura Ways is another slot from Relax Gaming packing the sort of features that can ignite under the right conditions. The tricky part was deciding whether to go for the Mega Bet, buy the bonus round or chance it in normal mode. Having both wilds and regular symbols expanding might feel like a no-brainer, but wild symbols were a relatively rare occurrence during testing, so they weren't as useful as originally anticipated. Naturally, there were times when wilds came in handy, especially since expanding symbols pay from any reel position. Then there are other times when the Mega Bet is deactivated and a wild hits amongst a bunch of chosen symbols, leaving you counting all the coins you missed out on. So, it goes.Free spins combine the anywhere paying style of Book of Ra with an added sudoku-like element of complexity. Obviously, there are a ton more ways to win here than in a regular 'book' slot, and it's easy to get caught up in calculating the what-ifs. However, Hazakura Ways was as tough a nut to crack as any high volatile, high reward Relax Gaming slot. Wilds could be rare, chosen symbols often landed in lower positions, thereby reducing their expanding capabilities, or they simply chose not to land much at all. Yet, unicorn spins are here to be had, and expanding symbols can really do a number with all those extra ways. So much so, Relax Gaming has capped Hazakura Ways' max win at 50,000x the bet. The bonus round that cracks the cap is sure to be an expansion bonanza.Though visually underwhelming, once again the Relax Gaming team has crafted a compelling, well-built slot. Hazakura Ways has more nods to other games than usual from Relax, but the end result is another unique machine for exasperating and/or rewarding players.

Title: Electric Wilds
review: Electric Wilds: OverviewIndependent developer Northernlights is the team behind the electrifying slot Electric Wilds. Known to craft games for different studios such as Yggdrasil Gaming and SG Digital, Electric Wilds is the result of a collaboration with Relax Gaming that is to be powered by their Silver Bullet platform.The word electrifying is usually a positive thing, but on its own, it doesn't mean much since so much depends on the context. On the one hand, the word is used to describe something adrenaline-filled that gets the blood surging, on the other hand, it can be quite a shocking experience. So which situation applies to Electric Wilds?Power lines make up the background to Electric Wilds while a 3 by 3 reel set covers most of the screen along with a green-lit display called The Matrix. No, not the life-like simulator helping power robot tech. The Matrix is more of a wild making machine; we'll get to it.Playable from 10 p/c to €/$ 30 per spin across all devices, Northernlights describes the mechanic as '9 individual reels with multiple in-game cameras'. Not quite sure what that last part means, but basically, players get 3 columns, 3 rows, and 5 paylines on which to land winners. Only three of a kinds are possible of course, starting with low pay J-A royals which look like Andy Warhol can art. The Futuristically styled high pays, meanwhile, consist of three coloured power capsules and a glowing-eyed robot head. The cyborg is worth the most from the bunch at 20 times the stake.So far, pretty standard stuff, but the numbers start to offer more clues as to whether the game is worth picking up or not. First is a stat everyone can get behind, RTP, which clocks in at 96.17%. The low volatility, rated 2 out of 5, is sure to be a bit more divisive, but it's the hit rate that leads to some odd gaming sessions.Strangely, the hit frequency during the base game is just 1 in 17, which is probably a lot lower than most players are accustomed to. Then again, the low number does indicate that the game may have more in common with the classic fruit slot than other genres. In any case, almost as rare is the Lightning Overprints feature, hitting 1 in 20 spins on average - which doesn't quite succeed in making up for the hit rate shortfall. Let's take a look at exactly what the features entail.Electric Wilds: FeaturesElectric Wilds free spinsIn keeping with the 'old UK pub mechanic' there are just two features to cover. The Lightning Overprints feature is where the Matrix comes into play. One any spin, little lightning bolt symbols may appear in the bottom right-hand side of the regular symbols. When an overprint appears like this, the corresponding position on the Matrix display is lit up.Every line of 3 bolts, vertically, horizontally, or diagonally, on the Matrix causes one symbol type on the grid to turn wild. Multiple lines mean multiple symbols turn wild. Lights on the Matrix generally clear on the next spin, but there is a chance some lights stay lit for the next spin. There is also a chance super lightning symbols appear on a spin. These look identical to the normal one, but they light up a random number of spots on the Matrix rather than just one.Should players manage to fill the grid with the same symbol, via wilds or just one symbol type, they trigger the Repeater bonus. The screen shifts to one covered in flashing lightning and 5 tubes - 1 broken, 4 operational. Hitting the start button causes electricity to move along the tubes before stopping at one.If it lands on a broken tube, the feature is over. If it lands on a non-broken one, players win the amount that triggered the feature again, plus the tube becomes broken. This process repeats until a broken tube is hit, or all 4 non-broken ones are struck awarding 4x the original win. The Repeater bonus has a theoretical frequency of 1 in 400.Finally, a free spins game has been included as well. Strangely, there was no mention of it anywhere, neither in the game sheet or the rules section of the paytable. Since it turned out to be more or less identical to the base game, we never bothered to investigate it any further.Electric Wilds: VerdictUnless you are absolutely mad for electricity, Electric Wilds is a tough one to warm to. Northernlights is a studio that has its share of hits and misses; sadly, Electric Wilds is one of the latter. Its main problem is that it isn't much fun to play. Low hit rate combined with a low volatility makes for some painful gaming. Most of the time, there simply isn't a lot going on and it quickly kills the spirit.The Matrix teases from time to time, but again, usually, fudge all happens. Occasionally, you'll get a few lines and wild substitutes, but not enough to save the day - it just shouldn't feel like such a triumph to get any old organic win.The game's tagline is 'Shockingly good wins.' Except not so much when you do the maths. For one, a full grid of the cyborg symbol is worth 100x, so you'll need to enter the Repeater bonus with that and win it 4 consecutive times to hit the game's 500 times the stake max potential.If you travel by train, and enjoy staring at power lines running alongside the track (and no one is judging), then Electric Wilds could very well be the game for you. Otherwise, it's hard to think of much else to commend it. Northernlights has come up with a twist on the 3x3 format, and kudos for trying something new. To be fair, it is curious initially. The problem is once you've seen the Matrix feature dish up a few wilds once or twice, there is a steep drop off in interest.

Title: The Great Albini 2
review: The Great Albini 2: Slot OverviewJoin Microgaming partner Foxium as they return to the stage to perform a trick or two in their sequel slot, The Great Albini 2. This time around, Foxium has made a number of big changes to the looks, features, and stats. Some of the upgrades have merit; others are as insubstantial as a cheap illusion. Buy your ticket to the show, and let's have a look at Albini's return.First up, the view. Presumably, for players who liked the original, the way Foxium made it seem as though you were sitting in the audience was a large part of the thrill. The reels were set up on an intimate stage, all thickly draped, as Albini bobbed away to one side, while his assistant Lily popped up at times. That has all largely gone in The Great Albini 2, owing to the way it is presented. It seems Foxium went for the mobile-friendly approach studio PG Soft is famous for, so when playing on a desktop, players get a blurry stage sitting behind an active game area crammed into a squished central window. The results are less immersive than part one, with less of a live performance feel to it than before, despite an excellently magical soundtrack.The Great Albini 2 comes in several mathematical forms, with RTPs ranging from 96.1% down to 92.1%. In all cases, players get a 5x4, 40-payline video slot spitting out a win at a rate of 27.19%. A medium volatile slot, the game is available on any device, where bets of 20 p/c to $/€12 may be set. The chance of hitting Albini Multipliers and Lily Extra spins in the bonus game is also increased.Along the 40 fixed paylines, starting from reel number one, players win when three or more matching pay symbols land. A payout of 0.67 to 1.33x the bet is paid for a line of five 10-A low pays, or 2 to 6.67x for five high pay Lucky Cups, Knives, Lilies, or Alibins. Wilds assist with this by landing on any reel to substitute all of the regular pay symbols. Wilds also payout up to 16.67x the bet when landing a line of five of them.The Great Albini 2: Slot FeaturesFoxium has completely overhauled the features, stripping out what the original had and replacing them with a cash symbol collection mechanic and a hold & win style bonus game.Collect FeatureKeep an eye out for Money Gems appearing on reels 1, 2, 3 or 4 in three different colours, representing three different value sets. Blue gems award 1-9x the bet, the purple gems award 10-20x, and red gems are worth 25-50x the stake in the base game. When a collect symbol lands on the last reel, the total value of all Money Gem symbols in view on the reels is awarded. Collect symbols may appear with an x2-x5 multiplier. This multiplier is applied to the total value of collected Money Gems.Bonus FeatureScatter symbols are present on reels 2, 3, or 4, and landing 3 of them at once triggers the bonus feature. Now, 3 spins are awarded to start with, in a bonus round where only Money Gems, Albini Multiplier symbols, or Lily Extra Spins symbols may land. When they do land, the number of spins left is set back to the starting value. When spins run out, the accumulated value of the Money Gems is multiplied by the win multiplier and awarded.The win multiplier increases whenever Albini Multiplier symbols land. These symbols have a value of 1-5x, which is added to the multiplier. When Lily symbols hit, they increase the starting value of the current spin count by +1.The Great Albini 2: Slot VerdictThe initial squeezed game area set a disappointing tone from the get-go that Albini 2 struggled to recover from. Instead of buying seats and being treated to a night out at the theatre, playing Albini 2 was closer to staring through a peephole to watch it for free. As mentioned, the soundtrack is quite magical, but the rest doesn't have the same stage presence as the previous game. To be fair, this might actually be a benefit for some players as much as it disappoints others, making The Great Albini 2 more of a straight-out gambling device, without all the theatrical flourishes. Whether this was done on purpose to streamline the process or because there simply wasn't room using the mobile-focused approach, who can say.The gameplay felt quite balanced in a way, where the base and bonus game are split between cash symbol collections and streak respins. The latter proved to be highly elusive during the review, as bonus round triggers were rare. It didn't help that the first time the bonus game activated, we ended up with a grand total of zero dollars and zero cents. Hey, these things can happen in any game. However, after squinting to see what was going on for so long, the zero win was like getting a piece of grit flicked in our eye for the trouble, almost prompting a walkout before the show had finished.The Great Albini 2's real headliner is its 20,000x the bet top prize, awarded when filling the grid with symbols in the bonus game. A big total, to be sure, yet it feels like there is a massive drop off for second prize or less, so a realistic win target would be advantageous to know.Peering at The Great Albini 2 for a while produced a few fun moments, and there was a touch of magic in the air, yet the tricks included are far from being on the cutting edge and playing on anything other than a mobile seems a tad pointless. In the end, The Great Albini 2 felt like a magician borrowing your pocket watch for a trick, placing it in a black velvet bag, then proceeding to bash it with a hammer. However, something didn't go according to plan, so instead of getting back a fully functioning watch, he hands you a bag full of broken bits.

Title: Twilight Princess
review: Twilight Princess: Slot OverviewSorry Twihards, but Twilight Princess from developer Pragmatic Play is not a playful reference to Bella Swan, but is instead a distant relative of Starlight Princess, a slot sharing similar traits and a number of different ones, which in turn is heavily inspired by Play'n GO's smash hit classic Moon Princess (there currently also seems to be a war going on between the two, both releasing 100 vs 1000 versions of these slots).
