There's also a buy free spins feature for players keen on quicker access to the bonus round.Wild With MultipliersThe wild symbol is an elaborate pink orb with a 'W' imprinted on it. The first thing wilds can do is substitute for any symbol except the scatter. When wilds hit, they land with a multiplier of x2, x3, x5, or x10, which applies to any win the wild is part of. When more than 1 wild is part of the same win, the multiplier values are added to each other. One wild can be part of more than one winning block at the same time, and a full screen of wilds pays 50 times the bet.Free SpinsThe golden orb object is Twilight Princess' scatter, and it lands on all reels. Hitting 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols awards a payout of 2x, 15x, or 100x the bet, respectively, as well as 10 free spins. During free spins, any wild symbol that appears on the screen remains on the reels until the free spins round ends. Scatters may land in free spins as well, overlaid on top of any symbol. Getting 2, 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols awards an extra 5, 10, 20, or 30 free spins.Buy Free SpinsFree spins can be instantly triggered from the base game by buying them for 100 times the bet. When buying free spins, 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols are guaranteed to land on the triggering spin.Twilight Princess slot - free spinsTwilight Princess: Slot VerdictEven though it might be argued Twilight Princess has more originality going on, mechanically speaking, than Starlight Princess, it doesn't feel like this is a game that had a whole lot of love lavished on it. The background is pretty plain, bordering on dull, and apart from the floating princess and some of the symbols, Twilight Princess didn't feel like a game which took the manga, anime concept and really went to town with it. Maybe if/when Pragmatic Play drops in a more appropriate soundtrack, this might help beef up the experience. As mentioned, there is a princess and an assortment of related symbols, but the theme use felt a little half-hearted when compared to some of the other slots in this category.The same might be said about Twilight Princess' features, which revolve around a wild multiplier that becomes sticky in free spins. Pretty basic, a little unimaginative, but darn it, the features have the technical capability to thrill. In the base game, wild multipliers land from time to time to get the pulse racing a bit harder, yet the base game didn't hold a candle to free spins where wilds are sticky when they appear on the reels, blasted by the Twilight Princess' magic staff. It didn't prove to be too difficult to get a number of sticky wilds on the board either, potentially leading to decent results. A tumble feature might have pushed things even further, but even without one, Twilight Princess can produce wins up to a cap of 7,500x the bet.Fans of sticky multiplier wild features will likely find a level of satisfaction from Twilight Princess, as will fans of anime/manga, even though it's not a game which really squeezes as much juice from the subject matter as possible. It's also not a game that really has its foot on the innovation gas. However, Twilight Princess does enough to scrape by, dressing up a satisfying set of features in a Sailor Moon-type outer coating.

Title: Robin of Sherwood
review: Robin of Sherwood Slot: IntroductionWe had no idea there was a Robin of Sherwood slot coming, let alone one that was ready for launch! Title: Timber Stacks
review: Timber Stacks: Slot OverviewTimber is, of course, processed bits of wood used to build houses or fences and whatnot, but it's also apparently a word lumberjacks shout to warn other people of a tree about to topple over. It's the latter definition that seems to fit Timber Stacks, an online slot from Pragmatic Play, best. You won't see many planks of wood in this game, though you are likely to see stacks of symbols fall in a manner vaguely resembling the felling of a tree. This effect plays into an Increasing Grid Size feature, tumbles – of which there can be a lot, free spins, and various betting options.The great outdoors is the setting for Timber Stacks. In a meadow bursting with daisies and long wavy grass where butterflies flit and bunnies bound about the place. It's a place where you lie down, maybe propped up against a log, then take in the towering trees and snow-capped mountains in the distance. At a guess, Timber Stacks reproduces a North American image, though maybe not, and players are free to pick anywhere rugged mountain terrain teems with the sorts of wild animals that appear on the game grid. Timber Stacks might not deliver the pinnacle of outdoor gambling from an audiovisual standpoint, but it does provide a very pleasing location to do a spot of gambling.Timber Stacks slot - base gameKicking off the gambling starts by selecting a stake of 20 c to $/€240 per spin, and players have the choice of activating the ante bet, which ups the stake by 25% whilst doubling the chance of winning the free spins feature. Gamble with the ante bet on or off, or even buy free spins, and the default RTP remains steady at 96.05%. With a highly volatile math model, Pragmatic Play has rated 5 out of 5; Timber Stacks is played on a growable gaming grid where the default size is 5 reels and 5 rows.Timber Stacks uses a ways system to evaluate wins, shooting off a payout when matching symbols land left to right on adjacent reels from the left-hand side. On the default grid, this means 3,125 ways to win are available. The tumble mechanic removes all winning symbols after they have paid and lets other symbols tumble downwards to fill the empty positions, creating a new chance to win. Tumbling continues until no more winning combinations appear on the screen, then awards the total of all wins. A total of ten pay symbols are in play here. These are 10-A card ranks as Timber Stacks' lows, then a fish, cougar, owl, bear, and wolf as the highs. Hitting a 5 OAK winning way pays 0.8 to 1 times the bet for the lows and 1.5 to 10 times the bet for the picture symbols. Landing on reels 2, 3, and 4, the wild helps connect wins by substituting for everything except the scatter.Timber Stacks: Slot FeaturesTimber Stacks slot - free spinsOut here in nature, Timber Stacks' features are its increasing Grid Size, free spins, and bonus buy.Increasing Grid SizeAfter each spin or tumble, if there are no more winning combinations on the screen, there is a chance that this feature triggers. When it does, an empty row of symbols is added to the bottom of the grid, and a random reel is chosen to fall. If reel 1 or 2 are selected to fall, all symbols from them fall to the right, adding their symbols from bottom to top in empty positions on the added bottom row. If reel 3 is selected, symbols from it fall either left or right, randomly, added symbols from bottom to top in empty positions on the bottom row. If reels 4 or 5 are chosen, symbols fall to the left, acting in a similar manner. After the fall, new symbols drop in from above to fill any empty positions. At its maximum size, the grid can be expanded to 10x5 where 100,000 ways to win are in play, and when tumbles end, the grid returns to the original 5x5 size.Free SpinsThe free spins round is triggered by landing 4 or 5 scatter symbols, awarding 8 or 10 free spins, respectively. During the free spins round, the Increasing Grid Size feature is available and behaves as it does in the base game.Buy Free SpinsFree spins may be bought for 120 times the bet. When buying free spins, 4 or 5 scatters will randomly land to trigger the feature.Timber Stacks slot - free spinsTimber Stacks: Slot VerdictAs they are well adept at doing, the Pragmatic Play team has once again created a good-looking, nicely functioning online slot. One that doesn't shoot for superstar status, nor comes across in any way sub-par. The numbers are strong, the finish has been done to a satisfying standard, and the end result is tough to pick major holes in. If anybody has a talent for knocking out decent slots on a consistent basis, it's Pragmatic Play. No, Timber Stacks didn't feel destined to win awards any time soon, but neither is it likely to be ridiculed for being a boo game. All in all, dependable stuff.What holds Timber Stacks back from being a better game are one or two things. One is that while the features it does have are totally fine at both triggering thrills and potentially big wins, something felt missing. If the Increasing Grid Size mechanic had been backed up with another supplementary feature, for instance, the extra variety would have been appreciated. Especially because when free spins trigger, nothing new is added there, nothing new occurs. On an anecdotal level, whilst the pay table did not specify this, it did seem more likely to trigger the Increasing Grid Size feature in free spins compared to the base game, which is a common move in slots. But since this isn't officially stated anywhere, maybe don't take it as a given. If a perceived lack of variety has you questioning the game's performance, there's no need to worry there since Timber Stacks has 10,000x the bet as a win cap.It also packs in a lot of consecutive tumbling action. So, if you're a fan of symbols tumbling together to form lengthy chains of wins, then it might be worth giving Timber Stacks a go. On the whole, it's a pretty sweet game, and if slung against a wall, Timber Stacks would, for the most part, stick. It wouldn't have been terrible if Timber Stacks came with one or two little extras to spice things up, but what it has is able to construct moments of joy.

Title: 4 Deals With The Devil
review: 4 Deals With The Devil: Slot OverviewSome say that instead of showing up with horns and a goatee, the devil appears in an alluring form, so as all the better to tempt people. It seems software provider 4ThePlayer has taken this line of thought when developing the online slot 4 Deals With the Devil. That or they've been watching Bedazzled with Liz Hurley as the devil, and Brandon Fraser who is granted seven wishes in an attempt to get the girl of his dreams. Players don't get seven wishes in this game, but they do get deals in the form of four free spins bonus rounds with wilds which can expand and roam.4 Deals With the Devil is set in what appears to be a throne room of sorts, sans infernos, brimstone, and torment. This domain is rather sedate, a tad tasteful even, decorated with braziers, a stained-glass window, creepers on pillars, that sort of thing. Stepping into 4 Deals With the Devil is more like walking into a crystal shop than a terrifying Dantean view of the underworld we are usually presented with.4 Deals With The Devil slot - base gameFirst things first, and as well as picking a stake of 10 p/c to $/€10, players select which of the four bonus rounds they would like to play for. Full details of each one are listed below, and you can change your mind at any time in the base game by hitting the 'Change Bonus' button on the upper right side. Any device is suitable for doing a bit of dealing on, while the theoretical return to player figure comes in at 96.5%.4 Deals With the Devil is hosted on a 6-reel, 4-row game panel, with 4,096 ways to win. There are no paylines; instead, wins are formed when matching symbols land on consecutive reels starting from the leftmost side of the grid. Pay symbols are a mixed bag of classic slot icons and more game-specific objects. They start with 10-A card ranks, adorned with objects like roses or bells, before getting to cherries, dice, a ring, a cat, a gargoyle, and a Lucky 7s. Landing a six of a kind winning way awards 1.5-2.5x the bet for the card symbols, rising to 3-7x the stake for the higher value lot.4 Deals With The Devil: Slot Features4 Deals With The Devil slot - free spins4ThePlayer often lets players have a certain say in what sort of gaming experience they will potentially have. In 4 Deals With the Devil, users choose one of four free spins bonus rounds they would prefer to trigger. As well as free spins, the other feature to look out for is the Devil Lady Wild Respin.Devil Lady Wild RespinWild symbols substitute for any pay symbols and can land 1, 2, or 3 positions high. Hitting at least one wild in the base game triggers a Devil Lady Wild Respin. During the respin, any wild in view is locked to reels and expands by 1 position. If a new wild symbol lands, another respin is awarded. Should a wild reach 4 positions high, it disappears.Free SpinsAt the start of the game, players choose which free spins round they would like to play for. As mentioned, this can be changed in the base game. Each one requires a different number of scatters to trigger it, has a different frequency, and offers slightly different rewards:Cool requires at least 4 scatters to trigger, is frequent and awards 9 free spins with a locked growing wild on reel 3.Medium requires at least 8 scatters to trigger, is average and awards 12 free spins with 2 locked growing wilds on reels 2 and 5.Hot requires at least 12 scatters to trigger, is infrequent and awards 15 free spins with 3 moving growing wilds.Xtra Hot requires at least 16 scatters to trigger, is rare and awards 20 free spins with 4 moving growing wilds.If the number of scatters in view is enough to trigger a higher bonus, players spin a wheel for a chance to win the higher one. If the spin is not successful, the chosen bonus is triggered instead. If the number of scatters in view is not enough to trigger the chosen bonus, but it is enough to trigger a smaller one, then players spin a wheel for a chance to win the smaller bonus. Losing this spin results in no bonus trigger.Expanding WildsThe Cool and Medium bonus have Expanding Wilds. These wilds begin as 1x1 sized symbols, which may grow in the bonus to 2, 3 or 4 high. When wilds grow, they may shift to another reel.Expanding & Jumping WildsThe Hot and Xtra Hot bonus has Expanding & Jumping Wilds. At the start of the round, these wilds are also 1x1 in size and move randomly about the game board. They can grow in the bonus to 2, 3, or 4-high.Buy FeatureClicking the bonus buy button gives players the chance to buy the Cool, Medium, Hot, or Xtra Hot bonus for 30, 50, 100, or 400 times the bet, respectively.4 Deals With The Devil slot - game mode options4 Deals With The Devil: Wild Lab: Slot Verdict4 Deals With The Devil felt like a game undergoing an identity crisis that wasn't totally sure what it was trying to be. Is it retro, old school, retro-modern, postmodern, post-postmodern, a visual essay on the nature of evil? Or are we just overthinking what is a slightly bedraggled game which might have benefited from a tighter coordination between its parts? Maybe fine-tuning the bits of the audio that didn't seem to fit or sprucing the weaker aspects of the visuals might have helped boost the game's appeal.It's certainly not all doom and gloom, though. Positives include bonus rounds that can flip from nada to something when larger wilds jump to the right spots on the board. Winning potential could be the thing to convince players sitting on the fence, unsure whether to give 4 Deals With The Devil a try. The paytable denotes wins of up to 10,000x (the home screen 5,000x), but a trip to the rules section mentions a win of 50,000x the bet occurring during simulated spins, so all those ways and expanded wilds do have the ability to deliver.4ThePlayer's continued effort to give players a measure of influence over a game is also appreciated. What's good here is if you pick a smaller bonus, there is a chance of triggering a larger one if enough scatters land. Vice versa, players who stick to the larger bonus, still have a chance of winning a smaller one if less scatters land. This got us thinking, though. Since players can win higher or lower bonuses, anyway, doing it like this kind of negates the point of picking a bonus in the first place. Would 4 Deals With The Devil have been just as good if the picking bonus thing had been axed, and players straight out won the free spins round corresponding to the number of scatter symbols in view? That's not really the 4ThePlayer's ethos, though; preferring to mix things up, do things differently to keep players on their toes, and doing deals is essentially the game's key selling point.

Title: Raging Dragons
review: Raging Dragons: Slot OverviewAfter a brief sojourn to the Middle East in Kings of Gold, developer iSoftBet return to more familiar territory. We are talking about the venerated Asian theme, of course, a genre iSoftBet can’t seem to get enough of. Neither does a segment of the games playing public either going by the frequency with which these slots are flying off the production line. It’s no bad thing, provided the quality and a bit of originality is there. Has iSoftBet managed to squeeze some of that into Raging Dragons?One thing iSoftBet usually nail is the audio-visual aspect to their games. There’s no denying the talented team who has created quite a dreamy view for Raging Dragons. It’s not exactly an original one, but the mountainous scenery has been designed in pleasing blue tones, accentuating the height of the surrounding cliff faces. Perched on top of the peaks are traditional Chinese buildings, pagoda-style while capping it all is the 5-reel, 3-row game area. What is a little different is the 5 multi-coloured lions sitting along the top of the reels. These aren’t just for decorative purposes either, since they play into the features covered below.iSoftBet offer their standard range of bet options from 20 p/c on the lower side, up to $/€20 per spin. Playable on any device, Raging Dragons does away with paylines, in favour of a 243 ways to win system. Here, winning combinations of three or more of a kind line up from the leftmost reel in any row. The system helps the game flow and creates a more modern-feeling than if the designer had paired the traditional subject matter with fixed paylines.When it comes to figures, Raging Dragons produces some pretty impressive numbers. At the time of testing, RTP was not available, but is expected to hover around the 96% mark. The volatility is high as are the individual symbol values, so the ride can be a little all over the place at times. The developer has decked the paytable out with 11 pay symbols, a scatter, and wilds. Pay symbols include standard 9-A card royals and premiums, which are more theme-based. Here you’ll find potion bottles, a chicken statue, a junk boat, a horse, and what looks like a kite. All have a real Asian flavour, though they aren’t the usual symbols you find in a slot, making a nice change. As to values, five premiums in a row are worth a fair pile coins, at 60 to 200x the stake.Raging Dragons: Slot FeaturesRaging Dragons - free spins optionsPlayers who like several features padding out their Asian gaming should be satisfied by the selection on offer at Raging Dragons. The variety is quite broad, with extras popping up during base and bonus games, conjuring up some pretty big wins should they all come together.Raging Dragons is a game that relies on a fair amount of player input. One area requiring some screen clicking is the Wild Dragon feature. Whenever a wild lands on reel 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, it applies a multiplier of 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, or 5x, respectively. Strangely, it's up to the player to choose which wild they want to activate as wilds only land on one reel during the base game.One of the most interesting extras is the mysterious Lucky Envelope feature. These red envelopes, or hongbao, are common in Asian culture where they are filled with money and given as gifts on certain holidays. In Raging Dragons, the red letter feature can be triggered on any spin. When activated, the enveloper opens up to award a cash prize of 8x, 88x, 888x, or 8888x the bet.Finally we get free spins which are triggered by 3 green orb scatters. As well as the bonus game, players get a payout of 2x, 5x, or 20x when 3, 4 or 5 scatters land. Now, in true Blueprint Gaming style, players must choose one of 6 free spins options: 10 free spins + wild multipliers of 10x, 15x, or 30x 13 free spins + wild multipliers of 8x, 10x, or 15x 15 free spins + wild multipliers of 5x, 8, or 10x 20 free spins + wild multipliers of 3x, 5x, or 8x 25 free spins + wild multipliers of 2x, 3x, or 5xThe sixth mystery option awards a random combination of free spins and multipliers from the above options. During the bonus, wilds can land on all five reels, and their multiplier values alternate on each spin. Players can extend the feature by landing 1 or 2 scatters which adds 2 or 4 extra spins to the remaining amount. Or, landing 3 scatters retriggers the initial free spins choice, plus the respective cash prize.Raging Dragons: Slot VerdictRaging Dragons is an enjoyable game that might do enough to entertain regular players as much as Asian fans. The bonus game’s multiplier-fest is a highlight, but the Dragon Reels and the ever-present lure of the red letter bonus during the main game help keep interest alive there. Despite the simple gameplay, the combination of features and the 243 win ways raise the game to above-average Asian standard.You’d kind of hope so since iSoftBet is a regular traveller to the eastern part of the globe. Their expertise shows in the high graphic standard and the theme presentation, which is clichéd in some ways, yet subtly different in others. When designing an Asian slot, studios are limited as to the imagery they can use – dragons etc. iSoftbet has rammed in plenty of those; however, the inclusion of things like the red envelope broadens the cultural experience. It helps that big wins can leap forth from the envelope, plus the game’s overall potential is high. Wins of up to 12,150 times the stake might broaden the appeal.All up, Raging Dragons is not a bad slot, leaning towards unmissable for players really into the Asian thing. It’s not quite so enchanting otherwise, but there is some decent gaming going on beneath the common outer wrapper.

Title: Fire Portals
review: Fire Portals: Slot OverviewWhile it possesses mundane definitions too, the word 'portal' often has fantastical connotations, as if passing through the right one would send someone to a magical realm, or a mage might create one to draw beings or objects of power to this plane of existence for malignant or benevolent purposes… Developer Pragmatic Play has delved into the magical side of the word when designing Fire Portals, an online slot heavy on esoteric arcana. The visuals could hardly have been any more inviting for players interested in the idea of stepping through a magical gate and ending up somewhere else, in this dimension or plane of existence or somewhere else entirely new. The free spins round might have been held in a more imaginative location, but whatever, the fire realm gets the job done, too.Fire Portals' features get the job done, too; at least, they do so on paper. In Fire Portals, they have the benefit of multiplying their values together when merging into one, which is a very nice trait. It's a trait that will arguably see more use in the bonus round since the Fire Portal Wilds are not removed between spins as they are in the base game. However, repeated bonus rounds failed to see them really perform much magic, even when building solid multiplier values, as they frequently ended up shutting down in a dead spin storm during our test sessions.Perhaps we hadn't managed to stir in the right reagents, or the session was performed under the wrong moon phase or something. Title: Book of Jones

Indiana Smith? It just doesn't sound as fittingly American as Indiana Jones. One more tidbit of internet lore, George Lucas' dog Indiana was the inspiration not only for Indiana Jones but for Han Solo's Wookie pal Chewbacca.And another thing, if we hadn't got movies starring an adventurer called Indiana Jones, we might well be reviewing a game right now called Book of Smith instead. Though it feels like we may have seen something like this in the past? In saying that, the thought of having a bunch of reels transformed into Fixed Symbol Reels is a heady one. Hard to say if the inclusion of Fixed Symbol Reels has had any impact on the game's max win, though, since the figure was not provided, though 5,000x full-screen wins are technically possible.To conclude, and probably repeat what's already been alluded to, Book of Jones is a decent book of' slot that didn't exactly blow socks off but wasn't a drag to play either. Most of what it does can be found in numerous other places, and while the Fixed Symbol Reels idea has merit, without it Book of Jones would have been pretty generic.

Title: Bugs Money
review: Bugs Money: Slot OverviewBugs Bunny - Bugs Money, geddit? Title: Aztec Spins

Should the wheel land on a Wheel Respin, it simply spins again.When the Aztec Wheel stops on a pay symbol, this specific symbol fills out both the 3rd and 4th reel, making them stacked. Moreover, should the wheel land on the Free Spins segment during the feature, then 6 additional free spins are awarded.Lastly, depending on the settings, players may be able to gamble their winnings. Of course, the Locked Symbols feature could result in a solid multi-line payout, and max potential has been calculated at 4,983 times your stake, so solid wins are possible. Capping the multiplier has capped winning potential to a degree, so Shah Mat tops out at 4,323 times the stake. Title: Rise of Giza PowerNudge

The free spins feature uses a progressive win multiplier that starts on x1. Following every nudge or subsequent free spin, the multiplier increases by +1. Collecting 3 or more scatters during the feature extends it by adding free spins in the same manner as in the main game. Perhaps worryingly, for some, free spins also come with a minimum guaranteed win of 5x the total bet. If you make it to the end of the feature and the minimum amount is not reached, extra free spins are awarded until the 5x is reached.In some instances, it may be possible to buy the round of free spins rather than trigger them. The cost of this is 80x the total bet and produces a spin which lands at least 3 overlay scatters.Rise of Giza PowerNudge - free spinsRise of Giza PowerNudge: Slot VerdictPowerNudge turned out to be quite a fun alternative to traditional cascading type features. It helps that winning combinations can start from any reel, preventing players from staring at the first three reels most of the time. Using this method also frees up the game board. For example, when winning symbols in the middle three reels drop, they might hook up with one or both outer reels to produce a longer win. It can also be a bit of a thrill, watching repeat winners nudge from one row to the next before exiting the grid by falling off the bottom.On the other side of the coin, PowerNudge does come across as a more restricted system than, say, reactions in a Megaways game. In large part, this is because there are fewer reels and a lot less ways to win. While repeat hits are possible, there are none of those insane moments that occur from time to time in a Megaways slot, where multiple symbols hit right across the grid, and it seems the whole thing is going to cascade. Symbols land stacked in Rise of Giza, but a full screen is limited to 150x the bet, so with a win multiplier in full swing, the game can muster up wins of 4,000x the bet max.There's a great chance certain players will get a real kick out of the new PowerNudge mechanic and the way it links symbols while creating consecutive winners. Rise of Giza is worth checking out if you're looking for a new or perhaps safer cascading game option. After the debut, it would be interesting to see PowerNudge let loose on something with a bit more muscle.

If you get 10 black cats, which is the highest paying symbol, you will be awarded a 100x win.A single cat symbol will double in a pay line that includes a wild symbol. Title: Codex of Fortune
review: Codex of Fortune: Slot OverviewFans of all things cylindrical will be chuffed to know developer NetEnt has cast their eyes back to an older slot titled Turn Your Fortune and given it a major overhaul. Well, we say major, but most of the time it is hard to tell the difference between the new one, Codex of Fortune, and its precursor. However, a few tweaks to the math model, an extra feature, and a loosening of its max win capabilities has transformed a mediocre game into something that might now appeal to a more demanding crowd of gamblers.Codex of Fortune is played over a game grid made up of 5 reels, 4 rows, and 40 fixed paylines. Visually, it is a slight improvement over Turn Your Fortune; the graphics are slightly crisper, though the main difference is a simple background colour change. Where Turn Your Fortune bathed itself in burgundy, Codex of Fortune slips into midnight blue. Essentially, there are no real aesthetic differences; both have a vaguely French Art Nouveau style, apparent in the font and influencing the symbols.While the looks might have remained more or less the same, the same cannot be said for what lies under the hood. NetEnt has traded the medium volatility for something with more grunt, boosting several other figures in the process. Potential is the headliner, but RTP is pretty eye-catching as well. Since there is a smidgen of strategy involved with one of the features, the return value can alter. Picking the average strategy generates an RTP value of 96%, while tinkering your approach can alter the return anywhere from 90.2% to a whopping 98%.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, regular wins hit at a rate of roughly 1 in 4 spins (25.4%), occurring when three or more matching symbols line up across a payline. Symbols have remained the same, so we get J-A royals for the low pays, followed by shells, fish, turtles, owls, and lions as the premiums. Land a five of a kind combo consisting of high-value symbols to fire off coins worth 3 to 10 times your stake. It is possible for any symbol type to land stacked on the reels, meaning full grid wins are on the cards. The Faberge inspired butterfly tile is the wild. It lands on any reel to substitute regular pay symbols to complete winning combinations.Codex of Fortune: Slot FeaturesFrom here, Codex of Fortune starts to diverge from its predecessor by adding a new Save the Keys feature to go along with Fortune Wins, Fortune Respins, and free spins. Fortune Wins is the name given to the device located on the left of the reels. This gadget has 5 horizontal levels, each containing 5 segments, raising in value the higher up you go. During Respins, prizes from the Fortune Wins max out at 200x the bet, while in free spins they are bumped up considerably to 10,000x the bet.Fortune Respins trigger when 2 scatter symbols land on the reels. For the respin, all non-winning symbols are removed from the grid, while one winning combination is locked in place, becoming the collectable symbol. Only blanks, symbols, or keys land on respins. If more of these symbols land on a respin, they are collected, and another respin is awarded. Every 5 symbols moves the cylinder up one horizontal level. When keys hit, they move the cylinder one position horizontally. Respins end when no new symbols land or if 20 have been collected.When respins conclude, a Save the Keys feature triggers. Here you can use the keys to collect a win from the Fortune Wins or save them to improve the prize values during free spins. Max RTP is achieved by saving keys whenever possible.To launch free spins, scatters need to land on reels 1, 3, and 5. Before this bonus round starts, a bonus reel spins to award 7-13 free spins, pick a special collectable symbol, and possibly a key symbol as well. Any previously saved keys can be used to start higher on the Fortune Wins. Moreover, in free spins, all collectable symbols landing on the reels are collected in the Fortune Wins meter. Each time the meter is filled with 20 spaces, players move one level up. Keys move the device horizontally as before. Prizes from the Fortune Wins are tallied up at the end of the round.Codex of Fortune: Slot VerdictIt might sound a tad convoluted on paper, but in action, it's all pretty straightforward. Basically, Codex of Fortune is a case of landing scatters to trigger respins or free spins, with the aim of racking up keys and collectable symbols to improve payouts from the Fortune Wins device. If you've played Turn Your Fortune, you'll certainly know the drill. The difference now is partly down to the Save the Keys feature – do you take the win or bank keys for possibly greater glory in free spins? They say a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush and all that, but way bigger prizes are possible in free spins, plus you get a better theoretical return by hanging on to the keys.Potential is one startling area where the two games differ. Turn Your Fortune was capable of the so-so total of 2,000x the bet - not bad, yet nothing wow magic either. Codex of Fortune, on the other hand, jacks that total to 10,000 times the stake – a figure far more likely to turn heads.At the end of the day, Codex of Fortune is no doubt a bigger temptation for gamblers who turned their noses up at Turn Your Fortune. However, aside from the much larger max win, it's business as usual for the rest of the game. So, if you weren't keen on graphics which were meh two years ago, or low-level paylines setup, even 10,000x might not be enough to persuade you to have a crack.

Title: Hades River of Souls
review: Hades - River of Souls: OverviewDeveloper Fantasma Games builds on the fantasy theme of their previous slot Heroes Hunt Megaways while taking a darker turn in the process. This time the Swedish studio takes players deep into the earth’s bowels where souls cross the river Styx to roam the underworld. Down there is a place where fortunes can be found by brave players or lucky ones at least. The goal, according to Fantasma, is to escape the underworld while picking up as many riches as possible.Despite the sinister premise we can get down with that mission, and Fantasma has crafted a moody world in which to do so. A 5-reel, 10-payline grid sits in a jagged cavernous underworld, in all its spectral glory. The creative team at Fantasma has crafted a great scene, but it might have had more impact if the grid was transparent so we could see more of it. Adding to the visual obstruction is a panel above the reels for special symbols, taking up even more of the screen. Not a major, just an observation.Around the game area what we do see are crags, and cliffs, while sparks rise ominously up from the ground. The scene provokes a frisson when you wonder what happens to the poor souls down there. But let’s look on the bright side, this is a cartoon, not the real thing.On the subject of sensory experience, the audio deserves a mention. It is hair rising on the back of your neck good at times. Along with a dark, rumbling soundtrack is some excellent chorus work, including a sweet Book of Ra type blast when certain symbols appear or actions take place.It’s not hard to imagine an eternity down there being a somewhat brutal fate. Fantasma has channelled some of those trying times into a highly volatile math model. Decent potential exists, but know that nabbing riches from the underworld isn’t going to be a walk in the park. Helping balance things out, in the long run, is a solid RTP of 96.56%, as well as a hit frequency of nearly one in five (19.49%).Playable across all devices from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, winners occur when three or more matching symbols land on one of the 10 pay lines – both ways. So winning combinations pay from left to right as well as right to left, upping your chances.The paytable is a nice collection of ancient Greek mythology. Starting with the low pays which Fantasma has cleverly styled after those old pots you see in museums inlaid with ravens, snakes, deer, bulls, and lions. The high pays, in ascending order are some sort of gyro, a helmet, Cerberus, Persephone, and of course, Hades as the most valuable pay symbol.Five Hades on a line is worth 10 times the stake, which, doubles to 20 thanks to pay both ways. According to legend, Hades was the oldest son of Cronus though the last to be regurgitated by him. Clearly, that experience earns him the right to head of the paytable.Hades - River of Souls: FeaturesHades River of Souls - free spinsJust as the underworld isn’t short of souls, nor is the slot version short on features. Players get base and bonus game features such as Avalanches, Wild Souls Multipliers, the Skull of Charon, and Hades Free Spins.Avalanches appear in all game modes, activating whenever there is a win. All symbols in the winning combination are removed to let new ones fall, providing more winning opportunities to win. Above the reels, special symbols are displaying for players to track, and hopefully, tumbledown when Avalanches occur.Wild symbols are the key to the Wild Souls Multiplier which starts at x1. The wild substitutes for any regular pay symbols and every 3 used in a winning combination increase the Wild Souls Multiplier by +1. When an Avalanche sequence ends, the multiplier is applied to the total win. During the base game, it resets to x1 on new spins.In what is possibly the most cheerful depiction of Charon ever, the grinning skull symbol triggers The Skull of Charon feature. The skull symbol may appear on any spin, activating when there are no more winning combinations. It then scoots around the reels, removing 2-10 random regulars to let new symbols fall for additional chances to win.This leads us to the highlight of the game - Hades Free Spins. The Golden Trident symbols are what you want here since 3 on the reels award 10 free spins. Any additional tridents in view add 5 more spins to the total, each. During free spins, 3 winning wilds increase the multiplier by +2, with the added benefit that it never resets between spins. The feature can be retriggered in the same way as it is triggered.Hades - River of Souls: VerdictHades - River of Souls is a well-made slot, possessing some genuinely entertaining moments. It can be tricky to crack, but the rewards are there for the bold and lucky. For some reason, it brought to mind Avatar UX’s PopRocks. Both are tough, high volatile slots that rely on a progressive multiplier to get the best out of. In Hades case, the best means potential wins of up to 5,058 times your stake. There is also a similar vibe in the two games, though Hades comes out trumps– largely helped by its superb sounds and great visual presentation.As to visuals, seeing special symbols above the reels in the queue is a double-edged sword. Epic, when they cascade in right where you want them - frustrating when they don’t. Overall it’s an interesting idea. All up, Fantasma Games has crafted another highly playable slot. It doesn’t quite match up to Heroes Hunt Megaways in terms of max payouts, or gameplay. But, it’s a nicely atmospheric game to immerse yourself in, with some interesting features, and potential to boot.

Title: Scroll of Dead
review: Scroll of Dead: Slot OverviewComing across the word 'of' in a slot title is a pretty reliable clue as to what sort of gaming you can expect to find. Namely, expanding symbols, chunky paytables, volatile gaming, and in most cases, Egyptian visuals. There are so many of these games now they have more or less formed their very own category. In fact, if they were officially assembled, they would easily be one of the biggest groupings in many casino lineups. Standing head and shoulders above others is Play'n GO's classic Book of Dead, which is the 'book' slot par excellence for many enthusiasts.Scroll of Dead utilises Play'n GO's expertise in this area, offering everything you would expect from this type of game – plus a twist. Scroll of Dead's twist is one of those alterations that seem obvious in hindsight and makes you wonder why it hasn't been more extensively used. When in motion, the new addition not only makes the game bigger but also increases the potential returns in the process.Set within a brazier-filled temple, two things instantly register. One is the extra 6th reel, sitting in a locked state until the requisite number of scatters break it open. Secondly, Rich Wilde has been dropped from the picture. Perhaps he's back at the institute lecturing or dusting antiquities at an undisclosed location. Either way, his exclusion is no major loss as Play'n GO seem to be phasing him out in favour of his vivacious daughter Cat as a replacement. Other than these two changes, the game has a very Book of Dead look and feel, reinforced by the striped reel dividers and similar-looking symbols.Scroll of Dead continues the honoured tradition of being a highly volatile adventure, with a rating of 9 out of 10. As per usual, the RTP is variable, where the most generous value is 96.28%, dropping to 94.28% or less in some circumstances. As you'd expect, any device is fine for taking on the temple, where stakes of 1 p/c to $/€100 may be selected. The reason penny stakes are possible is because players can set between 1 and 10 paylines.Symbols are both old and new, the old being 10 to A card royals, which have a familiar design, while high-pays include Ankhs, birds, snakes, plus Cleopatra type ladies. During the base game, lines of five premiums are worth 50 to 500 times the bet - that figure increasing to 100 to 750 times the bet when the extra reel is active, making six of a kind wins possible.Scroll of Dead: Slot FeaturesInstead of a book playing the role of wild/scatter, Scroll of Dead uses another popular Egyptian icon, the scarab. As the wild, scarabs land on any reel to replace regular pay symbols to complete line wins. As the scatter, 3, 4, or 5 scarabs in view award 8 free spins plus a payout of 2x, 20x, or 200x the bet.Two things happen before free spins begin. The first thing is the 6th reel is unlocked and becomes active for the duration of free spins. Secondly, 1 pay symbol is randomly selected to be the special expanding symbol. Chosen symbols expand to cover all positions on their reel when they can form a win, which is possible even when they are not adjacent to each other. Expanded symbols also pay all ways. Note that wilds do not replace expanded chosen symbols.The game also features an optional gamble round following wins in the base game. Correctly guessing the colour or suit of a hidden card doubles or quadruples the win value. Gamble rounds can be played up to 5 times in a row.Scroll of Dead: Slot VerdictScroll of Dead's raison d'etre is a relatively simple change, but the inclusion of a 6th reel certainly adds a new dimension. Book enthusiasts are no doubt aware having an extra reel isn't completely new. Greentube beat Play'n GO to the punch by about six years with Book of Ra Deluxe 6, which also had a 6th reel. The difference then was you had to increase the bet using the 'Extra Bet' option to have it active in all phases of the game, rather than just unlocking it when free spins triggered.On the subject of potential, providing an extra reel does have a positive effect, beating the payout of regular 'book' slots by 50%. Whereas a game like Book of Dead maxed out at 5,000x the bet, Scroll of Dead ups that total to 7,500x. In theory, at least, hitting the game's full potential is as straightforward as ever – just land the top expanding premium symbol on each reel during free spins.Aside from more reels, it is business as usual when playing Scroll of Dead. Solid line win values keep the base game interesting, and the production value is high. In many ways, Scroll of Dead is a simply designed game, yet it performs in the usual Triple-A Play'n GO fashion. This means attractive graphics and slick animations tying everything together to produce a class act.Within the ultra-saturated 'book of' category of games, there have been so many twists that it's hard to create something new. Scroll of Dead might not be totally original, but its 6th reel and larger than normal potential do set it apart from most of its competitors. Couple that with a well-established pedigree, and Scroll of Dead certainly has the goods to thrill players entertained by this style.Don't MissIf you can't have enough of Play'n GO's Egyptian themed series of slots, we also recommend giving Legacy of Dead as well as Scroll of Dead a spin.

Title: Cowabunga Dream Drop
review: Cowabunga Dream Drop: Slot OverviewSoftware provider Relax Gaming has dunked its progressive jackpot network in the briny to come up with Cowabunga Dream Drop, a totally tubular online slot, also available in a non-Dream Drop variant. The word 'cowabunga', if you were interested, is said to have originated on the Howdy Doody show in 1953, first uttered by Chief Thunderthud, before spilling into surf culture in the 50s and 60s, before finding its way into the vocabulary of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles in the 80s/90s, primarily spilling forth from pizza lover Michaelangelo's mouth. The word is generally used to express satisfaction or delight, so it would make an ideal exclamation for celebrating a Dream Drop win - more so the Mega than the Rapid.Some surfers seem willing to risk life and limb in search of the perfect ride, but even so, Cowabunga Dream Drop's break looks a little on the perilous side. In other words, you might want to keep driving down the coast to somewhere more forgiving unless you're a real daredevil. Otherwise, Cowabunga Dream Drop is held in a pretty typical spot for a beach-related slot – sand, warm blue water, bright sky, lazily floating clouds, palm trees, the usual. For those who were around when NetEnt's Wild Water slot was a hot release, it'll certainly bring back some memories.Cowabunga Dream Drop slot - base gameNo matter which version you play, the betting options are 20 c to $/€100 per spin, but when playing Cowabunga Dream Drop specifically, the higher the bet, the bigger the chance is to trigger a jackpot win. With a medium-high volatile math model running in the back, in the front, Cowabunga Dream Drop gets its surf up on a 5-reel, 3-row grid, where the middle three reels can expand up to 7 positions high, supplying 243 to 3,087 ways to win.Fish and humans divide up the pay table, with 4 fish coloured blue, green, orange, and red making up the low pay symbols, plus 2 surfer dudes and 2 surfer dudettes as the high pays. Hitting winning ways made up of 5 matching low pays is worth 0.15x to 0.2x the bet, or 0.6 to 2 times the bet is paid for getting 5 OAK premium wins. Life ring wilds appear on all reels, substituting for any regular pay symbol. A winning combination of 5 wilds pays 2 times the bet.Cowabunga Dream Drop: Slot FeaturesCowabunga Dream Drop slot - free spinsAs per usual, Dream Drop is the main event, supplemented by a Sync & Expand feature, Nudges, free spins, and in the non-DD version, players may buy the free spins round if they so choose.Sync & ExpandAt random, 2 or 3 middle reels may sync and expand up to 7 symbols high. Synced reels contain the same matching symbols in the same order.NudgeEvery so often, the reels stop, then nudge downward to improve a winning combination.Free SpinsLanding 2 scatter symbols in the base game triggers 5 free spins. For free spins, the middle three reels are always synced. Players get +1 additional free spin for every scatter that lands on the rightmost reel during the round.Buy Feature (Non-DD Version)For the cost of 60 times the bet, players can buy the free spins round. The RTP when buying the feature is 96.27%.Dream DropA Jackpot spin may trigger at random when the spin button is pressed, and the regular spin is played afterwards. During it, if at least one DD symbol lands on each reel, players enter the Dream Drop Bonus game. The Dream Drop Bonus grid has 5-reels, 5-rows, and all DD symbols from the triggering spin are brought over. For each jackpot, a different number of reels need to be filled by landing DD symbols - 1 for the Rapid, 2 for the Midi, 3 for the Maxi, 4 for the Major, and 5 for the Mega. The jackpot connected with the number of reels filled at the end is won. Starting values for the 5 jackpots are Rapid €1, Midi €5, Maxi €100, Major €25,000, and Mega €500,000.Cowabunga Dream Drop slot - jackpot featureCowabunga Dream Drop: Slot VerdictFor some, the business world using a surfing angle might come across as cheesily forced, and you know, there is a bit of that happening in Cowabunga Dream Drop. As if the suits are trying to be all hip and down with the kids. But Cowabunga Dream Drop is an online slot, after all, so thematically, let's not take it too seriously. The sun's out, the waves are up, sometimes terrifyingly so, and one dude looks like he's riding a shark while a wave breaks; what could be more bitchin' than that?Well, Cowabunga Dream Drop is a slot, after all, where the focus is on winning dough, so pulling off the ultimate and hitting the Mega jackpot where the capped prize is €3 million would be pretty bitchin'. Not many people are going to do that, though, and the rest of Cowabunga Dream Drop wasn't super gnarly. The high number of ways means players can theoretically catch a good ride, and outside the jackpots, Cowabunga Dream Drop can produce results of up to 6,000x the bet, which would be a lot more preferable to being popped on by a colony of seagulls.Cowabunga Dream Drop also possesses a measure of novelty due to the low frequency of surfing-related slots. It's tough to think of many competitors in this arena. NetEnt's 2014 release Wild Water? One possible contemporary due to the Speedboat Bonus round is ELK Studio's Sumo Sumo. However, apart from the water sports angle, the two slots have virtually nothing else in common. So, Cowabunga Dream Drop succeeds in providing a fairly unique vehicle for Relax Gaming's Dream Drop to strut. Without those jackpots, though, Cowabunga drops a few weight classes.

Title: Mysterious

It's also stacked with features including the choice of two different bonus rounds.Booting up the slot, it gives a promising first impression. In the background, mist creeps through a sleepy village, with a menacing manor on the hill beneath stormy skies. Sure, it's a bit clichéd, but it nicely brings to mind Bram Stoker's tortured village of Whitby or the Castlevania franchise and draws you in. Contributing to the immersion are three modes and intriguing characters next to the reels which we'll get to shortly. First comes the business of setting bets, which are available from 10 p/c up to $/€100 per spin, before heading out to solve the mystery.Turning to the paytable, the symbols are super crisp and oddly fitting. The default RTP is also fine and dandy on 96.50%, but it can be lowered by the operator so make sure to check the paytable before hitting the spin button. In the pantheon of Pragmatic slots, Mysterious has quite an entertaining base games with several features attached where the big dosh can spill out.Mysterious Slot (Pragmatic Play): FeaturesFree spins splash screenAs alluded to, the base game comes with 3 different Wild Modifiers that change according to the game mode. The highlighted character on the side of the reels signifies which mode and wild is active. No matter the mode, the wilds are able to substitute for any of the regular pay symbols. We get:The Lord: When Lord wilds are part of winning combinations, they reveal a multiplier of x2 or x3. More than one Lord Wild will multiply each other.The Lady: If the Lady Wild is part of winning combinations, the prize is paid, then she expands and reveals a stack of mystery symbols which can create more winners.The Baron: This Wild symbol can change nearby symbols into more wilds.The icing on the cake is the bonus game. The game shifts inside the manner and the game area is expanded to 6 reels and 4 rows with 4,096 win ways. Before kicking off, players can choose one of two free spin options:Locking Multiplier Free Spins: A clock symbol is introduced and when one lands it awards a random multiplier of x3, x6, x9, or x12 which is applied to the total win of that spin. If two clocks land, then 2 extra free spins are played with the multiplier locked at that level for both of them.Resurrecting Roaming Wilds Free Spins: This mouthful of a bonus game includes Wilds that fade away after each spin and float around the reels. If another wild lands in view the roaming wilds return for that spin in a random positions.Mysterious Slot (Pragmatic Play): VerdictAfter a few mediocre sessions with sub-par to okay slots to review, it was an absolute pleasure to play a game that was so well put together. Okay maybe we're getting into the swing of the game too much, but Mysterious can do that. It's evident that a lot of thought went into every element of the game and it shows. The money-making opportunities are more condensed during free spins sure, but the rotating wild modes, as well as the sheer atmosphere, keep the spinning interesting. The bonus game wasn’t as difficult to trigger as they can be with this developer, or so it seemed during our test run at least. That can seem like the case with some of Pragmatic's volatile beasts.All up, the Mysterious video slot is an excellent game that showcases a new direction for Pragmatic Play that fits it like a glove. And don't be put off by the spectres and doom, the theatrical horror is more camp hi-jinks than scary and makes the perfect gaming accompaniment to a dark and stormy night in.

Title: Lamp Of Infinity

Title: Alice in WildLand

Title: Great Rhino Megaways

Before launching, players are presented with 4 options to choose from with various rules and varying degrees of volatility:15 free spins with a starting win multiplier of 1x.10 free spins with a starting win multiplier of 5x.5 free spins with a starting win multiplier of 10x.Mystery Choice with a random number of free spins and a random starting win multiplier.Triggering the free spins feature with additional scatter symbols gives you more starting free spins. It’s not an awkward clunk of a Megaways debut that say, Raging Rhino Megaways was. The graphics are decent, animations are smooth, and the gameplay is slick and dependable. For straight forward Megaways gaming, it delivers the goods. Possible winnings aren’t bad either with potential capped at 20,000 times the stake. It's obviously tricky to hit anything so high in the base game, so max returns rely on the single extra feature to do the heavy lifting.At the end of the day, Great Rhino Megaways is technically capable of delivering some good gaming, there’s nothing overly wrong with it as such. It's just a pity that Pragmatic was so cautious with their debut, and copying Blueprint’s bonus game options won’t win it friends either. Ah well, the Megaways ball is finally up and rolling at the Pragmatic studios now, so the question is what approach will they take next –restrained and forgettable, or something more original? Let’s see.Don't Miss...There's a Christmas themed version of this game titled Christmas Carol Megaways. Title: Book of Ra Deluxe

Title: HipHopPop PopWins
review: HipHopPop: Slot OverviewAs wikiHow succinctly puts it, 'a rap battle is a verbal tussle, a contest of force where MCs flex their rap muscle, and if you wanna hustle to the top of the battle rap bustle – get ready to throw down in a rap scuffle.' Title: Iron Girl
review: Iron Girl IntroductionLet's just start off by saying that the first impression was far from the best. At first look, it appears flavourless, uninspiring and flat, as if missing that extra dimension you want to see in a slot. We all know, however, that even simplistic slots can become classics, which is why we kept spinning the reels to dig deeper into the unknown.That extra dimension we were talking about, it often comes in the form of a good story and distinctive characters, something that is a great challenge for game developers to fit into a slot. Symbols on the reels include 4 low-value symbols in the form of futuristic royal symbols, as well as 4 high paying symbols represented by the 4 villains where Quake, the scarred badass looking cyborg, is the most lucrative, award you 10 times the stake for 5 across a payline.There is no scatter symbol included in the game as it lacks a conventional free spins feature, but the wild, here represented by the main character Iron Girl, plays a very central role.Iron Girl FeaturesRespins feature with the award meter on top of the reelsetIn terms of features, the game includes a random Iron Armour feature. The Iron Armour can appear at any time and add up to 5 randomly placed wilds onto the reels which in turn can trigger the Villain respins. The Villain respins triggers when a winning combination of high paying symbols (Villains) appear on the reels. The highest paying combination will then be held in place for a respin along with any other matching symbol or wild, even if it's not part of the winning combination. The respins continue as long as new matching Villains or wilds are added to the reels. There's more to it than that, however.Above the reelset is a reward meter counting the amount of sticky Villains collected during the course of the respins feature. A reward known as Bounty Bonus may be triggered following the respins feature depending on your progress. This award is followed by an x2, x3 and x5 multiplier should you land at least 10, 12 or 14 Villains respectively.Iron Girl ConclusionWe're looking at a high variance slot according to information from Play'n GO with a relatively low max win potential of 1000 times the stake per single spin which is achieved by landing a full-screen top symbol or/and wilds along with the 5x multiplier. It's not a slot for those looking for memorable dream hits, but rather for those who want some play time or seeking a slot to help out with wagering as it's quite a balanced game. There are, however, many more entertaining and potentially more profitable slots we could think of.Visually, Iron Girl appears dull, as if something is missing, failing miserably to engage us. We simply don't feel the thrill nor intensity. An online slot that lacks the potential for massive wins, which alone can get your heart racing, needs to make up for it in some other aspect. Title: Big Buffalo Megaways

Title: Flodder

Title: Gus Goes Fishin'

Title: Dick The Farmer

Title: Adventures of Captain Blackjack

Each contains a bonus feature, such as:Extra spins – 3, 4, 5, 6, or 9 additional free spins.Multiplier - +1, +2, or +3 is added to the win multiplier.A mid symbol is upgraded to a wild symbol.A low symbol is upgraded to a mid-symbol.Free spins start with a win multiplier of x1 (or higher due to picks), and landing 2, 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols awards 1, 2, 3, or 4 additional feature picks. If all 16 features have been awarded, only extra free spins can be won from then on.Adventures of Captain Blackjack: Slot VerdictWhile we're in a historical mood, did you know in earlier forms of Blackjack, participants were paid out ten to one for landing the black Jack of Spades or Jack of Clubs plus an Ace of Spades? Any player familiar with the modern form of Blackjack will be aware that this rule has been scratched. A similar feeling of familiarity permeates Adventures of Captain Blackjack, which has a look and gameplay vaguely reminiscent of a number of previous JFTW releases. Not in a copying way, but a similar feel and spirit are aroused as in others they've done.On the subject of gameplay, Adventures of Captain Blackjack is pretty standard stuff. The Kraken Coin collection leading to possible Kraken Wheel spins adds interest to an otherwise humdrum base game. Despite theoretically being able to win more from free spins, the Kraken Wheel's top prize felt more achievable. The modest number of paylines and symbol values didn't exactly create major levels of optimism. Sure, there's the win multiplier bonus feature, if you can collect them from the feature pick section, though the value maxes out at x7, which is handy but still leaves players with plenty of work to do. Still, potential in free spins is technically decent, capped at 5,000x the bet or $/€250,000, presumably whichever comes first.All up, Adventures of Captain Blackjack was an okay game that feels like a fairly standard Just For The Win release. It's got the decent looks, sounds, and features we're used to from the studio, without being particularly noteworthy in any category. This isn't necessarily a bad thing; just pointing out that Adventures of Captain Blackjack isn't Just For The Win's way of starting off the year with a bang; but rather sees the studio easing themselves into it instead.

Title: Noble Sky

Title: Wild Toro 2

Several wild symbols appear at various points in the game; all can replace pay symbols to complete wins. The most basic wild is a logo covered tile; the others are entwined with the features.Wild Toro 2: Slot FeaturesFans of the first will be happy to know the Matador and Toro still aren't best friends, so when they see each other on the reels, the Toro Goes Berserk feature triggers. Other extras include walking wilds, walking wild multipliers, Matador Respins, Expanding Reels, and a selection of X-iter betting modes.First up, the Silver Matador symbol is a walking wild, while the Golden Matador is a walking wild with a progressive multiplier. If additional Toro symbols appear during respins, they inherit the current multiplier from the Toro already on the board.Beware the black Matador symbol. All wild symbols that appear during respins remain sticky.Bonus: guarantees the Toro Goes Berzerk feature for 100x the bet.Big Bonus: three spins with at least 1 Expanding Matador Respins feature for 250x the bet. All wild symbols are sticky, and expanded reels persist between spins.Super Bonus: the same as the Big Bonus with the added benefit that the highest multiplier achieved in a spin is added to any Gold Matador multiplier appearing on the following spin. This costs 500x the bet.Wild Toro 2: Slot VerdictSince Wild Toro was released, ELK has vastly developed its world-building skills via games like the Gold series of slots, and their experience has been put to great use in Wild Toro 2. On the other hand, some might see it as an acceptable trade-off for the vastly increased winning possibilities. For Wild Toro 2, ELK has pushed the maximum you can win to 10,000x the bet, making it a lot more potentially rewarding.To sum up, Wild Toro 2 isn't a paradigm shift, but ELK has stretched the first slot in several key areas. Sensorially enhanced, the game draws you in deeper, plus there's additional firepower from those multipliers and extra rows. Title: 9 Pots of Gold
review: 9 Pots of Gold Slot: OverviewMicrogaming partner studio Gameburger Studios returns to drop their third release 9 Pots of Gold. Building on the success of their previous slot 9 Masks of Fire comes a math clone that uses all of the same features and figures that resonated with enough players to warrant a remake. 9 Masks of Fire had a tribal, African vibe while 9 Pots of Gold uses that perennial favourite – the jolly Irish /Leprechaun theme. It has been timed to perfection too, scheduled for release around St Patrick's Day. Leprechauns are full of personality, and 9 Pots provides even more by naming its central character. Known as Lucky Lad Flynn, the sunglasses-wearing rapscallion is apparently the 'richest in the land.' What's the chance he is going to share some of those riches?Where 9 Masks went with a red and gold colour scheme, 9 Pots goes all-out Irish with green and gold and a shower of shamrocks. The 5 reel, 3 row, 20 payline grid takes up most of the space, but the ascending scatter prizes sit on the left-hand side tempting players to have a crack. To do so requires setting stakes, which start at 20 p/c and go as high as $/€60 a spin. This being a clone, we get the same stats out of the game's math model. That means an RTP rating of 96.24% along with medium volatility. One of 9 Masks’ drawcards was its relatively high hit rate of 39.75% which has also crossed over to 9 Pots of Gold.The symbols are all pretty much clichés of the genre and classic slots in general. In ascending order are a BAR, a shamrock, a leprechaun top hat, and a Celtic harp. The next three are '7s', and there are a single 7s, double 7s, and triple 7 symbols. The most valuable are the triple 7s at 37.5 times the stake but players can also score winners when mixes of 7s land. For example, you could have 2 double 7s and a triple 7 on a payline to trigger a payout. The pay symbols are all designed in a pleasant green colour, while the wild is a vibrant mushroom icon. It can substitute for any symbol except the free spins or pot symbols. The wild is also worth more than the triple 7s, and five of them return 125 times the stake.9 Pots of Gold Slot: FeaturesFree spin wheel in view9 Pots of Gold comes with two additional features. The first we'll cover is the Free Spins bonus round which comes into play when 3 or more scatter symbols land - they land on reels 2, 3, and 4 reels and 3 award a spin of the Free Spin Wheel. The Free Spin Wheel is separated into segments which have 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, or 30 free spins on them. Each segment comes with an x2 multiplier, except the 25 and 30 free spin segments which have an x3 multiplier. Scatters continue to land during free spins, and if three land they retrigger the initial number of free spins again.9 Pots of Gold's other key selling point is the scatter win feature called the Pot Pays. Whenever 3 or more pot scatter symbols land, they award an instant cash prize. The prizes on offer are 1x, 5x, 15x, 40x, 100x, 500x, and 2,000x the stake when 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9 pot symbols land. Keep in mind that pot symbol wins during free spins do not have the multiplier applied to the amount.9 Pots of Gold Slot: VerdictLike most clones, whatever you thought of the original will more or less be what you think of the follow-up. 9 Masks of Fire proved to be a fairly popular slot for Gameburger and its Celtic clone shares most of the same positive points. For one, it has bright visuals with hints of culture that produce a pleasing, and inviting look. Once the getting to know you phase has passed, there are a few things that keep players spinning. One is its high hit rate which provides constant payouts, and the second is the lure of that 2,000x jackpot prize for landing 9 scatters. Even if the top prize isn't struck, scatters provide smaller prizes to keep bankrolls ticking over.In short, its math model is designed to keep a certain type of player engaged. The concern for more dedicated gamblers is that despite the Pot Pays prize; it's not exactly a mega paying slot. Nor, with its medium volatility, is it seat of your pants exciting. But to be fair, 9 Pots doesn't shoot for that angle. It's happy to entertain a more laid back casual style of gaming. In that regards there is no reason why 9 Pots won't be as successful as the original slot was.One possible drawback is that 9 Pots is not as exotic as 9 Masks. This is due largely to the vast crowd of Irish themed slots out there. Something in abundance is never quite so desirable. Then again, plenty of players go for the Irish/Leprechaun thing so in that regard 9 Pots could be even more popular. For huge stakes and massive thrills, 9 Pots of Gold will struggle to fit the bill. But, all the elements are here to make it as popular as 9 Masks of Fire. The fact that 9 Pots of Gold it's not a high volatile roller coaster is unlikely to stop it from being an attractive proposal for many gamblers.

Title: Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax
review: Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax: Slot OverviewYggdrasil Gaming's DoubleMax slot mechanic has done the rounds with several of its partner studios, such as Peter & Sons and Reflex Gaming; now it's the time for buds Boomerang to have a turn. What's surprising is that instead of taking the easy option and making another Raptor DoubleMax, Boomerang has created a slot which refuses to conform to convention. The final product, Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax, does have a win multiplier that can double, but only in the base game, where it can also halve. When free spins come around, the game's maker has decided to flip the script by keeping the multiplier static while tossing in roaming wild stacks as a backup.Being a dragon game, Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax takes place in a fantasy world populated by the majestic beasts. Its background image, which is nicely done by the way, features a dragon flapping its wings over a scene of mountains, a valley, a castle, and so on. The quality of the artwork is quite high and should please fans of fantasy, especially fantasy containing flying serpents. For your listening pleasure, the music is suitably dramatic, and the character associated with the wild symbol gives Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax a slight air of anime, too. So far, so alright.Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax slot - base gameClicking the Total Bet section of the info bar brings up Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax's modest range of bets, where options go from 20 c to $/€12 per spin. A bonus buy is available as well, so when gambling regularly, the return to player comes in at 96.2%, rising to 96.5% for bought free spins. Volatility has been rated high, and the activity in both phases of play occurs on a 5-reel, 3-row matrix with 20 win lines.Winning combinations pay left to right from reel number one onwards, and there are 9 regular paying symbols. These are jagged J to A card ranks as the low pays, then a scythe, a pendant, flaming claws, a necklace, and a dragon as the high pays. Landing 5 OAK low pay combination awards 0.75 times the bet, whereas a line of 5 matching high pays is worth 1 to 2.5 times the bet. Wilds substitute for all symbols except the scatter.Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax: Slot FeaturesLegend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax slot - free spins wheelIf you're familiar with DoubleMax, then the singular way Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax uses the feature might shock you in a good or a not-so-good way. For one thing, Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax does not have a cascading wins system. However, it does have free spins with roaming wild stacks, plus a bonus buy.DoubleMaxWhen a win occurs in the base game, the win multiplier doubles in value for the next spin. When a spin occurs without creating a win, the win multiplier halves in value for the next spin. The multiplier can never go below x1, and there is no limit on how high the multiplier can go.Free SpinsFree spins are triggered by landing at least 3 scatter symbols. Players also get a payout of 1x, 2x, or 5x when 3, 4, or 5 scatters, respectively, land. When free spins begin, the multiplier achieved on the triggering base game spin carries over to the round. However, while free spins are active, the multiplier cannot be doubled or halved. It stays at the same value the whole time. At the start of the round, a stacked wild appears on the rightmost reel. Any wild appearing in free spins expands to cover the entire reel, and wild stacks move left one position on following spins. Wilds that reach the leftmost reel are removed on the next spin. Free spins are complete when all expanded wilds reach the leftmost reel.Buy BonusBuying the free spins round can be done by paying 86x the bet. When bought, a wheel awards a win multiplier of x2, x4, x8, or a random Mystery option of x16, x32, or x64, which persists throughout the round.Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax slot - free spinsLegend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax: Slot VerdictAfter reviewing a bunch of DoubleMax games by now, Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax did not turn out the way it was expected to. So far, one thing these games tend to have in common is a doubling of the multiplier following wins and cascades before resetting back to x1 for the next base game spin. Then, in free spins, the multiplier does not reset till the feature ends, maybe helping it achieve potentially stratospheric values. Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax dumps all of that to forge out on its path. A hat tip to Boomerang for daring to do so, but one wonders if the changes will attract more players than they repel or vice versa.One thing for fence sitters to keep in mind is that Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax has a 20,000x the bet win cap, which is in line with the higher tier DoubleMax games. So, final destinations with the altered mechanics can still end up in thrilling territory. The doubling/halving slower burn effect in the base game feels like a double-edged sword. It lacks the cascading pace of a regular DoubleMax game, but slow and steady could be just what others are after. Keep in mind, though, that the multiplier is saved per bet level, so you cannot build a multiplier while minimum betting then flip to max stake when a sizable multiplier is on the board. Possibly more contentious is the way the multiplier is locked in during free spins, especially if buying the bonus round, since you could well end up with an x2 through the whole thing. Not exactly in keeping with the DoubleMax spirit, though patient, lucky, base game grinding might be handsomely rewarded. As sweeteners, free spins are not set, and roaming full reel wilds are proven performers.It all adds up to a surprisingly fresh DoubleMax slot, which goes places others dare not tread. For that reason alone, it's worth DoubleMax mavens having a look, but whether Legend of the Dragon Wins DoubleMax wins out over the more typical way these sorts of slots operate remains to be seen.

Title: Wild Coyote Megaways
review: Wild Coyote Megaways: Slot OverviewHuh, funny, not long before this review was conducted, we reviewed Buster's Bones from NetEnt, which brought back memories of Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner and now along comes Wild Coyote Megaways, which is practically the animated cartoon's spitting image. It comes from casino game maker OneTouch which isn't a studio that hasn't pinged on the radar much till now. That's all about to change largely due to the Megaways association, in an online slot carrying some of the usual Megaways extras plus a few lesser-known additions.If you've seen any of the Road Runner/Wile E. Coyote cartoons, then Wild Coyote Megaways will feel comfortably familiar. Apparently, according to the Internet, Wile E. caught the Roadrunner once, in 1980, then asked viewers, 'Now what do I do?'Wild Coyote Megaways slot - base gameLocated mid-screen is Wild Coyote Megaways' gaming grid constructed of 6 vertically spinning reels and a 4 symbol top tracker reel which spins in a horizontal direction. With a highly volatile math model and a 96% RTP value, players can load up bets of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin on any preferred device.6-of-a-kind wins are the most desirable and pay 0.5 to 1 times the bet for the low pay 10-A card royals, or 1.2 to 10 times the bet for six bats, bombs, rockets, hammers or coyote premium symbols. Helping pull together wins is the regular wild symbol, but only from the tracker reel since it's the only reel it lands on. Wilds of all types substitute for any regular pay symbol. Lastly for now, Wild Coyote Megaways operates with a cascading wins system that removes winning symbols from the board and replaces them with new ones dropping from above. A cascade session stops when no new win is formed.Wild Coyote Megaways: Slot FeaturesWild Coyote Megaways slot - free spins splash screenTime for Wild Coyote Megaways to reach into its bag of tricks and show us what it's got. Specifically, what will be covered here are TNT Symbols, Roadrunner Wilds, free spins, and a bonus buy.TNT SymbolsTNT Symbols are mystery symbols, and whenever they land, they transform to reveal any pay symbol.Roadrunner WildsThe Roadrunner Wanted symbol appears only on the top tracker reel and is wild. When a Roadrunner symbol hits, it creates a stacked full reel wild beneath it on the main grid with a multiplier of up to x6 in the base game and always x6 in free spins.Free SpinsThe bonus round is triggered when 4, 5, 6, or 7 scatter symbols land to award 10, 12, 14, or 16 free spins, respectively. One thing added to free spins is a win multiplier starting at x1. Following winning cascades or spins, the multiplier increases by +1 and does not reset till the round ends. In addition, when symbols on the main reels match the symbol above them on the tracker, they are converted into wild symbols. Also, when a Roadrunner symbol hits, +4 free spins are awarded.To wrap things up, players who would prefer instant access to the bonus round can buy free spins for 100x the bet. This produces a spin which triggers the feature but does not produce any other winnings.Wild Coyote Megaways slot - free spinsWild Coyote Megaways: Slot VerdictIn the words of Weird Al Yankovic from the comedy film UHF 'Right now I'd like to show you one of my favourite cartoons. It's a sad, depressing story about a pathetic coyote who spends every waking moment of his life in the futile pursuit of a sadistic roadrunner who mocks him and laughs at him as he's repeatedly crushed and maimed! Hope you enjoy it!' To be fair, Weird Al's character George was in a bit of a mood when he said that and Wild Coyote Megaways, by contrast, is a bright, energetic slot which does a nice job of capturing some Saturday morning cartoon spirit. Interestingly, by a quick check, it appears neither Road Runner nor Wile E.
